documents.title: On the Third Day
documents.tagline: Hell is coming.
documents.overview: Cecilia and her son embark on a journey. On the third day, she is found wandering alone, not remembering what happened during this time. She is desperately looking for her son and finds herself wrapped in a brutal hunt, carried out by a religious fanatic, whom she faces off against. To her, he's a lunatic. To him, Cecilia is the enemy.
documents.plot:
On the Third Day (Spanish: Al 3er día) is a 2020 Argentine horror thriller directed by Daniel de la Vega from a screenplay by Alberto Fasce and Gonzalo Ventura, produced by Del Toro Films and Furia Films. It stars Mariana "Moro" Anghileri as Cecilia and Gerardo Romano as Enrique, with Diego Cremonesi as Fernando, Lautaro Delgado Tymruk, Osvaldo Santoro as Ventura, Osmar Núñez, Octavio Belmonte as Martín, Verónica Intile, Arturo Bonín and Rodolfo Ranni. Luciano Onetti composed the music. It runs about 85 to 88 minutes and carried the tagline "Hell is coming."

Cecilia, a young divorced mother, sets off into the night by car with her small son Martín, apparently eager to leave everything behind. On the way they have a serious, strange accident. Three days later Cecilia is found wandering alone and disoriented and cannot remember anything that happened in the meantime. Desperate to find her son, she struggles to make herself heard by the police and doctors while being pursued by the stubborn veteran detective Ventura and by her abusive ex-husband Fernando, confiding only in a kind doctor. In a parallel storyline, the film follows Enrique, a priest whom Cecilia encountered on her interrupted journey and who appears to be on a violent mission of his own, carrying an axe in his pick-up truck. As further disappearances and murders lead back to Cecilia and Martín, she is drawn into a brutal hunt led by the religious fanatic and must confront him. To her, he is a lunatic; to him, she is the enemy. Mirrors recur throughout the film, opening onto Cecilia's memories through hallucinations and double images, and the mystery is only fully revealed in the final act, which turns towards the supernatural.

The film premiered in Argentina on CineAR TV and the streaming platform CineAR Play in February 2021 and was later screened at the Fantasia International Film Festival. Reviews were divided. Adolfo C. Martínez of La Nación rated it good, praising de la Vega's handling of suspense and a cast in which Anghileri, Romano, Núñez and Santoro were impeccable. Santiago García of LeerCine found the plot predictable, the scares ineffective and Romano miscast. Signal Horizon, reviewing it at Fantasia, admired Anghileri's strong central performance but called the film a confused pastiche of giallo, possession and torture horror with weak computer effects and makeup.

documents.title: Robin Robin
documents.overview: A bird raised by mice begins to question where she belongs and sets off on a daring journey of self-discovery.
documents.plot:
Robin Robin is a 2021 British stop-motion animated musical short film directed by Dan Ojari and Mikey Please, who wrote the screenplay with Sam Morrison. Produced by Aardman Animations as its first collaboration with Netflix, the half-hour Christmas special was announced in November 2019 and stars the voices of Bronte Carmichael, Richard E. Grant, Gillian Anderson and Adeel Akhtar. Its puppets were needle-felted rather than made of plasticine. The film premiered at the BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2021 and was released worldwide on Netflix on 24 November 2021.

A bird's egg rolls into the path of a family of mice, and the robin that hatches from it is raised by them as one of their own. Robin (Carmichael) grows up believing she is a mouse and never learns to fly, but her clumsy enthusiasm keeps ruining the family's careful raids on the "Who-Man" houses for crumbs. When she spoils yet another outing, she begins to doubt that she really belongs, and although Dad Mouse (Akhtar) stands up for her, she feels guilty. Setting out on her own at night, she tries to break into another human house and meets a thieving Magpie (Grant), and the pair narrowly escape the house's malicious Cat (Anderson).

The Magpie takes Robin to his hideout, shows her the wonderful things he has collected, and tells her about the shiny star on top of the Christmas tree that supposedly brings people their wonderful things. The two resolve to steal the star. The heist goes well until Robin makes noise once again and hides in a shed, drawing the Cat's attention; she manages to drive the Cat off with fire, but blows up the whole shed in the process. Afterwards Robin wishes only to be a proper mouse. The next day her mouse family comes looking for her, but just as they are about to be reunited the Cat reappears. In the showdown Robin defeats the Cat and, at last, learns to fly. In the end Robin, the Magpie and the mice go crumb-hunting together: Robin distracts the humans, the Magpie wedges the door with a spoon, and the mice clear the dinner table.

Amira Macey-Michael, Tom Pegler, Endeavour Clutterbuck and Megan Harris voice Robin's mouse siblings. The score was composed by Ben Please and Beth Porter of the Bookshop Band and performed by the Bristol Ensemble, with lyrics by the directors. Robin Robin was well received by critics and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film, as well as at the British Academy Children's Awards and the NAACP Image Awards.

documents.title: The Shadow in My Eye
documents.overview: On March 21st, 1945, the British Royal Air Force set out on a mission to bomb Gestapo's headquarters in Copenhagen. The raid had fatal consequences as some of the bombers accidentally targeted a school and more than 120 people were killed, 86 of whom were children.
documents.plot:
The Shadow in My Eye (Danish: Skyggen i mit øje), released internationally as The Bombardment, is a 2021 Danish war drama film written and directed by Ole Bornedal. It depicts Operation Carthage, the 1945 Royal Air Force raid on the Gestapo headquarters in Copenhagen, during which one of the planes crashed near the Institut Jeanne d'Arc, leading other aircraft to mistake the school for the target and bomb it.

In German-occupied Denmark in 1945, an RAF Mosquito strafes a car carrying bridesmaids, mistaking it for a German staff vehicle. A boy named Henry, who witnesses the attack, is so traumatized that he loses the ability to speak, and his parents send him to Copenhagen to stay with his cousin Rigmor. Rigmor and her friend Eva, pupils at the Institut Jeanne d'Arc, a French-language Catholic school run by nuns, help Henry overcome his fear of open skies. Meanwhile, a young novice, Sister Teresa, who teaches the girls' class, struggles with her faith and, in an attempt to test God, begins an illicit romance with Frederik, a HIPO officer serving the German occupation authorities. At the request of the Danish resistance, the RAF plans to bomb the Shellhus, the Gestapo headquarters, to destroy its records and free imprisoned resistance members, though the Germans have placed hostages under its roof.

On the day of the raid, Eva quarrels with her parents over an unfinished bowl of porridge, Frederik, persuaded by Teresa, tells his parents he is deserting, and the head nun, Sister Hanna, moves to expel Teresa from the order. During the attack, the Mosquito flown by the pilots Pete and Andy hits a searchlight tower and crashes near the school, and other bombers strike the building, killing and wounding many pupils and teachers, while the Shellhus is hit and several prisoners escape. Henry regains his voice and helps firefighters identify wounded children. Rigmor and Teresa are trapped beneath the rubble as water from fire hoses floods the basement; Frederik tries to save Teresa, but she plunges into the water, perhaps to reach Rigmor, and the basement collapses. Eva's desperate parents finally find her at home, eating her cold porridge.

The film was released in Denmark in October 2021 and on Netflix internationally in March 2022. It drew criticism from the family of the real RAF pilot Peter Kleboe over its fictional opening attack, and the producers agreed to make editorial changes, an unusual step after a film's premiere.

documents.title: The Comeback Trail
documents.tagline: Hollywood has never pulled a stunt like this!
documents.overview: Two movie producers who owe money to the mob set up their aging movie star for an insurance scam to try and save themselves. But they wind up getting more than they ever imagined.
documents.plot:
The Comeback Trail is a 2020 American crime comedy film directed by Jay Roach. The movie follows two washed-up screenwriters, Howard Ratner and Jeremy Klein, who team up with a shady Hollywood producer, Seth Kaplan, to write a script for a biopic about a fictional boxer.

At its core, The Comeback Trail explores the themes of desperation, opportunism, and the commodification of art. The film delves into the darker side of Hollywood's power dynamics, where struggling artists are often forced to compromise their creative vision in pursuit of fame and fortune.

The movie also touches on the theme of toxic masculinity, as embodied by Seth Kaplan, a character who embodies the worst excesses of 1990s Hollywood. His character's ego, entitlement, and lack of empathy serve as a foil to the more vulnerable and insecure characters, highlighting the destructive nature of unchecked male privilege.

Furthermore, The Comeback Trail critiques the way in which art is often reduced to a commodity, with creators being exploited for their talent and creativity. The film's portrayal of the writers' struggles to maintain control over their work serves as a commentary on the broader cultural phenomenon of creative labor exploitation.

Overall, The Comeback Trail offers a scathing satire of Hollywood's excesses and the ways in which the industry can both enable and destroy artistic expression.

documents.title: A Fall from Grace
documents.tagline: Every Woman Has A Breaking Point
documents.overview: When a law-abiding woman gets indicted for murdering her husband, her lawyer soon realizes that a larger conspiracy may be at work.
documents.plot:
A Fall from Grace is a 2020 American thriller film produced, written and directed by Tyler Perry, the first of his films to be released by Netflix. It follows a novice attorney who defends a woman accused of killing the charming new husband who turned out to be a dangerous man. Crystal Fox, Phylicia Rashād, Bresha Webb and Mehcad Brooks star, and the cast includes Cicely Tyson in her final film role before her death in January 2021. Principal photography took place at Tyler Perry Studios in the fall of 2018 over just five days.

Jasmine Bryant is a public defender in a small Virginia town who routinely settles her cases with plea deals, while her husband Jordan, a police officer, is shaken after failing to save an elderly woman. Her boss Rory assigns her the case of Grace Waters, a woman charged with murdering her husband, Shannon DeLong. Grace insists she is guilty and wants only a plea deal that keeps her near her son Malcolm, but Jasmine is troubled by the case, not least because Shannon's body has never been found, and she decides to take it to trial despite Rory's objections about the cost and the media attention. Grace explains that after her divorce, her best friend Sarah Miller encouraged her to meet someone new, and she married Shannon, an artist, three months after meeting him at a gallery. He soon became cruel and secretive, stole from her accounts and forged documents to mortgage her house, she eventually lost her job at the bank, and on the final night she caught him in bed with another woman, beat him with a baseball bat and pushed him down the basement stairs. At trial Jasmine's defense collapses when Sarah admits on the stand that Grace confessed the killing to her, and Grace is convicted. As she is led away, however, Grace notices that Sarah is wearing a pendant identical to a supposedly one-of-a-kind piece of Shannon's, and she begins to see Sarah's hand in every stage of her relationship. Jasmine, now fired, visits Sarah's home, where she uncovers a sinister secret involving elderly women held captive, putting her own life in danger as Jordan races to find her.

Netflix released the film on January 17, 2020, and it was watched by 26 million viewers in its first week. Critics panned it, particularly its screenplay, giving it a 15% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 34, and viewers noted visible production errors such as boom microphones; the improvised line "Ashtray, bitch!" became an internet meme.

documents.title: Sky High
documents.overview: A commentary on Spanish society dressed as a thriller about the misadventures of a gang of young petty criminals after the real estate crash.
documents.plot:
Sky High (Spanish: Hasta el cielo) is a Spanish crime thriller from 2020, directed by Daniel Calparsoro from a screenplay by Jorge Guerricaechevarría. Miguel Herrán stars as Ángel, a young man from the outskirts of Madrid, with Carolina Yuste as Estrella, Luis Tosar as the crime boss Rogelio, Asia Ortega as his daughter Sole, Fernando Cayo as the detective Duque, Patricia Vico as Mercedes, César Mateo as Fernando and Ayax Pedrosa as Motos, alongside Richard Holmes and Dollar Selmouni. Produced by Vaca Films with RTVE, Movistar+ and Telemadrid, it was conceived as a portrait of Spanish society after the property crash, told through the rise of a gang of young criminals.

Ángel's life changes the night he speaks to Estrella in a nightclub. He ends up fighting her possessive boyfriend, Poli, who, rather than holding a grudge, invites him to join the crew of armed robbers he runs, a gang that has the Madrid police on the back foot. Ángel proves a natural and quickly climbs a ladder of heists, laundered cash, shady businesses and crooked lawyers, while the relentless Duque closes in on him.

Ignoring warnings from the people closest to him, Ángel keeps rising until he becomes the protégé of Rogelio, one of the men who control the city's black market. Working with Rogelio and getting close to his daughter Sole, he learns that power comes at a steep price, and he is forced to choose between his future as a robber and Estrella, the love of his life. The story follows his journey from the poorest suburbs toward the summit promised by the title. The soundtrack, by Carlos Jean, blends electronic and urban music and includes tracks by C. Tangana.

Filming took place over eight weeks from September 2019 in Madrid, Valencia, Ibiza and A Coruña, on a budget of about €4 million. The film was presented at the 23rd Málaga Film Festival in August 2020 and released in Spanish cinemas by Universal Pictures on 18 December 2020, grossing about €2.1 million there, before reaching a wider audience on Netflix. Spanish critics broadly saw it as an energetic update of the quinqui youth-crime films of the late 1970s and 1980s. El Mundo praised Calparsoro's command of the genre and singled out Yuste, as did El País, which called it good entertainment; others found it repetitive or felt its social critique fell flat. Netflix followed it with a sequel series in 2023.

documents.title: Pixie
documents.tagline: Shall we go see the big scary drug dealer now?
documents.overview: To avenge her mother's death, Pixie masterminds a heist but must flee across Ireland from gangsters, take on the patriarchy, and choose her own destiny.
documents.plot:
Pixie is a 2020 British comedy thriller film directed by Barnaby Thompson. Olivia Cooke stars as Pixie Hardy, a resourceful young woman, with Ben Hardy and Daryl McCormack as Frank and Harland, two best friends who become entangled in her schemes, Colm Meaney as her gangster stepfather Dermot O'Brien, and Alec Baldwin as Father Hector McGrath, the leader of a gang of corrupt priests. The supporting cast includes Ned Dennehy, Dylan Moran, Rory Fleck Byrne, Fra Fee and Turlough Convery. Filming began in Northern Ireland in August 2019, with locations including Killough.

In Sligo, the criminals Fergus and Colin gun down a gang of drug-trafficking priests and steal fifteen kilos of MDMA. When Colin discovers that Fergus plans to run away to San Francisco with his ex-girlfriend Pixie, he kills Fergus in a jealous rage and takes the drugs. Stood up at the airport, Pixie drowns her sorrows at a club, where she meets Frank and Harland, and when Frank later visits her for a portrait session, Harland accidentally runs over Colin as he arrives with a gun. The friends leave with Colin's body and the drugs, which belong to Pixie's stepfather Dermot, Fergus and Colin's boss, whose resentful son Mickey suspects Pixie, while Dermot's menacing enforcer Seamus is sent to investigate. Pixie insists on joining Frank and Harland as they drive to Dingle to sell the haul through their dealer's uncle, Raymond, who promptly tries to rob them. On the road, Pixie reveals that she masterminded the original robbery and had planned to double-cross both Fergus and Colin and escape to San Francisco alone. With Seamus, Dermot's gang and the vengeful priests all closing in, and a revelation about her mother's death fueling her anger, Pixie devises an audacious plan to sell the drugs back to Father Hector, leading to a showdown between rival gangsters and clergy in a church.

Paramount Pictures released Pixie in the United Kingdom on 23 October 2020. It holds a 76% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus says the film borrows shamelessly from similar heist thrillers but that Cooke's outstanding lead performance makes it a great getaway vehicle; Metacritic gave it a score of 45.

documents.title: The Wolf of Snow Hollow
documents.tagline: Welcome To Snow Hollow.
documents.overview: A stressed-out police officer struggles not to give in to the paranoia that grips his small mountain town as bodies turn up after each full moon.
documents.plot: Terror grips a small mountain town as bodies are discovered after each full moon. Losing sleep, raising a teenage daughter, and caring for his ailing father, officer Marshall struggles to remind himself there's no such thing as werewolves.

documents.title: Josee, the Tiger and the Fish
documents.tagline: Together they can fly.
documents.overview: With dreams of diving abroad, Tsuneo gets a job assisting Josee, an artist whose imagination takes her far beyond her wheelchair. But when the tide turns against them, they push each other to places they never thought possible, and inspire a love fit for a storybook.
documents.plot:
Josee, the Tiger and the Fish is a 2020 Japanese drama film directed by Sion Sono, produced by Shochiku, and based on the manga of the same name by Akihiko Yoshida. The movie follows the story of Josee, a young woman who has been confined to her home since childhood due to a rare condition that prevents her from moving or speaking.

The film begins with Josee's life in isolation, where she spends most of her time playing with a stuffed tiger and watching fish swim in a tank. Her only companion is a man named Kōichi, who visits her every day to bring her food and talk to her through the window. Despite their limited interactions, Kōichi has become an integral part of Josee's life, and she begins to develop feelings for him.

One day, Kōichi decides to take matters into his own hands and convinces a young man named Tetsuya to help him bring Josee out of her shell. Tetsuya is initially hesitant but eventually agrees to assist Kōichi in helping Josee overcome her condition. As they work together, the three form an unlikely bond, with Josee slowly beginning to interact with the world outside her home.

However, their progress is hindered by the complexities of Josee's condition and the societal expectations placed upon her. The medical professionals who have been caring for Josee are skeptical of Tetsuya's involvement, and Kōichi struggles to balance his desire to help Josee with the need to protect her from the outside world.

As the story unfolds, the film explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the human need for connection. Through Josee's character, the movie highlights the challenges faced by individuals with rare conditions and the importance of empathy and understanding in breaking down barriers.

The title "Josee, the Tiger and the Fish" is a metaphor for Josee's inner world, where she finds solace in her stuffed tiger and watches fish swim in her tank. The tiger represents her imagination and creativity, while the fish symbolize her longing for freedom and connection with the outside world.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a poignant and emotional conclusion as Josee begins to confront her condition and the limitations placed upon her. Through her journey, the movie offers a powerful exploration of the human spirit and the importance of finding ways to overcome adversity.

Overall, Josee, the Tiger and the Fish is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores themes of isolation, loneliness, and the power of human connection. With its unique blend of drama and fantasy elements, the movie offers a captivating and emotional viewing experience.

documents.title: Half Brothers
documents.tagline: There's no running from family.
documents.overview: A story about the complex connection with a brother who is based in Mexico, meant to be a metaphor of the relationship between neighboring countries America and Mexico.
documents.plot:
Half Brothers is a 2020 American road comedy-drama film directed by Luke Greenfield from a screenplay by Eduardo Cisneros and Jason Shuman. Luis Gerardo Méndez stars as Renato, a successful Mexican businessman, and Connor Del Rio as Asher, his carefree American half-brother, with José Zúñiga as their father, Flavio, Vincent Spano, Pia Watson and Juan Pablo Espinosa. Focus Features released it on 4 December 2020.

Renato, an executive at an aviation company in Mexico, is about to get married when he receives a call from a woman named Katherine, who tells him that his father, Flavio, is gravely ill and wants to see him in Chicago. Renato reluctantly agrees, though he has long resented Flavio, who emigrated to the United States during the Mexican peso crisis when Renato was a boy and never came back for him. At the hospital, Renato discovers that he has a half-brother, Asher, an irresponsible free spirit whom he had already crossed paths with at a coffee shop without knowing who he was.

Flavio asks his two sons to deliver an envelope marked "Eloise" to a man named Evaristo in St. Louis, the first stage in a series of clues that will take them on a journey across the country. Asher eagerly accepts, while Renato refuses, but after Flavio's death he grudgingly agrees to go. The trip proves chaotic: Asher steals a goat, which he names Renatito, from a ranch guarded by armed men, and the brothers clash repeatedly. In St. Louis they find an old factory that makes the radio-controlled planes Renato once flew with his father, and Evaristo, a friend who emigrated with Flavio, who reveals how the two men worked there as cheap laborers before Flavio helped turn the business around with Katherine. Following the trail of clues, the brothers gradually piece together their father's life in America and the reasons he never returned to Mexico, learning to understand him, and each other, along the way as they face their own failings and the meaning of family.

Combining broad road-trip comedy with a family drama about immigration, absent fathers and reconciliation, Half Brothers gave Méndez, known for Mexican comedies and the series Club de Cuervos, a leading role in an American studio release, playing opposite Del Rio in a bilingual story.

documents.title: Vacation Friends
documents.tagline: They came home with some extra baggage.
documents.overview: When a straight-laced couple that has fun with a rowdy couple on vacation in Mexico return to the States, they discover that the crazy couple they met in Mexico followed them back home and decide to play tricks on them.
documents.plot:
Vacation Friends is a 2021 American comedy film directed by Jonathan Hoffman and written by Jared Abrahamson and Will Breeden. The movie follows the story of two young couples, Jason and Emily (played by John Cena and Piper Hurd) and Luke and Erin (played by Lil Rel Howery and Yvonne Orji), who embark on a wild adventure together.

The film begins with Jason and Emily, a couple from suburban New Jersey, celebrating their fifth wedding anniversary. They are feeling unfulfilled in their relationship and decide to take a break from each other to focus on themselves. Meanwhile, Luke and Erin, a young couple from Los Angeles, are also going through a rough patch in their relationship.

The two couples meet at a music festival, where they strike up a conversation and discover that they have more in common than they initially thought. They decide to take a road trip together to Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, with the intention of rekindling their relationships and finding themselves.

As the trip progresses, the group's dynamics become increasingly complicated. Jason and Emily struggle to reconcile their differences, while Luke and Erin face challenges in their own relationship. The group also encounters various misadventures, including a wild night at a bar, a disastrous dinner date, and a chaotic encounter with a group of rowdy spring breakers.

Throughout the trip, the couples are forced to confront their own flaws and insecurities. Jason and Emily must deal with the reality of their stagnant relationship, while Luke and Erin face the consequences of their own immaturity. The group's interactions become increasingly raw and honest, leading to some uncomfortable but ultimately cathartic moments.

As the trip comes to a close, the couples are forced to confront the harsh realities of their relationships. Jason and Emily must decide whether they can work through their issues, while Luke and Erin face the possibility of breaking up for good. The film's climax features a dramatic confrontation between the two couples, which ultimately leads to some surprising revelations and a newfound sense of clarity.

In the end, Vacation Friends is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of love, relationships, and self-discovery. The film features a talented ensemble cast, witty dialogue, and plenty of laughs. While it may not be perfect, the movie's authentic portrayal of modern relationships makes it a relatable and entertaining watch.

documents.title: Miss Americana
documents.overview: A raw and emotionally revealing look at one of the most iconic artists of our time during a transformational period in her life as she learns to embrace her role not only as a songwriter and performer, but as a woman harnessing the full power of her voice.
documents.plot:
Miss Americana is a 2020 documentary film that delves into the life of Taylor Swift, an American singer-songwriter. The movie explores themes of identity, feminism, and the complexities of fame.

At its core, Miss Americana is a deeply personal and introspective film that examines the tensions between Swift's public persona and her private self. As she navigates the pressures of being a global superstar, Swift grapples with the expectations placed upon her as a woman in the entertainment industry. The film sheds light on the ways in which societal norms and media scrutiny can shape our perceptions of ourselves and our place in the world.

Throughout the documentary, Swift's character is portrayed as a multifaceted individual struggling to maintain her artistic integrity amidst the demands of fame. Her relationships with others, including her family and romantic partners, are also subject to scrutiny, highlighting the challenges of balancing personal and professional life.

One of the primary concerns of Miss Americana is the performative nature of identity in contemporary culture. Swift's character embodies this theme as she navigates the blurred lines between her public persona and private self. The film raises questions about the ways in which we present ourselves to the world, and whether these performances can ever truly be authentic.

Ultimately, Miss Americana presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. Through Swift's story, the documentary sheds light on the complexities of fame, identity, and the search for meaning in a hyper-mediated world.

documents.title: Save Yourselves!
documents.tagline: Turning off their phones was the dumbest idea on the planet.
documents.overview: A young Brooklyn couple head upstate to disconnect from their phones and reconnect with themselves. Cut off from their devices, they miss the news that the planet is under attack.
documents.plot:
Save Yourselves! is a 2020 American science fiction romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships and human connection in the face of catastrophic change. The movie takes place on a spaceship where two couples, struggling with their own issues, must navigate the challenges of isolation and confinement.

At its core, Save Yourselves! delves into the theme of love and relationships in the most unexpected ways. As the characters' initial romantic connections begin to fray under the pressure of their situation, they are forced to confront the true nature of intimacy and connection. The film masterfully weaves together humor, pathos, and wit to examine the ways in which people respond to crisis and the importance of human vulnerability.

The movie also touches on the theme of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships with others. As the characters' sense of self becomes increasingly tied to their romantic partners, they must confront the possibility that their identities may be more fluid than they initially thought. This exploration of identity is both poignant and humorous, highlighting the ways in which our relationships can both define and redefine us.

Ultimately, Save Yourselves! presents a nuanced and thought-provoking commentary on the human condition, one that celebrates the complexities and messiness of love and relationships while also acknowledging their transformative power.

documents.title: Disclosure
documents.tagline: Trans lives on screen
documents.overview: An investigation of how Hollywood's fabled stories have deeply influenced how Americans feel about transgender people, and how transgender people have been taught to feel about themselves.
documents.plot:
Disclosure, originally subtitled Trans Lives on Screen, is a 2020 American documentary directed by Sam Feder, who produced it with Amy Scholder. It examines how Hollywood film and television have depicted transgender people and how those depictions have shaped both trans people's understanding of themselves and the wider public's view of them. Laverne Cox served as an executive producer and is one of the central interviewees.

Every person interviewed in the film is transgender. Alongside Cox, the participants include Jen Richards, Susan Stryker, Alexandra Billings, Jamie Clayton, Chaz Bono, Yance Ford, Trace Lysette, Mj Rodriguez, Angelica Ross, Candis Cayne, Lilly Wachowski and Leo Sheng. Combining their testimony with hundreds of clips, the documentary traces gender-nonconforming characters back to silent films such as D. W. Griffith's Judith of Bethulia and follows them up to series such as Pose. It notes that, according to GLAAD, most Americans say they do not personally know a trans person, so their ideas come largely from the media. The interviewees discuss recurring patterns: trans characters played for laughs in sitcoms and cross-dressing comedies such as Tootsie; trans women cast as psychopathic killers in Psycho, Dressed to Kill and The Silence of the Lambs; scenes of characters vomiting on discovering a trans person's body, as in The Crying Game and Ace Ventura: Pet Detective; and the trope of the shocking "disclosure" that frames trans people as deceivers. They also criticize the casting of cisgender male stars as trans women, the scarcity of trans men on screen, the frequent casting of trans women as sex workers or murder victims, and the erasure of Black trans people. The film contrasts these images with portrayals the participants found affirming, from Yentl to Bugs Bunny, and with the recent rise of trans actors in shows such as Orange Is the New Black, Sense8 and Pose, while stressing that visibility alone has not ended discrimination.

Feder, inspired by The Celluloid Closet, compiled hundreds of film and television titles with Cox's input, and editor Stacy Goldate shaped the material thematically rather than chronologically. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020 and was released on Netflix on June 19, 2020. It was acclaimed by critics in outlets including Variety, the Los Angeles Times and Sight and Sound, holds a 98% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and won the GLAAD Media Award for Outstanding Documentary.

documents.title: Amulet
documents.tagline: Have faith in fear
documents.overview: Tomaz, an ex-soldier now homeless in London, is offered a place to stay at a decaying house, inhabited by a young woman and her dying mother. As he starts to fall for Magda, Tomaz cannot ignore his suspicion that something insidious might also be living alongside them.
documents.plot:
Amulet is a 2020 British supernatural horror film written and directed by Romola Garai in her feature directorial debut. Carla Juri, Alec Secăreanu, Angeliki Papoulia and Imelda Staunton star in the story of a homeless former soldier who is offered shelter in a decaying London house occupied by a young woman and her dying mother, and who gradually comes to suspect that something unnatural also lives there. The film premiered in the Midnight section of the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020 and was released later that year.

Secăreanu plays Tomaz, a man from an unnamed Eastern European country who once served as a border guard at a remote forest outpost. In flashbacks, he recalls Miriam, a woman fleeing across the border whose life he spared and who took refuge with him, and the discovery of a strange amulet buried in the woods. In the present, Tomaz works as a day labourer in London and sleeps in a derelict building with other migrants. When the squat is set on fire, he collapses in an alley and is found by Sister Claire, a nun played by Staunton.

After visiting him in hospital, Claire offers Tomaz a new start, taking him to a crumbling house where a young woman, Magda, played by Juri, cares for her bedridden mother and needs help with repairs. Magda is initially hostile and Tomaz is reluctant to remain, but the two slowly grow close as he fixes the house. Strange things begin to accumulate: unnerving noises from the attic, a bizarre creature found in the plumbing, and the violent, unseen presence of the mother, whom Magda refuses to let him see. As Tomaz's attraction to Magda deepens, he realises that the house holds a secret connected to his own past, and the film moves toward revelations about guilt, abuse and punishment.

Garai uses the gothic haunted-house framework to explore themes of male violence, trauma and atonement, and she gradually shifts the film from slow-burning psychological unease into overt body horror. Cinematographer Laura Bellingham's muted imagery and the film's deliberate pacing were frequently noted by reviewers.

Amulet received generally positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 73 percent; the consensus observes that although its chilly dread never becomes spine-tingling terror, the film remains smart and solidly disquieting, marking a promising debut for Garai.

documents.title: The Mole Agent
documents.tagline: It's never too late to become a spy.
documents.overview: When a daughter becomes concerned about her mother's well-being in a retirement home, private investigator Romulo hires Sergio, an 83-year-old man who becomes a new resident—and a mole inside the home, who struggles to balance his assignment with becoming increasingly involved in the lives of several residents.
documents.plot:
The Mole Agent is a 2020 documentary film that explores the life of an undercover agent who infiltrated the Japanese government's intelligence agency in the 1970s and 1980s. 

At its core, The Mole Agent delves into themes of deception, loyalty, and identity. It raises questions about the nature of truth and how it can be manipulated by those in power. The film also touches on the complexities of cultural exchange and the blurred lines between espionage and diplomacy.

Through the story of this undercover agent, who was tasked with gathering intelligence while pretending to be a loyal Japanese citizen, the documentary sheds light on the moral dilemmas that arise when individuals are forced to navigate multiple identities and allegiances. The film ultimately poses profound questions about the human condition, encouraging viewers to consider the consequences of deception and the importance of authenticity in our personal and professional lives.

The Mole Agent is a thought-provoking exploration of the gray areas between loyalty, duty, and self-preservation, leaving audiences with a deeper understanding of the complexities of espionage and the human cost of secrecy.

documents.title: Devotion
documents.tagline: In America’s forgotten war, they made history.
documents.overview: The harrowing true story of two elite US Navy fighter pilots during the Korean War. Their heroic sacrifices would ultimately make them the Navy's most celebrated wingmen.
documents.plot:
Devotion is a 2022 American biographical war film directed by J. D. Dillard and written by Jake Crane and Jonathan Stewart, based on Adam Makos's book about the friendship between naval aviators Jesse L. Brown and Tom Hudner during the Korean War. It stars Jonathan Majors as Brown and Glen Powell as Hudner, with Christina Jackson, Joe Jonas and Thomas Sadoski.

In early 1950, Lieutenant Tom Hudner joins Fighter Squadron 32, where Ensign Jesse Brown is the only Black pilot. The unit flies the powerful but dangerous F4U Corsair. Hudner begins giving Brown rides and meets his wife Daisy and their daughter Pam, and he learns that Brown privately shouts racist abuse at himself in the mirror to steel himself before missions. Before the squadron deploys on the USS Leyte to the Mediterranean, Daisy makes Hudner promise to be there for Jesse. When a squadron mate dies in a landing crash after ignoring instructions, Brown explains that had he always done as he was told, racist superiors would have ended his career long ago. On shore leave in Cannes, Brown charms Elizabeth Taylor into inviting the squadron to a casino, and after Hudner fights a Marine who harassed Brown, Brown tells him not to fight his battles but simply to stand by him.

When war breaks out in Korea, the Leyte is redeployed, and in November 1950 the squadron is ordered to destroy bridges on the Yalu River while firing only on the Korean side. Brown disobeys Hudner's order to retreat and destroys the last bridge alone; Hudner's report notes the disobedience, which Brown fears will cost him promotions. While supporting Marines at the Battle of Chosin Reservoir, Brown's plane is hit and he crash-lands in the mountains. Seeing that he is alive but trapped, Hudner deliberately crash-lands beside him, but he cannot free Brown, who dies shortly after a rescue helicopter arrives. With recovery judged too risky, the squadron destroys the wreckage with Brown's body inside. Months later, President Harry S. Truman awards Hudner the Medal of Honor, and Daisy tells him that she only asked him to be there for Jesse, not to save him. A closing note says that Brown's remains have never been recovered and that the families remain close.

Devotion premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 12, 2022, and was released by Sony Pictures on November 23. Despite positive reviews (81% on Rotten Tomatoes), it grossed only about $21.7 million against a $90 million budget.

documents.title: The Christmas Chronicles: Part Two
documents.tagline: The battle to save Christmas is on.
documents.overview: Kate Pierce is reluctantly spending Christmas with her mom’s new boyfriend and his son Jack. But when the North Pole and Christmas are threatened to be destroyed, Kate and Jack are unexpectedly pulled into a new adventure with Santa Claus.
documents.plot:
The Christmas Chronicles: Part Two is a 2020 American Christmas fantasy film directed by Chris Columbus and written by Marc Silverstein, Ivan Menchell, and Noah Schnapp. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2018 film The Christmas Chronicles.

The story begins with two years having passed since the events of the first film. Kurt (played by Darby Camp) is now 12 years old, and she's struggling to cope with the loss of her father, who died in a tragic accident during their adventures with Santa Claus (Kurt Russell). The holiday season has become increasingly difficult for Kurt, as she feels abandoned by Santa and struggles to connect with him.

Meanwhile, Nick (played by Josh Hutcherson) is dealing with his own issues. He's been feeling left out of the family dynamics since his father passed away, and he's struggling to find his place in the world. His relationship with his mother, Kate (played by Goldie Hawn), has become strained due to her busy schedule as a single parent.

As Christmas approaches, Santa Claus is facing a new challenge: a group of rogue elves who are threatening to ruin the holiday season. The elves, led by a mysterious figure known as "The Kringle Killer," have stolen the magical crystal that powers Santa's sleigh, and they're using it to spread chaos and destruction around the world.

Kurt, Nick, and their friend Gus (played by Christian Navarro) team up with Santa to embark on a mission to retrieve the stolen crystal. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes, ferocious creatures, and even a rival group of elves who claim to be working for Santa.

As the story unfolds, Kurt begins to confront her feelings about her father's death and her relationship with Santa. She learns that her father had been working closely with Santa to help him deal with the growing threat of the rogue elves, and she realizes that she has a crucial role to play in saving Christmas.

The movie culminates in an action-packed showdown between Kurt, Nick, Gus, and Santa against the Kringle Killer and his minions. In the end, they successfully retrieve the stolen crystal, and Christmas is saved.

Throughout the film, there are several heartwarming moments that highlight the importance of family, friendship, and the true spirit of Christmas. The movie also explores themes of grief, loss, and healing, as Kurt navigates her complicated emotions about her father's death.

Overall, The Christmas Chronicles: Part Two is a fun, action-packed holiday film that's perfect for families to enjoy together. With its blend of adventure, humor, and heart, it's sure to become a new Christmas classic.

documents.title: How to Train Your Dragon: Snoggletog Log
documents.original_title: How to Train Your Dragon: Snoggletog Log
documents.overview: When Hiccup and Toothless begin sharing stories of their special relationship with their respective families as they prepare for the Snoggletog Festival, it quickly becomes clear that the new generation of Vikings don’t remember the bond between dragon and human.
documents.plot: When Hiccup and Toothless begin sharing stories of their special relationship with their respective families as they prepare for the Snoggletog Festival, it quickly becomes clear that the new generation of Vikings don’t remember the bond between dragon and human.

documents.title: Billie Eilish: The World's a Little Blurry
documents.original_title: Billie Eilish: The World's a Little Blurry
documents.overview: This documentary offers a deeply intimate look at extraordinary teenager Billie Eilish. Award-winning filmmaker R.J. Cutler follows her journey on the road, onstage, and at home with her family as the writing and recording of her debut album changes her life.
documents.plot:
Billie Eilish: The World's a Little Blurry is a documentary film that delves into the life and career of pop sensation Billie Eilish, showcasing her journey from a young girl with a passion for music to a global superstar. At its core, the film explores themes of identity, creativity, and the pressures of fame.

One of the primary concerns of the documentary is Billie's struggle to maintain her individuality in the face of overwhelming commercial success. As she navigates the cutthroat music industry, she must confront the tension between staying true to herself and conforming to the expectations of others. This internal conflict is reflected in her music, which often grapples with themes of anxiety, self-doubt, and the fragility of mental health.

The film also sheds light on Billie's complex relationship with her family, particularly her parents, who have been instrumental in shaping her career. Their influence is both a blessing and a curse, as it has allowed Billie to achieve incredible success but also raised questions about the cost of fame and the impact of parental pressure on artistic expression.

Throughout the documentary, Billie's creative process is also put under scrutiny, revealing the meticulous attention to detail that goes into crafting her music. Her innovative approach to songwriting and production is a testament to her unique perspective and artistic vision, which has captivated audiences worldwide.

Ultimately, Billie Eilish: The World's a Little Blurry presents a nuanced portrait of a young artist navigating the complexities of fame, identity, and creativity. By offering an intimate look at Billie's life and career, the documentary invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences with success, self-expression, and the blurred lines between personal and public lives.

documents.title: Home Sweet Home Alone
documents.tagline: No parents. No problem.
documents.overview: After being left at home by himself for the holidays, 10-year-old Max Mercer must work to defend his home from a married couple who tries to steal back a valuable heirloom.
documents.plot:
Home Sweet Home Alone is a 2021 American Christmas comedy film and the sixth installment in the Home Alone franchise. Directed by Dan Mazer and written by Mikey Day and Streeter Seidell, it stars Ellie Kemper, Rob Delaney, Archie Yates, Aisling Bea, Kenan Thompson, Pete Holmes and Ally Maki, with Devin Ratray reprising his role as Buzz McCallister from the first two films. Produced by 20th Century Studios, it was released on Disney+ on 12 November 2021.

Jeff and Pam McKenzie are quietly trying to sell their house without telling their children, Abby and Chris. Jeff has lost his job, and Pam's salary is not enough to keep up with the mortgage. To make matters worse, Jeff's smug, successful brother Hunter and his family are coming to stay with them for Christmas. During an open house, ten-year-old Max Mercer and his mother Carol stop in to use the bathroom. Jeff shows Max a box of old dolls, including a defective one with an upside-down face, and Carol mentions that dolls with rare flaws can be worth a fortune. Soon afterward Jeff discovers that the doll has disappeared.

Max's large family is preparing to fly to Tokyo for the holidays. Annoyed by the commotion, Max falls asleep in a car parked in the garage, and the family leaves for the airport without him. When he wakes the next morning, he is delighted to find himself home alone. Jeff, convinced that Max stole the doll, which he hopes will save his family from financial ruin, recruits Pam to help him break into the Mercer house to get it back. Overhearing the couple's plans and assuming they are dangerous burglars, Max turns his home into a fortress filled with elaborate booby traps. When Jeff and Pam attempt their break-in, they suffer a series of painful slapstick injuries, while Max's mother scrambles to get back to her son and the truth about the missing doll comes to light.

The film received generally negative reviews. Critics found its humor flat and noted that the story, which makes the bumbling intruders sympathetic and the child something of an antagonist, inverted the appeal of the original film without improving on it. Many reviewers argued that the franchise had little left to offer. Ratray's brief return as Buzz, now a police officer, was one of the film's most discussed nods to the original.

documents.title: Eiffel
documents.tagline: You will never look at it the same way again.
documents.overview: The government is asking Eiffel to design something spectacular for the 1889 Paris World Fair, but Eiffel simply wants to design the subway. Suddenly, everything changes when Eiffel crosses paths with a mysterious woman from his past.
documents.plot:
Eiffel is a 2021 French romantic drama directed by Martin Bourboulon from a screenplay credited to Caroline Bongrand and other writers. Romain Duris stars as the engineer Gustave Eiffel, with Emma Mackey as Adrienne Bourgès and Pierre Deladonchamps as her husband, the journalist Antoine de Restac. Presented as "freely inspired by real events," the film builds a fictionalized love story around the creation of the Eiffel Tower. It premiered in March 2021 at the Alliance Française French Film Festival in Australia and was released in France by Pathé in October 2021.

In 1886, fresh from his success designing the iron framework for the Statue of Liberty, Eiffel is looking for his next major project ahead of the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. His engineers propose a tall metal tower, but he initially dismisses the idea in favor of designing a metro system for the city. To promote his firm he reconnects with an old acquaintance, Antoine de Restac, and at a society dinner meets Antoine's wife Adrienne. The encounter shakes him, and to the astonishment of the guests he suddenly announces that he will build a 300-metre tower.

Flashbacks to Bordeaux in 1860 reveal the source of his reaction. While building an iron bridge over the Garonne, the young Eiffel dived into the river to save a worker and then sought timber for safety scaffolding from Bourgès, a wealthy local businessman. There he met Bourgès's spirited daughter Adrienne, who supported his request, and the two fell passionately in love despite the disapproval of her family. In the present, Eiffel struggles to win the contract, raise money, overcome public hostility to his design and solve formidable engineering problems with the tower's foundations, while his rekindled feelings for Adrienne threaten both her marriage and his reputation.

The film received mostly positive reviews in France and grossed about $13.6 million worldwide. Critics praised its production design, its depiction of the tower's construction and the chemistry between Duris and Mackey. Others were skeptical of the invented romance; Peter Debruge of Variety described it as less a biopic than a sketchy piece of historical fiction, while David Stratton of The Australian noted its ambition.

documents.title: Coven
documents.overview: French Basque Country, year 1609. The men of a small fishing village have gone to sea. Judge Rostegui, who has been charged by the king with ridding the country of the devil's wiles, arrests Ana and her friends and accuses them of witchcraft.
documents.plot:
Coven (Basque: Akelarre) is a 2020 historical drama directed by Pablo Agüero, starring Amaia Aberasturi and Àlex Brendemühl, with Daniel Fanego, Garazi Urkola and Yune Nogueiras in supporting roles. Set during the witch hunts of the early 17th century, it was produced by a group of Spanish, French and Argentine companies including Sorgin Films, Lamia Producciones, Kowalski Films and La Fidèle Productions.

In 1609, in a fishing village of the Basque Country, the men are away at sea when a group of young women who have gathered in the woods for a night of singing and dancing are seized by the authorities. Judge Rostegui, sent by the king to purge the region of witchcraft, accuses them of being witches and resolves to obtain their confession by any means. He is particularly obsessed with learning about the akelarre, the sabbath at which the Devil is supposed to initiate his followers and couple with them. Although the young women deny everything and there is no evidence against them, they are imprisoned, interrogated and tortured in an effort to force them to sign confessions.

When yet another friend is arrested, Ana decides on a desperate strategy. She declares that she is a witch who has bewitched the others, and begins giving the judge an elaborate account of the sabbath, in truth a distorted version of the innocent gathering the girls had held before their arrest. Her aim is to buy time until the village men return from their fishing voyage. Fascinated, Rostegui delays the executions when Ana claims that her powers awaken only under the full moon, and he even agrees to supply everything she says the ceremony requires, arousing the suspicion of some of his own men. Warned that the fishermen will soon be back and the prisoners freed, he hurries the women into the forest to stage the ritual. There, Ana leads her companions in a performance of dance and Basque song that captivates the judge but terrifies his men and the village priest. In the ensuing confusion the women flee through the woods until they are trapped at the edge of a cliff, where, joining hands and inspired by an old woman's song about the tide and the full moon, they leap into the sea before the astonished men.

Coven was well received by critics, earning an 86% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 14 reviews. It won five of its nine nominations at the 35th Goya Awards and was nominated in six categories at the 8th Feroz Awards.

documents.title: Dirty Sexy Saint
documents.tagline: Of all the bars in all of Chicago, she walks into his.
documents.overview: Clay Kincaid hates the nickname 'Saint', he got for being too kind to stray animals and desperate people. Especially when it comes to women. With a rough and damaged past that has left him jaded, he doesn't do committed relationships. This is before he meets Samantha Jamieson, an heiress turned runaway in need of help. When she starts to work as a waitress at his bar, he discovers that she is someone truly special and amazing… someone that could warm his damaged heart.
documents.plot:
Dirty Sexy Saint is a 2019 American romantic drama film directed by Tosca Musk for the streaming service Passionflix, which released it on 8 December 2019. It is based on the novel of the same name by the New York Times bestselling romance authors Carly Phillips and Erika Wilde (the pen name of Janelle Denison), adapted for the screen by Joany Kane and Musk, who also served as an executive producer. Michael Buttiglieri produced, Margaret Goodspeed edited and Ben Collier composed the score. The film stars David A. Gregory as Clay Kincaid and Jordan Lane Price as Samantha Jamieson, with Matt Magnusson and Luke Guldan as Clay's brothers Mason and Levi, Steven Hauck as Samantha's father Conrad, and Jamie Choi, Alena Chinault, Brian Cade and Maia Guest in supporting roles. It runs 104 minutes and was promoted with the tagline "Of all the bars in all of Chicago, she walks into his."

Clay Kincaid owns a flourishing bar in Chicago. He hates the nickname "Saint," which he earned for being too kind to stray animals and to desperate people, especially women, and he knows he is more sinner than saint where women are concerned. Behind his success lies a rough and damaged past that has left him jaded and that may yet come back to haunt him, and as a result he does not do committed relationships. Everything changes when Samantha, a rebellious heiress turned runaway who is in need of help, walks into his bar. Clay helps her slowly get back on her feet and offers her a job as a waitress. As they work side by side, he discovers that she is someone truly special, someone who might be able to warm his damaged heart and who may be exactly the person he needs in his life. The emotional climax comes when Clay finally opens up to Samantha about his troubled past.

Markos Papadatos of Digital Journal gave the film an A rating, calling it entertaining, poignant and well crafted. He praised Gregory, whose years on the daytime drama One Life to Live he felt had paid off, for a bold, raw and vulnerable performance, singling out a gut-wrenching, monologue-heavy scene in which Clay reveals his past, described Price as sensational and credited Musk for her work as director, co-writer and showrunner. He also noted the film's emphasis on responsibility, morality and helping others in a time of need.

documents.title: Poupelle of Chimney Town
documents.original_title: 映画 えんとつ町のプペル
documents.overview: The story is about a young boy named Lubicchi and a trashman named Poupelle who meet on a Halloween night in a city that is full of tall chimneys. The chimneys pour out black smoke and the true sky cannot be seen.
documents.plot:
Poupelle of Chimney Town is a visually stunning and imaginative film that explores the themes of loneliness, community, and the power of human connection in a world where technology has created a sense of isolation. The story follows Poupelle, a young girl who lives in a world where humans have abandoned their homes to live in towering chimneys, and her journey to find a new home and belonging.

At its core, the film is a poignant exploration of loneliness and the human need for connection. Poupelle's journey is not just about finding a physical place to call home, but also about finding a sense of belonging and acceptance. The film highlights the consequences of a society that values efficiency and convenience over human relationships and community.

The movie also touches on the theme of technology and its impact on our lives. In this world, humans have created a complex system of chimneys and pipes to sustain themselves, but in doing so, they have lost touch with their emotions and connections with each other. Poupelle's journey serves as a reminder that even in a world dominated by technology, there is still room for human connection and empathy.

The film's use of animation and visuals adds another layer of depth to the story, creating a sense of wonder and magic that underscores the importance of community and human connection. Overall, Poupelle of Chimney Town is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that explores the complexities of human relationships in a world where technology has changed the way we live and interact with each other.

documents.title: A Perfect Enemy
documents.overview: Successful architect Jeremy Angust is approached on his trip to the Tokyo International Airport by a chatty girl called Texel Textor. She is a strange young woman who seems to be looking for captive victims whom she forces to listen to her strange stories. Jeremy loses the flight because of Texel and once they are installed in the lounge area, he will not be able to get rid of the annoying stranger. Although the meeting seems fortuitous, soon there be a turn that will transform the character of that encounter into something much more sinister and criminal.
documents.plot: Famed architect Jeremy Angust is approached on his trip to the Paris Airport by a chatty girl named Texel Textor who needs a ride. He obliges and after they part ways at the airport entrance, he misses his flight. As he settles in the lounge, he encounters the mysterious young Texel again, who insists on telling her strange story — and the conversation grows stranger and more twisted until it turns sinister and deadly.

documents.title: Alien Xmas
documents.overview: A young elf mistakes a tiny alien for a Christmas gift, not knowing her new plaything has plans to destroy Earth's gravity — and steal all the presents.
documents.plot: A young elf mistakes a tiny alien for a Christmas gift, not knowing her new plaything has plans to destroy Earth's gravity — and steal all the presents.

documents.title: Jackass Forever
documents.tagline: Some people never learn.
documents.overview: Celebrate the joy of a perfectly executed shot to the groin as Johnny Knoxville, Steve-O and the rest of the gang return alongside some newcomers for one final round of hilarious, wildly absurd and often dangerous displays of stunts and comedy.
documents.plot:
Jackass Forever is a 2022 American comedy film directed by Jeff Tremaine and written by John Francis Daley, Jonathan Goldstein, Brendan Hay, and Dan Sterling. The film is the fifth installment in the Jackass franchise.

The movie begins with Johnny Knoxville (played by Johnny Knoxville), Steve-O (Steve-O), Dave England (Dave England), Jason "Wee Man" Acuña (Jason "Wee Man" Acuña), and Ehren McGhehey (Ehren McGhehey) reuniting for a new series of stunts, which they call the "Jackass Forever Tour." The film takes place several years after the events of Jackass Presents: Family Reunion – Part II.

Throughout the movie, the cast members embark on various adventures and perform outrageous stunts. One notable segment features Wee Man attempting to break multiple world records for most hamburgers eaten in one sitting while being attacked by a swarm of bees. Another scene showcases Steve-O's attempt to ride a bull while wearing a pair of oversized novelty sunglasses.

Meanwhile, Johnny Knoxville is struggling with the loss of his mother and finds solace in performing stunts as a way to cope with his grief. The film also explores the cast members' personal lives, including Ehren McGhehey's struggles with addiction and Jason "Wee Man" Acuña's experiences with racism.

As the tour progresses, the Jackass crew faces various challenges, including a disastrous trip to Japan and a confrontation with a group of angry locals. The film also features several celebrity cameos, including Jeff Tremaine, who appears as himself, and Rob Riggle, who plays a fictionalized version of himself.

Throughout the movie, the cast members' signature blend of humor, camaraderie, and reckless abandon is on full display. The film's climax features an epic stunt involving all five main cast members, which culminates in a massive explosion and a shower of sparks.

Overall, Jackass Forever is a raunchy, irreverent comedy that celebrates the absurdity and unpredictability of life. With its trademark blend of humor, heart, and outrageous stunts, the film is sure to delight fans of the franchise and newcomers alike.

documents.title: The Social Dilemma
documents.tagline: The technology that connects us also controls us.
documents.overview: This documentary-drama hybrid explores the dangerous human impact of social networking, with tech experts sounding the alarm on their own creations.
documents.plot:
The Social Dilemma is a thought-provoking documentary that delves into the darker side of social media and its impact on society. At its core, the film explores the tension between individual freedom and collective responsibility in the digital age.

One of the primary themes of The Social Dilemma is the manipulation of users through algorithms designed to maximize engagement and profit. This raises questions about the ethics of data collection, surveillance capitalism, and the commodification of personal information. As the documentary reveals, these systems can create a culture of addiction, where individuals become trapped in an endless loop of scrolling, liking, and sharing, often at the expense of their mental health and well-being.

Another key theme is the role of social media in shaping our perceptions of reality and influencing our relationships with others. The film highlights how platforms like Facebook and Instagram can create curated personas that distort our understanding of ourselves and others, leading to feelings of isolation, loneliness, and disconnection.

The Social Dilemma also touches on the issue of echo chambers and the spread of misinformation. By showcasing the ways in which algorithms amplify extreme views and limit exposure to opposing perspectives, the documentary reveals how social media can become a breeding ground for polarization and conflict.

Ultimately, The Social Dilemma presents a stark warning about the dangers of unchecked technological advancement and the need for individuals, policymakers, and industry leaders to take responsibility for creating a healthier digital ecosystem. By examining the consequences of our addiction to social media, the film encourages us to rethink our relationship with technology and strive for a more balanced, empathetic, and informed online presence.

The documentary's central message is that we must be aware of the ways in which social media shapes our lives and take steps to mitigate its negative effects. By doing so, we can work towards creating a digital landscape that promotes meaningful connections, critical thinking, and collective well-being.

documents.title: Body Brokers
documents.tagline: Drugs. Rehab. Profit.
documents.overview: Utah and his girlfriend Opal, are drug addicts living on the streets in rural Ohio. After getting recruited by body broker Wood, and offered treatment in Los Angeles, Wood takes Utah under his wing and introduces him to treatment center mogul Vin. Wood and Vin bring Utah in on their lucrative and illegal dealings, where saving lives comes second to the bottom line.
documents.plot:
Body Brokers is a 2021 American crime drama written and directed by John Swab. It stars Jack Kilmer, Michael Kenneth Williams, Jessica Rothe, Alice Englert, Peter Greene, Frank Grillo and Melissa Leo. The film exposes the world of addiction treatment fraud, in which rehab centers exploit insurance billing and pay addicts to recruit other addicts.

The film opens with an advertisement for New West Recovery, a Los Angeles rehab center founded by former addict Vin. In voice-over, Vin explains that the Affordable Care Act turned addiction treatment into a vast and profitable industry across Southern California. In Columbus, Ohio, homeless addicts Utah and Opal rob convenience stores to pay for drugs, and Opal also does sex work for truckers. While they are panhandling, they meet Wood, a recruiter for New West, who buys them a meal and offers them a chance to get clean. Opal assumes he is a preacher and refuses, but Utah flies with Wood to Los Angeles. A few weeks later, Utah is doing well, and he finally persuades Opal to enroll. He then learns that New West has paid him a fee for referring her.

Utah becomes one of Wood's recruiters, earning tens of thousands of dollars from referrals, unnecessary tests and pointless procedures billed to insurers, while Vin cheerfully explains the schemes. Utah struggles with his conscience. The fraud seems victimless until the corrupt Dr. Riner demands a bigger share of a lucrative surgical procedure and insults the two recruiters. Wood beats him to death and buries the body, and Vin tells them to lie low. Soon afterwards, Vin sends Utah to pick up a new recruit in a car at the Los Angeles airport. Utah lets the man shoot up one last time, gives in to temptation himself and dies of an overdose. The film suggests Vin arranged the meeting to get rid of a witness to Riner's murder. An epilogue presents statistics on addiction and overdose deaths, says many similar businesses still operate, and recommends free twelve-step programs as the most effective treatment.

Principal photography took place in Oklahoma in August 2019. Vertical Entertainment acquired the film in December 2020 and released it in limited theaters in the United States on February 19, 2021. Reviews were mixed to positive. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said the film attempts an ambitious balance of genre thrills and a serious social message but fumbles too often to fully succeed. Metacritic reported generally favorable reviews.

documents.title: A Christmas Carol
documents.tagline: A Holiday classic reimagined.
documents.overview: London, 1843. Ebenezer Scrooge, a bitter old man, despises the Christmas holiday. Over the course of Christmas Eve night he is visited by three ghosts to show him his past, present and future.
documents.plot:
A Christmas Carol is a 2019 British dark fantasy drama based on Charles Dickens's 1843 novella. Written by Steven Knight, with Tom Hardy and Ridley Scott among its executive producers, it was made as a three-part series and aired in the United States on FX on 19 December 2019 as a single presentation, before being broadcast on BBC One between 22 and 24 December 2019. Guy Pearce stars as Ebenezer Scrooge, with Andy Serkis as the Ghost of Christmas Past, Stephen Graham as Jacob Marley and Charlotte Riley as Lottie Scrooge, and Joe Alwyn, Vinette Robinson and Billy Barratt in supporting roles.

The adaptation reimagines the familiar story with a darker, more adult tone. It opens with Jacob Marley awakening in his grave after a boy urinates on his headstone. Meanwhile, his former business partner Scrooge, a ruthless asset stripper with extensive industrial interests, sits in his office despising Christmas and the hypocrisy he believes it represents, telling his nephew Fred that people who claim to be good during the festive season should behave that way all year. His clerk Bob Cratchit and Bob's wife Mary struggle to support their family, including their disabled son Tim.

In a purgatorial realm, Marley is bound in chains and lockboxes and told by the Ghost of Christmas Past that he will find no rest unless he helps Scrooge achieve redemption. Marley confronts Scrooge with the human cost of their business, including the workers exploited in their mills and the lives lost through their greed, and warns him that three spirits will visit him. The Ghost of Christmas Past takes a variety of guises to lead Scrooge through his memories, revealing the cruelty of his childhood at a boarding school and the traumas that shaped him. Subsequent visions expose the suffering of the Cratchit family and confront Scrooge with his treatment of Mary, while the spirits question whether he is capable of genuine change or merely seeking to escape punishment.

Knight's version expands the story's political themes, presenting Scrooge as a product of trauma and industrial capitalism, and it places stronger emphasis on the perspectives of the Cratchits and of Marley himself.

The adaptation received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes about 52 percent of critics gave it a positive review; reviewers praised Pearce's performance and the bleak atmosphere while some found its reworking of the familiar story overly grim and drawn out.

documents.title: Isi & Ossi
documents.overview: Isi and Ossi couldn't be any more different: She's a billionaire's daughter from Heidelberg, he's a struggling boxer from the nearby town of Mannheim. But when Isi meets Ossi, the two quickly realize that they can take advantage of one another: She dates the broke boxer to provoke her parents and get them to fund a long-desired chef training in New York. He tries to rip off the rich daughter to finance his first professional boxing match. Their plans soon develop into emotional chaos that challenges everything the two believe to know about money, career and love.
