documents.title: Earth and Blood
documents.overview: A sawmill owner and his teenage daughter become tangled in a deadly feud when a drug dealer stashes stolen cocaine on their remote property.
documents.plot:
Earth and Blood (French: La Terre et le Sang) is a 2020 French action thriller film directed by Julien Leclercq and starring Sami Bouajila, Eriq Ebouaney and Samy Seghir, with Sofia Lesaffre and Redouanne Harjane. It depicts a violent siege at an isolated sawmill after a young employee hides a gang's stolen cocaine there, forcing the mill's owner into a last stand to protect his teenage daughter.

A raid on a police evidence room leaves two of four robbers dead; the survivors escape with eight kilos of cocaine. Meanwhile, sawmill owner Saïd learns from a scan that he has cancer and not long to live, and he plans to sell the mill, which once belonged to his sister-in-law's father, to pay for the further education of his teenage daughter, Sarah, who has impaired hearing and speech. One of his employees, Yanis, a young parolee, meets his half-brother, one of the surviving robbers, who has decided not to hand the drugs over to the drug lord Adama and asks Yanis to hide them at the mill. Adama captures the two robbers and kills one of them. Growing suspicious, Saïd questions Yanis, finds the drugs in a truck, locks him inside the mill and drives off for help, but turns back on learning that the gang is coming.

Adama's brother Moussa arrives first and threatens Yanis and Sarah at gunpoint before Saïd shoots him. With Adama and his men closing in and the phone lines cut, Saïd arms Yanis with a shotgun and sends him into the woods with Sarah while he draws the gang into a series of traps, killing them one by one. Trapped when the gang sets the mill ablaze, he breaks out in a heavy log loader and crushes a pursuing car. In the woods, a henchman finds Yanis and Sarah hiding in a shed and stabs Yanis; Sarah runs to a farmhouse for help, and Saïd arrives too late to save Yanis. Adama wounds Saïd badly and goes after Sarah to avenge his brother, killing the old farmer who sheltered her. Sarah leaps from an upper floor but is caught, and as Adama tries to break her neck, Saïd arrives and kills him with an axe, collapsing in his daughter's arms as a police helicopter approaches.

Netflix released the film on April 17, 2020. Decider likened it to a French take on Rambo: Last Blood, praising Bouajila's and Lesaffre's acting but faulting the thin screenplay and stylized slow motion, while The Guardian's Peter Bradshaw found the characters sketched in too quickly and the film like a truncated version of a longer work.

documents.title: Summer of 85
documents.tagline: Whoever dies first, the other promises to dance on his grave.
documents.overview: What do you dream of when you're 16-years-old and in a seaside resort in Normandy in the 1980s? A best friend? A lifelong teen pact? Scooting off on adventures on a boat or a motorbike? Living life at breakneck speed? No. You dream of death. Because you can't get a bigger kick than dying. And that's why you save it till the very end. The summer holidays are just beginning, and this story recounts how Alexis grew into himself.
documents.plot:
Summer of '85 is a poignant coming-of-age drama that delves into the complexities of adolescent desire, identity, and the blurred lines between innocence and experience.

The film's narrative revolves around a young man's summer of self-discovery, as he navigates his first same-sex encounter with an older man. This pivotal moment serves as a catalyst for exploring themes of vulnerability, consent, and the struggle to reconcile one's desires with societal expectations.

Throughout the movie, the director masterfully weaves together elements of nostalgia, longing, and the fragility of youth, creating a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. The film's use of vibrant colors, evocative soundscapes, and poignant performances all contribute to an immersive cinematic experience that captures the essence of this pivotal moment in a young man's life.

Ultimately, Summer of '85 presents a nuanced exploration of the human experience, one that is both tender and unflinching. The movie invites viewers to reflect on their own experiences of identity, desire, and the complexities of growing up, making it a powerful and thought-provoking watch.

documents.title: The Owners
documents.tagline: Respect your elders... or else.
documents.overview: A group of friends think they found the perfect easy score - an empty house with a safe full of cash. But when the elderly couple that lives there comes home early, the tables are suddenly turned. As a deadly game of cat and mouse ensues, the would-be thieves must fight to save themselves from a nightmare they could never have imagined.
documents.plot:
The Owners is a 2020 horror thriller film directed by Julius Berg in his feature debut, which he co-wrote, adapted from the graphic novel Une nuit de pleine lune by Hermann Huppen and Yves H. Maisie Williams stars as Mary, with Sylvester McCoy and Rita Tushingham as the elderly Dr. Richard Huggins and his wife, Ellen, and Jake Curran, Ian Kenny and Andrew Ellis as three young criminals. An international co-production between the United States, the United Kingdom and France, set in rural England in the 1990s, it was released in the United States in September 2020 by RLJE Films.

Three young men, Gaz, Nathan and Terry, plan to break into the remote country home of Dr. Huggins and his wife, believing that it contains a safe full of cash. Nathan's girlfriend, Mary, reluctantly becomes involved when she arrives to collect her car to drive to work and is persuaded to come along. When the young men fail to open the safe, Mary enters the house, and she tells Nathan that she is pregnant. When the elderly couple return home, the intruders tie them up and threaten them to make them open the safe, but Richard recognizes Nathan and Terry from their childhood, and Nathan begins to lose his nerve.

Tension within the group explodes when Gaz, trying to take control, stabs Nathan and then threatens Ellen with a circular saw after Richard twice gives a false combination; Mary kills Gaz with a sledgehammer. Mary and Terry free the couple, and Richard offers to operate on the wounded Nathan while Ellen tends to Terry's injured foot. But the couple's behavior grows increasingly strange, and Mary begins to suspect that the seemingly harmless pensioners are far more dangerous than the criminals who invaded their home. As the night wears on, the tables turn completely, and Mary finds herself trapped in a house of horrors, fighting to survive and escape from the couple who have their own sinister plans for her.

The Owners received mixed reviews. Much of the attention focused on the casting of McCoy and Tushingham, veteran British actors best known for genial roles, as the sinister couple, and on Williams in one of her first film leads after Game of Thrones, while the film's escalating violence and twists divided reviewers.

documents.title: Made in Italy
documents.overview: A bohemian artist travels from London to Italy with his estranged son to sell the house they inherited from his late wife.
documents.plot:
Made in Italy is a 2020 comedy-drama film written and directed by James D'Arcy in his feature directorial debut. It stars Liam Neeson as Robert Foster, a once-famous artist, and Neeson's son Micheál Richardson as Robert's estranged son, Jack, who travel together to restore a dilapidated Tuscan villa years after the death of Jack's mother, with Valeria Bilello as Natalia and Lindsay Duncan as the estate agent Kate.

Jack, a gallery manager, is reeling because his wife, Ruth, wants a divorce and her family plans to sell the gallery he has run for years. Hoping to buy it, he decides to sell the Italian house he co-owns with Robert, which had belonged to his mother, an Italian woman killed in a car crash years earlier. In Italy they find the house derelict. Kate advises that some work would raise its value, and although Jack is ready to sell it as it is, Robert, overwhelmed by memories of his wife, decides to help renovate. They befriend locals, including Natalia, a divorced restaurant owner who shares custody of her young daughter. As Natalia and her daughter help paint, Robert explains that after his wife's death he sent Jack to boarding school to shield him from reminders of her, and that he has neither painted nor driven since.

Jack and Natalia grow close, and he confides how Ruth has taken everything from him and how Robert never supported his career. Finding Robert's workspace full of paintings of his mother and of himself as a child, Jack confronts his father for shutting him out and begins wrecking it until Robert holds him. They finally share memories of her, and Robert tearfully blames himself for her death, as he was too absorbed in painting on the day of the accident. When a couple who want to buy the house treat it with contempt, Robert refuses to sell, and Jack returns angrily to England. Robert follows, having sold his London home to buy Jack's share of the villa so that Jack can buy the gallery, and plans to host painting holidays in Italy. When Ruth refuses to sell after all, Jack hands her the signed divorce papers and returns to Italy, telling his father that he only ever wanted him. He reconciles with Natalia, and the film ends with father and son painting a wall together.

IFC Films acquired U.S. rights and released the film in theaters and on video on demand on 7 August 2020. Reviews were mixed, with 44% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44; critics praised the performances and setting but found the story slight.

documents.title: The Worst Person in the World
documents.tagline: One woman's quest for love and meaning in the modern world.
documents.overview: The chronicles of four years in the life of Julie, a young woman who navigates the troubled waters of her love life and struggles to find her career path, leading her to take a realistic look at who she really is.
documents.plot:
The Worst Person in the World is a 2021 Norwegian black comedy film directed by Joachim Trier, written by Espen Sandberg and Joachim Trier, and starring Andrea Riseborough, Anders Linnet Nordvang, and Jonas Holmlund.

The film follows Julie (Andrea Riseborough), a young woman who struggles to find direction in her life. The story is presented as a series of vignettes, each set at a different point in Julie's life, from her teenage years to adulthood.

In the first vignette, we see Julie as a teenager, feeling disconnected and uncertain about her future. She is portrayed as awkward and introverted, but also fiercely independent and determined to forge her own path.

As the film progresses, we follow Julie through various relationships and experiences, including a brief romance with a charismatic but troubled young man named Aman (Anders Linnet Nordvang). However, their relationship ultimately ends in heartbreak, leaving Julie feeling lost and uncertain about what she wants from life.

Throughout the film, Julie's character is portrayed as complex and multifaceted, struggling to reconcile her desire for independence with her need for human connection. Her relationships with others are often fraught with tension and uncertainty, but also marked by moments of tenderness and vulnerability.

One of the most striking aspects of The Worst Person in the World is its use of non-linear storytelling. Each vignette is presented as a self-contained unit, yet they are all linked together by Julie's ongoing journey of self-discovery. This structure allows the film to explore different themes and emotions, while also creating a sense of continuity and coherence.

As the film progresses, we see Julie navigate various careers and relationships, including a stint as a journalist and a brief romance with a man named Thomas (Jonas Holmlund). However, each of these experiences ultimately ends in disappointment or heartbreak, leaving Julie feeling lost and uncertain about her future.

Ultimately, The Worst Person in the World is a film about the complexities and challenges of growing up. It is a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of identity, relationships, and the search for meaning in life. Through its non-linear structure and complex characters, the film creates a sense of depth and complexity that rewards close attention and reflection.

Overall, The Worst Person in the World is a powerful and moving film that explores the complexities of human experience with wit, nuance, and sensitivity.

documents.title: Ted K
documents.tagline: In the woods no one can hear you think.
documents.overview: The True Story of Ted Kaczynski, the infamous Unabomber, who wants to destroy modern technology to create a world for himself in the Montana wilderness.
documents.plot:
Ted K is a 2021 American independent biographical crime drama directed, co-produced and co-edited by Tony Stone, who co-wrote the screenplay with Gaddy Davis and John Rosenthal. Sharlto Copley stars as Ted Kaczynski, the former mathematics professor who withdrew to a survivalist life in the Montana wilderness and became the domestic terrorist known as the Unabomber, waging a nationwide mail-bombing campaign against modern technology and the destruction of nature.

Since 1971, Kaczynski has lived alone in a primitive cabin near Lincoln, Montana without electricity or running water. Convinced that technology is ruining the planet, he watches development encroach on the woods around him and decides that a life in nature is no longer possible. His resentment turns into sabotage: he wrecks a neighbour's snowmobile, cuts a power line and destroys construction equipment. The constant roar of jets overhead becomes his breaking point, and he resolves to take revenge on the people he holds responsible for harming society. After looking up the address of United Airlines president Percy Wood at the local library, he begins sending bombs through the mail. The FBI takes up the case when a device seriously injures Wood at his home, and Kaczynski alters his appearance to avoid recognition. A computer-store owner, Hugh Scrutton, becomes the first person killed by one of his bombs.

Short of money and quarrelling with his brother David over the phone, Kaczynski writes a 35,000-word manifesto and taunts newspapers with letters written in the first-person plural, while the press dubs him the "Unabomber". He promises The New York Times and The Washington Post that he will stop killing if they publish his manifesto, and the Post prints it on September 19, 1995. David recognises his brother's writing style and goes to the authorities. Kaczynski is arrested in 1996 and sentenced to life in the federal supermax prison in Florence, Colorado, for murdering three people and injuring twenty-three more; an epilogue notes that the hunt for him was the largest manhunt in FBI history.

Copley joined the project in 2018, and the film was shot over four seasons in and around Lincoln. It premiered at the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in March 2021 and was released in the United States in February 2022 by Neon's Super Ltd. Critics were largely positive, giving it 85% on Rotten Tomatoes and 70 on Metacritic, with particular praise for Copley's intense performance.

documents.title: Faster Than Light: the Dream of Interstellar Flight
documents.original_title: Faster Than Light: the Dream of Interstellar Flight
documents.overview: “Faster Than Light” explores the longstanding quest to develop spacecraft with enough power and speed to reach the stars. The film asks: What will it take to reach a newly discovered planet circling our Sun’s nearest neighbor, Proxima Centauri? Based on real science and engineering, “Faster Than Light” takes audiences on a thrilling journey into the future, aboard laser-driven space sails, antimatter engines, and even warp drive – right out of science fiction. “Who can say how far, and how fast, our technology will one day take us?” said director Thomas Lucas.
