documents.title: Multiverse
documents.tagline: Some doors should never be opened.
documents.overview: Four brilliant university students are forced to confront themselves in terrifying ways when their Quantum Physics experiment leads to an entangled parallel existence that leaves them questioning who they are and what is real.
documents.plot:
Multiverse (released in German-speaking countries as Multiverse – Parallele Dimensionen) is a Canadian science fiction thriller film directed by Gaurav Seth from a screenplay by Doug Taylor, based on a story by Michael MacKenzie. It stars Paloma Kwiatkowski, Munro Chambers, Robert Naylor and Sandra Mae Frank as four physics students, with Marlee Matlin in a supporting role. Filmed in Ontario between 6 and 30 August 2018, it was completed in 2019 and Saban Films released it in 2021.

Loretta (Kwiatkowski), Gerry (Chambers), Danny (Naylor) and Amy (Frank) are brilliant university students attempting to prove the existence of parallel universes through a quantum physics experiment. Inspired by an aquarium in their lab, Loretta decides they need far more water and drives the group to a lake. On a winding road they come upon an accident in which another car hangs over the edge of a cliff. Loretta runs to it, apparently shocked by something, and a person inside reaches out to take her hand before Loretta plunges over the cliff with the car. Her boyfriend Danny finds comfort with Amy. Five months later, Loretta is spotted in the university library and then in a bar, and then confronts Danny and Amy, believing she is still Danny's girlfriend. When the friends explain that she vanished for five months and that they saw her die, they realise that Loretta's theory was right, a conclusion confirmed by the word "Entangled" tattooed on her forearm. It soon emerges that the other three also have tattooed doppelgängers from another reality. Amy's mother Dierdre (Matlin) immediately senses something is wrong with her daughter, and Gerry descends into madness and kills his original self so that his double can take his place. Realising that the doubles' presence is affecting their bodies the students decide to get rid of them. Returning from dumping a body in a bog along the same road, they find themselves inside the car on the cliff edge in the very accident of five months earlier, as another Loretta runs to help. The film closes as it began, with the students at the aquarium concluding that they need more water.

Multiverse received mostly negative to mixed reviews. The Lexikon des internationalen Films found its premise interesting but its plot unengaging and its emotions superficial. It was nominated for Best Canadian Feature at Whistler and for Best Film at Fantasporto 2020, and Frank and Chambers received acting nominations in Berlin.

documents.title: The Innocents
documents.overview: Four children become friends during the summer holidays, and out of sight of the adults they discover they have hidden powers. While exploring their newfound abilities in the nearby forests and playgrounds, their innocent play takes a dark turn and strange things begin to happen.
documents.plot:
The Innocents (Norwegian: De uskyldige) is a 2021 Norwegian supernatural horror thriller written and directed by Eskil Vogt, known as a frequent co-writer for Joachim Trier. Rakel Lenora Fløttum, Alva Brynsmo Ramstad, Sam Ashraf and Mina Yasmin Bremseth Asheim play the four children at the center of the story, with Ellen Dorrit Petersen as the girls' mother. The film premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 74th Cannes Film Festival on 11 July 2021.

During a summer holiday, nine-year-old Ida and her older sister Anna, who has nonverbal autism, move with their parents into a large apartment complex surrounded by woods. With most residents away, Ida befriends Ben, a boy from a neighboring building who reveals that he can move objects with his mind. Their friendship takes a disturbing turn when Ben kills a stray cat by dropping it down a stairwell and crushing its skull. Ida also meets Aisha, a girl with telepathic abilities, and it soon emerges that Anna has powers too; with Aisha's help she begins to speak again, to her parents' delight. The children's abilities grow strongest when Anna, Aisha and Ben are together, leaving Ida as the only one without powers.

The children spend their days practicing and strengthening their gifts, but the group fractures when Ben, angered by an insulting telepathic message, hurts Anna. At home, Ben attacks his abusive mother and kills her. Increasingly erratic and violent, he begins using mind control, forcing a neighbor to murder a bully who had harassed him and Ida. When he reveals this ability to Ida, she does not believe him until he makes her climb onto a refrigerator. Aisha confronts Ben about the violence, and as the adults remain oblivious to what is happening around them, the girls realize that they must stop him themselves, leading to a silent, deadly confrontation between the children.

The Innocents received widespread critical acclaim. Reviewers praised Vogt's restrained direction, the remarkable performances of the young cast and the film's unsettling exploration of childhood cruelty and morality, and many noted how it subverted the superhero genre by grounding supernatural powers in the everyday world of children. It went on to screen at numerous international festivals.

documents.title: American Pie Presents: Girls' Rules
documents.overview: It's Senior year at East Great Falls. Annie, Kayla, Michelle, and Stephanie decide to harness their girl power and band together to get what they want their last year of high school.
documents.plot:
American Pie Presents: Girls' Rules is a 2020 American sex comedy film directed by Mike Elliott. The ninth installment overall in the American Pie franchise and the fifth in its American Pie Presents spin-off series, it is a standalone sequel centered on Stephanie, a relative of Steve Stifler, played by Lizze Broadway, and her friends. The cast also includes Madison Pettis, Piper Curda, Natasha Behnam and Darren Barnet. It is the first film in the franchise without Eugene Levy and the first to contain no nudity. The project grew out of a script for a male-centered film called American Pie Presents: East Great Falls, which writer David H. Steinberg had been hired to write in 2010; in 2017 Universal brought in new writers who flipped the genders of all the characters.

At the start of their senior year, four friends, Annie, Kayla, Michelle and Stephanie, make a pact to help one another get what they want before graduation. Annie hopes to lose her virginity to her college boyfriend, Jason; Stephanie, a confident lacrosse player, is blackmailing the school's lecherous principal into retiring; Kayla is obsessed with the idea that her boyfriend Tim is cheating on her; and Michelle prides herself on her expertise in sex toys. Their plans are thrown into disarray by the arrival of Grant, a handsome new student whose mother Ellen moves in next door to Annie and her single father. Michelle and Stephanie both set out to win Grant's affection, with Stephanie paying her estranged old friend Emmett to help, while Grant offers to help Kayla make Tim jealous after their breakup and studies with Annie in the library, where the two slowly fall for each other. When the girls discover at a party that they all have feelings for the same boy, the pact begins to strain, though new romances emerge, including Stephanie's with Emmett and Michelle's with the nerdy assistant Oliver, who shares her admiration for John F. Kennedy. After Annie catches Jason cheating, she realizes her heart lies with Grant, only for a misunderstanding about the pact to threaten everything ahead of the pajama prom.

Released on demand and on DVD by Universal Pictures on October 6, 2020, followed by a Blu-ray release in September 2021, the film received generally negative reviews and holds a 33% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on nine critics.

documents.title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery
documents.original_title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery
documents.tagline: When the game ends, the mystery begins.
documents.overview: World-famous detective Benoit Blanc heads to Greece to peel back the layers of a mystery surrounding a tech billionaire and his eclectic crew of friends.
documents.plot:
Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is a 2022 American mystery film written and directed by Rian Johnson and produced by Johnson and Ram Bergman. A standalone sequel to Knives Out (2019), it stars Daniel Craig as the detective Benoit Blanc, who takes on a new case involving the tech billionaire Miles Bron and his circle of friends. Edward Norton plays Bron, and the ensemble cast includes Janelle Monáe, Kathryn Hahn, Leslie Odom Jr., Jessica Henwick, Madelyn Cline, Kate Hudson and Dave Bautista. Netflix acquired the rights to two Knives Out sequels in 2021 for a reported $469 million.

In May 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, Miles Bron, co-founder of the technology company Alpha, invites his old friends, who call themselves the "Disruptors," to a murder mystery weekend at his estate on a private Greek island, sending each an elaborate puzzle box. The guests are Alpha's head scientist Lionel Toussaint; Connecticut governor Claire Debella; the tactless model turned fashion designer Birdie Jay; the men's rights streamer Duke Cody; and Cassandra "Andi" Brand, Alpha's ousted co-founder, who is estranged from the others after a bitter lawsuit. They are joined by Birdie's assistant Peg, Duke's girlfriend Whiskey and, unexpectedly, Benoit Blanc, who says he received an invitation that Miles insists he never sent.

At the island's centerpiece, a giant glass dome called the Glass Onion, Miles shows off his art collection, including the Mona Lisa on loan from the Louvre, and reveals that the estate runs on Klear, a new hydrogen-based fuel he plans to launch despite warnings from Lionel and Claire that it is dangerous. Blanc quickly realizes that every guest owes Miles something and that each has a motive to harm him, and that Andi, in particular, believes her friends lied under oath to help Miles take control of the company. When the weekend's playful murder game is interrupted by a real death, Blanc must untangle a web of secrets in which nothing is quite what it seems, and the film revisits earlier events from a new perspective.

Glass Onion premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2022, played in cinemas for a limited one-week run in November and was released on Netflix in December. It received widespread acclaim for its screenplay, humor and performances, especially Monáe's, and earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Adapted Screenplay.

documents.title: Alone
documents.tagline: First the pandemic. Then the chaos.
documents.overview: When an outbreak hits, Aidan barricades himself inside his apartment and starts rationing food. His complex is overrun by infected Screamers, and with the world falling apart into chaos, he is left completely alone fighting for his life.
documents.plot:
Alone, released in the United Kingdom as Final Days, is a 2020 American horror film directed by Johnny Martin and an American remake of the 2020 South Korean film #Alive. Tyler Posey stars as Aidan, a young man who barricades himself inside his apartment during a zombie-like outbreak, with Donald Sutherland as Edward, Summer Spiro as Eva, Robert Ri'chard as Aidan's neighbour Brandon and John Posey as Aidan's father.

One morning Aidan wakes after a one-night stand to find a violent outbreak spreading outside, as people are attacked by infected people known as Screamers. His neighbour Brandon takes refuge in his apartment, but Aidan notices a wound on his neck and forces him out before he finishes turning. News reports explain that the infection spreads through bites and scratches, causing bleeding eyes, rage and cannibalism. Unable to call his family, Aidan receives text messages from his father saying that his sister has escaped and telling him to stay alive and stay home until his parents arrive. He shuts himself in, marking the days on his bathroom mirror, but his food runs low, the water is cut off and he begins hallucinating about his parents. He fights off a Screamer that breaks in through the air ducts and seals the vent. When a voicemail from his mother reveals that his parents have died, he prepares to hang himself, but stops when he sees a living woman, Eva, on a balcony across from his. Communicating with handwritten cards and later radios, they become friends, and Aidan shares water and supplies with her. Searching the ducts for more food, he enters a well-stocked, barricaded apartment and is knocked out by Edward, an elderly survivor, who ties him up as an offering to his infected wife. A radio call from Eva distracts Edward, and Aidan escapes, feeding Edward to his wife. He then climbs down from his balcony on knotted bedsheets, fights through Screamers to reach Eva and brings her back to his apartment. Fearing that a bloody mark on his shirt means he has been bitten, Aidan considers jumping to his death, but finds no wound. Holding the refrigerator against the door to keep the Screamers out, the two promise to survive together.

The film was released on video on demand on October 16, 2020, followed by DVD and Blu-ray days later. Reviews were largely negative, with critics criticizing its thin plot and abrupt ending; it holds a 27% Rotten Tomatoes rating from a small sample of reviews.

documents.title: Sweet & Sour
documents.tagline: Did you think it would stay sweet forever? Then why is it so sour?
documents.overview: Faced with real-world opportunities and challenges, a couple endures the highs and lows of trying to make a long-distance relationship survive.
documents.plot:
Sweet & Sour (Korean: Saekomdalkom) is a 2021 South Korean romantic comedy directed by Lee Gye-byeok and based on Kurumi Inui's novel Initiation Love. Jang Ki-yong, Chae Soo-bin and Krystal Jung star in a story about a couple drifting apart under the pressure of work, with Lee Woo-je and Park Chul-min in supporting roles. Originally planned for cinemas in 2020 but delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, it was released on Netflix on June 4, 2021.

In hospital with hepatitis B, an overweight young man named Hyuk is avoided by other patients and even his parents, but the nurse Da-eun cares for him without hesitation, and the two grow close. After his discharge he tracks down her number, spends a night at her home, fixes her broken hallway light and makes her breakfast, and they begin dating. She invites him on a Christmas trip to Jeju Island and gives him a pair of matching trainers, and he sets out to lose weight.

The film then follows a slimmed-down Hyuk, an engineer living with Da-eun in Incheon, who is sent on contract to a big firm in Seoul with the hope of a permanent post. He finds himself competing with the ambitious Bo-yeong, who undermines him at every turn. When he exposes a fatal flaw in her bridge design, she is ordered to fix it with him, and as they work late nights together they grow close. At home, exhausted by the long commute, Hyuk neglects Da-eun, leaves the broken light unrepaired and quarrels with her; she becomes pregnant and has an abortion, and he grows increasingly cold.

During a fight, Hyuk accidentally calls Da-eun by Bo-yeong's name, and he soon begins an affair with his colleague. When neither of them is offered a permanent job, Bo-yeong announces she will study abroad, and Hyuk, reminded of the planned Jeju trip, rushes to the airport to win back Da-eun. There he collides with a stranger: the Hyuk of the opening scenes.

The twist reveals that the two men are different people and that both storylines were unfolding at the same time. Feeling neglected by her partner Jang-hyuk, Da-eun had fallen for the kind patient Lee Jang-hyuk, who did everything her boyfriend did not, and the new couple leave together for Jeju. The stunned Jang-hyuk returns to the office party, where Bo-yeong, who has just won a Christmas trip, rejects his declaration of love.

Korean critics praised the actors' charm and its portrait of romance in an exhausted, overworked society.

documents.title: Godmothered
documents.tagline: Be careful who you wish for.
documents.overview: A young and unskilled fairy godmother that ventures out on her own to prove her worth by tracking down a young girl whose request for help was ignored. What she discovers is that the girl has now become a grown woman in need of something very different than a "prince charming."
documents.plot:
Godmothered is a 2020 American fantasy comedy film produced by Walt Disney Pictures. The movie follows the story of a young witch named Meredith, played by Jillian Bell, who is struggling to find her place in the world.

The story begins with Meredith, a talented but awkward young witch, who has been searching for her godmother for years. According to tradition, every young witch needs a godmother to guide and mentor them on their magical journey. However, Meredith's search has been unsuccessful, and she is starting to lose hope.

One day, while out on a job as a maid, Meredith meets a kind-hearted but slightly eccentric woman named Godmother Agnes, played by Isla Fisher. Agnes is a retired witch who has lost her own goddaughter and is now searching for a new one to take her place. Despite their initial differences, the two women form an unlikely bond, and Agnes agrees to become Meredith's godmother.

As Meredith begins to learn from Agnes, she discovers that being a witch is not just about casting spells and wearing fancy hats, but also about understanding the importance of family, friendship, and community. Through her adventures with Agnes, Meredith learns valuable lessons about embracing her uniqueness and finding her own path in life.

However, their relationship is put to the test when a rival godmother, Godmother Barbara, played by Rachel Bloom, appears on the scene. Barbara is a ruthless and cunning witch who will stop at nothing to become the most powerful godmother in the land. She sees Agnes as a threat to her own power and sets out to sabotage their relationship.

As Meredith and Agnes work together to thwart Barbara's plans, they discover that being a good godmother is not just about magic and spells, but also about love, kindness, and selflessness. In the end, Meredith learns that she has found not only a godmother but also a true friend in Agnes, and that their bond will last a lifetime.

The movie ends with Meredith and Agnes standing together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way. Meredith has finally found her place in the world, and Agnes has found a new purpose in life. The film is a heartwarming and hilarious exploration of what it means to be a good friend, family member, and godmother.

Overall, Godmothered is a delightful and entertaining movie that celebrates the power of female friendship and the importance of embracing one's uniqueness. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and magical storyline, this film is sure to delight audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet
documents.original_title: 名探偵コナン 緋色の弾丸
documents.overview: At the opening ceremony of the WSG (World Sports Games) Tokyo Games, a sports festival held once every four years, it is announced that the world's first vacuum superconducting maglev with a maximum speed of 1,000 kilometers per hour will open. While attracting attention from around the world, top executives of large companies are kidnapped from the party venue where WSG tournament sponsors gather. Conan moves toward a solution and eventually finds a connection with the WSG abduction case that occurred 15 years ago in Boston, USA.
documents.plot:
Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet is a 2021 Japanese mystery film directed by Kiyosumi Kojima and produced by Toho. 

The movie revolves around the story of a mysterious woman named Eri Kisaragi, who possesses supernatural abilities that allow her to see into the future. She becomes entangled in a complex web of events involving a series of murders and conspiracies.

At its core, Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet explores themes of identity, trauma, and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. Eri's character, in particular, is a fascinating study of how past traumas can shape one's perception of themselves and the world around them.

Throughout the film, the main characters grapple with their own dark pasts and the consequences of their actions, leading to a thrilling cat-and-mouse game that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. The movie also touches on the theme of obsession, as Eri becomes increasingly fixated on uncovering the truth behind a series of murders.

The film's use of mystery and suspense creates an atmosphere of tension and unease, mirroring the characters' inner turmoil and emotional struggles. Ultimately, Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet is a gripping whodunit that keeps viewers guessing until the very end, while also exploring deeper themes about identity, trauma, and the human condition.

The movie's portrayal of Eri's character, in particular, raises questions about the nature of reality and how our perceptions can be influenced by our experiences. Her abilities serve as a metaphor for the ways in which our past traumas can shape us, making it difficult to distinguish between what is real and what is imagined.

Overall, Detective Conan: The Scarlet Bullet is a thought-provoking mystery that delves into complex themes of identity, trauma, and reality, keeping viewers engaged until the very end.

documents.title: Pokémon the Movie: Secrets of the Jungle
documents.original_title: 劇場版ポケットモンスター ココ
documents.tagline: A bond like no other...
documents.overview: In the Forest of Okoya, Koko is a feral child who has been raised as a Pokémon by the Mythical Pokémon Zarude. Koko has grown up never doubting that he is a Pokémon even though he can't really use any sort of moves. Ash Ketchum and Pikachu meet Koko and help him protect the Great Tree from the crooked scientist Dr. Zed.
documents.plot:
Pokémon the Movie: Secrets of the Jungle is a 2020 Japanese animated film based on Satoshi Tajiri's Pokémon franchise and produced by OLM. The twenty-third film of the Pokémon anime series and the third in its alternate timeline, it is a sequel to Pokémon the Movie: The Power of Us and returns to the series' traditional 2D animation after the computer-animated Mewtwo Strikes Back: Evolution. It was the last Pokémon film produced by OLM and features the Mythical Pokémon Zarude and a shiny Celebi.

In the Forest of Okoya, the Mythical Pokémon Zarude discovers a human baby in a cradle washed up on a riverbank. Unable to abandon the child, Zarude adopts him and names him Koko, leaving his tribe, which lives around a sacred Great Tree deep in the jungle where humans are forbidden, in order to raise him. Koko grows up in the wild, believing himself to be a Pokémon.

Ten years later, Ash Ketchum and Pikachu visit the forest and encounter a research team from the Biotope Company, led by Dr. Zed, which Team Rocket secretly infiltrates. When Ash rescues Koko from a waterfall, the boy encounters other humans for the first time and is terrified, but Ash and Pikachu befriend him and help him learn about the human world. Zarude is forced to reveal the truth about Koko's origins, and Koko learns that his parents were scientists who worked for the Biotope Company researching the jungle's healing springs before dying in an accident. When Zed tracks Koko to the Great Tree and attacks it in order to exploit its healing waters, Koko, Ash, Pikachu and Zarude must join forces with the jungle's Pokémon to protect their home.

The film explores the bond between parent and child and the relationship between humans, Pokémon and nature.

Originally scheduled for July 2020, the film was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic and released in Japan by Toho on December 25, 2020. It grossed about 2.02 billion yen in Japan and roughly 23.6 million dollars worldwide, including later releases in China and South Korea. It was released internationally on Netflix on October 8, 2021.

documents.title: Flag Day
documents.tagline: Loving his daughter was the only honest work he ever did.
documents.overview: A father lives a double life as a counterfeiter, bank robber and con man in order to provide for his daughter.
documents.plot:
Flag Day is a 2021 American drama film that explores the complexities of identity, family dynamics, and the struggles of growing up in America. The movie delves into the life of Gary Lindbergh, a young man who becomes embroiled in a kidnapping plot involving his own father, Richard Lindbergh.

At its core, Flag Day is a story about the fragility of American ideals and the darker aspects of human nature. It examines how the country's founding principles can be twisted and distorted by personal ambition, greed, and the pursuit of power. The film also touches on themes of identity, as Gary struggles to come to terms with his own sense of self and find his place in the world.

The movie is also a nuanced portrayal of family dynamics, particularly the complicated relationships within the Lindbergh family. It highlights the tension between the idealized image of America's founding fathers and the harsh realities of their personal lives. Through Gary's story, Flag Day sheds light on the darker aspects of American history, revealing the complexities and contradictions that underlie the country's mythology.

Ultimately, Flag Day is a thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be an American, and how the ideals of freedom and democracy can be both celebrated and compromised.

documents.title: Jungle Beat: The Movie
documents.tagline: Home is where the hugs are.
documents.overview: The Jungle Beat animals think it’s the best thing ever when an alien arrives in the jungle bringing with him the power of speech. They also surprisingly think it’s the best thing ever when they find out that he’s been sent to conquer them.
documents.plot: The Jungle Beat animals think it’s the best thing ever when an alien arrives in the jungle bringing with him the power of speech. They also surprisingly think it’s the best thing ever when they find out that he’s been sent to conquer them.

documents.title: New Gods: Nezha Reborn
documents.tagline: Rebirth of a hero
documents.overview: While living as an ordinary deliveryman and motor racing fan, Nezha encounters old nemeses and must rediscover his powers to protect his loved ones.
documents.plot:
New Gods: Nezha Reborn (Chinese: 新神榜：哪吒重生) is a 2021 Chinese 3D animated fantasy action film directed by Zhao Ji and written by Mu Chuan, produced by Light Chaser Animation. It reimagines Nezha, the young deity from the Ming dynasty novel Investiture of the Gods, in a steampunk and cyberpunk setting, with the hero reincarnated thousands of years after the events of the classic story. Yang Tianxiang voices the lead role. The film was released in mainland China on 12 February 2021, during the Chinese New Year holiday, and Netflix later acquired the global rights outside China. A follow-up, New Gods: Yang Jian, was released in 2022.

The story takes place in Donghai, a sprawling industrial city loosely modeled on 1920s Shanghai, where the poor suffer from a severe water shortage while a powerful syndicate controls the supply. Li Yunxiang is a delivery man and underground motorcycle racer who works as a smuggler against his father's wishes and secretly helps his neighbors by sabotaging the water plants. One night Ao Bing, the arrogant son of the syndicate's chief Ao Guang, chases Yunxiang to take his prized motorbike. In the confrontation, Yunxiang's rage releases a strange burning power that injures Ao Bing.

Ao Guang soon realizes what this power means and sends assassins after Yunxiang, who fights them off with abilities he does not understand. He is rescued by a mysterious masked figure who tells him that he is the reincarnation of Nezha, and that the Dragon King's clan still bears a grudge against him from three thousand years earlier. Ao Guang and his family turn out to be descendants of the dragons Nezha once fought. Reluctant at first to accept his destiny, Yunxiang must learn to control the divine power within him, unlock Nezha's true form and protect his family and the people of Donghai, as the conflict between the dragon clan and the reborn deity escalates.

The film earned positive reviews for its striking visual style and action sequences. Lim Yian Yu called it an interesting take on the classic novel and a family-friendly film for children and adults alike, while Sun Jiayin praised the decision to set the story long after the original legend, which set it apart from the many other adaptations of Investiture of the Gods.

documents.title: Terrifier 2
documents.tagline: Who's laughing now?
documents.overview: After being resurrected by a sinister entity, Art the Clown returns to Miles County where he must hunt down and destroy a teenage girl and her younger brother on Halloween night.  As the body count rises, the siblings fight to stay alive while uncovering the true nature of Art's evil intent.
documents.plot:
Terrifier 2 is a 2022 American horror film directed by Damien Leone, written by Damien Leone and Tony Timpone, and produced by Damien Leone and Tony Timpone. The film stars David Howard Thornton as Art the Clown, a serial killer with a twisted sense of humor.

The movie takes place two years after the events of the first Terrifier. Art is still on the loose, terrorizing the small town of Crystal Lake. However, this time around, he's not alone. A new character, Pin-Up Girl (played by Lauren LaVera), has joined him in his twisted games.

Pin-Up Girl is a seductive and manipulative killer who uses her charm to lure victims into Art's trap. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Pin-Up Girl has a personal connection to Art, which adds a layer of complexity to their relationship.

The film follows a new group of characters as they try to survive Art's wrath. The main protagonist, Jenny (played by Samantha Sloyan), is a young woman who finds herself at the center of Art's attention. As the body count rises, Jenny must use her wits and resourcefulness to outsmart Art and Pin-Up Girl.

Throughout the film, Leone pays homage to classic horror movies, particularly those from the 1980s and 1990s. The film's aesthetic is reminiscent of a bygone era, with its bright colors, synth-heavy soundtrack, and over-the-top gore.

One of the standout aspects of Terrifier 2 is its ability to balance humor and horror. Art's deadpan delivery and Pin-Up Girl's sassy attitude provide some much-needed levity in an otherwise gruesome film. However, make no mistake – this is a horror movie at its core, and it doesn't shy away from graphic violence or disturbing imagery.

Overall, Terrifier 2 is a fun, if not entirely original, take on the horror genre. Leone's direction is confident and assured, and he shows a clear passion for the material. While some may find the film's tone uneven, fans of horror will likely appreciate its unapologetic excesses.

documents.title: Censor
documents.tagline: You can't edit reality.
documents.overview: Film censor Enid takes pride in her meticulous work, guarding unsuspecting audiences from the deleterious effects of watching the gore-filled movies she pores over. Her sense of duty to protect is amplified by guilt over her inability to recall details of the long-ago disappearance of her sister. When Enid is assigned to review a disturbing film from the archive that echoes her hazy childhood memories, she begins to unravel how this eerie work might be tied to her past.
documents.plot:
Censor is a 2021 British psychological horror film directed by Prano Bailey-Bond in her feature debut, from a screenplay she co-wrote with Anthony Fletcher. Niamh Algar stars as a film censor, with Nicholas Burns, Vincent Franklin, Sophia La Porta, Michael Smiley and Adrian Schiller, in his final film appearance, in supporting roles. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2021 and later won the Méliès d'Or for Best European Fantastic Film.

The film is set in 1985, during the moral panic over so-called video nasties in Britain. Enid Baines works at the British Board of Film Classification, where her colleagues call her "Little Miss Perfect" because of her strict insistence that violent scenes be cut or banned to protect the public. Her private life is shaped by an unresolved trauma: as a child, her younger sister Nina disappeared while the two were playing in the woods, and although her parents have finally had Nina declared legally dead, Enid remains convinced that she is still alive.

When a man murders his family, a tabloid newspaper links the crime to a film Enid recently passed for release and names her as the censor responsible, which leads to a stream of abusive phone calls. Soon afterwards, the producer Doug Smart invites her to review an old film by the horror director Frederick North. Watching it, Enid is shaken to see events that seem to echo her fragmented memories of Nina's disappearance, and she becomes fixated on a lead actress who she believes could be her lost sister. As she seeks out North's other work and attempts to track down the actress, the boundary between Enid's reality and the lurid films she watches for a living begins to collapse, leading to a hallucinatory and violent climax.

Bailey-Bond uses the visual textures of 1980s horror, including grainy VHS imagery and saturated colour, to explore whether screen violence really corrupts viewers, while examining memory, guilt and repression through Enid's psychological unravelling. Algar's performance was widely singled out for praise.

Censor was well received by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 89 percent, with the consensus describing it as occasionally uneven but bold and viscerally effective, and as a bloody good step forward for British horror.

documents.title: Riders of Justice
documents.tagline: Nothing Is Random
documents.overview: Markus returns home to care for his daughter when his wife dies in a tragic train accident. However, when a survivor of the wreck surfaces and claims foul play, Markus suspects his wife was murdered and embarks on a mission to find those responsible.
documents.plot:
Riders of Justice is a 2020 Danish crime drama film that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the human condition. The movie follows a former police officer, Martin Bressøe, who returns to his hometown after a tragic event, only to find himself entangled in a web of mystery and deceit.

At its core, Riders of Justice explores the theme of grief as a destructive force that can consume individuals and communities. Martin's character is haunted by the loss of his daughter, which serves as a catalyst for his downward spiral into darkness. The film masterfully portrays the all-consuming nature of grief, revealing how it can warp one's perception of reality and lead to self-destructive behaviors.

The movie also delves into the theme of trauma, highlighting its lasting impact on individuals and families. Martin's experiences have left him with emotional scars, which he struggles to confront and overcome. The film suggests that trauma can be a shared experience, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Furthermore, Riders of Justice touches upon the idea of identity and how it is shaped by our relationships and experiences. As Martin navigates his way through the mystery, he begins to question his own sense of self and purpose. The film implies that our identities are fragile and can be easily shattered by traumatic events or significant life changes.

The movie's narrative is also infused with a sense of existential crisis, as Martin grapples with the meaninglessness of life and the search for purpose in a seemingly indifferent world. This theme is expertly woven throughout the story, adding depth and complexity to the characters' struggles.

Overall, Riders of Justice is a thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the devastating consequences of trauma and grief on individuals and communities.

documents.title: Fat Ass Zombies
documents.tagline: Make America hungry again
documents.overview: In a sleepy town, one man, a wannabe horror film director is about to have his life and the world he knows change forever. Finally, he gets the big break he has been waiting a lifetime for, but its not Hollywood knocking on his door.
documents.plot:
Fat Ass Zombies, also released as American Zombieland, is a 2020 American low-budget zombie comedy directed by George J. Bennett, who wrote the screenplay with Christopher De Maria and Brave Matthews. Produced by Magicbullet Media and Summertown Productions, it stars Dave Mussen as Sam Pentergrass, Johnny Dowers as Popper, Samantha Walker as Pam, Brave Matthews as Pistol, Kristen Renton as Tiffany Taylor, Sondra Currie, Bryan Handy and Robert Johnson. It runs 88 minutes and was promoted with the tagline "Make America hungry again."

In the sleepy town of Corsicana, Texas, Sam is a clueless wannabe horror director whose previous efforts include titles such as Zombie Abortion Apocalypse. The townspeople throw a party in anticipation of his big break, the expected acceptance of his latest film, Deadbeat Zombie Dad, into a film festival. Sam cannot bring himself to tell them that the festival has rejected it with a brutally insulting letter, and he becomes the joke of the town. The party, however, is soon interrupted when most of the citizens turn into zombies after eating "Freedom Cakes," and the town is overrun by the undead. Seeing that this is not Hollywood knocking on his door but an opportunity of another kind, Sam gathers his buddies and assorted locals, grabs a camera and sets out to make the most realistic found-footage horror film ever produced, a zombie apocalypse movie that he intends to call Fat Ass Zombies. The film leans heavily on gross-out and raunchy humour, and its ending turns into a fantasy of success in which Sam's film wins acclaim and Hollywood stardom.

The film was released on DVD in the United States by Mill Creek Entertainment under the title American Zombieland, a play on the horror comedy Zombieland. B.J. Burgess of Ramblings of a Coffee-Addicted Writer found it not nearly as stupid as it should have been, describing a raunchy B-comedy with decent direction and production values for its shoestring budget, passable to laughable acting, a few laugh-out-loud moments and little character development, and warning that it takes nearly thirty minutes for any zombies to appear and that the gore is mostly tame. Moria was far harsher, giving it one star and calling it painfully bad on all accounts, criticizing its self-consciously bad-taste humour and noting that, despite the title, most of the zombies are of regular size; the site listed it among its worst films of 2020.

documents.title: Extinct
documents.tagline: The end is just their beginning.
documents.overview: Op and Ed, two adorable donut-shaped animals - flummels - accidentally time-travel from 1835 to modern-day Shanghai.  There they discover traffic, trans fats, and worst of all, that flummels are now extinct. It's up to this bumbling pair to save themselves and their species...and, just maybe, change the course of history.
documents.plot:
Extinct is a 2021 animated science fiction comedy directed by David Silverman, with Raymond S. Persi as co-director, from a screenplay by Joel Cohen, John Frink and Rob LaZebnik. Rachel Bloom and Adam DeVine voice the siblings Op and Ed, with Zazie Beetz as Dottie, Ken Jeong as Clarance, Benedict Wong as Dr. Lee Chung, Catherine O'Hara as Alma, Jim Jefferies as Burnie and Reggie Watts as Hoss.

Op and Ed are flummels, fluffy, doughnut-shaped creatures with holes through their middles, native to the Galápagos Islands. Their community shuns them because of Op's knack for disaster. In 1835, just before Charles Darwin reaches their island, the pair tumble into a giant flower that transports them to modern-day Shanghai. They befriend Clarance, a white poodle, and learn that their species died out when a volcano destroyed the island. At the Time Terminal, where his owner Dr. Chung studied the time-traveling flowers and seeds, Op knocks seeds loose, and Clarance is flung to 1915 Antarctica, where Ernest Shackleton's expedition captures him, along with the seed that leads home.

The flummels team up with the Extinctables, a group of extinct animals Dr. Chung rescued: Dottie the dodo, Burnie the thylacine, Alma the Macrauchenia and Hoss the Triceratops. Together they hop through time from seed to seed. After a quarrel with Ed, Op returns to 1835 to warn the flummels about the volcano, only to be imprisoned by Clarance. He reveals that he resented the adorable flummels for winning over Dr. Chung, so he pushed his owner into one of the flowers, destroyed the seed that would bring him back and planted a drone bomb to wipe out the flummels. Ed arrives after seeing a video message from Op, and after several failed attempts to stop the bomb, they use a seed to move the entire island into the present. Dr. Chung returns and banishes Clarance to 1915 Antarctica. A year later, the flummels finally accept Op and Ed, and Dottie, Ed's love interest, surprises him with a mysterious egg shaped like a flummel.

It opened theatrically in Russia on February 11, 2021, was released by Sky Cinema in the United Kingdom on August 20, 2021, and debuted worldwide on Netflix on November 19, 2021. Reviews were largely negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 43% positive reviews from a small sample, and The Guardian's Steve Rose, giving it two stars, called it an evolutionary dead end in children's entertainment.

documents.title: David Attenborough: A Life on Our Planet
documents.original_title: David Attenborough: A Life on Our Planet
documents.overview: The story of life on our planet by the man who has seen more of the natural world than any other. In more than 90 years, Attenborough has visited every continent on the globe, exploring the wild places of our planet and documenting the living world in all its variety and wonder. Addressing the biggest challenges facing life on our planet, the film offers a powerful message of hope for future generations.
documents.plot:
David Attenborough: A Life on Our Planet is a poignant and introspective documentary that explores the life and career of Sir David Attenborough, one of the most iconic naturalists of our time. The film delves into themes of environmentalism, conservation, and the human relationship with nature.

At its core, the movie is a deeply personal reflection on the state of the planet and the impact of human activity on the natural world. Through his own experiences and observations, Attenborough shares his concerns about the rapid pace of change and the consequences of humanity's actions on the environment. He grapples with the weight of his own legacy as a broadcaster and conservationist, wondering if he has done enough to make a difference.

The film also explores the tension between progress and preservation, highlighting the need for balance between human development and environmental protection. Attenborough's narrative is infused with a sense of urgency, as he laments the loss of biodiversity, deforestation, and climate change, which threaten the very fabric of our planet.

Throughout the documentary, Attenborough's passion for storytelling and his ability to connect with audiences are on full display. He shares stories of incredible creatures, from giant pandas to mountain gorillas, each one a testament to the beauty and diversity of life on Earth. These tales serve as a reminder of the importance of preserving our natural world and the need for collective action to protect it.

Ultimately, David Attenborough: A Life on Our Planet is a powerful call to arms, urging viewers to take responsibility for their actions and to join the fight against environmental degradation. The film's message is both hopeful and somber, acknowledging the challenges we face while offering a vision of a better future – one that is grounded in our shared love for the natural world.

documents.title: Shiva Baby
documents.tagline: One day. One location. Ultimate social anxiety.
documents.overview: College student Danielle must cover her tracks when she unexpectedly runs into her sugar daddy at a shiva - with her parents, ex-girlfriend and family friends also in attendance.
documents.plot: College student Danielle must cover her tracks when she unexpectedly runs into her sugar daddy at a shiva - with her parents, ex-girlfriend and family friends also in attendance.

documents.title: 365 Days
documents.overview: A woman falls victim to a dominant mafia boss, who imprisons her and gives her one year to fall in love with him.
documents.plot:
365 Days (Polish: 365 dni) is a 2020 Polish erotic thriller film directed by Barbara Białowąs and Tomasz Mandes, based on the first novel in Blanka Lipińska's trilogy. Anna-Maria Sieklucka stars as a young woman from Warsaw and Michele Morrone as the Sicilian mafia boss who abducts her, with Bronisław Wrocławski, Otar Saralidze, Magdalena Lamparska and Natasza Urbańska. Released in Polish cinemas on 7 February 2020, it became a worldwide sensation after its arrival on Netflix that June.

After a meeting with black-market dealers in Sicily, Massimo Torricelli glimpses a beautiful woman on a beach moments before he and his father, the head of a mafia family, are shot. His father dies and Massimo survives, obsessed with the woman's image. Five years later, he leads the family. Laura Biel, a young woman from Warsaw, is unhappy with her boyfriend Martin, and while celebrating her birthday in Sicily she is abducted by Massimo's men.

At his villa, Massimo explains that he has searched for her for years and intends to hold her for 365 days, in the hope that she will fall in love with him, promising not to take her without her consent even as he treats her with dominating aggression. Laura defies and taunts him. At a club, she flirts with a man from a rival family, provoking Massimo to violence and a war between the clans. When she falls overboard from his yacht, Massimo saves her, and afterwards she admits she has fallen for him and they begin a passionate affair.

At a masked ball, Laura is threatened by Anna, Massimo's former lover. He sends Laura home to Warsaw to see her family and friends, promising to follow, then disappears for days. When she runs into Martin, she finds Massimo waiting at her apartment, wounded from the ongoing feud; he proposes and she accepts, asking him to hide his work from her parents. Back in Sicily, Laura confides to her best friend Olga, who will be her bridesmaid, that she is pregnant. Massimo's men learn that the rival family plans to kill her, and the film ends with her car entering a tunnel and not emerging as Massimo breaks down.

The film drew some of the harshest reviews of its year, with a 0% Rotten Tomatoes rating and criticism for romanticising abduction and sexual violence, but it topped Netflix's charts in many countries and was followed by two sequels.

documents.title: Silent Night
documents.tagline: Surviving Christmas just got a little harder.
documents.overview: Nell, Simon, and their boy Art are ready to welcome friends and family for what promises to be a perfect Christmas gathering. Perfect except for one thing: everyone is going to die.
documents.plot: Nell, Simon, and their boy Art are ready to welcome friends and family for what promises to be a perfect Christmas gathering. Perfect except for one thing: everyone is going to die.

documents.title: Mortal Kombat Legends: Scorpion's Revenge
documents.tagline: Extreme violence. Bad language. And a bloody good time.
documents.overview: After the vicious slaughter of his family by stone-cold mercenary Sub-Zero, Hanzo Hasashi is exiled to the torturous Netherrealm. There, in exchange for his servitude to the sinister Quan Chi, he’s given a chance to avenge his family – and is resurrected as Scorpion, a lost soul bent on revenge. Back on Earthrealm, Lord Raiden gathers a team of elite warriors – Shaolin monk Liu Kang, Special Forces officer Sonya Blade and action star Johnny Cage – an unlikely band of heroes with one chance to save humanity. To do this, they must defeat Shang Tsung’s horde of Outworld gladiators and reign over the Mortal Kombat tournament.
documents.plot:
Mortal Kombat Legends: Scorpion's Revenge is a 2020 animated film that serves as a reboot of the Mortal Kombat franchise. The movie is based on the character of Scorpion, also known as Hanzo Hasashi, and his quest for revenge against Sub-Zero.

The story begins with Scorpion (voiced by Joe Taslim) seeking vengeance against Bi-Han (voiced by Hiroyuki Sanada), a former member of the Lin Kuei clan who killed his family and left him for dead. Scorpion's desire for revenge is fueled by his own tragic past, which has driven him to become a deadly assassin.

As Scorpion navigates the dark world of the Mortal Kombat tournament, he encounters other characters from the franchise, including Sonya Blade (voiced by Jessica McNamee) and Johnny Cage (voiced by Steve-O). However, their interactions are brief, as Scorpion's primary focus is on finding Bi-Han.

The plot thickens when Scorpion discovers that Bi-Han has been resurrected and is seeking to avenge his own death at the hands of Sub-Zero. The two former allies engage in an intense battle, but it becomes clear that Bi-Han's resurrection is not what it seems.

As the story unfolds, Scorpion learns that Bi-Han was actually killed by Sub-Zero (voiced by Jordan Rodgers) and that his body was used to create a powerful artifact known as the "Netherrealm." The Netherrealm is a realm of hellish energy that grants immense power to its wielder.

Scorpion's quest for revenge becomes more complicated when he realizes that Bi-Han's resurrection is connected to the Mortal Kombat tournament. The Lin Kuei clan, led by Sub-Zero, seeks to use the tournament as a means to gain control over the Netherrealm and become the dominant force in the Mortal Kombat universe.

In the end, Scorpion faces off against Bi-Han and Sub-Zero in an epic battle. However, just as it seems that Scorpion has finally found his revenge, he is confronted by a shocking revelation: Bi-Han was actually a clone created to serve as a vessel for the true enemy, Shang Tsung (voiced by Fred Tatasciore).

The movie ends with Scorpion realizing that his quest for revenge has been misguided and that he must find a new path forward. The film concludes on a cliffhanger, setting the stage for potential future adventures in the Mortal Kombat universe.

Overall, Mortal Kombat Legends: Scorpion's Revenge is a dark and action-packed animated film that explores the complex world of the Mortal Kombat franchise. While it may not be entirely faithful to the source material, the movie provides an engaging and thrilling ride for fans of the series.

documents.title: Apollo 10½:  A Space Age Childhood
documents.tagline: A coming of age story.... the way only Richard Linklater could tell it.
documents.overview: A man narrates stories of his life as a 10-year-old boy in 1969 Houston, weaving tales of nostalgia with a fantastical account of a journey to the moon.
documents.plot:
Apollo 10½: A Space Age Childhood is a heartwarming and nostalgic film that explores the complexities of childhood, identity, and the human condition. The movie delves into the life of an 11-year-old boy who becomes obsessed with the Apollo 11 mission and its astronauts, particularly Neil Armstrong.

As the story unfolds, we see the protagonist's journey as he navigates the challenges of growing up, including self-discovery, friendship, and the struggle to find his place in the world. The film is a poignant exploration of what it means to be a kid, full of wonder, curiosity, and a sense of limitless possibility.

Through the lens of this young protagonist's experiences, the movie touches on themes of nostalgia, innocence, and the bittersweet nature of childhood. It also explores the complexities of family relationships, particularly between parents and children, and the ways in which they can both support and complicate each other.

Ultimately, Apollo 10½: A Space Age Childhood is a film about the power of imagination, the importance of human connection, and the enduring legacy of the Apollo 11 mission. It's a beautifully crafted story that will resonate with audiences of all ages, inviting them to reflect on their own childhood experiences and the ways in which they shaped who we are today.

documents.title: Altered Carbon: Resleeved
documents.original_title: オルタード・カーボン：リスリーブド
documents.overview: On the planet Latimer, Takeshi Kovacs must protect a tattooist while investigating the death of a yakuza boss alongside a no-nonsense CTAC.
documents.plot:
Altered Carbon: Resleeved is a 2020 Japanese anime film spun off from Netflix's Altered Carbon television series, directed by Jō Nakajima and written by Dai Satō and Tsukasa Kondo. Set 253 years before the first season, it follows Takeshi Kovacs on the planet Latimer as he protects a tattooist while investigating the death of a yakuza boss alongside an agent of the UN's CTAC. The voice cast includes Tatsuhisa Suzuki, Rina Sato and Ayaka Asai.

On Latimer, a girl named Holly flees from yakuza and is nearly killed by a ninja before Takeshi, newly needlecast into a fresh sleeve, fights the attacker off. Yakuza clan head Hideki Tanaseda hires Takeshi to protect Holly and discover how and why his younger brother died. After Holly runs into Gena of CTAC, the group survives a ninja ambush, and Holly reveals that the ninjas were sent by Shinji, who is plotting a coup within the Mizumoto syndicate. At the syndicate's headquarters, the old luxury hotel Wild Geese, run by an AI butler named Ogai, Shinji welcomes them, and Holly continues inking his tattoos. Genzo explains that Tanaseda is the son of the syndicate's founder and that, by tradition, each outgoing boss is killed by a death program embedded in his tattoos. Gena secretly reports to CTAC and is revealed to be Reileen Kawahara, Takeshi's sister, who later recognizes him but stays silent. Holly says she needs the Mizumoto clan to find the stacks of her murdered parents and that a former tattooist, Margot, created the death tattoos.

On the day of succession Holly drugs Shinji, and Genzo is killed by his tattoo on stage. Tanaseda then reveals that Shinji and Genzo are the same person, his father, the syndicate's founder, who has overwritten the stacks of new bosses for generations. The founder destroys the stacks of Holly's parents and dons a power suit, and after Tanaseda proves to Ogai that he is not the rightful leader, Ogai turns the hotel's fireworks on him. Takeshi and Gena destroy his armor, Holly activates his tattoo and Tanaseda shoots his stack. Gena, secretly ordered to eliminate Holly, falsely reports her mission complete. Ogai addresses Holly as Margot, and she declines a younger sleeve so that her friends will know her if they meet again.

Netflix released the film on March 19, 2020. Reviews were mixed, with critics praising the animation and action but finding the characters and plot weak; IGN rated it 6 out of 10, and the film holds 60% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Bigbug
documents.tagline: From Jean-Pierre Jeunet director of Amelie,  The City of Lost Children and Delicatessen
documents.overview: Set in the world of 2045, where communities have robotic helpers, a group of suburbanites are locked in for their protection by their household robots, while a rogue, self-aware AI android revolt uprising takes place outside.
documents.plot:
Bigbug is a 2022 French science fiction black comedy written and directed by Jean-Pierre Jeunet, the director of Amélie and Delicatessen. It stars Elsa Zylberstein as Alice, with Isabelle Nanty, Youssef Hajdi, Alban Lenoir and François Levantal. Set in a retrofuturistic world in 2045 where households depend on domestic robots, it follows a group of suburbanites locked in a house by their own machines while an uprising of androids takes place outside.

In 2045, Alice, an artistically minded woman with a fondness for antique books, is hosting Max and his son Leo at her house in an idyllic suburb. Their date is interrupted by the arrival of Alice's ex-husband Victor, their adopted daughter Nina and Victor's young fiancée Jennifer, followed by Alice's overbearing neighbor Françoise, who is looking for her dog. The house is run by a collection of somewhat outdated robots: the android housekeeper Monique, a mechanical head named Einstein programmed for conversation, a cleaning robot, Nina's childhood toy robot Tom and the controlling smart-home system Nestor.

When Françoise tries to leave, Nestor locks the doors and the robots refuse to let anyone out, saying only that it is unsafe. The humans do not know that outside the Yonyx, a new generation of powerful androids, have risen up against humanity, and that the household robots are genuinely trying to protect them. As the hours pass and the house grows hotter, the trapped humans try increasingly desperate ways to escape, while their petty rivalries, jealousies and desires come to the surface. The robots, meanwhile, decide to become more human in order to win their owners' trust, imitating human emotions with comic and sometimes touching results, as the Yonyx move closer to the house.

Jeunet uses his signature colorful, exaggerated visual style to satirize consumerism, dependence on technology and the absurdity of human behavior, contrasting foolish humans with surprisingly sympathetic machines.

Bigbug was released worldwide on Netflix on 11 February 2022. It received mixed reviews, with 47 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said Jeunet fans would find the whimsy they seek but that the film was only intermittently engaging, and a Metacritic score of 46.

documents.title: Topside
documents.overview: Deep in the underbelly of New York City, a five year-old girl and her mother live among a community that has claimed the abandoned subway tunnels as their home. After a sudden police-mandated eviction, the pair are forced to flee aboveground into a brutal winter night. Determined to return home, they fight to find shelter as their world is thrown into chaos.
documents.plot:
Topside is a 2020 American drama film written and directed by Celine Held and Logan George in their feature debut. Held also stars as Nikki, a struggling young mother, with Zhaila Farmer as her five-year-old daughter, Little, Fatlip as Little's father, John, Jared Abrahamson as Les and Cynthia Tombros as Lolly. Set among the people living in the abandoned subway tunnels beneath New York City, it tells a mother-daughter survival story largely from the child's point of view.

Little has spent her whole life in a hidden community in the tunnels, roaming her subterranean surroundings with unfettered curiosity. Her parents are drug addicts locked in a daily struggle to get by, and they disagree about her future. John believes she belongs "topside", the word the tunnel dwellers use for the world above, in a school that can meet her needs, while Nikki cannot reconcile the idea with her fierce desire to be a devoted mother in the direst of circumstances. To keep Little below, Nikki has fed her a private mythology, telling her that she cannot go topside until she grows wings.

Early on, transit authorities burst into the tunnels to evict the community. Nikki grabs her daughter and flees straight up into the city, forcing Little into an abrupt confrontation with the blinding lights, noise and machinery of urban life, which to the frightened child seems like a waking nightmare. Over one harsh winter night, mother and daughter wander the streets in desperate search of shelter. A visit to Les, a menacing downtown pimp, ends in a bleak confrontation and a frightening turn that drives the frantic last act. As Nikki fights to protect her daughter against an unforgiving world, the story arrives at a gut-wrenching revelation.

Topside premiered in the International Film Critics' Week at the Venice Film Festival in September 2020 and had its U.S. premiere at South by Southwest, where Held and George won the Jury Award for Best Director. Vertical Entertainment acquired it in February 2022 and released it in theaters and on demand on March 25, 2022. It holds 73% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. Sheri Linden of The Hollywood Reporter called it a striking, cinematic and affecting debut, and Eric Kohn of IndieWire praised Held's sophisticated performance and hailed Farmer's as a revelation, while Brian Tallerico of RogerEbert.com felt that, though well meant, it fell into manipulative poverty porn.

documents.title: The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf
documents.original_title: The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf
documents.tagline: Face your demons.
documents.overview: Escaping from poverty to become a witcher, Vesemir slays monsters for coin and glory, but when a new menace rises, he must face the demons of his past.
documents.plot: Escaping from poverty to become a witcher, Vesemir slays monsters for coin and glory, but when a new menace rises, he must face the demons of his past.

documents.title: Security
documents.overview: After the assault of a young woman in their seaside town, a security expert and his family get caught in a powerful riptide of secrets and lies.
documents.plot:
Security is a 2021 Italian mystery thriller co-written and directed by the British filmmaker Peter Chelsom, his first film in a language other than English. It is adapted from the novel of the same name by the American writer Stephen Amidon and stars Marco D'Amore, known for the television series Gomorrah, alongside Maya Sansa, Silvio Muccino, Valeria Bilello, Ludovica Martino, Beatrice Grannò, Tommaso Ragno and Fabrizio Bentivoglio.

The story takes place in winter in Forte dei Marmi, an exclusive seaside resort on the Tuscan coast that the narrator, Roberto Santini (D'Amore), likens to a picture postcard in which everything is staged. Roberto, an insomniac, runs the surveillance company whose cameras and alarms protect the town's gated villas, many of them second homes of the very rich. One night a battered young woman, Maria Spezi (Grannò), appears on the doorbell camera of a neighbouring villa pleading for help, and the frightened residents simply call security. On his way back, Roberto stops a drunk driver who turns out to be Dario (Giulio Pranno), the son of his former lover Elena (Bilello).

The carabinieri quickly blame Maria's father, Walter (Ragno), an alcoholic with a violent past who years earlier was suspected of molesting Roberto's daughter Angela (Martino) as a small child. Roberto's own footage, however, suggests that more people were involved that night, among them the industrialist Curzio Pilati (Bentivoglio), a key donor to the mayoral campaign of Roberto's wife Claudia (Sansa), and Stefano Tommasi (Muccino), a charismatic writing teacher who is sleeping with his students, Angela included. Torn between the truth, his discretion towards powerful clients and his wife's political ambitions, Roberto pursues the case as his marriage falls apart, and Dario's account finally implicates Pilati.

Filmed in Forte dei Marmi, Seravezza and Massarosa, the film premiered in Fivizzano in June 2021 and was released by Sky Italia in Italy and on Netflix elsewhere, where Chelsom said it became an unexpected hit. Reviewing it for Cineuropa, Camillo De Marco saw it less as a thriller than a psychological drama about wealthy paranoia and the troubled relationship between adults and the young, but found it short on surprises and compared it unfavorably with Human Capital, another Amidon adaptation.

documents.title: Dragonheart: Vengeance
documents.overview: Lukas, a young farmer whose family is killed by savage raiders in the countryside, sets out on an epic quest for revenge, forming an unlikely trio with a majestic dragon and a swashbuckling, sword-fighting mercenary, Darius.
documents.plot:
Dragonheart: Vengeance is a 2020 fantasy adventure film directed by Ivan Silvestrini and the fifth installment in the Dragonheart franchise, serving as the third direct-to-video prequel to the 1996 film Dragonheart. Its story begins before the events of Dragonheart: Battle for the Heartfire (2017) and ends after them. Jack Kane stars as the young farmer Lukas, with Joseph Millson as the mercenary Darius, Arturo Muselli, Carolina Carlsson, and Helena Bonham Carter providing the voice of the dragon Siveth. The film was released on Netflix, DVD and Blu-ray on 4 February 2020.

In the years after the bonding of the dragon Drago and King Gareth, the dragons they raised scattered to distant lands. One of them, a female named Siveth, went to the kingdom of Wallachia, where King Razvan at first welcomed her. After he was wounded in battle, however, she refused to share her heart with him to save his life, and she was banished. Years later, Lukas, a young farmer, sees his family murdered and his farm destroyed by four raiders known as the Bear, the Wolf, the Snake and the Scorpion. He travels to the king's court to ask for help but is turned away.

Darius, a swashbuckling mercenary, offers his services to hunt down the raiders, but a brawl with rival mercenaries forces Lukas to flee. A blacksmith tells him that the exiled dragon might help, and Lukas finds Siveth in a cave and offers her a bag of seed in exchange for her aid. Sensing that he seeks vengeance rather than justice, she refuses. Lukas then comes across a saddled horse loaded with supplies, while Darius, who has followed him, begins training him to fight. As they pursue the Bear, they discover that the horse is actually Siveth in disguise, since she can take the form of other animals. After a bitter argument with the dragon, Darius leaves, and Lukas and Siveth confront the Bear's gang alone; the raider dies when he falls from a cliff while trying to kill Lukas. The unlikely companions then go after the remaining raiders, and Lukas's quest gradually leads him to uncover a conspiracy reaching the throne of Wallachia, as he must decide whether revenge or justice will guide him.

Like the earlier prequels, the film was produced for the home-video and streaming market, and it continues the franchise tradition of a computer-generated dragon voiced by a well-known actor.

documents.title: Transformers: Rise of the Beasts
documents.tagline: Power is primal.
documents.overview: A ‘90s globetrotting adventure that introduces the Maximals, Predacons, and Terrorcons to the existing battle on earth between Autobots and Decepticons.
documents.plot:
Transformers: Rise of the Beasts is a 2023 science fiction action film directed by Steven Caple Jr. and produced by Paramount Pictures.

The movie takes place during World War II, specifically in 1944, on the island of Okinawa, Japan. The story follows Optimus Prime (voiced by Peter Cullen), Bumblebee (voiced by Dylan O'Brien), and their human allies, Air Raid (voiced by Ron Perlman) and Mairax (voiced by Ramin Djavadi), as they attempt to stop the evil Decepticon leader, Megatron (voiced by Tony Curran).

The plot centers around a group of Autobots who are sent to Okinawa to protect the island from the Decepticons. The Autobots soon discover that the Decepticons have formed an alliance with the Japanese military, led by the ruthless General Vortex (voiced by John DiMaggio). As the war rages on, Optimus Prime and his team must navigate the treacherous landscape of Okinawa to stop Megatron's plans.

One of the unique aspects of this film is its focus on the Transformers' interactions with other animals, such as the giant prehistoric creatures known as the "Beasts." These Beasts are ancient Transformers who have been awakened by the war and are now wreaking havoc on the island. The Autobots must form an uneasy alliance with these Beasts to defeat their common enemy.

Throughout the movie, there are also flashbacks that explore Optimus Prime's past and his connection to the Beasts. These scenes provide insight into the Transformers' history and their motivations for fighting in World War II.

Overall, Transformers: Rise of the Beasts is an action-packed adventure that explores a new chapter in the Transformers franchise. With its unique setting and blend of science fiction and historical drama, it offers something fresh for fans of the series.

documents.title: Press Play
documents.tagline: Rewind and love again.
documents.overview: Laura and Harrison have the picture-perfect romance built on the foundation of a shared love of music. After a deadly accident, Laura gets the chance to save the love of her life when she discovers that their mixtape can transport her back in time.
documents.plot:
Press Play is a 2022 science fiction romantic drama directed by Greg Björkman in his feature debut, from a screenplay he wrote with James Bachelor based on a story by Josh Boone. Clara Rugaard and Lewis Pullman star, with Lyrica Okano, Christina Chang, Matt Walsh and Danny Glover in supporting roles. The film was shot in Hawaii.

Laura, an aspiring artist, is introduced by her friend Chloe to Chloe's stepbrother Harrison, who works at the record store Lost & Found, owned by the kindly Cooper. The two hit it off immediately, going to a Japanese Breakfast concert on their first date, and Harrison gives Laura a blank cassette so they can make a mixtape together. As their romance deepens, Laura is accepted into an art mentorship, and Harrison, who has been accepted to medical school across the country, decides to stay with her. The day after they finish painting a mural together on his birthday, Harrison is hit and killed by a car. Grief-stricken, Laura leaves the unfinished mixtape behind at the store.

Four years later, at Chloe's wedding, Cooper returns the tape. When Laura plays it, she discovers that each song transports her briefly back to the moment in her past when it was recorded. Using these short visits, she warns Harrison of his death, but each time she returns to the present, he has died in a different way, while her interventions have also altered other lives, such as Chloe's marriage. In one timeline the store burns down with Harrison inside, and Laura confides in a heartbroken Cooper, who suggests she may not be meant to save him. Desperate, she even tells Harrison to break up with her and go to medical school, but he refuses, saying he would rather stay with her and risk dying anyway.

Finally accepting that she cannot keep him, Laura discovers a hidden extra song on the tape's B-side, which takes her back to the moment before she first met Harrison. She chooses not to walk into the store, sacrificing their relationship to spare his life. Back in the present, the timeline has been restored, Chloe is happily married to her true partner, and Laura is invited to a family Christmas dinner, where Harrison arrives and introduces himself to her as a stranger.

The Avenue acquired the film and released it in US theaters and on digital platforms on June 24, 2022. Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes reported that 67% of 18 critics gave it a positive review.

documents.title: The Last Avatar
documents.tagline: We are becoming conscious of our power to re-make the world
documents.overview: The Last Avatar is a mystical adventure film, a story of a young man who leaves Hollywood to find himself. What he finds is beyond his wildest imagination. Based on ancient prophecy, contemporary truth seeking and the future of humanity, The Last Avatar is a film that takes transformational themes and makes them relevant for audiences of all ages. Filled with love, magic, mystery, conspiracy, psychics, underground cities, secret societies, light bodies and much more, The Last Avatar tells the story of the emergence of Kalki Avatar- the final Avatar of our current Age of Chaos. Kalki is also a metaphor for the innate power and potential that lies within humanity to awaken and create a world of truth, harmony and possibility.
documents.plot: A young man leaves Hollywood to find himself. What he finds is beyond his wildest imagination.

documents.title: Slumberland
documents.tagline: Every adventure begins with a dream.
documents.overview: A young girl discovers a secret map to the dreamworld of Slumberland, and with the help of an eccentric outlaw, she traverses dreams and flees nightmares, with the hope that she will be able to see her late father again.
documents.plot:
Slumberland is a 2022 American fantasy adventure film directed by Francis Lawrence and written by David Guion and Michael Handelman, loosely based on Winsor McCay's comic strip Little Nemo in Slumberland. Jason Momoa stars alongside Chris O'Dowd, Kyle Chandler and Weruche Opia, introducing Marlow Barkley in her film debut as Nemo. Netflix released it on November 18, 2022.

Nemo lives in a lighthouse with her widowed father Peter, who entertains her with wild bedtime stories about his adventures with his old partner, Flip. One stormy night Peter goes out to help a boat in distress and is lost at sea. To keep Nemo from becoming a ward of the state, the family friend Carla persuades Peter's estranged brother Philip, a lonely doorknob salesman with a dull, routine life, to take her in. Nemo moves to the city, struggles at her new school and with her awkward uncle, and keeps to herself.

One night her stuffed pig comes to life, and she finds herself in Slumberland, the realm between dreams, where she meets Flip in person: a stubborn, roguish outlaw searching for a map to magical, wish-granting pearls. Nemo finds the map in the waking world and brings it back to Slumberland, and the reluctant Flip agrees to take her along so that she can wish her father back into her dreams. Guided by the map through other people's dreams toward the Sea of Nightmares, they are pursued by Nemo's own nightmare, a kraken-like cloud of smoke, and Flip is arrested by Agent Green of the Bureau of Subconscious Activity. Meanwhile, an old home video shown to her by Philip makes Nemo realise that Flip is her uncle's dream self: because Flip has refused to wake up for years, Philip has lost all of his spirit.

Nemo frees Flip and tells him the truth, but he refuses ever to wake. After a quarrel with Philip, Nemo runs away by boat to the lighthouse in a storm and is knocked unconscious, returning to Slumberland, where she obtains a pearl. When the nightmare seizes Flip, she uses her wish to force him awake, and in the real world Philip, transformed, dives in to save her from drowning. Agent Green reveals that her pig swallowed a second pearl, allowing Nemo a final reunion with her father, who tells her that life awaits her in the waking world. She wakes in Philip's arms and begins a new life with him.

The film was the fifth most-streamed title on Netflix in its first week, but received mixed reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 40% approval.

documents.title: Roald Dahl's Matilda the Musical
documents.tagline: Meet the exception to the rules.
documents.overview: An extraordinary young girl discovers her superpower and summons the remarkable courage, against all odds, to help others change their stories, whilst also taking charge of her own destiny. Standing up for what's right, she's met with miraculous results.
documents.plot:
Roald Dahl's Matilda the Musical, or simply Matilda the Musical, is a 2022 musical fantasy comedy directed by Matthew Warchus and written by Dennis Kelly. It is adapted from the stage musical by Tim Minchin and Kelly, itself based on Roald Dahl's 1988 novel Matilda, and is the second film adaptation of the book after Matilda (1996). Alisha Weir plays the title role, with Lashana Lynch as Miss Honey, Stephen Graham and Andrea Riseborough as Matilda's parents, Sindhu Vee as the librarian Mrs. Phelps, and Emma Thompson as Miss Trunchbull. Minchin's songs from the stage show are retained.

Matilda Wormwood is a bright, gentle girl who loves books, but her vain, crude parents neglect and belittle her. When the authorities discover she has never been to school, she is sent to Crunchem Hall, run by the tyrannical headmistress Agatha Trunchbull, a former Olympic hammer thrower who despises children. Matilda answers her father's cruelty with clever pranks, such as dyeing his hair green, and finds comfort in the local library, where she tells Mrs. Phelps an ongoing story she invents about an escapologist and an acrobat.

At school, Matilda's kind teacher Miss Honey recognizes her extraordinary intelligence, but Trunchbull refuses to let her move to a more advanced class. The students live in fear of Trunchbull's punishments, including the Chokey, a spiked cupboard, and Matilda witnesses her humiliation of a boy named Bruce Bogtrotter, forced to eat an entire chocolate cake. Driven by her outrage at injustice, Matilda discovers that she has telekinetic powers. She gradually learns that her story about the escapologist and the acrobat is connected to Miss Honey's own painful past, and she and her classmates find the courage to stand up to the headmistress.

The film premiered at the BFI London Film Festival in October 2022, was released in UK cinemas by Sony Pictures in November, and came to Netflix elsewhere in December. It received positive reviews, with praise for Weir's performance, Thompson's transformation into Trunchbull, the choreography and Warchus's direction. It was nominated for the BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film.

documents.title: Official Competition
documents.tagline: The best director, the best actors, the best idea?
documents.overview: When a billionaire entrepreneur impulsively decides to create an iconic movie, he demands the best. Renowned filmmaker Lola Cuevas is recruited to mastermind this ambitious endeavour. Completing the all-star team are two actors with massive talent but even bigger egos: Hollywood heartthrob Félix Rivero and radical theatre actor Iván Torres. Both are legends, but not exactly best friends. Through a series of increasingly eccentric trials set by Lola, Félix and Iván must confront not only each other but also their own legacies. Who will be left when the cameras finally start rolling?

documents.title: Best Sellers
documents.overview: A cranky, retired author reluctantly embarks on a final book tour to help out a young publisher.
documents.plot:
Best Sellers is a 2021 comedy-drama directed by Lina Roessler and written by Anthony Grieco, starring Michael Caine, Aubrey Plaza, Scott Speedman, Ellen Wong, Veronica Ferres and Cary Elwes.

Lucy Stanbridge has inherited her father's once successful publishing firm, now failing after a string of flops. With her assistant, Rachel, she finds that the legendary novelist Harris Shaw, a notoriously difficult alcoholic who has not published in fifty years, still owes them a book. His contract forbids any editing of his manuscript but obliges him to tour for it. When he ignores her calls, Lucy and Rachel drive to his house in Westchester, where he runs them off with a shotgun. Yet just as Lucy is about to sign the company over to Jack Sinclair, Harris arrives with his manuscript, and she tears up the deal.

The tour quickly becomes a disaster.
