documents.title: Thirteen Lives
documents.tagline: 5000 people, 17 countries, 1 miracle that united the world.
documents.overview: Based on the true nail-biting mission that captivated the world. Twelve boys and the coach of a Thai soccer team explore the Tham Luang cave when an unexpected rainstorm traps them in a chamber inside the mountain. Entombed behind a maze of flooded cave tunnels, they face impossible odds. A team of world-class divers navigate through miles of dangerous cave networks to discover that finding the boys is only the beginning.
documents.plot:
Thirteen Lives is a 2022 biographical drama film directed by Ron Howard, based on the true story of the 2018 Thai cave rescue. The movie stars Dwayne Johnson, Yeasmin "Yaya" Fonseca, and Samson Kayo.

The film begins with Aron Ralston (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), an American outdoorsman who becomes trapped in a narrow canyon in Utah while on a solo hike. He is forced to amputate his own arm to free himself from the boulder that has pinned him down for five days. The incident leaves him emotionally scarred and sets him on a path of self-discovery.

The story then shifts to the 2018 Thai cave rescue, where a group of young soccer players, led by 12-year-old Lukman (played by Chaiyaphum Suntivong), become trapped in the Tham Luang Nang Non cave in northern Thailand. The cave's narrow passages and fast-flowing water make it impossible for them to escape on their own.

As the rescue efforts begin, a team of international experts, led by John Volanthen (played by Viggo Mortensen) and Rick Stanton (played by Joel Edgerton), is assembled to help locate the missing boys. The team faces numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, flooding, and limited access to medical supplies.

Meanwhile, back in the United States, Aron Ralston becomes involved with a group of young Thai soccer players who are training in Utah. He begins to mentor them, sharing his expertise on wilderness survival and teamwork. One of these players, Lukman, is particularly drawn to Aron's teachings and eventually joins him on an expedition to the cave.

As the rescue efforts progress, the team faces numerous setbacks, including a failed attempt to extract one of the boys using a makeshift rope. The situation becomes increasingly dire as the days turn into weeks, and the world watches anxiously for news of the missing boys.

In a dramatic climax, John Volanthen and Rick Stanton finally locate Lukman and his friends in the cave. They work tirelessly to guide them out of the cave, facing numerous challenges along the way. The rescue is ultimately successful, but not without its costs: one of the boys dies during the ordeal.

The film ends with Aron Ralston reflecting on the experience and how it has changed him. He realizes that his own near-death experience in the canyon had prepared him for the challenges he faced in the cave. The movie concludes with a message about the power of teamwork, perseverance, and the importance of never giving up.

Overall, Thirteen Lives is a gripping and emotional drama that explores themes of survival, redemption, and the human spirit.

documents.title: A Week Away
documents.overview: Troubled teen Will Hawkins has a run-in with the law that puts him at an important crossroad: go to juvenile detention or attend a Christian summer camp. At first a fish-out-of-water, Will opens his heart, discovers love with a camp regular, and sense of belonging in the last place he expected to find it.
documents.plot: Troubled teen Will Hawkins has a run-in with the law that puts him at an important crossroad: go to juvenile detention or attend a Christian summer camp. At first a fish-out-of-water, Will opens his heart, discovers love with a camp regular, and sense of belonging in the last place he expected to find it.

documents.tagline: 65 million years ago, prehistoric Earth had a visitor.
documents.overview: After a catastrophic crash on an unknown planet, pilot Mills quickly discovers he's actually stranded on Earth…65 million years ago. Now, with only one chance at rescue, Mills and the only other survivor, Koa, must make their way across an unknown terrain riddled with dangerous prehistoric creatures in an epic fight to survive.
documents.plot:
65 is a 2023 American science fiction thriller film written and directed by Scott Beck and Bryan Woods. Adam Driver stars as a space pilot stranded on prehistoric Earth, with Ariana Greenblatt as the young girl he struggles to keep alive. Beck and Woods produced the film with Sam Raimi, Deborah Liebling and Zainab Azizi, and Sony Pictures released it under its Columbia Pictures label on March 10, 2023.

Sixty-five million years ago, Mills, a pilot from the planet Somaris, reluctantly accepts a two-year deep-space expedition to pay for treatment for his seriously ill daughter, Nevine. During the voyage, his ship is struck by an asteroid field and crashes on an uncharted planet, which is Earth. Mills finds that the passengers in cryosleep have been killed, and is on the verge of taking his own life when he discovers one survivor, a young girl named Koa. With no common language and a broken translator, they can barely communicate.

Mills learns that the ship's escape shuttle has landed on a mountain about fifteen kilometers away, and to persuade Koa to come with him, he falsely tells her that her family is waiting there. As they make their way through the jungle, they discover that the planet is inhabited by dinosaurs and other predators. They free a small creature from a tar pit, only to see it killed; they are separated when a rockfall blocks a cave in which they shelter from a huge carnivore that Mills blinds in one eye; and each saves the other from attacks and from quicksand. Along the way, Koa watches video messages from Nevine, and the two slowly form a bond. Mills also discovers that a much larger asteroid will strike the planet within hours.

When they reach the shuttle, Koa learns that Mills lied about her family, and he confesses that Nevine died while he was away, promising to protect Koa. As they prepare to leave, falling debris knocks the shuttle down the mountain. They fight off a pair of Tyrannosaurus rex, with Koa distracting them using a projection of Nevine, and finally kill the carnivore Mills wounded earlier. They launch the shuttle just as the asteroid strikes, triggering the mass extinction that ends the age of the dinosaurs.

65 received mixed to negative reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 36% approval, with a consensus describing it as sodden science fiction. It grossed about $60 million worldwide against a $45 million budget.

documents.title: The Paramedic
documents.overview: Unable to face his new reality in a wheelchair, Ángel develops a deadly obsession with the woman who left him and unleashes a sinister revenge plot.
documents.plot:
The Paramedic (Spanish: El practicante) is a 2020 Spanish psychological thriller directed by Carles Torra and written by David Desola and Hèctor Hernández Vicens. Mario Casas stars as a psychopathic paramedic in Barcelona, opposite Déborah François as his girlfriend, with Guillermo Pfening, Celso Bugallo and Raúl Jiménez in the supporting cast. A Babieka Entertainment and Zabriskie Films production, it was shot in Catalonia, including in Lleida.

Ángel Hernández is a paramedic who shows no empathy for the people he treats and routinely steals from them, selling valuables to a local fence. At home he is possessive and controlling toward his girlfriend Vanesa, known as Vane. The couple have been unable to conceive, and Ángel blames Vane, even when a fertility test reveals that he has a low sperm count, which he hides from her. When an ambulance driven by his colleague Ricardo crashes during an emergency, Ángel is left paralyzed from the waist down. He blames Ricardo, and his disability deepens his paranoia and cruelty. Convinced Vane is cheating, he berates and gaslights her and installs spyware on her phone. After she discovers the surveillance, she leaves him.

Months later, Ángel is still obsessed with her. He stalks Vane and learns that she has begun a relationship with Ricardo and is pregnant with his child. Pretending he wants to return her belongings, Ángel lures her back to the apartment, sedates her and holds her captive, sending Ricardo a message in her name to keep him away. He fantasizes about raising the baby with her, using injections to keep her from walking, and when an elderly neighbor becomes suspicious, Ángel murders him; he later kills Ricardo as well. Although he deceives the police who come asking questions, Vane eventually escapes while he is out and drags herself to the stairwell, where a final struggle sends Ángel plunging down the stairs. He survives, completely paralyzed, unable to speak or breathe on his own.

Netflix released the film on September 16, 2020. Reviews were mixed, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting that half of eight critics' reviews were positive. Spanish critics focused on Casas's physical and dramatic transformation; Cinemanía awarded three and a half stars out of five, and HobbyConsolas called it a very successful film with strong performances and a great ending, while acknowledging that it does not reinvent the genre.

documents.title: Bigfoot Family
documents.tagline: The truth is out there… and it’s big!
documents.overview: Bigfoot, Adam's father, wants to use his fame for a good cause. Protecting a large wildlife reserve in Alaska sounds like the perfect opportunity! When Bigfoot mysteriously disappears without a trace, Adam and his animal friends will brave anything to find him again and save the nature reserve.
documents.plot: Bigfoot, Adam's father, wants to use his fame for a good cause. Protecting a large wildlife reserve in Alaska sounds like the perfect opportunity! When Bigfoot mysteriously disappears without a trace, Adam and his animal friends will brave anything to find him again and save the nature reserve.

documents.title: Lullaby
documents.tagline: Have you checked the baby?
documents.overview: A new mother discovers a lullaby in an ancient book and soon regards the song as a blessing. But her world transforms into a nightmare when the lullaby brings forth the ancient demon Lilith.
documents.plot:
Lullaby is a 2022 American-Canadian supernatural horror film directed by John R. Leonetti from a screenplay by Alex Greenfield and Ben Powell, produced by companies including Alcon Entertainment, Envision Media Arts, Wonderfilm Media and Heroes and Villains Entertainment. It stars Oona Chaplin as Rachel and Ramón Rodríguez as her husband John, with Liane Balaban as Rachel's sister Vivian, Kira Guloien as the demon Lilith and Alex Karzis as Rabbi Cohen. Michael Galbraith was the cinematographer, and the film runs 89 minutes under the tagline "Have you checked the baby?"

Rachel and John are proud new parents of a baby boy, Eli, but parenthood proves hard: six months on, Rachel is a sleep-deprived wreck and Eli is a fussy baby who cries constantly. In a box of baby things sent by her mother, which once belonged to Vivian, who lost both her baby, Zachary, and her husband under strange circumstances, Rachel finds an old book illustrated with demons and monsters that contains a lullaby. Out of desperation she sings it, and Eli miraculously falls asleep, so that at first the song seems a blessing. Soon, however, the couple hear voices and see strange things on the baby monitor, and Rachel glimpses an evil crone that seems to threaten her son. She visits Vivian in a mental institution and learns that her sister went through the same experience before losing her child, while John consults a tattooed rabbi who tells him of other ways to protect Eli. The lullaby, it emerges, has summoned the ancient demon Lilith, a taker of children served by her own deformed offspring, and the parents must face her to save their son.

The film was released on video on demand and digital platforms by Vertical in December 2022. Critics found it competent but formulaic. Jeffrey M. Anderson of Combustible Celluloid gave it two stars out of four, crediting committed performances and effective set design while calling the story all too familiar and its use of Jewish culture a checklist of terms. Jim Morazzini of Nerdly gave it two out of five, praising its dark, atmospheric look and its treatment of the stresses of new parenthood, but criticizing recycled jump scares and unconvincing computer effects. Kat Hughes of Ghouls Magazine was more positive, praising Chaplin's quiet strength and the film's place in the growing field of Jewish horror, and calling it one of Leonetti's strongest efforts as a director.

documents.title: Infamous
documents.tagline: Viral fame is a dangerous game.
documents.overview: Two young lovers rob their way across the southland, posting their exploits to social media, and gaining fame and followers as a result.
documents.plot:
Infamous is a 2020 American crime thriller written and directed by Joshua Caldwell. Bella Thorne stars as Arielle, a young woman obsessed with social media fame, with Jake Manley as her boyfriend Dean, Amber Riley, Michael Sirow and Marisa Coughlan. The film was released by Vertical Entertainment on 12 June 2020.

Arielle lives in a small Florida town with her mother, Janet, and Janet's deadbeat boyfriend, Bobby. She dreams of escaping to Hollywood and becoming famous, but her social media accounts have few followers. When she gets into a fight at a party and beats up another girl, the brawl is filmed and posted online, and Arielle gains a burst of new followers. She meets Dean Taylor, who is new to town and living with his father as a condition of his parole after serving time for armed robbery and assault. Dean's father is a violent drunk.

When Arielle discovers that her savings have been stolen, she accuses Bobby, who shoves her into a wall. She leaves, threatening to kill him, and goes to Dean's house, where she finds his father beating him. In the struggle that follows, Dean's father falls down the stairs and dies. Afraid of being blamed, the couple flee, and they begin committing robberies to fund their journey. Arielle starts filming and livestreaming their crimes, and their posts quickly go viral, turning the young outlaws into internet sensations with a rapidly growing audience. As they rob their way across the southern United States in the style of a modern Bonnie and Clyde, Arielle becomes more and more addicted to the attention, pushing for bigger and more dangerous heists. They are joined by Miles, a fan who wants to share in their notoriety, while the police close in, and Dean begins to realize that Arielle cares more about her followers than about him, leading to a violent climax broadcast to the world.

Infamous received negative reviews from critics, who found its satire of social media obvious and its story derivative of earlier outlaw films, although Thorne's performance was praised.

documents.title: Deep Blue Sea 3
documents.tagline: Deadlier than ever.
documents.overview: Dr. Emma Collins and her team are spending their third summer on the island of Little Happy studying the effect of climate change on the great white sharks who come to the nearby nursery every year to give birth. Along with the last two inhabitants of this former fishing village, their peaceful life is disrupted when a "scientific" team led by her ex-boyfriend and marine biologist Richard show up looking for three bull sharks who we soon learn aren't just any bull sharks.
documents.plot:
Deep Blue Sea 3 is a 2020 American science fiction horror film directed by John Pogue and starring Tania Raymonde, with Nathaniel Buzolic, Emerson Brooks, Bren Foster and Reina Aoi. The third and final instalment of the Deep Blue Sea series and a direct sequel to Deep Blue Sea 2, it follows a marine biologist whose research outpost is threatened by genetically enhanced bull sharks. Warner Bros. Home Entertainment released it direct-to-video on July 28, 2020.

Dr. Emma Collins continues the work of her late father on climate change and great white sharks on Little Happy, a partly submerged artificial island in African waters. She lives there with her small team, Spinnaker, Miya and her father's best friend Eugene Shaw, and with local friends Nandi and her brother Bahari.

Their peace is disrupted when Emma's former boyfriend, Dr. Richard Lowell, arrives on the boat Thasos with a team claiming to be scientists. They are tracking the last three offspring of Bella, the intelligent bull shark behind the disasters of the earlier films, who has been found dead in fishing nets. The bull sharks have already killed three great whites, and soon one of Richard's men is found sliced in half. Emma helps the team sedate and capture the largest of them, but Bahari is later killed by one of the two remaining sharks while fishing.

Richard admits that the sharks are dangerously intelligent and that he has used a beacon from their mother to lure them. The leader of the mercenaries, Lucas, who works for the company Genotic Labs, then seizes command, planning to escape with the captured shark and destroy the island and its inhabitants with a mine. Spying on them with an underwater drone, Emma's team learns of the plan, and a violent battle erupts as the mercenaries blow up parts of the island.

Richard, finally siding with Emma, is killed by a shark as he leaps from the boat to join her. Spinnaker is also killed and Miya is feared dead. Sally, a great white that has befriended Emma, saves her from one of the mercenaries. Emma plants the mine on the Thasos, sinking it when Lucas detonates it, and Shaw sacrifices himself to kill two of the bull sharks. Emma and Nandi kill Lucas, and Emma destroys the last shark in a garbage compactor. As they leave the ruined island, they find Miya alive, and Sally swims off into the ocean.

Deep Blue Sea 3 holds 73% approval on Rotten Tomatoes from a small number of reviews, and Bloody Disgusting called it enjoyable despite its flaws.

documents.title: Primal: Tales of Savagery
documents.overview: Genndy Tartakovsky's Primal: Tales of Savagery features a caveman and a dinosaur on the brink of extinction. Bonded by tragedy, this unlikely friendship becomes the only hope of survival.
documents.plot:
Primal: Tales of Savagery is an adult animated series that delves into the primal and instinctual aspects of human nature, exploring the darker corners of our psyche. The show's narrative is driven by a caveman named Zog, who embarks on a perilous journey through time, encountering various prehistoric creatures and civilizations along the way.

At its core, Primal: Tales of Savagery is a primal exploration of the human condition, examining the raw emotions, desires, and fears that drive us as individuals. The series delves into themes of survival, dominance, and the struggle for power, often blurring the lines between good and evil. Through Zog's journey, the show poses questions about the nature of humanity, our capacity for violence, and the consequences of unchecked primal instincts.

The series also touches on the idea of cultural and societal conditioning, highlighting how our environments and experiences shape us into the individuals we become. As Zog navigates different eras and encounters various cultures, he is forced to confront his own limitations and the harsh realities of the world around him.

Ultimately, Primal: Tales of Savagery presents a visceral and unflinching portrayal of human nature, one that is both captivating and unsettling. By embracing its darker aspects, the series offers a thought-provoking commentary on our shared humanity, inviting viewers to confront their own primal instincts and the complexities of our existence.

documents.title: Hustle
documents.tagline: Are you obsessed with this game?
documents.overview: After discovering a once-in-a-lifetime player with a rocky past abroad, a down on his luck basketball scout takes it upon himself to bring the phenom to the States without his team's approval. Against the odds, they have one final shot to prove they have what it takes to make it in the NBA.
documents.plot:
Hustle is a sports drama film released in 2022, directed by Jody Lee Lipes and produced by Happy Madison Productions. The movie stars Adam Sandler as Stanley Sugarman, a talent scout who discovers an unpolished basketball player with immense potential.

The story begins with Stanley Sugarman (Adam Sandler), a struggling talent scout who has lost his way after being fired from his previous job. He is desperate to revive his career and prove himself once again. One day, while watching a game in the park, he spots an unpolished but talented basketball player named Bo Cruz (Jonathan Majors). Stanley recognizes the potential in Bo and decides to take him under his wing.

As Stanley works with Bo, he realizes that the young man has incredible skills on the court, but lacks the confidence and polish required to succeed at the highest level. Despite this, Stanley is determined to help Bo become a star player. He takes Bo to various gyms and courts around New York City, where they face numerous challenges and setbacks.

Throughout their journey, Stanley and Bo develop an unlikely friendship, with Stanley serving as both a mentor and a father figure to Bo. As Bo's skills improve, he begins to attract attention from top college coaches and NBA scouts. However, Bo struggles with the pressure of living up to his potential, and Stanley must find ways to keep him grounded and focused.

As the story unfolds, we see flashbacks of Stanley's own life, including his troubled childhood and his experiences as a young talent scout. These scenes provide insight into Stanley's motivations and backstory, adding depth to his character.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Bo is offered a chance to play for a top college team, but he must decide whether to take the opportunity or stay with Stanley in New York City. In the end, Bo chooses to pursue his dreams, leaving Stanley heartbroken but proud of the young man he has helped become.

The film concludes with Stanley reflecting on his journey and the lessons he has learned from Bo. Despite facing numerous setbacks and disappointments throughout his career, Stanley remains optimistic and determined to continue helping talented athletes achieve their goals.

Overall, Hustle is a heartwarming and inspiring story about the power of mentorship and perseverance. With Adam Sandler delivering a standout performance as the charismatic but troubled talent scout, the movie is a must-see for sports fans and anyone looking for an uplifting underdog story.

documents.title: Decision to Leave
documents.tagline: The Closer You Look, The Harder You Fall.
documents.overview: From a mountain peak in South Korea, a man plummets to his death. Did he jump, or was he pushed? When detective Hae-joon arrives on the scene, he begins to suspect the dead man’s wife Seo-rae. But as he digs deeper into the investigation, he finds himself trapped in a web of deception and desire.
documents.plot:
Decision to Leave (Heeojil gyeolsim) is a 2022 South Korean neo-noir romantic mystery directed, co-written and produced by Park Chan-wook. Park Hae-il plays the married detective Jang Hae-jun, and Tang Wei plays Song Seo-rae, a Chinese immigrant whose husband's death brings them together.

Hae-jun, an insomniac Busan detective, sees his wife Jung-an, a nuclear plant manager in Ipo, only on weekends. He and his partner Soo-wan investigate the death of Ki Do-soo, a retired immigration officer found at the foot of a mountain he often climbed. Suspicion falls on Seo-rae, Ki's much younger widow and a caregiver for the elderly, because of her apparent lack of grief and the injuries on her body. During nightly stakeouts outside her apartment, Hae-jun becomes infatuated with her, and she notices him. An alibi and CCTV footage seem to clear her. She also reveals that she helped her terminally ill mother die in China, and that she came to Korea to climb a mountain left to her by her grandfather, an independence fighter. When letters suggest Ki killed himself, Hae-jun closes the case, and the two grow close. Then Hae-jun discovers that Seo-rae swapped phones with a client who has dementia, and that the phone's step count reveals she climbed the mountain on the day of the killing. He confronts her, calls himself "shattered", hides the evidence and tells her to throw the phone into the sea.

Thirteen months later, Hae-jun has moved to Ipo, depressed and sleepless, when he runs into Seo-rae with her new husband, Im Ho-shin, who is found dead in his pool the next day. A Chinese immigrant confesses to killing Ho-shin, but Hae-jun eventually realizes that Seo-rae set the killing in motion. Jung-an leaves him. Seo-rae tells him that Ho-shin had found a recording of Hae-jun telling her he loved her and that she began loving him the moment he stopped. She then buries herself in a pit on a beach as the tide rises, leaving behind the phone with Hae-jun's incriminating words. Hae-jun searches the shore in anguish, unaware that she lies beneath the sand.

Shooting began in October 2020. It premiered in competition at the 2022 Cannes Film Festival, where Park won Best Director, and opened in South Korea on June 29, 2022, at number one. Mubi released it in North America and later made it its most-streamed film. It was acclaimed by critics, scoring 85 on Metacritic, and it made the Oscar shortlist as South Korea's entry and received two BAFTA nominations.

documents.title: Lost Bullet
documents.overview: A small time delinquent, turned police mechanic for a go fast task force, is forced to defend his innocence when his mentor is killed by dirty cops.
documents.plot:
Lost Bullet (French: Balle perdue) is a 2020 French action thriller directed by Guillaume Pierret in his feature debut and written by Pierret, Alban Lenoir and Kamel Guemra. Lenoir stars as a mechanic who is framed for murder and must battle corrupt police officers, with Nicolas Duvauchelle, Ramzy Bedia, Stéfi Celma and Rod Paradot in supporting roles.

Lino, a skilled mechanic, builds an armored Renault Clio to ram into a jewelry store and help his foster brother Quentin pay off a debt, but the car smashes through more walls than planned, and Lino is caught and jailed while Quentin escapes. Police detective Charas has Lino released on day leave to modify cars for his drug squad, and eventually secures him a pardon and a garage. When Charas and Lino visit Quentin to ask whether he has been building the traffickers' fast cars, two corrupt squad members, Areski and Marco, shoot Charas dead. Lino flees but is arrested, and when he refuses to lie for Areski, Areski frames him for the killing.

Lino breaks out of the interrogation room and confronts his lover Julia, a member of the squad, who tries and fails to arrest him. Realizing that the burnt car recovered by the police is not Charas's Renault 21, he returns to the junkyard where Charas died, and with Quentin he overpowers the drug runners. Quentin reveals where the Renault, which still holds the fatal bullet from Areski's gun, has been hidden. Julia, persuaded by Quentin's account and other evidence, helps him. At the farm where the Renault is hidden, Marco fatally shoots Quentin, and Lino kills Marco. Areski and his corrupt colleagues try to stop Lino before he reaches police headquarters, but Lino fits the Renault with bull bars, rams through their barricade and, with Julia, fights Areski. Although Areski sets the car on fire, Lino drives it to the garage to put out the flames, forensics recovers the bullet, Areski goes on the run, and Lino is reunited with Julia and rejoins the team.

Netflix released the film worldwide on June 19, 2020, and it became a streaming hit, viewed more than 37 million times in its first month. It received generally favorable reviews, including a Metacritic score of 78, and The Hollywood Reporter called it one of the best French action films in a while, praising Lenoir's stunts. It launched a franchise, with Lost Bullet 2 following in 2022 and Last Bullet in 2025.

documents.title: The Funeral Home
documents.tagline: Dare you visit?
documents.overview: Bernardo is an undertaker. He runs his mortuary business in the same house where he resides. In the front, he has his clients. And in the back, his dysfunctional family lives amongst coffins, wreaths, and the mischievous but nonviolent ghosts that visit on a daily basis. But when a malevolent entity enters the scene, it wreaks havoc on the already fractured household.
documents.plot:
The Funeral Home (Spanish: La funeraria), also known as The Undertaker's Home, is an Argentine horror film written and directed by Mauro Iván Ojeda. Luis Machín, Celeste Gerez and Camila Vaccarini lead the cast, with Hugo Arana, Graciela Bonomi and Susana Varela in supporting roles. It was Arana's last film; the actor died of COVID-19 in October 2020, two months after its festival premiere.

Bernardo, an undertaker, lives with his wife Estela and his stepdaughter Irina in a funeral home that is haunted by restless spirits. Bernardo and Irina both suspect that the strange occurrences might allow them to see loved ones they have lost, but Estela is miserable. She believes her husband is obsessed with the paranormal and quietly resents her because she could not give him a child of his own, and she is convinced that the house has been poisoned by the occult dabbling of Bernardo's late father, Salvador. The tension in the household is so great that Irina has had to give up the ballet she loves.

Bernardo finally calls in a psychic named Ramona to rid the building of its ghosts. Inside, Ramona receives visions that explain the haunting: Estela had manipulated Bernardo into placing his father in a nursing home, and in revenge Salvador summoned a demon to kill her and Irina. He came to regret the pact once he understood that the creature would not stop until his son was dead too, and the spirits he conjured in an effort to hold it back are what now fill the house. Irina comes back from her grandmother's to help with the cleansing, but soon grows terrified and asks her grandmother to collect her. When the old woman arrives she is possessed, and the demon uses her to murder Ramona. Pursued through the house, Irina briefly encounters the ghost of her dead father before the attacks resume, and she discovers the corpses of Estela and Bernardo. Estela briefly stops the possessed grandmother, and Irina takes refuge in a portable toilet. The assault ends at daybreak, when Salvador's bargain expires. The demon leaves Irina a ballet costume, and she puts it on and dances for her family's ghosts.

The film premiered as The Undertaker's Home at the Fantasia festival on 21 August 2020, then opened in a handful of American cinemas in January 2021 before arriving on digital platforms a month later as The Funeral Home. Reviews were positive, with 80% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Fatal Affair
documents.overview: Ellie tries to mend her marriage with her husband Marcus after a brief encounter with an old friend, David, only to find that David is more dangerous and unstable than she'd realized.
documents.plot:
Fatal Affair is a 2020 American psychological thriller directed by Peter Sullivan, who wrote the screenplay with Rasheeda Garner. It stars Nia Long, Omar Epps, Stephen Bishop and KJ Smith, and was produced by Hybrid Films for Netflix, with Long among its producers.

Ellie Warren, an attorney, has moved from San Francisco to a new house on the coast with her husband, Marcus, who is recovering from being struck by a hit-and-run driver while cycling, after their daughter, Brittany, left for college. At work Ellie meets her firm's new technology consultant, David Hammond, whom she has not seen since college twenty years earlier. She does not know that David is in anger management therapy following an incident involving a woman named Deborah. Drinks between them turn sexual in a club bathroom before Ellie stops it. David then begins stalking her with calls and texts, watching and breaking into her house, hacking her security system and dating her friend Courtney, who dismisses Ellie's warnings. Ellie tells neither Marcus nor the police.

From an old classmate, Ellie learns that David was suspected, though never charged, of murdering his ex-wife, Deborah, and her new boyfriend. He deletes an e-mail Ellie sends Courtney about the case, and Ellie is horrified to find him golfing with Marcus. In David's apartment she discovers photos of Deborah and of herself on his computer, and when she warns Courtney, David attacks her friend. With the police hunting him, David fakes his suicide by murdering a homeless man and leaving the burned body in his place, along with a note confessing his crimes. One night a message summons Ellie to the office, where she finds her assistant murdered. Racing home, she calls the police and finds David waiting; she knocks him out with a vase but chooses not to kill him, then discovers the body of Brittany's boyfriend, Scott, and frees Marcus and Brittany. David kills the lone police officer who responds, and as Brittany escapes by car, he fights Ellie and Marcus. Ellie stabs him, and after he seizes the officer's gun, Marcus intervenes and David falls to his death from a seaside cliff. Months later Brittany returns to school, and the Warrens put their new house up for sale.

Netflix released the film on July 16, 2020, and it was the platform's most-streamed film that weekend. Critics panned it, giving it 19% on Rotten Tomatoes and 34 on Metacritic.

documents.title: Alice
documents.tagline: Revenge is long overdue.
documents.overview: Alice spends her days enslaved on a rural Georgia plantation restlessly yearning for freedom. After a violent clash with plantation owner Paul, Alice flees through the neighboring woods and stumbles onto the unfamiliar sight of a highway, soon discovers a shocking reality that lies beyond the tree line.
documents.plot:
Alice is a 2022 American crime thriller written and directed by Krystin Ver Linden in her directorial debut. Loosely drawing on the account of Mae Louise Miller, who escaped from slavery in the 1960s, it follows a woman held in servitude on an isolated Georgia estate who escapes and discovers that the outside world is living in 1973. Keke Palmer stars, with Jonny Lee Miller, Common, Gaius Charles and Alicia Witt.

Alice is one of the "domestics" forced to work on Paul Bennet's plantation, run as though the 19th century had never ended. Bennet resents her love for fellow captive Joseph and plans to marry him off to another woman. When the couple try to flee, Joseph is shot by Bennet's overseer Aaron and seemingly killed, and Alice is tied to a stake on the ground as punishment. She later wounds Bennet and runs through the surrounding forest, emerging onto a highway, where she meets Frank, a truck driver. Frank takes her to a hospital and then to his home, and gradually helps her grasp that it is 1973 and that slavery was abolished long ago. Reading about emancipation and figures such as Malcolm X and Angela Davis, she realises she has been deceived her entire life. She tracks down Bennet's ex-wife Rachel, confirming the truth and convincing Frank of her story, and, inspired by Pam Grier's heroine in Coffy, persuades him to return with her to free the others and take her revenge. Back at the plantation she confronts Bennet, who admits he simply never told his workers they could leave, and sets the place ablaze with a Zippo lighter Joseph had found. She shoots Bennet in the legs and leaves him staked to the ground as he once left her, and is overjoyed to discover that Joseph survived.

Palmer, who also served as an executive producer, plays Alice, with Common as Frank, Miller as Bennet, Charles as Joseph and Witt as Rachel. The film was shot in Savannah, Georgia, beginning in October 2020. It premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 23, 2022, and Roadside Attractions and Vertical Entertainment released it on March 18, taking about $174,000 in its opening weekend. Reviews were mixed, with 29% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics felt its attempt to confront racism fell short, although Palmer's performance was widely praised. It received three NAACP Image Award nominations and a Saturn Award nomination for Best Independent Film.

documents.title: Argentina, 1985
documents.overview: In the 1980s, a team of lawyers takes on the heads of Argentina's bloody military dictatorship in a battle against odds and a race against time.
documents.plot:
Argentina, 1985 is a 2022 historical legal drama produced and directed by Santiago Mitre, who wrote it with Mariano Llinás. It stars Ricardo Darín as prosecutor Julio César Strassera and Peter Lanzani as his deputy, Luis Moreno Ocampo, with Alejandra Flechner as Strassera's wife and Norman Briski. The film recounts the 1985 Trial of the Juntas, in which the leaders of Argentina's military dictatorship were prosecuted for systematic torture, murder and forced disappearances, seen from the perspective of the prosecution team.

Less than two years after the return of democracy, the military courts have refused to try the junta, and the case falls to Strassera, a public prosecutor. The defendants hire senior, experienced lawyers, while Strassera struggles to find anyone willing to join his team. He is at first wary of Moreno Ocampo, whose family has strong military ties, but with no other options he accepts his help. As death threats arrive and a security detail is assigned to him, Moreno Ocampo suggests recruiting young law graduates, since established lawyers are unwilling to risk their careers or safety on such a divisive case.

The young team travels across the country gathering the testimony of victims and their families, racing against time and facing intimidation, while Moreno Ocampo is rejected by his own relatives. On the first day of the trial a bomb threat is received, but Strassera persuades the judges to continue. As survivors take the stand to describe the horrors they endured, the proceedings, filmed and partly broadcast around the world, begin to shift public opinion. Strassera, encouraged by his family, prepares a closing argument addressed not only to the judges but to the whole nation, ending with the famous words "Never again".

The film combines courtroom drama with touches of humor, celebrating the ordinary people who helped bring the dictatorship to justice.

Argentina, 1985 premiered at the Venice Film Festival, where it won the FIPRESCI Prize, and became the most-watched Argentine film of 2022. Acclaimed by critics, with 96 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, it won the Golden Globe for Best Foreign Language Film and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film.

documents.title: Plan A
documents.tagline: The untold story of Jewish revenge.
documents.overview: Germany 1945, Max, a Jewish Holocaust survivor, meets a radical group of Jewish resistance fighters, who, like him, lost all hope for their future after they were robbed of their existence and their entire families were killed by the Nazis. They dream of retaliation on an epic scale for the Jewish people. An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Max starts identifying with the group's monstrous plans...
documents.plot:
Plan A is a 2021 historical thriller written and directed by the Israeli brothers Yoav and Doron Paz. Based on historian Dina Porat's book Vengeance and Retribution Are Mine, it dramatises the real postwar conspiracy of Nakam, a group of Jewish Holocaust survivors led by Abba Kovner, who planned to kill six million Germans by poisoning the water supplies of major cities, starting with Nuremberg. August Diehl stars, with Sylvia Hoeks and Michael Aloni.

In occupied Germany in 1945, Max, a gaunt survivor of the death camps, walks back to his home town in search of his missing wife and son, only to find a former neighbour living in his house, who pulls a gun on him and makes clear that the end of the war has not ended the killing of Jews. Max eventually reaches a camp where survivors are being processed for passage to Palestine and falls in with a unit of the Jewish Brigade, the British army formation whose soldiers are covertly hunting down Nazis and collaborators. Confronted by a soldier who asks why the camp inmates never fought back, he is drawn into their world. The brigade's commander, Michael, persuades him to infiltrate Nakam, which is suspected of preparing a major attack in Nuremberg that could jeopardise hopes for a Jewish state. Among Nakam's members, including Ana, Max finds people who share his grief and rage and who argue that the murder of six million Jews can be answered only by six million German deaths. Taking a job connected to the city's water system, he copies a blueprint of the network, becoming both an insider in the plot and an informant, and is increasingly torn between two visions of justice: a new life in Palestine or indiscriminate retribution. The plan begins to collapse when Kovner, unable to obtain poison in Europe, travels to Palestine to find it; on his return voyage aboard a British ship he is arrested and throws the poison into the sea, leaving the conspiracy without the means to carry out its attack.

Diehl plays Max, with Hoeks as Ana, Aloni as Michael and Ishai Golan as Kovner, alongside Nikolai Kinski and Oz Zehavi. The film was shot in Germany, Israel and Ukraine and is largely in English. Signature Entertainment released it in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand from September 2021. Reviews were mixed: The Guardian's Cath Clarke gave it two stars out of five, finding it handsome and decently acted but too neatly packaged and lacking in tension.

documents.title: Emancipation
documents.overview: Inspired by the gripping true story of a man who would do anything for his family—and for freedom. When Peter, an enslaved man, risks his life to escape and return to his family, he embarks on a perilous journey of love and endurance.
documents.plot:
Emancipation is a historical drama film directed by Antoine Fuqua, released in 2022 under the production company Escape Artists. The movie is based on the true story of Whistle Stop, a former slave who escapes from his plantation owner, Edwin Epps (played by Ben Foster), and embarks on a perilous journey to freedom.

The film follows the story of Whistle Stop (played by Will Smith), a young enslaved man who is brutally treated by his master, Edwin Epps. Despite being given the nickname "Whistle Stop" due to his habit of whistling while working, Whistle Stop is subjected to physical and emotional abuse at the hands of Epps.

One day, Whistle Stop decides that he has had enough of his life as a slave and sets out on an escape plan. He begins by befriending a fellow slave named Tibeats (played by Raymond J. Barry), who helps him prepare for his journey to freedom.

As Whistle Stop makes his way through the treacherous terrain, he faces numerous challenges, including harsh weather conditions, treacherous terrain, and encounters with hostile slave catchers. Despite these obstacles, Whistle Stop perseveres, driven by his determination to be free.

Throughout his journey, Whistle Stop also grapples with the moral implications of his actions. He is forced to confront the harsh realities of slavery and the consequences of his own survival. The film explores themes of freedom, identity, and the human spirit's capacity for resilience in the face of oppression.

The movie features powerful performances from Will Smith and Ben Foster, who bring depth and nuance to their characters. The cinematography is also noteworthy, capturing the stark beauty of the American South during the 19th century.

Overall, Emancipation is a powerful and moving film that sheds light on a pivotal moment in American history. It is a testament to the enduring power of the human spirit and a reminder of the ongoing struggle for freedom and equality.

documents.title: Black Box
documents.tagline: There is no escape from who you really are.
documents.overview: After losing his wife and his memory in a car accident, a single father undergoes an experimental treatment that causes him to question who he really is.
documents.plot: After losing his wife and his memory in a car accident, a single father undergoes an experimental treatment that causes him to question who he really is.

documents.title: Mr. Malcolm's List
documents.tagline: Seeking true love. Conditionally.
documents.overview: When she fails to meet an item on his list of requirements for a bride, Julia Thistlewaite is jilted by London’s most eligible bachelor, Mr. Malcolm. Feeling humiliated and determined to exact revenge, she convinces her friend Selina Dalton to play the role of his ideal match. Soon, Mr. Malcolm wonders whether he’s found the perfect woman...or the perfect hoax.
documents.plot:
Mr. Malcolm's List is a romantic comedy-drama film that explores themes of love, self-discovery, and empowerment. The movie follows the story of Poppy, a young woman who creates a list of qualities she wants in a partner, only to find herself on a journey of self-discovery as she navigates her relationships.

At its core, Mr. Malcolm's List is a film about embracing individuality and not settling for someone who doesn't truly understand and appreciate you. Poppy's list serves as a catalyst for her growth, forcing her to confront her own desires and values. Through her experiences, the movie highlights the importance of self-awareness, confidence, and authenticity in relationships.

The film also touches on themes of feminism and female empowerment, showcasing Poppy's journey from being a passive observer to becoming an active participant in shaping her own destiny. As Poppy navigates her relationships, she learns to prioritize her own needs and desires, ultimately finding love on her own terms.

Furthermore, Mr. Malcolm's List explores the complexities of human connection and intimacy, delving into the nuances of emotional vulnerability and trust. The movie suggests that true love requires a deep understanding of oneself and one's values, as well as a willingness to be open and honest with one's partner.

Overall, Mr. Malcolm's List is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates individuality, self-discovery, and the power of female empowerment.

documents.title: Spencer
documents.tagline: Every fairy tale ends.
documents.overview: During her Christmas holidays with the royal family at the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, England, Diana decides to leave her marriage to Prince Charles.
documents.plot: During her Christmas holidays with the royal family at the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, England, Diana decides to leave her marriage to Prince Charles.

documents.title: What Lies Below
documents.tagline: Fear comes to the surface.
documents.overview: Liberty, a socially awkward 16-year-old, returns from two months at camp to a blindsided introduction of her mother’s fiancé, John Smith, whose charm, intelligence, and beauty paint the picture of a man too perfect to be human.
documents.plot:
What Lies Below is a 2020 American horror film written and directed by Braden R. Duemmler. Ema Horvath stars as Liberty "Libby" Wells, with Mena Suvari as her mother, Michelle, Trey Tucker as Michelle's boyfriend, John Smith, and Haskiri Velazquez as Libby's friend Marley.

Sixteen-year-old Libby returns from summer camp to her family's lake house, where her mother, a romance novelist, introduces her to her new boyfriend, John, an aquatic geneticist who says his work helps creatures adapt to changing environments. He gives Libby a bracelet bearing symbols of a fertility goddess. That night Libby overhears loud lovemaking, then pretends to sleep as John stands watching in her doorway. Michelle falls ill and announces that she has accepted John's marriage proposal, while Libby learns that John studies parasites. John's behavior toward her grows increasingly invasive: he touches her while cleaning up her menstrual blood and sneaks into the bathroom while she showers. Removing the bracelet, Libby finds a red mark on her wrist, and she invites Marley to stay.

That night Libby sees John wade into the lake, which glows red, yet soon appears dry, claiming to sleepwalk. Michelle begins vomiting and sends Libby to town for medicine and a pregnancy test. When Libby tells Marley that John groped her and Michelle announces she is pregnant, Michelle accuses her daughter of lying. Noticing that John has a nictitating membrane, Libby tries to pull her mother away, and Michelle slaps her. In the basement, Libby finds symbols on her own wrist matching those on the walls and discovers Michelle in a water tank hooked to an IV, then watches from hiding as her mother gives birth to a dying creature. After calling the police, she finds Marley's body being devoured by parasites in another tank. John overpowers Libby as she tries to flee with Michelle, and she wakes bound as several identical copies of John peel back the walls to reveal many unconscious women in tanks. John forces her to swallow a glowing substance he regurgitates, and Libby awakens in a tank among women seemingly in pupal states; as water fills it, she panics, then smiles, able to breathe underwater.

Cath Clarke of The Guardian gave the film one star out of five, writing that its baffling erotic plot was less damaging than its wooden acting and poor judgment. Screen Rant's Jack Wilhelmi rated it three out of five, praising Horvath and Suvari while finding the rest of the film derivative.

documents.title: Ferry
documents.overview: Before he built a drug empire, Ferry Bouman returns to his hometown on a revenge mission that finds his loyalty tested — and a love that alters his life.
documents.plot: Before he built a drug empire, Ferry Bouman returns to his hometown on a revenge mission that finds his loyalty tested — and a love that alters his life.

documents.title: Girl
documents.overview: A young woman returns to her small hometown intent on killing her abusive father only to discover someone murdered him the day before. As the girl searches for answers, she uncovers a family legacy more dangerous than she'd imagined.
documents.plot:
Girl is a 2020 Canadian-American thriller written and directed by Chad Faust, who also appears in the film. Bella Thorne stars as a young woman known only as Girl, who returns to her hometown intending to kill her abusive father, with Mickey Rourke as the town's sheriff, Elizabeth Saunders, Lanette Ware and Glen Gould. Shot in 2019 in Sudbury, Ontario, it was released in December 2020.

Girl travels by bus back to the small, decaying town of Golden, carrying her father's hatchet, with the intention of killing him. Before arriving, she calls her mother, who reveals that her father has sent a letter threatening to kill her; Girl asks for the return address, but her mother refuses to give it. Walking into town from the highway, Girl turns down a ride from the local sheriff and stops at a bar, where she finds her father's address in a phone book and has a tense encounter with a woman named Betty.

When she reaches her father's house, she discovers that someone has already murdered him. Her attempt to report the killing gets nowhere, and when she calls her mother, she vows to find out who is responsible, although her mother urges her to come home. At a laundromat she meets a man who calls himself Charmer, and after initial wariness she begins to flirt with him, telling him how her father taught her to throw hatchets expertly when she was a child. However, Charmer soon reveals himself to be dangerous, and Girl realizes that her father's death is connected to a wider web of secrets in the town. As she digs deeper, she finds that the people of Golden know more about her father and his death than they admit, and that her family's past is bound up with violence. Using her skill with the hatchet and her determination, Girl must fight to survive and uncover the truth about her father, her mother and the town.

Girl received mixed reviews, with a 59 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that despite Thorne's impressive work in the title role, it struggled to distinguish itself from other female-led revenge thrillers. Critics noted its bleak, atmospheric setting and its deliberately minimalist approach.

documents.title: Jeepers Creepers: Reborn
documents.tagline: Evil's Back. For More.
documents.overview: Forced to travel with her boyfriend to a horror festival, Laine begins to experience disturbing visions associated with the urban legend of The Creeper. As the festival arrives and the blood-soaked entertainment builds to a frenzy, she becomes the center of it while something unearthly has been summoned.
documents.plot:
Jeepers Creepers: Reborn is a 2022 American horror film directed by David Armitage and written by Armitage. The movie serves as a sequel to the original Jeepers Creepers (2001) and its sequel, Jeepers Creepies 3 (2017).

The story follows Darry Jenner (Christian James), a young man who is haunted by his family's dark past. His grandfather, Darry's father, was killed by the Creeper, a monstrous creature that feeds on human flesh. The Creeper has been awakened and is now terrorizing a small town in Georgia.

As the body count rises, Darry teams up with a group of friends to uncover the truth behind his family's connection to the Creeper. They soon discover that the creature is not just a mindless beast but a vessel for an ancient evil that has been awakened by human greed and disrespect for nature.

Throughout the film, Darry delves deeper into his family's history, learning about the dark secrets they kept hidden and the true nature of the Creeper. He also discovers that he himself may be connected to the creature, making him a potential target.

The movie takes a darker tone than its predecessors, exploring themes of trauma, grief, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's climax features a gruesome showdown between Darry and the Creeper, which will leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, Jeepers Creepers: Reborn is a tense, unsettling horror film that delivers on its promise of gore and terror. While it may not be as iconic as the original, it provides a satisfying conclusion to the series for fans who have been waiting for more.

documents.title: Licorice Pizza
documents.overview: The story of Alana Kane and Gary Valentine running around and falling in love in the San Fernando Valley, 1973.
documents.plot:
Licorice Pizza is a 2021 American coming-of-age comedy-drama film written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson. The movie takes place in the early 1970s, specifically in the San Fernando Valley region of Los Angeles.

The story revolves around Gary Valentine (played by Cooper Hoffman), a charismatic but awkward teenager who runs his family's struggling pizza parlor, Gary's Pizza. Gary is a bit of an outsider among his peers and struggles to find his place in the world. He becomes infatuated with Alana Haines (played by Alana Haim), a beautiful and popular high school student who is also the daughter of a wealthy businessman.

As Gary navigates his relationships, he befriends Alana's brother, Mason (played by Sean Penn), a charismatic but troubled musician who becomes a mentor to Gary. Through Mason, Gary gains insight into the world of rock music and begins to develop his own sense of identity.

Meanwhile, Gary also catches the eye of Alana's mother, Susan (played by Maya Rudolph), who is struggling to balance her career ambitions with her family life. As Gary and Alana grow closer, they must navigate the complexities of their social differences and confront the challenges of growing up in a rapidly changing world.

Throughout the film, Anderson explores themes of identity, class, and the struggles of adolescence. The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Benny Safdie as Gary's friend and confidant, and Tom Waits as Alana's father, who is struggling to come to terms with his own mortality.

The title "Licorice Pizza" refers to the iconic San Fernando Valley pizza parlor that serves as the backdrop for much of the film. The movie's use of period-specific music, fashion, and cultural references adds to its nostalgic charm and helps to transport viewers back to the early 1970s.

Ultimately, Licorice Pizza is a poignant and humorous exploration of the complexities of growing up in America during a time of great social change. Through Gary's journey, Anderson offers a nuanced and empathetic portrayal of adolescence, capturing the struggles, triumphs, and awkwardness that define this pivotal stage of life.

documents.title: Rogue
documents.tagline: When the hunter becomes the prey.
documents.overview: Battle-hardened O’Hara leads a lively mercenary team of soldiers on a daring mission: rescue hostages from their captors in remote Africa. But as the mission goes awry and the team is stranded, O’Hara’s squad must face a bloody, brutal encounter with a gang of rebels.
documents.plot: Battle-hardened O’Hara leads a lively mercenary team of soldiers on a daring mission: rescue hostages from their captors in remote Africa. But as the mission goes awry and the team is stranded, O’Hara’s squad must face a bloody, brutal encounter with a gang of rebels.

documents.title: Bruised
documents.tagline: It's not a second chance. It's a last chance.
documents.overview: Jackie Justice is a mixed martial arts fighter who leaves the sport in disgrace. Down on her luck and simmering with rage and regret years after the fight, she's coaxed into a brutal underground fight by her manager and boyfriend Desi and grabs the attention of a fight league promoter who promises Jackie a life back in the Octagon. But the road to redemption becomes unexpectedly personal when Manny - the son she gave up as an infant - shows up at her doorstep. A triumphant story of a fighter who reclaims her power, in and out of the ring, when everyone has counted her out
documents.plot:
Bruised is a 2021 American action-drama film written and directed by Halle Berry. The movie follows the story of Jackie Justice, a former MMA fighter who seeks redemption after a tragic accident in her past.

At its core, Bruised explores themes of trauma, grief, and the complexities of female empowerment. Jackie's journey is marked by a deep-seated need for control and a desperate attempt to reclaim her sense of identity and purpose. As she navigates the dark underbelly of the MMA world, she must confront the painful memories of her past and the ways in which they have shaped her into the person she is today.

Throughout the film, Berry delves into the idea that trauma can be both a source of strength and a crippling burden. Jackie's experiences have left her with physical and emotional scars, but it is through her struggles that she begins to find a sense of purpose and belonging. The movie also touches on the theme of female solidarity and the ways in which women can support and uplift each other in the face of adversity.

One of the most striking aspects of Bruised is its portrayal of the complexities of female rage and the ways in which it can be both a source of power and a destructive force. Jackie's character is multifaceted and nuanced, embodying both vulnerability and ferocity. As she navigates her journey, Berry masterfully captures the intensity and emotionality of this inner conflict, creating a deeply human and relatable character.

Ultimately, Bruised is a powerful exploration of the human condition, one that delves into the darkest corners of the human experience and emerges with a message of hope and resilience.

documents.title: Lightyear
documents.tagline: Infinity awaits.
documents.overview: Legendary Space Ranger Buzz Lightyear embarks on an intergalactic adventure alongside a group of ambitious recruits and his robot companion Sox.
documents.plot:
Lightyear is a 2022 science fiction adventure film directed by Angus MacLane, produced by Pete Docter, David Silverman, Kira Naylor, and others. The movie serves as a spin-off to the Toy Story franchise.

The story follows Buzz Lightyear (voiced by Chris Evans), a space ranger who has been presumed dead for 800 years. According to his legend, he was last seen battling Emperor Zurg's forces in a distant galaxy. However, it is revealed that Buzz actually crash-landed on a planet called Axiom, where he encountered a group of alien creatures known as the "Star Command" recruits.

The main character, Buzz Lightyear, is not the same space ranger from his legend but rather an alternate version who was created by Star Command to be a prototype for their new line of space rangers. He is sent on a mission to explore the galaxy and gather data about the evil Emperor Zurg's plans.

As Buzz navigates this new reality, he meets a young girl named Ivy (voiced by Keke Palmer), who becomes his companion and friend. Together, they embark on an adventure to stop Emperor Zurg from taking over the galaxy.

Throughout the film, Buzz struggles with his identity and purpose, as he grapples with the fact that he is not the legendary space ranger he thought he was. He also faces challenges from within Star Command, who are skeptical of his abilities and question his loyalty.

The movie features stunning visuals, impressive action sequences, and a heartwarming story about self-discovery and friendship. The film's themes of identity, purpose, and belonging are timely and relatable, making it an enjoyable watch for both children and adults.

Overall, Lightyear is a thrilling adventure that explores the origins of Buzz Lightyear and his journey to becoming the iconic space ranger we know and love from Toy Story.

documents.title: Mothering Sunday
documents.overview: On a warm spring day in 1924, house maid and foundling Jane Fairchild finds herself alone on Mother's Day. Her employers, Mr. and Mrs. Niven, are out and she has the rare chance to spend quality time with her secret lover. Paul is the boy from the manor house nearby, Jane's long-term love despite the fact that he's engaged to be married to another woman, a childhood friend and daughter of his parents' friends. But events that neither can foresee will change the course of Jane's life forever.
documents.plot:
Mothering Sunday is a 2021 British drama film directed by Evangeline Lilly, based on the novel of the same name by Graham Moore.

The movie revolves around the complex and intricate relationships between characters, particularly those centered around grief, love, and identity. The story explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human need for connection in a world that often feels overwhelming and chaotic.

At its core, Mothering Sunday is a poignant exploration of the fragility of human emotions and the ways in which we cope with loss and heartbreak. Through the eyes of the protagonist, Mrs. Selwyn, the film delves into the intricacies of grief, revealing the ways in which it can both consume and transform us.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, class, and social status, highlighting the tensions between old money and new, as well as the constraints placed on women by societal expectations. However, these themes are woven together with a deep sense of empathy and understanding, creating a narrative that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

Ultimately, Mothering Sunday is a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on their own relationships, emotions, and desires. The film's nuanced portrayal of complex characters and its thoughtful examination of universal themes make it a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant viewing experience.

documents.title: A Nice Girl Like You
documents.tagline: Naughty can be nice
documents.overview: Lucy Neal is thrown for a loop when she is accused of being too inhibited by her ex-boyfriend. In an effort to prove him wrong, Lucy creates a rather wild to-do list that sends her on a whirlwind and surprising journey of self-discovery, friendship, and new love.
documents.plot: Lucy Neal is thrown for a loop when she is accused of being too inhibited by her ex-boyfriend. In an effort to prove him wrong, Lucy creates a rather wild to-do list that sends her on a whirlwind and surprising journey of self-discovery, friendship, and new love.

documents.title: The Larva Island Movie
documents.overview: Back at home, Chuck relates the island shenanigans of his larva pals Red and Yellow to a skeptical reporter in this movie sequel to the hit cartoon.
documents.plot:
The Larva Island Movie is a 2020 South Korean computer-animated comedy film based on Larva Island, the spin-off of the animated series Larva produced by the studio TUBA n. Directed by Ahn Byoung-wook, it features the voices of Hong Beom-gi and Kang Shin-hyung as the larvae and Eddy Lee as Chuck, with Ahn Hyo-min, Kim Yeon-woo, Choi Nak-yoon, Tom Wayland and Erica Schroeder. Netflix billed the 89-minute film as a sequel to the show, and it was released on the service on 23 July 2020 with a TV-Y7 rating.

The original Larva shorts followed the urban misadventures of two grubs, the small, short-tempered Red and his bigger, dimmer best friend Yellow, neither of whom speaks a human language. Larva Island moved them to a tiny deserted island shared with Chuck, a shipwreck survivor. In the movie, Chuck is back home in New York City, where he nearly steps on a dung beetle but spares it because of the friends he once had among such creatures. Over a meal at a restaurant, he recounts his outlandish survival story to Grace, a reporter who wants to publish it, though he worries that nobody will believe him. His recollections trigger flashbacks to his time on the island: hunger and loneliness, repeated failures to build boats and rafts, storms, freezing cold, scorching heat, typhoons, a volcanic eruption and icebergs. He tells of how he survived thanks to Red and Yellow, whose antics included Red's rivalry for the affection of a female larva and Yellow's endless flatulence, and of other island companions such as Clara, a trained seal who washed ashore, and a tiny alien who took over the body of a crab to become a robotic "Crabsformer". Gradually, the whole restaurant becomes captivated by his stories, and the film adds a sentimental coda to Chuck's arc.

Much of the film consists of footage repurposed from episodes of the series, linked by new framing scenes, and critics were unimpressed. John Serba of Decider advised viewers to skip it, calling it a clip show disguised as a sequel whose relentless fart jokes become an endurance test, while conceding that its animation is simple and colorful. Bob Hoose of Plugged In described it as a poor man's Minions aimed at very young children, noting its mild messages about friendship and seeing things from another's point of view.

documents.title: The Deal
documents.tagline: Are you ready to die?
documents.overview: A mother fights to save her ailing daughter after a global pandemic worse than any seen before ravaged the planet, leaving resources so scarce you must pay for them with your life.
documents.plot:
The Deal is a 2022 American dystopian science fiction thriller film directed by Orsi Nagypál. It was created by Sumalee Montano, who also co-produced it and plays one of the lead roles, and was made by Dean Devlin's Electric Entertainment together with actor-producer Lisa Brenner and LinLay Productions, with Balkanic Media also credited. Alongside Montano, the cast includes Emma Fischer, Alastair Mackenzie, Taz Skylar, Lisa Brenner and Pearl Mackie. The film, which runs about 91 minutes, was released in the autumn of 2022 as an exclusive on The Roku Channel; in Germany it was distributed as The Deal – Der verwüstete Planet.

The story is set in a future devastated by a global pandemic worse than any before it and by climate change, where overpopulation and global warming have left resources desperately scarce and food shortages afflict the survivors. A totalitarian government known as the Bureau has introduced the "Deal" as its answer to the crisis: anyone who accepts it by their twentieth birthday is guaranteed work, shelter and everything they need to survive, but only for twenty more years, after which they are put to death to make room for others. Tala Bayani (Montano), a mother who took the Deal, is approaching the end of her term before she has managed to secure the survival of her daughter Analyn (Fischer), who suffers from kidney disease. With her time running out, Tala begins to fight back against the regime to save her child, and the two women find themselves trapped and racing to find a way out.

In an interview with the magazine Positively Filipino, Montano said that she modelled Tala on her own Filipina mother, Linda Montano, and the sacrifices she made in raising her as a single parent; the article described the mother-daughter relationship as the emotional centre of the film, taking precedence over its computer-generated cityscapes. Reviewing it for Week99er, Becky found that the premise of a pandemic followed by food shortages felt uncomfortably close to contemporary reality, but said the film held the attention with an interesting story and a couple of unexpected twists, and was relieved that its ending was less dark than she had anticipated, though some threads were left open. The German film magazine Filmdienst was less impressed, judging that the film failed to exploit the dramatic potential of its premise and settled into a thriller plot rendered rather pale, partly because of its low budget.

documents.title: Bullet Train
documents.tagline: The end of the line is just the beginning.
documents.overview: Unlucky assassin Ladybug is determined to do his job peacefully after one too many gigs gone off the rails. Fate, however, may have other plans, as Ladybug's latest mission puts him on a collision course with lethal adversaries from around the globe—all with connected, yet conflicting, objectives—on the world's fastest train.
documents.plot:
Bullet Train is an action-thriller film directed by David Leitch, released in 2022 under Columbia Pictures. The movie follows the story of Ladybug (played by Brad Pitt), a skilled assassin working for an international crime syndicate.

The plot revolves around Ladybug's mission to retrieve a briefcase containing $40 million from a high-speed train traveling across Japan. However, things take a turn when Ladybug discovers that he is not the only one on the train with his sights set on the briefcase.

As Ladybug navigates through the crowded train, he encounters other assassins, including Lemon (played by Brian Tyree Henry), Tangerine (played by Aaron Taylor-Johnson), and Hornet (played by Joey King). Each of these characters has their own agenda, making it difficult for Ladybug to determine who is friend or foe.

Throughout the film, Ladybug engages in a series of intense battles with his fellow assassins, showcasing his exceptional fighting skills. As the train hurtles through Japan's countryside, Ladybug must use his wits and cunning to outmaneuver his opponents and stay one step ahead of the game.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that each assassin has their own personal vendetta against someone on the train, adding an element of complexity to the plot. The film's pacing is fast-paced and action-packed, with a series of thrilling set pieces that keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

One of the standout aspects of Bullet Train is its ensemble cast, which brings together a diverse range of characters with unique personalities and motivations. The chemistry between the actors is palpable, making it easy to become invested in their respective storylines.

Overall, Bullet Train is an adrenaline-fueled thrill ride that will keep viewers entertained from start to finish. With its breakneck pace, witty dialogue, and impressive action sequences, this film is a must-see for fans of the action-thriller genre.

documents.title: Butchers
documents.tagline: Rest in pieces
documents.overview: A family of sadistic butchers lives deep inside the backcountry. From the dead of winter to the dog days of summer, anyone who crosses their path is dead meat.
documents.plot:
Butchers is a 2020 Canadian slasher film directed by Adrian Langley, who co-wrote it with Daniel Weissenberger. Simon Phillips and Michael Swatton star as Owen and Oswald Watson, two sadistic brothers living in the backcountry, with Julie Mainville, Anne-Carolyne Binette, James Hicks, Frederik Storm and Samantha De Benedet. Filmed in Ontario, it was released in select theaters and on demand in January 2021. The film features the 1919 recording of "A Good Man Is Hard to Find" by Marion Harris.

Divided into three chapters, titled "The Beginning of the End," "The Middle of Nowhere" and "The End Is Here," the film opens in the dead of winter, as Owen and Oswald bury their mother on the grounds of their remote home in rural North Dakota. As they finish, they notice that a car carrying a young couple, Steven and Celeste, has broken down on the nearby country road. Owen's chillingly casual reaction makes it clear that the brothers view the stranded travelers as a stroke of luck, and the couple fall into their hands.

The story then jumps forward to the height of summer. The Watsons have kept Celeste captive, abusing her and making her pregnant, and she has been reduced to a state of helpless despair. On the same lonely road, another car breaks down, carrying four friends: Jenna, Taylor, Mike and Chris. With no phone signal and no help in sight, they split up to look for assistance, and soon find their way to the Watson property, where the brothers run a makeshift slaughterhouse in which anyone who crosses their path is treated as meat. Captured and terrorized, the young people must fight to survive the brothers' twisted games, while Celeste's presence raises the question of whether anyone can escape the farm alive.

Butchers received mixed reviews. Martin Unsworth of Starburst gave it three stars out of five, calling it an unoriginal but fun watch for viewers with strong stomachs, and Chris Cummings of Nerdly rated it two and a half stars, finding it enjoyable if not groundbreaking. Phuong Le of The Guardian gave it two stars, describing it as relying on worn-out horror tropes. Critics widely praised Phillips and Swatton's menacing performances as the brothers, while finding the victims thinly written.

documents.title: The Walking Dead: The Journey So Far
documents.original_title: The Walking Dead: The Journey So Far
documents.overview: This two-hour retrospective in which the entire cast will tell the stories of their characters from the moment they were introduced through to where they were left at the end of the last episode of season 7. Beautifully shot interviews of the cast and the EPs are punctuated by clips of the most crucial moments in the series.  If someone has never seen a moment of The Walking Dead before, this special will catch them up on the plot, characters, locations, and unique terminology of the series leading up to season 8.
documents.plot:
The Walking Dead: The Journey So Far is a 2016 American documentary retrospective special produced by AMC Studios, with international distribution through Fox International Channels, about AMC's post-apocalyptic horror drama The Walking Dead, the television series developed by Frank Darabont from the comic books by Robert Kirkman, Tony Moore and Charlie Adlard. It was broadcast by AMC in a two-hour slot on Sunday, 16 October 2016, one week before the premiere of the show's seventh season on 23 October, with the program itself running about 96 minutes.

Built from newly filmed interviews with the cast and the series' executive producers, intercut with clips from the most pivotal moments of the first six seasons, the special has the actors tell the stories of their own characters from the moment each was introduced to where they stood at the end of the previous season. The story is retold season by season, beginning with the moment sheriff's deputy Rick Grimes, played by Andrew Lincoln, wakes from a coma in a Georgia hospital to find the world overrun by flesh-eating walkers, and searches for his wife Lori, his son Carl and his partner Shane. The retrospective then traces the group's path through the Atlanta camp and the Centers for Disease Control, Hershel Greene's farm and the fatal rivalry between Rick and Shane, the fortified prison and the war with the Governor of Woodbury, the scattering of the survivors and the trap of Terminus, and the move to the walled Virginia community of Alexandria. It ends with the conflict with the Saviors and their leader Negan, culminating in the first brutal swing of Negan's bat in the sixth-season finale, recounted by Jeffrey Dean Morgan and other members of the cast. The special was designed both to give viewers who had never seen an episode a chance to catch up on the plot, characters, locations and unique terminology of the series, and to offer devoted fans a refresher course before the new season.

The Walking Dead was then AMC's flagship series and a ratings phenomenon, executive produced by Kirkman, showrunner Scott M. Gimple, Gale Anne Hurd, David Alpert, Greg Nicotero and Tom Luse. The special served as the lead-in to a seventh season in which the survivors, fractured and bereaved after Negan's brutal example, would be forced to live under his rule.

documents.title: One Night in Bangkok
documents.tagline: Six Hours. Five Hits. Who Will Survive?
documents.overview: A hit man named Kai flies into Bangkok, gets a gun, and orders a cab. He offers a professional female driver big money to be his all-night driver. But when she realizes Kai is committing brutal murders at each stop, it's too late to walk away. Meanwhile, an offbeat police detective races to decode the string of slayings before more blood is spilled.
documents.plot:
One Night in Bangkok is a 2020 American action thriller film written and directed by Wych Kaosayananda, starring Mark Dacascos as a hitman on a night of revenge, with Vanida Golten, Michael S. New, Kane Kosugi and Sahajak Boonthanakit. Released by Grindstone Entertainment Group, it was issued in the United States directly on DVD and digital download on 25 August 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Kai Kahale (Dacascos), a middle-aged Hawaiian former soldier, flies into Bangkok and orders a cab through an app. The driver is Fha (Golten), a young Anglo-Thai woman, and he offers her 6,000 dollars to drive him around the city all night without asking questions. His first stop is a law firm, where he shoots a lawyer in her office; the second is the apartment of a police officer, whom he kills with the words "This is for Lisa." As the bodies are discovered, an offbeat detective begins piecing together the string of killings. Over food at a roadside stall, Kai tells Fha that his daughter, her husband and their little girl died in a crash in Thailand and that he wants to meet everyone involved; shaken, Fha confesses that she too was involved in an accident in which a child died. After shooting a young man at a nightclub for destroying a family with his Porsche, Kai admits that he knows the car in the crash was hers and that he chose her as his driver on purpose, but that he will not kill her, preferring to let her live with her guilt.
