At a hospital he kills the wealthy gallery owner Davies (Boonthanakit), who had bribed the police to falsify reports and protect his son, along with his wife, bodyguard and son, and is wounded escaping in a doctor's disguise. Fha admits that she lied about the accident out of fear of the boy's father and used the money she received to pay for her sick brother's treatment. Kai offers her his bitcoins should he not return from his final target, a Japanese fixer with underworld ties (Kosugi). After defeating the fixer's men, a weakened Kai loses their hand-to-hand fight, but the detective arrives in time to shoot the fixer, and Kai insists that Fha was his hostage, not his accomplice. As she drives him to hospital, he loses consciousness.

Critics compared the film to Collateral and the John Wick series, and it holds a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Francesco Ceccamea of the Italian magazine Nocturno reviewed it favourably, calling Dacascos's lead role the most incisive of his career.

documents.title: Songbird
documents.tagline: The only way out is together.
documents.overview: During a pandemic lockdown, Nico, a young man with rare immunity, must overcome martial law, murderous vigilantes and a powerful family to reunite with his love, Sara.
documents.plot:
Songbird is a 2020 American dystopian science fiction thriller inspired by the COVID-19 pandemic, directed by Adam Mason from a screenplay he wrote with Simon Boyes and produced by Michael Bay among others. KJ Apa and Sofia Carson lead an ensemble that includes Craig Robinson, Bradley Whitford, Peter Stormare, Alexandra Daddario, Paul Walter Hauser and Demi Moore.

In 2024 the coronavirus has mutated into COVID-23 and the world is in its fourth year of quarantine. The United States has become an authoritarian police state where citizens must take daily temperature checks on their phones, and the infected are forcibly removed from their homes to quarantine camps known as Q-Zones. Nico Price, a motorbike courier who is immune after surviving the virus, is in a virtual relationship, with no physical contact allowed, with Sara Garcia, a young artist who lives with her grandmother Lita. Nico works for Lester, whose courier firm serves wealthy clients such as Piper and William Griffin, a couple quietly dealing in illegal immunity wristbands. William is having an affair with May, a singer who performs online, and May forms a bond with Michael Dozer, a disabled veteran who operates surveillance drones for Lester.

When Lita falls ill and fails her temperature check, Nico vows to keep Sara from being taken. He seeks a wristband for her, but a lead from the Griffins turns out to be a trap set by Emmett Harland, the ruthless head of the "sanitation" department. Lita dies, and Sara escapes her building in a stolen hazmat suit before Emmett catches her, notes that she has shown no symptoms despite her exposure, and has her detained.

Meanwhile, Piper throws William out after learning of his affair, and when he tries to kill May to keep her quiet, Michael shoots him with an armed drone. Piper finally gives Nico a wristband. Back at Sara's building Nico kills Emmett in self-defence, and with help from Lester and Michael he races to the Q-Zone, slipping the bracelet onto Sara just before she is scanned. As they embrace for the first time, she tells him she is immune too.

Released on premium video-on-demand by STX Entertainment on December 11, 2020, the film was heavily criticised, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 9% approval and calling it muddled, tedious and uninspired.

documents.title: Happy Halloween, Scooby-Doo!
documents.tagline: Scooby-Doo and Shaggy’s favorite holiday is upon us!
documents.overview: Scooby-Doo and the gang team up with their pals, Bill Nye The Science Guy and Elvira Mistress of the Dark, to solve this mystery of gigantic proportions and save Crystal Cove!
documents.plot:
Happy Halloween, Scooby-Doo! is a 2020 animated mystery film that serves as a reboot of the classic franchise. The movie follows the Mystery Inc. gang - Fred Jones, Daphne Blake, Velma Dinkley, Shaggy Rogers, and Scooby-Doo - as they embark on a new adventure.

The story begins with the gang attending a Halloween party at the Creepy Carnival, a traveling amusement park that has been revived after being closed for years. The carnival is owned by Mr. Jenkins (voiced by Rob Paulsen), who claims to have found a way to bring back the spirits of his deceased wife and daughter.

However, things take a dark turn when the gang discovers that the carnival's new owner, Mr. Jenkins' nephew, has been using the park as a front for a sinister plot. The nephew, along with his accomplices, is attempting to summon an ancient evil spirit known as "The Carnival King" using a magical artifact.

As the gang delves deeper into the mystery, they uncover a series of clues and puzzles that lead them on a wild goose chase through the carnival. Along the way, they encounter various suspects, including Mr. Jenkins' rival, who is trying to sabotage the carnival's reopening.

Throughout the movie, the gang uses their signature skills to solve the mystery, with Velma using her research skills, Daphne using her fashion sense to gather clues, and Shaggy and Scooby using their... um, unique abilities to sniff out leads. Fred, as usual, takes charge of the group's efforts.

As the story unfolds, the gang discovers that the Carnival King is a vengeful spirit who was wronged by Mr. Jenkins' family in the past. The spirit is seeking revenge on the living and will stop at nothing to claim the carnival as its own.

In the climactic final act, the gang faces off against the Carnival King and its minions in an epic battle of wits and bravery. With Scooby-Doo's help, they manage to outsmart the evil spirits and shatter the magical artifact, freeing the carnival from its curse.

The movie concludes with the gang celebrating their victory at a new Halloween party, this time without any supernatural threats. As they enjoy themselves, Velma reflects on how the mystery was solved, and Shaggy and Scooby share a laugh about their role in uncovering the truth.

Overall, Happy Halloween, Scooby-Doo! is a fun and spooky adventure that stays true to the spirit of the original franchise while introducing new characters and plot twists.

documents.title: The Hand of God
documents.original_title: È stata la mano di Dio
documents.overview: In 1980s Naples, Italy, an awkward Italian teen struggling to find his place experiences heartbreak and liberation after he's inadvertently saved from a freak accident by football legend Diego Maradona.
documents.plot:
The Hand of God is a 2021 Italian sports drama film directed by Paolo Sorrentino, not "by The Apartment". 

The Hand of God explores the complexities of human relationships and the blurred lines between reality and fantasy. The story revolves around a young boy who becomes obsessed with playing football and finds solace in his imagination, which he uses to cope with the difficulties of his life.

Through the protagonist's journey, the film delves into themes of isolation, loneliness, and the struggle for human connection. It also touches on the idea of escapism, as the boy uses his imagination to temporarily escape the harsh realities of his environment.

The Hand of God is a poignant and introspective film that examines the fragility of childhood innocence and the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

documents.title: The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson
documents.original_title: The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson
documents.overview: In 1893, heavily pregnant Molly Johnson and her children struggle in isolation to survive the harsh Australian landscape after her husband left to go droving sheep in the high country. One day, she finds a shackled Aboriginal fugitive named Yakada wounded on her property. As an unlikely bond begins to form between them he reveals secrets about her true identity. Realizing Molly’s husband is actually missing, new town lawman Nate Clintoff starts being suspicious and sends his constable to investigate.
documents.plot:
The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson is a 2022 Australian Western drama film directed by Rachel Perkins. The movie is based on the 1929 novel "The Drover's Wife" by A.B. Facey, but it also incorporates elements from the life of Molly Johnson, an Aboriginal woman who was part of the famous Burke and Wills expedition in 1860.

The story begins with Molly (played by Jessica Mauboy), a young Aboriginal woman living on a station in Western Australia. She is married to Drover (played by Damon Herriman), a rugged and experienced stockman. The couple's life is marked by hardship, isolation, and the struggles of their community.

As the story unfolds, we see Molly's daily life, her relationships with her family and friends, and her deep connection to the land and its people. However, the arrival of Burke (played by Damon Herriman) and Wills (played by Kris McQuade), two British explorers on a journey across Australia, sets off a chain of events that will change Molly's life forever.

Burke and Wills are seeking to cross the continent from east to west, but their expedition is fraught with danger, and they face numerous challenges along the way. Molly becomes embroiled in their story, and her interactions with the explorers have significant consequences for both herself and those around her.

Throughout the film, Perkins explores themes of colonialism, racism, and the complex relationships between Aboriginal people and European settlers. The movie also delves into the personal struggles of its characters, particularly Molly, who must navigate the challenges of being a woman in a patriarchal society.

As the story reaches its climax, Molly finds herself at the center of a tragic event that will have far-reaching consequences for her community. The film's ending is both poignant and powerful, highlighting the resilience and strength of Aboriginal women in the face of adversity.

Overall, The Drover's Wife: The Legend of Molly Johnson is a powerful and moving film that sheds light on a significant period in Australian history. With its strong performances, stunning cinematography, and thought-provoking themes, it is a must-see for anyone interested in Westerns or Aboriginal culture.

documents.title: Malcolm & Marie
documents.tagline: Madly in love.
documents.overview: As a filmmaker and his girlfriend return home from his movie premiere, smoldering tensions and painful revelations push them toward a romantic reckoning.
documents.plot: As a filmmaker and his girlfriend return home from his movie premiere, smoldering tensions and painful revelations push them toward a romantic reckoning.

documents.title: Host
documents.tagline: Someone new has joined the meeting.
documents.overview: Six friends hire a medium to hold a séance via Zoom during lockdown — but they get far more than they bargained for as things quickly go wrong. When an evil spirit starts invading their homes, they begin to realize they might not survive the night.
documents.plot:
Host is a 2020 British independent supernatural horror film directed by Rob Savage, who co-wrote it with Gemma Hurley and Jed Shepherd. A screenlife film that takes place entirely on a Zoom video call, it stars Haley Bishop, Jemma Moore, Emma Louise Webb, Radina Drandova, Caroline Ward and Edward Linard as a group of friends, with Seylan Baxter as a medium. It was conceived and shot during the COVID-19 pandemic, with the cast filming themselves at home while Savage directed them remotely.

During a lockdown in London in July 2020, Haley, Jemma, Radina, Emma, Caroline and Teddy join the weekly Zoom call they use to keep in touch. For fun, Haley has arranged an online séance led by a medium named Seylan, who warns them to treat the spirits with respect, although only Haley and Caroline take the ritual seriously. Teddy soon drops out of the call, and Jemma, bored, claims to feel the presence of a school friend who killed himself. When Seylan's connection drops, Jemma admits that she made the story up as a joke.

Moments later, strange things begin to happen. Haley's chair is yanked across the room, Caroline sees the legs of a hanging body in her attic, a photograph reveals a figure hanging in Haley's home and a glass shatters on its own. When Seylan reconnects, she explains that Jemma's invented story may have allowed a malevolent spirit to wear the guise of the fictional friend and cross into the world of the living. She tells them to close the séance properly, but the entity keeps interrupting. As the presence moves from house to house and their connections fail one by one, the isolated friends can only watch on their screens as each of them is targeted.

Running just under an hour, the film exploits the familiar features of video calls, from frozen screens and dropped connections to face filters, to generate scares, capturing the anxiety of pandemic isolation.

Host debuted on the streaming service Shudder on 30 July 2020 and was released in cinemas and on digital platforms by Vertigo Releasing on 4 December 2020. It received widespread acclaim, with 99 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and grossed about 444,000 dollars against a budget of around 100,000 dollars.

documents.title: Mr. Harrigan's Phone
documents.tagline: Some connections never die.
documents.overview: Craig, a young boy living in a small town befriends an older, reclusive billionaire, Mr. Harrigan. The two form a bond over books and an iPhone, but when the man passes away the boy discovers that not everything dead is gone.
documents.plot:
Mr. Harrigan's Phone is a 2022 American supernatural coming-of-age horror film written and directed by John Lee Hancock, based on the novella of the same name by Stephen King from his 2020 collection If It Bleeds. Donald Sutherland plays the reclusive billionaire John Harrigan and Jaeden Martell plays Craig, the boy who befriends him, with Joe Tippett as Craig's father and Kirby Howell-Baptiste as his teacher. Produced by Blumhouse Productions and Ryan Murphy, the film was released on Netflix in October 2022.

In a small Maine town in 2003, young Craig, who has recently lost his mother, is hired by the retired businessman Harrigan to read aloud to him three times a week. Over the following years the two develop a genuine friendship, talking about books, money and life. As a teenager, Craig starts high school, where he grows close to his teacher Ms. Hart and becomes the target of a bully named Kenny Yankovich. After a lottery scratch card from Harrigan wins him three thousand dollars, Craig buys the old man an iPhone, and despite his suspicion of new technology, Harrigan becomes fascinated by it and by the power of the internet.

When Harrigan dies, a grieving Craig secretly slips the phone into his coffin before the burial. He then learns that Harrigan has left him a large trust fund to pay for his education and his ambitions as a writer. Calling the dead man's number to leave a message of thanks, Craig is startled to receive a cryptic reply. Soon afterwards, when he confides his troubles to the phone, the people who have hurt him begin to die in mysterious circumstances, starting with Kenny. Craig comes to believe that Harrigan is somehow acting on his behalf from beyond the grave, and when tragedy strikes someone he cares about, he must decide whether to ask for vengeance and what it would mean to use such a power.

The film is a quiet, melancholy story about grief, friendship and the moral cost of revenge, with its horror elements kept understated. It also reflects on how smartphones changed people's relationships with information and with one another.

Reviews were mixed. On Rotten Tomatoes about 46 percent of critics' reviews are positive; the consensus praises the layered performances of Sutherland and Martell but argues that the film never quite connects with the intriguing themes of King's novella.

documents.title: Gabriel's Inferno: Part II
documents.overview: Professor Gabriel Emerson finally learns the truth about Julia Mitchell's identity, but his realization comes a moment too late. Julia is done waiting for the well-respected Dante specialist to remember her and wants nothing more to do with him. Can Gabriel win back her heart before she finds love in another's arms?
documents.plot:
Gabriel's Inferno: Part II is an erotic fantasy film that explores the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of one's actions. The movie delves into the theme of temptation, as the protagonist, Gabriel, finds himself entangled in a web of desire and deception.

The film also touches on the idea of free will versus destiny, as Gabriel struggles to reconcile his own desires with the expectations placed upon him by others. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for his journey, driving him to confront the darker aspects of his own nature.

Furthermore, the movie examines the theme of power dynamics and control, particularly in relationships where one party seeks to dominate or manipulate the other. Gabriel's experiences serve as a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of self-awareness.

Ultimately, Gabriel's Inferno: Part II is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of desire, free will, and the consequences of one's actions.

documents.title: Ben 10 Versus the Universe: The Movie
documents.original_title: Ben 10 Versus the Universe: The Movie
documents.tagline: Ben 10 is ready to take on the universe in his most epic adventure yet
documents.overview: A blast from Ben's past returning to do double the damage on Team Tennyson and planet Earth itself, forcing Ben to go interstellar to save the day.
documents.plot:
Ben 10 Versus the Universe: The Movie (2020) is an animated science fiction film that delves into the complexities of friendship, sacrifice, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond one's control. At its core, the movie explores the theme of unity in the face of adversity, as Ben Tennyson and his friends must band together to save the multiverse from destruction.

The film also touches on the idea of responsibility and the weight of power. As Ben discovers new alien forms and abilities, he is faced with the daunting task of deciding how to use these powers for the greater good. This internal conflict serves as a catalyst for Ben's growth as a character, as he learns to balance his desire for adventure and exploration with the need to protect those around him.

Furthermore, the movie examines the concept of identity and self-discovery. As Ben navigates different dimensions and encounters various versions of himself, he is forced to confront the idea that there may be more to being a hero than just having cool powers or gadgets. This journey of self-discovery allows Ben to develop a deeper understanding of his own strengths and weaknesses, ultimately leading him to become a more confident and compassionate leader.

Ultimately, Ben 10 Versus the Universe: The Movie presents a narrative that is both action-packed and emotionally resonant, as it explores the complexities of friendship, power, and personal growth in a way that is both entertaining and thought-provoking.

documents.title: The Woman King
documents.tagline: Her reign begins.
documents.overview: The story of the Agojie, the all-female unit of warriors who protected the African Kingdom of Dahomey in the 1800s with skills and a fierceness unlike anything the world has ever seen, and General Nanisca as she trains the next generation of recruits and readies them for battle against an enemy determined to destroy their way of life.
documents.plot:
The Woman King is a historical action film directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, released in 2022 by TriStar Pictures. The movie takes place in the late 18th century and follows the story of Nanisca (Viola Davis), a skilled warrior and leader of the Agojie, an all-female military unit that protects the kingdom of Oyo from external threats.

The film begins with Nanisca's backstory, where she was trained by her mother, Nawi (Lashana Lynch), to become a great warrior. As Nanisca grows older, she becomes one of the most skilled fighters in the Agojie and is chosen as the leader after her mother's death.

However, when a slave ship arrives at the kingdom, carrying enslaved Africans who are being sold into slavery, Nanisca must confront the harsh reality of the transatlantic slave trade. The slave ship brings with it a ruthless and cunning slave trader named General Ekwefi (Thuso Mbedu), who is determined to capture and sell the enslaved Africans.

As tensions rise between the Agojie and the slave traders, Nanisca must navigate the complexities of her own identity as a woman in a male-dominated society. She also must confront her own demons and make difficult choices that will impact the lives of those around her.

Throughout the film, Prince-Bythewood explores themes of female empowerment, sisterhood, and the resilience of African women in the face of oppression. The movie features stunning action sequences, impressive fight choreography, and a powerful performance from Viola Davis as Nanisca.

Overall, The Woman King is a thrilling and emotionally charged film that celebrates the strength and courage of African women throughout history. With its richly detailed setting and complex characters, the movie offers a fresh perspective on the transatlantic slave trade and its impact on African communities.

documents.title: Hard Kill
documents.tagline: Take on a madman. Save the world.
documents.overview: The work of billionaire tech CEO Donovan Chalmers is so valuable that he hires mercenaries to protect it, and a terrorist group kidnaps his daughter just to get it.
documents.plot: The work of billionaire tech CEO Donovan Chalmers is so valuable that he hires mercenaries to protect it, and a terrorist group kidnaps his daughter just to get it.

documents.title: The Gray Man
documents.overview: When a shadowy CIA agent uncovers damning agency secrets, he's hunted across the globe by a sociopathic rogue operative who's put a bounty on his head.
documents.plot:
The Gray Man is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Anthony and Joe Russo from a screenplay by Joe Russo, Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely, adapted from Mark Greaney's 2009 novel. Ryan Gosling plays the CIA operative Sierra Six and Chris Evans the mercenary hunting him, with Ana de Armas, Jessica Henwick, Regé-Jean Page, Wagner Moura, Julia Butters, Dhanush, Alfre Woodard and Billy Bob Thornton. Produced by AGBO, it opened in a limited theatrical release on July 15, 2022, and arrived on Netflix a week later.

In 2003 the CIA official Donald Fitzroy visits Court Gentry in a Florida prison, where he is serving time for killing his abusive father to protect his brother, and offers him freedom in return for joining Sierra, a secret programme of deniable assassins. Eighteen years later, working as Sierra Six with agent Dani Miranda, he is sent to kill a target in Bangkok during the Songkran festival. The dying man reveals that he was Sierra Four and hands Six an encrypted drive containing evidence of corruption by Denny Carmichael, the official who ordered the hit.

Six refuses to come in, sends the drive to his former handler Margaret Cahill in Prague and asks the now-retired Fitzroy for help. Carmichael turns to Lloyd Hansen, a sadistic ex-CIA operative turned contractor, who kidnaps Fitzroy's niece Claire, whom Six once protected, and holds her at a Croatian estate while posting a huge bounty that draws assassins from around the world. Carmichael's deputy Suzanne Brewer is sent to keep Lloyd under control.

Betrayed in Vienna by the forger Laszlo Sosa, Six survives Lloyd's team with Miranda's help, and the two decrypt the drive in Prague before the dying Cahill blows up her home to cover their escape. A massive gunfight follows across the city, including a battle on a tram. The hired killer Lone Wolf seizes the drive for Lloyd, but Six and Miranda follow him to the estate. Fitzroy is killed during the rescue, Lone Wolf hands the drive to Miranda in disgust at Lloyd's methods, and Six fights Lloyd in a hedge maze until Brewer shoots Lloyd dead. Brewer then uses the evidence to protect the agency rather than punish Carmichael, keeping Claire as leverage, until Six escapes and drives away with her.

With a reported budget of about 200 million dollars, it was one of Netflix's most expensive films. Critics were divided, giving it a 45% Rotten Tomatoes approval, but it was popular with viewers and a sequel was announced.

documents.title: Don't Listen
documents.tagline: Don't listen to them.
documents.overview: After the strange death of his young son at their new home, Daniel hears a ghostly plea for help, spurring him to seek out a renowned paranormal expert.
documents.plot: After a tragic turn of events at the new home he's fixing up, Daniel hears a ghostly plea for help, spurring him to seek out a famous paranormal expert.

documents.title: Fearless
documents.overview: A teen gamer is forced to level up to full-time babysitter when his favorite video game drops three superpowered infants from space into his backyard.
documents.plot:
Fearless is a 2020 American animated science fiction action comedy directed by Cory Edwards, who wrote it with John Murphy, produced by Vanguard Animation and released on Netflix. Its voice cast includes Gabrielle Union, Jadakiss, Miguel J. Pimentel, Yara Shahidi and Miles Robbins. The story follows two high school seniors who must protect three superpowered babies who have escaped from a video game into the real world.

Reid, a teenage gamer known online as Fe@rLeSS_, is an expert at the superhero game Planet Master and the first player to reach its penultimate level. There, the game's hero, Captain Darius Lightspeed, reveals that he has three children, Kira, Xander and Titus, and Reid leaves them in a daycare while he searches for the final level. The game's villain, Dr. Arcannis, kidnaps the babies to steal their superpowers and conquer Earth, but the infants escape in a pod. When Reid agrees to accept the consequences of continuing, the pod travels through a wormhole and crash-lands behind his house in the real world.

Reid and his classmate Melanie, who has come over to work on a science project, discover the babies and agree to look after them. Their task is far from easy: the infants have unpredictable powers, the U.S. military, led by General Jayne Blazerhatch, has detected the pod and is closing in, and Arcannis has followed the babies through the wormhole. After a call from Lightspeed is cut short when one of the babies breaks the communicator, Reid and Melanie go on the run. Captured by the military and then outmatched by Arcannis, who seizes the children, the two teenagers must work together with Lightspeed to rescue the babies, racing to reach Arcannis's ship before he can drain their powers.

The film plays with video game conventions and the idea of a gamer forced into real-world responsibility, combining slapstick humor with superhero action.

Fearless was released on Netflix on August 14, 2020. It received mixed reviews; Polygon's Tasha Robinson wrote that it was not terrible, but that no one involved seemed to have put in much effort.

documents.title: Cats & Dogs 3: Paws Unite
documents.overview: It's been ten years since the creation of the Great Truce, an elaborate joint-species surveillance system designed and monitored by cats and dogs to keep the peace when conflicts arise. But when a tech-savvy villain hacks into wireless networks to use frequencies only heard by cats and dogs, he manipulates them into conflict and the worldwide battle between cats and dogs is BACK ON. Now, a team of inexperienced and untested agents will have to use their old-school animal instincts to restore order and peace between cats and dogs everywhere.
documents.plot:
Cats & Dogs 3: Paws Unite! is a 2020 American spy comedy directed by Sean McNamara, the third and final installment of the Cats & Dogs series and a stand-alone sequel to Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore (2010). Melissa Rauch, Max Greenfield and George Lopez lead the voice cast. Unlike the first two films, it was released straight to video in the United States, on September 15, 2020.

A decade after the Great Truce ended the war between cats and dogs, Roger, a Border Collie, and Gwen, a cat, are partners in F.A.R.T. (Furry Animals Rivalry Termination), a secret organization that keeps the peace without humans ever knowing. Roger, who gave up field work after his mentor was injured, has been stuck at a desk. The two live in the same apartment building in suburban Seattle with their owners: Max, a middle school tennis player pressured by his mother to win a state championship, and Zoe, whose struggling musician father, Ollie, faces eviction.

When the agents' communications go down and local cats and dogs suddenly begin fighting again, Roger and Gwen investigate. With tips from park dogs and alley cats, they learn that someone has stolen wireless access codes in order to broadcast frequencies audible only to cats and dogs, turning them against each other so that humans will stop adopting them and choose reptiles and birds instead. The mastermind is Pablo, a cockatoo at a pet store, and his reptile accomplices. Along the way the partners also try to bring their lonely owners together, trapping Max and Zoe in a stalled elevator, where the two open up about their pressures, share a kiss and become friends.

At the pet store, Roger, Gwen and their ally Duke are captured, and the frequency is activated as Max and Zoe arrive, but the agents break free and fight off Pablo's snakes and tarantula. Pablo, softened by the affection of a boy who visits the store, turns against his lizard henchman and shuts down the signal. Roger's missing mentor, Old Ed, admits he let himself be captured so that Roger would regain his confidence in the field. Zoe's father sells his song and saves their home, and Max wins his championship.

Critics were largely negative, faulting the cheap-looking effects, clichéd story and lack of wit. Common Sense Media praised some of the humor, particularly from George Lopez.

documents.title: JJ+E
documents.tagline: Two worlds. One love.
documents.overview: Elisabeth and John-John live in the same city, but they inhabit different worlds.
documents.plot:
JJ+E (Swedish: Vinterviken, "Winter Cove") is a 2021 Swedish romantic drama film directed by Alexis Almström and written by Dunja Vujovic, based on the young adult novel Vinterviken by Mats Wahl. Produced by Filmlance International with SVT and released by Netflix, it stars Elsa Öhrn as Elisabeth and Mustapha Aarab as John-John, with Magnus Krepper as Elisabeth's father Frank, Marika Lagercrantz as Victoria, Simon Mezher as Jacob, the singer Loreen as John-John's mother Maria, Albin Grenholm as Patrik, Jonay Pineda Skallak as Sluggo and Elsa Bergström Terent as Patricia. The music was composed by Vittorio Grasso.

John-John, known as JJ, is the son of a single immigrant mother and grows up in a working-class housing estate in Stockholm, surrounded by a multicultural group of friends led by his downstairs neighbor Sluggo, whose gang drifts into burglary and petty crime; his mother's boyfriend, a security guard, warns that they will all end up behind bars. Elisabeth lives in a seaside villa with her wealthy father and younger sister Patricia and is withdrawn and sarcastic, still grieving the death of her mother. Their worlds collide when JJ, out on a joyride in a stolen boat with Sluggo, rescues Patricia from drowning. Both are then admitted to the same performing arts school, and a slow, hesitant courtship develops as they rehearse for a school performance, explore the city and meet each other's friends, while hiding the relationship from her disapproving father. Sluggo's crimes, which include breaking into Elisabeth's home, increasingly entangle JJ, and when he is backed into a corner with no way out, the gulf between their lives threatens to tear the couple apart in a dark final act.

JJ+E premiered on Netflix on 8 September 2021. Critical reception was mixed. Decider's Jade Budowski praised its grounded portrait of Stockholm, the chemistry of the leads and the star quality of Elsa Öhrn, but felt the film wavered between romance and crime story before taking an absurd turn in its last minutes. Roger Moore of Movie Nation found the courtship scenes the strongest and valued its depiction of Sweden's multicultural underclass, yet called the surrounding melodrama a collection of clichés and the whole a formulaic, tepid teen romance.

documents.title: The Tender Bar
documents.tagline: Between the ones who love you and the ones who leave you is the journey of a lifetime.
documents.overview: J.R. is a fatherless boy growing up in the glow of a bar where the bartender, his Uncle Charlie, is the sharpest and most colorful of an assortment of quirky and demonstrative father figures. As the boy’s determined mother struggles to provide her son with opportunities denied to her — and leave the dilapidated home of her outrageous if begrudgingly supportive father — J.R. begins to gamely, if not always gracefully, pursue his romantic and professional dreams, with one foot persistently placed in Uncle Charlie’s bar.
documents.plot: JR is a fatherless boy growing up in the glow of a bar where the bartender, his Uncle Charlie, is the sharpest and most colorful of an assortment of quirky and demonstrative father figures. As the boy’s determined mother struggles to provide her son with opportunities denied to her — and leave the dilapidated home of her outrageous if begrudgingly supportive father — JR begins to gamely, if not always gracefully, pursue his romantic and professional dreams, with one foot persistently placed in Uncle Charlie’s bar.

documents.title: Hunt
documents.tagline: Two rivals, a hidden truth.
documents.overview: Agents of the Korean National Intelligence Service (KNIS), Pyung-ho at Int’l Dept. and Jung-do at Domestic Dept. are both independently hunting a North Korean mole within the agency. During this investigation, they come face to face with an unbearable truth and must deal with an unthinkable plot to assassinate the South Korean president.
documents.plot:
Hunt (Korean: 헌트) is a 2022 South Korean spy action thriller directed by Lee Jung-jae in his feature directorial debut. Lee and Jung Woo-sung star as two intelligence chiefs who come to suspect each other while hunting a mole inside their agency, with Jeon Hye-jin, Heo Sung-tae and Go Youn-jung, in her film debut, in the supporting cast. It premiered in the Midnight Screenings section of the 2022 Cannes Film Festival on 19 May, where it received a seven-minute standing ovation, and Megabox released it in South Korea on 10 August 2022.

In the 1980s, under the military dictatorship of President Chun Doo-hwan, Park Pyong-ho, head of the foreign unit of the Agency for National Security Planning, and Kim Jung-do, head of its domestic unit, are guarding the president in Washington, D.C., when a team of assassins strikes. Jung-do shoots the last gunman as he holds Pyong-ho hostage, and the two men blame each other. Afterward, the agency's director reveals that a North Korean mole code-named Donglim is working inside the agency and plotting to kill the president, and both chiefs are ordered to find him.

A botched operation in Japan to bring over a defecting North Korean physicist, and the betrayal of a failed military mission to the North, push the rivals to investigate each other. Each uncovers the other's secret. Jung-do leads a conspiracy to assassinate the president in revenge for the Gwangju massacre and was behind the Washington attack, while Pyong-ho is Donglim. Learning that the North now plans to invade and intends to eliminate him, Pyong-ho is rescued by Jung-do and drawn into the assassination plot in Bangkok, but fearing that the killing will trigger the invasion, he turns against the attack on the motorcade. A bomb set by a North Korean agent fails to kill the president, and Jung-do dies in the blast. Later, Pyong-ho is ambushed and killed while offering the young woman Yoo-jeong an escape to America, after it is revealed that she really is a North Korean agent.

After the Cannes screening, Lee re-edited the film and changed key lines to make the 1980s political background clearer to foreign audiences, presenting the new version at the Toronto International Film Festival. Hunt topped the South Korean box office on release and drew more than 4.3 million admissions. Critics were mixed, with 69% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52, though some found the plot needlessly convoluted.

documents.title: The Kissing Booth 3
documents.tagline: The end of an era. The beginning of everything else.
documents.overview: It’s the summer before Elle heads to college, and she has a secret decision to make. Elle has been accepted into Harvard, where boyfriend Noah is matriculating, and also Berkeley, where her BFF Lee is headed and has to decide if she should stay or not.
documents.plot:
The Kissing Booth 3 is a 2021 American teen romantic comedy directed by Vince Marcello, who wrote it with Jay Arnold. The third and final instalment in the Netflix trilogy adapted from Beth Reekles' novel The Kissing Booth, it stars Joey King as Elle, Joel Courtney as her best friend Lee and Jacob Elordi as Lee's older brother Noah, with Taylor Zakhar Perez, Maisie Richardson-Sellers and Molly Ringwald. It was released on Netflix on August 11, 2021.

After graduation, Elle still has not decided between Berkeley, where she promised to go with Lee, and Harvard, where Noah is already apartment-hunting for them. When Lee and Noah's parents announce that they are selling the family beach house, the friends, along with Lee's girlfriend Rachel, spend one last summer there. Facing Berkeley's deadline, Elle chooses Harvard, upsetting Lee, and to make amends she promises to complete their childhood beach bucket list together. Complications multiply when Noah's friend Chloe comes to stay and Marco, the boy Elle once kissed, takes a job nearby. Elle struggles to divide her time between the brothers, while also resenting her father's new girlfriend Linda, a friend of her late mother, whom she fears is trying to replace her.

Marco and Noah clash repeatedly, and at a Fourth of July party Marco punches Noah, who refuses to fight back; Marco confesses he still has feelings for Elle, but she turns him down. Elle argues bitterly with her father, who reminds her of everything he has sacrificed for her and her brother and that he too deserves love. Noah, having seen her Berkeley acceptance letter and fearing that she is choosing Harvard only for him, breaks up with her. A furious argument with Lee follows, in which Elle declares that all her choices that summer have been about pleasing everyone else. Lee and Noah's mother advises her to decide for herself what she wants.

Rachel, having watched the strains in Elle and Noah's relationship, breaks up with Lee, hoping they will reunite one day. Elle accepts Linda, reconciles with her father, parts amicably with Marco and makes peace with Lee. Realising she has never worked out what makes her happy, she applies to the University of Southern California to study game design. Six years later, now a game developer, she returns home, where Lee and Rachel are engaged, and at the kissing booth she meets Noah again, and the two agree to go for a motorcycle ride.

Like its predecessors, it was poorly reviewed (25% on Rotten Tomatoes).

documents.title: Borrego
documents.tagline: Fight your way out.
documents.overview: A young botanist relocates to a small desert town to study an invasive plant species. While out on research, she comes to the aid of a downed plane only to find herself taken captive by an inexperienced drug mule who forces her to lead a trek across the sweltering desert to his drop. A local sheriff is drawn into the hunt as his rebellious daughter sets out to find the missing botanist, all the while being pursued by a local drug receiver.
documents.plot:
Borrego is a 2022 American survival crime thriller written and directed by Jesse Harris in his feature directorial debut. Lucy Hale stars as a young botanist, with Nicholas Gonzalez, Leynar Gomez, Olivia Trujillo and Jorge A. Jimenez. The film was released in theaters and on demand by Saban Films on 14 January 2022 and later arrived on Netflix, where it entered the global top ten in its first week. Harris has said that the story was inspired by his father, who is a botanist.

The botanist moves to a small town in the Anza-Borrego Desert in Southern California to study an invasive plant species that is spreading through the area. While working alone in the desert, she witnesses the crash of an ultralight aircraft being used to smuggle drugs across the border from Mexico. The pilot, an inexperienced and reluctant drug mule, survives the crash and, desperate to complete his delivery, takes Elly hostage and forces her to guide him across the harsh terrain on foot, carrying the drugs on their backs.

As the two struggle through the heat with limited water, they are pursued from several directions. The local sheriff realizes something has happened when the botanist goes missing, and his teenage daughter becomes involved in the search. Meanwhile, the dangerous man waiting to receive the shipment, is determined to recover it at any cost. She must rely on her knowledge of the desert's plants and landscape to survive, while the uneasy relationship between captor and captive develops as both realize they may be victims of the same ruthless operation. The paths of all the characters converge as the story heads toward a violent climax.

The film received mixed reviews from critics, with a 27 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Some reviewers were positive: James Verniere of the Boston Herald gave it a B+ and called it a well-made and gripping crime thriller, and Movie Mensch praised Hale's performance in a timely thriller. Jeffrey Anderson of Common Sense Media gave it three stars out of five, while Jon Mendelsohn of Comic Book Resources called it dull and Sheila O'Malley of RogerEbert.com gave it two stars.

documents.title: Encounter
documents.tagline: When you stand by each other, you can get through anything.
documents.overview: A decorated Marine goes on a rescue mission to save his two young sons from an unhuman threat. As their journey takes them in increasingly dangerous directions, the boys will need to leave their childhoods behind.
documents.plot:
Encounter (stylized as ENCOUИTƎЯ) is a 2021 science fiction thriller and crime drama directed by Michael Pearce, who co-wrote the screenplay with Joe Barton. Riz Ahmed stars as Malik Khan, a former US Marine, with Octavia Spencer, Janina Gavankar, Rory Cochrane, Lucian-River Chauhan and Aditya Geddada. The film premiered at the 48th Telluride Film Festival in September 2021 and was released in a limited theatrical run by Amazon Studios in December 2021 before streaming on Prime Video a week later.

Malik is a decorated Marine veteran whose two young sons, Jay and Bobby, live with their mother Piya and her new partner Dylan. Piya has been feeling ill, which Dylan dismisses as a bug. One night Malik appears at the house unannounced, wakes the boys and tells them they are going on a road trip. As they drive through the desert, Malik grows tense whenever they pass police cars, and when a hostile officer pulls them over, Malik becomes convinced that the man has been taken over by a parasitic organism from another planet. He overpowers the officer and leaves him on the road.

Malik then admits to his sons that this is not a vacation but a rescue mission: alien parasites carried by insects are spreading across the country, taking control of human hosts, and their mother has already been infected. Jay, the older boy, is torn between his admiration for his father and growing doubts about what he is being told, especially as Malik's behavior becomes more erratic. Meanwhile Hattie, Malik's parole officer, and the authorities begin searching for Malik, who is suspected of kidnapping his children. As the journey continues, the film gradually reveals the truth about Malik's mental state, his past, and the trauma he carries from his military service, turning what began as an alien-invasion thriller into an intimate drama about a father's love, mental illness and the bond between parent and child.

Encounter received mixed reviews, with 54 percent of 125 critics' reviews counted as positive on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics widely praised Ahmed's performance and the young actors, particularly Chauhan, while some felt that the film's shift in genre was unevenly handled and that it failed to fully commit to either of its storylines.

documents.title: Stand by Me Doraemon 2
documents.original_title: STAND BY ME ドラえもん2
documents.tagline: Can he ever be a good husband to Shizuka?
documents.overview: He and her beloved Shizuka are finally married! Nobita's childhood dream was supposed to come true on his wedding day, but for some reason, Nobita doesn't show up... One of the most popular episodes from the original story transcends time and space, and leads to Nobita's future. Doraemon and Nobita's great adventure begins in order to fulfill his grandmother's wish to see his bride at first sight. This is a story of tears and bonds, set in the past, present and future.
documents.plot:
Stand by Me Doraemon 2 is a heartwarming and nostalgic film that explores the complexities of childhood friendships and the importance of holding onto memories from one's past. The movie delves into the theme of nostalgia, as the main characters reminisce about their adventures with Doraemon in the summer of 1965.

The story also touches on the idea of growing up and letting go. As the characters face new challenges and responsibilities, they must come to terms with the fact that their carefree childhood days are slowly fading away. This theme is beautifully captured through the character of Nobita, who struggles to balance his desire for adventure with the need to take responsibility for his actions.

Furthermore, the film highlights the significance of friendship and loyalty in overcoming adversity. The bond between Nobita and his friends is put to the test as they navigate the challenges of adolescence, but ultimately, their relationships are strengthened by their shared experiences.

The movie also explores the theme of time travel and its consequences. Doraemon's ability to travel through time serves as a metaphor for the complexities of growing up and the importance of learning from one's past mistakes. The film encourages viewers to appreciate the present moment and not take anything for granted, while also acknowledging the value of nostalgia and the lessons learned from past experiences.

Overall, Stand by Me Doraemon 2 is a poignant and uplifting film that celebrates the beauty of childhood friendships and the importance of holding onto memories from one's past.

documents.title: The Last Mercenary
documents.tagline: The daddy of all secret agents.
documents.overview: A legendary secret service agent comes out of hiding and returns to France to help the son he's never met get out of trouble.
documents.plot:
The Last Mercenary (French: Le Dernier Mercenaire) is a 2021 French action comedy directed by David Charhon from a screenplay he co-wrote with Ismael Sy Savane. Jean-Claude Van Damme stars as Richard Brumère, a legendary former secret agent, with Alban Ivanov, Assa Sylla and Samir Decazza in the supporting cast. The film was released worldwide on Netflix on 30 July 2021, and it plays as an affectionate parody of the action films that made Van Damme famous, while giving him a role that mocks his own screen persona.

Years earlier, during a covert operation, Richard fathered a son, Archibald, with the former wife of his colleague Jouard. Because Richard could not raise the boy himself, the boy's mother arranged that he would receive two things from the state: a regular financial allowance and a guardian to look after him, together with legal immunity linked to Richard's service. An agent named Fernand was assigned to the task and has cared for Archibald ever since, so the young man has always believed that Fernand is his father.

The arrangement collapses when a zealous government minister discovers that a phantom employee has been paying Archibald money for years. Cutting off the payments also cancels his immunity, and because of a bureaucratic mix-up, Archibald is suddenly identified as a wanted terrorist accused of arms and drug trafficking. Government agents raid his home using a secret electronic device nicknamed the Big Mac, which disables Fernand's pacemaker and causes a fatal heart attack, and Archibald is arrested. Learning that his son is in danger, Richard returns to France and stages a rescue, at first hiding his identity under an alias. Father and son go on the run, pursued by the government and caught up in a conspiracy involving the minister and the Big Mac device, while Archibald slowly learns the truth about the father he never knew.

The film relies on slapstick, absurd disguises and self-referential jokes, including nods to Van Damme's trademark martial arts, alongside a story about an absent father attempting to make amends.

The Last Mercenary received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes about 58 percent of critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic assigned it a score of 48 out of 100, with critics enjoying Van Damme's self-parody while finding the comedy uneven.

documents.title: The Most Beautiful Boy in the World
documents.original_title: The Most Beautiful Boy in the World
documents.overview: In 1971, due to the world premiere of Death in Venice, Italian director Lucino Visconti proclaimed his Tadzio as the world’s most beautiful boy. A shadow that today, 50 years later, weighs Björn Andrésen’s life.
documents.plot:
The Most Beautiful Boy in the World is a 2021 documentary film that explores the life of Gust Avrakotos, a former child actor who rose to fame as a teen heartthrob in the 1970s. The film delves into themes of identity, trauma, and the complexities of masculinity.

Through Gust's story, the documentary sheds light on the darker side of Hollywood's Golden Age, where child actors were often exploited and manipulated for their youthful charm. The film raises questions about the long-term effects of this exploitation on individuals, particularly those who are forced to navigate the treacherous waters of fame at a tender age.

The Most Beautiful Boy in the World also touches on themes of toxic masculinity, as Gust struggles to reconcile his public persona with his private self. His journey serves as a powerful commentary on the societal expectations placed upon men, particularly those who are perceived as vulnerable or effeminate.

Furthermore, the documentary highlights the importance of human connection and empathy in healing from trauma. Through Gust's relationships with his loved ones, including his mother and a close friend, the film shows how these connections can provide solace and support during times of darkness.

Ultimately, The Most Beautiful Boy in the World is a poignant exploration of the human cost of fame, identity, and the complexities of masculinity. It serves as a powerful reminder of the need for empathy, understanding, and support for those who have been affected by trauma and exploitation.

documents.title: Cyrano
documents.tagline: Have you ever loved someone?
documents.overview: A man ahead of his time, Cyrano de Bergerac dazzles whether with ferocious wordplay at a verbal joust or with brilliant swordplay in a duel. But, convinced that his appearance renders him unworthy of the love of a devoted friend, the luminous Roxanne, Cyrano has yet to declare his feelings for her—and Roxanne has fallen in love, at first sight, with Christian.
documents.plot:
Cyrano is a 2021 romantic musical drama film directed by Joe Wright from a screenplay by Erica Schmidt, adapted from her 2018 stage musical, itself based on Edmond Rostand's 1897 play Cyrano de Bergerac. Peter Dinklage and Haley Bennett reprise their stage roles as Cyrano and Roxanne, alongside Kelvin Harrison Jr. as Christian and Ben Mendelsohn. The songs were written by members of the band the National, and the vocals were recorded live on set in Sicily.

Roxanne, a beautiful orphan of modest means, attends the theater with the vain Duke De Guiche, who is determined to marry her, though she longs to marry for love. As she takes her seat, she and Christian de Neuvillette, a newly recruited soldier, are instantly smitten with each other. Her childhood friend Cyrano de Bergerac, a highborn cadet with dwarfism, drives the lead actor off the stage with rhyming insults and then wins a duel against a man who mocks his appearance. Roxanne has no idea that Cyrano is desperately in love with her, and she asks him to arrange a meeting with Christian. Heartbroken, Cyrano finds that Christian cannot express his feelings, and so he writes passionate letters to Roxanne that Christian delivers as his own.

When Roxanne meets Christian in person, his clumsy words disappoint her, until Cyrano, hiding in the shadows, whispers to him what to say. De Guiche sends word that he will have Roxanne one way or another, so she and Christian marry in haste, and the furious duke sends Cyrano and Christian's unit to the front. At war, Cyrano writes to Roxanne daily in Christian's name and risks his life to keep Christian safe. When De Guiche orders the unit on a suicide mission, Christian sees Cyrano's tear-stained farewell letter and realizes that Roxanne truly loves the man who wrote it. Urging Cyrano to tell her the truth, he charges the enemy guns and is killed. Three years later, Cyrano is poor and ailing from unhealed wounds. Sensing the end, he visits Roxanne and recites Christian's last letter from memory, revealing that he wrote them all. They declare their love before he dies in her arms.

Cyrano premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on September 2, 2021, and was released widely in the US and UK on February 25, 2022. Although it grossed only $6.4 million on a $30 million budget, critics praised Dinklage's and Bennett's performances and the music; Rotten Tomatoes reported 85% approval. It received Golden Globe nominations including Best Motion Picture.

documents.title: Trollhunters: Rise of the Titans
documents.tagline: They will rise.
documents.overview: The Guardians of Arcadia reunite to battle the nefarious Arcane Order, who've reawakened the primordial Titans.
documents.plot:
Trollhunters: Rise of the Titans is a 2021 American computer-animated fantasy action film directed by Johane Matte, Francisco Ruiz Velasco and Andrew Schmidt, and written by Guillermo del Toro, Marc Guggenheim and Dan and Kevin Hageman. It is the finale of del Toro's Tales of Arcadia franchise, which includes the series Trollhunters, 3Below and Wizards, and brings together the heroes of all three shows. The voice cast includes Emile Hirsch, Lexi Medrano, Charlie Saxton, Kelsey Grammer, Alfred Molina, Steven Yeun, Nick Frost, Colin O'Donoghue, Diego Luna, Tatiana Maslany and Nick Offerman.

A year after the events of Wizards, the master wizard Douxie and Nari, a former member of the villainous Arcane Order, lure the Order's Belloc and Skrael onto a subway train, where they are joined by the former Trollhunter Jim Lake Jr., his girlfriend Claire and his best friend Toby. The battle goes badly: Jim is wounded, the train runs out of control, and Nari is captured by the Order after swapping bodies with Douxie in an attempt to deceive them.

Regrouping in a rebuilt Camelot, the heroes learn from Blinky that the Arcane Order intends to awaken the Titans, giant ancient beings, and have them converge on Arcadia Oaks, the center of the universe, to destroy and remake the world. Before her connection is broken, Nari passes Jim a cryptic message about a ninth configuration and an artifact called the Krohnisfere. Failing to prevent the ritual that breaks the Genesis Seals, the heroes split into teams that travel across the world, from Hong Kong to Brazil and Greenland, to stop the rising Titans. As allies fall and the final Titan approaches Arcadia, Jim must uncover the meaning of Nari's words and rally his friends for a battle on which the fate of everything depends.

The film emphasizes friendship, sacrifice and destiny, offering a conclusion that ties together the many characters and storylines of the franchise.

Rise of the Titans was released on Netflix on July 21, 2021. It received positive reviews, with an 88 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of critics; Den of Geek praised its stakes, visual effects, imagination and humor, while noting that few characters other than Jim receive full development.

documents.title: Batman: Soul of the Dragon
documents.tagline: Get ready for the ultimate showdown.
documents.overview: Bruce Wayne faces a deadly menace from his past, with the help of three former classmates: world-renowned martial artists Richard Dragon, Ben Turner and Lady Shiva.
documents.plot:
Batman: Soul of the Dragon is a 2021 American animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and DC Entertainment, the 43rd entry in the DC Universe Animated Original Movies line. Directed by Sam Liu and executive produced by Bruce Timm, it tells an original story set in the 1970s and inspired by the martial arts films of that era. David Giuntoli voices Bruce Wayne/Batman, with Mark Dacascos as Richard Dragon, Kelly Hu as Lady Shiva, Michael Jai White as Ben Turner/Bronze Tiger and James Hong as O-Sensei; White reprised his role from the television series Arrow and Hu hers from the video game Batman: Arkham Origins. The film is dedicated to comic book writer Dennis O'Neil, who died in 2020.

Years earlier, while training to become a crime-fighter, the young Bruce Wayne studies at Nanda Parbat, a hidden monastery in the Hindu Kush run by the martial arts master O-Sensei, alongside fellow students Shiva, Richard Dragon, Jade, Ben Turner and Rip Jagger. O-Sensei entrusts Shiva with Soul Breaker, a Muramasa sword, while forbidding his students to pass through a certain door. One night Rip breaks through it and kills Jade with the sword, which proves to be the key to a mystical gate leading to the realm of the serpent god Nāga. Demons pour through, and to close the gate O-Sensei sacrifices himself by stepping into Nāga's dimension. Years later, Richard learns that millionaire Jeffrey Burr, leader of the Kobra cult, has obtained the gate, and he travels to Gotham City to warn Bruce, only for both men to be attacked by the Axe Gang, hired by Burr's enforcer Schlangenfaust, who is hunting for Soul Breaker. Richard discovers Bruce's secret identity, and the two seek out Shiva, now a crime lord in Gotham's Chinatown, before the sword is stolen. Reuniting with Ben, now a martial arts teacher, the former classmates track the cult to a fortified island where Burr plans to open the gate by sacrificing kidnapped children, intending to become Nāga's earthly avatar, and they must stop the ritual before the god is unleashed.

The film was released on digital platforms on January 12, 2021, followed by Blu-ray and DVD on January 26. It was well received, with 93% of 15 critics' reviews positive on Rotten Tomatoes, and DVD Talk rated it "Recommended".

documents.title: Blade of the 47 Ronin
documents.overview: In this sequel to "47 Ronin," a new class of warriors emerges among the Samurai clans to keep a sought-after sword from falling into the wrong hands.
documents.plot:
Blade of the 47 Ronin is a 2022 American action fantasy film directed by Ron Yuan and written by John Swetnam, Aimee Garcia and AJ Mendez. It is a sequel to 47 Ronin (2013), taking place three centuries after the events of the first film and following the struggle for survival of the last descendants of the legendary samurai. The cast includes Anna Akana, Mark Dacascos, Teresa Ting, Dustin Nguyen and Dan Southworth. Netflix released it as an original film on October 25, 2022.

Three hundred years after the ronin Oishi and Kai killed Lord Kira and the witch Mizuki to avenge their master, Lord Asano, rival clans of samurai and witches continue to exist in secret. In the present day, a witch named Yurei is hunting for the mystical Tengu sword once used by the 47 Ronin, intending to unite it with the Witch Sword, and he has been killing off the descendants of the ronin who brought about his ancestor's downfall. Lord Arai, himself a descendant of the 47 Ronin, tries to find the sword first with the help of a witch called Hirano, but both are ambushed and killed by Yurei and his ninjas.

In Budapest, the samurai lords Okoro, Maeda, Shinshiro, Ikeda and Nikko gather to discuss Arai's death. Suspecting Yurei, they fear an ancient prophecy foretelling that the true descendant of the 47 Ronin will wield both the Witch and Warrior Blades and defeat him. Onami, a swordswoman in Shinshiro's service, enlists Reo, a former agent and skilled tracker, to locate the descendant before Yurei does. Their search leads to Luna, an Asian American thief who has been summoned to claim Arai's inheritance, the Warrior Blade, and who tries to sell it at a nightclub before Onami and Reo intervene.

After Yurei's forces attack Shinshiro's hotel and are driven back, Luna is taken to the Record Keeper, Dash, and his assistant Hana, who reveal more of the clans' hidden history. Dash foresees a vision of Yurei uniting the two swords and annihilating the samurai. As the lords fall out of contact and Yurei closes in, Luna is forced to confront her own lineage and decide whether to embrace the destiny the prophecy describes. The film culminates in a battle between the samurai and Yurei's forces for control of the blades.

Unlike the 2013 original, a big-budget theatrical release starring Keanu Reeves and set in feudal Japan, the sequel was released directly to streaming and moves the story to the modern day, with a cast drawn largely from martial arts and genre film veterans.

documents.title: The Amityville Harvest
documents.tagline: They're in his house. But he's in their minds.
documents.overview: While staying at an aging manor to research its liquor-smuggling history, Christina and her documentary video team interview their spooky host Vincent—but no one can capture his image or voice on video. After shocking dreams and bloody encounters, the crew members fall under Victor’s hypnotic spell.
documents.plot:
The Amityville Harvest is a 2020 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Thomas J. Churchill. It stars Kyle Lowder, Sadie Katz, Brandon Alan Smith and Alexa Pellerin, with Johanna Rae, Michael Cervantes, Eva Ceja, George W. Scott, Keavy Bradley, Eileen Dietz and Paul Logan in supporting roles. One of the many loosely connected low-budget films to use the Amityville name, it was released on DVD, video on demand and digital platforms on 20 October 2020 by Lionsgate Home Entertainment, and it was the last Amityville film released before the death of Ronald DeFeo Jr., the real-life killer whose crime inspired the series, in March 2021.

Documentary filmmaker Christina Weingarten (Katz) travels with her crew to the large colonial home of the rich eccentric Vincent Miller (Lowder) on Long Island to interview him for a segment called "My Civil War" about his family's connection to the assassination of Abraham Lincoln. Her team includes her younger sister Nancy (Pellerin), lighting technician Cosmo (Smith), audio engineer Scratch (Cervantes), hearing-impaired make-up artist Janet (Rae), photographer Lexy (Ceja) and new crew member Ottis (Scott). Vincent, a Confederate apologist, proudly recounts his ancestor's role in plotting the assassination and teases a family history of fire and Prohibition-era liquor smuggling, but after hours of interviews the crew discovers that none of his image or voice has been recorded. Unknown to them, he is a vampire who can communicate telepathically. His house stands next to his funeral parlour, the subject of several missing-person reports, where the young Lana (Bradley) was attacked by her dead boyfriend Robbie (Logan) and where a sinister mortician, Randolph (Patrick Mulderrig), butchers victims in the basement. Cosmo is secretly searching for Lana, while the crew suffer disturbing dreams and fall under Vincent's hypnotic spell, and the dead return as ghouls. Eventually the sisters are left fighting to escape through the basement, and the film ends on an Amityville town sign.

The film received largely negative reviews. Screen Rant said its twist failed, Nightmarish Conjurings criticised its chaotic editing and poor effects, and Horror Society gave it one out of five, though Cryptic Rock rated it three out of five. Writing for Bloody Disgusting, Joe Lipsett called it overstuffed, with three or four films' worth of storylines, while praising its practical gore effects.

documents.title: LEGO Star Wars Holiday Special
documents.tagline: To: Luke. From: Your father.
documents.overview: As her friends prep for a Life Day holiday celebration, Rey journeys with BB-8 on a quest to gain a deeper knowledge of the Force at a mysterious Jedi Temple. There, she embarks on a cross-timeline adventure through beloved moments in Star Wars history, coming into contact with iconic heroes and villains from all eras of the saga. But will she make it back in time for the Life Day feast?
documents.plot:
The LEGO Star Wars Holiday Special is a heartwarming and humorous celebration of the Star Wars universe, focusing on the character of Chewbacca and his family during the Wookiee holiday, Life Day. The special explores themes of family, tradition, and cultural identity.

At its core, the story revolves around Chewbacca's desire to connect with his family and understand the significance of Life Day, a celebration that holds great importance for the Wookiees. As he navigates this unfamiliar holiday, Chewbacca learns valuable lessons about the importance of embracing his heritage and finding common ground with those around him.

The special also touches on themes of loneliness and isolation, as Chewbacca struggles to balance his duties as Han Solo's co-pilot with his desire to connect with his family. This internal conflict serves as a poignant reminder that even in a galaxy filled with adventure and excitement, it's the simple moments of connection and community that truly bring meaning to our lives.

Throughout the special, the LEGO Star Wars universe is infused with its signature blend of humor, wit, and lighthearted charm, making for an entertaining and engaging viewing experience. Ultimately, the LEGO Star Wars Holiday Special is a feel-good story that celebrates the power of family, tradition, and self-discovery in a way that's both nostalgic and accessible to audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Evil Eye
documents.tagline: Trust your mother's instincts.
documents.overview: A seemingly perfect romance turns dark when a mother becomes convinced her daughter’s new boyfriend has a sinister connection to her own past.
documents.plot: A seemingly perfect romance turns dark when a mother becomes convinced her daughter’s new boyfriend has a sinister connection to her own past.

documents.title: Combat Wombat
documents.tagline: She kicks wom-butt
documents.overview: Maggie Diggins, a wombat turned Wonder Woman, unintentionally becomes the city's superhero after she begrudgingly saves a rookie superhero sugar glider from certain doom.
documents.plot:
Combat Wombat is a 2020 Australian computer-animated superhero comedy directed by Ricard Cussó and written by Matthew James Kinmonth. Produced in Brisbane by Like a Photon Creative, with producers Kristen Souvlis and Nadine Bates, and financed with support from Screen Queensland and Screen Australia, it is the second film in the studio's Tales from Sanctuary City franchise, after The Wishmas Tree. Deborah Mailman voices Maggie Diggins, alongside Ed Oxenbould as Sweetie, Frank Woodley as Flightless Feather, Judith Lucy as CeCe and George Pullar as Bradley Burrows.

Maggie, a wombat, seems to have everything she could want: she is happily married to her childhood sweetheart Bradley, the two have secure jobs digging tunnels for a construction company, and they have just moved into their dream home. Then a mining accident traps them underground, and Bradley sacrifices himself to help Maggie escape before he is buried under the rubble. The city's superhero, the emu Flightless Feather, rescues everyone except Bradley, and Maggie blames him. After the police give up searching for her husband, the grief-stricken widow becomes obsessed with finding out what went wrong. When she reluctantly saves Sweetie, a young, superhero-obsessed sugar glider, from falling to his death, she becomes famous as Sanctuary City's new superhero, "Combat Wombat", much to the displeasure of the vain Flightless Feather. With Sweetie as her loyal if sometimes annoying sidekick, Maggie uncovers a conspiracy involving Flightless Feather's manager, the koala CeCe, who justifies her schemes as a way of giving people a role model and turns out to be an aggressive drop bear, putting the city in danger.

Combat Wombat premiered at the Brisbane International Film Festival in October 2020 and was released in Australian cinemas on 15 October 2020, distributed by Universal locally and by Odin's Eye internationally, in a limited run on 42 screens, grossing about 164,000 Australian dollars. Reviews were positive. Writing for ArtsHub, reviewer Naavikaran gave it four stars, calling it fresh and funny and praising Mailman's performance, her middle-aged, non-skinny heroine and the mature treatment of grief. The Australian Council on Children and the Media recommended it for children six and over, praising its humor and voice cast. A sequel, Combat Wombat: Back 2 Back, was released in 2024.

documents.title: Monsters of Man
documents.overview: A robotics company vying to win a lucrative military contract team up with a corrupt CIA agent to conduct an illegal live field test. They deploy four weaponized prototype robots into a suspected drug manufacturing camp in the Golden Triangle, assuming they'd be killing drug runners that no one would miss. Six doctors on a humanitarian mission witness the brutal slaughter and become prime targets.
documents.plot:
Monsters of Man is an Australian independent science fiction action film written and directed by the cinematographer and commercials director Mark Toia. Neal McDonough stars as a rogue CIA officer, with Brett Tutor, Jose Rosete, David Haverty and Paul Haapaniemi. The story concerns an amoral robotics company that field-tests its military robots by unleashing them on unsuspecting people in the jungles of the Golden Triangle, while the CIA evaluates their effectiveness. High Octane Films released it on streaming and DVD in December 2020.

Offered the chance by a rogue CIA major to bid on a lucrative military contract, a robotics company illegally air-drops four prototype combat robots into the jungle in Cambodia to stage a live test against drug traffickers. A group of young volunteer doctors who have strayed into the area witness the machines massacring an entire village, and on the orders of the company's chief executive the robots are set to hunt them down to eliminate witnesses. Unknown to the CIA, a former Navy SEAL named Mason has been living in the village, and he takes it upon himself to protect the surviving villagers and doctors.

From a nearby base, the company's engineers, Kroger, Fielding and Jantz, watch the slaughter with mounting horror, never having been told that indiscriminate killing was part of the test. They want to pull out, but their CIA handler Boller threatens their lives and their families, and they continue, not without a degree of pride in their creations' performance. One robot, BR4, damaged on landing, begins showing signs of self-awareness, resisting the team's attempts to shut it down or trigger its self-destruct, and seeking to upload a backup of itself to the internet so that it can escape the jungle.

As the executives decide to preserve BR4's evolving core, the engineers send the other robots after it, and Boller heads into the rainforest to mark it for a drone strike that will also wipe out any surviving witnesses. Mason leads the survivors in a desperate effort to evade and destroy the machines. In the end BR4, having learned the value of life, activates its self-destruct to protect the remaining humans, killing Boller and the last operational robot. Afterwards, as the CIA officer calls the operation a complete mess, the company chief declares the test a massive success.

Critics praised the quality of the robot effects, calling them better than those of many blockbusters, but found it overlong.

documents.title: Love Hard
documents.tagline: A romantic comedy about the lies we tell for love.
documents.overview: An LA girl, unlucky in love, falls for an East Coast guy on a dating app and decides to surprise him for Christmas, only to discover that she's been catfished. But the object of her affection actually lives in the same town, and the guy who duped her offers to set them up if she pretends to be his own girlfriend for the holidays.
documents.plot: An LA girl, unlucky in love, falls for an East Coast guy on a dating app and decides to surprise him for Christmas, only to discover that she's been catfished. But the object of her affection actually lives in the same town, and the guy who duped her offers to set them up if she pretends to be his own girlfriend for the holidays.

documents.title: Midnight at the Magnolia
documents.tagline: This New Year's Eve, the countdown to love is on.
documents.overview: Longtime friends and local radio hosts Maggie and Jack fake it as a couple for their families and listeners in hopes of getting their show syndicated.
documents.plot:
Midnight at the Magnolia is a 2020 Canadian romantic comedy television film directed by Max McGuire and written by Carley Smale. Produced by Neshama Entertainment, it stars Natalie Hall and Evan Williams, with Alison Brooks, Steve Cumyn, Michael Gordin Shore, Susan Hamann, Hannah Gordon, Victoria Maria, Peter Michael Dillon and Sean Williams. Although set in Chicago, it was shot in Ottawa in January 2020, before the COVID-19 pandemic, and was released on Netflix on 5 November 2020.

Maggie Quinn (Hall) and Jack Russo (Williams), best friends since childhood, host Windy City Wake-Up, a morning radio show known for its relationship advice. When an on-air chat about introducing their partners to their families becomes a hit, their producer Deb (Brooks) tells them that a larger network, run by Judd Crawford (Dillon), wants to syndicate them nationally, provided they introduce their partners live during a New Year's Eve broadcast. Jack proposes holding the event at the Magnolia, the struggling restaurant and jazz club co-owned by their fathers Steve (Cumyn) and Martin (Shore). Days after Christmas, however, both are dumped, Maggie by her boyfriend Seb (Sean Williams). To save the opportunity, Jack suggests they pretend to be a couple. When Jack's parents catch them in a staged kiss, both families are overjoyed, having long believed they belonged together. Maggie's sister Amanda (Maria) sees that Maggie has always loved Jack, and Steve hands Jack the ring of Maggie's late mother. Jack's high-school girlfriend Bianca Bell (Gordon) tells him that Maggie was heartbroken when he did not take her to the prom, and that she broke up with him because he loved Maggie. After Jack forgets a dinner marking the anniversary of her mother's death, Maggie tells him he always puts her second. At the party Judd floats the idea of giving them separate shows, and as midnight approaches the pair confess on air that the relationship was a sham. Maggie leaves the stage, but Jack declares his love, turns down a solo show and sings a song he wrote for her, and they share a real midnight kiss. A year later he proposes with her mother's ring.

Reviews were mixed. Kirsten Hawkes of Parent Previews gave it a B+, finding Hall and Williams charming enough to carry an unremarkable script, while Roger Moore of Movie Nation called it as bland as bargain-shelf white bread and lamented the leads' lack of chemistry. It was nominated for Best TV Movie at the 2022 Canadian Screen Awards.

documents.title: Don't Kill Me
documents.overview: After Mirta dies of a drug overdose with her lover, she resuscitates alone and discovers she's part of a violent world she never knew existed.
documents.plot:
Don't Kill Me (Italian: Non mi uccidere) is an Italian romantic horror film from 2021, written and directed by Andrea De Sica and adapted from the young-adult novel of the same name by Chiara Palazzolo. Produced by Vivo Film with Warner Bros. Pictures Italia and support from the IDM Südtirol film fund, it stars Alice Pagani as Mirta and Rocco Fasano as Robin, with Silvia Calderoni as Sara, Fabrizio Ferracane as Luca Bertozzi and Anita Caprioli as Amalia. It was shot in South Tyrol and Rome.

The film opens with nineteen-year-old Mirta in a car with her boyfriend Robin, who drives recklessly with his eyes closed while she shouts directions at him. They stop at a quarry, where Robin persuades the nervous Mirta to try a drug with him for the first time; she agrees, asking him not to kill her. Both die of an overdose. Robin's death seems final, but a few hours after the funeral Mirta smashes her way out of her family's burial vault, confused and angry, and wanders back home to find her parents mourning her. Her hands show signs of necrosis, she drifts through her memories, and she discovers that she has a savage hunger for human flesh. She has become one of the "Overdead", people who return after a violent death: she is nearly immortal, can survive gunshots and will not age, but she will decay unless she regularly feeds on the living, and starvation is the only way to destroy her kind. Flashbacks fill in her romance with Robin, as she wonders whether a second life is worth living without him. Meanwhile, a centuries-old secret society, the Benandanti, has been tracking her resurrection, and its operatives, led by a man determined to capture and starve her, close in, revealing a violent world she never knew existed.

Don't Kill Me was released in Italy on digital download and video on demand on 21 April 2021, and on Netflix internationally in February 2022. Reviews were mixed. Alex Wiggan of It's a Stampede! found it a captivating little horror film with brisk storytelling, a gritty look, an effective soundtrack including a cover of 10cc's "I'm Not in Love" and a committed central performance by Pagani, despite its debts to Twilight. On Through the Shattered Lens, Lisa Marie Bowman praised the atmospheric first half, which recalled Jean Rollin and Jess Franco, as well as Pagani's sympathetic turn and Ferracane's villain, but felt that it lost its way once Mirta is captured and ended with an unsatisfying "to be continued" conclusion.
production_companies: IDM Südtirol - Alto Adige Film Fund

documents.title: Spin
documents.tagline: Music is everything.
documents.overview: Rhea lives with her tight-knit multigenerational family.
