After her mother’s death, she has been her father’s emotional rock, and her life revolves around her family’s restaurant, her eclectic group of friends, and her after-school coding club. Everything changes when she falls for aspiring DJ Max and a long lost passion for music is reignited. Rhea discovers that she has a natural gift for creating beats and producing music that blends her Indian heritage, but must find the courage to follow her true inner talent.
documents.plot:
Spin is a 2021 American comedy film made as a Disney Channel Original Movie. Directed by Manjari Makijany from a screenplay by Carley Steiner and Josh A. Cagan, it stars Avantika as Rhea Kumar, with Abhay Deol as her father Arvind, Meera Syal as her grandmother Asha, Aryan Simhadri as her younger brother Rohan, Michael Bishop as Max, and Jahbril Cook, Kerri Medders and Anna Cathcart as her friends. It premiered on Disney Channel on August 13, 2021.

Rhea is an Indian-American high school student whose mother, Meera, died eight years earlier. She juggles school with shifts at her family's restaurant, Spirit of India, where she works alongside her father, still grieving his wife, her brother and her nani, Asha. At school she and her friends Watson, Molly and Ginger are organizing a homecoming fundraiser inspired by the Hindu festival of Holi, and when Ginger's DJ falls through, Rhea recommends Max, a classmate and DJ she met during a dinner shift. The event is a success, and in return Max agrees to teach Rhea how to use a turntable. At a record store they meet their favorite DJ, Luka Cent, who encourages them to enter a competition called the Battle of the Beatmasters. Rhea discovers a real talent for mixing music and helps Max create a track, but her new passion causes her to neglect the restaurant and her schoolwork. When Max fails to credit her at the fundraiser, the two argue, and her father grounds her for two months. Heartbroken, Rhea turns to her grandmother, who gives her a box of her mother's belongings, including her cassettes. Inspired by her mother's music, and urged on by her friends, who enter her in the contest themselves, Rhea begins crafting a track of her own that blends her family's heritage with her new sound, while she still has to face her father and decide whether to compete against Max.

Spin received mostly positive reviews, with praise for its performances and the way it subverts typical Disney Channel tropes. Paste's Amy Amatangelo welcomed its limited focus on romance, and Mashable's Proma Khosla wrote that it fits naturally into the Disney Channel movie library.

documents.title: The Boss Baby: Get That Baby!
documents.original_title: The Boss Baby: Get That Baby!
documents.overview: Think you've got what it takes to be the boss? This interactive special puts your skills to the test and matches you up with one of 16 jobs at Baby Corp.
documents.plot:
The Boss Baby: Get That Baby! is an animated film that explores several themes, primarily centered around family dynamics and the challenges of sibling relationships. At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of brotherly love and rivalry, as the titular character, Tim Templeton, navigates his complicated bond with his new baby brother, Francis Francis E. Francis.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and self-discovery, particularly for Tim, who struggles to adjust to his new role as a big brother. As he tries to balance his responsibilities towards Francis with his own desires and interests, Tim learns valuable lessons about empathy, responsibility, and the importance of family.

Furthermore, The Boss Baby: Get That Baby! explores the theme of corporate culture and the cutthroat world of business, as embodied by the villainous Francis Francis E. Francis, who is determined to take over Puppy Co. and become the top dog in the company. This subplot adds a layer of satire to the film, poking fun at the excesses of corporate America and the consequences of prioritizing profits over people.

Ultimately, the movie's themes are woven together by its exploration of family values and the importance of finding one's place within the family unit. Through Tim's journey, the film shows that even in the midst of chaos and conflict, love and support can be found, and that being a good sibling is just as important as being a good child.

documents.title: The Scary House
documents.overview: When a big-city family moves to a remote town, two young brothers and their new friends try to solve the menacing mystery that haunts their home.
documents.plot:
The Scary House (German: Das schaurige Haus) is a 2020 Austrian-German family horror film directed by Daniel Prochaska, his first feature for cinemas. The screenplay by Marcel Kawentel and Timo Lombeck adapts the 2011 novel of the same name by Martina Wildner, part of her Allgäu horror trilogy. It stars León Orlandianyi, Benno Rosskopf and Julia Koschitz, and was produced by Gerald Podgornig and Thomas Hroch of Austria's Mona Film with Germany's Naked Eye Filmproduktion, in association with ORF.

Sixteen-year-old Hendrik (Orlandianyi) moves with his mother Sabine (Koschitz) and his eight-year-old brother Eddi (Rosskopf) from Hanover to Bad Eisenkappel in Carinthia, where Sabine has taken a job at the Obir dripstone caves. The move is also meant to help the family cope with the father's death in an accident. For Hendrik it is a culture shock: the locals speak a dialect he can barely understand, and something seems wrong with the run-down house that estate agent Gerold Röckl (Michael Pink) found for them. Eddi starts sleepwalking and speaking Slovene, Hendrik is plagued by nightmares, and their mother grows increasingly desperate. After a difficult start the brothers make friends with the bold Ida (Marii Weichsler) and the nerdy Fritz (Lars Bitterlich), and the four set out to uncover the secret of the house.

The film departs from the book in several ways: the brothers were made older, they arrive with their widowed mother rather than both parents, and because the setting moved from the Allgäu to Carinthia, Slovene replaced the novel's Romanian. It was shot over 34 days in the summer of 2019 in Vienna and southern Carinthia. Following a premiere at the Wildenstein waterfall in Gallizien in September 2020 and a screening at Vienna's SLASH festival, it opened in Austrian cinemas on 30 October 2020 and reached Netflix in May 2021, where it entered the top ten in more than 50 countries.

Germany's film rating agency FBW gave it the rating "particularly valuable", praising suspense that goes well beyond typical children's adventures and a well-timed horror effect. Christian Klosz of Film plus Kritik commended its story, witty dialogue and the culture clash between the city family and local Carinthian colour, and The New York Times called it an effective family horror film. It won the audience award for best youth film at the Goldener Spatz and earned four Austrian Film Award nominations, including for Koschitz and Pink.

documents.title: Justice Society: World War II
documents.tagline: The fight for justice is the greatest battle of all time.
documents.overview: When the Flash finds himself dropped into the middle of World War II, he joins forces with Wonder Woman and her top-secret team known as the Justice Society of America.
documents.plot:
Justice Society: World War II is a 2021 animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation. The movie takes place during World War II and follows the adventures of a team of superheroes from the Justice Society of America, a precursor to the modern-day Justice League.

The story begins with Alan Scott (voiced by Jason O'Mara), a young man who discovers he has the ability to control fire after being struck by lightning. He becomes the superhero known as the Green Lantern and joins forces with other heroes, including Hawkman (voiced by Paddy Considine) and Doctor Fate (voiced by Seth Gabel). Together, they form the Justice Society of America.

As World War II rages on, the Justice Society is recruited by the United States government to help fight against the Nazis. The team soon discovers that the Nazis have teamed up with a villainous sorcerer named Black Adam (voiced by Darik Hilliard), who seeks to conquer the world and destroy all magic.

The Green Lantern, Hawkman, Doctor Fate, and their allies embark on a perilous journey across Europe, battling against Nazi forces and facing off against Black Adam's minions. Along the way, they meet other heroes from different eras, including Wildcat (voiced by James Arnold Taylor), Stargirl (voiced by Meghie Deysac), and Hour-Man (voiced by Matt Bomer).

As the war intensifies, the Justice Society discovers that Black Adam's ultimate goal is to summon an ancient evil known as Shazam, who will grant him immense power. The team must stop Black Adam and his minions before it's too late.

The movie features a mix of action, adventure, and humor, with plenty of nods to classic comic book characters and storylines. The animation is vibrant and engaging, bringing the world of the Justice Society to life in a way that feels both nostalgic and fresh.

Throughout the film, the heroes face numerous challenges and setbacks, but ultimately, they work together to defeat Black Adam and save the world from destruction. In the end, the Justice Society emerges victorious, having saved countless lives and proved themselves as true champions of justice.

Overall, Justice Society: World War II is a thrilling and entertaining ride that celebrates the spirit of teamwork and heroism. With its richly detailed world-building and memorable characters, it's a must-see for fans of superhero movies and comic books alike.

documents.title: Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One
documents.original_title: Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One
documents.tagline: Naughty or nice. Trick or treat. Hero or villain.
documents.overview: Following a brutal series of murders taking place on Halloween, Thanksgiving, and Christmas, Gotham City's young vigilante known as the Batman sets out to pursue the mysterious serial killer alongside police officer James Gordon and district attorney Harvey Dent.
documents.plot:
Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One is a 2021 animated superhero film directed by Chris Palmer and produced by Bruce Timm, Sam Register, and Michael Goguen. The movie is based on the comic book series of the same name by Jeph Loeb and Tim Sale.

The story begins with James Gordon Jr., the son of Commissioner James Gordon, being kidnapped by a group of thugs. Young James Jr. is taken to an abandoned warehouse where he witnesses a murder committed by a mysterious figure known as Holiday Killer. The film then jumps forward in time to show James Gordon Sr. becoming the new commissioner of Gotham City.

As Commissioner Gordon, he faces various challenges and villains, including the Riddler (Edward Nigma), who has returned to Gotham after a long absence. The Riddler is determined to prove his intellectual superiority over Batman by committing a series of murders and leaving clues for him to solve.

Meanwhile, Bruce Wayne is struggling with his own demons as he tries to balance his life as a billionaire philanthropist with his nocturnal activities as the Dark Knight. He is haunted by nightmares and struggles to connect with his parents' memory.

The story takes a dark turn when the Holiday Killer strikes again, targeting Commissioner Gordon's family. The killer is revealed to be none other than Harvey Dent, who has been driven mad by his own guilt and sense of justice.

As Batman delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that the Holiday Killer is using an antique calendar as a symbol of their crimes. He also encounters the Riddler, who is determined to outsmart him at every turn.

The film ends with Batman and Harvey Dent forming an uneasy alliance to take down the Holiday Killer, but not before the killer reveals that they have one final target in mind: Commissioner Gordon's family.

Overall, Batman: The Long Halloween, Part One sets the stage for a thrilling and complex story that explores the darker side of Gotham City. With its intricate plot, memorable characters, and stunning animation, this film is sure to delight fans of the Batman franchise.

documents.title: Batman: The Long Halloween, Part Two
documents.original_title: Batman: The Long Halloween, Part Two
documents.tagline: The clock is ticking. The days are numbered. The end has just begun.
documents.overview: As Gotham City's young vigilante, the Batman, struggles to pursue a brutal serial killer, district attorney Harvey Dent gets caught in a feud involving the criminal family of the Falcones.
documents.plot:
Batman: The Long Halloween, Part Two is a 2021 American animated superhero mystery film produced by Warner Bros. Animation and DC Entertainment, the concluding half of a two-part adaptation of the DC Comics storyline of the same name. Directed by Chris Palmer, it is the 46th entry in the DC Universe Animated Original Movies line. Jensen Ackles voices Bruce Wayne / Batman, Josh Duhamel plays Harvey Dent / Two-Face and Naya Rivera plays Selina Kyle / Catwoman in her final film role, with Billy Burke as Captain Gordon, Titus Welliver as Carmine Falcone, Julie Nathanson as Gilda Dent, Troy Baker as the Joker and Katee Sackhoff as Poison Ivy. The two-part film is dedicated to Rivera's memory.

In the three months since Alberto Falcone's death, the Holiday killer has struck the Falcone and Maroni crime families on Valentine's Day, Saint Patrick's Day and April Fools' Day, while Bruce, under Poison Ivy's control, has signed many of his assets over to Falcone until Catwoman rescues him. Scarecrow's fear toxin forces Batman to relive his parents' deaths, and Bruce recalls how his father once saved Falcone's life. After Holiday kills Luigi Maroni on Father's Day, Sal Maroni offers to testify against Falcone, and Batman later finds Holiday's guns in the Dents' basement. In court, Maroni accuses Harvey of being Holiday and throws acid in his face. Disfigured, Harvey escapes from a trap set by Falcone's men and finds refuge in the sewers with Solomon Grundy. Batman learns that Catwoman is Falcone's daughter, while Harvey, now calling himself Two-Face, frees inmates from Arkham Asylum and leads an assault on Falcone's building, killing the mob boss, whose daughter Sofia also dies. Two-Face surrenders, claiming responsibility for the murders, but Batman confronts Gilda, the woman Alberto once loved, and discovers she is the true killer, driven by hatred of Falcone.

Batman: The Long Halloween was announced in August 2020 at DC FanDome, and its voice cast was revealed in March 2021. Part One was released in June 2021; Part Two was made available on digital platforms on 27 July 2021 and on DVD and Blu-ray on 10 August, and a deluxe edition combining both parts followed in September 2022. Critics praised it as a satisfying conclusion: ComicBookMovie and IGN commended its epic resolution and the way it wrapped up the main plot threads, CBR lauded its dynamic portrayal of DC's villains and strong character development.

documents.title: Intersect
documents.tagline: Never is safe.
documents.overview: A group of young Miskatonic University scientists invent a time machine, only to learn that they are being manipulated by mysterious, unseen forces from another dimension.
documents.plot:
Intersect is a 2020 American science fiction thriller written and directed by Gus Holwerda in his feature debut, following his documentary about atheism, The Unbelievers. Jason Spisak, who also produced, stars as the physicist Ryan Winrich, with Leeann Dearing as Caitlin Webb, Abe Ruthless as Nate Beaumont, James Morrison as their mentor Bill Marshall and Jose Rosete as Abner Rosen; the scientist Richard Dawkins voices the laboratory computer, Quantum 42, and the physicist Lawrence Krauss appears as a professor. Dartagnan Driscoll, Kelcey Bligh, Ryan Adelson and Jacob Lacy play the main characters as children.

Ryan, Caitlin and Nate, friends since childhood, are young researchers at Miskatonic University, the fictional institution in Arkham, Massachusetts, borrowed from the fiction of H. P. Lovecraft. Their project is a machine that can send physical objects through time, and after several test mice are destroyed, they find the setting that lets matter pass safely through space-time. Nate, who turns out to be Caitlin's boyfriend, has a few drinks one night and decides to become the first person to travel through the portal himself, and the attempt kills him.

From this point the film moves backward, retracing the three friends' shared past through their high-school years, when they studied physics under the inspiring teacher Mr. Marshall, faced bullying, and dealt with grief, with a religious subplot running alongside. Ryan comes to suspect that the experiment is connected to strange events from his own childhood, when he could see creatures invisible to everyone else. In the closing stretch the story reveals itself as a time-loop paradox: the scientists have been manipulated all along by unseen, sinister observers from another dimension, Lovecraftian beings drawn by their work, and the ending is left open. The film is full of nods to its influences, including a model of the machine from the 1960 version of The Time Machine and a reference to Flatland.

After a festival premiere in Boston, at the Boston SciFi Film Festival on 12 February 2020, Intersect was released on video on demand that September. Reviews were mostly negative. JoBlo's critic found it overlong, disjointed and melodramatic, with weak computer effects, though better in its last half-hour; Moria judged its reverse coming-of-age story less interesting than the time-travel premise; and Rue Morgue called the final reveal satisfying but the journey a slog.

documents.title: Troll
documents.tagline: Mountains will move.
documents.overview: Deep inside the mountain of Dovre, something gigantic awakens after being trapped for a thousand years. Destroying everything in its path, the creature is fast approaching the capital of Norway. But how do you stop something you thought only existed in Norwegian folklore?
documents.plot:
Troll is a 2022 Norwegian epic monster film directed by Roar Uthaug and written by Espen Auken, starring Ine Marie Wilmann, Kim Falck, Mads Sjøgård Pettersen and Gard B. Eidsvold. It follows a ragtag group who must stop an ancient giant troll awakened inside a Norwegian mountain before it wreaks havoc across the country. Uthaug developed the project with Motion Blur as his film Tomb Raider was nearing completion, drawing on a folklore-inspired idea he had been considering for more than twenty years. Principal photography took place from August to November 2021, with locations including Dovre, Lom, Askim and Ulsteinvik, and the score was written by Johannes Ringen.

As a child, Nora Tidemann listens to her father Tobias tell stories about trolls and how they shaped the mountains. Years later, a tunneling operation through the mountains of Dovre triggers an eruption that kills workers and protesters. Nora, now a paleontologist, is recruited by the government along with other experts, and while most blame a methane pocket, she and the prime minister's adviser Andreas notice that the area is marked by enormous impressions resembling footprints. When a second incident destroys a house near Lesja, Nora, Andreas and Captain Kris Holm of the Norwegian special forces seek help from Tobias, who lost his professorship for believing that myths had a basis in fact. In the mountains, they accidentally awaken a troll some 50 metres tall that had been camouflaged against the mountainside, capturing the first video proof of its existence. Military attacks only irritate the creature, Tobias is killed while trying to communicate with it, and an attempt to repel it with church bells, based on old legends, instead sends it on a destructive rampage. As the troll heads for Oslo and the government prepares a drastic nuclear option, Nora and Andreas follow Tobias's notes to the Royal Palace, where they uncover a long-buried secret about the fate of Norway's trolls, transforming Nora's understanding of the creature and what drives it.

Netflix released Troll on 1 December 2022. It received generally positive reviews, holding a 90% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus says that its rich mythology and exciting action make up for a familiar monster-movie formula, and a Metacritic score of 62. A sequel, Troll 2, was released in 2025.

documents.title: Broker
documents.tagline: Some Leave. Some Retrieve.
documents.overview: Boxes are left out for people to anonymously drop off their unwanted babies.
documents.plot:
Broker is a 2022 South Korean black comedy film directed by Lee Chang-dong and written by Park Chan-wook. The movie stars Song Kang-ho, Lee Jung-eun, and Park Hae-il.

The story revolves around Sung-su (played by Song Kang-ho), a middle-aged man who has been working as an orphanage director for over 20 years. He is known for his strict rules and harsh treatment of the children in his care. However, after being fired from his job due to a scandal involving one of the orphans, Sung-su finds himself at a crossroads.

He decides to become a real estate agent, but he soon discovers that it's not as easy as he thought it would be. He is forced to work for a corrupt and ruthless broker named Jang (played by Park Hae-il), who takes advantage of his naivety and pushes him to sell properties to desperate clients.

As Sung-su navigates the cutthroat world of real estate, he meets a young woman named Yeon-kyo (played by Lee Jung-eun), who is also working as an agent. Despite their initial differences, they develop a complicated relationship, with Sung-su becoming increasingly obsessed with her.

Throughout the movie, Sung-su's character undergoes significant development as he confronts his own flaws and weaknesses. He begins to question his values and morals, particularly when it comes to his treatment of children in the orphanage. As he becomes more entrenched in the world of real estate, he is forced to confront the harsh realities of the industry and the people who work within it.

One of the most striking aspects of Broker is its exploration of themes such as class struggle, social inequality, and the exploitation of vulnerable individuals. The movie sheds light on the dark underbelly of South Korea's real estate market, where desperate people are often taken advantage of by ruthless brokers like Jang.

The film also features a number of memorable supporting characters, including Sung-su's eccentric colleagues and clients. These characters add to the movie's humor and satire, highlighting the absurdity and cruelty of the real estate industry.

Ultimately, Broker is a thought-provoking and unflinching critique of the social and economic systems that perpetuate inequality and exploitation. Through its complex characters and nuanced exploration of themes, the movie offers a searing indictment of the darker aspects of human nature.

The ending of the film is both haunting and thought-provoking, leaving the audience to ponder the consequences of Sung-su's actions and the broader implications of the real estate industry. Overall, Broker is a masterful work of cinematic storytelling that will leave viewers on the edge of their seats and lingering long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Making The Witcher
documents.overview: Journey into the extraordinary world of "The Witcher" — from casting the roles to Jaskier's catchy song — in this behind-the-scenes look at the series. Go behind the monsters, the ballads and every bit of magic that went into bringing The Witcher's Continent to life.
documents.plot:
Making The Witcher is a 2020 British behind-the-scenes documentary special about the first season of the Netflix fantasy series The Witcher, adapted from the novels and stories of the Polish author Andrzej Sapkowski. Produced by The Workhouse Picture Company and running about 32 minutes, it was released on Netflix on 26 August 2020. It features interviews with showrunner Lauren Schmidt Hissrich, executive producer Tomek Bagiński and cast members including Henry Cavill, Anya Chalotra, Freya Allan, Joey Batey, Eamon Farren, Adam Levy, Mimi Ndiweni and MyAnna Buring.

The special was released during the long gap between the first and second seasons, when production of the second season had been halted by the COVID-19 pandemic, and it revisits the making of the first. Netflix promoted it as a journey into the world of the show, from the casting of the main roles to the bard Jaskier's catchy song "Toss a Coin to Your Witcher", and as a look behind the monsters, the ballads and the magic that went into bringing the Continent to the screen. Across its half-hour running time it touches on the history of the Continent and the first season's non-linear timeline, the relationships between Geralt of Rivia, Yennefer and Ciri, the show's magic system, the importance of the property in Poland, and the series' portrayal of women, with Chalotra praising Sapkowski's complex female characters. It also covers the design of the creatures, built through a combination of practical effects and computer-generated imagery, as well as costume and set design and their architectural influences, the fight choreography, and the experiences of the episode writers, among them Declan de Barra, who wrote the fourth episode, "Of Banquets, Bastards and Burials". The actors also discuss how they approached their characters, frequently complimenting one another's work.

Reception was mixed. Writing for FilmObserver, a self-described devoted fan of the franchise found the special rushed and more like an extended commercial than a documentary, arguing that it tried to cram far too many subjects into 30 minutes and lingered on familiar backstory at the expense of genuine behind-the-scenes material. The reviewer nonetheless enjoyed the too-brief segments on monster creation, costume and set design, which offered real production footage rather than clips from the show, as well as de Barra's insights and the actors' interviews.

documents.title: The Noel Diary
documents.overview: Cleaning out his childhood home at Christmas, a novelist meets a woman searching for her birth mother. Will an old diary unlock their pasts — and hearts?
documents.plot:
The Noel Diary is a 2022 American Christmas romantic drama directed by Charles Shyer, his final film before his death in 2024, and based on Richard Paul Evans's novel of the same name. Justin Hartley stars as Jake Turner, a best-selling author, with Barrett Doss as Rachel Campbell, Bonnie Bedelia, Essence Atkins and James Remar. Netflix released the film on 24 November 2022.

Jake, a successful novelist, learns from a lawyer that his estranged mother, Lois, has died and left him everything, including her house in Connecticut. Returning home for the first time since leaving at seventeen, twenty years earlier, he sets about clearing out the cluttered house, which his mother filled with hoarded belongings, and settling her estate. He reconnects with Ellie, the kindly next-door neighbor, who tells him that his father, Scott, who abandoned the family after Jake's older brother died in an accident as a child, attended the funeral hoping to see him. Ellie also enlists Jake's help with a dating app.

Among his mother's things, Jake discovers a diary, and at the same moment Rachel Campbell, a woman who has been watching the house, introduces herself. She is searching for her birth mother, Noel, who it turns out was once Jake's nanny and wrote the diary. Over dinner, at which Rachel insists on splitting the bill, not realizing how successful Jake is, she explains that she values certainty and stability, including her engagement to Alan, a tax attorney, and hopes that finding her birth mother will fill a void she has felt since being adopted. Despite their attraction, Jake and Rachel set off on a road trip together to follow the clues in the diary. Their search leads them to people from Noel's past and forces Jake to confront long-buried memories of his brother's death, his mother's grief and his father's absence, while Rachel must decide whether the life she has planned is the one she truly wants.

The Noel Diary received generally favorable reviews. It holds a 69 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on sixteen reviews and a Metacritic score of 63, with critics describing it as a more thoughtful and melancholy alternative to typical holiday romances and praising the chemistry of Hartley and Doss.

documents.title: Swingers
documents.overview: Observational documentary unlocking the doors of Britain's hidden swinging scene via access to one of the country's most popular swinging clubs and candid interviews with the club's founder, staff and clientele.
documents.plot:
Swingers is a 2020 British observational documentary made for Channel 4, which broadcast it on 24 August 2020; the 47-minute film, which credits Belinda Stewart-Wilson, later remained available on the channel's streaming service All 4. One of Channel 4's observational documentaries exploring British sexuality, likened by reviewers to programmes such as A Very British Brothel and Dogging Tales, it unlocks the doors of Britain's hidden swinging scene through unusually open access to Liberty Elite, a swinging and fetish club with around 12,000 members and one of roughly 200 such clubs in the United Kingdom, at a time when, according to the programme, more than 1.5 million Britons take part in swinging.

The documentary centres on Valentine's Day, one of the biggest nights in the club's calendar. Behind the scenes, the 78-year-old owner John painstakingly uncovers the jacuzzi and prepares a buffet of cocktail sausages, dips and crisps, while the manager, Chantelle, puts up heart-shaped decorations; the club also hosts regular themed evenings such as Mature Mischief on Wednesdays. The film then follows several guests as they pack their lingerie and sex toys for the night and talk candidly to the camera about their lives. Siobhan, 67 and single, enjoys a joyful sex life through swinging and has a playroom of her own. Justin and Hannah, who have been swinging at home for two years, are visiting the club for the first time. Simon and Carolyn, a couple who have swung for four years and feel it strengthens their connection, are dismayed by the poor grammar of some messages on swinging apps. Malika, a single mother and lap dancer, says she has not met a decent man in thirty years, and Martyn turned to the scene after a bad break-up. Interviews touch on difficult episodes in some of the guests' pasts, and the film also shows the morning-after clean-up, as staff deal with what has been left behind.

Reviewers welcomed its candour. Barbara Speed of the i called it a pleasingly banal, human look at British swinging rather than a display of glamour, though she found the interviewer's repeated questions about whether guests were looking for love irritating, concluding that the real taboo was the idea that people might enjoy swinging for its own sake. Rhiannon Evans of Grazia hailed it as the best documentary of 2020, noting that it caused a stir on social media and praising its warm, sympathetic and non-judgemental approach.

documents.title: The Doorman
documents.tagline: Be careful who you trust.
documents.overview: A former Marine turned doorman at a luxury New York City high-rise must outsmart and battle a group of art thieves and their ruthless leader — while struggling to protect her sister's family. As the thieves become increasingly desperate and violent, the doorman calls upon her deadly fighting skills to end the showdown.
documents.plot:
The Doorman is a 2020 American action thriller directed by Ryuhei Kitamura. Ruby Rose stars as Ali Gorski, a former Marine who takes a job as a doorman at a luxury building, with Jean Reno as the criminal mastermind Victor Dubois, Aksel Hennie as Borz, and Rupert Evans as her brother-in-law Jon Stanton. The film follows Ali as she defends her family from a gang of thieves searching for valuable artworks hidden inside the building. It was first released theatrically in Russia on 1 October 2020, followed by a direct-to-digital release in the United States on 9 October 2020.

In Bucharest, Marine Gunnery Sergeant Ali Gorski is protecting a convoy carrying an ambassador's family when it is ambushed by mercenaries. Despite fighting fiercely, she cannot prevent the deaths of the ambassador, his wife and their daughter. Traumatised, Ali leaves the Marines and returns to New York City, where her uncle Pat helps her get a job as a doorman at the Carrington, an elegant old apartment building.

Ali discovers that the building is also home to Jon Stanton, the widower of her late sister, and his children, Max and Lily. She and Jon had an affair while her sister was alive, which was partly why Ali enlisted, and she reluctantly accepts an invitation to their Easter dinner. Over the holiday weekend, her fellow doorman Borz kills Pat, revealing himself to be part of a crew led by Victor Dubois. The thieves lock down the building in search of a collection of stolen paintings hidden somewhere in its walls, and they torture an elderly resident, living under an assumed name, who once concealed them. Learning that the paintings are in the apartment now occupied by the Stantons, the gang takes Jon and Lily hostage while Max escapes. Ali must use her combat training to fight her way through the building, outwitting the mercenaries floor by floor, with Max helping her through clever tricks such as sending a message in Morse code over the building's intercom.

The film borrows the single-building siege structure of Die Hard, with a female protagonist at its centre, and it is built around a series of close-quarters fight scenes staged by Kitamura.

The Doorman received negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 24 percent; the consensus says that it only leads to an assortment of tired clichés that serve as reminders of better action films.

documents.title: Barbie: Princess Adventure
documents.tagline: Life doesn't happen on camera. Life is what happens when the cameras are off.
documents.overview: With new friends in a new kingdom, Barbie learns what it means to be herself when she trades places with a royal lookalike in this musical adventure.
documents.plot:
Barbie: Princess Adventure is a 2020 computer-animated musical adventure comedy television film directed by Conrad Helten and written by Ann Austen. Released on Netflix in the United States on September 1, 2020, it is the 37th entry in the Barbie film series and the first feature adaptation of the series Barbie: Dreamhouse Adventures. America Young voices Barbie, with Erica Lindbeck as Princess Amelia, Ritesh Rajan as Ken, Dave Fennoy as the royal adviser Alfonso and Angelo Restaino as Prince Johan.

Barbie is an American teenager who hopes to inspire others through her vlog but has only a small audience. She and her friends receive an all-expenses-paid invitation to the European kingdom of Floravia, not realizing that the trip has been arranged with a hidden agenda by Floravia's Princess Amelia. By watching Barbie's videos, Amelia has noticed that the two look almost identical. Her life and her picture-perfect public image are rigidly controlled by Alfonso, and she has never been allowed to find her own identity or voice. She proposes that the two switch places for a week before her coronation, so that she can finally experience life outside the palace gates.

Barbie agrees, and while Amelia enjoys her week of freedom, Barbie takes on the role of princess, sharing dances with Prince Johan, Amelia's fiancé from a neighboring kingdom. Barbie also faces a dilemma of her own when an unscrupulous content aggregator offers her a major platform, forcing her to decide what changes she is willing to accept. Johan uncovers the ruse and kidnaps the princess, hoping to force Amelia to marry him so that he can rule both his country and Floravia, and Barbie too is captured. With help from Ken, their friends and Barbie's puppies, Barbie and Amelia escape and foil Johan's plot. Amelia is crowned, Alfonso learns to trust her to make her own decisions, and both girls resolve to stay true to themselves.

Produced by Mattel Television and Mainframe Studios, the film was the first Barbie production from Mattel Television after its 2019 rebrand. Its soundtrack album was released digitally on August 28, 2020. Jennifer Green of Common Sense Media praised its diverse cast, snappy music, contemporary dancing and messages of self-affirmation and living offline, writing that these animated adventures offer upbeat fun, while Screen Rant noted its similarities to the Princess Switch films.

documents.title: The Haunting of Margam Castle
documents.tagline: The most haunted building in the United Kingdom.
documents.overview: A team of American parapsychologists travel to Wales to conduct a study of Margam Castle, one of the UK's most haunted buildings.
documents.plot:
The Haunting of Margam Castle is a 2020 British supernatural horror film written and directed by Andrew Jones, his twenty-fifth feature in seven years, and produced by North Bank Entertainment with his wife Sharron Jones as co-producer. Set and shot at Margam Castle, a Tudor-Gothic country house built in the 1830s near Port Talbot in South Wales and long reputed to be one of the most haunted buildings in Britain, it stars Amy Quick and Ashton Spear alongside a group of veteran genre actors: Derren Nesbitt, Jane Merrow, Caroline Munro, Judy Matheson, Garrick Hagon and Vernon Dobtcheff. It was released in September 2020 and runs 81 minutes.

At an American university, Professor Annie Holzer (Quick) and Dr. Daniel Barron (Spear) are told by their dean (Hagon) to boost the department's flagging finances with a study of Margam Castle in Wales, a place he doubts they have even heard of. They assemble a team of parapsychologists and cross the Atlantic, encountering superstitious locals and cultural differences before arriving to spend the night in the castle. The historian Hugh Morgan (Nesbitt) supplies its history and the psychic Edith Withers (Merrow) her expertise, but the researchers soon find themselves trying to survive the ghostly figures that inhabit the building, drawn from the castle's legends of a gamekeeper and children in Victorian clothing, as messages appear on mirrors and a sinister little girl haunts them.

In an interview with The Schlock Pit, Jones said that his producing partner Rob Graham suggested the castle after a ghost walk there, and that the building offered a level of production value far beyond his earlier films. Influenced by Pete Walker's House of the Long Shadows and Hammer films, he cast Munro, Merrow and Matheson because they had appeared in Hammer productions, and praised the cast for enduring cold November night shoots and cinematographer Jon McLaughlin for capturing the Gothic atmosphere with limited lighting. The Schlock Pit called it an admirable British horror film in which the castle is the star. Richard E. Rock, a novelist who lives near the castle, was less impressed, finding the story thin, the characters dull, the performances wobbly and the clichés plentiful, but praised Nesbitt and the beautifully shot location and called it an interesting curio.

documents.title: Operation Christmas Drop
documents.overview: While gathering evidence to support closing a tropical U.S. Air Force base, a congressional aide warms to its generous captain.
documents.plot:
Operation Christmas Drop is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the themes of love, redemption, and the power of human connection during the most wonderful time of the year. The movie tells the story of Captain Brixton "Bryce" Walker (played by Noah Centineo), a U.S. Air Force pilot who returns to his hometown on Christmas Eve after a decade away.

As Bryce navigates his complicated past and reconnects with old friends, he finds himself drawn to a kind-hearted local woman named Kat Meredith (played by Kathryn Newton). Through their blossoming romance, the film showcases the transformative power of love and second chances. The movie also delves into themes of community, small-town charm, and the importance of embracing one's roots.

One of the most significant themes in Operation Christmas Drop is the idea that everyone deserves a fresh start and a chance to rediscover themselves. Bryce, in particular, must confront his past mistakes and learn to forgive himself and others. The film's portrayal of this theme is both poignant and uplifting, making it a delightful holiday watch.

Overall, Operation Christmas Drop is a feel-good movie that celebrates the magic of Christmas, the beauty of small-town America, and the human spirit's capacity for love, forgiveness, and redemption.

documents.title: Copshop
documents.tagline: Someone's gotta take the hit.
documents.overview: On the run from a lethal assassin, a wily con artist devises a scheme to hide out inside a small-town police station. However, when the hit man turns up at the precinct, an unsuspecting rookie cop finds herself caught in the crosshairs.
documents.plot:
Copshop is a 2021 American neo-noir action thriller directed by Joe Carnahan, who co-wrote the screenplay with Kurt McLeod from a story by McLeod and Mark Williams. Gerard Butler, Frank Grillo and Alexis Louder head the cast, supported by Toby Huss and Chad L. Coleman. Almost the entire story unfolds inside a small-town police station that turns into a battlefield between a hired killer, a rookie officer and a fast-talking con man. STXfilms released the film in the United Kingdom in September 2021, with an American release by Open Road Films following the same month.

Grillo plays Teddy Murretto, a fixer and con artist on the run from people who want him dead. When his bullet-riddled car breaks down near the desert town of Gun Creek, Nevada, he deliberately punches rookie officer Valerie Young, played by Louder, so that he will be arrested and locked away from his pursuers. His plan unravels when hitman Bob Viddick, played by Butler, stages a drunk-driving incident and gets himself booked into the very same station. From their neighbouring cells, Viddick calmly lets Murretto know who he is and why he has come.

Tension escalates when a hidden incendiary device sets off the fire alarm, a corrupt officer is caught up in the scheme, and Viddick attempts to break free and finish his job. Young, a sharp-shooting and quick-thinking officer, intervenes and begins to piece together what is happening. Murretto explains that his criminal employers had sent him to bribe the state attorney general, and that the job went badly wrong, leaving him a marked man. As word spreads, a second, far more unhinged assassin, played by Huss, arrives with his own crew, and the station becomes the site of a bloody siege in which alliances shift constantly and Young must decide which of the two dangerous prisoners, if either, she can trust.

Carnahan stages the material as a tightly contained, darkly humorous throwback to 1970s genre cinema, mixing sudden bursts of violence with sardonic dialogue. The film draws on themes of loyalty, corruption and survival, with Young serving as the moral centre among cynical criminals.

Critics gave Copshop generally positive notices, singling out Alexis Louder's breakout performance and Carnahan's energetic direction, although some found the story slight and the violence excessive.

documents.title: Mother/Android
documents.tagline: We are all programmed to survive.
documents.overview: Georgia and her boyfriend Sam go on a treacherous journey to escape their country, which is caught in an unexpected war with artificial intelligence. Days away from the arrival of their first child, the couple must face No Man’s Land—a stronghold of the android uprising—in hopes of reaching safety before giving birth.
documents.plot:
Mother/Android is a 2021 American post-apocalyptic science fiction thriller written and directed by Mattson Tomlin in his feature directorial debut. Chloë Grace Moretz and Algee Smith star as a young couple, with Raúl Castillo in a key supporting role. The film follows a pregnant woman and her boyfriend as they attempt to reach the relative safety of Boston during an uprising of artificial intelligence. It was released on Hulu on 17 December 2021, and was produced in part by Matt Reeves's company 6th & Idaho.

The story begins on Christmas Eve, when college student Georgia Olsen discovers that she is pregnant. Her boyfriend Sam asks her to marry him, but Georgia is unsure both about the relationship and about becoming a mother, and decides not to tell her parents yet. That night, at a Christmas party, the household androids that have become a normal part of everyday life suddenly turn violent, accompanied by a piercing screech, while smartphones begin to explode in the hands of their owners. Georgia and Sam flee as society collapses around them.

Nine months later, Georgia is close to giving birth and the couple are travelling through the woods of New England, avoiding roads and patrolling machines. They hope to reach Boston, which humans have fortified against the androids, and have heard rumours of a boat that carries new mothers and infants to Asia, where people are said to live in peace. Along the way they encounter a military camp, desperate survivors and a mysterious man named Arthur, played by Castillo, who claims to know a way through android territory. Each stage of the journey forces Georgia and Sam to weigh trust against survival, while the approaching birth makes their situation ever more precarious and tests the strength of their relationship.

At its heart the film is less a robot action story than an intimate drama about impending parenthood, fear and commitment, using the apocalypse as a backdrop for Georgia's uncertainty about the future she is bringing a child into. Moretz carries much of the film, with the action set pieces kept relatively restrained.

Critical response was mostly negative. On Rotten Tomatoes about one third of critics' reviews are positive; the consensus notes that the film rises above its budget on a visual level but is less successful in its storytelling.

documents.title: America: The Motion Picture
documents.tagline: This summer they're redrawing history.
documents.overview: A chainsaw-wielding George Washington teams with beer-loving bro Sam Adams to take down the Brits in a tongue-in-cheek riff on the American Revolution.
documents.plot:
America: The Motion Picture is a 2021 American adult animated comedy film directed by Matt Thompson, in his feature directorial debut, and written by Dave Callaham. An R-rated parody of George Washington and the fight against the British, it features the voices of Channing Tatum, Jason Mantzoukas, Olivia Munn, Bobby Moynihan, Judy Greer, Will Forte, Raoul Max Trujillo, Killer Mike, Simon Pegg and Andy Samberg. The film was announced in 2017 as a Netflix original produced by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller alongside Will Allegra, Thompson, Adam Reed, Tatum, Reid Carolin and Peter Kiernan. Its humor relies on deliberate anachronism and Americentrism, scrambling dates, historical figures, battles and inventions, and moving events from across American history into its 1776 setting.

In July 1776, Benedict Arnold massacres the signers of the Declaration of Independence, blows up Independence Hall and steals the document. At Ford's Theatre, George Washington watches a play with his childhood best friend Abraham Lincoln, until Arnold transforms into a werewolf and kills Lincoln, whose dying wish is for Washington to win the revolution and name the new country "America". At Lincoln's funeral Washington meets Martha Dandridge, who urges him to carry on the fight. He assembles a team of misfits: the hard-partying Samuel Adams, champion horseman Paul Revere, Thomas Edison, here a female Chinese scientist rescued from execution by the British, and the Native American hunter Geronimo. Together they set out to forge a silver bullet capable of killing Arnold, enlisting the blacksmith John Henry and raiding the Titanic in Boston for silver spoons, where they stumble on British plans for a secret superweapon and accidentally sink the ship. After Arnold kidnaps Martha, an ambush at a secret meeting called the Gettysburg Address costs Revere his loyal horse, and King James challenges Washington to a battle, only for Arnold to kill the king and seize power for himself. Washington must rally a hastily assembled American army against the British and their plan to turn Americans British with a rain of tea, leading to a climactic battle against Arnold.

Netflix released the film on June 30, 2021. Critics gave it generally negative reviews, finding it unfunny; it holds a 35% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it outrageous and possibly patriotic but not very funny, and a Metacritic score of 38.

documents.title: Nightbooks
documents.tagline: Write for your life.
documents.overview: Alex, a boy obsessed with scary stories, is trapped by a witch in her modern, magical New York City apartment. His original hair-raising tales are the only thing keeping him safe as he desperately tries to find a way out of this twisted place.
documents.plot:
Nightbooks is a 2021 American dark fantasy film directed by David Yarovesky from a screenplay by Mikki Daughtry and Tobias Iaconis, based on J. A. White's 2018 children's book. It stars Winslow Fegley as Alex, Lidya Jewett as Yasmin and Krysten Ritter as the witch Natacha, and was released on Netflix on September 15, 2021.

Alex Mosher, a boy from Brooklyn who loves writing scary stories, overhears his parents worrying about his obsession and about how he is coping after a recent incident. Upset, he grabs his notebooks, which he calls his "nightbooks", and heads for the basement to burn them in the furnace, but the elevator stops on a dark floor where an open apartment door reveals a television playing his favorite film, The Lost Boys. Inside, he eats a slice of pumpkin pie and passes out. He wakes up as the prisoner of Natacha, a beautiful witch who lives in a magical apartment and who shows him a closet full of clothes belonging to children who were "not useful" to her. When she learns that he writes scary stories, she spares him on one condition: he must read her a new story every night, and each one must have an unhappy ending. Alex is put to work alongside Yasmin, another captive child who serves as housekeeper, while Natacha's sometimes-invisible cat, Lenore, keeps watch over them. The apartment travels around the world in search of new victims, and its doors open only with Natacha's keys. Searching her vast library for inspiration, Alex discovers notes left in the margins of books by a girl who seems to have been planning an escape, and he nicknames her "Unicorn Girl" after the necklace she describes. As Alex and Yasmin become friends and win over Lenore, they use the notes to plan their own escape, but the apartment holds dark secrets, and Natacha keeps asking Alex why he wanted to destroy his stories.

Nightbooks received positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it has an 87% approval rating based on 25 reviews, with a consensus that, though busy and overly familiar, it offers a fun and genuinely scary gateway to horror for younger viewers, and Metacritic gave it a score of 65 out of 100.

documents.title: Metal Lords
documents.tagline: Metal up your ass.
documents.overview: For teenage misfits Hunter and Kevin, the path to glory is clear: Devote themselves to metal. Win Battle of the Bands. And be worshipped like gods.
documents.plot:
Metal Lords is a 2022 American teen comedy-drama directed by Peter Sollett from a screenplay by D. B. Weiss. It stars Jaeden Martell, Adrian Greensmith and Isis Hainsworth as misfit high school students who form a heavy metal band, with Noah Urrea and Phelan Davis. Rage Against the Machine guitarist Tom Morello served as executive producer and wrote music for the film, which was released on Netflix on April 8, 2022.

Hunter Sylvester is a brash, uncompromising metalhead who despises the popular kids at his school; his best friend Kevin Schlieb is a shy boy who plays a single drum in the marching band. Determined to win the school's Battle of the Bands, Hunter signs them up under a deliberately offensive name and buys a full drum kit for Kevin on his stepfather's credit card. Kevin throws himself into practice, learning Hunter's playlists of metal classics by ear, and turns out to be a gifted drummer.

The pair still need a bassist. Kevin is drawn to Emily, a temperamental Scottish student who plays the cello brilliantly, and the two begin a relationship, but Hunter refuses to let her join, fearing that she will be their Yoko Ono. Meanwhile Clay, the leader of a polished pop-rock band, hears Kevin playing and recruits him for a wedding gig. After Hunter mocks Emily in class and she breaks his guitar, the friends fall out, and Kevin begins rehearsing with Clay's band. At a party, a vision of metal legends Scott Ian, Tom Morello, Kirk Hammett and Rob Halford, appearing as his conscience, persuades Kevin that he truly loves Emily.

Hunter, whose emotionally distant father has sent him to a rehabilitation clinic as punishment, meets Dr. Troy Nix, a former guitarist from a band he idolises, who tells him how playing with people he did not care for nearly destroyed him. Kevin breaks Hunter out of the clinic, Hunter apologises to Emily and recognises her as a kindred spirit, and Kevin returns Clay's sobered-up regular drummer to his band.

At the contest, Emily joins Hunter and Kevin on electric cello. Forced to change the band's name on the spot, they rename themselves Skullflower and win over the crowd with an original song, until a drunk bully knocks Hunter into the amplifiers and breaks his leg. They finish second, but their performance goes viral, and the three keep playing together.

Reviews were generally positive, with 62% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Avatar: Agni Kai
documents.plot: Avatar: Agni Kai is a 2020 film based on Avatar: The Last Airbender that centers on the Agni Kai duel between Zuko and Azula, with Yasmin Kassim and Nikki SooHoo in the cast.

documents.title: No One Gets Out Alive
documents.tagline: Don’t try to leave. It’ll only make things worse.
documents.overview: An immigrant in search of the American dream is forced to take a room in a boarding house and soon finds herself in a nightmare from which she can't escape.
documents.plot:
No One Gets Out Alive is a British supernatural horror film of 2021 directed by Santiago Menghini, in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Jon Croker and Fernanda Coppel, loosely adapted from Adam Nevill's 2014 novel of the same name. Cristina Rodlo stars as Ambar, an undocumented Mexican immigrant, with Marc Menchaca as the landlord Red, David Figlioli as his brother Becker and David Barrera as Ambar's uncle Beto. Netflix released it on 29 September 2021.

After her mother's death, Ambar leaves Mexico for Cleveland, Ohio, where she works off the books and lives on her savings. Looking for somewhere to stay, she takes a room in a run-down boarding house run by Red, who demands the first month's rent in advance. Strange things begin to happen almost at once. She glimpses Red's mentally ill brother Becker beating his head against a door; some rooms are crammed with odd artifacts, including images of ritual sacrifice; and Ambar starts seeing ghostly women around the house. A coworker steals the rest of her savings, promising a fake ID, and Ambar loses her job.

Terrified by her visions, Ambar flees the house, but penniless, she has to turn to Red, who promises to return her deposit if she comes back for it. The money is not there; instead, Becker forces wine on her. Two Romanian women who have also moved in visit her; she falls asleep and wakes to find the brothers tying up the women. She fights back and Beto, coming to look for her, is attacked by Becker. Red explains that their archaeologist father brought a stone box back from Mexico in 1963 and, with their mother Mary, murdered women for it, the ghosts Ambar has seen; after the brothers killed their father for sacrificing their mother, Becker insisted on continuing, because each sacrifice made him healthier.

Becker ties Ambar to a stone slab before the box, where the other woman has been beheaded, and opens it. Beto frees her, but she is drawn into a vision of her dying mother, who tries to strangle her, while a huge moth-like creature emerges from the box. Ambar fights back, smothering her mother in the vision, and the creature retreats. Arming herself with an obsidian-edged macuahuitl, she wounds Red and kills Becker, then ties the injured Red to the slab and watches the monster bite off his head. As she leaves, her broken ankle heals, and with a moth on her hand she turns back toward the basement, her veins darkening like Becker's.

Reviews were mixed.

documents.title: Savage Salvation
documents.tagline: Payback is dirty.
documents.overview: Newly engaged Shelby John and Ruby Red want a fresh start after their struggles with addiction, but when Shelby discovers his beloved Ruby dead on their porch, he embarks on a vengeful killing spree of the dealers who supplied her. Armed with nothing but adrenaline and a nail gun, Shelby begins to unleash chaos on the town’s criminal underbelly, as he hunt’s down crime lord Coyote. Sheriff Church must race against the clock to put an end to Shelby's vigilante justice before the entire town descends into a bloodbath.
documents.plot:
Savage Salvation is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Randall Emmett. Jack Huston stars as a recovering addict who seeks revenge on the drug trade after his fiancée dies of an overdose, pursued by a sympathetic sheriff played by Robert De Niro, with John Malkovich, Willa Fitzgerald and Quavo in supporting roles. Developed under the title Wash Me in the River, it was released in the United Kingdom as Savage Justice.

Sheriff Mike Church, who lost his own son to drugs, laments how opioids have ravaged his once-close community. Shelby John wins a plastic ring from a claw machine and proposes to his girlfriend Ruby Red, promising her a diamond one day, and after another binge the couple resolve to get clean together. They endure a brutal withdrawal and begin rebuilding their lives: Ruby volunteers at the local church and works in a thrift store, Shelby saves for a real ring, and at a family birthday party Ruby's brother-in-law Peter offers him a job. But their dealer, Elvis, noticing that Shelby has stopped buying, lies to Ruby that Shelby has relapsed, and she injects heroin and dies of an overdose. Shelby works his way up the supply chain. He tortures Elvis with a nail gun until he names his supplier, Darius, before killing him; Darius in turn points him to a dealer called Coyote, whose men Shelby wipes out. Church, whose late son played on Shelby's high school team, arrives and urges him to surrender, but when one of Coyote's men badly wounds Church's partner, Shelby kills the gunman and Church shoots Coyote. A number Coyote called before dying leads Shelby to the true head of the local drug trade: Peter, who years earlier took over the business of a man he had delivered for. Shelby tries to make him inject himself as Ruby did; wounded in the ensuing fight, he overpowers Peter and kills him with the drug. Keeping a promise to Ruby, Shelby is baptised in the river while Church waits on the bank.

Huston plays Shelby, with De Niro as Church, Malkovich as Peter, Fitzgerald as Ruby, Quavo as Coyote, Swen Temmel as Elvis, Clay Wilcox as Darius and Meadow Williams as Detective Zeppelin. De Niro and Malkovich joined in 2020, with Huston replacing Taylor Kitsch, who had replaced Machine Gun Kelly; filming ran from November 2020 to January 2021. The Avenue Entertainment released it on December 2, 2022. The Guardian's reviewer enjoyed it as deliciously camp pulp, and it made about $750,000 from home video sales.

documents.title: Borat Subsequent Moviefilm
documents.tagline: Delivery of prodigious bribe to American regime for make benefit once glorious nation of Kazakhstan.
documents.overview: 14 years after making a film about his journey across the USA, Borat risks life and limb when he returns to the United States with his young daughter, and reveals more about the culture, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the political elections.
documents.plot:
Borat Subsequent Moviefilm is a satirical comedy film directed by Jason Woliner and written by Jay Roach, Sacha Baron Cohen, Anthony Hines, Dan Mazer, Eric Saindon, Jena Friedman, Lee Kern, and Aneru Ujapho. The film is the sequel to the 2006 film Borat: Cultural Learnings of America for Make Benefit Glorious Nation of Kazakhstan.

The movie takes place five years after the events of the first film. Borat Sagdiyev (Sacha Baron Cohen) returns to the United States, this time with his daughter Tutar (Maria Bakalova), a 15-year-old girl who is being raised by her father in Kazakhstan. The story begins with Borat's attempt to reunite with his ex-wife, Maria (Maria Bamford), and their son, Jozef (Zachary Goldberg). However, things do not go as planned, and Borat ends up getting into various misadventures.

One of the main plot points of the film is Borat's attempt to become a social media influencer. He creates an Instagram account and starts promoting himself as a "woke" and "PC" individual, which leads to him being banned from several platforms. Meanwhile, Tutar becomes a viral sensation on social media due to her provocative behavior and outrageous comments.

As the story progresses, Borat becomes embroiled in various American politics and culture. He attends a rally for Donald Trump (Jeremy Allen White), where he gets into a heated argument with a group of protesters. He also visits a gun range, where he attempts to buy a firearm but is thwarted by a background check.

Throughout the film, Borat's interactions with his daughter Tutar are a highlight. The two engage in various pranks and schemes, often targeting their neighbors and acquaintances. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that Tutar is not just a pawn in her father's games, but also a complex and independent individual who is navigating her own identity.

The film's climax features Borat's attempt to run for president of Kazakhstan. He uses his social media fame to gain support from his countrymen, but ultimately fails to win the election. The movie ends with Borat returning to Kazakhstan, where he is met with a hero's welcome. However, it becomes clear that Tutar has grown up and moved on from her father's antics.

Overall, Borat Subsequent Moviefilm is a satirical commentary on American politics, culture, and society. The film uses humor and absurdity to critique the excesses of modern America, while also exploring themes of identity, family, and belonging.

documents.title: BLACKPINK: Light Up the Sky
documents.tagline: The rise of a global phenomena.
documents.overview: Record-shattering Korean girl band BLACKPINK tell their story —  and detail the hard fought journey of the dreams and trials behind their meteoric rise.
documents.plot: Record-shattering Korean girl band BLACKPINK tell their story —  and detail the hard fought journey of the dreams and trials behind their meteoric rise.

documents.title: Welcome to Sudden Death
documents.overview: Jesse Freeman is a former special forces officer and explosives expert now working a regular job as a security guard in a state-of-the-art basketball arena. Trouble erupts when a tech-savvy cadre of terrorists kidnap the team's owner and Jesse's daughter during opening night. Facing a ticking clock and impossible odds, it's up to Jesse to not only save them but also a full house of fans in this highly charged action thriller.
