documents.title: Once Upon a Snowman
documents.tagline: Every snowman starts somewhere.
documents.overview: The previously untold origins of Olaf, the innocent and insightful, summer-loving snowman are revealed as we follow Olaf’s first steps as he comes to life and searches for his identity in the snowy mountains outside Arendelle.
documents.plot:
Once Upon a Snowman is a 2020 American animated fantasy short film written and directed by Trent Correy and Dan Abraham and produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios. Set during the events of Frozen (2013), it follows the snowman Olaf in the moments after Elsa brings him to life and before he meets Anna, Kristoff and Sven. Josh Gad reprises his role as Olaf, with Chris Williams as the shopkeeper Oaken and Idina Menzel, Kristen Bell and Jonathan Groff also credited in their original roles. It was released exclusively on Disney+ on 23 October 2020.

High in the North Mountain, after fleeing her coronation, Elsa unknowingly brings Olaf to life with her powers while singing. Before he can do anything, her discarded cape flies through the air and knocks him down the mountainside into a tree. Confused about who he is and why he exists, the newborn snowman sets out to find an identity of his own. He arrives at Wandering Oaken's Trading Post and Sauna, where he overhears Kristoff singing to Sven and gets flattened at the front door by Anna, who does not notice him.

Inside the store, Olaf meets Oaken and asks for a nose, ideally a carrot, but Oaken has sold the last of them and kindly helps him try out a variety of alternatives. Among the objects is an old-fashioned picture viewer with images of summer, and Olaf is immediately enchanted, dreaming of experiencing warm weather himself. Leaving with a new nose, he is chased by a pack of wolves through the snowy wilderness, passing unnoticed by Anna and Kristoff, who are arguing about love, and inadvertently diverting the wolves toward them. His misadventures continue as he witnesses events from the original film from his own perspective and finally ends up in the woods where he first meets Anna, Kristoff and Sven, recognizing that the people he has been looking for are his friends.

Animator Trent Correy, who had animated the scene of Olaf's creation in Frozen, conceived the short as a way to explore the character's first moments of life. The team aimed to keep continuity with the original film while offering a fresh perspective on its scenes. Critics found the short a charming addition for fans of the franchise, praising its humor and animation.

documents.title: Locked Down
documents.tagline: Some people unravel faster than others
documents.overview: During a COVID-19 lockdown, sparring couple Linda and Paxton call a truce to attempt a high-risk jewellery heist at one of the world's most exclusive department stores, Harrods.
documents.plot:
Locked Down is a 2021 romantic comedy film that explores the complexities of relationships and personal growth during lockdown. The story revolves around Emily (played by Anne Hathaway), a high-end jewelry designer who finds herself trapped in her luxurious apartment with her boyfriend, Ben (played by Chiwetel Ejiofor). As they navigate their confined space, they begin to reevaluate their relationship and confront the underlying issues that have been simmering beneath the surface.

Through Emily's character, the film delves into themes of isolation, loneliness, and the human need for connection. As she becomes increasingly dependent on Ben, she starts to realize that her sense of identity is deeply tied to her relationship with him. The lockdown serves as a catalyst for self-discovery, forcing Emily to confront her own desires, fears, and insecurities.

The film also explores the theme of power dynamics in relationships, highlighting the ways in which even the most seemingly equal partnerships can be influenced by societal expectations and personal biases. As Emily and Ben's relationship is put to the test, they must confront their own flaws and weaknesses, leading to a deeper understanding of themselves and each other.

Ultimately, Locked Down is a nuanced exploration of love, relationships, and personal growth, offering a witty and engaging commentary on the human experience during times of isolation and confinement.

documents.title: Sing a Bit of Harmony
documents.original_title: アイの歌声を聴かせて
documents.overview: Satomi is fine being alone until an AI named Shion joins her class with a song and a promise to make her happy. While Shion’s musical numbers and princess gowns don’t quite pass as human, her antics bring Satomi closer to four other classmates. Together, they make memories worth saving, but even our most precious data can be erased.
documents.plot:
Sing a Bit of Harmony (Japanese: Ai no Utagoe o Kikasete, literally "Let Me Hear Ai's Singing Voice") is a 2021 Japanese animated musical science fiction film in the slice-of-life genre, directed by Yasuhiro Yoshiura and produced by J.C.Staff as a co-production with Funimation. Yoshiura wrote the script with Ichirō Ōkouchi, Kanna Kii created the original character designs and Ryo Takahashi composed the score. The voice cast includes Tao Tsuchiya, Haruka Fukuhara, Asuka Kudo, Kazuyuki Okitsu and Mikako Komatsu.

In an unspecified near future, the technology company Hoshima uses a small Japanese town as a testing ground for robots and systems run by artificial intelligence. High school student Satomi Amano lives with her mother, Mitsuko, an AI specialist employed by Hoshima. Because of an incident in her past, Satomi is shunned by her classmates and estranged from her childhood friend Tōma Suzaki. Mitsuko is preparing a secret trial of a new AI designed to be indistinguishable from a human: for a few days it will attend Satomi's class in a lifelike robotic body as an exchange student named Shion Ashimori. Soon after being introduced, Shion startles everyone by recognizing Satomi, asking whether she is happy and bursting into song.

Determined to make Satomi happy, Shion helps her make friends, solves those friends' problems and works to mend Satomi's bond with Tōma, always through song. Meanwhile, someone is secretly altering the school's security recordings and Shion's telemetry so that her unusual behavior stays hidden from Hoshima. When the company finds out, Shion is forcibly taken away to be deleted, and every device holding footage or memories of her is confiscated. Satomi then learns that Shion is a modified version of an AI that Tōma gave her when they were children. Satomi, Mitsuko and the friends break into Hoshima to rescue Shion, and despite the company's security guards they bring her to the roof, where Tōma connects her to the building's antenna. Shion uploads herself to a satellite, and encouraged by Shion, who now watches over her from orbit, Satomi reconciles with Tōma.

 It had its international premiere at the Scotland Loves Animation festival in Glasgow on October 2, 2021, where it won the Audience Award, before opening in Japan on October 29, 2021. It won the Best Animation Film Award at the 2021 New York City Film & Television Festival and was nominated for Excellent Animation of the Year at the 2022 Japan Academy Film Prize.

documents.title: Homunculus
documents.overview: A homeless man meets a medical school student who pays him to volunteer for a surgical procedure known as trepanation, drilling a hole in his skull, which ends up giving him the ability to communicate with the dark side of people’s subconscious minds.
documents.plot:
Homunculus (Japanese: ホムンクルス) is a 2021 Japanese psychological thriller film directed by Takashi Shimizu, the creator of Ju-On, from a screenplay by Eisuke Naito, Naruki Matsuhisa and Shimizu. It is a live-action adaptation of Hideo Yamamoto's manga of the same name, serialised in Weekly Big Comic Spirits from 2003 to 2011. Produced by Avex Pictures with Booster Project, it stars Go Ayano, Ryo Narita, Yukino Kishii, Anna Ishii and Seiyo Uchino, with the theme song "Trepanation" by Millennium Parade. It opened in Japanese cinemas on 2 April 2021 and was released worldwide on Netflix on 22 April 2021.

Susumu Nakoshi (Ayano), a 34-year-old amnesiac, lives in his car between a luxury hotel and a park full of homeless people in western Shinjuku. He is approached by Manabu Ito (Narita), an eccentric medical student, who offers him 700,000 yen to undergo trepanation, drilling a hole in his skull, which is supposed to awaken a sixth sense. After the operation, Nakoshi finds that when he closes one eye he sees the people around him in grotesque, surreal forms. Ito theorises that these visions are homunculi, images of each person's hidden psyche shaped by their deepest trauma. Nakoshi begins confronting the people he sees, among them a feared yakuza boss (Uchino), whose cruelty stems from a childhood accident with a sickle, and a high-school girl known only by the number 1775 (Ishii). Each time he helps someone face their trauma, he takes part of their homunculus onto himself. He also keeps encountering a woman (Kishii) whom he believes to be Nanako, his girlfriend from before his amnesia. He eventually sees her true self and realises she is not Nanako but a woman linked to the car accident that killed Nanako and robbed him of his memory. Recovering his past, he remembers that Nanako had suffered a miscarriage and that she ran into the path of a car during a bitter argument with him. Accepting his guilt, Nakoshi lets the woman go and leaves the experiment behind. He also exposes Ito's own trauma involving his father, and Ito, losing his sanity, drills into his own skull and sews an eye shut so that he can see homunculi himself.

The film departs significantly from the manga, adding Nakoshi's amnesia and Nanako's death and reworking Ito's arc. Reviews were largely negative: The Asian Cinema Critic gave it 4.5 out of 10, praising some ideas and visuals but calling it overlong and weighed down by exposition, though Ayano's performance was generally praised.

documents.title: The Boy Behind The Door
documents.overview: Bobby tries to save himself and his best friend when they are kidnapped on their way home from school.
documents.plot:
The Boy Behind The Door is a psychological horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our actions. The movie revolves around an 8-year-old boy who is kidnapped by a mysterious woman, and his father's desperate attempt to rescue him.

At its core, the film explores the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. The protagonist's father is portrayed as a complex character, struggling to cope with the loss of his son and the guilt that comes with it. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the father's actions are motivated by a desire to protect his son from the trauma he has already experienced.

The film also touches on the theme of manipulation and control, highlighting how those in positions of power can exploit and manipulate others for their own gain. The mysterious woman who kidnaps the boy is a master manipulator, using her charm and beauty to lure him into her trap.

Furthermore, The Boy Behind The Door critiques the societal expectations placed on men to be providers and protectors, often at the expense of their emotional well-being. The father's character is a prime example of this, as he struggles to balance his desire to rescue his son with his own emotional pain.

Overall, The Boy Behind The Door is a thought-provoking film that explores the darker aspects of human nature, highlighting the devastating consequences of trauma and manipulation.

documents.title: Stuck
documents.overview: A gymnastics coach must deal with a man who has taken an interest in the young girls she coaches. The man makes a bold move and the coach responds with an even bolder one.
documents.plot: A gymnastics coach must deal with a man who has taken an interest in the young girls she coaches.

documents.title: Bloodthirsty
documents.tagline: Ambition can be killer.
documents.overview: When indie singer Grey struggles to write her sophomore album, she teams up with a mysterious producer at his secluded cabin. Though their bond strengthens her music, it also starts to irreparably alter Grey’s body and mind.
documents.plot: When indie singer Grey struggles to write her sophomore album, she teams up with a mysterious producer at his secluded cabin. Though their bond strengthens her music, it also starts to irreparably alter Grey’s body and mind.

documents.title: The Binding
documents.overview: While visiting her fiancé's mother in southern Italy, a woman must fight the mysterious and malevolent curse intent on claiming her daughter.
documents.plot: While visiting her fiancé's mother in southern Italy, a woman must fight the mysterious and malevolent curse intent on claiming her daughter.

documents.title: Wish Upon a Unicorn
documents.overview: Two children discover that their mother is gone. The youngest of the pair, adventurer and upcomming singer, Long Johnson forces his older sister, Lily Johnson, to hunt down a unicorn with magical blood.
documents.plot:
Wish Upon a Unicorn is a 2020 American family fantasy comedy film written and directed by Steve Bencich, produced by Universal 1440 Entertainment and Indy Entertainment and released by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on DVD and digital platforms on 15 September 2020, later streaming on Netflix. It stars Ryan Kiera Armstrong as Mia and Summer Fontana as her older sister Emma, with Chloe Webb as their grandmother Rose, Jonathan Lajoie as their father and Kevin J. O'Connor as Willie, alongside Tait Blum, Jon Gries and André Gower. Rated PG, it runs 93 minutes.

Emma and Mia have recently lost their mother, and their father has lost his job in Chicago, so the family moves to the country home where their mother grew up to live with Grandma Rose and help on her ranch. Rose is fading and losing her memory, but her joyful, eccentric spirit revives as she sets the girls to work on the chores. The sisters face bullies at their new school, and at the local general store they meet Willie, a conspiracy-minded local who tells Bigfoot stories and recognizes in Mia a fellow believer. In the woods, Mia spots a sparkling unicorn colt bathed in rainbow light, names him Rocco and discovers the good luck he brings, but no one else can see him and her skeptical father laughs off her claims. Mia researches unicorn lore to prove they exist, and when the more practical Emma finally starts to believe, she too can see Rocco; the sisters even take him to school to deal with a bully. Willie, however, knows the legends as well, and when he learns of Rocco's presence he sets out to capture the colt, intending to kill him and drink his blood to gain eternal youth. When Rose falls ill and is taken to hospital, she pulls out her tubes to help her granddaughters chase down the unicorn-napper, rescue Rocco and return him to his mother.

Reviewers found it a gentle film for young children. Barbara Shulgasser-Parker of Common Sense Media called it sweet and perfectly tailored to its target audience, with smart, amusing dialogue and a charming performance from Webb, though loose in its logic. Roger Moore of Movie Nation described it as cutesy, corny and little-kid friendly, a lightweight cross between Prancer and E.T. with modest effects but enough goofy gags and one-liners to avoid being insipid, while noting it was too undemanding for anyone over eight.

documents.title: PAW Patrol: Jet to the Rescue
documents.original_title: PAW Patrol: Jet to the Rescue
documents.overview: A royal relative steals a gem with the power to make things fly, the Paw Patrol takes to the skies to stop him and save Barkingburg.
documents.plot:
PAW Patrol: Jet to the Rescue is a 2020 Canadian-American animated adventure special based on PAW Patrol, the computer-animated preschool television series created by Keith Chapman and produced by Spin Master Entertainment with animation by Guru Studio. Running 56 minutes, it was released in September 2020 and sends the team into the skies in a fleet of jets. The voice cast includes Joey Nijem as Ryder, Lilly Bartlam as Skye, Justin Paul Kelly as Chase, Lukas Engel as Marshall, Keegan Hedley as Rubble, Berkley Silverman as Everest and David López as Tracker, with Caoimhe Judd as the Princess of Barkingburg, Anya Cooke as her pampered dog Sweetie and Ashton Frank as the Duke of Flappington.

Ryder and the pups are invited to Barkingburg Castle for the Princess's birthday, where they hope to surprise her with a gift, but attention centres on the precious Gem of Barkingburg, which has been passed to her that evening and has the power to make things fly. The Duke of Flappington, a boy who claims to be her distant cousin, is welcomed to the party but secretly conspires with the selfish Sweetie to steal the gem and seize power. When the team tries to stop the theft, Ryder and most of the pups slide into a dungeon and are locked in a remote chamber deep inside the castle, while Skye and two others escape capture but are shut outside and unable to reach Ryder. The Duke combines the gem with the Gem of Flappington in a sceptre and uses it to lift Barkingburg into the clouds as his own kingdom, sending a giant eagle-shaped aircraft and eagle drones against the pups' jets. Skye, who leads the mission, has to overcome her fear of eagles to free her friends, and Sweetie, double-crossed by the Duke, backs out of the scheme before the pups save the Princess and her kingdom.

Common Sense Media rated it suitable from age four, describing it as a standalone adventure with only minor peril and a more involved, action-packed story that might hold the interest of fans who had outgrown the television show, and praising its messages about teamwork and the courage to face one's fears, as well as Tracker's use of Spanish phrases. The Australian Council on Children and the Media judged it best suited to children aged three to five, highlighting its messages of kindness and self-belief.

documents.title: American Murder: The Family Next Door
documents.original_title: American Murder: The Family Next Door
documents.overview: Using raw, firsthand footage, this documentary examines the disappearance of Shanann Watts and her children, and the terrible events that followed.
documents.plot:
American Murder: The Family Next Door is a documentary series that delves into the dark and twisted world of the DeCoster family, whose seemingly idyllic life was marred by sinister secrets and shocking violence. At its core, the series explores the themes of toxic masculinity, the dangers of patriarchal dominance, and the devastating consequences of unchecked power dynamics within families.

The documentary sheds light on how the father, Michael DeCoster, became increasingly controlling and manipulative, using his position of authority to exploit and abuse those around him. This toxic behavior is expertly woven throughout the narrative, revealing a complex web of psychological manipulation, gaslighting, and emotional abuse that ultimately led to tragic consequences.

The series also touches on the theme of the "perfect" facade, where appearances can be deceiving, and the idea that even the most seemingly ordinary families can harbor dark secrets. The documentary raises questions about the societal pressures that can lead individuals to conform to toxic norms, and how these pressures can be perpetuated by those in positions of power.

Furthermore, American Murder: The Family Next Door serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of ignoring red flags and the importance of recognizing the warning signs of abuse. The series highlights the devastating impact of Michael DeCoster's actions on his family members, particularly his wife and children, who were left to pick up the pieces of their shattered lives.

Overall, American Murder: The Family Next Door is a thought-provoking exploration of the darker aspects of human nature, revealing the devastating consequences of unchecked power dynamics and toxic masculinity.

documents.title: Curious George: Go West, Go Wild
documents.original_title: Curious George: Go West, Go Wild
documents.tagline: Lets get crazy.
documents.overview: While farm-sitting, George accidentally lets the farm animals escape. Ted, George and wannabe cowboy Emmett must round 'em up, accounting for every animal -- and emerging with some new skills, to boot.
documents.plot:
Curious George: Go West, Go Wild is a 2020 American animated family comedy, the fifth feature in the film franchise based on Margret and H. A. Rey's books about the mischievous monkey George and his friend Ted, the Man with the Yellow Hat. Directed by Michael LaBash from a screenplay by Sherri Stoner and Jana Howington, it was produced by Imagine Entertainment, Universal Animation Studios and Universal 1440 Entertainment, with Brian Grazer, Ron Howard and David Kirschner among the executive producers and music by Germaine Franco. Frank Welker voices George and Jeff Bennett voices Ted, with Max Mittelman as Emmett, April Stewart as Ginny, Phil Morris as Frank Stetson, Adrienne Barbeau as Ginny's mother and Dee Bradley Baker in several animal roles.

George and Ted travel west by train to Ted's cousin Ginny's farm, having promised to look after it while she goes on vacation with her adventurous mother. Ted, however, knows nothing about farms and little about country life, and the place is run day to day by Emmett, a young farmhand and would-be cowboy who is still learning the ropes himself. George's curiosity and antics quickly upend the farm's routine, and when a runaway wagon rolls down a hill and smashes the corrals, the animals escape and scatter into the countryside.

Despite his inexperience, Emmett keeps his head and organizes a roundup, and the three set off to bring home every last cow, sheep and even a llama. Their trek takes them across a rickety old covered bridge and a wide river, where Emmett rescues a sheep and a dog swept away on a log, and they must flee a shelter threatened by a flash flood. Emmett practices lassoing again and again until he masters it, and his perseverance inspires the cautious Ted to try fishing and horseback riding and George to learn the harmonica. Meanwhile, Ginny finds a similar freedom from her own cautiousness on her trip. By the end, every animal is accounted for and the friends have all gained new skills.

The film premiered exclusively on the streaming service Peacock on 8 September 2020, alongside the arrival of the Curious George television series on the platform, and was released on DVD and digital on 15 December 2020. Common Sense Media described it as a gentle preschool adventure with mild peril and a positive message about being open to new experiences and trying new things.

documents.title: After We Fell
documents.overview: Just as Tessa's life begins to become unglued, nothing is what she thought it would be. Not her friends nor her family. The only person that she should be able to rely on is Hardin, who is furious when he discovers the massive secret that she's been keeping. Before Tessa makes the biggest decision of her life, everything changes because of revelations about her family.
documents.plot:
After We Fell is a 2021 American romantic fantasy film directed by Matt Eskandari, written by Anna Todd, and produced by Voltage Pictures.

The movie serves as the fourth installment in the After series, based on the novels by Anna Todd. The story follows Tessa Young (Josephine Langford) and Hardin Scott (Hero Fiennes-Tiffin), who are still navigating their complicated relationship after the events of the previous films.

As the story unfolds, Tessa is struggling to balance her feelings for Hardin with her growing connection to Noah Flynn (Dylan Arnold), a charming and charismatic student at her school. Meanwhile, Hardin's past demons resurface, threatening to destroy his relationship with Tessa once again.

Throughout the film, the characters face numerous challenges, including internal conflicts, external pressures, and the consequences of their actions in previous installments. The movie explores themes of love, loyalty, and self-discovery as the characters navigate their complex web of relationships.

One of the standout aspects of After We Fell is its ability to balance lighthearted moments with more serious and emotional scenes. The film features a talented young cast, including Josephine Langford, Hero Fiennes-Tiffin, and Dylan Arnold, who deliver nuanced performances that bring depth and complexity to their characters.

Overall, After We Fell is a romantic fantasy film that explores the ups and downs of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and talented cast, it's sure to delight fans of the series and newcomers alike.

documents.title: After Ever Happy
documents.overview: As a shocking truth about a couple's families emerges, the two lovers discover they are not so different from each other. Tessa is no longer the sweet, simple, good girl she was when she met Hardin — any more than he is the cruel, moody boy she fell so hard for.
documents.plot:
After Ever Happy is a 2022 American romantic thriller film directed by Isaac Ezban and written by Jessica Sorensen. The movie serves as the fourth installment in the After series, based on the novels by Anna Todd.

The story picks up where the previous films left off, with Tessa Young (Josephine Langford) and Hardin Scott (Hero Fiennes-Tiffin) navigating their complicated relationship. However, it becomes clear that their love is put to the test as they face new challenges and secrets from their pasts.

As Tessa struggles to reconcile her feelings for Hardin with her own sense of identity and self-worth, she begins to uncover dark secrets about his family's history and the true nature of their relationship. Meanwhile, Hardin's own demons resurface, threatening to destroy everything he holds dear.

Throughout the film, the tension between Tessa and Hardin builds as they engage in a game of cat and mouse, each trying to outmaneuver the other. The stakes are raised when Tessa discovers a shocking truth about Hardin's family that forces her to reevaluate their entire relationship.

The movie explores themes of love, loyalty, and the complexities of human relationships. As with previous installments in the series, After Ever Happy delves into the darker aspects of romance, revealing the messy and often toxic nature of relationships.

Ultimately, the film builds towards a dramatic confrontation between Tessa and Hardin, leaving the audience wondering what the future holds for these two complex characters. Will they find a way to overcome their differences and make their relationship work, or will the secrets and lies tear them apart?

Overall, After Ever Happy is a gripping and intense addition to the After series, offering plenty of twists and turns to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

documents.title: White Noise
documents.tagline: You can’t hear it if it's everywhere.
documents.overview: A professor, husband and father to four is torn asunder by a rail car chemical spill that releases an “Airborne Toxic Event”, forcing him to confront his biggest fear – his own mortality.
documents.plot: Jack Gladney, professor of Hitler studies at The-College-on-the-Hill, husband to Babette, and father to four children/stepchildren, is torn asunder by a chemical spill from a rail car that releases an "Airborne Toxic Event" forcing Jack to confront his biggest fear - his own mortality.

documents.title: Hello, Goodbye, and Everything in Between
documents.original_title: Hello, Goodbye, and Everything in Between
documents.tagline: Every ending is a new beginning.
documents.overview: Clare and Aidan, who after making a pact that they would break up before college, find themselves retracing the steps of their relationship on their last evening as a couple. The epic date leads them to familiar landmarks, unexpected places, and causes them to question whether high school love is meant to last.
documents.plot:
Hello, Goodbye, and Everything in Between is a 2022 American romantic drama directed by Michael Lewen in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Amy Reed and Ben York Jones adapted from Jennifer E. Smith's novel of the same name. Jordan Fisher, who also served as an executive producer, and Talia Ryder were cast in September 2020, followed the next month by Ayo Edebiri, Nico Hiraga and the rest of the ensemble, and principal photography began in October 2020. Netflix released the film on July 6, 2022.

Clare, a high school senior who has moved from state to state since her parents' divorce, returns to a West Coast town and is talked into a Halloween party by her old friend Stella. There she meets Aidan, an aspiring musician whose doctor parents would prefer he study medicine, and the two spend a spontaneous night together. Clare, who plans to become a lawyer and does not want a boyfriend after watching her parents' high school romance fall apart, accepts his proposal of a pact: they will date until the end of the following summer and then break up after one epic final date.

On the eve of Clare's departure for Dartmouth, Aidan stages a surprise tour of places from their relationship, hoping to change her mind: a show by his old band, the ice rink where they had their first fight, a speedboat ride recalling the day he first said he loved her. Overwhelmed, Clare invites Stella and their friend Scotty along, and Aidan realizes she is avoiding the romance. A break-in at their school to let Scotty tag a wall ends with Aidan hurting his hand, and at the hospital Clare learns he was not accepted at Berklee and never told her. After a painful night apart, her mother helps her see that a relationship cannot work if its end is fixed in advance. Clare tells Aidan she loves him, and they part on good terms; he takes a year in Los Angeles to pursue music while she goes to New Hampshire, and they later reunite at the playground from their first night.

Fisher plays Aidan, Ryder plays Clare, Edebiri plays Stella and Hiraga plays Scotty, with Jennifer Robertson, Eva Day, Julia Benson, Dalias Blake, Patrick Sabongui, Sarah Grey and Djouliet Amara. Critical reaction was lukewarm: only 29% of the 21 reviews counted by Rotten Tomatoes were positive, while Metacritic's score of 54 indicated mixed reviews.

documents.title: The Medium
documents.tagline: A story about shamanism in Thailand.
documents.overview: A horrifying story of a shaman’s inheritance in the Isan region of Thailand. But the goddess that appears to have taken possession of a family member turns out not to be as benevolent as it first appears.
documents.plot:
The Medium is a supernatural folk horror film of 2021 shot as a mock documentary in the Isan language, directed by Banjong Pisanthanakun and co-written and produced by the Korean filmmaker Na Hong-jin. Sawanee Utoomma stars as Nim, a village shaman, with Narilya Gulmongkolpech as her niece Mink, Sirani Yankittikan as Mink's mother Noi and Boonsong Nakphoo as the shaman Santi.

A documentary crew travels to Isan in north-eastern Thailand to film Nim, a medium who says she is possessed by Ba Yan, a local goddess. Nim inherited the role after her sister Noi refused it and became a Christian. At the funeral of Noi's husband Wiroj, Nim explains that misfortune has dogged his family's men: his father, a factory owner, killed himself after an insurance fraud, and his son Mac supposedly died in a road accident. Noi now lives with her daughter Mink and Manit's family. Mink begins to behave strangely, shifting between personalities and hearing voices, and she loses her job over her behaviour at work. Nim suspects Ba Yan has chosen Mink as her next host, but Noi forbids a ceremony. Nim then learns that Mac actually hanged himself after an incestuous relationship with Mink and fears his ghost is haunting her.

After Mink attempts suicide, Noi, believing Ba Yan is punishing her through her daughter, secretly hires another medium to pass the goddess to Mink. The rite fails and Mink runs away, to be found a month later delirious in her grandfather's ruined factory. Ba Yan's statue is found beheaded, and the more powerful shaman Santi declares that Mink is possessed by countless evil spirits, the legacy of her paternal ancestors' crimes. As Santi prepares a great exorcism, Mink terrorises the household, even killing and eating the family dog. Nim dies in her sleep the day before the ritual. At the ruined factory, Noi offers herself as a vessel to draw out the spirits, while at home Mink is sealed in her room. Lured by what sounds like her son crying, Manit's wife opens the door and is stabbed, and the ritual collapses as the spirits seize the participants. Mink arrives at the factory and, when Noi tries to cast out the spirits, calls her mother before burning her alive. A mid-credits scene shows Nim, before her death, doubting that Ba Yan was ever inside her.

The film won the best feature award at the Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival, topped the South Korean box office in July 2021 and was Thailand's Oscar submission. It holds 81% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love
documents.original_title: A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love
documents.overview: After 15 years, Pat moves home from Hawaii with his two sons and through a series of coincidences, or Godwinks, ends up stuck in traffic next to his high school sweetheart, Margie, at Christmas.
documents.plot:
A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love is a heartwarming holiday romance film that explores the complexities of love, loss, and second chances. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of finding redemption and forgiveness in the face of past mistakes.

The story follows a woman who returns to her hometown for Christmas, only to reconnect with an old flame who has been carrying around emotional scars from their past. As they rekindle their romance, they must confront the pain and heartache that drove them apart in the first place.

Through the lens of this second chance at love, the movie sheds light on the power of forgiveness and the importance of facing one's mistakes head-on. The film suggests that it's never too late to make amends and start anew, and that sometimes, all it takes is a little bit of courage and vulnerability to heal old wounds.

The movie also touches on the theme of nostalgia and the bittersweet nature of revisiting past loves. As the protagonist navigates her feelings for her old flame, she must confront the memories and emotions that have been holding her back from moving forward. This introspection serves as a poignant reminder that love can be both a source of joy and pain, and that sometimes, it's necessary to let go of the past in order to move towards a brighter future.

Ultimately, A Godwink Christmas: Second Chance, First Love is a film about the transformative power of love and forgiveness, and the idea that even in the most unexpected ways, we can find redemption and happiness.

documents.title: Paris, 13th District
documents.overview: Émilie meets Camille who is attracted to Nora, who crosses paths with Amber. Three girls and a boy – They’re friends, sometimes lovers and often both.
documents.plot:
Paris, 13th District is a French drama film that explores the complexities of human relationships and the struggles of finding one's place in the world. The movie delves into the life of a young woman, Camille, who moves to Paris with her family and navigates the challenges of adolescence amidst the vibrant cityscape.

At its core, the film is a poignant portrayal of loneliness and disconnection in modern urban life. Camille's experiences are deeply rooted in her feelings of isolation and disorientation as she tries to find her footing in this new environment. The movie masterfully captures the sense of disconnection that can come with growing up and trying to establish one's identity.

The film also touches on themes of family dynamics, love, and the search for belonging. Camille's relationships with those around her are multifaceted and nuanced, reflecting the complexities of human connection in all its forms. The movie raises questions about what it means to belong, not just to a place or community, but to oneself.

Through its thoughtful and introspective narrative, Paris, 13th District offers a powerful exploration of the human experience, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable.

documents.title: Father of the Bride
documents.tagline: Love is simple. Family is not.
documents.overview: A father coming to grips with his daughter’s upcoming wedding through the prism of multiple relationships within a big, sprawling Cuban-American family.
documents.plot:
Father of the Bride is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Gaz Alazraki and written by Matt Lopez, based on Edward Streeter's 1949 novel. A reimagining of the 1950 and 1991 films and the third screen version of the story, it relocates the tale to a Cuban-American family in Miami and stars Andy García, Gloria Estefan, Adria Arjona, Isabela Merced, Diego Boneta and Chloe Fineman. Produced by Plan B Entertainment, it premiered on HBO Max.

Guillermo "Billy" Herrera is a successful, stubborn Miami architect married to Ingrid. At a counseling session, Ingrid tells him she is tired of his workaholism and wants a divorce, and they plan to tell their daughters: Sofia, a newly graduated lawyer, and Cora, a rebellious aspiring fashion designer. Before they can, Sofia arrives home and announces that she is engaged to a fellow lawyer, Adan Castillo, that they plan to marry within a month, and that they intend to move to Mexico to work for a non-profit. Billy and Ingrid agree to keep the divorce secret until after the wedding. Billy wants a big traditional Cuban celebration while the couple prefer something small, and Sofia asks Cora to design her gown, irritating the eccentric wedding planner Natalie Vance.

Adan's wealthy father, Hernan, arrives with his family and clashes repeatedly with Billy over the cost and scale of the event, offending him by offering to cover anything he cannot afford, throwing an extravagant engagement party on his yacht and proposing his island mansion as the venue. Billy eventually admits that he dislikes Adan and his family, then makes peace with Sofia and confides the divorce to Adan at the bachelor party. At the rehearsal, with a storm approaching, Cora overhears the secret and blurts it out to the guests. Sofia is hurt that her parents and fiancé hid it from her but reconciles with her father. The storm wrecks the decorations and knocks out the only bridge to the venue, so the two families pool their resources to hold the wedding at the Herrera home, with Natalie officiating. Sofia and Adan marry with Billy's blessing, and he and Ingrid rekindle their romance.

The project was announced in 2020 at Warner Bros., and principal photography began in Atlanta in June 2021. Released on HBO Max in June 2022, the film earned 80% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 65, with critics noting that it diverged smartly from its predecessors while keeping the story's timeless charm.

documents.title: The Call
documents.overview: In the fall of 1987, a group of small-town friends must survive the night in the home of a sinister couple after a tragic accident occurs. Needing only to make a single phone call, the request seems horribly ordinary until they realize that this call could change their life…or end it.
documents.plot:
The Call is a 2020 American supernatural horror film directed by Timothy Woodward Jr. and written by Patrick Stibbs. It stars Lin Shaye and Tobin Bell, appearing on screen together for the first time, alongside Chester Rushing, Erin Sanders, Mike C. Manning, Sloane Morgan Siegel and Judd Lormand. It was Woodward's second collaboration with Shaye after The Final Wish (2018). The film opened in select US theatres and drive-ins on 2 October 2020, reached video on demand on 30 October and was released on Blu-ray in December 2020.

In the autumn of 1987, Chris (Rushing) moves with his mother to the small town of Willow Falls after his parents' divorce. On his first day at school he meets Tonya (Sanders), who introduces him to brothers Zack (Manning) and Brett (Siegel). They tell him that Tonya's younger sister Laura disappeared from the daycare run by Edith Cranston (Shaye), a former schoolteacher whom the town suspects of the crime and rumours call a witch, and that they have long tormented Edith and her husband Edward (Bell) by vandalising their home. Chris refuses to join in when the others throw bricks through the Cranstons' windows. Worn down by years of abuse, Edith hangs herself. Days later Edward summons the four teenagers to his house and reveals that Edith has left them her fortune: each will receive $100,000 if they go upstairs, dial a number on an old telephone and stay on the line for one minute. The call connects to a phone placed in Edith's casket at her request. One by one they are pulled into a personal hell in which Edith's spirit forces them to relive their worst memories: for Zack and Brett, the beatings from their abusive father; for Chris, the car crash that killed his pregnant girlfriend Sarah. Chris escapes but returns to help Tonya, whose own nightmare reveals that she killed Laura out of jealousy and blamed Edith. After Chris shoots Edward, Tonya vanishes into the room with the phone, and Chris, realising no one can escape the house, steps back into his own hell.

The film received generally negative reviews, with a 44% Rotten Tomatoes rating from 25 reviews and a consensus citing a lack of genuine scares and an overload of genre tropes. Leslie Felperin of The Guardian called it a shonky assemblage of tired tropes redeemed mainly by Shaye's game performance, while Drew Tinnin of Dread Central gave it three out of five, praising Shaye and the dark revenge story despite tonal problems.

documents.title: You've Got This
documents.overview: An ad creative and a successful exec have a great marriage — until he wants to be a dad just as her star is rising. Then he brings someone new home.
documents.plot:
You've Got This (Ahí te encargo) is a Mexican romantic comedy of 2020 directed by Salvador Espinosa from a screenplay by Tiaré Scanda and Leonardo Zimbrón, released worldwide on Netflix. Mauricio Ochmann stars as Alejandro, known as Alex, an advertising creative desperate to become a father, with Esmeralda Pimentel as his wife Cecilia, or Ceci, Regina Reynoso as the waitress Alicia, Matteo Giannini as her baby Alan, and Juan Martín Jáuregui and Moisés Arizmendi in supporting roles.

Alex and Ceci want different things. Ceci, a lawyer at an energy company, is devoted to her career and has no interest in children, while Alex longs for a baby and one day asks her to start a family as soon as possible. She refuses: she has just been offered a partnership at her firm, a rare promotion for a woman, and is thrilled about it. That same day Alex runs into Alicia, a waitress he once promised to help if she ever needed it, and she asks him to look after her baby son Alan for three days while she deals with something important. Reluctantly he agrees and tries to keep the baby hidden at home, but Ceci soon discovers him and furiously insists that the child go back to his mother at once.

The day Alicia is due to return comes and goes, and Alex searches for her in vain until a friend tells him she is back. Returning the baby, he learns that she has been undergoing treatment for brain cancer; she begs him to adopt Alan, and although he refuses, he takes mother and son home when she collapses. Ceci walks in as he invites Alicia to stay, and in the ensuing fight Alex all but admits that he married her to have a child. Ceci moves in with a friend and ignores his calls, finally asking him to be out when she collects her things. Alex plans to adopt Alan and move in with his mother, but he is fired for bringing the baby to work, and when he goes back to apologise he tells his boss frankly how her staff see her; she rejects his advice but agrees to think about rehiring him. He finds Ceci at the meeting that will confirm her promotion and they reconcile, just as word comes that Alicia is in hospital. Ceci's chief tells her the partnership is already hers and she need only sign, so she signs and rushes off with Alex. Alicia dies, and the couple adopt Alan. As Ceci packs for a new post in Hong Kong, Alex reveals plane tickets for himself and the baby to join her.

Filmed over six weeks in Mexico City and Valle de Bravo, the film premiered on Netflix on 2 October 2020.

documents.title: One Way
documents.tagline: No wrong turn goes unpunished.
documents.overview: On the run with a bag full of cash after a robbing his former crime boss—and a potentially fatal wound—Freddy slips onto a bus headed into the unrelenting California desert. With his life slipping through his fingers, Freddy is left with very few choices to survive.
documents.plot:
One Way is a 2022 American action crime thriller directed by Andrew Baird from a screenplay by Ben Conway. Colson Baker, the musician also known as Machine Gun Kelly, stars as Freddy Sullivan, a small-time criminal on the run, with Storm Reid as Rachel, Kevin Bacon as Freddy's father, Travis Fimmel as a fellow passenger named Will, and Drea de Matteo, Meagan Holder, Rhys Coiro and Luis Da Silva in supporting roles.

Freddy, a low-level Los Angeles hoodlum, has stolen a bag of cash and cocaine from his criminal associates, a gang run by the sociopathic Vic, played by de Matteo. Shot in the gut while escaping, he boards a long-distance bus bound for a small town in Georgia, and most of the film unfolds on board. Badly wounded and growing weaker, Freddy works the phone throughout the journey, in tense calls with Vic, with his ex-girlfriend Christine, a nurse, with a nervous associate, and with his deadbeat father, whose contact in Freddy's phone is saved under an insult. Along the way, he is betrayed by his own father.

In the seat in front of him sits Rachel, a precocious young woman who is probably underage but claims to be 21. Out of minutes on her own phone, she persuades Freddy to lend her his so that she can make arrangements to meet a mysterious stranger named Smokie, who is clearly grooming her. The cramped bus fills with fellow passengers who are by turns kind, rude and sinister, among them the unsettling Will. As the miles pass, Freddy must contend with his worsening injury while deciding whether to put himself at further risk to protect Rachel from the danger she is heading toward.

Baker and Fimmel were cast in September 2020, Bacon joined that November, and Reid in February 2021. Principal photography began on February 2, 2021, in Thomasville, Georgia. Saban Films released the film in theaters and on video on demand in the United States on September 2, 2022. Reviews were mixed, with 53% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 46. The Guardian's Leslie Felperin felt the director overused woozy handheld camerawork and fluttery editing but found the script better than expected at exploiting its confined setting and the odd community of a long bus journey; she judged that Baker could act but was consistently upstaged by Reid, whose character had the more interesting story.

documents.title: In the Earth
documents.tagline: Nature is a force of evil.
documents.overview: As a deadly virus ravages the world, Dr. Martin Lowery embarks on a mission to reach test site ATU327A, a research hub deep in the Arboreal Forest. The arduous journey, guided by park scout Alma, is set back by a nighttime attack that leaves the two bruised and shoeless. When they run into Zach, a man living off the grid, they gratefully accept his help. Zach’s intentions aren’t exactly what they seem, however, and a path out of the forest and into safety quickly fades as the line between myth and science blurs.
