The Lair is a 2022 British action horror film directed by Neil Marshall, who co-wrote it with Charlotte Kirk. Kirk stars as Royal Air Force pilot Kate Sinclair, alongside Jonathan Howard, Jamie Bamber and Leon Ockenden.

In 2017, Sinclair and her weapons systems officer, Terry Johnson, are shot down over Afghanistan. Insurgents kill Johnson, and Sinclair, with no way to call for help, takes refuge in an abandoned Soviet bunker. Her pursuers follow her inside and accidentally wake clawed humanoid creatures from stasis. The monsters slaughter the insurgents while the wounded Sinclair escapes. U.S. soldiers in a Humvee pick her up and takes her to a small outpost, where she tells Major Roy Finch what she saw. That night, the creatures attack the outpost, kill several soldiers and carry off the bodies, and Finch is knocked unconscious. The survivors wait out the attack in the armory. An older local man, Kabir, remembers that a star fell from the sky just before the Soviet invasion in 1979, and that villagers, including his father, disappeared for years until the Soviets withdrew.

The team examines a creature left behind and finds human organs under its tough hide. When Finch wakes up, he explains what his superiors told him. The Soviets invaded Afghanistan to recover a crashed alien spacecraft and then spliced alien DNA with human subjects at a secret site the Americans were never able to locate. The supposedly dead creature revives, reads Sinclair's mind through tentacles in its head, and Finch kills it with a grenade, sacrificing himself. The survivors return to the bunker to destroy it with explosives, and when a soldier named Hook is dragged underground, Sinclair leads a rescue. The creatures have set a trap, and the military has learned the location and will drop a bunker-buster bomb in 20 minutes. Kabir recognizes his transformed father among the monsters before he dies. Only Sinclair, Hook and Wilks, who stayed on the surface, make it out. They rescue Wilks from insurgents and escape in a stolen vehicle just before the bomb destroys the site. Later, an American black ops team searches the outpost for a specimen but finds nothing.

The Lair received mixed reviews. Variety called it more hectic than scary but praised Marshall's brisk staging of bloody action, and the Los Angeles Times considered it a good genre picture, though not a great one. RogerEbert.com praised its practical creature effects. It grossed about $157,000 worldwide.

documents.title: Love and Leashes
documents.tagline: Will you dominate me?
documents.overview: Love never hurt so good for two co-workers who enter a contractual relationship as partners in consensual play, pleasure and pain.
documents.plot:
Love and Leashes is a South Korean romantic comedy of 2022 directed by Park Hyun-jin and adapted from the webtoon Moral Sense by Gyeoul, about an office romance built on a dominant-submissive arrangement. Seohyun stars as public relations manager Jung Ji-woo and Lee Jun-young as her new colleague Jung Ji-hoo, with Lee El as Ji-woo's best friend Hye-mi, Seo Hyun-woo as team leader Hwang, Ahn Seung-gyun as the youngest employee Lee Han and Kim Bo-ra as Ji-hoo's former girlfriend Hana.

Ji-hoo joins a public relations firm and notices that Ji-woo, a capable manager, is constantly undermined by her male colleagues. Because their names are so alike, a parcel addressed to him lands on her desk, and she opens it to find a leather collar and leash. He insists they are for his dog until a sex shop coupon falls out. Grateful that she keeps his secret, he misreads her apology for her bossy manner as an admission that she is a dominant and asks her to become his mistress; she is stunned, having assumed the gear was meant for a partner. At a company event he tearfully confesses that a past girlfriend left him over his desires, leaving him ashamed, and Ji-woo assures him she does not think him a pervert. Testing him with a blindfold, she asks why he chose her, and he says he admires her confidence, maturity and integrity. She agrees, researches BDSM all night, and the two sign a three-month contract with her as the dominant partner.

As gossip spreads and Ji-woo turns her commanding streak on co-workers such as Han, Ji-hoo grows jealous, and an after-hours session nearly gets them caught by a guard. Ji-woo realises she has feelings for him, but he refuses to date. They rescue Hye-mi from a violent man at a themed love hotel. On the contract's last day Hana visits Ji-hoo and blames his selfishness for his loneliness; in their final session he kisses Ji-woo and admits he has avoided love for fear of being hurt, and she walks out. When Han accidentally emails a recording of one of their sessions to the whole office and the managers' warning turns into harassment, Ji-hoo takes the blame and declares his love despite her safeword. Ji-woo has Han expose the managers' own affairs, and the couple begin dating openly while keeping their dynamic.

Netflix released the film in February 2022, timed for Valentine's Day. It scored 80% on Rotten Tomatoes from a handful of reviews, though OhmyNews noted its niche subject limited its appeal.

documents.title: Beast
documents.tagline: Fight for family.
documents.overview: A recently widowed man and his two teenage daughters travel to a game reserve in South Africa. However, their journey of healing soon turns into a fight for survival when a bloodthirsty lion starts to stalk them.
documents.plot:
Beast is a survival action horror film of 2022 directed by Baltasar Kormákur; Ryan Engle wrote the script from a story by Jaime Primak Sullivan. Idris Elba stars as Dr Nate Samuels, a recently widowed father, with Iyana Halley and Leah Sava Jeffries as his teenage daughters Meredith and Norah, Sharlto Copley as his old friend Martin Battles, a wildlife biologist, and Tafara Nyatsansa as the reserve worker Banji.

Hoping to reconnect with his daughters, Nate brings them to the Mopani Reserve in South Africa, managed by Martin, who introduced him to his late wife. Martin shows them the village where she grew up, and Nate admits his guilt at having drifted apart from her after their separation, before she was diagnosed with terminal cancer. Touring restricted areas, Martin points out a lion pride he helped raise, then discovers that most of a nearby Tsonga community has been killed. Suspecting a rogue lion, he goes to investigate and is mauled, and the lion then attacks Nate, who escapes into the car; Meredith speeds off but crashes into a tree, stranding them. With the radio out of range, Nate assembles a tranquilliser rifle. In the next attack Meredith rescues the injured Martin and Norah drives the lion off with a dart. Martin guesses that poachers slaughtered the animal's pride, turning it against humans.

That night the poachers themselves arrive, offering a ride for money until they see Martin, a committed anti-poaching campaigner. The lion falls on them, killing most, and Nate recovers their truck keys. Martin holds the beast off so the girls can escape, Meredith suffering a deep wound, and when the car tumbles into a ravine he sacrifices himself by igniting leaking fuel, badly burning the lion. Low on fuel, the family shelters in an abandoned school used by the poachers. Locking his daughters inside, Nate lures the lion toward Martin's pride; it overpowers him, but the pride's males kill it, and Banji arrives to save the unconscious Nate. Recovered, he tells his daughters he loves them, and later the reunited family return to the reserve to recreate a photograph his wife took beside her favourite tree.

Shot in South Africa in 2021, the film was released by Universal Pictures in August 2022 and grossed $59.1 million worldwide on a $36 million budget. Critics were mostly positive, giving it 68% on Rotten Tomatoes, and its lion earned a Visual Effects Society Award nomination.

documents.title: The House of the Lost on the Cape
documents.overview: A strange old woman allows a teenage runaway and a young orphan to stay in an abandoned house that overlooks the sea. However, when a menacing entity threatens their new home, they must band together and face their fears to save it.
documents.plot:
The House of the Lost on the Cape (Japanese: Misaki no Mayoiga) is a 2021 Japanese animated fantasy drama directed by Shinya Kawatsura and produced by David Production, based on the novel by Sachiko Kashiwaba, which won the Noma Children's Literature Award. Reiko Yoshida wrote the screenplay and Yuri Miyauchi composed the score, with the closing song "Mayoiga" performed by Hitsujibungaku. Part of a project marking the tenth anniversary of the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, it features the voices of Mana Ashida as Yui, Sari Awano as Hiyori and Shinobu Otake as Kiwa, with Takuya Tasso, Sally Amaki, Mikio Date, Shohei Uno and Takeshi Tomizawa.

In the aftermath of the tsunami of 11 March 2011, two girls who do not know each other find themselves without a home. Seventeen-year-old Yui has run away from her abusive father, who blamed her for her mother leaving the family, while eight-year-old Hiyori lost her parents in a car accident and has not spoken since; the relatives who took her in lost their house in the disaster. At an evacuation shelter they meet Kiwa, a strange but kind old woman who takes pity on them and invites them to live with her as her granddaughters in an old, somewhat dilapidated house on a cape overlooking the sea, a mayoiga, which legend says looks after lost travelers. Although they followed Kiwa on impulse, the girls find comfort in the house and in her warm hospitality, and their wounded hearts gradually begin to heal. Then strange phenomena appear: curious beaked creatures that Kiwa calls "fushigitto" gather around the house, frightening Hiyori at first before proving harmless, while a black snake with red eyes seems malevolent. With help from friendly spirits of local folklore, including kappa, a zashiki-warashi, komainu guardian statues and jizō, Kiwa and the girls confront demons that feed on people's grief after the disaster.

The film opened in Japan on 27 August 2021 and won the Best Animation Film award at the Mainichi Film Awards. Eleven Arts released it in North America in September 2022, and it screened at the Annecy festival before a French release in 2023. French critics were largely positive: Les Fiches du cinéma called it a beautiful, delicate film about resilience and Télérama praised its subtle emotions, while Le Monde found the script somewhat predictable and Le Figaro considered it an underwhelming therapy film.

documents.title: Black Crab
documents.tagline: Hope burns brightest in the cold.
documents.overview: To end an apocalyptic war and save her daughter, a reluctant soldier embarks on a desperate mission to cross a frozen sea carrying a top-secret cargo.
documents.plot:
Black Crab (Swedish: Svart krabba) is a 2022 Swedish action thriller directed by Adam Berg, who adapted Jerker Virdborg's 2002 novel of the same name with Pelle Rådström. Noomi Rapace stars as Caroline Edh, a speed skater conscripted into a small unit sent to skate across frozen sea behind enemy lines. Netflix released the film on 18 March 2022.

In a flashback, Edh and her young daughter, Vanja, are caught in an enemy attack on civilians. Years later Edh is a soldier summoned to a base where Colonel Raad briefs a hand-picked team: the inexperienced signals specialist Karimi, the seasoned Danish soldier Malik, the Norwegian sniper Granvik and their leader, Captain Forsberg. They must skate across the ice-covered Stockholm archipelago to deliver two canisters to the research base on Ödö, which could win the war. Edh calls it a suicide mission but agrees when she is told that Vanja has been found alive in a refugee camp. Joined by Lieutenant Nylund, the team sets off as the base comes under attack. Forsberg drowns after breaking through thin ice, an enemy helicopter destroys their shelter after Karimi uses the radio, and Karimi and Malik are fatally wounded in a shootout with an elderly couple who had stayed behind.

Opening the canisters, the survivors find vials marked with a biohazard warning, apparently a biological weapon, and the dying Malik warns that it would mean not the end of the war but the end of everything before taking his own life. Granvik is killed in an enemy attack, and Edh shoots Nylund when he deserts with the vials to destroy them. Collapsing on the ice, she wakes at the base with frostbite, is decorated and promoted, and then learns that the promise of her daughter was only a ruse to keep her going. With Nylund, who survived, she steals the vials back from the laboratory during an evacuation. Cornered by the commander, Nordh, she steps off a cliff holding the vials and an unpinned grenade, and in death she is reunited with Vanja underwater.

Jakob Oftebro, Erik Enge, Dar Salim, Ardalan Esmaili, Aliette Opheim, David Dencik, Susan Taslimi and Stella Marcimain Klintberg appear in supporting roles. Reviews were mixed, with 50% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a consensus calling it exciting in the moment but bleak and derivative. The Guardian admired Berg's suspenseful handling of the ice but found its pacifist message hollow, while IGN called Rapace powerful throughout.

documents.title: The Colony
documents.tagline: Will Earth wait for us?
documents.overview: In the not-too-distant future: after a global catastrophe has wiped out nearly all of humanity on Earth, an elite astronaut from Space Colony Kepler must make a decision that will seal the fate of the people on both planets.
documents.plot: In the not-too-distant future: after a global catastrophe has wiped out nearly all of humanity on Earth, an elite astronaut from Space Colony Kepler must make a decision that will seal the fate of the people on both planets.

documents.title: The Devil Below
documents.tagline: They're not alone.
documents.overview: A group of four amateur adventurers who specialize in exploring remote and forsaken places pay a visit to Shookum Hills, a town in the remote Appalachian Mountains which was abandoned decades ago due to a mysterious coal mine fire.
documents.plot:
The Devil Below is a 2021 American horror film directed by Bradley Parker from a script by Eric Scherbarth and Stefan Jaworski. It stars Alicia Sanz as Arianne, an adventurer leading a scientific expedition to a vanished mining town, with Adan Canto as Darren, Will Patton as the former mine owner Schuttmann, Zach Avery and Chinaza Uche. The project was announced in 2018 under the title Shookum Hills and filmed in Kentucky that May.

In the prologue, miners leaving the Shookum Hills coal mine are attacked by an unseen creature that paralyzes Schuttmann and drags away his son, Eric. Years later, Arianne guides Darren, Shawn, Terry and Jaime in search of Shookum Hills, a town that disappeared from maps in the 1970s along with its people, supposedly because an underground coal fire opened sinkholes. Evading a pursuing car, the group climbs an electric fence to reach the abandoned mine. There they dismantle an electrified barrier around a sinkhole and lower sensors inside, and Terry is suddenly dragged in. Arianne and Jaime search for him in vain, while a local man, Dale, confronts the others for opening the hole and is knocked out. Fleeing on foot after crashing Dale's truck, the group loses Shawn to a creature, and Dale is also killed.

Locals led by Schuttmann rescue the survivors and explain that monsters living in the tunnels were the real reason the town emptied; the remaining residents have stayed to keep them contained. Returning to the sinkhole with two locals, the group is ambushed; both locals sacrifice themselves, and Jaime dies when a creature knocks away his grenade. Darren admits that he is working for a coal company seeking a rare mineral in the caves. Arianne reaches the surface but is paralyzed and taken to the creatures' lair, where she finds Darren and Shawn alive. Shawn explains that the creatures live like a colony of insects and feed their victims to a bloated queen. Recovering from the venom, Arianne kills the queen with a grenade from Darren. Climbing out, Darren is poisoned and cuts the rope to save her. The locals pull Arianne free and drive the creatures back with flamethrowers, and Schuttmann, telling her of his son's death, persuades her to help keep the creatures contained.

The Devil Below was released by Vertical Entertainment in limited theaters and on video on demand in the United States on March 5, 2021. Reviews were negative, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting a 15% approval rating from 13 critics.

documents.title: Blood Red Sky
documents.overview: A woman with a mysterious illness is forced into action when a group of terrorists attempt to hijack a transatlantic overnight flight. In order to protect her son she will have to reveal a dark secret, and unleash the inner monster she has fought to hide.
documents.plot:
Blood Red Sky is a 2021 German action thriller film directed by Ceri Thomas and written by Thomas and Michael Petroni. The movie stars Helen Mirren, Alex Rees, and Patrick Malahide.

The story begins with a group of young girls from different countries who are invited to attend an elite boarding school in Germany called the "Höhere Schule für Mädchen" (Higher School for Girls). Unbeknownst to them, this is actually a front for a secret organization that trains young women as assassins and spies.

The main character, Lena (played by Alex Rees), is a 16-year-old girl from England who is struggling to cope with the loss of her mother. She is recruited by the school's headmistress, Frau Müller (played by Helen Mirren), who reveals that she has been chosen for this special program.

As Lena begins her training at the school, she discovers that the other girls are also being trained in various skills such as marksmanship, hand-to-hand combat, and espionage. The girls are taught to be ruthless and efficient killers, with no regard for human life.

However, things take a dark turn when Lena discovers that Frau Müller's true intentions are not what they seem. She is revealed to be working for a powerful organization that uses the school as a recruitment tool for their assassins. The girls are forced to carry out missions on behalf of this organization, often with devastating consequences.

As Lena delves deeper into the truth, she must confront her own demons and make difficult choices between loyalty to Frau Müller and doing what is right. Along the way, she forms alliances with some of the other girls, including a rebellious student named Anna (played by Hanna Alström).

The plot thickens as Lena uncovers more about the organization's true purpose and the extent of their operations. She must use all her skills and training to take down Frau Müller and the organization, while also trying to escape the school and its deadly traps.

In the end, Lena emerges victorious but scarred by her experiences at the school. She manages to destroy the organization's headquarters and bring Frau Müller to justice, but not before she exacts a personal revenge on her former mentor.

Throughout the movie, Helen Mirren delivers a chilling performance as the ruthless and cunning headmistress, bringing depth and nuance to a character that could have easily been one-dimensional. The film's action sequences are intense and well-choreographed, making for a thrilling ride from start to finish.

Overall, Blood Red Sky is a gripping and suspenseful thriller that explores themes of loyalty, power, and the exploitation of young women. With its strong performances, clever plot twists, and high-octane action, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Gold
documents.tagline: Survive at any cost
documents.overview: In the not-too-distant future, two drifters traveling through the desert stumble across the biggest gold nugget ever found and the dream of immense wealth and greed takes hold. They hatch a plan to excavate their bounty, with one man leaving to secure the necessary tools while the other remains with the gold. The man who remains must endure harsh desert elements, ravenous wild dogs, and mysterious intruders, while battling the sinking suspicion that he has been abandoned to his fate.
documents.plot:
Gold is a 2022 Australian survival thriller film directed by Anthony Hayes, who co-stars alongside Zac Efron and Susie Porter. It was released internationally on 13 January 2022 before debuting on the streaming service Stan on 26 January, and a limited theatrical and video-on-demand release followed on 11 March 2022.

In a dystopian near future, a lone traveller named Virgil arrives at a remote outpost and pays a local man, Keith, to drive him across an inhospitable desert to a place known as the Compound. During the journey the car overheats, and while stopped the two men stumble on an enormous gold nugget buried in the ground. Unable to dig it out with their basic tools, they agree that one of them must stay to guard the find while the other leaves to fetch an excavator. Keith suggests that Virgil does not have what it takes to survive alone, but Virgil insists on staying, since he was the one who found the gold. Keith leaves him with the remaining supplies and promises to return in five days. As the days pass under the scorching sun, Virgil's body and mind begin to deteriorate, and paranoia sets in. He builds a shelter from the wreckage of a crashed plane, fends off wild dogs, and loses precious water in a clumsy encounter with a snake. When a woman appears in the desert, suspicious of his reasons for being there and contemptuous of people fleeing the cities for the resources of her land, accuses him of hiding something, the encounter ends in violence. A sandstorm then destroys his camp and leaves him badly wounded, and as he drifts between consciousness and delirium, haunted by visions and visited by another mysterious scavenger, he clings to his radio and to the hope that Keith will return before the desert claims him.

On Rotten Tomatoes, 65% of 51 critics' reviews of Gold are positive, with a consensus that Efron's committed central performance makes the film worth watching even when the film as a whole struggles to match it. It grossed about $230,000 worldwide in theaters.

documents.title: Sword Art Online the Movie -Progressive- Aria of a Starless Night
documents.original_title: 劇場版 ソードアート・オンライン-プログレッシブ- 星なき夜のアリア
documents.tagline: This might be a game, but it's not something you play!
documents.overview: One month after Kayaba Akihiko's game of death began, the death toll continues to rise, two thousand players having already lost their lives to the ultra-difficult VRMMO world of Sword Art Online. On the day of the strategy meeting to plan out the first-floor boss battle, Kirito, a solo player who vows to fight alone to get stronger, runs into a rare, high-level female player. She gracefully dispatches powerful monsters with a single rapier that flashes like a shooting star in the night...
documents.plot:
Sword Art Online: Progressive - Aria of a Starless Night is a Japanese animated science fiction film based on the light novel series "Sword Art Online" by Reki Kawahara. The movie takes place after the events of Sword Art Online: Progressive - Scherzo of Deep Night.

The story follows Kirito and his friends, including Asuna, Rika Shinozaki, and Lisbeth, as they participate in a new virtual reality game called "Eclipse." In this game, players are transported to a world inspired by the works of Edgar Allan Poe. The main objective is to uncover the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of the game's creator.

As Kirito delves deeper into the game, he discovers that something sinister is at play. He must navigate through the dark and eerie world, solving puzzles and overcoming challenges to unravel the mystery. Along the way, he encounters new characters, including a mysterious woman named Rika Shinozaki, who seems to be connected to the game's creator.

Throughout his journey, Kirito faces off against formidable foes, including a powerful AI entity known as "The Puppeteer." As the stakes grow higher, Kirito must confront his own demons and make difficult choices that will impact the fate of the world in Eclipse.

One of the standout aspects of the movie is its exploration of themes such as grief, trauma, and the psychological effects of virtual reality. The film's use of atmospheric sound design and visuals creates a haunting and immersive experience, drawing the viewer into the dark and twisted world of Eclipse.

Overall, Sword Art Online: Progressive - Aria of a Starless Night is a gripping and thought-provoking addition to the Sword Art Online franchise. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and stunning visuals, it's a must-watch for fans of science fiction and adventure.

documents.title: The Lost Girls
documents.tagline: A family legend. A neverending fantasy.
documents.overview: Inspired by the classic tale of Peter Pan, The Lost Girls chronicles four generations of Darling women as they struggle in the aftermath of their adventures with Peter Pan in Neverland. Like her grandmother and her mother Jane before her, Wendy must escape Pan’s hold on her and the promise he desperately wants her to keep. As her daughter Berry comes into Peter’s orbit, Wendy must fight to save her relationship with her daughter while reconciling her legacy.
documents.plot:
The Lost Girls is a 2022 British fantasy drama written and directed by Livia De Paolis, who also plays the adult Wendy. Based on Laurie Fox's 2003 novel of the same name, it is inspired by J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan and is set several generations after the original story, exploring the consequences of Peter's promise to keep returning to the women of the Darling family. Vanessa Redgrave, Joely Richardson, Iain Glen, Louis Partridge and Julian Ovenden co-star. The film was released in cinemas and on streaming platforms on 17 June 2022.

Wendy Braverman is the granddaughter of the original Wendy Darling. As a little girl, she listens to her grandmother, Nana Wendy, tell stories of Neverland and promise that Peter Pan will one day come for her too and that she will be enchanted by him. Wendy is homeschooled by her protective father, who fears losing her as he lost his wife Jane, Wendy's mother, who disappeared years before.

When Wendy is a teenager, Peter appears at her window one night, and she falls in love with him. He flies her to Neverland and makes her promise never to grow up. There she has a disturbing encounter with Captain Hook and a vision of her missing mother. Back home, Wendy waits for Peter to return, but the years pass without him. Nana Wendy warns her that she will love another man, but that it will never be enough. As an adult, Wendy marries a kind man named Adam and starts a family, yet she remains haunted by memories of Peter and visions of Hook, and her longing for the boy who never grew up strains her marriage. When Peter reappears and she asks him about her mother, Wendy begins to understand a painful pattern that has shaped generations of women in her family, each enchanted by Peter and left unable to fully live their adult lives. She must decide how to protect her own daughter from the same fate.

The film reinterprets the Peter Pan story from the perspective of the girls Peter leaves behind, treating his visits less as a magical gift than as a source of lasting loss and emotional damage. It drew attention for its cast, which brought together Vanessa Redgrave and her daughter Joely Richardson, with Louis Partridge as an ageless, charming and ultimately unsettling Peter Pan. Reviews were generally negative, with critics finding its ideas intriguing but its execution uneven.

documents.title: Zeros and Ones
documents.tagline: It's always deadliest before the dawn.
documents.overview: Called to Rome to stop an imminent terrorist bombing, a soldier desperately seeks news of his imprisoned brother — a rebel with knowledge that could thwart the attack. Navigating the capital's darkened streets, he races to a series of ominous encounters to keep the Vatican from being blown to bits.
documents.plot:
Zeros and Ones is a 2021 thriller written and directed by Abel Ferrara and shot in Rome, the director's adopted home, during the COVID-19 lockdown. Ethan Hawke stars in a dual role as JJ, an American soldier, and his twin brother, with Cristina Chiriac, Phil Neilson, Valerio Mastandrea, Dounia Sichov, Babak Karimi, Stephen Gurewitz and Ferrara's daughter Anna in supporting parts. Developed from an older Ferrara script idea about the post-9/11 war on terror, it was produced by Maze Pictures, Rimsky Productions and Almost Never Films, with cinematography by Sean Price Williams; cast and crew worked in masks and social bubbles, and masks, hand sanitizer and video calls appear on screen.

The film opens and closes with Hawke speaking directly to the audience as himself about the picture. In the story, a gaunt, bearded JJ arrives in a deserted, locked-down Rome on a murky undercover mission, called there to stop an imminent terrorist bombing. He is desperate for news of his twin brother, a messianic revolutionary who is being held captive and tortured and whose fate shifts with each unreliable witness; the brother, glimpsed in brief scenes, rants about fascism and asks why no one sets themselves on fire anymore. Moving through the city at night with armed soldiers and foreign agents on his trail, JJ exchanges terse instructions with strangers in black cars, holds cryptic conversations in a mosque, shares a fraught intimacy with a young mother and her child and buys drugs in a seedy club.

His shadowy errands finally come together when he is caught up in a massive bombing of the Vatican, apparently a staged false-flag operation designed to inflame an ancient conflict between rival civilizations, while the film's dialogue repeatedly casts Jesus as a radical soldier and war casualty. It ends on a hopeful note, with footage of Anna Ferrara running through Rome at sunrise as life returns to the city.

Zeros and Ones premiered in competition at the 74th Locarno Film Festival on August 12, 2021, where Ferrara won the Pardo for Best Direction, and Lionsgate released it in select US theaters and on digital platforms on November 19, 2021. Reviews were mixed, with a 54 percent Rotten Tomatoes rating. The Hollywood Reporter found it a minor, cryptic work rescued in part by Hawke's committed performance and its eerie, lo-fi images, while RogerEbert.com described it as on-the-nose but driven by Ferrara's blunt elemental force, likening it to a kind of action painting.

documents.title: Father Christmas Is Back
documents.overview: Four sisters – Caroline, Joanna, Paulina, and Vicky – reunite for the Christmas Holiday in a Yorkshire mansion. However, their estranged father, James, joins in for the first time since he left the family behind decades prior. The group attempts to get through the holiday despite comedic misunderstandings, while also uncovering the long-buried secret that tore their family apart, so many years ago.
documents.plot:
Father Christmas Is Back is a British festive comedy from 2021, co-directed by Philippe Martinez and Mick Davis. Elizabeth Hurley, Nathalie Cox, Talulah Riley and Naomi Frederick play four sisters reunited for the holidays, with John Cleese as their uncle John, Kelsey Grammer as their estranged father James, Caroline Quentin as their mother Elizabeth, Kris Marshall as Peter and April Bowlby as Jackie.

Caroline, a perfectionist, hosts Christmas for her sisters at the Yorkshire mansion she shares with her husband Peter and their children, Daisey and Henry. When the tree topples over on 22 December, Peter and the children redecorate it with homemade ornaments. The guests arrive: free-spirited Vicky, fresh from couch-surfing around the United States; Joanna, a glamorous fashion editor, with her boyfriend Felix; their mother Elizabeth; and Paulina, a scholar writing a thesis on the Beatles, while Uncle John watches from a distance. Caroline presents her meticulously planned schedule, but tensions flare when Vicky teases Joanna about her age. Vicky then admits that she spent two weeks in Florida with their father, James, who walked out on the family years before, and soon afterwards James arrives with his much younger American girlfriend, Jackie, having been invited by Vicky without anyone's knowledge.

The sisters turn on Vicky, who storms off in Felix's Rolls-Royce and spends the night with the barman at the village pub, while Elizabeth stays out all night with John. At the church fundraiser on Christmas Eve, Vicky sells Joanna's designer clothes for a pittance and offers Felix's car as a prize, forcing the couple to buy back their belongings. When John and James go outside to settle their differences, James instead proposes to Jackie. He later apologises to his daughters for leaving 27 years earlier, explaining that he had quietly supported them all along and that their mother kept him informed. Jackie's elaborate light display then blows the old house's electrics. On Christmas Day Peter finds a positive pregnancy test and assumes it is Caroline's, but Joanna admits it is hers. Elizabeth finally reveals why James left: she had become pregnant by John, who is Vicky's biological father. With Caroline's dinner ruined, the family spends the day serving their meals at a nursing home.

Filmed at Birdsall House near Malton in September 2020, the film was released by Netflix on 7 November 2021. A sequel, Christmas in Paradise, followed in 2022.

documents.title: Nope
documents.tagline: What’s a bad miracle?
documents.overview: Residents in a lonely gulch of inland California bear witness to an uncanny, chilling discovery.
documents.plot:
Nope is a 2022 American science fiction horror film written, directed, and co-produced by Jordan Peele. The movie stars Daniel Kaluuya, Keke Palmer, and Steven Yeun.

The story takes place in the fictional town of Sanderson, California, where a young couple, Otis (Daniel Kaluuya) and his sister, Emerald (Keke Palmer), live with their father, OJ (Keegan-Michael Key). The family runs a horse ranch, but they're struggling to make ends meet.

One night, the siblings witness something extraordinary - a UFO hovering above their property. As word of the sighting spreads, Otis and Emerald become an unlikely sensation, drawing attention from wealthy investors and media outlets. However, things take a dark turn when the family discovers that the UFO is not just a one-time event but part of a larger phenomenon.

The movie delves into themes of gentrification, colonialism, and the exploitation of marginalized communities. The aliens, which are referred to as "the Noopes," seem to be drawn to the town's history and cultural significance, particularly its connection to the African American experience.

As Otis and Emerald try to navigate their newfound fame, they must also confront the sinister forces that seek to exploit the UFO sightings for personal gain. The film builds towards a tense and unsettling climax, exploring the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control.

Throughout the movie, Peele pays homage to classic sci-fi films like "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" and "E.T.," while also subverting expectations and challenging his audience's perceptions. The Noopes are both fascinating and terrifying, embodying a sense of otherness that is both captivating and unsettling.

Ultimately, Nope is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores the complexities of human nature in the face of the unknown. With its talented cast, clever script, and Peele's signature social commentary, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and horror.

documents.title: Do Revenge
documents.tagline: I'll do yours if you do mine.
documents.overview: A dethroned queen bee at a posh private high school strikes a secret deal with an unassuming new student to enact revenge on one another’s enemies.
documents.plot:
Do Revenge is a 2022 American teen comedy film written and directed by Olivia Wilde. The movie follows the story of two high school students, Amber Reynolds (Mila Brener) and Daphne Dickson (Alba Baptista), who were once inseparable friends in their youth.

The film begins with Amber, now a successful and popular student at an elite private school, who is struggling to cope with her new life. She has become isolated from her friends and family due to the pressures of being a socialite. Meanwhile, Daphne, who was once Amber's best friend, has moved away and is now attending a different high school.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Amber discovers that Daphne is now a student at her new school, and she decides to take revenge on her for abandoning their friendship. Amber starts by sabotaging Daphne's life, including ruining her relationships with her friends and family, and even getting into a physical altercation with her.

However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that Amber's actions are motivated by more than just a desire for revenge. She is struggling to cope with her own personal demons, including a troubled home life and a strained relationship with her mother. Through her interactions with Daphne, Amber begins to confront her past and work through her emotional issues.

As the plot unfolds, it becomes clear that both Amber and Daphne are complex characters with their own set of problems. While Amber appears to be the perfect student on the surface, she is hiding a dark secret: she has been struggling with anxiety and depression. Meanwhile, Daphne seems to have it all together, but her life is actually falling apart.

Throughout the film, Wilde explores themes of female friendship, class differences, and the pressures of high school life. The movie also features a standout performance from Baptista, who brings depth and nuance to the character of Daphne.

In the end, Amber's actions lead to a confrontation with her mother, which forces her to confront her emotional demons once and for all. The film ends on a hopeful note, as Amber begins to rebuild her life and form new connections with those around her.

Overall, Do Revenge is a thought-provoking and entertaining film that explores the complexities of female friendship and the pressures of high school life. With standout performances from its cast, including Baptista and Brener, the movie is sure to resonate with audiences.

documents.title: Purple Hearts
documents.overview: An aspiring musician agrees to a marriage of convenience with a soon-to-deploy Marine, but a tragedy soon turns their fake relationship all too real.
documents.plot:
Purple Hearts is a 2022 American romantic drama film directed by Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum and written by Jessica Sorensen. The movie stars Sofia Carson, Nicholas Galitzine, and Tom Hiddleston.

The story revolves around Mariana (Sofia Carson), a young woman who joins the military to escape her troubled past. She meets Luke (Nicholas Galitzine), a charming and charismatic soldier who is also struggling with his own demons. The two form an instant connection, but their relationship is put to the test when they are deployed to Afghanistan.

As Mariana and Luke navigate the challenges of war, they must also confront their personal issues. Mariana is haunted by her past, including a traumatic event that led to her joining the military. Luke, on the other hand, is struggling with PTSD and feelings of guilt over his role in a tragic accident during his previous deployment.

Despite the obstacles, Mariana and Luke's relationship deepens, and they find comfort in each other's arms. However, their love is put to the test when Luke is injured in combat, leaving him with a broken leg and a damaged sense of purpose.

As Mariana cares for Luke, she begins to confront her own demons and find healing through their relationship. Meanwhile, Luke must come to terms with his past mistakes and learn to forgive himself. The two must also navigate the complexities of military life, including the challenges of being in a long-distance relationship and dealing with the trauma of war.

Throughout the movie, Mariana and Luke's love for each other is tested by the harsh realities of war. However, their bond ultimately proves strong enough to overcome even the most difficult challenges. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Mariana and Luke reunited and looking towards a future together.

One of the standout aspects of Purple Hearts is its portrayal of complex characters and relationships. Sofia Carson shines as Mariana, bringing depth and nuance to her performance. Nicholas Galitzine is equally impressive as Luke, conveying a sense of vulnerability and strength that makes his character relatable and endearing.

Overall, Purple Hearts is a powerful and emotional romance that explores the complexities of love, trauma, and healing in the face of adversity. With its strong performances and thought-provoking themes, this movie is sure to resonate with audiences looking for a compelling and uplifting story.

documents.title: Never Back Down: Revolt
documents.overview: An amateur fighter is lured by a trafficking syndicate specializing in elite underground fighting where her brutal captor forces her to fight or face certain death.
documents.plot:
Never Back Down: Revolt is an American martial arts film of 2021 directed by Kellie Madison and written by Audrey Arkins, a standalone sequel to Never Back Down: No Surrender (2016) and the fourth entry in the Never Back Down series. Darker than its predecessors, it follows kidnapped women forced to fight in an underground ring. Olivia Popica stars as Anya, with Brooke Johnston as the promoter Mariah, Michael Bisping as her enforcer Janek, Neetu Chandra as the reigning champion Jaya, Tommy Bastow as Anya's brother Aslan and James Faulkner as Julian.

Anya and Aslan are Russian immigrants in London, orphaned when their parents were killed in the Chechen war. Anya has looked after her brother ever since, working as a housekeeper and backing his failing MMA career. Short of cash, Aslan agrees to throw a bout for Julian, a wealthy businessman, but Anya, unaware of the deal, urges him on and he wins, costing Julian £30,000. When one of Julian's bodyguards attacks Aslan, Anya beats the man, impressing Julian's associate Mariah, who offers her fights to clear her brother's debt. Mariah takes her to Rome for a match, but they end up at an isolated villa.

Anya soon realizes she has been trafficked. When she tries to flee, Janek beats her and locks her in a makeshift cell with other women, amateur fighters likewise lured by Mariah. Led by Jaya, they explain that they are made to fight one another for rich gamblers, and that refusal means being sent to a brothel in Albania. Anya starts planning an uprising, though the jaded women, Jaya above all, think it hopeless. Valentina, brain-damaged by past beatings, unwittingly betrays the plan, and as punishment Mariah makes Jaya fight her; rather than be sold into sexual slavery, Valentina begs Jaya to kill her, and Jaya reluctantly does. Now with nothing left to lose, Jaya joins Anya in leading the revolt.

Aslan holds Julian at gunpoint to force Anya's release, but she manages to call him on the villa doctor's phone, giving him the location and asking for the police. The women rise up and kill their captors; Jaya finishes off Janek with a scalpel. They storm the arena and attack the watching millionaires, and although some of the women die, all of the captors are killed. Anya beats Mariah to death after she tries to kill her, and Anya and Jaya walk out through the front door to freedom.

The film was shot in London during the COVID-19 pandemic and was released digitally and on DVD in November 2021 to mixed reactions.

documents.title: Trees of Peace
documents.tagline: Where there is life, there is hope.
documents.overview: In April of 1994, four women from different backgrounds and beliefs are trapped and hiding during the Rwandan genocide. Their fight for survival against all odds unites the women in an unbreakable sisterhood.
documents.plot:
Trees of Peace is an American drama film written and directed by Alanna Brown in her feature directorial debut. Inspired by true events from the 1994 Rwandan genocide, it stars Eliane Umuhire, Charmaine Bingwa, Ella Cannon and Bola Koleosho as four women of different backgrounds who hide together in a hole beneath a house for 81 days, with Tongayi Chirisa in a supporting role. Produced by RR Productions, Abstract Entertainment and A Brown Girl Films, with Ron and Michelle Ray providing the financing and Nicole Avant among the executive producers, it completed production in November 2019 and premiered at the 2021 Santa Barbara International Film Festival. Netflix acquired the global rights in March 2022 and released the 98-minute English-language film worldwide on 10 June 2022.

The film opens with Annick (Umuhire) reading from the journal in which she recorded the days spent in hiding. As the violence between Hutu and Tutsi engulfs Rwanda in April 1994, four women take refuge in the storage basement under the kitchen of the house Annick, a pregnant moderate Hutu, shares with her husband Francois (Chirisa), who supplies them with rations and news from outside. With her are Mutesi (Koleosho), a young and angry Tutsi woman who blames the Hutu for the killings; Jeanette (Bingwa), a nun whose faith is repeatedly tested; and Peyton (Cannon), an American on a Peace Corps-style mission who hopes to atone for past sins. At first the women distrust and clash with one another, and at one point Mutesi spitefully eats more than her share of the food. As they share their histories of miscarriage, rape and family strife, Mutesi admits that she does not want to die with her anger, and a sisterhood begins to form. The women draw portraits of one another, learn to read English and become devoted to Seeds of Love, Trees of Peace, a children's book Peyton carries in her bag, while they must stifle their cries as they hear people being executed outside. Over the weeks they suffer nightmares, hallucinations and suffocating conditions. Closing title cards note the role of women in Rwanda's post-genocide recovery.

Trees of Peace received a 100% critics' rating on Rotten Tomatoes and reached Netflix's top ten in dozens of countries. Radhika Menon of Decider praised the superb ensemble, singling out Koleosho, and its blend of claustrophobic dread with hope, while The Hindu's Tamma Moksha called it a moving survival story whose characters slipped into stereotype.

documents.title: Time Is Up
documents.tagline: Falling in love is a state of change.
documents.overview: Vivien, an accomplished student with a passion for physics, and Roy, a troubled young man, are involved in an accident that forces them to reclaim their lives one minute at the time.
documents.plot:
Time Is Up is a 2021 English-language Italian romantic drama directed by Elisa Amoruso, who co-wrote the screenplay with Lorenzo Ura and Patrizia Fiorellini. It stars Bella Thorne as Vivien, Benjamin Mascolo as Roy, Sebastiano Pigazzi as Steve and Nikolay Moss as the swim coach Dylan, with Emma Lo Bianco and Giampiero Judica as Vivien's parents and Roberto Davide as Roy's father. Principal photography began in November 2020, and much of the story unfolds in Rome.

Vivien is an affluent high school student with a passion for math and physics, dating Steve, the clean-cut star of the school swim team. Roy, a poor, heavily tattooed swimmer on the same team, is told that unless he improves his times he will miss an upcoming meet in Rome, which he needs to secure a college scholarship; otherwise, his father reminds him, he will end up working in the family garage. After Vivien follows her mother and sees her with another man, she wanders into a rough part of town and is harassed by a group of teenagers, until Roy steps in to help.

Steve has become distant and unreachable, and Vivien, insecure about her abilities, postpones an important quantum physics test. Roy knows the reason for Steve's absences: he is secretly involved with Dylan, their coach, and Steve warns Roy to keep quiet. Roy beats Steve in a race and qualifies for the trip to Rome. After learning that her parents separated a year earlier, Vivien flies to Rome to surprise Steve but spends the day exploring the city with Roy, and the two grow close. A painful discovery and a serious accident then upend her life, and back home she must piece together what really happened and decide whom to trust.

The film deals with first love, self-confidence, family breakdown and the pressure of expectations, with music playing a central role in the story.

Time Is Up was released in the United States on 9 September 2021 by Voltage Pictures and in Italy on 25 October 2021 by 01 Distribution. It was panned for its acting and screenplay, with Decider calling it a forgettable mess, though its music received praise. A sequel, Game of Love, followed in 2022.

documents.title: Ambulance
documents.tagline: It was supposed to be a simple heist.
documents.overview: Decorated veteran Will Sharp, desperate for money to cover his wife's medical bills, asks for help from his adoptive brother Danny. A charismatic career criminal, Danny instead offers him a score: the biggest bank heist in Los Angeles history: $32 million.
documents.plot:
Ambulance is a 2022 action thriller film directed by Michael Bay, starring Jake Gyllenhaal, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, and Eiza González.

The movie follows Will (Jake Gyllenhaal), a former Army medic who has lost his job due to a traumatic event. He's struggling to find work as an ambulance driver, but things take a turn when he's hired by a wealthy client, Dr. Kim (Hoon Lee), to transport him and his wife, Sophia (Eiza González), to a medical facility.

However, the situation quickly turns deadly when Will discovers that Dr. Kim is involved in a large-scale opioid trafficking operation. The doctor has been using his wealth and influence to smuggle large quantities of fentanyl into the country, and he's willing to do whatever it takes to keep his operation running smoothly.

As Will tries to escape with Sophia, they're pursued by Dr. Kim's henchmen, who will stop at nothing to silence them. The two must use their wits and resourcefulness to evade capture and bring down Dr. Kim's empire.

Throughout the film, Bay's signature style is on full display, with high-octane action sequences, heart-pumping suspense, and a healthy dose of humor. Gyllenhaal delivers a strong performance as Will, bringing depth and nuance to his character despite being typecast in a more typical "tough guy" role.

The film also features a standout supporting turn from Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, who plays a mysterious and charismatic figure with his own agenda. The chemistry between the leads is undeniable, and their banter adds a welcome layer of humor to an otherwise intense thriller.

Overall, Ambulance is a tense, adrenaline-fueled ride that's sure to appeal to fans of action movies. While it may not be Bay's most subtle or nuanced work, he delivers on his promise of high-octane thrills and spills, making for a fun and entertaining watch.

documents.title: Long Story Short
documents.tagline: Love... blink and you'll miss it.
documents.overview: Teddy wakes up the morning after his wedding to discover that he's jumped forward a year in his life to his first anniversary. Trapped in an endless cycle of time jumps, transported another year ahead every few minutes, he is faced with a race against time as his life crumbles around him.
documents.plot: Teddy wakes up the morning after his wedding to discover that he's jumped forward a year in his life to his first anniversary. Trapped in an endless cycle of time jumps, transported another year ahead every few minutes, he is faced with a race against time as his life crumbles around him.

documents.title: Arlo the Alligator Boy
documents.overview: Upon learning that he is from New York City, a wide-eyed boy, who is half human and half alligator, decides to leave his sheltered life in the swamp and search for his long lost father. A musical adventure.
documents.plot:
Arlo the Alligator Boy is an animated film that explores the complexities of identity, community, and acceptance. The story revolves around Arlo, a young alligator boy who struggles to find his place in a world where he doesn't quite fit in with either humans or other alligators.

At its core, the movie delves into themes of self-discovery and belonging. Arlo's journey is a powerful metaphor for navigating the challenges of growing up and finding one's own unique identity. As he navigates the complexities of his mixed heritage, Arlo must confront the expectations of those around him and learn to embrace his individuality.

The film also touches on the importance of community and acceptance. Through Arlo's relationships with the people and creatures in his life, the movie highlights the value of finding a supportive network that celebrates diversity and promotes inclusivity. By exploring these themes, Arlo the Alligator Boy offers a heartwarming and thought-provoking tale that encourages viewers to embrace their own uniqueness and celebrate the beauty of differences.

Overall, the movie's narrative is infused with a sense of wonder, curiosity, and openness, making it a delightful and engaging watch for audiences of all ages.

documents.title: Dangerous
documents.tagline: Killer instincts die hard.
documents.overview: A reformed sociopath heads to a remote island after the death of his brother. Soon after his arrival, the island falls under siege from a deadly gang of mercenaries, and when he discovers their role in his brother’s demise, he sets out on a relentless quest for vengeance.
documents.plot:
Dangerous is a 2021 action thriller directed by David Hackl, his fifth feature, starring Scott Eastwood, Tyrese Gibson, Famke Janssen, Kevin Durand and Mel Gibson. It was produced by Kevin DeWalt, Ben DeWalt and Doug Falconer through Minds Eye Entertainment and Falconer Pictures, and was Falconer's last film as a producer before his sudden death in July 2021. Shooting took place in Canada, including Kamloops and the Okanagan, between November and December 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Dylan Forrester, a former assassin with psychopathic tendencies, has been keeping his instincts in check with mood-stabilizing medication under the supervision of Dr. Alderwood. When his brother Sean dies suddenly, Dylan breaks his parole to travel to Guardian Island, which belongs to his family, hoping to make peace with his mother, Linda, who fears what he is and urges him to leave. Agent Shaughnessy is hunting him, convinced he is too dangerous to be free. On the island, Sheriff McCoy discovers that Dylan is a fugitive and locks him in a bunker.

A fixer named Cole then arrives with a team of mercenaries and kills the sheriff. Freed by a hotel employee named Jo, Dylan returns to protect his family, taking out several of Cole's men. He suspects that Sean had been hiding something, and the survivors discover a secret passage that leads to a Japanese World War II submarine loaded with Yamashita's gold. Sean had partnered with Cole in buying the island to find the treasure. In a shootout around the submarine, Dylan and an ally named Massey turn one of its deck guns on the mercenaries before Cole kills Massey and takes Linda hostage. Dylan dumps the gold Cole wanted into the water, Shaughnessy arrives and is wounded, and Dylan finally stabs Cole to death and rescues his mother. Leaving with some of the gold, he says goodbye to Dr. Alderwood by phone and throws his medication into the ocean.

Eastwood plays Dylan, Durand plays Cole, Janssen plays Shaughnessy, Tyrese Gibson plays Sheriff McCoy and Mel Gibson plays Dr. Alderwood. Lionsgate released the film in American and Canadian theaters and on demand on 5 November 2021. Reviews were negative, with 30% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27, and it received two Golden Raspberry nominations and two Canadian Screen Award nominations. It later reached streaming top-ten charts in 17 countries.

documents.title: Under Wraps
documents.overview: Three friends try to save their mummified friend, Harold, from greedy criminals by returning him to his resting place before midnight on Halloween.
documents.plot:
Under Wraps is an American family horror comedy made for television in 2021, directed by Alex Zamm, who wrote it with William Robertson, as a remake of the 1997 film of the same name, the first Disney Channel Original Movie. Produced by MarVista Entertainment and Brightlight Pictures, it features Malachi Barton in the role of Marshall, with Christian J. Simon as Gilbert, Sophia Hammons as Amy and Phil Wright as the mummy Harold, plus Melanie Brook as Buzzy, Brent Stait as the villain Kubot and Karin Konoval as the collector Ravensworth.

Twelve-year-old Marshall loves horror films, unlike his timid best friend Gilbert, and is struggling to accept Ted, the man his divorced mother is dating. The boys see a body being carried into the house of their creepy neighbour, Mr. Kubot. On a museum trip they team up with Amy, a newcomer who shares Marshall's taste for horror, and hear of an Egyptian mummy couple, one of whom has mysteriously gone missing. Sneaking into Kubot's house, the three find the mummy, which comes to life and follows them home. Marshall hides him in his bedroom, names him Harold and introduces him to pizza and hot sauce, and the kids plan to make a mummy film with him for a school project. When Harold wanders off to the museum where his beloved's sarcophagus lies, they discover that his amulet is what brought him to life.

Their monster-expert friend Buzzy translates the amulet: unless both mummies are back in their sarcophagi by the third day, Harold will crumble to dust. Meanwhile, Amy tells Marshall how she came to accept her stepfather, encouraging him to give Ted a chance. Kubot, realising that a living mummy could make him rich, snatches the amulet from Harold at the school's Halloween carnival and delivers him to Ravensworth at an abandoned ice cream factory. Gilbert loses his nerve but returns to retrieve the amulet, revived Harold fights off the henchmen, and Buzzy's trap knocks out Kubot and Ravensworth. The friends break into the museum to reunite Harold with his love before he returns to his sarcophagus, and Gilbert admits that his fear of losing his friends drove him back.

Shot in and around Vancouver, the film premiered on Disney Channel on 1 October 2021 and on Disney+ a week later. Reviews were mixed, though Common Sense Media gave it four out of five stars for its diversity, spookiness and humour.

documents.title: Too Close for Christmas
documents.overview: When Hayley accepts an invitation to spend Christmas with her sister’s new in-laws, her seemingly perfect holiday takes a turn when Paul, Hayley's brother-in-law's brother, unexpectedly shows up. Still harboring a grudge against Paul for ending her last relationship, Hayley reluctantly spends time with Paul and slowly realizes she may have been too quick a judge on Paul
documents.plot:
Too Close for Christmas is a 2020 Canadian-American romantic holiday television film directed by Ernie Barbarash and written by Nicole Baxter, made for Lifetime by the Motion Picture Corporation of America, Brad Krevoy Television and Hideaway Pictures. It stars Jessica Lowndes as Hayley Parker and Chad Michael Murray as Paul, with Vanessa Sears as Hayley's sister Amy and Steve Byers, Rob Stewart, Deanna Jarvis, Chris Farquhar and Seana McKenna in supporting roles. It runs 88 minutes and premiered on Lifetime on Friday, 4 December 2020.

Hayley is a perfectionist Manhattan event planner who works hard but is still waiting for a long-overdue promotion and keeps fretting about a co-promotion that is on the cards. For the first time in many years she accepts an invitation to spend Christmas with her sister Amy and Amy's new in-laws at the family's holiday home, on one condition: that Paul, the brother of Amy's husband, will not be there. Hayley has a bad history with him from Amy's wedding, holding a grudge against him for ending her last relationship. To everyone's surprise, Paul unexpectedly shows up, though only for one night, or so Hayley thinks until his flight to a ski trip in Switzerland is cancelled the next morning. Forced to spend the days before Christmas together, the two clash, but Paul draws her into a series of holiday activities and recruits her to help the committee planning the town gala, where she takes charge of ticket sales. Hayley, who usually eats only greens and protein, is surprised by how much she enjoys the ribs at the local diner, and she gradually gets the emotionally guarded Paul to open up and embrace the family's Christmas food traditions. As Paul encourages her to stop selling herself short at work, she realizes she may have judged him too quickly, and after a late setback in their relationship he apologizes, showing her that she deserves better in both her career and her love life.

Reviews were mixed. Alakananda Bandyopadhyay of MEAWW found the romance a gush of warmth, praising the leads' ease in their roles and Barbarash's festive direction while finding the score too cartoonish. Rissi JC of RissiWrites enjoyed it as a fun enemies-to-lovers comedy with good banter between Lowndes and Murray, while noting the spark was weaker at the turning point. Jesse Burleson of Views on Film gave it one and a half stars, calling it a predictable slog and finding Murray mostly annoying.

documents.title: The Desperate Hour
documents.tagline: Time is running out.
documents.overview: A woman desperately races to save her child after police place her hometown on lockdown due to an active shooter incident.
documents.plot:
The Desperate Hour is a 2021 thriller directed by Phillip Noyce and written by Chris Sparling. Naomi Watts stars as a mother racing to reach her son after his school is locked down because of an active shooter, told almost entirely through her phone calls. The film was shot in the North Bay area of Ontario in 2020 and premiered under its original title, Lakewood, at the 2021 Toronto International Film Festival.

Amy, recently widowed and still struggling with grief, takes a personal day off work. She sees her young daughter, Emily, off on the school bus, and finds her teenage son, Noah, still in bed, claiming to be sick. Amy goes for a long run through the woods, taking routine calls as she jogs, when police cars race past and an alert arrives on her phone: all local schools are on lockdown because of a shooting at the high school.

Miles from home and from her car, Amy frantically works her phone to learn what is happening. Piece by piece she discovers that a gunman has opened fire at the school and killed a student, and that Noah is not at home after all; his truck has been spotted in the school parking lot. A mechanic near the school tells her that police are searching the truck, and questions from an officer relayed through a 911 dispatcher make her fear that her own son might be the shooter. The police later reassure her that the gunman is not a student and that Noah is not under suspicion.

Desperate to reach the school, Amy makes her way to the highway and catches a ride. Using a phone number obtained by her boss, she calls the shooter herself; he answers briefly before hanging up, and she learns he is a former school employee. Police scold her for interfering, but after a short, frightened call from Noah, who is trapped with other hostages, they ask her to call the gunman again to distract him while officers prepare to breach the room. Arriving at the scene, she hears gunfire over the line and loses contact. At the police barricade, she finally sees Noah emerge alive, and mother and son are joyfully reunited. Afterward, Noah posts a message online condemning school shootings and urging people to stand up against them.

The film was released in theaters by Roadside Attractions and Vertical Entertainment on February 25, 2022. It was poorly received; Rotten Tomatoes reported 28% approval, its consensus saying that Watts gives her all but the film falls short as both a thriller and social commentary, and Metacritic gave it 35 out of 100.

documents.title: The Bubble
documents.tagline: Where will you be when disaster strikes?
documents.overview: Sneaking out. Hooking up. Melting down. The cast and crew of a blockbuster action franchise attempt to shoot a sequel while quarantining at a posh hotel.
documents.plot: Sneaking out. Hooking up. Melting down. The cast and crew of a blockbuster action franchise attempt to shoot a sequel while quarantining at a posh hotel.

documents.title: Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie
documents.original_title: Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie
documents.tagline: We'll always rise to the challenge!
documents.overview: When a mysterious stranger arrives from the future with a dire warning, Leo is forced to rise and lead his brothers, Raph, Donnie, and Mikey in a fight to save the world from a terrifying alien species.
documents.plot:
Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie is a 2022 animated action-comedy film produced by Nickelodeon Movies. The movie serves as a reboot of the TMNT franchise and offers a fresh take on the classic characters.

The story begins with four brothers, Leonardo (voiced by Brady Noon), Donatello (voiced by Omar Miller), Michelangelo (voiced by Kyle Mooney), and Raphael (voiced by Bowen Yang), who are living in New York City. The brothers are mutated turtles from the sewers of New York, trained in the art of ninjutsu by their sensei Splinter (voiced by Josh Brener).

The movie starts with the Turtles trying to live a normal life on land, but they struggle to fit in and find their place in society. However, their lives are disrupted when Shredder (voiced by John Cena), the leader of the Foot Clan, returns from the dead and seeks revenge against the Turtles.

Shredder is aided by his loyal ally, Baxter Stockman (voiced by Ryan Kiera Armstrong), a mad scientist who creates an army of robotic ninjas to take down the Turtles. The Turtles must band together to stop Shredder's evil plans and save their city from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the Turtles face various challenges as they try to balance their ninja training with their everyday lives. They also encounter new allies, including April O'Neil (voiced by Maddie Capaldi), a young journalist who becomes entangled in the Turtles' adventures.

As the story unfolds, the Turtles discover that Shredder's plan is not just about revenge, but also about harnessing the power of the "Ninja Code," an ancient energy source that could grant him immense power. The Turtles must use their skills and teamwork to stop Shredder and his minions before it's too late.

The movie features plenty of action-packed sequences, humor, and heart, making it a fun and entertaining ride for fans of the TMNT franchise. The animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the characters and world to life in a way that will appeal to both old and new fans.

In the end, the Turtles successfully defeat Shredder and his robotic ninjas, saving their city from destruction. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about teamwork, friendship, and being true to themselves. The movie concludes with the Turtles returning to their sewers, ready to face whatever adventures come their way next.

Overall, Rise of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Movie is a fun and action-packed adventure that offers a fresh take on the classic TMNT characters. With its vibrant animation, humor, and heart, it's a must-see for fans of the franchise and anyone looking for a fun animated movie experience.

documents.title: Swan Song
documents.tagline: A thought-provoking exploration of love, loss, and sacrifice.
documents.overview: In the near future, Cameron Turner is diagnosed with a terminal illness. Presented with an experimental solution to shield his wife and son from grief, he grapples with altering their fate.
documents.plot: In the near future, Cameron Turner is diagnosed with a terminal illness. Presented with an experimental solution to shield his wife and son from grief, he grapples with altering their fate in this thought-provoking exploration of love, loss, and sacrifice.

documents.title: Black Friday
documents.tagline: They have no idea what tonight has in-store.
documents.overview: A group of toy store employees must protect each other from a horde of parasite infected shoppers.
documents.plot:
Black Friday is a 2021 American horror comedy directed by Casey Tebo from a screenplay by Andy Greskoviak. Devon Sawa, Ivana Baquero, Ryan Lee, Stephen Peck and Michael Jai White star alongside Bruce Campbell, who also served as a producer. The film satirises the retail frenzy of the post-Thanksgiving shopping day by turning a toy store's doorbuster sale into a creature feature.

The story begins when a parasitic organism attacks an employee preparing a big-box store for its Black Friday sale, turning him into a monster. Elsewhere, divorced father Ken Bates drops his daughters off for Thanksgiving dinner with their mother and her new husband because he has to work the overnight shift at the We Love Toys store. He picks up his timid co-worker Chris and joins colleagues including Marnie, Brian, Archie and Ruth under the store's officious manager Jonathan Wexler, while impatient crowds gather outside.

When the doors open and the shoppers pour in, the parasite is already spreading among them, and the customers turn violent as they mutate into murderous creatures. The staff find themselves fighting for their lives. In the store's Santa's Village display, Marnie discovers that the transformed shoppers are being absorbed into a growing organic sac. A possessed police officer crashes a patrol car through the front window, killing Ruth, and Archie is killed after rescuing Chris. The survivors barricade themselves in the stockroom, where shared slices of turkey give way to bitter arguments about their disappointing lives and Marnie's frustration with Ken over their non-romance.

After a mutant breaks in, Ken is bitten and stays behind, believing himself infected, while the others try to escape. The building catches fire as the sac grows into a gigantic monster filling the store. Jonathan sacrifices himself to let the others get away, and Brian confesses that it was he, not a creature, who bit Ken before he too is killed by the giant monster. Ken rejoins Chris and Marnie outside, and together they trick the creature into swallowing a forklift, causing it to collapse into the flames. As the three drive off, more enormous monsters can be seen rising from other stores.

Screen Media Films released the film theatrically in November 2021. It received mixed reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 65% approval from 17 critics, while RogerEbert.com's Brian Tallerico called it an easy, forgettable B-movie watch.

documents.title: A Taste of Hunger
documents.overview: Maggie and Carsten love each other, they have two wonderful children and run their own gourmet restaurant; Malus. They want it all. And they have it all. Almost. They are missing the coveted Michelin Star. It has been their dream, on which they gambled everything to win. One day Carsten receives a letter saying that his wife loves somebody else. But who sent the letter and why? In their continuous passion and pursuit for the ultimate recognition, they forget that the meals of life are best enjoyed together.
documents.plot:
A Taste of Hunger (Danish: Smagen af sult) is a 2021 Danish drama directed by Christoffer Boe, who wrote it with Tobias Lindholm, co-writer of Another Round and The Hunt. Produced by Zentropa with Swedish partners, it stars Nikolaj Coster-Waldau as the chef Carsten and Katrine Greis-Rosenthal as his wife and business partner Maggie, with Charlie Gustafsson as Frederik, Dag Malmberg as Stellan, Nicolas Bro as Torben, and Flora Augusta and August Christian Høyer-Kruse-Vinkel as Chloe and August. The film opens with the epigraph "If you ask me what I want, I'll tell you I want everything."

Carsten and Maggie love each other, have two children and run Malus, their ambitious gourmet restaurant in Copenhagen. They have gambled everything on one dream: a Michelin star. The story moves back and forth in time across chapters named after the elements of cooking, such as Sweet, Sour, Salt, Fat and Heat. The first flashback shows how they met, when Carsten was catering a party and Maggie, a guest, wandered into his kitchen; their attraction was immediate. Over the years the restaurant consumes their lives. Carsten's single-minded pursuit of perfection breeds frightening outbursts when anything goes wrong, and Maggie, whose eye for presentation and atmosphere shapes Malus, comes to look outside the marriage for what she lacks.

In the present, on a night when the couple are about to steal a private moment, a solo diner arrives whom they are certain is the anonymous Michelin inspector they have been waiting for. Their signature dish goes wrong, and convinced that the restaurant, and with it everything they own, will fail without the star, Maggie races into the night to track down the stranger and persuade him to give them another chance. She has a second reason to panic: she has intercepted a letter addressed to Carsten saying that his wife loves somebody else. As she searches Copenhagen for the diner and for the author of the message, further flashbacks reveal the origins of her affair, which leads to a blackmail scheme, while a subplot involves one of their children going missing.

Nordisk Film released the film in Danish cinemas in June 2021, and Magnolia Pictures distributed it in the United States in January 2022. Critics admired the lead performances and the film's mouthwatering food and look at the restaurant world's dark side, but RogerEbert.com and Variety felt its chapter structure and later melodrama were overcooked and less satisfying than its opening.

documents.title: See How They Run
documents.tagline: The greatest murder ever staged.
documents.overview: In the West End of 1950s London, plans for a movie version of a smash-hit play come to an abrupt halt after a pivotal member of the crew is murdered. When world-weary Inspector Stoppard and eager rookie Constable Stalker take on the case, the two find themselves thrown into a puzzling whodunit within the glamorously sordid theater underground, investigating the mysterious homicide at their own peril.
documents.plot:
See How They Run is a 2022 British comedy film directed by Sam Bain and Chris Morris, written by Sam Bain and Chris Morris, and produced by DJ Films. The movie stars Sam Rockwell, Saoirse Ronan, Adrien Brody, and David Tennant.

The story revolves around the murder of a wealthy businessman, Richard Harrow (played by Adrien Brody), who is found dead in his mansion with no signs of forced entry or struggle. Detective Toby Wilson (played by Sam Rockwell) is tasked with solving the case, but he's not exactly the most competent detective.

As the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that everyone at the party where Harrow was killed had a motive for the murder. The suspects include Harrow's wife, Catherine (played by Saoirse Ronan), who stands to gain a large inheritance; Harrow's business partner, James (played by David Tennant); and Harrow's personal assistant, Thomas (played by Jack Lowden).

As Detective Wilson interviews the suspects, he discovers that each of them had a secret relationship with Harrow at some point. The web of deceit becomes increasingly complex as Wilson tries to untangle the truth from the lies.

Throughout the investigation, Wilson's own life is revealed through flashbacks, showing his troubled past and his struggles with addiction. His partner, Detective Sophie Hopkins (played by Phoebe Waller-Bridge), provides a voice of reason and support, but even she seems to be hiding secrets.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Harrow was not as innocent as he seemed. He had many secrets and was involved in some shady dealings. The suspects' motives for the murder become increasingly complex, and Wilson must use all his wits to uncover the truth.

In the end, Detective Wilson discovers that the killer is none other than Catherine, who had been planning her revenge against Harrow for years. However, just as she's about to be arrested, it's revealed that she was actually working with James, who had been manipulating her all along.

The movie ends with Detective Wilson and Sophie Hopkins finally solving the case, but not before they've both been shaken by the revelations about Harrow's life and the secrets he kept. The film is a witty and clever comedy of errors, full of twists and turns that keep the viewer guessing until the very end.

Overall, See How They Run is a hilarious and engaging mystery that keeps you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. With its talented cast, witty script, and clever plot twists, it's a must-see for fans of comedy and mystery alike.

documents.title: Prey
documents.tagline: They hunt to live. It lives to hunt.
documents.overview: When danger threatens her camp, the fierce and highly skilled Comanche warrior Naru sets out to protect her people. But the prey she stalks turns out to be a highly evolved alien predator with a technically advanced arsenal.
documents.plot:
Prey is a 2022 American science fiction action film directed by Dan Trachtenberg and produced by 20th Century Studios. The movie takes place in 1751, during the Comanche Native American tribe's time of great prosperity.

The story follows Naru (played by Amber Midthunder), a young Comanche warrior who is trained by her father, Captain Takoda (played by Wes Studi). Naru is an exceptional hunter and warrior, but she struggles to live up to her family's expectations. She is also haunted by a traumatic event from her past.

When a group of European colonizers arrives in the area, tensions rise between the Comanche and the outsiders. The Comanche are skilled hunters and warriors, but they lack the technology and firepower that the Europeans possess. As the conflict escalates, Naru finds herself at the forefront of the battle to protect her tribe's land and way of life.

As the story unfolds, Naru discovers that she has a unique connection to the Yautja (also known as the "Predators"), an alien species that have been hunting humans for sport. The Yautja are drawn to Naru's strength and ferocity, and they begin to hunt her as part of their ritualistic games.

Throughout the film, Naru must confront her own identity and purpose, as well as the threat posed by the Yautja. She is aided in her fight by her tribe and a small group of allies, including a mysterious figure known only as "Wolf" (played by Dakota Johnson).

Prey is a thrilling and visually stunning film that explores themes of colonialism, identity, and the clash between cultures. The movie features impressive action sequences and a strong performance from Amber Midthunder, who brings depth and nuance to her portrayal of Naru.

Overall, Prey is a gripping and entertaining sci-fi action film that offers something new and exciting for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Parallel Mothers
