documents.overview: Two unmarried women who have become pregnant by accident and are about to give birth meet in a hospital room: Janis, middle-aged, unrepentant and happy; Ana, a teenager, remorseful and frightened.
documents.plot: Two unmarried women who have become pregnant by accident and are about to give birth meet in a hospital room: Janis, in her late-thirties, unrepentant and happy; Ana, a teenager, remorseful and frightened.

documents.title: American Siege
documents.tagline: No one walks away.
documents.overview: An ex-NYPD officer-turned-sheriff of a small rural Georgia town has to contend with a gang of thieves who have taken a wealthy doctor hostage.
documents.plot:
American Siege is a 2022 American action thriller film written and directed by Edward Drake from a story he developed with Corey Large. It stars Timothy V. Murphy, Bruce Willis, Rob Gough, Johann Urb, Anna Hindman, Johnny Messner, Cullen G. Chambers and Janet Jones, with Trevor Gretzky in a supporting role. Shot on a reported budget of $10 million between November and December 2020, with locations including Fitzgerald, Georgia, Bellingham, Washington, and Victoria, British Columbia, it was released in theatres and on demand in the United States by Shout! Studios on 7 January 2022.

In a small, backwater Georgia town controlled by the wealthy and powerful businessman Charles Rutledge (Murphy), teenager Brigit Baker (Sarah May Sommers) disappeared ten years earlier. Her boyfriend Roy Lambert (Gough), who was sent to prison for punching Rutledge, has spent the decade behind bars and now wants the truth. Soon after his release he teams up with Brigit's sister Grace (Hindman) and Toby Baker (Urb), and the heavily armed trio storm the house of the local pharmacist, Dr. John Keats (Chambers), and take him hostage, believing that he was the last person to see Brigit and knows what happened to her. A bank-grade security door on his basement suggests he is hiding something. Sheriff Ben Watts (Willis), a burnt-out former NYPD officer, heavy drinker and corrupt lawman on Rutledge's payroll, heads to the scene with his deputy Kyle Rutledge (Gretzky), Charles's son. As the siege drags on, Watts begins to suspect that Rutledge is tied to Brigit's disappearance and is hiding a larger conspiracy, while Rutledge loses patience and sends his private militia, led by the sinister Silas (Messner), to deal with the situation, leading to a long armed standoff outside the pharmacist's house.

American Siege was panned by critics; on Rotten Tomatoes only 8% of 13 critics' reviews were positive. Cath Clarke of The Guardian found it tiresome and oddly dull, criticising Willis's wooden, lethargic performance while allowing that its missing-girl story had an interesting twist and that Murphy brought icy menace. Jeffrey M. Anderson of Combustible Celluloid gave it two stars out of four, calling it riddled with bad ideas and dialogue but enlivened by the hostage-takers, especially Hindman's spitfire Grace. Willis's performance was among those cited for a Golden Raspberry category later rescinded after he retired because of aphasia.

documents.title: Born a Champion
documents.tagline: Once in a lifetime, opportunity knocks twice.
documents.overview: After a blood- soaked jujitsu match in Dubai, fighting legend Mickey Kelley falls to superstar Blaine. But years later, an online video proves that Blaine cheated, and the world demands a rematch. Can the aging underdog get back into shape in time to vanquish his foe, get revenge, and claim his prize?
documents.plot:
Born a Champion is a 2021 American martial arts drama directed by Alex Ranarivelo, who co-wrote the screenplay with star Sean Patrick Flanery. Flanery plays Mickey Kelley, a Gulf War veteran and one of the first American black belts in Brazilian jiu-jitsu, with Katrina Bowden, Dennis Quaid, Maurice Compte, Costas Mandylor and Reno Wilson in supporting roles. Mixed martial artist Edson Barboza appears as Mickey's rival, with appearances by Renzo Gracie.

The story is framed as a documentary narrated by Mickey's loyal friend Rosco, nicknamed "Taco," who first met him when Mickey subdued a group of men harassing him without throwing a punch. In the early 1990s, the former Marine travels to Dubai to teach jiu-jitsu to the family of a sheikh. On the flight he meets Layla, a young woman who has accepted modeling work from a wealthy businessman named Dimitris. When Mickey discovers that the job is a front for exploitation, he rescues her and sends her home, and back in America the two fall in love, marry and start a family.

With a baby on the way and money tight, Mickey accepts an offer to compete in a small unsanctioned fighting tournament in Dubai, despite Layla's misgivings. He easily wins his early bouts, but in his third fight, against the rising star Marco Blaine, who is backed by Dimitris, he extends his hand in a gesture of respect and is ambushed with a flying knee. Badly beaten, Mickey is left with a detached retina and a damaged eye socket and is told he may never be medically cleared to fight again. Years later, he lives in obscurity, working as a bouncer and custodian and teaching occasional private lessons, while Blaine has become a celebrated champion under the promoter Mason, played by Quaid. When footage of the original fight surfaces online and goes viral, proving that Blaine cheated, public demand grows for a rematch. Seeing a chance to secure his son's future and reclaim his honor, and spurred on after a family tragedy, Mickey trains relentlessly for one last fight, whatever the risks to his health.

The film, originally titled Mickey Kelley, was announced in July 2019 and shot in Petaluma, California, that summer. Flanery, a longtime jiu-jitsu practitioner who also produced, described it in the credits as a love letter to the art. It received a limited theatrical and video-on-demand release on January 22, 2021, followed by Blu-ray and DVD days later. Reviewers found it earnest and authentic in its martial arts detail but predictable.

documents.title: Blaze
documents.tagline: I know what I saw.
documents.overview: After a young girl witnesses a violent crime, she summons an imaginary dragon to help process her anger and protect her on her journey into womanhood.
documents.plot:
Blaze is a 2022 Australian drama co-written and directed by the artist Del Kathryn Barton in her feature film debut and produced by Causeway Films. Julia Savage stars as Blaze, a twelve-year-old girl, with Simon Baker as her father Luke, Yael Stone, Josh Lawson, Remy Hii and John Waters. The film premiered in the International Narrative Competition at the 2022 Tribeca Festival in New York and was released in Australian cinemas in August 2022 and in the United States in January 2023.

Blaze is a sensitive, imaginative girl who lives with her loving but somewhat uncertain single father, Luke. Walking home one day, she becomes the sole witness to the brutal sexual assault of a young woman, Hannah, who is killed in the attack. The experience leaves Blaze deeply traumatized; she withdraws into near silence, and her father struggles to understand how to help her.

To cope with what she has seen, Blaze retreats into a vivid inner world, populated by a glittering, life-size dragon named Zephy and filled with color, creatures and fantastical imagery. As the police build their case, they need Blaze's testimony to secure a conviction, and she is drawn into the legal process, facing interviews and the prospect of giving evidence in court, which the film portrays as poorly equipped to deal with a child's trauma. Meanwhile, Blaze's fantasies, rendered through Barton's own artwork, stop-motion animation, puppetry and elaborate design, swing between comfort and terror, while she also confronts the confusing changes of adolescence and her awakening anger at the violence men inflict on women. Gradually, through her imagination and her bond with her father, Blaze begins to find her voice and a measure of agency and healing.

Blaze received critical acclaim, with particular praise for Savage's performance and Barton's bold visual style. Metacritic gave it a score of 85, indicating universal acclaim, and it held an 88 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Peter Debruge of Variety called it the debut of a distinctive new voice despite a certain woodenness in its narrative, while critics in The Guardian and Time Out described it as breathtaking.

documents.title: Redemption Day
documents.tagline: Taking his wife was their last mistake.
documents.overview: When his wife is kidnapped by terrorists for ransom, veteran war hero Brad Paxton races against the clock to rescue her in a daring and deadly operation that pits him against powerful and dark forces.
documents.plot:
Redemption Day is a 2021 American action thriller directed and co-written by Hicham Hajji. It stars Gary Dourdan as U.S. Marine captain Brad Paxton and Serinda Swan as his wife Kate, with Andy García as Ambassador Williams, Brice Bexter as Younes Laalej, Martin Donovan as Tom Fitzgerald, Robert Knepper as an oil lobbyist, Ernie Hudson and Samy Naceri as the terrorist leader Jaafar El Hadi. Saban Films distributed it.

Brad, still haunted by his combat tour in Syria, lives in New York with Kate, an archaeologist, and their daughter. Kate travels to Morocco on an expedition with French-Algerian archaeologist Jean Rashidi to search for an ancient city buried beneath the desert. When the team accidentally crosses the border into Algeria, militants kidnap Kate, Jean and their Moroccan guide, Amir Jadid, who is later released. The kidnappers, led by El Hadi, a fugitive wanted by Interpol, demand a $10 million ransom and decide to execute Kate if it is not paid by the evening prayer.

Brad flies to Rabat, where he teams up with Younes, a Moroccan government liaison and former soldier who once served alongside him. Ambassador Williams reluctantly backs their intelligence-gathering effort despite Fitzgerald's objections. With help from Moroccan counterterrorism officials, they trace El Hadi to a compound in Abadla and drive there. Williams persuades the president to send Navy SEALs as support. At night, Brad and Younes kill most of the guards, and Brad finds and hides Kate, but Jean is executed when the French government fails to pay. El Hadi forces Younes to arrange the transfer of the ransom to an offshore account and tries to flee, but the arriving SEALs kill him. Brad and Younes blow up the compound and are left for dead as the SEALs fly Kate out. The next day, Brad and Kate reunite at the Moroccan border. Jadid, rewarded by Fitzgerald with American citizenship, is murdered on his way out. This reveals that Fitzgerald is working for an oil company that also funds the terrorist networks. Younes secretly watches Fitzgerald and his associates and sends Brad evidence of their corruption.

The film was released in January 2021 and received largely negative reviews. Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 14% approval rating and Metacritic a score of 22 out of 100. In Variety, Joe Leydon wrote that if the film were any more generic, it would open with a bar code instead of credits.

documents.title: Black as Night
documents.tagline: Find your own way to slay.
documents.overview: A teenage girl with self-esteem issues finds confidence in the most unlikely way, by spending her summer battling vampires that prey on New Orleans' disenfranchised with the help of her best friend, the boy she's always pined for, and a peculiar rich girl.
documents.plot: A teenage girl with self-esteem issues finds confidence in the most unlikely way, by spending her summer battling vampires that prey on New Orleans' disenfranchised with the help of her best friend, the boy she's always pined for, and a peculiar rich girl.

documents.title: Moonshot
documents.tagline: Find the space to connect.
documents.overview: In a future where Mars is terraformed and colonized by the best humanity has to offer, two very different college students wind up joining forces and sneak onboard a space shuttle to the red planet in order to be united with their significant others.
documents.plot:
Moonshot is a 2022 American science fiction romantic comedy directed by Christopher Winterbauer, in his feature debut, and written by Max Taxe. Cole Sprouse and Lana Condor star as two college students on a voyage to Mars, with Mason Gooding, Emily Rudd, Michelle Buteau, Cameron Esposito and Zach Braff as a tech billionaire. The film premiered on HBO Max on March 31, 2022, and was removed from the service a few months later.

In 2049, Walt is a barista on a college campus who has applied thirty-seven times, without success, to the Kovi Industries programme that sends students to live on Mars. At a party he meets Sophie, a serious, driven student whose boyfriend Calvin is already on Mars, and falls for Ginny, a girl who leaves for the planet the next morning. A few weeks later Sophie arrives at his café in tears because Calvin has decided to extend his stay, and Walt persuades her to book a seat on the next shuttle, then tricks her into helping him stow away, passing himself off as Calvin.

During the long voyage the two grow close. Walt learns more about the real Calvin, and Sophie begins to see that her boyfriend may have placed her second to his dream of terraforming Mars. Forced to deliver a talk on terraforming, a subject he knows nothing about, Walt instead speaks so movingly about love that two passengers decide to marry, and Sophie is touched. As they approach Mars, however, she tells him that she will stay with Calvin and will help him no further, and Walt calls her a coward.

On arrival Sophie reunites with Calvin and Walt is arrested. Ginny tells him that she has moved on. The company's founder, Leon Kovi, reveals that the staff knew about Walt from the shuttle's cameras all along, and that he has leaked the footage, which has gone viral on Earth. To avoid a lawsuit, Walt accepts a contract to stay on Mars as the face of the company, but finds life as a promotional celebrity hollow. Sophie, realising she and Calvin have grown apart, ends the relationship and leaves for Earth, and Walt follows her onto the returning shuttle, where they reunite and kiss.

Critics found it pleasant but ordinary, giving it 64% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and praising Condor's performance.

documents.title: Asakusa Kid
documents.tagline: I'm a comedian, you fool!
documents.overview: In 1965, Takeshi Kitano drops out of a university and enters the Asakusa France Za, which is a performance theater. He becomes an apprentice to Senzaburo Fukami, who is a legendary entertainer. Senzaburo Fukami demands that Takeshi Kitano keep the mindset of an entertainer, not only on stage, but also in his daily life. Takeshi Kitano cultivates his dream of becoming an entertainer with other apprentices. Due to the popularity of TV, people attend the theater less and less, but Takeshi Kitano spends his youthful days with Senzaburo Fukami and other apprentices who are full of talent and unique personalities.
documents.plot:
Asakusa Kid is a 2021 Japanese biographical drama written and directed by Gekidan Hitori for Netflix, adapted from "Beat" Takeshi Kitano's 1988 memoir about his apprenticeship to the comedian Senzaburo Fukami, which had already been filmed in 2002 by Makoto Shinozaki. Produced by Django Film and Nikkatsu, it stars Yuya Yagira as Kitano and Yo Oizumi as Fukami, with Mugi Kadowaki as Chiharu, Nobuyuki Tsuchiya as Kitano's comic partner Kiyoshi, Honami Suzuki as Fukami's wife Mari, Hiroyuki Onoue and Morio Kazama. The film runs 123 minutes.

After opening with an older Kitano about to step on stage, the film flashes back to the early 1970s. Kitano, a university dropout, works as an elevator boy and general dogsbody at the France-za, a burlesque theater in Tokyo's Asakusa district whose shrinking audience cares more about the strippers than the comedians performing skits between their routines. The venue is run by Fukami, a famous old-school vaudevillian known for his dapper style and his contempt for the new manzai comedy duos making their names on television. Fukami at first gives the eager newcomer a hard time, then agrees to train him in comedy and tap dance, insisting that he keep an entertainer's mindset not only on stage but in everyday life. Kitano befriends Chiharu, a straight-talking stripper whose dreams of a singing career are behind her, and spends his youth among other gifted, eccentric apprentices as television draws audiences away from the theater. As Kitano's ambition outgrows the failing France-za, he leaves to form the manzai duo Two Beat with Kiyoshi and rises to stardom, while Fukami and his loyal wife Mari face growing misfortune. The film ends with the older Kitano walking through the neighborhood and theater where he learned his craft.

Asakusa Kid was released on Netflix on 9 December 2021. In Variety, Richard Kuipers described it as a safe, traditional and enjoyable biopic that offers little penetrating insight into Kitano but a respectful, touching portrait of Fukami, noting a slowish first half and praising its flights of fantasy, such as Fukami's tap routine and Chiharu's dream of being a torch singer. He called Yagira, a former best actor winner at Cannes, excellent in capturing Kitano's timing and tics, and Oizumi funny and dignified. Other critics similarly praised the leads while finding it conventional and more nostalgic than revealing.

documents.title: A Classic Horror Story
documents.overview: Five people travelling by camper crash into a tree. When they recover, the road they were driving on has been replaced by an impenetrable forest and a wooden house.
documents.plot:
A Classic Horror Story is a 2021 Italian horror film directed by Roberto De Feo and Paolo Strippoli, who wrote it with Lucio Besana, David Bellini and Milo Tissone. It stars Matilda Lutz, Francesco Russo, Peppino Mazzotta, Will Merrick and Yuliia Sobol. Netflix released the film worldwide on 14 July 2021.

Elisa, a young woman uncertain about her decision to end a pregnancy, arranges a ride-share to her family's home in Calabria, where she is scheduled to have an abortion. She joins a camper van driven by Fabrizio, a film-obsessed travel blogger, along with Riccardo, a doctor, and Sofia and Mark, an outgoing couple. When Elisa's morning sickness forces them to pull over, Mark takes the wheel. That night, drinking as he drives, he swerves to avoid a dead animal in the road and crashes into a tree.

When Elisa wakes the next morning, the others are treating Mark's broken leg, and the group realizes that the road has vanished: they are now in a clearing surrounded by dense forest, with no explanation of how they got there. In the clearing stands a rustic wooden house. Exploring nearby, Fabrizio and Riccardo find a grotesque altar with three crucified, pig-headed figures, while inside the house Elisa discovers a mural depicting three figures from local legend, Osso, Mastrosso and Carcagnosso, venerated by a secret society that offers human sacrifices in exchange for prosperity. That night, screams from the house draw most of the group inside, where they find a girl imprisoned in a cocoon of straw, her tongue cut out. As masked figures emerge from the woods and the travelers are subjected to brutal rituals one by one, Elisa fights to survive and uncovers a twist that reframes everything that has happened, with the film commenting on horror conventions and Italian society.

The film received mixed reviews from critics, with a 58 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on twelve reviews. Reviewers praised its visual style and atmosphere, which draw openly on folk horror and on familiar genre classics, while some found its self-aware ending divisive. In July 2021, The New York Times included it among its top five horror films to stream.

documents.title: Motherly
documents.overview: Kate and her daughter Beth live alone in an isolated farmhouse in the woods, but when Kate slowly begins to suspect that something sinister is happening, her motherly instincts are put to the test.
documents.plot:
Motherly is a 2021 Canadian psychological horror thriller directed by Craig David Wallace. Lora Burke stars as Kate, a woman living in an isolated rural house with her young daughter Beth, played by Tessa Kozma, after her husband was imprisoned for the death of a little girl. The cast also includes Kristen MacCulloch and Nick Smyth as the dead girl's parents, and Colin Paradine as a local police officer.

Kate lives in seclusion with nine-year-old Beth, and a police officer named Hal stops by from time to time to check on them. Beth hopes her father Brad will come home for her ninth birthday, unaware of the full truth: two years earlier Brad was convicted of murdering Beth's young friend Courtenay, and he has since taken his own life in prison. One evening, Courtenay's parents, Lewis and Mary, break into the house. They have become convinced that the evidence against Brad never made sense and that Kate was the real killer, and it emerges that Brad and Mary had been having an affair.

The intruders hold Kate and Beth captive while they try to extract a confession, and the night spirals into violence. When Hal arrives for one of his checks, he finds Lewis on the verge of killing Kate as she admits to having framed Brad, and he shoots Lewis, only for Kate to kill Hal because he has now learned the truth. Mary overpowers Kate and tries to flee with Beth, but Kate escapes and wounds her, and Mary is finally killed by Beth with a pitchfork. In the film's final twist, Beth is revealed to be the true killer of Courtenay, a disturbed child whose crime Kate had concealed by setting up her husband. Declaring that she is avenging her father's death, Beth stabs her mother to death and walks away from the house. As the credits roll, a passing stranger notices the blood on her clothes and asks if she needs help, and Beth faintly smiles.

The film premiered at the London FrightFest Film Festival on August 26, 2021, screened at several other Canadian and international festivals and was released on video on demand by Entertainment Squad on November 16, 2021. It grossed a little over $117,000 outside North America. Critical response was positive, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting an 86% approval rating from seven reviews. Spencer Creaghan's music earned a nomination for Best Original Score at the 10th Canadian Screen Awards in 2022.

documents.title: A California Christmas
documents.overview: With his carefree lifestyle on the line, a wealthy charmer poses as a ranch hand to get a hardworking farmer to sell her family’s land before Christmas.
documents.plot:
A California Christmas is a heartwarming holiday film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and the power of love and forgiveness. The movie follows the story of a woman who returns to her hometown in California after a painful past experience, only to find herself reuniting with an old flame and confronting the mistakes of her past.

At its core, A California Christmas is a film about second chances and the possibility of redemption. It delves into the theme of forgiveness, both towards oneself and others, and how it can lead to healing and personal growth. The movie also touches on the idea of finding one's true identity and purpose in life, as the protagonist navigates her feelings and tries to rediscover herself.

The film also explores the complexities of family relationships, particularly the tension between parents and children, and the difficulties of reconciling past conflicts. Through its portrayal of these themes, A California Christmas offers a nuanced and relatable exploration of the human experience during the holiday season.

Overall, A California Christmas is a feel-good movie that celebrates the magic of love, forgiveness, and new beginnings, set against the picturesque backdrop of California's festive atmosphere.

documents.title: Dogtanian and the Three Muskehounds
documents.tagline: One for all and all for one!
documents.overview: France, 17th century, under the reign of Louis XIII. Dogtanian is an impetuous and innocent peasant from Gascony, as well as a skilled swordsman, who travels to Paris with the purpose of making his dream come true: to join the Corps of Muskehounds of the Royal Guard.
documents.plot:
Dogtanian and the Three Muskehounds (Spanish: D'Artacán y los tres mosqueperros), released in North America as The Dog Knight, is a 2021 Spanish-Indian animated adventure comedy film directed by Toni García and written by Doug Langdale. It is based on the 1981 Spanish-Japanese television series of the same name, itself adapted from Alexandre Dumas's 1844 novel about d'Artagnan and the Three Musketeers, and was produced by Apolo Films, the cinema studio of BRB Internacional, together with the Indian company Cosmos Maya. The original Spanish voice cast includes Miguel Ángel Pérez as Dogtanian, Ana Esther Alborg as Juliette, Ana María Marí as Milady de Winter, Luis Bajo as Count Rochefort and Carlos Kaniowsky as Treville.

Dogtanian, a young and eager swordsman, travels to Paris dreaming of joining the legendary Muskehounds. At their headquarters, Monsieur de Treville tells him that his father was framed by Cardinal Richelieu and judges him unfit to become a Muskehound. Shortly afterwards Dogtanian accidentally runs into each of the three Muskehounds in turn and ends up challenged to duels with all of them, but when the Cardinal's guards interrupt and a fight breaks out, his courage wins the three over. One night he rescues Juliette, a young lady he has met, from the Cardinal's men, and she reveals that Richelieu is plotting to start a war between France and England so that he can seize power across Europe. Queen Anne of Austria plans to send a letter to the King of England to secure peace, together with a diamond necklace given to her by King Louis, and if the Cardinal's agents steal the necklace, war could follow. Remembering a conversation he overheard between Richelieu's spy, Count Rochefort, and the cunning Milady de Winter, Dogtanian joins the Muskehounds in a race to Calais to stop Milady before she can escape across the Channel. Along the way he enlists the help of a pirate, Captain Bloodhound, and must prove his skill with the sword while also seeking the truth about the plot that disgraced his father.

On Rotten Tomatoes, four of seven critics' reviews of the film are positive. A television series continuing the story after the events of the film, titled Dogtanian, The Hero, was reported to be in development, though no further news about it has emerged.

documents.title: My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission
documents.original_title: 僕のヒーローアカデミア THE MOVIE ワールド ヒーローズ ミッション
documents.tagline: Their fight is our future.
documents.overview: A mysterious group called Humarize strongly believes in the Quirk Singularity Doomsday theory which states that when quirks get mixed further in with future generations, that power will bring forth the end of humanity. In order to save everyone, the Pro-Heroes around the world ask UA Academy heroes-in-training to assist them and form a world-class selected hero team. It’s up to the heroes to save the world and the future of heroes in what is the most dangerous crisis to take place yet in My Hero Academia.
documents.plot:
My Hero Academia: World Heroes' Mission is a 2021 Japanese animated superhero film based on an original story featuring the characters of Kōhei Horikoshi's manga My Hero Academia. Produced by Bones and distributed by Toho, the third film in the franchise was directed by Kenji Nagasaki from a script by Yōsuke Kuroda and features the voices of Daiki Yamashita as Izuku Midoriya, Nobuhiko Okamoto as Katsuki Bakugo and Yuki Kaji as Shoto Todoroki.

In a world where most people are born with superpowers called Quirks, a doomsday cult called Humarise believes that Quirks will eventually become so powerful that they will destroy humanity. Led by Flect Turn, the cult plants bombs around the world filled with Trigger gas, which drives the Quirks of anyone exposed out of control until they die, intending to wipe out all Quirk users. After the first bomb is detonated, the World Heroes Association dispatches professional heroes and students from U.A. High School to locations around the globe in an attempt to stop the attacks.

Izuku, Bakugo and Todoroki are sent with their mentor Endeavor to Otheon, the country believed to house Humarise's headquarters. While pursuing a jewel thief, Izuku encounters Rody Soul, a street-smart young courier struggling to support his younger siblings. When Rody accidentally picks up a briefcase containing important information stolen from Humarise, Izuku is framed for mass murder by the corrupt local police, who are secretly working for the cult. Forced to go on the run with Rody, Izuku must learn to trust the cynical boy and protect him from the cult's assassins, while Bakugo and Todoroki lead the effort to stop Flect Turn's plan before the remaining bombs can be detonated.

The film expands the series' world beyond Japan and explores themes of trust, prejudice and responsibility, with Rody's relationship with Izuku at its emotional center.

World Heroes' Mission was released in Japan on August 6, 2021, and in the United States and Canada by Funimation on October 29, 2021. It grossed about 47 million dollars worldwide and was one of the highest-grossing domestic films of the year in Japan. It received generally positive reviews, with 87 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Both Sides of the Blade
documents.overview: Jean and Sara have been living together for 10 years. When they first met, Sara was living with François, Jean’s best friend and an admirer from back when he played rugby. Jean and Sara love each other. One day, Sara sees François in the street. He does not notice her, but she is overtaken by the sensation that her life could suddenly change. François gets back in touch with Jean. For the first time in years. He suggests they start working together again. From here on, things spiral out of control.
documents.plot:
Both Sides of the Blade (Avec amour et acharnement, literally "With Love and Fury"), at first marketed in English as Fire, is a French romantic drama of 2022 directed by Claire Denis, who wrote the screenplay with Christine Angot, adapting Angot's 2018 novel Un tournant de la vie. Juliette Binoche stars as Sara, with Vincent Lindon as her partner Jean and Grégoire Colin as her former lover François. The supporting cast includes Bulle Ogier as Jean's mother Nelly and Issa Perica as his son Marcus.

The film opens with Sara and Jean on holiday, swimming in the sea and embracing. Back in wintry Paris, Sara presents a radio show. Jean, an ex-convict and onetime professional rugby player, has been an absent father to his mixed-race teenage son Marcus, who is being raised by Jean's mother Nelly in the suburb of Vitry. One day Sara catches sight of her estranged ex-boyfriend François in the street, and the encounter floods her with emotion. François, once a close friend of Jean's as well, is launching a sports agency to recruit young rugby players, and he contacts Jean to offer him work as a talent scout. His return to their lives threatens the relationship Sara and Jean have shared for ten years.

Made under COVID-19 restrictions, the film was shot in Paris, partly at the Maison de la Radio, the headquarters of Radio France, and wrapped in early February 2021. Denis said the lockdowns drew her and the actors closer while also leaving them exhausted, and the pandemic is present on screen: shooting in the Paris Métro, she found it impossible to pretend it did not exist, and characters wear masks in some scenes outside the apartment. The film also marked the acting debut of Hana Magimel, the daughter of Binoche and Benoît Magimel.

The English title comes from a song of the same name written for the film by Stuart A. Staples of Tindersticks and heard at its close. Denis publicly objected to the name Fire, and IFC Films adopted the new title in April 2022.

The film premiered in competition for the Golden Bear at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival on 12 February 2022, where Denis won the Silver Bear for Best Director. IFC Films gave it a limited American release on 8 July 2022, and Ad Vitam Distribution opened it in France on 31 August, where it opened eighth. It grossed about $1.8 million worldwide. Critics responded warmly, with Rotten Tomatoes' consensus crediting Denis and Binoche for a relationship drama that cuts deep.

documents.title: Army of One
documents.tagline: They left her for dead. Big mistake.
documents.overview: Out hiking, Special Forces Brenner Baker stumbles onto a Cartel's compound. Her husband's killed and she's left for dead. The Cartel made two mistakes, killed her husband and left her alive. They won't live to make another.
documents.plot:
Army of One is a 2020 American action thriller film directed by Stephen Durham from a screenplay he wrote with Mary Ann Barnes, Ellen Hollman and David Dittlinger. Produced by 2nd Nature Films, Popcorn and Soda Productions and Split Point Productions, it stars Hollman as a former special forces soldier seeking revenge, with Matt Passmore, Gary Kasper, Geraldine Singer, Kendra Carelli and Stephen Dunlevy in supporting roles. The film was released in the United States in December 2020 and runs about 87 minutes.

Brenner Baker (Hollman), a decorated Army Ranger, is happily married to Dillon (Passmore), a police detective who still bears the physical and psychological scars of a violent incident involving masked men. Hoping to escape the stress of their jobs, the couple take a road trip into the backwoods of Alabama. Along the way they are harassed by a belligerent local in a pickup truck, and when they run into him again at a diner they learn that he is Butch (Kasper), whose seemingly kindly mother, known as Mama (Singer), defuses the confrontation and lets them leave unharmed. Later, out hiking, the couple are caught in the rain and take shelter in an apparently empty, secluded cabin, only to discover a hidden store of drugs and guns belonging to Butch's family, a criminal clan tied to a cartel and involved in drug dealing and human trafficking. They are captured and interrogated, and both are shot, but the gang fails to check whether Brenner is dead before dumping her in an open grave. Wounded and grieving, she climbs out and uses her combat and survival skills to hunt down the family one by one, while also trying to free other prisoners they hold captive.

Reviews were mixed. Eoin of The Action Elite called the film a slick and effective action picture with a star-making turn from Hollman, who performed her own stunts, including a one-shot fight sequence reportedly rehearsed for only an hour and filmed in a single take; he found the villains so hateful that their comeuppance was satisfying, while conceding that the story was nothing new. Andrew Stover of Film Threat gave it 5 out of 10, writing that its rapid action sequences enliven an otherwise uneven and insipid revenge tale, that its bloody, hammy and clichéd antics fall short of the genre's best, and that Dillon's traumatic backstory is left unexplored.

documents.title: Finding You
documents.tagline: Trust the journey.
documents.overview: Finley, a talented aspiring violinist, meets Beckett, a famous young movie star, on the way to her college semester abroad program in a small coastal village in Ireland. An unexpected romance emerges as the heartthrob Beckett leads the uptight Finley on an adventurous reawakening, and she emboldens him to take charge of his future, until the pressures of his stardom get in the way.
documents.plot:
Finding You is a 2021 American coming-of-age romantic comedy written and directed by Brian Baugh, based on Jenny B. Jones's 2011 young adult novel There You'll Find Me. Rose Reid stars as an aspiring violinist and Jedidiah Goodacre as a film star, with Katherine McNamara, Tom Everett Scott and Vanessa Redgrave. Roadside Attractions released it in American cinemas on May 14, 2021.

After failing an audition for a New York music conservatory, violinist Finley Sinclair joins a study abroad programme in a small Irish village, the same programme her late brother Alex once attended. On the flight she is upgraded and falls asleep on the shoulder of Beckett Rush, the arrogant-seeming star of the Dawn of the Dragon fantasy franchise, who is heading to Ireland to shoot the next film. Finley stays with Alex's former host family, the Callaghans, whose daughter Emma is a devoted Beckett fan, and discovers that he is staying at their bed and breakfast too.

Nora Callaghan gives Finley Alex's notebook of sketches, and she resolves to find the place in the last, unfinished drawing: a broken Celtic cross in a churchyard, labelled with her name. Beckett, pressured by his manager father Montgomery to keep the studio happy so he can land a multi-film deal, makes a bargain with Finley: she will help him rehearse and he will help her search. For a class project, Finley must also spend time with Cathleen Sweeney, a cantankerous elderly woman rumoured to have married her sister Fiona's sweetheart for money.

In the village pub a fiddler, Seamus, teaches Finley to play with joy and freedom, and she and Beckett fall in love, keeping their romance secret from the press. But photographs of them kissing are leaked, embarrassing his co-star Taylor, with whom his father has staged a fake romance, and Montgomery pressures Beckett to sign the deal and end things with Finley. Meanwhile Cathleen reveals that she married the violent Mr. Sweeney in her sister's place to save her, but her letters to Fiona have always come back unopened.

Choosing to stay with the dying Cathleen rather than fly home for her audition, Finley sees Fiona arrive in time to reconcile. Beckett finds the cross from Alex's sketch, bearing a verse from Deuteronomy that Finley takes as a message from her brother. Beckett turns down the franchise deal to go to college, Finley wins her place at the conservatory, and the two are reunited in New York. Reviews were mixed, with 53% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Back to the Outback
documents.tagline: Dangerously cute and on the loose
documents.overview: Tired of being locked in a reptile house where humans gawk at them like they are monsters, a ragtag group of Australia’s deadliest creatures plot an escape from their zoo to the Outback, a place where they’ll fit in without being judged.
documents.plot:
Back to the Outback is a 2021 Australian animated adventure comedy film directed by Alex Spiller and produced by Weed Road Pictures, in association with Screen Australia and the Australian Film Institute. The movie follows the story of a group of orphaned koalas who embark on an epic journey through the Australian outback.

The film begins with a dramatic scene where a group of orphaned koalas are being transported to a wildlife sanctuary when their plane crashes, killing everyone on board except for four young koalas: Bubba, Boomer, Bluey, and Brenda. The four koalas find themselves stranded in the Australian outback, surrounded by venomous snakes, spiders, and other deadly creatures.

As they try to survive and find a way back home, the koalas meet a friendly and eccentric kangaroo named Kip, who becomes their guide and mentor. Kip teaches the koalas how to navigate the harsh desert environment, hunt for food, and avoid predators.

However, their journey is not without its challenges. The group soon discovers that they are being pursued by a ruthless and cunning dingo named Scorch, who seeks to capture them and sell them to a sinister wildlife collector. Along the way, the koalas also encounter other dangers, including treacherous terrain, raging rivers, and even a massive saltwater crocodile.

Despite these obstacles, the four koalas work together, using their unique skills and personalities to overcome each challenge. Bubba, the brave and fearless leader, takes charge of the group and keeps them safe. Boomer, the tech-savvy koala, uses his knowledge of technology to help the group navigate and find food. Bluey, the curious and adventurous koala, loves to explore and discover new things. And Brenda, the gentle and caring koala, looks out for her friends and keeps everyone's spirits high.

As they journey deeper into the outback, the koalas learn valuable lessons about teamwork, perseverance, and believing in themselves. They also develop a strong bond with Kip, who becomes like a surrogate father to them.

In the end, the group faces off against Scorch in an epic battle, using all their skills and cunning to outwit him and escape his clutches. With Kip's help, they finally reach the safety of a wildlife sanctuary, where they are reunited with other orphaned animals and begin a new life together.

Throughout the film, the animation is vibrant and colorful, bringing the Australian outback to life in stunning detail. The characters are well-developed and relatable, making it easy for audiences to become invested in their journey. The story is full of action, adventure, and heart, making Back to the Outback a fun and entertaining film for both children and adults.

Overall, Back to the Outback is a thrilling and inspiring animated adventure that celebrates the beauty and diversity of the Australian outback. With its lovable characters, exciting plot twists, and stunning animation, it's a must-see film for anyone who loves animals, adventure, or just a good story well-told.

documents.title: Cuando Sea Joven
documents.overview: 70-year-old Malena gets a second chance at life when she magically turns into her 22-year-old self. Now, posing as "Maria" to hide her true identity, she becomes the lead singer of her grandson's band and tries to recover her dream of singing, which she had to give up at some point.
documents.plot:
Cuando sea joven (English: When I'm Young) is a 2022 Mexican musical romantic comedy directed by Raúl Martínez and written by Juan Carlos Garzón and Angélica Gudiño. It is a remake of the 2014 South Korean hit Miss Granny, directed by Hwang Dong-hyuk, and stars Verónica Castro and Natasha Dupeyrón as the older and younger versions of the same woman. The cast also includes Michael Ronda, Eduardo Santamarina, Édgar Vivar, Manuel "Flaco" Ibáñez, Pierre Louis, Alejandra Barros and Maribel Fernández.

Malena is a sharp-tongued 70-year-old widow who lives with her son's family and spends her days bickering with those around her. Though she adores her grandson Víctor, a struggling musician, she begins to feel that she has become a burden to the people she loves. Then, in a moment of magic, she discovers that she has been transformed into her 22-year-old self.

Thrilled by her second chance at youth, Malena adopts the name María to hide her identity and sets out to enjoy the life she gave up decades ago, when she sacrificed her own ambitions to raise her son alone. She still dresses and talks like a grandmother, which leads to plenty of comic misunderstandings. Her powerful singing voice soon attracts attention, and she becomes the lead singer of Víctor's band, which suddenly begins to find success. As María's star rises, she must decide whether to keep her new life or return to her old one, especially when her family needs her and a crisis forces her to weigh her own dreams against her love for them.

Produced by 3Pas Studios, the company of Eugenio Derbez and Ben Odell, in association with LimeLight Productions, CJ ENM and The Lift, the film was distributed by Pantelion Films. It was released in Mexico on 15 September 2022 and in the United States on 23 September 2022. Reviews were positive. Avi Offer of NYC Movie Guru called it sweet, funny and tender, with the right balance of humor and heart, and CineMovie.tv described it as wholesome entertainment for the whole family. Common Sense Media gave it four stars out of five, observing that although body-swap and transformation stories have been told many times, this version avoids complete predictability.

documents.title: Tall Girl 2
documents.tagline: Growing up is a tall order.
documents.overview: After Jodi Kreyman gains popularity, her miscommunications start causing rifts with those around her and now she really needs to "stand tall".
documents.plot:
Tall Girl 2 is a 2022 American teen romantic comedy directed by Emily Ting and written by Sam Wolfson, a sequel to the 2019 film Tall Girl. Netflix commissioned Wolfson to write it in December 2020, with Ava Michelle returning as Jodi, and principal photography ran from April 12 to May 21, 2021, in New Orleans. The film was released on February 11, 2022.

Now newly popular, Jodi sets her sights on the spring musical and lands the lead role of Kim in Bye Bye Birdie, but the success unsettles her, bringing anxiety attacks and a nagging inner voice that feeds her doubts. Tommy is cast opposite her, and her boyfriend, Dunkleman, starts to feel sidelined. Those around her have struggles of their own: her sister, Harper, wants to prove she is more than a pageant contestant, and her friend Fareeda hopes her parents will back her ambition to design clothes. Kimmy, the bully Jodi beat for the part, sets out to make her fail, though Schnipper, still smitten with Jodi after their kiss, refuses to help, and Kimmy soon realizes Jodi's nerves are doing the work for her.

After Dunkleman tells Jodi she can skip their anniversary dinner to rehearse and then resents it when she does, the couple drift apart. Jodi kisses Tommy, and when she confesses, Dunkleman reacts angrily and they break up; he then makes a pact with Stella, Stig's sister, who is nursing her own heartbreak, never to see their exes again. At the cast's pre-show "burning ceremony", Jodi plans to burn the shoes Dunkleman gave her but changes her mind, and it is Kimmy who rescues them from the flames, beginning her change of heart. Jodi tells Tommy she still loves Dunkleman, blesses Fareeda's romance with Stig, and gets a pep talk from Dunkleman, whom Stella scolds for how he behaved. On opening night Kimmy turns down Jodi's offer to take her place and instead promises to feed her lines from the wings. The show succeeds, Jodi finally silences her inner critic, and Dunkleman, who had spent the night taking photos from the lighting booth, declares his love; they reconcile.

Ava Michelle stars as Jodi, with Griffin Gluck as Dunkleman, Sabrina Carpenter as Harper, Luke Eisner as Stig and Steve Zahn as Jodi's father, Richie. Reviews were mixed, with some critics considering it a modest improvement on the first film; Rotten Tomatoes recorded 71% approval from seven reviews, while Metacritic's score of 35 indicated generally unfavorable reviews.

documents.title: Death to 2020
documents.tagline: "What a shit show!"
documents.overview: 2020: A year so [insert adjective of choice here], even the creators of Black Mirror couldn't make it up… but that doesn't mean they don't have a little something to add. This comedy event that tells the story of the dreadful year that was — and perhaps still is? The documentary-style special weaves together some of the world's most (fictitious) renowned voices with real-life archival footage.

This comedy event that tells the story of the dreadful year that was — and perhaps still is? The documentary-style special weaves together some of the world's most (fictitious) renowned voices with real-life archival footage.

documents.title: Seoul Vibe
documents.tagline: Drive back to 1988.
documents.overview: Chasing speed, dreams and money, a team of drivers get involved in the slush fund investigation of a powerful figure during the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
documents.plot:
Seoul Vibe (Korean: 서울대작전, literally "Seoul Grand Operation") is a 2022 South Korean action comedy film directed by Moon Hyun-sung from a story by Sua Shin. It stars Yoo Ah-in as Park Dong-wook, the leader of a crew of drivers and mechanics, with Go Kyung-pyo, Lee Kyu-hyung, Park Ju-hyun and Ong Seong-wu as his team, and Moon So-ri, Kim Sung-kyun and Oh Jung-se in supporting roles.

In the run-up to the 1988 Seoul Olympics, smuggler and racer Dong-wook and his team, DJ Oh Woo-sam, Bok-nam, his younger sister Park Yoon-hee and Joon-ki, are blackmailed by prosecutor Ahn Pyung-wook into infiltrating the operation of Kang In-sook, a powerful underground chairwoman, and her right-hand man, Lee Hyun-kyun, to uncover the previous regime's secret slush fund. In exchange their criminal records will be erased; refusal means prison. After winning a car race held to recruit Kang's new drivers, the crew transports her money in modified cars confiscated by the prosecution, while Woo-sam works as a DJ in her nightclub and discovers a secret room. Lee tests their loyalty with a staged ambush and rewards them with a gold watch.

Shaken, Dong-wook wants to quit, but the others steal Kang's ledgers from the secret room, and he rejoins them. They then find that Pyung-wook has been killed: the watch was a listening device, and Lee knew they were informants all along. Lee captures and tortures Woo-sam, burns their hideout and frames the crew for the murder. Dong-wook takes the ledgers to Pyung-wook's superior along with a tape revealing that Kang plans to blame Lee and flee to the United States with the money. Playing it for Lee, he strikes a deal to bring Kang down, then enlists his racing rival Galchi with a bribe of rare sneakers. As Yoon-hee rescues Woo-sam, the crew leads Lee on a chase that ends with his crash, and he kills himself rather than face prison. Dong-wook boards Kang's plane, records her confession and drives his car out of the cargo hold, parachuting to safety. Kang is arrested, and the crew keeps some of the money as they set off for Los Angeles.

Produced by Andmarq Studio with MCMC and UAA, the film began shooting in Incheon in August 2021; filming was halted twice by positive COVID-19 tests and resumed in December 2021. It was released on Netflix on August 26, 2022.

documents.title: Demonic
documents.tagline: It's not a dream, it's not reality.
documents.overview: A young woman unleashes terrifying demons when supernatural forces at the root of a decades-old rift between mother and daughter are ruthlessly revealed.
documents.plot:
Demonic is a 2021 American supernatural horror film directed by Will Bowden and written by Brian DeLeeuw. The movie follows the story of a young woman named Erin, played by Olivia Luccardi, who returns to her hometown of New Haven, Connecticut, after a traumatic event in her past.

Upon her return, Erin discovers that her childhood home has been taken over by a mysterious and malevolent presence, which seems to be connected to an ancient evil entity known as the "Demonic". The entity is said to have been awakened by a group of occultists who performed a dark ritual in the house, unleashing a powerful and malevolent force upon the world.

As Erin delves deeper into the mystery, she begins to experience strange and terrifying occurrences, including visions, nightmares, and unexplained events. She soon realizes that she is being stalked by the entity, which seems to be manipulating her perceptions of reality.

Erin's investigation leads her to a local occult shop, where she meets a mysterious woman named Sarah, played by Tati Gabrielle. Sarah claims to have knowledge about the entity and offers to help Erin understand what is happening to her. However, it becomes clear that Sarah has her own motivations and may not be entirely trustworthy.

As the story unfolds, Erin discovers that the entity is connected to an ancient cult that was thought to be extinct. The cult's leader, a charismatic figure known as Father, played by Jake Weber, seems to be behind the ritual that awakened the entity. However, it becomes clear that Father has his own agenda and may not be what he seems.

The plot thickens as Erin and Sarah work together to uncover the truth about the entity and its connection to the cult. Along the way, they encounter a series of terrifying and supernatural events, including possession, hallucinations, and unexplained deaths.

In the climactic final act, Erin and Sarah face off against Father and the entity in a desperate bid to stop the ritual and banish the evil presence from the world. The movie culminates in a shocking twist, as it is revealed that Erin herself may be connected to the entity and has been playing a crucial role in its awakening.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of the entity and its connection to Erin. The final shot of the movie shows Erin standing alone, surrounded by an eerie and unsettling atmosphere, suggesting that she may still be under the influence of the entity.

Overall, Demonic is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of trauma, possession, and the supernatural. With its slow-burning tension and creepy atmosphere, it's sure to appeal to fans of the genre.

documents.title: ariana grande: excuse me, i love you
documents.original_title: ariana grande: excuse me, i love you
documents.overview: Ariana Grande takes the stage in London for her Sweetener World Tour and shares a behind-the-scenes look at her life in rehearsal and on the road.
documents.plot:
Ariana Grande: Excuse Me, I Love You (styled in lowercase) is a 2020 American concert documentary directed by Paul Dugdale that follows the pop singer Ariana Grande on stage and behind the scenes during her 2019 Sweetener World Tour. It was executive produced by Grande together with Scooter Braun, Allison Kaye and Scott Manson of SB Projects and Jesse Ignjatovic and Evan Prager of Den of Thieves, with Samon Fisher, Liz Garbus and Dan Cogan among the producers. The audio of the tour had already been released a year earlier on the live album K Bye for Now (SWT Live).

Most of the performance footage was filmed at Grande's show at the O2 Arena in London. The concert portion runs through a 25-song set list, opening with "Raindrops (An Angel Cried)" and "God Is a Woman" and including "Bad Idea", "Break Up with Your Girlfriend, I'm Bored", "R.E.M.", "7 Rings", "Breathin", "Needy", "NASA", "Into You", "Dangerous Woman", "Break Free" and "No Tears Left to Cry", before closing with "Thank U, Next". Between songs the film cuts to candid moments away from the stage, showing Grande with her dancers, band and crew such as Scott and Brian Nicholson, as well as rehearsals, preparations and casual conversations on the road, presenting a playful and affectionate side of the singer and her team.

Grande announced the film on social media in early December 2020, and Netflix released the trailer a few days later, along with themed profile icons for subscribers. It premiered on Netflix on 21 December 2020, marking the first anniversary of the tour's final show. Critical response was mixed to positive: Metacritic gave it a weighted score of 70 based on four reviews, while Rotten Tomatoes reported a 50% approval rating. The New York Times praised Grande's charming and relatable presence and the film's unguarded moments, and NME awarded four stars, describing it as euphoric pure pop even if it is not especially revealing. Mashable called it a gift to fans that recalled the days before the COVID-19 pandemic but regretted the lack of deeper rehearsal or songwriting footage. IndieWire gave it a C, likening it to a commercial for a polished product, and Common Sense Media felt the meticulously staged show and superficial chats offered little real insight into Grande's personality.

documents.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid
documents.tagline: New school. Old cheese.
documents.overview: Greg Heffley is a scrawny but ambitious kid with an active imagination and big plans to be rich and famous – he just has to survive middle school first.
documents.plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid is a 2021 animated comedy film directed by Swinton Scott in his feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Jeff Kinney based on his 2007 book of the same name. It is the second adaptation of the book, following the 2010 live-action film, and it serves as an animated reboot of the Diary of a Wimpy Kid film series and its fifth instalment overall. Brady Noon voices Greg Heffley, with Ethan William Childress as Rowley Jefferson, Hunter Dillon as Rodrick, and Erica Cerra and Chris Diamantopoulos as Greg's parents. Produced by 20th Century Animation, the film was released on Disney+ in December 2021.

Best friends Greg Heffley and Rowley Jefferson are about to begin middle school. Greg's older brother Rodrick gives him advice on how to survive, warning him above all to avoid the Cheese Touch, the curse said to fall on anyone who touches an old slice of cheese rotting on the playground. Worried that Rowley's childish behaviour will make them targets for bullies, Greg tries to persuade his friend to start acting his age, while keeping the legend of the cheese to himself so as not to frighten him.

When school begins, the pair struggle to fit in, largely because of Rowley's innocent habits, such as asking other kids if they want to "play" instead of "hang out", but they manage to avoid falling to the very bottom of the social ladder. On Halloween, Greg and Rowley must take Greg's little brother Manny trick-or-treating, and Greg quickly realises that Manny's costume helps them collect huge amounts of candy. Over the school year, a series of misadventures, from a disastrous safety patrol incident to a rivalry for the school cartoonist position, sees Rowley's popularity rise while Greg's schemes keep backfiring. Their friendship falls apart, until Greg finally makes a sacrifice involving the dreaded cheese to protect Rowley.

The film retains the hand-drawn look of Kinney's illustrations by rendering them in three-dimensional computer animation, and keeps the episodic structure and self-centred narration of the books.

Reviews were mixed, with critics praising the faithful visual style but finding that the story offered little new compared with the earlier live-action film.
