documents.title: Intrusion
documents.tagline: The quietest towns hide the darkest secrets.
documents.overview: When a husband and wife move to a small town, a home invasion leaves the wife traumatized and suspicious that those around her might not be who they seem.
documents.plot:
Intrusion is a 2021 American psychological thriller directed by Adam Salky and written by Christopher Sparling, starring Freida Pinto as Meera Parsons and Logan Marshall-Green as her husband Henry, with Robert John Burke as Detective Stephen Morse. The film follows a couple whose new life in the New Mexico desert is shattered by a violent home invasion.

Seeking a quieter life away from Boston, Meera, a therapist, and Henry, an architect, move into an isolated, ultramodern house that Henry designed and built in Corrales, New Mexico. Shortly after their arrival, their home is burglarized, though only a laptop and their phones are stolen. A few nights later, masked intruders return, tie up Meera and pursue the couple through the house, until Henry uses a handgun he had secretly kept to kill two of the men. The third is critically wounded and taken to the hospital.

The police tell the couple that the intruders belonged to a family with a criminal history and are suspected in the disappearance of a young relative, college student Christine Cobb, a case that may never be solved unless the surviving man recovers. Meera, a cancer survivor, is deeply traumatized, while Henry urges her to move on. When the surviving intruder dies and Meera notices that Henry lied about where he went that night, her suspicions grow. Investigating on her own, she discovers that the intruders had worked on the construction of the house, and Henry offers an explanation involving financial fraud and blackmail. A videotape recorded by one of the intruders, however, leads Meera to a terrible secret hidden within the house itself, and she discovers that the man she married is far more dangerous than the strangers who broke in.

The film explores trust, trauma and the idea of the home as a place of hidden danger, building toward a final confrontation between husband and wife.

Intrusion was released by Netflix on September 22, 2021. It received negative reviews, with 23 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 39.

documents.title: Pelé
documents.overview: Against the backdrop of a turbulent era in Brazil, this documentary captures Pelé's extraordinary path from breakthrough talent to national hero. Mixing rare archival footage and exclusive interviews, this documentary celebrates the legendary Brazilian footballer who personified football as art.
documents.plot:
Pelé is a 2021 biographical documentary about the Brazilian footballer Pelé, directed by Ben Nichols and David Tryhorn and produced for Netflix, with Kevin Macdonald, Jon Owen and Jonathan Rogers as executive producers. Combining extensive archival footage with new interviews, it charts the player's journey from breakthrough talent to national hero against the backdrop of a turbulent era in Brazilian history, including the military dictatorship.

The film follows Pelé from his childhood to his debut for Santos at 15, his selection for Brazil at 16 and the 1958 World Cup final, in which he scored twice at the age of 17. Overnight a global icon, he became football's first millionaire while still a teenager, and in a candid interview he admits that he found it hard to remain faithful amid the adulation, saying he had affairs, some of which produced children he learned about only later. Brazil's group-stage exit at the 1966 World Cup in England, where he was injured again, is described by Pelé as the saddest moment of his life, and he vowed at the time never to play in another tournament. The documentary sets his career against the 1964 military coup and the repression that followed, and asks whether he knew of the torture carried out by the regime; he concedes that it would be a lie to say he was unaware. Former teammate Paulo Cézar Caju criticises him for never speaking out, while journalist Juca Kfouri describes how winning the 1970 World Cup became a matter of state, with military personnel among the team staff and pressure on Pelé to play. The film recounts his feud with coach João Saldanha, who claimed Pelé's eyesight was failing before being replaced by Mário Zagallo, and culminates in Brazil's 4–1 victory over Italy in the 1970 final in Mexico, in which Pelé scored and set up two goals, making him the only player with three World Cup titles. His later years at Santos and his final spell with the New York Cosmos are also covered.

Alongside Pelé himself, now able to walk only with assistance, the film features family members, former teammates, coaches, journalists and politicians. Netflix released it on February 23, 2021. Reviews were moderately positive, with 82% on Rotten Tomatoes; The Guardian's Andrew Pulver found it admiring but more sedate than Asif Kapadia's Maradona film, praising its context on the 1960s, while The Hollywood Reporter called it a polished, well-intentioned biography.

documents.title: The Takedown
documents.tagline: Two cops. One case. No clue.
documents.overview: Ousmane Diakité and François Monge are two cops with very different styles, backgrounds and careers. The unlikely pair are reunited once again for a new investigation that takes them across France. What seemed to be a simple drug deal turns out to be a much bigger criminal case wrapped in danger and unexpected comedy.
documents.plot:
The Takedown (Loin du périph) is a 2022 French action comedy directed by Louis Leterrier from a screenplay by Stéphane Kazandjian, based on characters created for David Charhon's 2012 film On the Other Side of the Tracks. Omar Sy and Laurent Lafitte return as the mismatched police partners Ousmane Diakité and François Monge, joined by Izïa Higelin as Alice Gauthier, Dimitri Storoge as Antoine Brunner, Stéphane Pezerat as Commissioner Mercier and Sabrina Ouazani as Yasmine.

A decade after their first case, Ousmane is a commander in the Paris criminal brigade, and after a viral video of him fighting a suspect he is pushed to front a national police recruitment campaign, while François, a captain in the 12th arrondissement, is criticized by colleagues for getting in the way of investigations. The two meet again by chance when François finds half of a corpse on a high-speed train. The victim, Kevin Marchal, came from Valergnes, a town in the Alps, and Ousmane travels there to escape the campaign, with François tagging along. With help from local officer Alice, they learn Kevin was shot off his motorbike onto the tracks and had been running a drug lab in his mother's house. A brawl in a strip club with a bouncer who seems immune to pain, and the man's sudden death, lead them to a security firm whose guards share the tattoo of a militia, the Sons of Clovis. Commissioner Mercier quickly closes the case, but Ousmane refuses to leave. A friend of Kevin's reveals that the victim feared the militia and had asked Mercier for protection.

Following Mercier, the duo is threatened by Brunner, the town's far-right mayor, and attacked on the road. In Brunner's basement they discover plans for coordinated attacks on mosques, synagogues and a migrant center, carried out by fighters taking pain-numbing methamphetamine. In the final showdown, François distracts the militia while Ousmane sabotages their weapons and fights Alice, who turns out to be Brunner's ally. The pair stop a bomb at the migrant center and arrest Brunner and Alice, and François ends up as the face of the recruitment campaign.

Filmed in spring 2021 in Paris and the Alps, the film was released on Netflix on 6 May 2022 and logged more than 78 million hours viewed in its first 28 days. French reviews were mixed: Ouest-France praised the chemistry of Sy and Lafitte, while Les Inrockuptibles felt its political satire and action scenes were less successful than its comedy.

documents.title: Tentacles
documents.tagline: How well do you know the one you love?
documents.overview: A young Los Angeles couple Tara and Sam fall head over heels into a new romance, entwining their lives—until their intimacy transforms into something terrifying.
documents.plot:
Tentacles is a 2021 American romantic horror film directed by Clara Aranovich from a screenplay by Alexandra Pechman, with a story credit shared with Nick Antosca, both of whom had worked on the anthology series Channel Zero. Produced by Blumhouse Television, it was released on Hulu on 12 February 2021 as the Valentine's Day instalment of Into the Dark, the monthly holiday-themed horror anthology series, and was the series' first new feature since July 2020, following a hiatus caused by the COVID-19 pandemic; it was filmed under pandemic restrictions. Dana Drori and Casey Deidrick star, with Kasey Elise in a supporting role. It runs about 84 minutes.

Sam (Deidrick), a commercial photographer in Los Angeles, meets Tara (Drori), a mysterious drifter who lives in vacant houses and seems to have plenty of money from uncertain sources, at an open house. The two share an instant, intensely physical connection, and Tara is soon living in the run-down family home Sam inherited from his parents, renovating it in exchange for a place to stay. As they fall ever deeper in love and race through the milestones of a relationship towards marriage, Sam's business partner and longtime best friend Esther (Elise) worries that they are moving far too quickly, but he ignores her. Tara then reveals that an ex-boyfriend is stalking her, break-ins follow, and Sam's health begins to deteriorate for reasons no one can diagnose, with piercing earaches and moments of disorientation. In its final act the film reveals that Sam, not Tara, is the one in danger, and their consuming romance turns into a tale of transformation and aquatic body horror.

Critics found the film underpowered. Matt Donato of /Film gave it 5 out of 10, writing that its first forty minutes hazily build a relationship between thinly written characters, that Aranovich's attempts at style, such as a fast-motion sex montage and distorted camera views, were not enough, and that its tentacled horror arrives only after the viewer's attention has waned, though he did not fault the performers. Drew Koenig of Tell-Tale TV credited the film with subverting the familiar story of a woman endangered by an untrustworthy man by revealing Sam as the victim of a different kind of toxic love, but felt that Tara's characterisation and the final twist muddied its romantic metaphor and that, while decently paced, it lacked teeth.

documents.title: Squared Love
documents.overview: A celebrity journalist and renowned womanizer starts to rethink his life choices after he falls for a mysterious model who leads a double life.
documents.plot:
Squared Love (Polish: Miłość do kwadratu) is a 2021 Polish romantic comedy film directed by Filip Zylber and written by Marzanna Polit and Wiktor Piątkowski. Produced by Endemol Polska and set in Warsaw, it stars Adrianna Chlebicka and Mateusz Banasiuk, with Mirosław Baka, Agnieszka Żulewska, Krzysztof Czeczot, Anna Smołowik, Tomasz Karolak, Bartłomiej Kotschedoff, Jacek Knap and Helena Mazur in supporting roles. It was released on Netflix on 11 February 2021, and Netflix later reported in its first-quarter investor letter that 31 million households had sampled it. It was followed in 2023 by two sequels, Squared Love All Over Again and Squared Love Everlasting.

Monika Grabarczyk (Chlebicka) is a devoted primary-school teacher, beloved by her pupils though disliked by her demanding, test-obsessed principal (Karolak). Early each morning, however, she swaps her glasses and ponytail for a curly wig, blue contact lenses and glamorous clothes to work as Klaudia, a mysterious model on billboards across the city who only works before nine. She hates modelling and keeps it secret, believing no school would tolerate it, but needs the money to pay off the debts her widowed mechanic father (Baka) owes to loan sharks; he knows nothing of it and only laments that she is not in love. Stefan Tkaczyk (Banasiuk), known to the world as Enzo, is a shallow, womanising model who loves the sports cars he gets to borrow and lives with his boss and lover Alicja (Żulewska) in an open relationship. Their first meeting goes badly when he picks Klaudia up after her car breaks down on the way to a shoot and mistakes her for a prostitute. When Alicja throws Enzo out, he moves in with his brother, whose wife has left the family, and has to look after his young niece Ania (Mazur), who turns out to be one of Monika's pupils. Cast together in an advertising campaign, Enzo feels a spark with Klaudia on set while also being drawn to Monika on school trips, unaware that they are the same woman, while her double life grows ever harder to keep hidden.

The film was poorly received; on Rotten Tomatoes only 17% of six critics' reviews were positive. John Serba of Decider found its secret-identity premise unconvincing and its script cluttered, though he credited Chlebicka with bringing some sincerity to the dual role, while Roger Moore of Movie Nation called it vapid and noted the leads' thin chemistry, singling out its soundtrack of mostly American pop songs.

documents.title: Survive the Game
documents.tagline: Your land. Your rules. Your fight.
documents.overview: When cop David is injured in a drug bust gone wrong, his partner Cal chases the two criminals who shot him. They all land at a remote farm owned by troubled vet Eric, and as Cal and Eric plot their defense, more of the gang arrives - along with a wounded David. Outnumbered, the three heroes must use stealth, smarts, and good shooting to take down the drug-dealing mob.
documents.plot:
Survive the Game, also released as Killing Field, is a 2021 American action thriller directed by James Cullen Bressack from a screenplay by Ross Peacock, his first feature script. It stars Chad Michael Murray as a troubled military veteran and Bruce Willis as a veteran detective, with Swen Temmel, Michael Sirow, Kate Katzman, Zack Ward, Donna D'Errico and Canyon Prince. It was produced by Randall Emmett and George Furla's Emmett/Furla Oasis with Lionsgate, which distributed the film.

Detective David Watson and his younger partner Cal stake out a drug deal by a gang David has long pursued, but the operation goes wrong, a gunfight breaks out and David is shot. The criminal couple Mickey Jean and Violet escape and take refuge on a remote farm owned by Eric, a former soldier who has withdrawn there and turned to drink after the deaths of his wife Hannah and their daughter. The pair hold Eric hostage while they wait for their boss to arrive, but Cal tracks them to the property, leading to a tense stand-off in which Mickey holds a gun to Eric while Cal holds a knife to Violet's throat.

When the gang's leader, Michael, who bears a grudge against David, learns what has happened, he sends a large force of armed men to the farm to eliminate every witness, bringing the wounded David with them as a captive. Eric reveals his military skills, and he and Cal devise a plan to defend the farm against the much larger group. Eric must also persuade his friend Andrew, who unexpectedly visits, to leave before the gangsters kill him. Outnumbered, the men rely on stealth and marksmanship through a series of gun battles and hand-to-hand fights, and David eventually rejoins them as they take on the drug ring.

The film was released in select theaters and on video on demand in the United States on October 8, 2021, followed by DVD and Blu-ray on October 12. Most critics were negative: on Rotten Tomatoes only one of seven reviews was positive. Bobby LePire of Film Threat was an exception, awarding it 8 out of 10 and praising its energetic, no-frills action and the performances of Murray and Ward while finding the car chase finale a letdown, whereas Oliver Armknecht of Film-Rezensionen criticized its cheap-looking action, its throwaway story and how seldom Willis appears despite his billing. Willis's performance was among those nominated for a special Golden Raspberry category devoted to his 2021 films, which was rescinded after he retired because of aphasia.

documents.title: 13 Minutes
documents.tagline: Every second counts.
documents.overview: As a new day begins in the small American town of Minninnewah, the residents start their day as ordinary as the next. Mother Nature, however, has other plans for them. Inhabitants have just 13 minutes to seek shelter before the largest tornado on record ravages the town, leaving them struggling to protect their loved ones and fighting for their lives. Left to deal with the aftermath, four families must overcome their differences and find strength in each other in order to survive.
documents.plot:
13 Minutes is a 2021 American-Canadian disaster drama written, directed and produced by Lindsay Gossling in her feature debut, from a story co-written with Travis Farncombe. The ensemble cast includes Amy Smart, Thora Birch, Anne Heche, Trace Adkins, Peter Facinelli, Paz Vega, Yancey Arias, Sofia Vassilieva and Will Peltz. Its title refers to the brief window residents have to seek shelter once a tornado is detected.

The film is set in the fictional Oklahoma town of Minninnewah and follows four families whose lives are intertwined. Jess, a mechanic, learns that her 19-year-old daughter, Maddy, is pregnant, and Maddy agonizes over whether to have an abortion. The medical professional who examines her is Tammy, an overbearing devout Christian, who unprofessionally tries to persuade her to keep the baby. Tammy and her farmer husband, Rick, are also parents to Luke, who is gay and afraid of coming out; when he finally tells them, they react with homophobic panic. Brad is the town's television weatherman, and his wife, Kim, heads the local emergency response team. Meanwhile Ana is trying to save enough money to buy a home for herself and her husband, Carlos, an undocumented immigrant.

As these personal dramas unfold, a massive storm system develops and spawns what becomes the largest tornado on record. When the twister finally strikes, late in the story, it tears through Minninnewah in the space of the titular thirteen minutes, leaving death and devastation in its path. In the aftermath, the survivors, some of them badly injured, must deal with loss and grief, and several of the problems that consumed them before the storm are rendered irrelevant or resolved by sudden turns of fate. The community begins to rebuild, facing both death and new beginnings.

The film was shot in Oklahoma. Quiver gave it a limited theatrical release in the United States on October 29, 2021, followed by video on demand in December, grossing about $67,000 worldwide from releases in the UAE and Portugal. Reviews were largely negative, with 27% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 40. The Guardian's Leslie Felperin found the plotting weakened by convenient turns of fate that punish the less sympathetic characters, and The Globe and Mail called it soapy melodrama in which the tornado feels incidental. Rex Reed of The New York Observer was more positive, finding it sometimes contrived but strengthened by its likable cast.

documents.title: Fresh
documents.tagline: It’s not for everyone.
documents.overview: Frustrated by scrolling dating apps only to end up on lame, tedious dates, Noa takes a chance by giving her number to the awkwardly charming Steve after a produce-section meet-cute at the grocery store.
documents.plot:
Fresh is a 2022 American horror thriller directed by Mimi Cave in her directorial debut from a screenplay by Lauryn Kahn. It stars Daisy Edgar-Jones as Noa and Sebastian Stan as Steve, with Jonica T. Gibbs as Mollie, Charlotte Le Bon as Ann, Andrea Bang as Penny and Dayo Okeniyi as Paul. Co-produced by Legendary Pictures and Adam McKay's Hyperobject Industries, the film uses the conventions of romantic comedy to satirize modern dating before turning into a darkly comic horror story.

Noa, a young woman in Portland, is fed up with online dating and the crude men it brings her. One day at a supermarket she meets Steve, a charming and funny stranger, and the two hit it off. After several dates, Steve invites her on a weekend getaway to a surprise destination. Despite the misgivings of her best friend Mollie, Noa agrees and spends the night before the trip at Steve's secluded luxury home, where he drugs her drink.

Noa wakes up chained in a cell. Steve calmly explains that he deals in human flesh, which he both eats and sells to wealthy clients with cannibalistic tastes, and that he plans to keep her alive for as long as possible so that her meat stays fresh, removing parts of her body over time. In an adjacent cell, another captive, Penny, tells Noa what has happened to the women before them. Meanwhile, Mollie grows worried and begins investigating with the help of Paul, a bartender who served Noa and Steve on their first date. She discovers that Steve is not who he claimed to be. Inside the house, Noa decides that her only chance of survival is to win Steve's trust by pretending to be fascinated by his world, playing a dangerous game of seduction to find a way out.

The film's opening romantic-comedy section runs for about half an hour before the title card appears, a structure that heightens its commentary on the dangers women face in modern dating.

Fresh premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 20, 2022, and was released on Hulu in the United States on March 4, 2022, and on Disney+ internationally. It received generally positive reviews, with 82 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 67.

documents.title: Lamb
documents.tagline: Mother. Nature.
documents.overview: An Icelandic couple live with their herd of sheep on a beautiful but remote farm. When they discover a mysterious newborn on their land, they decide to keep it and raise it as their own. This unexpected development and the prospects of a new family brings them much joy before ultimately destroying them.

documents.title: Last Survivors
documents.overview: The pic is set in the aftermath of an apocalyptic event that forces people into extreme isolation. A father and son, who have been living off grid for 20 years, encounter an outsider who threatens to destroy the utopia they’ve built.
documents.plot:
Last Survivors, previously known by the working title SHTF, is a 2021 American thriller directed by Drew Mylrea in his feature directorial debut. Drew Van Acker, Alicia Silverstone and Stephen Moyer star in the film, which is set in an apparently post-apocalyptic world in which a father has raised his now adult son in complete isolation deep in the woods, far from what he describes as the ruins of civilization.

For more than twenty years, Troy and his son Jake have lived off the grid following what Troy insists was a catastrophic event that destroyed much of society and left its survivors desperate and violent. Troy has relentlessly drilled into Jake the belief that every outsider is an immediate threat who must be eliminated, and he kills and buries anyone who stumbles across their homestead. When a stranger shoots and wounds Troy, Jake is forced to venture out alone to find antibiotics to save him.

During his search Jake comes upon a woman working outside an isolated house. Despite his father's orders, he cannot bring himself to kill her. Instead he slips into her home, takes antibiotics and steroids and returns to tend to Troy. Drawn back to her, Jake secretly hides some of their food stores so that his father will believe supplies are running low, giving him an excuse to go hunting. He returns to the house and confronts the woman, who tells him her name is Henrietta. As their conversations continue, it becomes increasingly clear to the audience that the outside world may never have suffered any generalized collapse at all. Troy grows suspicious of his son's absences, while Jake begins to doubt everything his father has told him about what lies beyond the forest, setting the two men on a collision course.

Principal photography took place in Butte, Montana, and wrapped in January 2021. The film received a generally favorable response: on Rotten Tomatoes 71% of 17 critics' reviews are positive. Martin Unsworth of Starburst gave it three stars out of five, writing that it follows the familiar path of post-apocalyptic films while remaining engaging. Angie Han of The Hollywood Reporter was more critical, arguing that the film clearly had a lot on its mind but that its reticence kept it from exploring its more challenging ideas, while Common Sense Media described it as a solid evening of entertainment likely to spark family discussion.

documents.title: Hilda and the Mountain King
documents.tagline: Such is the life of an adventurer.
documents.overview: When Hilda wakes up in the body of a troll, she must use her wits and courage to get back home, become human again — and save the city of Trolberg.
documents.plot:
Hilda and the Mountain King, marketed as Hilda: The Mountain King, is a 2021 animated fantasy adventure directed by Andy Coyle and written by Luke Pearson. It adapts Pearson's graphic novel of the same name and continues the season-two finale of the animated series Hilda. Bella Ramsey, Ameerah Falzon-Ojo, Oliver Nelson and Daisy Haggard lead the voice cast. It was produced by Silvergate Media and Mercury Filmworks.

At the end of the series' second season, a changeling spell has swapped Hilda with Baba, a young troll. Now a troll herself, Hilda runs away from her troll mother, Trylla, and turns to stone in the sunlight. In Trolberg, her mother Johanna finds Baba in Hilda's place and sets off to find her daughter. Meanwhile, Erik Ahlberg imposes a curfew and forms a Safety Patrol to deal with the rise in troll activity. Each night, Hilda turns back from stone, but the city's bells keep her out. She finds a huge cave where an imprisoned giant troll, Trundle, promises to make her human again if she does several tasks for him. She brings him troll mead, silences the bells that hold him and finally retrieves a red orb from the ruins of the legendary Mountain King's castle. When she touches the orb, she sees a giant creature looming over Trolberg's walls.

Johanna reaches the Stone Forest with Ahlberg's grudging help, and she and Hilda are reunited. When Trylla is reunited with Baba, the spell is broken. Trundle then puts the orb back in, revealing it as his missing eye, declares himself the Mountain King and leads the trolls against Trolberg. Hilda realizes what the vision meant: Amma, mother of all trolls, lies beneath the city and will rise to defend her children if they are attacked. Ahlberg destroys Trundle anyway, and Amma begins to wake. Hilda throws the eye at Ahlberg so that he sees the vision too, and he calls off the attack.

The trolls gather peacefully around Amma. Ahlberg resigns, and his deputy Gerda Gustav sets up an annual "Night of the Trolls" when trolls may visit their mother. Hilda's family stays in touch with Baba's.

Production wrapped in July 2021, and Netflix released the film on December 30, 2021. It is dedicated to two members of the animation crew who died during production. Reviews were positive: Polygon noted its darker tone, Variety praised its emotional wisdom and Screen Rant praised its visuals and music.

documents.title: The Royal Treatment
documents.overview: Isabella runs her own salon and isn’t afraid to speak her mind, while Prince Thomas runs his own country and is about to marry for duty rather than love. When Izzy and her fellow stylists get the opportunity of a lifetime to do the hair for the royal wedding, she and Prince Thomas learn that taking control of their own destiny requires following their hearts.
documents.plot:
The Royal Treatment is a 2022 American romance film directed by Rick Jacobson and written by Holly Hester. It stars Laura Marano and Mena Massoud, and apart from them and a few other actors, most of the cast is from New Zealand, where it was filmed. Released on Netflix on January 20, 2022, it became the streaming service's most-watched film that week.

Isabella, known as Izzy, is a hairdresser who runs a salon in Manhattan. When a fire caused by a faulty microwave damages the salon, the landlord's assistant, Doug, insists that she pay for the repairs, and Izzy has to give up the money she had been saving to travel the world. Meanwhile Prince Thomas of the kingdom of Lavania, visiting New York, asks his assistant Walter to book him a haircut, and Walter mistakenly calls Izzy's salon. Izzy agrees to cut the prince's hair for $500, but she walks out halfway through after seeing how badly a housekeeper is treated. Intrigued, Thomas comes to the salon to have his haircut finished, and the two spend a fun night together walking through the city. Soon afterwards, Thomas's fiancée Lauren and her mother hire Izzy and her coworkers to do hair and makeup for the royal wedding, and the team travels to Lavania for a $50,000 fee. At the castle, a strict royal assistant, Madam Fabre, tests the team's skills, and Izzy impresses her by transforming a manservant. She explores the kingdom with Thomas, including a poor district the royal family considers dangerous, and inspires local people to donate gifts for underprivileged children, encouraging Thomas to do more for his people. As their friendship deepens, Lauren's mother notices that the two are growing too close, and Thomas learns that his arranged marriage is tied to the royal family's financial troubles, leaving him to decide between duty and love.

The Royal Treatment received negative reviews from critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, 35% of 17 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 36 out of 100, although Courtney Howard of Variety gave it a positive review, writing that it infuses expected genre trappings with unexpected delights.

documents.title: The Eternal Daughter
documents.tagline: An exquisite ghost story.
documents.overview: An artist and her elderly mother confront long-buried secrets when they return to a former family home, now a hotel haunted by its mysterious past.
documents.plot: An artist and her elderly mother confront long-buried secrets when they return to a former family home, now a hotel haunted by its mysterious past.

documents.title: Secret Headquarters
documents.tagline: When the secret is out, the adventure begins.
documents.overview: While hanging out after school, Charlie and his friends discover the headquarters of the world’s most powerful superhero hidden beneath his home. When villains attack, they must team up to defend the headquarters and save the world.
documents.plot:
I have information on Secret Headquarters.

Secret Headquarters is a 2022 American superhero comedy film directed by Chris McKay and written by Matthew Robinson. The movie stars Will Poulter, Octavia Spencer, and Keegan-Michael Key.

The story follows Sheldon (Will Poulter), a young boy who discovers that his parents are superheroes known as the "Guardians" in their secret lives. However, when he tries to join them on one of their missions, they realize that he's not ready for the responsibility and send him back home.

Sheldon is heartbroken but soon finds himself caught up in a battle between the Guardians and an evil villain named The Archon (Jack Huston). As Sheldon navigates this new world, he teams up with his parents' sidekick, Jack (Keegan-Michael Key), to help stop The Archon from taking over the city.

Throughout the movie, Sheldon learns valuable lessons about responsibility, teamwork, and being true to oneself. With the help of his family and friends, he proves that even a young boy can make a difference in saving the day.

The film is a fun and action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, family, and growing up. The cast delivers great performances, with Will Poulter bringing a lovable and relatable energy to the lead role.

documents.title: Bones and All
documents.tagline: You can’t run from who you are.
documents.overview: Abandoned by her father, a young woman embarks on a thousand-mile odyssey through the backroads of America where she meets a disenfranchised drifter. But despite their best efforts, all roads lead back to their terrifying pasts and to a final stand that will determine whether their love can survive their otherness.
documents.plot:
Bones and All is a 2022 romantic horror film directed by Luca Guadagnino and written by David Kajganich, adapted from Camille DeAngelis's 2015 novel Bones & All. Set in the late 1980s, it stars Taylor Russell as Maren Yearly and Timothée Chalamet as Lee, two young cannibals who fall for each other on a road trip across America, with Mark Rylance, Michael Stuhlbarg, André Holland and Chloë Sevigny in support.

In 1988, teenage Maren sneaks out to a sleepover in Virginia and bites off part of a classmate's finger. She and her father, Frank, flee to Maryland, and soon after her 18th birthday he abandons her, leaving money, her birth certificate and a cassette in which he recounts how she killed her babysitter as a small child and how he covered for her through years of similar incidents. Maren sets out for Minnesota, where her unknown mother, Janelle, was born. In Ohio she meets Sully, an odd older "eater" who found her by scent, and after joining him in feeding on a dead woman she runs away. At an Indiana store she meets Lee, another eater, who kills a man who had been harassing a customer and offers her a ride in the dead man's truck.

On the road they fall in love. In Lee's Kentucky hometown, Maren sees how he avoids talking about his absent father, while his younger sister Kayla, unaware of what he is, scolds him for always leaving. They meet two more men, Jake and Brad, whose casual relish for eating people disturbs Maren, and after Lee kills a carnival worker, she is wracked with guilt to learn the man had a family. Maren tracks down her adoptive grandmother, Barbara, and then Janelle, who has committed herself to a psychiatric hospital in Fergus Falls and has eaten her own hands; Janelle's letter says Maren would be better off dead. Maren leaves Lee, rebuffs Sully, who has been following her, and later returns to Kentucky, where she learns about the night Lee's abusive father vanished. Reunited, Lee admits that his father was also an eater and that he consumed him. The couple try to build an ordinary life in Ann Arbor until Sully breaks in and attacks Maren; they kill him, but Lee is mortally wounded and asks her to eat him "bones and all", which she does.

The film premiered at the 79th Venice International Film Festival in September 2022, winning the Silver Lion for direction and the Marcello Mastroianni Award for Russell. Reviews were positive, with 82% on Rotten Tomatoes, but grossed only $15.2 million worldwide against a $16–20 million budget.

documents.title: Constantine: The House of Mystery
documents.tagline: Enter a world where magic can't save you.
documents.overview: John Constantine wakes up in the eerie House of Mystery with no recollection of how he got there. Fortunately, Zatanna and his friends are all there. Unfortunately, they have a bad habit of turning into demons and ripping him to shreds, over and over again!
documents.plot:
Constantine: The House of Mystery is a 2022 American animated supernatural horror short film in Warner Bros. Animation's DC Showcase line, directed by Matt Peters from a script by Ernie Altbacker and produced by Warner Bros. Animation, DC and Warner Bros. Home Entertainment, with Rick Morales and Jim Krieg as producers and Sam Register as executive producer. Running a little over 26 minutes, it is the longest short in its collection and was the anchor of the anthology release DC Showcase: Constantine – The House of Mystery, issued on Blu-ray and digital in early May 2022 alongside the shorts Kamandi: The Last Boy on Earth!, The Losers and Blue Beetle. Matt Ryan reprises his live-action and animated role as John Constantine, with Camilla Luddington as Zatanna, Ray Chase as Jason Blood and Etrigan, Robin Atkin Downes as Nergal, Damian O'Hare as Chas, Grey Griffin and Lou Diamond Phillips. Its tagline was "Enter a world where magic can't save you."

The story follows on directly from the animated film Justice League Dark: Apokolips War (2020), at the end of which Constantine persuaded the Flash to reset the timeline and undo the world-ending catastrophe. Constantine wakes up in the eerie House of Mystery with no memory of how or why he got there. To his relief, Zatanna and his friends are all there with him, but they have a bad habit of turning into demons and ripping him to shreds, and every time he dies he wakes up again to repeat the cycle. As he searches for the truth behind his imprisonment in the mansion, flashbacks reveal how his hellish trap is tied to the events of Apokolips War: for tampering with the fabric of reality, he has been cursed to spend eternity among the deadly threats inside the house, a punishment that the reviewer Max Byrne likened to that of Prometheus. True to the DC comic series The House of Mystery that inspired it, the short ends with a twist.

The short was well received. James Harvey of The World's Finest called it gripping, twisted and occasionally funny, arguably the strongest short in the collection, praising Ryan's performance, Peters's direction, Altbacker's story and Robert J. Kral's score. Max Byrne of Dark Knight News described it as a short, sharp shock, gory and delightfully evil, highlighting its horror-inspired score and voice cast. Sam Stone of CBR found it the most gruesome and somewhat out of place in an eclectic anthology, but always a delight for Ryan's return as the Hellblazer.

documents.title: Zack Snyder's Justice League
documents.tagline: Us united.
documents.overview: Determined to ensure Superman's ultimate sacrifice was not in vain, Bruce Wayne aligns forces with Diana Prince with plans to recruit a team of metahumans to protect the world from an approaching threat of catastrophic proportions.
documents.plot:
Zack Snyder's Justice League is a 2021 superhero film directed by Zack Snyder, based on the DC Comics team of the same name. The movie follows the story of five superheroes who must come together to save the world from an ancient evil.

The film begins with Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck), aka Batman, who has been training himself physically and mentally after the events of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. He is approached by the Justice League's leader, Diana Prince (Gal Gadot), also known as Wonder Woman, who informs him that an ancient being known as Steppenwolf has returned to Earth with a plan to harvest three powerful artifacts.

Meanwhile, Arthur Curry (Jason Momoa), aka Aquaman, is introduced as he tries to find his place in the world and understand his connection to the underwater kingdom of Atlantis. He eventually joins forces with Batman and Wonder Woman to stop Steppenwolf's plans.

The team also includes Barry Allen (Ezra Miller), aka The Flash, who has been struggling to control his powers after the events of Justice League. They are joined by Cyborg (Ray Fisher), a half-human, half-robot who is still learning to control his abilities.

As Steppenwolf's plan unfolds, the team must work together to stop him and save the world from destruction. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles and challenges that test their skills and teamwork.

Throughout the film, Snyder explores themes of unity, sacrifice, and the power of friendship. The movie also delves into the characters' backstories and emotional struggles, adding depth to the story.

One notable aspect of the film is its visual style, which features a mix of practical and CGI effects. Snyder's direction creates a sense of grandeur and spectacle, bringing the Justice League to life in a way that feels both epic and intimate.

Overall, Zack Snyder's Justice League is a thrilling adventure that brings together some of DC Comics' most iconic superheroes. While it may not be perfect, the film offers a unique take on the characters and their relationships, making it a must-see for fans of the franchise.

documents.title: Dark Web: Cicada 3301
documents.tagline: A true hacker story that never happened.
documents.overview: Genius hacker Connor discovers Cicada 3301, an online treasure hunt that could be a recruiting tool for a secret society. Soon Conner, art-expert friend Avi, and secretive librarian Gwen are dashing from graffiti sites to ancient libraries to uncover real-world clues. But they must outrun aggressive NSA agents, also hot on the trail of Cicada, who want the glory for themselves.
documents.plot:
Dark Web: Cicada 3301 is a thought-provoking thriller that delves into the darker corners of human psychology and the blurred lines between reality and conspiracy theories. The movie masterfully weaves together elements of mystery, suspense, and paranoia, creating a sense of unease that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

At its core, Dark Web: Cicada 3301 explores the theme of obsession, as embodied by the enigmatic Cicada 3301 figure. This character's relentless pursuit of knowledge and truth becomes an all-consuming force that drives the protagonist to the edge of sanity. The film expertly captures the sense of desperation and fixation that can come with being drawn into a complex web of intrigue.

The movie also delves into the realm of conspiracy theories, skillfully using them as a metaphor for the darker aspects of human nature. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the truth is often more sinister than we might initially suspect, and that the pursuit of knowledge can sometimes lead us down a rabbit hole of paranoia and mistrust.

Furthermore, Dark Web: Cicada 3301 touches on the theme of identity, as the protagonist navigates a world where reality is constantly shifting and the lines between truth and fiction become increasingly blurred. This sense of disorientation is mirrored in the character's own identity crisis, as they struggle to reconcile their past with their present.

Throughout the movie, these themes are expertly intertwined, creating a complex tapestry that keeps the viewer on the edge of their seat. Ultimately, Dark Web: Cicada 3301 is a thought-provoking thriller that challenges us to question our assumptions about the world and the nature of truth itself.

documents.title: Settlers
documents.tagline: How far would you go to build a new life?
documents.overview: Remmy and her parents, refugees from Earth, have found peace on the Martian outskirts until strangers appear in the hills beyond their farm. Told as a triptych, the film follows Remmy as she struggles to survive in an uneasy landscape.
documents.plot:
Settlers is a 2021 British science fiction thriller written and directed by Wyatt Rockefeller in his feature debut. It stars Sofia Boutella as Ilsa, Ismael Cruz Córdova as Jerry and Jonny Lee Miller as Reza, with Brooklynn Prince and Nell Tiger Free playing the daughter, Remmy, as a child and as a young woman.

The film takes place on Mars, where Reza, Ilsa and their young daughter Remmy live on a remote, barren homestead. One morning they find the word "LEAVE" written on their window, and soon afterwards bandits attack the farm. Reza is killed. Jerry, one of the attackers, survives and takes over the homestead. He asks Ilsa and Remmy for thirty days to prove himself and earn their trust. As the weeks pass, Ilsa seems to warm to him, but at the end of the thirty days she tries to shoot him. The gun Jerry deliberately left within reach turns out to be empty, and Jerry kills Ilsa in the struggle that follows.

Remmy, now alone with the man who destroyed her family, becomes withdrawn and resentful. She spends her time with Steve, a pet-like utility robot she found in a storage unit. Exploring the farm, she learns that it lies inside a large force-field bubble that keeps the air breathable, so the bandits must have come from outside or from another protected settlement. Years go by. Remmy grows into a young woman who barely speaks to Jerry. When he insists that they have a child together and she tries to leave, he stops her, ties her up and attempts to rape her. Steve intervenes, striking Jerry in the neck with its drill, and Remmy frees herself and kills him. Finally free but alone, Remmy decides to set out into the unknown Martian landscape, leaving Steve to look after the farm.

Critics described the film as a stark, minimalist science fiction western, an intimate drama about survival, power and trust. IFC Midnight acquired the American distribution rights in April 2021. Settlers premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on June 18, 2021, and was released in the United States on July 23, 2021. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said the film was serious to a fault but that viewers looking for a non-sensational take on space colonization might find it a rewarding voyage.

documents.title: Rise of the Mummy
documents.tagline: Evil has been unearthed.
documents.overview: A group of archaeology students awaken an ancient mummy. After being trapped in a time loop, the only way they can escape, is to defeat the mummy. As the body count rises, it seems the Mummy has to collect the souls of those who woke him to be able to walk the earth - for good.
documents.plot:
Rise of the Mummy, also known as Mummy Resurgence, is a 2021 British low-budget horror film directed by Antonia Johnstone from a screenplay by Shannon Holiday. A sequel to The Mummy Reborn (2019), it was made by Jagged Edge Productions, one of the companies of the prolific producer Scott Jeffrey, and stars Abi Casson Thompson, Megan Purvis, Stephanie Lodge, Amanda-Jade Tyler, Arthur Boan, Mya Brown, Barbara Dabson and Johnstone herself. Johnstone, who had previously appeared as an actress in the producer's The Leprechaun's Game, also handled make-up and costumes. The film was released on video on demand in the United States in early 2021, followed by a British release on 3 April 2021, and runs about 90 minutes.

A prologue shows a group of people being chased through a forest by the mummy before performing a ritual that stops the creature and the "time loop" its awakening has created; the soldiers involved kill everyone connected with the incident. Some months later the British military hands the now dormant mummy to a university, where a group of archaeology students and their lecturer study it and learn about mummification and the creature's mysterious origins. When someone tries to steal the mummy's necklace, it rises again and begins stalking and killing those trapped inside the building. Its victims return as possessed servants who hunt down the survivors, and no one can escape, because time has frozen and anyone leaving one room finds themselves back where they started. The mummy needs to collect the souls of those who woke it in order to walk the earth for good, but the heroine discovers that it has only 24 hours to do so, and the survivors must stay alive until sunrise.

Phil Wheat of Nerdly found that the camp humour of the first film had been toned down in favour of a more traditional British mummy picture, but felt the film ended with a whimper as the survivors simply run out the clock, while leaving room for a third instalment. Don Anelli of Don's World of Horror and Exploitation called it enjoyable if flawed, praising the time-loop conceit, the practical, jerky-moving mummy and the creepy possessed followers, but finding the first half, dominated by classroom lessons on mummification, sluggish. One commenter also noted that the supposed university was evidently filmed in a secondary school.

documents.title: Safer at Home
documents.tagline: Isolation is a killer.
documents.overview: Two years into the pandemic, a group of friends throw an online party with a night of games, drinking and drugs. After taking an ecstasy pill, things go terribly wrong and the safety of their home becomes more terrifying than the raging chaos outside.
documents.plot:
Safer at Home is a 2020 American romantic comedy film directed by Chris Renz and written by Chris Renz and Brian Duffield. The movie was released on Netflix in 2021.

The story revolves around Mike (played by Mike Epps), a man who has been living with his wife, Beth (played by Kristin Davis), for over 20 years. They have two children together but are now empty nesters. After Beth's mother passes away, she leaves behind a large inheritance that includes a house in the countryside.

Mike and Beth decide to leave their city life behind and move to the country to start a new chapter in their lives. However, things take an unexpected turn when they discover that the house is infested with raccoons. The couple must navigate this challenge while also dealing with their own relationship issues and learning to adapt to their new life together.

As Mike tries to find ways to evict the raccoons from the house, he begins to reconnect with Beth on a deeper level. They start to rekindle their romance and rediscover the things that brought them together in the first place. Along the way, they also learn valuable lessons about communication, trust, and compromise.

Throughout the movie, Mike's character undergoes significant development as he learns to let go of his insecurities and become more confident in himself. He also becomes more patient and understanding, which helps him to better connect with Beth.

The ending of the movie is heartwarming and uplifting, as Mike and Beth finally find a sense of peace and happiness together. They learn to appreciate the simple things in life and find joy in each other's company once again.

Overall, Safer at Home is a charming romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and personal growth. The movie features strong performances from its leads, Mike Epps and Kristin Davis, and offers plenty of laughs and heartwarming moments along the way.

documents.title: Cop Secret
documents.tagline: To solve this crime, they'll need to break all the rules
documents.overview: When Bússi, Iceland's toughest cop, is forced to work with a new partner to solve a series of bank robberies, the pressure to close the case as soon as possible proves too much for him.
documents.plot:
Cop Secret, released in Iceland as Leynilögga, is a 2021 Icelandic action comedy directed by Hannes Þór Halldórsson, who wrote it with Nína Pedersen and Sverrir Þór Sverrisson. Expanded from a mock trailer that Auðunn Blöndal, Halldórsson and Sverrisson made for television in 2011, it stars Blöndal as Bússi and Egill Einarsson as Hörður, with Björn Hlynur Haraldsson as Rikki and Steinunn Ólína Þorsteinsdóttir as police chief Þorgerður.

Böðvar "Bússi" Böðvarsson, Reykjavík's toughest rule-breaking cop, is investigating a string of bank robberies in which nothing seems to be stolen. Chasing a motorcyclist from the latest heist through the city and a shopping mall, to the dismay of his by-the-book partner, Klemenz, he crosses paths with his rival Hörður Bess of neighboring Garðabær, a pansexual millionaire and former male model who speaks fifteen languages. Bússi, who is in denial about his sexuality and drifting from his girlfriend, Lilja, is drawn to Hörður as the two foil a robbery together and capture the motorcyclist, Stefanía, whose only clue is a vague warning about an upcoming women's football match between Iceland and England. After a drunken kiss, Þorgerður assigns them as partners when Klemenz asks to be reassigned.

They trace the gang to Rikki Ferrari, a former model who vanished after an explosion and who addresses his henchmen only in dubbed English, and a burned USB drive leads them to a virus designed to crash Iceland's security systems. Bússi breaks up with Lilja, accepts that he is gay and spends the night with Hörður, but Rikki blackmails him with photographs into handing in his badge. While the entire police force guards the stadium, where Rikki has planted a bomb, his gang uses the virus to rob the national gold reserves. Bússi stows away on their getaway truck, reunites with Hörður, whose brother is being held hostage, and discovers that Klemenz was the inside man. After escaping a German torturer, Bússi declares his love for Hörður; Klemenz dives in front of a bullet fired by Rikki, Bússi blows up Rikki's speedboat, and the bomb is defused seconds before Iceland wins the match. The two departments are merged, and the couple later raise a child together.

The film premiered in competition at the Locarno Film Festival in August 2021 and opened in Iceland that October, finishing second at the local box office for the year behind No Time to Die. It earned 84% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Dreamcatcher
documents.tagline: Get ready for a killer night out.
documents.overview: The film centers on two estranged sisters who, along with their friends, become entrenched in a 48 hour whirlwind of violence after a traumatic experience at an underground music festival.
documents.plot: The film centers on two estranged sisters who, along with their friends, become entrenched in a 48 hour whirlwind of violence after a traumatic experience at an underground music festival.

documents.title: The Tiger Rising
documents.tagline: Let your imagination run wild.
documents.overview: When 12-year-old Rob Horton discovers a caged tiger in the woods near his home, his imagination runs wild and life begins to change in the most unexpected ways. With the help of a wise and mysterious maid, Willie May  and the stubborn new girl in school, he must navigate through childhood memories, heartache, and wondrous adventures.
documents.plot:
The Tiger Rising is a 2022 American family drama film written and directed by Ray Giarratana, based on Kate DiCamillo's 2001 novel of the same name. Christian Convery stars as a grieving twelve-year-old boy, with Madalen Mills, Sam Trammell, Katharine McPhee, Dennis Quaid and Queen Latifah. It was released in cinemas on January 21, 2022, and on digital platforms in early February.

Rob Horton has recently moved with his father, Robert, to the Kentucky Star, a run-down motel in the small town of Lister, Florida, six months after his mother Caroline died of cancer. His father works for the motel's harsh owner, Beauchamp, and refuses to let Rob speak of his mother. Quiet and withdrawn, Rob keeps his feelings locked inside an imaginary suitcase, and suffers from an itchy rash on his legs. One morning, walking through the woods before school, he comes upon a real tiger locked in a cage.

On the school bus, where he is tormented by the Threemonger brothers, Rob meets Sistine Bailey, a fierce, angry newcomer from Philadelphia who insists her father will soon come to take her away. When the class laughs at her name, Rob reveals that he knows all about Michelangelo's paintings in the Sistine Chapel, something his mother taught him along with drawing and wood carving. The principal sends Rob home until his rash clears, fearing it is contagious, and he spends his days doing chores at the motel, where the kind housekeeper Willie May suggests that his rash comes from sorrow he holds inside.

Rob shows Sistine the tiger, and around her he begins to open up. Beauchamp, who owns the animal and is afraid of it, pays Rob to feed it and gives him the keys to the cage. Sistine insists the tiger must be set free, while Willie May warns that this would be impossible. Rob finally gives in and the two children release it into the woods, but moments later a shot rings out: in a struggle with the armed Beauchamp, Robert has accidentally killed the tiger.

Devastated, Rob attacks his father, shouting that he wishes he had died instead of his mother, and makes him say Caroline's name aloud. Father and son embrace and finally grieve together, and Rob's rash begins to fade. Sistine too accepts that her father is not coming and that her life is now in Lister. The film received poor reviews, with a 17% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Sentinelle
documents.overview: Transferred home after a traumatizing combat mission, a highly trained French soldier uses her lethal skills to hunt down the man who hurt her sister.
documents.plot:
Sentinelle is a 2021 French action thriller film directed by Julien Leclercq, who wrote it with Matthieu Serveau. It stars Olga Kurylenko as Klara, a French soldier traumatized by her service in the Middle East who seeks revenge after her sister is raped and left in a coma, with Marilyn Lima as her sister, Tania, Michel Nabokoff as the Russian tycoon Leonid Kadnikov and Carole Weyers as the police captain Catherine Muller.

Klara serves in Syria as an interpreter for the French Army's Opération Chammal. After a suspected terrorist is detained, she watches his young son detonate explosives hidden on his body at his father's command. Suffering from trauma and migraines, she is transferred home to Nice, where she moves in with her mother and Tania and joins the soldiers patrolling the streets under Opération Sentinelle. On duty she is impulsively violent, and when her painkillers run out she buys street drugs. After a night out, during which Tania leaves a nightclub with a group of Russians, Klara learns that her sister has been raped and beaten into a coma. From the club's security footage she identifies the man Tania left with: Captain Muller names him as Yvan Kadnikov, son of an influential Russian tycoon. Both father and son hold diplomatic passports and immunity, placing them beyond easy reach.

Refusing to wait for justice, Klara confronts Yvan at the nightclub, where he denies touching Tania and his friends throw her out. She then breaks into Leonid's villa at Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat but is captured, and Leonid boasts that it was he who raped Tania, since his son is gay, before ordering his guards to drown her. Klara fights her way out. Tania wakes from her coma but refuses to press charges, and when an assassin sent by Leonid attempts to kill her in hospital, Klara catches and beats the woman. Stealing weapons from her garrison's armory, Klara storms Leonid's hideout, kills his bodyguards and throws him over a banister, then kills Yvan after he stabs her, escaping as police arrive. Leonid survives the fall, but three months later Klara, disguised as a hotel hostess, stabs him to death in his Dubai suite. Returning secretly to Nice, she sees from a distance that Tania has recovered, and walks away as a fugitive.

Filmed over 35 days in late 2019 in Brussels, Nice and Casablanca, the film had its post-production interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Rotten Tomatoes reported 70% approval from ten critics, with reviewers calling it lean but illogical.

documents.title: Rubikon
documents.tagline: Take a deep breath. It is your last.
documents.overview: The company soldier Hannah and the scientists Gavin and Dimitri are researching an algae project on board the Rubikon space station, which is supposed to permanently supply humanity with oxygen and food. But suddenly the earth disappears below them in a brown, toxic fog and all contact is broken off - are they the last survivors of humanity? Should they initiate the safe station, dare the return flight and thereby risk their lives?
documents.plot:
Rubikon is a 2022 Austrian English-language science fiction thriller directed by Magdalena Lauritsch, who co-wrote the screenplay with Jessica Lind. Produced by Samsara Filmproduktion and Graf Film, it stars Julia Franz Richter, Mark Ivanir and George Blagden, with Nicholas Monu, Jonas Emilian Gerzabek and Daniela Kong.

In 2056, the environment has collapsed, nation states have given way to corporations with private armies, and only the rich can afford homes with clean air. Aboard the space station Rubikon, owned by the Nibra corporation, the scientist Dimitri Krylov has developed edible algae that produce oxygen. The corporate soldier Hannah Wagner arrives with Gavin Abbott, a chemist and heir to a powerful family, on a secret mission to bring the algae back to Earth. The rest of the crew, including Dimitri's son, departs for home but loses contact and burns up in the atmosphere amid debris created by eco-activists. Soon after, Hannah, Gavin and Dimitri watch as a brown toxic cloud engulfs the whole planet and all contact is lost.

Dimitri explains that the station's algae-based life support can sustain the three of them, but would fail if one of them died. Hannah discovers she is pregnant by Gavin, since her mandatory sterilization chip stopped working when the link to Earth went dead. When contact is restored, around three hundred corporate leaders and their families hiding in an underground bunker beg the crew to bring the algae down and save them. Hannah and Gavin want to return, but Dimitri sabotages their landing module, which explodes after they escape. Hannah then reveals that she was to send the algae culture down on an unmanned cargo shuttle, and the pair adapt it to carry people, until Hannah learns that the leaders sacrificed the soldiers who escorted them to the bunker and halts the launch. Gavin kills himself, believing that the others cannot survive alone and will have to return, but Dimitri admits he invented that danger to stop Gavin's earlier suicide attempt. Years later, Hannah's daughter picks up a radio signal revealing that some people have survived in southern camps.

Shot in a Vienna studio in late 2020, the film was presented at Karlovy Vary, opened the Kitzbühel festival and reached Austrian cinemas on 16 September 2022. Critics praised its visuals and production design but found it slow. It won Austrian Film Awards for production design and sound.

documents.title: Phobias
documents.tagline: What do you fear?
documents.overview: Five dangerous patients, suffering from extreme phobias at a government testing facility, are put to the ultimate test under the supervision of a crazed doctor and his quest to weaponize fear.
documents.plot: Five dangerous patients, suffering from extreme phobias at a government testing facility, are put to the ultimate test under the supervision of a crazed doctor and his quest to weaponize fear.

documents.title: Happening
documents.overview: Annie, a bright young student, is facing an unwanted pregnancy in 1960s France, where abortion is illegal.
documents.plot: France, 1963. Anne is a bright young student with a promising future ahead of her. But when she falls pregnant, she sees the opportunity to finish her studies and escape the constraints of her social background disappearing. With her final exams fast approaching and her belly growing, Anne resolves to act, even if she has to confront shame and pain, even if she must risk prison to do so.

documents.title: Catherine Called Birdy
documents.tagline: Don't call me lady.
documents.overview: A teenage girl in Medieval England navigates life and tries to avoid the arranged marriages her father maps out for her.
documents.plot:
Catherine Called Birdy is a 2022 medieval coming-of-age comedy written for the screen, co-produced and directed by Lena Dunham, adapted from Karen Cushman's 1994 novel of the same name. Bella Ramsey stars as the title character, alongside Billie Piper, Andrew Scott, Lesley Sharp and Joe Alwyn. It premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released by Amazon Studios, streaming on Prime Video from October 7.

In 13th-century Lincolnshire, fourteen-year-old Catherine, known as Birdy, lives with her father Lord Rollo, her mother Lady Aislinn and her brother Robert, while another brother, Edward, is a monk. Headstrong and mischievous, she spends her days causing trouble with her nurse Morwenna and her peasant friend Perkin, and records everything in her diary. When the indulgent but feckless Rollo learns that the family is nearly bankrupt, he resolves to restore its fortunes by marrying Birdy to a wealthy suitor, and her first period makes the search urgent. Unwilling to give up her freedom, Birdy sabotages one prospective husband after another with outlandish antics.

Birdy's dashing Uncle George, on whom she has a crush, returns from the Crusades, but she catches him kissing her friend Aelis, and George breaks both their hearts by marrying a rich widow, Ethelfritha. When Aislinn becomes pregnant again, Birdy fears for her mother's life. A new suitor arrives, the much older Sir Henry Murgaw, whom Birdy nicknames Shaggy Beard; her attempts to repel him only intrigue him, and he gives her a purse of money to spend once she agrees to marry him. Learning that Robert loves Aelis but cannot afford her bride price, Birdy gives him the money.

Birdy runs away to Uncle George's household, where she discovers that his adventures were far less romantic than she imagined, and she realises she would miss her family too much to flee with Ethelfritha. She returns home to find her mother in a difficult labour, and Rollo helps Aislinn through the birth of twin girls. Resigned to marrying for her family's sake, Birdy tearfully leaves with Shaggy Beard, but Rollo stops the carriage and challenges the suitor to a duel. Despite his poor swordsmanship, Rollo prevails when Shaggy Beard feigns an injury to escape, and the marriage is called off. Birdy vows to preserve whatever freedom she can.

The film was well received, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 88% positive reviews and praising it as a fresh, well-told coming-of-age story.

documents.title: Trust
documents.overview: Set in the glamour of the New York and Paris art scenes, gallery owner Brooke Gatwick and her newscaster husband Owen Shore, face temptation, jealousy, twists and mystery when two seductive newcomers enter their lives.
documents.plot:
Trust is a 2021 American erotic romantic drama directed by Brian DeCubellis, from a screenplay by Kristen Lazarian, K.S. Bruce and DeCubellis based on Lazarian's play Push. Victoria Justice and Matthew Daddario star as a married couple whose relationship is tested by temptation, with Katherine McNamara, Lucien Laviscount and Ronny Chieng in supporting roles. The film uses a non-linear structure, repeatedly doubling back on itself as characters reveal the ruses and deceptions behind earlier scenes. It was released in March 2021.

In New York City, Brooke Gatwick and Owen Shore have been together since high school and are now married. Brooke is preparing to open her own art gallery with an exhibition of paintings by the provocative artist Ansgar Doyle, while Owen works as a television news anchor. The couple have been struggling to start a family, and the pressures of Brooke's new venture add to the tension. Ansgar openly flirts with Brooke and constantly contacts her late at night, irritating Owen. Hoping that a break will help them conceive, Owen secretly buys tickets for a Christmas trip to Paris, but Brooke wants to concentrate on the gallery.

When Brooke notices suspicious text messages on Owen's phone, she begins to suspect that he is cheating. Ansgar tells her that a film director, Damien Light, wants to buy his work and meet them in Paris, and Brooke reluctantly agrees to go, while a frustrated Owen accepts an assignment in Las Vegas for the same dates. Brooke later catches Owen leaving the house in the middle of the night and visiting an address advertised online as a discreet place for lovers. At a bar with his friend Adam, Owen meets Amy, who says she is a journalism student at Columbia and recognizes him from his news program. Owen eventually brings Amy home, where they are interrupted, and as Brooke and Owen each face temptation, the film rewinds to reveal how much of what happened was planned, and the couple must decide whether their marriage can survive the lies they have told each other.

On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of 50 percent based on ten reviews, with an average rating of 6.2 out of 10. Reviewers were divided, with some finding its twisting structure clever and others regarding it as contrived.

documents.title: The Fallout
documents.tagline: Nothing will ever be the same.
documents.overview: In the wake of a school tragedy, Vada, Mia and Quinton form a unique and dynamic bond as they navigate the never linear, often confusing journey to heal in a world that feels forever changed.
documents.plot:
The Fallout is a 2021 American drama film written and directed by Megan Park in her feature directorial debut. Jenna Ortega stars as Vada Cavell, a high school student coping with the emotional aftermath of a shooting at her school. Maddie Ziegler, Niles Fitch, Will Ropp, Julie Bowen, John Ortiz, Lumi Pollack and Shailene Woodley appear in supporting roles, and the score was composed by Finneas O'Connell. The film premiered at South by Southwest in March 2021, where it won awards, and was released on HBO Max by New Line Cinema in January 2022.

Vada leaves class to go to the restroom after her younger sister Amelia calls her about getting her first period. While she is there, a gunman opens fire in the school. Vada hides in a stall with Mia, a popular dancer and social media influencer she barely knows, and they are soon joined by Quinton, whose brother is killed in the attack. The shooting leaves many students dead and changes all three survivors.

In the weeks that follow, Vada withdraws from her parents, her sister and her best friend Nick, who throws himself into gun-control activism, and instead spends more and more time with Mia, with whom she shares an intense, unspoken understanding. Unable to return to the bathroom where she hid and overwhelmed by sudden panic at ordinary sounds, she experiments with drugs and alcohol to numb herself, and her relationship with Mia grows romantic. She reaches out to Quinton, who is grieving his brother in his own way, and her attempts to find comfort sometimes push people further away. Sessions with a therapist, Anna, offer some help, as do moments of reconciliation with her family, including a heartfelt conversation in which Amelia admits her fear that Vada blamed her for the phone call that day. The film follows Vada's uneven, nonlinear path through trauma, emphasizing that recovery does not follow a neat timeline.

The Fallout received positive reviews from critics, who praised Park's sensitive direction and screenplay, its realistic depiction of trauma among teenagers and especially Ortega's performance, which many considered a breakthrough. The film won the Grand Jury Award and Audience Award for narrative feature at South by Southwest.

documents.title: Green Snake
documents.original_title: 白蛇 II: 青蛇劫起
documents.tagline: Dependence arises from the previous life.
documents.overview: While trying to free her sister from Fahai's clutches, Xiao Qing winds up in a dystopian city and meets a mysterious man who can't recall his past life.
documents.plot:
Green Snake, known in China as White Snake 2: The Tribulation of the Green Snake, is a 2021 Chinese adult animated fantasy film directed by Amp Wong and produced by Light Chaser Animation together with Alibaba Pictures, Tianjin Maoyan Weiying Culture Media and Bilibili. It is the sequel to the 2019 animated film White Snake, and like its predecessor it is inspired by the Chinese folktale Legend of the White Snake, one of the country's best-known traditional stories. Tang Xiaoxi voices the green snake Verta, with Zhang Fuzheng, Wei Chao, Zhao Mingzhou and Zheng Xiaopu among the voice cast. The film was released in China in July 2021.

In the traditional legend, the white snake spirit Bai Suzhen falls in love with a mortal, while her companion, the green snake Xiaoqing, stands loyally by her side against the monk Fahai, who considers their union a violation of the natural order. Green Snake shifts the focus to the younger sister. At the start of the film, Verta tries and fails to save her elder sister Blanca, the white snake, from imprisonment beneath Leifeng Pagoda by the demon-slaying monk Fahai. In her desperate attempt, she is cast into Shura City, a bleak and violent realm resembling a modern metropolis, where lost souls who cling to obsession and resentment are trapped.

Stripped of her demonic powers, Verta must survive in this chaotic world of warring factions, monsters and sudden cataclysms in which the landscape is periodically torn apart. She encounters a mysterious masked man who repeatedly saves her life, and a range of other strange inhabitants, some of them allies and others enemies. Driven by her determination to escape and rescue Blanca, Verta must overcome her own anger and desire for vengeance while uncovering the truth about the masked stranger and about the cycle of attachment and suffering that binds the inhabitants of Shura City.

The film reinterprets the classic tale through a darker and more action-oriented lens, combining Buddhist ideas of karma and reincarnation with a dystopian, cyberpunk-inspired setting, and it was noted for its ambitious, detailed computer animation and large-scale action sequences.

Green Snake performed strongly at the Chinese box office, earning about 200 million yuan, roughly 31 million US dollars, in its first three days of release, and it was later made available to international audiences through streaming.

documents.title: Wheel of Fortune and Fantasy
documents.overview: An unexpected love triangle, a seduction trap, and a random encounter are the three episodes, told in three movements to depict three female characters and trace the trajectories between their choices and regrets.
documents.plot:
Wheel of Fortune and Fantasy, released in Japan as Gūzen to Sōzō ("Chance and Imagination"), is a 2021 Japanese romantic drama anthology written and directed by Ryusuke Hamaguchi. Its three stories of coincidence and missed connections are led by Kotone Furukawa, Katsuki Mori and Fusako Urabe, with Hyunri, Ayumu Nakajima, Kiyohiko Shibukawa, Shouma Kai and Aoba Kawai.

In "Magic (or Something Less Assuring)", model Meiko (Furukawa) listens in a taxi as her best friend, Tsugumi, gushes about a magical first meeting with a man. Realizing he is her own ex-boyfriend, Kazuaki, Meiko confronts him at his office, and their heated exchange ends in an embrace before she runs off. Days later Kazuaki passes the café where the two women sit; Meiko imagines exposing their past and forcing him to choose, but in reality she quietly excuses herself and leaves the couple to plan their date.

In "Door Wide Open", student Sasaki begs French professor Segawa not to fail him, but is refused. When Segawa later wins the Akutagawa Prize, Sasaki pressures his lover Nao (Mori), a married mother, into a honey trap. In Segawa's office, with the door left open at his insistence, Nao reads an erotic passage from his novel aloud and asks provocative questions, but the unmoved professor draws her into a sincere conversation. She admits she was recording, and he asks for the file; mistyping his address, she sends it to a university administrator, and the scandal ends Segawa's career and her marriage. Years later she meets Sasaki, now an unrepentant editor, on a bus, kisses him and steps off.

In "Once Again", set after a computer virus has made people abandon digital technology, Natsuko (Urabe) attends her girls' high school reunion and recognizes no one. At a train station she spots a woman she believes is a long-lost classmate and goes home with her, before both realize they have mistaken each other. The host, Aya, offers to play Natsuko's first love so she can voice feelings she never resolved, and Natsuko in turn plays the classmate Aya admired, letting her confess the emptiness behind her apparently perfect life. As they part, Aya remembers her classmate's name and the women embrace.

The film won the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the 71st Berlin International Film Festival in March 2021 and opened in Japan that December. It earned 99% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 86.

documents.title: I'm Your Man
documents.tagline: 93% of women want one, she doesn't.
documents.overview: Alma is a scientist at Berlin's famous Pergamon Museum. In order to obtain research funds for her studies, she accepts an offer to participate in an extraordinary experiment. For three weeks, she must live with a humanoid robot with artificial intelligence designed to allow it to morph into that of her ideal life partner. Enter Tom, a machine in human form, created to make her happy.
documents.plot: Alma is a scientist coerced into participating in an extraordinary study in order to obtain research funds for her work. For three weeks, she has to live with a humanoid robot tailored to her character and needs, whose artificial intelligence is designed to be the perfect life partner for her. Enter Tom, a machine in human form in a class of its own, created solely to make her happy.

documents.title: Gaia
documents.tagline: She will transform us
documents.overview: A park ranger takes shelter with two survivalists after an attack by mysterious creatures in a primordial forest.
documents.plot:
Gaia is a South African horror thriller of 2021 produced and directed by Jaco Bouwer from a screenplay by Tertius Kapp, an eco-horror tale set deep in an ancient forest. Monique Rockman stars as Gabi, a forestry worker, with Carel Nel as the survivalist Barend, Alex van Dyk as his son Stefan and Anthony Oseyemi as Gabi's colleague Winston.

Gabi and Winston, employees of the national forestry service, are travelling by river through the Tsitsikamma forest when she loses the drone she is piloting. Heading into the trees alone to recover it, she steps into a trap and a wooden stake pierces her foot. Limping deeper into the forest as night falls under a strange red glow, she shelters in a wooden house, where its occupants, the Afrikaner survivalists Barend and Stefan, who set the trap, tend her wound. Winston, searching for her after hearing her scream, is hunted by strange creatures and overrun by a fast-growing fungus. Gabi grows close to Stefan, but she dreams of fungi sprouting from her body and then finds patches on her skin.

Barend, once a plant pathologist, explains that he withdrew to the forest after his wife Lily died of bone cancer thirteen years earlier, that Stefan was conceived in this house during their honeymoon, and that he has met God in the woods. When the creatures break in, they prove to be people consumed by the fungus, which feeds on eyes, mouths and lungs and spreads through spores; Barend reveres the vast organism at its heart, older than humanity, and makes offerings to the tree where it lives. Gabi and Barend find Winston covered in fungi and begging to die, and he impales himself on an arrow. Stefan secretly gives Gabi one of the sacred mushrooms and shows her his mother, transformed into a living tree still wearing her wedding ring. Barend rants that humanity has doomed the world, persuades Stefan to stay when Gabi tries to take him to the city, and prepares to sacrifice his son, but Gabi returns and in the struggle Stefan stabs his father in the spine. Barend is later seen with fungus growing from his back, offering his blood to the organism. Eventually Gabi too is overtaken by the fungus and begs Stefan to kill her, which he apparently does. Stefan then goes to the city and eats a meal, and the leftovers are swiftly covered with fungus.

Shot in the Garden Route region, Gaia premiered at South by Southwest in March 2021 and was released by Decal that June. Critics praised its chilling visuals, giving it 84% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Offseason
documents.tagline: Something is off on this island.
