documents.overview: Upon receiving a mysterious letter that her mother's grave has been vandalized, Marie travels to the desolate island town where she's buried. Just as she arrives, the island closes for the season, leaving Marie trapped in a nightmare.
documents.plot:
Offseason is a 2021 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Mickey Keating. It stars Jocelin Donahue, Joe Swanberg, Richard Brake and Melora Walters, with Jeremy Gardner and April Linscott in supporting roles. Keating began developing the story in 2018 after reading William Faulkner's "A Rose for Emily" and Shirley Jackson's "The Summer People", and shot it with cinematographer Mac Fisken in and around New Smyrna Beach, Florida, wrapping in February 2020. The film premiered at South by Southwest on 17 March 2021, also played at Sitges, and was released by RLJE Films on video on demand and in limited theatres on 11 March 2022.

Marie Aldrich (Donahue) receives a mysterious letter from a cemetery caretaker urging her to come at once, because the grave of her famous, mentally troubled mother Ava (Walters) has been vandalised. With her boyfriend George (Swanberg) she drives to Lone Palm Beach, the remote island town where Ava grew up and is buried, even though her mother had insisted that not even her ashes should return there. The keeper of the island's only drawbridge (Brake) warns them that the town is closing for the off-season and that the bridge will soon be raised until spring, but lets them through. Marie finds Ava's headstone broken in half, while the fog-bound, nearly deserted town is populated by off-kilter locals, among them a florist, Miss Emily (Linscott), who studies her with glassy eyes, and a man known only as the Fisherman (Gardner). Roads seem to loop back on themselves, the couple are cut off once the bridge goes up, and white-eyed figures begin closing in. Divided into chapters by title cards, the story has Marie weighing her mother's ravings about a pact with an aquatic deity against the dangers around her, as she uncovers a generational curse and a Lovecraftian deity demanding sacrifices from the townspeople.

Critics praised the atmosphere more than the story. Rotten Tomatoes counted a 68% approval rating from 65 reviews, its consensus crediting strong performances by Donahue and Walters, while Metacritic's score of 55 indicated mixed reviews. Tomris Laffly of Variety found it thinly conceived but full of genuinely spine-tingling images and sounds, Slashfilm likened its subtle creeps to John Carpenter's The Fog, and Dread Central singled out Brake's unhinged performance, whereas RogerEbert.com and The A.V. Club found it derivative and aimless.

documents.title: Army of Thieves
documents.tagline: Before Vegas, one locksmith became a legend.
documents.overview: A mysterious woman recruits bank teller Ludwig Dieter to lead a group of aspiring thieves on a top-secret heist during the early stages of the zombie apocalypse.
documents.plot:
Army of Thieves is a 2021 heist film directed by Chris McKay and written by Chris McKay and Adam Sztykiel. The movie takes place in an alternate universe where the events of Deadpool 2 occurred, but with some key differences.

The story follows Dieter Deitz (played by Daniel Radcliffe), a young thief who works for a gang led by Lacey (played by Natasha Lyonne). However, after being betrayed and left for dead by his partner, Dieter sets out on a solo mission to steal the world's largest diamond, known as the "Heart of Europe," which is currently in transit from Berlin to Amsterdam.

Dieter's plan involves infiltrating the armored transport vehicle carrying the diamond, but he soon discovers that it's being escorted by an elite team of mercenaries led by the ruthless and cunning Lacey. As Dieter navigates the complex web of thieves and con artists, he must use his wits and cunning to stay one step ahead of his enemies.

Along the way, Dieter meets a mysterious woman named Kate (played by Lucy Fry), who claims to be an expert in safe-cracking and helps him on his mission. As they work together, Dieter begins to question his own morals and loyalties, particularly when he discovers that Lacey's true intentions for the diamond are far more sinister than he initially thought.

As the stakes grow higher, Dieter finds himself in a cat-and-mouse game with Lacey and her team, with the fate of the diamond and the world hanging in the balance. In the end, Dieter must use all his skills and resources to outwit his enemies and claim the Heart of Europe for himself.

Throughout the movie, Radcliffe delivers a standout performance as Dieter, bringing a sense of vulnerability and humor to the role. The supporting cast is equally impressive, with Lyonne and Fry delivering memorable performances as the ruthless and cunning Lacey and Kate.

Overall, Army of Thieves is a fun and action-packed heist film that explores themes of loyalty, morality, and redemption. With its witty dialogue, clever plot twists, and standout performances, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Bantú Mama
documents.tagline: A contemporary tale about a different kind of re-encounter between Africa and the Caribbean.
documents.overview: A French woman of African descent manages to escape after being arrested in the Dominican Republic. She finds shelter in the most dangerous district of Santo Domingo, where she is taken in by a group of children. By becoming their protégée and maternal figure, she will see her destiny change inexorably.
documents.plot:
Bantú Mama is a 2021 Dominican drama directed by Ivan Herrera from a screenplay he wrote with its star, Clarisse Albrecht. Produced by Herrera, Albrecht, Franmiris Lombert and Nicolas LaMadrid through Point Barre in association with Aurora Dominicana and Basecamp Studio, it was filmed in the Dominican Republic, France and Senegal. Albrecht plays Emma, with Scarlet Reyes as T.I.N.A., Arturo Perez as $hulo and Euris Javiel as Cuki, along with Donis Taveras. The dialogue is in Spanish and French, and the film runs 77 minutes.

Emma, a French woman of African descent, finds welcome peace and color on a trip to the Dominican Republic, far from her gray life in France. Just as she is about to fly home, however, she is arrested for drug trafficking. After tense police interrogations, a fortuitous car accident allows her to escape, and she seeks refuge in one of the most dangerous districts of Santo Domingo. There she is taken in by three siblings who live on their own, since their mother is dead and their father is in prison. Only the youngest, Cuki, retains a childlike whimsy, while his sister T.I.N.A. and brother $hulo have hardened themselves to survive on the streets and keep their father's illicit business going. Hiding in their makeshift household, Emma longs to return home, but as Cuki grows ever more attached to her she becomes their protégée and a maternal figure, and the four form a family built on joy and hope amid the dangers outside. The children are curious about her Bantu heritage and the African diaspora, and she gleefully demonstrates the Maasai jumps Cuki once saw on television, as her destiny changes in unexpected ways.

Bantú Mama premiered at South by Southwest on 16 March 2021, the first Dominican feature selected by the festival. It was chosen as the Dominican Republic's submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film, and Array acquired distribution rights for several English-speaking territories before releasing it on Netflix on 17 November 2022. Critics praised its lyricism. In Variety, Manuel Betancourt called it a quiet achievement and a dreamy treatise on motherhood and motherlands, admiring Sebastián Cabrera Chelin's affectionate cinematography, which he compared to Barry Jenkins's work, and its refusal of drug-mule clichés. Other reviewers lauded the child performances but found the circumstances of Emma's escape and discovery somewhat contrived.

documents.title: Ride or Die
documents.overview: Rei helps the woman she's been in love with for years escape her abusive husband. While on the run, their feelings for each other catch fire.
documents.plot:
Ride or Die (Japanese: 彼女, Kanojo, meaning both "she" and "girlfriend") is a 2021 Japanese romantic thriller directed by Ryūichi Hiroki and written by Nami Kikkawa for Netflix, adapted from Ching Nakamura's adult manga Gunjō. The screenplay departs freely from its source, recasting the story as a road movie and giving names to the two heroines, who are anonymous in the manga. Kiko Mizuhara stars as Rei Nagasawa and Honami Sato as Nanae Shinoda, with Yōko Maki as Rei's lover Mika, Shunsuke Tanaka and Anne Suzuki as Rei's brother Masato and his wife Yu, and Shinya Niiro as Nanae's husband Kotaro; Sara Minami and Yui Uemura play the women as schoolgirls.

The film opens with Rei, glamorous and assured, picking up a man in an elegant bar and going home with him to his high-rise apartment, where they have sex beneath his wedding photograph; she then kills him. The man, it emerges, is Nanae's husband. Rei is an independently wealthy plastic surgeon and a lesbian living semi-openly with Mika when, out of the blue, she receives a call from Nanae, a classmate from their elite girls' school whom she has not seen in ten years and has loved since adolescence. Seeing the bruises left by Kotaro's abuse, Rei needs only a slight push from Nanae to resolve to kill him, abandoning her partner and career.

Nanae is nonetheless shocked that Rei took her literally, and insists that she is straight, yet she does not abandon her friend, and the two flee together in a red BMW convertible. On the road their first euphoria gives way to strain as they realise they cannot escape, and they talk more and more seriously of dying together. Encounters with controlling men, including a presumptuous taxi driver and Rei's well-meaning but overbearing brother, punctuate the journey, while flashbacks trace their history back to the art class where they first met. Hiding at Masato's home, they plan to surrender but run away once more for a final night by the sea, where they confront their conflicting feelings and finally make love. The next morning Rei calls the police from a payphone, so that she can claim sole responsibility for the killing and shield Nanae.

The film was shot in sequence during the COVID-19 pandemic and released worldwide on Netflix on 15 April 2021. Variety praised its sensual, female-driven storytelling as far ahead of typical Japanese LGBTQ films and Mizuhara's committed performance, while finding its 142 minutes drawn out; reviews were generally favorable.

documents.title: Secret Magic Control Agency
documents.overview: The Secret Magic Control Agency sends its two best agents, Hansel and Gretel, to fight against the witch of the Gingerbread House.
documents.plot:
Secret Magic Control Agency, also known as Hansel & Gretel, is a 2021 English-language Russian animated spy comedy film directed by Aleksey Tsitsilin and produced by Wizart Animation, CTB Film Company and QED International. A loose adaptation of the Brothers Grimm fairy tale, it features the voices of Sylvana Joyce as Gretel, Nicholas Corda as Hansel, Erica Schroeder as the witch Ilvira, Marc Thompson as the King and Mary O'Brady as Baba Yaga.

In a fantasy kingdom where all magic is regulated by the Secret Magic Control Agency, the king is kidnapped by sentient food enchanted with black magic. To keep the public calm, the prime minister keeps the abduction secret and leaves the investigation to the agency, which pairs its agent Gretel with her estranged brother Hansel, a con artist who poses as a wizard. Their search leads them to a pastry shop whose pantry is full of living baked goods and a potion room holding enchanted vanilla extract, but after a chase with a dog-shaped cookie destroys the shop, the siblings are turned into children. With no one at the agency believing them, they turn to Baba Yaga, a witch said to eat children, and learn that the extract came from the swamplands. There the Lake Witch mistakes them for spies of Ilvira, the witch of the gingerbread house and the king's former cook, and spares them only because her daughter recognizes Gretel as the agent who once saved her. Freeing Ilvira's captured henchmen, they are led to her lair and discover her plan: to make the king fall in love with her through magic so she can become queen and claim the power of the crown. Ilvira locks the siblings in an oven, where they finally have it out. Gretel resents Hansel's swindling, while he resents her putting her career before family, and he reveals that he gave up an honest life to pay for her education, passing the money off as a royal scholarship. Reconciled, they escape, make an antidote and race to the royal wedding, but the marriage is sealed before they can stop it. Using a gadget Hansel stole from the agency, they escape being baked into cookies, recover the antidote and drop Ilvira into her own batter. Gretel is named Best Agent, Hansel declines a magic license as he cannot do real magic, and the siblings agree to work together.

Released in Russia by Sony on 18 March 2021, the film debuted on Netflix a week later and topped its global viewing charts in its first week, receiving generally positive reviews for its animation.

documents.title: Firebird
documents.tagline: Risk everything, trust no one.
documents.overview: At the height of the Cold War, a troubled soldier forms a forbidden love triangle with a daring fighter pilot and his female comrade amid the dangerous surroundings of a Soviet Air Force Base.
documents.plot:
Firebird is a 2021 romantic war drama film directed by Peeter Rebane in his feature debut and based on Sergey Fetisov's memoir The Story of Roman. Set in the Soviet Air Force during the Cold War, it tells the true story of a forbidden love affair between a private and a fighter pilot. Tom Prior, who co-wrote and co-produced the film with Rebane, stars as Sergey, with Oleg Zagorodnii as Roman and Diana Pozharskaya as Luisa.

Sergey, a young private in the Soviet Air Force, has only a few weeks of military service left. He and his friends chafe under their commanders' strict control, he seems to be drifting into a romance with Luisa, the base commander's secretary, and his hobby of photography is barely tolerated by his superiors. When a new fighter pilot, Roman, arrives at the base, Sergey is assigned to assist him, and an intense attraction grows between them despite the threat of prison that hangs over homosexual relationships under the Soviet regime. They consummate their relationship and are nearly discovered by a KGB agent, and Roman urges Sergey to study acting in Moscow rather than go back to his family's farm. A year after leaving the service and starting a new life in the theater, Sergey is invited to Roman's wedding to Luisa, where he can barely hide his disappointment and his enduring love. Roman and Luisa have a son, but the marriage is a facade, and Roman still longs for Sergey. Leaving his wife and child, ostensibly to study in Moscow, he secretly rents an apartment with Sergey, and the two live together happily and travel together. When Luisa and the boy visit Moscow for Christmas, however, she discovers the truth, and her fury forces the men apart. Roman is later sent to fight in the Soviet–Afghan War and is killed. Sergey visits Luisa, who is still bitter toward him, and returns to his acting life in Moscow; he is last seen watching a performance of Stravinsky's ballet The Firebird, to which Roman had introduced him.

Rebane received Fetisov's memoir in 2014, and he and Prior interviewed the author before his death in 2017. Firebird premiered at the BFI Flare festival in London on 17 March 2021 and won an honorable mention for Best First Feature at San Francisco's Frameline festival. Reviews were mixed, with 57% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49.

documents.title: The Ravine
documents.tagline: A story of evil, hope, and the afterlife.
documents.overview: This true story begins on a weekday morning in a peaceful suburb of Akron, Ohio, the town awakens to discover that Rachel Turner and her son, Evan, have been brutally murdered during the night. A short while later, Danny Turner is found in his car at the bottom of a ravine, after having taken his own life.
documents.plot: This true story begins on a weekday morning in a peaceful suburb of Akron, Ohio, the town awakens to discover that Rachel Turner and her son, Evan, have been brutally murdered during the night. A short while later, Danny Turner is found in his car at the bottom of a ravine, after having taken his own life.

documents.title: Summer Ghost
documents.overview: An urban legend says that lighting fireworks at an abandoned airfield will beckon the “summer ghost,” a spirit that can answer any question. Three teenagers, Tomoya, Aoi, and Ryo, each have their own reason to show up one day. When a ghost named Ayane appears, she reveals she is only visible to those “who are about to touch their death.” Compelled by the ghost and her message, Tomoya begins regularly visiting the airfield to uncover the true purpose of her visits.
documents.plot:
Summer Ghost (Japanese: Samā Gōsuto) is a 2021 Japanese animated fantasy drama short film, about 40 minutes long. It was directed by the animator and illustrator Loundraw in his directorial debut and produced by his company Flat Studio, with a script by Hirotaka Adachi. In Japanese, Chiaki Kobayashi voices Tomoya Sugisaki, Miyuri Shimabukuro voices Aoi Harukawa, Nobunaga Shimazaki voices Ryō Kobayashi and Rina Kawaei voices Ayane Satō.

Tomoya, Aoi and Ryō are high school students who have met through social media. They decide to investigate a rumor about a "Summer Ghost" that appears at night on an abandoned airfield whenever fireworks are lit. The ghost really does appear: a young woman named Ayane. She tells them she can only be seen by people who have already reached out toward death. Flashbacks show why each of them qualifies. Tomoya has lost hope because his controlling mother is forcing him to give up his love of art and concentrate on his studies. Aoi is suicidal after being bullied. Ryō has a terminal illness and less than a year to live.

Tomoya returns alone and learns how Ayane died. She was struck by a car, and the driver hid her body in a suitcase and buried it to avoid punishment. Tomoya becomes obsessed with finding her remains so that her mother can have closure. When Aoi happens to see him searching, she and Ryō join the effort, and together the three eventually succeed. A year later, in the summer, Tomoya and Aoi return to the abandoned airfield. Their friendship has given Tomoya the courage to stand up to his mother and pursue his artistic ambitions, and Aoi has found the confidence to confront her bullies. Ryō, however, has died in the hospital with the two of them at his side, and they have come to the airfield to meet him again, this time as a ghost.

Loundraw announced the project in June 2020 as part of the Project Common multimedia project and unveiled it in February 2021. Akira Kosemura, Itoko Toma, Guiano and Hideya Kojima composed the music. Avex Pictures released the film in Japanese theaters on November 12, 2021, the same day as its international premiere at the Leeds International Film Festival in England. GKIDS screened it in North America in 2022, including a premiere at Anime Expo on July 3, and released it on Blu-ray and digital platforms with Shout! Factory on November 1, 2022. A Japanese limited-edition Blu-ray, released in March 2022, included an 80-minute documentary about the production.

documents.title: Stutz
documents.tagline: Meet a different kind of therapist.
documents.overview: In candid conversations with actor Jonah Hill, leading psychiatrist Phil Stutz explores his early life experiences and unique, visual model of therapy.
documents.plot:
Stutz is a 2022 American documentary film produced and directed by actor Jonah Hill about his own therapist, the psychiatrist Phil Stutz. Built around a series of conversations between the two men, it explores Stutz's life and career, his doctor-patient relationships and the practical approach to therapy he has developed, alongside Hill's own struggles with self-esteem. Shot mostly in black and white by Christopher Blauvelt, it began streaming on Netflix on 14 November 2022. In August 2022 Hill announced that he would not promote any of his upcoming work, including Stutz, in order to protect himself from anxiety attacks.

The film first presents itself as a single therapy session in which Hill, flipping the usual roles, questions Stutz about his methods. Using Stutz's voice as a guide and line animation that recreates the diagrams he sketches on index cards for his patients, it lays out his "tools", visualisation exercises with names such as Life Force, The Shadow, Part X, The Snapshot and The Grateful Flow, intended as practical ways of working through sadness and anxiety. Roughly 25 minutes in, Hill reveals the artifice: the office is a replica set with a green-screen background, the conversations have been filmed over many months, and even his long hair is a wig worn for continuity. The image briefly breaks into colour before returning to monochrome, and from then on the film becomes more openly about its own making and about the bond between the two men.

Hill guides the viewer through Stutz's biography, from his Manhattan childhood, when people already seemed drawn to confide their problems in him, to his decades-long life with Parkinson's disease and a relationship he describes as on and off for 40 years. Hill speaks about the insecurity and body image issues that followed him through his success, at one point holding up a large cardboard cutout of his 14-year-old self. The two discover that they share the loss of a brother who died young; Hill's brother Jordan Feldstein died in 2017.

The film was very well received. Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 96% approval rating from 23 reviews and Metacritic's score of 76 indicated generally favourable reviews. The New York Times praised how it navigates vulnerability, insight and artistry, the Los Angeles Times found it simple but emotionally affecting, and IndieWire likened it to a cross between The Rehearsal and a self-help tape.

documents.title: Project Wolf Hunting
documents.tagline: A floating hell with no escape.
documents.overview: During transport from the Philippines to South Korea, a group of dangerous criminals unites to stage a coordinated escape attempt. As the jailbreak escalates into a bloody, all-out riot, the fugitives and their allies from the outside exact a brutal terror campaign against the special agents onboard the ship.
documents.plot:
Project Wolf Hunting, released in Korea as Neukdae Sanyang ("Wolf Hunt"), is a 2022 South Korean science fiction action horror film directed by Kim Hong-sun. Seo In-guk plays the tattooed gang leader Park Jong-doo and Jang Dong-yoon the withdrawn prisoner Lee Do-il, with Park Ho-san, Jung So-min, Sung Dong-il and Choi Gwi-hwa. Almost all of its blood-soaked action takes place aboard the cargo ship Frontier Titan as it carries fugitives from the Philippines to Korea.

After an earlier attempt to fly Korean criminals home from the Philippines ends in a deadly bombing at the airport, the authorities move a new group of fugitives by sea under heavy police guard. Jong-doo, a violent and sadistic killer, earns an early beating from the tough detective Lee Seok-woo, but he has planned an escape in advance. Meanwhile a doctor repeatedly slips down into the hold with medical supplies, where a secret passenger is kept in a drugged sleep: Alpha, a genetically engineered super soldier being smuggled to Korea, linked to a pharmaceutical company's anti-aging research.

Once the ship is at sea, Jong-doo slips his handcuffs, accomplices kill the guards and seize the bridge to cut off communications, and the freed prisoners launch a bloody riot against their police escorts. The carnage wakes Alpha, a near-invulnerable berserker of enormous strength, who begins tearing through criminals and officers alike. A small band of survivors, including the determined officer Lee Da-yeon and Do-il, joins forces against him. Do-il proves to be far more than a prisoner: he was himself an unwilling subject of the company's experiments, which gave him superhuman abilities, and after he tried to escape, its agents killed his wife and took his son. He has quietly followed Alpha's trail to find the people responsible, and the film's final stretch pits him against Alpha and the company's other enhanced soldiers.

The film premiered in the Midnight Madness section of the Toronto International Film Festival on September 16, 2022, and opened in South Korea on September 21. It grossed about $3.9 million worldwide on a budget of roughly $9.1 million. It earned 88% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 53, critics relishing its extreme gore and spectacle while faulting thin characters and a convoluted backstory.

documents.title: Get the Goat
documents.overview: Bruceuilis, a policeman from the countryside, is assigned to rescue Celestina, a goat considered heritage of his small city, and travels to São Paulo. There, he meets police clerk Trindade, who decides to venture out into the field, even though it is not his specialty.
documents.plot:
Get the Goat (Portuguese: Cabras da Peste) is a 2021 Brazilian buddy-cop action comedy directed by Vitor Brandt, who wrote it with Denis Nielsen, and produced by Halder Gomes's company Glaz Entretenimento for Netflix. Edmilson Filho, a comedian and former martial-arts champion, stars as the rural policeman Bruceuilis Nonato, opposite Matheus Nachtergaele as the São Paulo officer Renato Trindade, with Letícia Lima as Captain Priscila, the singer Falcão as the congressman Zeca Brito, Leandro Ramos, Evelyn Castro, Juliano Cazarré, Valéria Vitoriano, Eyrio Okura as Ping Li and Victor Allen.

Bruceuilis, named after Bruce Willis, is a fearless, hyper-motivated cop in a sleepy small town where crime rarely goes beyond the theft of an electric fan, yet he treats every call as a matter of life and death, to the constant annoyance of his superiors. Trindade, by contrast, belongs to a special unit in São Paulo but is slight, timid and terrified of getting hurt, and he prefers office work to the street. Both men end up demoted, Trindade after being blamed for a colleague's death.

Fate unites them through a goat. Bruceuilis is entrusted with Celestina, a goat regarded as the heritage of his town and the mascot of an upcoming festival, but she escapes and is taken by a drug dealer who uses her as a courier. Sent to São Paulo to recover her after yet another fiasco, Bruceuilis teams up with Trindade and persuades him to leave his desk for a case that could transform both their careers: stopping the trafficker Ping Li, who is negotiating a huge narcotics deal with a mysterious kingpin known only as Luva Branca (White Glove). Bickering and badly matched, the pair clash with dangerous criminals and with the officers officially in charge of the investigation, and their inexperience turns every step into slapstick as they try to prove themselves heroes.

Netflix released the film on 18 March 2021. Its fights mix boxing, kung fu and karate, with choreography by Gomes and Filho, and its 1980s-style score includes "Calor do Cão," a forró parody of "The Heat Is On" by Gaby Amarantos and Júnior Groovador. Reviewers called it a bright, silly and good-natured comedy that touches on drug trafficking, corrupt politicians and the spread of guns with a light touch; The Upcoming judged it no first-class comedy but an enjoyable diversion.

documents.title: Luckiest Girl Alive
documents.overview: A successful woman in New York City finds her life upended when she is forced to confront a dark truth that threatens to unravel her meticulously crafted life.
documents.plot:
In 2015, TifAni "Ani" FaNelli, a respected New York women's magazine columnist, appears to have a picture-perfect life. As she prepares to marry her fiancé Luke Harrison, Ani meets with Aaron Wickersham, a documentary director who is making a short film about a 1999 school shooting she survived as a teenager. Aaron tells Ani that a former classmate, Dean Barton, who became a successful writer and advocate for gun control, has agreed to take part, though Ani declines to be involved.
Luke informs Ani that his firm has offered him a job opportunity in London and suggests that she should take a MFA program there to allow her to write. Ani agrees, despite having hopes of someday working at The New York Times. They later have dinner with a couple Luke knows; the husband turns out to be Ani's former teacher, Andrew Larson.
In a series of flashbacks, TifAni is seen joining the prestigious Brentley School, where she quickly befriends a clique of popular students, including Dean and his friends Liam and Peyton. It is revealed that TifAni was gang-raped at a school dance after party by all three boys while intoxicated. TifAni shared what happened with the headmaster and Mr. Larson, who encourages TifAni to tell her eccentric mother, Dina, but TifAni refuses. However, TifAni tells her friend Arthur who had been continuously bullied by the three boys.
Ani's past slowly begins to haunt her, affecting her relationship with Luke. Aaron tells Ani that Dean wants to meet with her to apologize on camera; she agrees under the condition that Aaron keeps them separate until she is ready. Meanwhile, Ani struggles with her strained relationship with Dina, who claims she always found Ani difficult and alludes that she is only marrying Luke for money.
At the documentary filming, Dean shows up unexpectedly early, causing Ani to flee in a panic. Further flashbacks reveal that Ani has been struggling to deal with the trauma of what happened. The school shooting takes place not long after, perpetrated by Arthur and his friend Ben. Peyton and Liam are killed, and Dean is wounded severely and left unable to walk. Prior to the funerals, Dean started a rumor that TifAni slept with him and helped Arthur and Ben plan the shooting. Supposedly, this was because he did not want to be her boyfriend. TifAni is consequently shunned by everyone, including Dina, who blames TifAni for causing her own rape by drinking and partying excessively.
At a presentation of his new book, Ani meets with Dean, who shows little remorse for what he did and threatens to recapitulate his story of her participation in the shooting if she tells anyone. However, after being pressed by her during the conversation, Dean admits he raped her. Having secretly recorded their conversation, Ani leaves and decides to share her experience after encouragement from her boss and ends up writing a piece for The New York Times.

documents.title: The Outfit
documents.tagline: Everyone has something up their sleeve.
documents.overview: Leonard is an English tailor who used to craft suits on London’s world-famous Savile Row. After a personal tragedy, he’s ended up in Chicago, operating a small tailor shop in a rough part of town where he makes beautiful clothes for the only people around who can afford them: a family of vicious gangsters.
documents.plot:
The Outfit is a 2022 American crime thriller and the directing debut of Graham Moore, who wrote it with Johnathan McClain. Mark Rylance stars as an English tailor whose shop serves Chicago gangsters, with Zoey Deutch, Johnny Flynn, Dylan O'Brien, Nikki Amuka-Bird and Simon Russell Beale in supporting roles.

In Chicago in 1956, Leonard Burling, a bespoke cutter who once had a shop on Savile Row, works in a neighborhood run by Irish mob boss Roy Boyle. Roy's son Richie and his enforcer Francis use the shop as a drop for cash and messages, and Leonard puts up with it because the gangsters are his best customers. His receptionist, Mable, with whom he shares a complicated bond, is Richie's girlfriend. One night Francis brings in Richie, shot in a clash with the rival LaFontaine family, and forces Leonard to stitch him up and hide a case holding an FBI surveillance tape. The tape came from the Outfit, the national crime syndicate, and Richie believes it will expose the informant in their ranks.

Over one long night, Leonard sets the gangsters against each other. He nudges Richie to suspect Francis, who then kills Richie. Leonard and Francis lie to Roy about where his son is, and Leonard distracts the boss with the story of how his wife and daughter died in a fire in London. Mable is the real informant, and Leonard persuades Francis to betray Roy to LaFontaine so he can take over. When LaFontaine turns out to be a woman, Violet, Leonard warns her and her guards shoot Francis. She leaves with a tape that is a decoy. Leonard reveals that he planted fake Outfit messages and that the real FBI recorder in the shop captured the whole night. He gives the recording to Mable to deliver and tells her to keep the money. As he sets fire to the shop, a wounded Francis attacks him. Leonard admits he was once an enforcer himself, whose old gang killed his family, and kills Francis with his shears before walking away in a new suit.

The film was shot in March and April 2021 at the Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre near London, with cinematographer Dick Pope, editor William Goldenberg and composer Alexandre Desplat. It premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival on February 14, 2022, and Focus Features released it on March 18. It opened to $1.5 million but was widely praised. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it an old-school thriller made by a solid story and Rylance's "tightly tailored performance".

documents.title: Hollywood Stargirl
documents.tagline: Find your place among the stars.
documents.overview: When Stargirl's mother is hired as the costume designer on a movie, they relocate to L.A., where Stargirl quickly becomes involved with an eclectic assortment of characters.
documents.plot: When Stargirl's mother is hired as the costume designer on a movie, they relocate to L.A., where Stargirl quickly becomes involved with an eclectic assortment of characters.

documents.title: Carter
documents.tagline: No memory. One mission.
documents.overview: Carter, who awakens two months into a deadly pandemic originating from the DMZ that has already devastated US and North Korea. He who has no recollections of his past finds a mysterious device in his head, and a lethal bomb in his mouth. A voice in his ears gives him orders to avoid getting killed and he's thrown into a mysterious operation while the CIA and North Korean coup chase him close.
documents.plot:
Carter is a South Korean action thriller of 2022 directed by Jung Byung-gil, who wrote it with Jung Byeong-sik, and released by Netflix. Joo Won stars as the title character, with Lee Sung-jae as the North Korean general Kim Jong-hyuk, Jeong So-ri as Han Jung-hee, Kim Bo-min as the girl Jung Ha-na, Jung Jae-young as her father, Dr Jung Byung-ho, and Camilla Belle and Mike Colter in supporting roles.

A pandemic has broken out from the Korean Demilitarized Zone, spreading a virus that turns its victims violent and zombie-like and ravaging both the United States and North Korea. In a Seoul motel, a man wakes in a bloodied bed with a cross-shaped scar on the back of his head and no memory. CIA agents burst in demanding to know where Dr Jung is, and a woman's voice in an earpiece tells him that his name is Carter and that he must obey her to survive. Following her orders, he escapes and fights his way through a bathhouse full of gangsters. The voice belongs to Jung-hee, an official of North Korea's ruling party, which has joined with the South to develop a cure. Dr Jung has cured his own daughter Ha-na, whose antibodies are the key to a vaccine, but the girl vanished on the way north, apparently seized by the CIA. Carter's mission is to rescue her and deliver her to a North Korean laboratory. He is told he is a South Korean-born naturalised North Korean who volunteered to save his own infected daughter, while the CIA insists he is a former agent called Michael Bane, thought killed in Syria.

After battle upon battle, Carter brings Ha-na to North Korea, only for General Kim to betray him and Jung-hee and launch a coup. Escaping execution, Carter follows them to a biomedical facility where Ha-na has been reunited with her father. There he learns that Jung-hee is his wife, shoots Kim, and finds their infected daughter Yoon-hee, whom Dr Jung sedates with an antidote. Fleeing by jeep toward a Chinese train carrying the infected to Dandong, Jung-hee and the doctor restore Carter's memories through an implanted device: he accepted the mission in exchange for his family's freedom, and had his memories blocked so he could not betray the North. They board the train and Yoon-hee wakes, seemingly cured, but a bomb explodes as the train crosses a bridge, sending it toward a fall.

Filmed in Osong in 2021, Carter drew praise for its live-action stunts and Joo Won's performance but criticism for its story, scoring 35% on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Dancing on Glass
documents.overview: When immense pressure threatens a ballerina in a new lead role, she and another dancer escape into a friendship that isolates them from the real world.
documents.plot:
Dancing on Glass (Las niñas de cristal) is a 2022 Spanish psychological drama directed by Jota Linares, his third feature, from a screenplay he wrote with Jorge Naranjo. Produced for Netflix by Federation Spain, the new Spanish branch of Federation Entertainment, it stars María Pedraza and Paula Losada as two young dancers drawn together by the pressures of a national ballet company, with Mona Martínez, Marta Hazas, Olivia Baglivi, Ana Wagener and Iria del Río in supporting roles.

After María, the star of the National Classical Ballet, takes her own life, Irene Solís is chosen to replace her in the lead of the company's biggest production, Giselle. The decision devastates Ruth, who believed she was the obvious successor, and Irene becomes the target of the jealousy and cruelty of the other dancers, struggling under the impossible expectations of the company's tyrannical director, Norma, and her own family while battling bulimia. Her dancing begins to suffer until she befriends Aurora Ruiz, a lonely newcomer dominated by her mother, a former ballerina who pushes her daughter to succeed in her place, and who hides a large birthmark on her face behind her hair. Aurora teaches Irene her trick of disappearing into an imaginary world while she dances, and Irene finds that she performs at her best when Aurora is in the room. Isolated from everyone else and crushed by the sacrifices that success in dance demands, the two young women lean on one another as rehearsals intensify, and their relationship becomes ever closer and more obsessive, a joint flight forward in search of themselves, while Norma watches their friendship with suspicion. As opening night approaches, it becomes clear that, as the story began with the death of one of their own, the premiere will be a matter of life and death.

Filming took place in Madrid between February and April 2021. The film was presented in the official selection of the 25th Málaga Film Festival on March 25, 2022, and released worldwide on Netflix on April 8, 2022. In El País, Javier Ocaña praised Pedraza's commendable physical and artistic work and the solidity of Martínez and Baglivi, calling it a more than worthwhile film from a director perhaps overwhelmed by ambition in an excessively harsh ending. Decider's Jade Budowski admired Pedraza's mesmerizing dancing and her chemistry with Losada but found the story too familiar from films such as Black Swan and the running time overlong.

documents.title: Ray Donovan: The Movie
documents.tagline: You can't outrun your legacy.
documents.overview: A showdown decades in the making brings the Donovan family legacy full circle. As the events that made Ray who he is today finally come to light, the Donovans find themselves drawn back to Boston to face the past. Each of them struggles to overcome their violent upbringing, but destiny dies hard, and only their fierce love for each other keeps them in the fight.
documents.plot:
Ray Donovan: The Movie is a 2022 American made-for-television crime drama written by David Hollander and its star, Liev Schreiber, and directed by Hollander. It serves as the conclusion of the Showtime series Ray Donovan, which the network had cancelled unexpectedly after its seventh season ended in January 2020, leaving many storylines unresolved; following fan petitions, Schreiber announced that more of the story would be told. Schreiber plays the Los Angeles fixer Ray Donovan, with Jon Voight as his father Mickey, Eddie Marsan, Dash Mihok and Pooch Hall as his brothers Terry, Bunchy and Daryll, Kerris Dorsey as his daughter Bridget, Katherine Moennig, Kerry Condon as Molly Sullivan, Josh Hamilton, and Alan Alda as the therapist Dr. Arthur Amiot. Bill Heck and Chris Gray play Mickey and Ray as younger men.

The film picks up after the season seven finale, in which Bridget's husband Smitty was killed during a deal that went wrong after being set up by Mickey. Mickey flees to Boston carrying stock certificates belonging to the Sullivan family, and Ray goes after him. Early on, a beaten Ray is seen telling Dr. Amiot that he killed his father, and the story builds toward how that statement came to be. After Smitty's funeral the brothers gather for a drunken wake.

Interwoven with the present are flashbacks to Boston decades earlier, when a Hollywood film shooting in the city made the young Mickey a local celebrity and taught the young Ray the skills that would later make him a fixer. Returning to these places, Ray confronts his own role in his father's downfall, including the murder he framed Mickey for, which sent him to prison for some twenty years. In the present, Molly Sullivan shoots Ray in the stomach after learning of her father's death. Wounded, Ray finds Mickey and apologizes to him, but Bridget, determined that the family's cycle of violence must end, shoots her grandfather dead, and Ray takes responsibility for the killing. The film closes ambiguously, with Ray drifting off in an ambulance as an underwater image shows him rising to the surface; the creators said whether he survives was left to viewers.

The film premiered on Showtime on 14 January 2022. Critics generally considered it a satisfying send-off, praising the flashback sequences and Heck's performance, though some found the treatment of supporting characters rushed. It received an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Television Movie.

documents.title: Werewolves Within
documents.tagline: A whodunnit with teeth.
documents.overview: When a proposed pipeline creates hostilities between residents of a small town, a newly-arrived forest ranger must keep the peace after a snowstorm confines the townspeople to an old lodge. But when a mysterious creature begins terrorizing the group, their worst tendencies and prejudices rise to the surface, and it is up to the ranger to keep the residents alive, both from each other and the monster which plagues them.
documents.plot:
Werewolves Within is a 2021 American comedy horror film directed by Josh Ruben and written by Josh Ruben and Michael Siller. The movie takes place in the fictional town of Red Rock, where a group of friends reunite for a wedding.

The story begins with Sam (Sam Richardson), a successful businessman who has lost his way after a painful divorce. He returns to his hometown of Red Rock for his friend's wedding, hoping to reconnect with old friends and find some closure. Upon arrival, he discovers that the town is hosting a "Werewolf Hunt" competition, where participants must figure out who among them is a werewolf.

Sam joins forces with his old friend, Emily (Milana Vayntrub), and together they start gathering clues to identify the werewolf. As the competition heats up, Sam finds himself drawn into a web of relationships and alliances that lead him to question everyone's intentions.

As the night wears on, the group discovers that one of their own is indeed a werewolf, but it's not who they expected. The werewolf is revealed to be none other than Emily's fiancé, Mike (Harvey Guillén). However, just as Sam thinks he has solved the mystery, new clues emerge, and the group realizes that there are multiple werewolves in the mix.

The plot thickens as alliances are formed and broken, and the group starts to turn on each other. In a shocking twist, it's revealed that one of the participants is not who they claim to be. The true identity of the imposter is slowly uncovered, leading to a thrilling climax.

As the night reaches its peak, Sam and Emily find themselves in a desperate bid to survive the werewolf attacks and uncover the truth behind the competition. In the end, only two people are left standing: Sam and Mike's best friend, Alex (Sam Leakey).

In a stunning finale, it's revealed that Alex is not who he claims to be either. The true identity of the imposter is finally exposed, leading to a chaotic confrontation between the remaining survivors.

The movie ends with Sam and Emily emerging victorious but shaken by their experience. As they reflect on what happened, they realize that some wounds may never fully heal, and that sometimes, the truth can be more terrifying than fiction.

Werewolves Within is a clever blend of horror and comedy, with a talented ensemble cast bringing depth and humor to the story. The movie's clever plot twists and unexpected turns keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

documents.title: Kimi
documents.tagline: She's not the only one listening.
documents.overview: A tech worker with agoraphobia discovers recorded evidence of a violent crime but is met with resistance when she tries to report it. Seeking justice, she must do the thing she fears the most: she must leave her apartment.
documents.plot:
Kimi is a 2022 American thriller film directed by Steven Soderbergh and written by David Koepp. The movie stars Zoë Kravitz as Richard, a young woman who sets out to find her missing father, John (played by J.K. Simmons), after his disappearance in the Pacific Ocean.

The story begins with Richard's life unraveling. She is struggling to cope with the loss of her mother and feeling disconnected from her father, who she barely knows. When her father goes missing while on a solo sailing trip, Richard sets out to find him, despite her initial reluctance.

As Richard searches for her father, she becomes increasingly obsessed with finding him. She tracks his last known location to a small island in the Pacific, where she hopes to find some clues about his disappearance. Along the way, she encounters various characters who provide her with information and guidance, including a local fisherman (played by Ed Harris) and a mysterious woman (played by Kaitlyn Dever).

As Richard delves deeper into her father's disappearance, she uncovers a complex web of secrets and lies that lead her to question everything she thought she knew about him. Through a series of flashbacks, we see glimpses of Richard's childhood and her relationship with her father, which suggests that he may have been hiding something from her.

As the story unfolds, Richard becomes more and more entangled in a cat-and-mouse game with an unknown adversary who seems to be one step ahead of her. The tension builds as she navigates the treacherous waters of the Pacific, facing numerous challenges and obstacles along the way.

Throughout the film, Soderbergh employs his signature style of non-linear storytelling, jumping back and forth in time to reveal clues about Richard's father's disappearance. The pacing is deliberate and measured, building tension and suspense as the story hurtles towards its climax.

Ultimately, Richard discovers a shocking truth about her father's disappearance that challenges everything she thought she knew about him. In a thrilling finale, she confronts the unknown adversary in a tense showdown that will leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, Kimi is a gripping thriller that explores themes of family, identity, and obsession. With its complex characters, intricate plot, and stunning cinematography, it's a must-see for fans of suspenseful storytelling.

documents.title: A Good Person
documents.tagline: Sometimes we find hope where we least expect it.
documents.overview: Allison's life falls apart following her involvement in a fatal accident. The unlikely relationship she forms with her would-be father-in-law helps her live a life worth living.
documents.plot:
A Good Person is a 2023 American drama film written, directed and produced by Zach Braff. It stars Florence Pugh, Morgan Freeman, Celeste O'Connor, Molly Shannon and Chinaza Uche in the story of a young woman's painful recovery after a fatal accident.

Allison, a young aspiring musician, is engaged to her high school sweetheart, Nathan. The day after their engagement party, she takes her eyes off the road while driving and crashes, killing Nathan's sister Molly and Molly's husband and leaving herself badly injured. A year later, consumed by guilt and depression, Allison lives with her mother, Diane, who tries to rein in her addiction to painkillers. Meanwhile, Nathan's father, Daniel, a former police officer, is raising his orphaned teenage granddaughter, Ryan, who is struggling with the loss of her parents and is bullied at school. After a humiliating encounter with former classmates, Allison joins an addiction recovery group, where she unexpectedly finds Daniel. At a meeting he admits that his drinking once caused blackouts during which he became violent, and that on one occasion he destroyed the hearing in one of Nathan's ears.

An uneasy bond forms between Allison and Daniel, but when Ryan confronts her about her responsibility for her parents' deaths, Allison relapses. Ryan later invites both Allison and Nathan to a concert, where Nathan arrives with his new girlfriend; hurt, Allison follows Ryan to an after-party and relapses again. She cannot stop Ryan from being taken advantage of in a back room, but a drunken Daniel bursts in and threatens the young man with a handgun until Nathan steps in front of the weapon and talks him down. Outside, Daniel tells Allison that he had seen her as a test from God and now considers her a waste. Accepting her role in the crash, Allison checks into rehab. A year later she is writing songs again and reconnecting with Nathan. When Daniel dies, leaving Ryan in their care until she goes to college, Allison finds a letter he left her, explaining his tattoo, "amor fati", meaning to love one's fate, and she and Ryan embrace after the wake.

Braff's project was announced in February 2021, and Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer produced and distributed the film, releasing it in limited theaters on March 24, 2023, before a wide expansion a week later. It grossed $3.1 million. Reviews were mixed, with 57% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 50; critics found it baggy and schmaltzy despite terrific performances.

documents.title: The Pale Blue Eye
documents.tagline: Every heart tells a tale.
documents.overview: A seasoned detective investigates a series of murders at the U.S. Military Academy in West Point in 1830. He is assisted in his investigation by an intelligent and eager young cadet named Edgar Allan Poe, who will go on to become one of America's most influential authors and the originator of the detective genre.
documents.plot: West Point, New York, 1830. When a cadet at the burgeoning military academy is found hanged with his heart cut out, the top brass summons former New York City constable Augustus Landor to investigate. While attempting to solve this grisly mystery, the reluctant detective engages the help of one of the cadets: a strange but brilliant young fellow by the name of Edgar Allan Poe.

documents.title: Senior Year
documents.tagline: High school has changed. But she hasn’t.
documents.overview: A thirty-seven-year-old woman wakes up from a twenty-year coma and returns to the high school where she was once a popular cheerleader to finish her senior year and become prom queen. The main plot is the empowerment of LGBTQ rights and progress through the years.
documents.plot:
Senior Year is a 2022 American comedy film directed by Alex Hardcastle, in his feature debut, from a screenplay by Andrew Knauer, Arthur Pielli and Brandon Scott Jones. Rebel Wilson, who also produced, stars as a woman who wakes from a twenty-year coma and returns to high school, with Angourie Rice playing her teenage self. Mary Holland, Sam Richardson, Zoe Chao, Justin Hartley and Chris Parnell co-star. Netflix released the film on May 13, 2022.

In 1999, after a humiliating birthday party, fourteen-year-old Australian newcomer Stephanie Conway resolves to become one of the popular kids. By 2002 she has remade herself as cheer captain, girlfriend of the popular Blaine, and a frontrunner for prom queen, which she hopes will lead to a charmed life like that of a famous alumna, Deanna Russo. She remains friends with Martha and Seth, who secretly loves her. Her rival Tiffany, Blaine's ex, has her cheer stunt sabotaged at a pep rally, and Stephanie falls into a coma.

She wakes in 2022 at the age of 37. Her father Jim and Martha, now the school principal, help her return to Harding High to finish her senior year, where Seth works as the librarian. Tiffany has married Blaine and moved into Deanna's old mansion, their daughter Bri is a social media star, prom king and queen have been abolished, and cheerleading has become bland and inoffensive. Stephanie wins back popularity online with a racy cheer routine that goes viral, but clashes with Martha, who felt abandoned by her years earlier, while growing closer to Seth.

Tiffany uses Bri's influence to restore the prom crown and plans an exclusive afterparty, so Stephanie throws a rival party at Martha's lake house without asking. At the prom, Bri withdraws so Stephanie wins queen, but Seth is hurt after seeing a drunken Blaine try to kiss her, and Tiffany has the party shut down. Her ride home is driven by an adult Deanna, now divorced and struggling, who warns her not to repeat her mistakes. Stephanie makes peace with Tiffany, publicly apologises, and at graduation finally lands her old cheer move with her friends, kisses Seth and reconciles with Martha.

Critics were largely unimpressed, with a 23% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 47.

documents.title: Ticket to Paradise
documents.tagline: They’re in this together for better or worse.
documents.overview: A divorced couple teams up and travels to Bali to stop their daughter from making the same mistake they think they made 25 years ago.
documents.plot:
Ticket to Paradise is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Ol Parker and starring George Clooney and Julia Roberts as the lead characters.

The movie begins with David (George Clooney) and his wife, Georgia (Julia Roberts), who are divorced but still living together in Bali. They have been married for over 20 years and have two daughters together. However, their marriage has become stale, and they've grown apart. The couple's relationship is put to the test when they discover that their daughter, Lily (Kaitlyn Dever), is getting married to a man named Wes (Maxime Bouttier) who is not her biological father.

David and Georgia decide to team up and stop the wedding, as they believe it would be a mistake for Lily. They embark on a mission to win her back and convince her that she's making a huge error in choosing Wes. Along the way, they must confront their own past mistakes and learn to communicate with each other again.

As David and Georgia navigate their complicated feelings towards each other, they also have to contend with the challenges of modern dating and the changing landscape of relationships. They meet new people, including a charming local woman named Veronica (Hannah E. Gadsby), who becomes a confidant for Georgia.

Throughout the movie, George Clooney and Julia Roberts deliver witty banter and comedic chemistry, making their characters' interactions both humorous and endearing. The film's tone is light-hearted and fun, with plenty of laughs and romantic moments.

As David and Georgia work to win Lily back, they also have to confront their own personal demons. David struggles with feelings of inadequacy and jealousy, while Georgia grapples with her own sense of identity and purpose. Through their journey, the couple learns to communicate more effectively and understand each other's needs.

In the end, David and Georgia succeed in stopping the wedding, but not before Lily has a change of heart and realizes that she's made a mistake by choosing Wes. The movie concludes on a hopeful note, with David and Georgia rekindling their romance and looking forward to a brighter future together.

Overall, Ticket to Paradise is a charming and entertaining romantic comedy that explores the complexities of love, relationships, and personal growth. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and beautiful setting, the film is sure to delight audiences and leave them feeling uplifted and inspired.

documents.title: The Jack in the Box: Awakening
documents.original_title: The Jack in the Box: Awakening
documents.tagline: Once you open the box... you can't escape it.
documents.overview: When a vintage Jack-in-the-box is opened by a dying woman, she enters into a deal with the demon within that would see her illness cured in return for helping it claim six innocent victims.
documents.plot:
The Jack in the Box: Awakening is a 2022 British supernatural horror film written and directed by Lawrence Fowler and produced by Fowler Media. A thematic sequel to Fowler's The Jack in the Box (2019), it shares none of that film's characters or story, with the demon in the box as the only connecting figure. It stars Matt McClure as Edgar Marsdale, Mollie Hindle as Amy, Nicola Wright as Olga Marsdale and James Swanton as the demon Jack, with Michaela Longden as Janet, Jason Farries as Frank and Victor Mellors as Mr Huxley. The film carries the tagline "Once you open the box... you can't escape it."

Olga Marsdale, a wealthy collector of vintage toys, lies bedridden with terminal bone cancer in her country mansion. Aware of its cursed history, she acquires through the dealer Huxley the oldest jack-in-the-box ever discovered, which is said to contain a demon able to grant a wish in exchange for six sacrifices. She rearranges the revolving letters on its top from "JACK" to "LIFE" and turns the crank, and the dial shows that six lives will be needed for her cure. Huxley becomes the first victim, mauled by a three-clawed demonic clown and pulled into the box, which slams shut as the dial counts the death. Olga browbeats her timid son Edgar, who serves as her factotum, into gathering five more sacrifices, and, horrified yet strangely captivated, he overcomes his squeamishness out of desperation to save his mother. Amy, a young woman recently separated from her boyfriend, has just taken a job as the estate's new housemaid hoping for a fresh start, and with fellow staff members Janet and the chef Frank she finds herself confined within the estate's high walls, with no phone signal, as Edgar feeds one victim after another to the box.

The film was released on digital platforms in the United Kingdom on 3 January 2022 and in the United States later that month, and on DVD through 4Digital Media. Reviews were mixed. Phil Hoad of The Guardian found it too beholden to The Conjuring, noting an atmospheric English gothic strain and a disturbing oedipal mother-son relationship but criticizing rote killings and thin supporting characters. HorrorBuzz praised McClure's rounded performance, Longden and Cameron Bryson's camerawork, while finding it formulaic and wishing for more of Olga and Edgar's relationship. Road Rash Reviews gave it three stars, calling it a solid, creepy and well-made clown horror with impressive monster effects despite a few plot holes.

documents.title: Girl in the Basement
documents.overview: Sara is a teen girl who is looking forward to her 18th birthday to move away from her controlling father Don. But before she could even blow out the candles, Don imprisons her in the basement of their home.
documents.plot:
I have information on "Girl in the Basement" (2021). 

"Girl in the Basement" is a psychological thriller television film that premiered on Lifetime in 2021. The movie follows the story of Sarah, a young woman who returns to her childhood home after being away for several years. She discovers that her mother has been living in the basement and claims she's been taking care of herself.

As Sarah tries to reconnect with her mother, she begins to uncover disturbing secrets about their family's past. Her mother reveals that she was involved in a cult-like group when Sarah was younger, and that she had been hiding from the outside world for years.

Sarah becomes increasingly unsettled as she learns more about her mother's past and the reasons behind her isolation. She starts to question everything she thought she knew about her family and their history. As tensions rise between Sarah and her mother, it becomes clear that there is more to the story than meets the eye.

Throughout the film, Sarah struggles with feelings of anger, betrayal, and confusion. Her relationship with her mother deteriorates as she tries to understand why her mother has been keeping such a dark secret from her for so long.

The movie takes a dark turn when it's revealed that Sarah's mother was involved in some sinister activities, including human trafficking and abuse. As the truth comes to light, Sarah is forced to confront the reality of her family's past and the harm that has been done.

Ultimately, "Girl in the Basement" is a gripping thriller that explores themes of trauma, family secrets, and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly the lead actress who brings depth and nuance to the complex character of Sarah.

documents.title: All About Sex
documents.tagline: Love, sex, relationships and everything in between
documents.overview: Three friends in their mid-20s struggle to navigate their professional and personal lives, colliding head on with the messy, hilarious and dreadful growing pangs of adulthood.
documents.plot:
All About Sex, also known as Natural Disasters, is a 2021 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Dakota Gorman in her feature directorial debut. Gorman loosely based the story on her own experiences of battling depression and the anxieties of early adulthood. Produced by Salt & Light Films in association with Warrior Woman Productions, with Nicole Rio and Kelly Bumford as producers, it stars Gorman, Natalee Linez and Emma Deckers, with Dillon Lane, Matt Angel, Chris Costanzo, James Hyde and Parvesh Cheena in supporting roles. Gravitas Ventures acquired the North American rights in January 2021 and Myriad Pictures handled international sales; in the United Kingdom, Signature Entertainment released it digitally on 26 July 2021. The film runs about 75 minutes.

The film follows three best friends in their mid-twenties, Sage (Gorman), Casey (Linez) and Morgan (Deckers), who are caught in the grip of quarter-life crises as they try to balance their careers and their love lives and stumble through the messy, embarrassing and confusing pitfalls of becoming adults. Sage is a talented graphic artist who spends her time complaining in a coffee shop, and the friends talk frankly about sex and lean on one another as each of them stalls on the way to true adulthood. Morgan's extracurricular activities eventually catch up with her, even as she falls in love with Lowick (Angel), a kind and ordinary man. Across the intersecting storylines the women's sexual encounters, from the absurd to the upsetting, serve as a springboard for exploring mental illness and the expectations society places on young people.

Umar Ali of The Upcoming found the film unabashedly crude and frank but said its script balances the ribald jokes with genuine pathos and strong character development; he praised the three leads for carrying the film where the screenplay falters and called it an ambitious, if rough-edged, and thoroughly entertaining exploration of adulthood. Shane A. Bassett of The People's Movies described it as a kind of millennial mumblecore romance that goes nowhere yet remains enlightening, singling out Deckers as the standout and comparing Gorman's potential to that of Greta Gerwig. Other reviewers felt the script was contrived and unfocused.

documents.title: 8-Bit Christmas
documents.tagline: How far would you go to score the ultimate gift?
documents.overview: In suburban Chicago during the late 1980s, ten-year-old Jake Doyle embarks on a herculean quest to get the latest and greatest video game system for Christmas.
documents.plot:
"8-Bit Christmas" is a 2021 American comedy-drama film directed by Brian Levant and written by Chris Columbus, Brian Levant, and Matthew Fogel. The movie stars Josh Gad, Peyton List, and Will Friedle.

The story revolves around Tyler (played by Jacob Tremblay), an 11-year-old boy who lives in Detroit with his mother, Cathy (played by Madeline Zima). On Christmas Eve, Tyler discovers a VHS tape of the 1983 film "Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension" and becomes obsessed with it. He decides to write a letter to Buckaroo Banzai (played by Peter Weller), his favorite character from the movie.

Tyler's mother is initially hesitant about his obsession, but eventually warms up to the idea of him writing to Buckaroo Banzai. With her help, Tyler sends the letter and waits for a response. However, he soon realizes that Buckaroo Banzai is not just a fictional character but also a real person who was a scientist and adventurer in the 1980s.

As Tyler delves deeper into Buckaroo's life, he learns about his adventures and the challenges he faced during the Cold War era. Inspired by Buckaroo's story, Tyler decides to write a screenplay for an original film that combines science fiction and action elements with Christmas themes.

Tyler's mother supports him in his creative endeavors, and together they work on writing the script. However, their efforts are met with skepticism from Cathy's friends and family, who think it's just a silly idea. Undeterred, Tyler continues to write and refine his script, drawing inspiration from Buckaroo Banzai and other classic sci-fi films.

As Christmas Eve approaches, Tyler finally completes his screenplay and sends it to Peter Weller, the actor who played Buckaroo Banzai in the 1983 film. To his surprise, Weller responds with a letter of encouragement and offers to meet with him.

The movie takes a heartwarming turn as Tyler's mother and friends come together to support him on Christmas Eve. They watch a screening of "Buckaroo Banzai" at home, and Tyler finally gets the chance to meet Peter Weller in person.

Throughout the film, there are also flashbacks that show Buckaroo Banzai's adventures during the Cold War era, which serve as an inspiration for Tyler's own creative endeavors. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Tyler having found his passion and purpose through his love of science fiction and adventure films.

Overall, "8-Bit Christmas" is a heartwarming story about the power of imagination, creativity, and perseverance. It celebrates the magic of classic sci-fi films and the impact they can have on young people's lives.

documents.title: Bingo Hell
documents.tagline: Are you feeling lucky?
documents.overview: In the Barrio of Oak Springs live a strong and stubborn group of elderly friends who refuse to be gentrified. Their leader, Lupita, keeps them together as a community, a family. But little did they know, their beloved Bingo hall is about to be sold to a much more powerful force than money itself.
documents.plot:
Bingo Hell is a 2021 American comedy horror film directed by Gigi Saul Guerrero, who wrote the screenplay with Shane McKenzie and Perry Blackshear. The fifth entry in the Welcome to the Blumhouse anthology series, it stars Adriana Barraza as Lupita, an elderly resident of the town of Oak Springs, with L. Scott Caldwell as her friend Dolores, Richard Brake as the sinister Mr. Big, Joshua Caleb Johnson as Dolores's grandson Caleb, Clayton Landey as Morris and Bertila Damas as the hairdresser Yolanda.

Mario, who has just sold the town's bingo hall, comes home in a daze, talks to a picture of his dead wife about the sale and, coaxed by an ominous voice, gorges himself on bingo balls until he chokes to death. The next morning Lupita makes her rounds of Oak Springs, visiting her friend Clarence at his auto repair shop and Yolanda at her salon. Dolores, meanwhile, is angry with her daughter-in-law Raquel for failing to discipline Caleb, a boy who breaks into cars, and she bristles when Lupita compares Caleb to her late son. A bingo night is cut short because Mario has not paid the electricity bill. Soon flyers announce that the hall is under new management, and Lupita and her friends find that it has been turned into a glitzy casino, where Raquel wins ten thousand dollars from the owner, Mr. Big. The next morning Raquel is gone, along with her winnings. After Clarence wins one hundred thousand dollars, he unknowingly drinks motor oil while celebrating and dies after sticking his arm into a car motor. Finding his body and seeing Morris receive a disintegrating stamp on his hand from Mr. Big, Lupita realizes the whole town is being lured into the hall. She heads there with Eric and her shotgun; when Caleb, blaming the place for his mother's disappearance, tries to break in, Eric chases him inside, and Mr. Big kills Eric. When Mr. Big begins crushing Lupita's head against a podium, Caleb shoots him in the back. Lupita destroys the TV, the residents turn on Mr. Big, and Caleb sets fire to the money as they escape, leaving him to burn.

Filmed in New Orleans in early 2021, Bingo Hell premiered at Fantastic Fest on 24 September 2021 and was released by Amazon Studios on 1 October. It holds a 66% Rotten Tomatoes rating, with a consensus describing it as moderately effective, socially conscious horror.

documents.title: The People We Hate at the Wedding
documents.original_title: The People We Hate at the Wedding
documents.tagline: Save the hate.
documents.overview: A dysfunctional family that can't seem to get along and get it together reluctantly reunites for a family wedding. As their many skeletons are wrenched from the closet, it turns out to be just what this singular family needs to reconnect.
documents.plot:
The People We Hate at the Wedding is a 2022 American romantic comedy directed by Claire Scanlon from a screenplay by the Molyneux sisters, based on the 2016 novel of the same name by Grant Ginder. It stars Kristen Bell as Alice, Ben Platt as her brother Paul, Allison Janney as their mother Donna and Cynthia Addai-Robinson as their older half-sister Eloise, with Karan Soni, Dustin Milligan, Tony Goldwyn, Isaach de Bankolé, Jorma Taccone and Julian Ovenden.

Alice and Paul are struggling American siblings who live far from their family. Paul, who works at a rehab center, is anxious about his partner Dominic's wish to open their relationship, while Alice, an executive assistant at an architecture firm, is having an affair with her married boss, Jonathan. Both are estranged from their mother Donna and from Eloise, Donna's daughter from her first marriage to a wealthy French-British playboy named Henrique, who spent her childhood summers with her father in Britain and never truly bonded with her half-siblings.

When Eloise, now wealthy, becomes engaged and invites her American family to her wedding in England, the widowed Donna happily accepts, while Alice and Paul reluctantly agree to go, still resentful of their mother's ties to Henrique and of Eloise's privileged life. Once in England, the trip quickly turns chaotic: Paul's relationship with Dominic unravels, Donna rekindles her romance with her ex-husband, and Alice embarks on a fling with Dennis, a friendly Nebraskan she met on the plane, while hiding her own entanglement. As old grudges, secrets and misunderstandings resurface in the days before the ceremony, the family's simmering conflicts threaten to ruin the wedding, and the siblings must face what really drove them apart.

The film is a comedy about dysfunctional families, sibling rivalry and the misunderstandings that can poison relationships over the years.

The People We Hate at the Wedding was released on Amazon Prime Video on November 18, 2022. It received mostly negative reviews, with 31 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it intriguingly cast but largely laugh-free, and a Metacritic score of 42; The New York Times praised the casting while finding the script uneven.

documents.title: Just Say Yes
documents.overview: Incurable romantic Lotte finds her life upended when her plans for a picture-perfect wedding unravel -- just as her self-absorbed sister gets engaged.
documents.plot:
Just Say Yes is a 2021 Dutch romantic comedy directed by Appie Boudellah and Aram van de Rest and written by Appie Boudellah, Mustapha Boudellah, Marie Kiebert and Maarten van den Broek. Starring Yolanthe Cabau, Huub Smit and Jim Bakkum, it follows a hopelessly romantic television producer whose life unravels just as her sister prepares for the wedding she has always wanted for herself. Netflix released the film on 2 April 2021.

Lotte, 33, produces programmes for the struggling channel Regio Fun, based in the A'DAM Toren, where her boyfriend of five years, Alex, hosts his own talk show. She has long waited in vain for him to propose, and she is working on a pitch she hopes will rescue the station's ratings, while editor-in-chief Fritz brings in Chris, a commercially minded creative whose ideas she dislikes. When Alex claims her pitch as his own, the relationship collapses on live television, and Lotte, having lived with him, moves in with her sister Estelle, a self-absorbed influencer who once supported her but has long been unreliable. Estelle then gets engaged to Lotte's boss John and asks Lotte and her friend Kim to organise the wedding; though stung, Lotte agrees. When presenter Beau fails to show up for a recording, Chris pushes Lotte in front of the camera, and she proves a natural as ratings soar. Uninterested in fame, she nonetheless strikes a bargain with Chris: he will help her win Alex back if she keeps presenting. A makeover brings her plenty of attention, and she and Chris slowly grow closer. Alex, whose own show has been cancelled, abruptly proposes, and Lotte, wrong-footed, gives him another chance. On the eve of Estelle's wedding, however, she discovers that Alex is cheating with Kim and that Estelle knew. Her confrontation with her sister at the ceremony brings the wedding to a halt, but the sisters eventually make peace, Estelle marries John after all, and Chris turns up at the wedding and finally kisses Lotte.

Cabau plays Lotte, with Bakkum as Chris, Smit as Fritz, Noortje Herlaar as Estelle, Juvat Westendorp as Alex, Edwin Jonker as John and Pip Pellens as Kim. The supporting cast includes Winston Post as Beau, Nienke Plas, Josylvio, Kim-Lian van der Meij, Nina Warink, Lisa Michels and Patricia Paay. Released by Netflix, the film draws much of its comedy from behind the scenes of a small Dutch television channel chasing ratings.

documents.title: Sex Appeal
documents.tagline: The only science she doesn't get is chemistry.
documents.overview: Avery, a teenager with a tendency towards perfectionism, enlists her friend Larson to help her prepare for her first time with her long-distance boyfriend.
documents.plot:
Sex Appeal, stylized as SexAPPeal, is a 2022 American teen sex comedy directed by Talia Osteen in her feature debut and written by Tate Hanyok, who also served as an executive producer. Developed by American High for Hulu and produced with LD Entertainment, Nickel City Pictures and Lit Entertainment Group, it stars Mika Abdalla, also in her first feature lead, and Jake Short, with Fortune Feimster, Margaret Cho, Rebecca Henderson, Mason Versaw, Paris Jackson, Artemis Pebdani and Hayden Szeto.

Avery Hansen-White (Abdalla) is a hyper-achieving high school senior with a perfect record, a wall of medals and a full scholarship to MIT, who avoids anything she cannot excel at and has no time for proms. She is raised by three supportive mothers: the nurturing Deb (Feimster), the artist Suze (Cho) and Suze's partner Kim (Henderson). Her long-distance boyfriend Casper (Versaw), whom she met at the previous STEMCon, a science competition nicknamed "nerd prom", hopes they will sleep together for the first time at the upcoming event a month away. Avery finds this logical, but she knows almost nothing about sex. When the competition asks entrants to build an app that solves a problem in their personal lives, she decides to make her own first time perfect her project, interviewing classmates and collecting data. For hands-on research, she recruits her lifelong best friend Larson (Short), a good-natured boy who once let her set him on fire for science and who has long harbored feelings for her. As their experiments progress, Larson understands far better than Avery how emotionally risky the arrangement is, and she gradually realizes that relationships involve less science and more heart. The story is framed by a flash-forward in which Avery freezes on stage at STEMCon.

The project was announced in March 2021, with Cho, Jackson and Henderson joining the cast that April. Filming took place in and around Syracuse, New York, including Syracuse Studios, the village of Liverpool and Onondaga Lake Park. The film premiered on Hulu on 14 January 2022 and was later released internationally on Disney+ and in Latin America on Star+. Reviews were mixed, with 55% on Rotten Tomatoes. Common Sense Media praised its positive message about relationships and diverse cast, Decider recommended it for its empathy and consistent tone despite its uneven humor, and Paste and Screen Rant found the heroine's ignorance of sex implausible and the characters thinly developed, while praising Abdalla.

documents.title: The Requin
documents.tagline: Terror will surface.
documents.overview: A couple on a romantic getaway find themselves stranded at sea when a tropical storm sweeps away their villa. In order to survive, they are forced to fight the elements, while sharks circle below.
documents.plot:
The Requin, released in the United Kingdom as From Below, is a 2022 American horror thriller film written and directed by Le Van Kiet. Its title is an archaic name for the great white shark or requiem shark, taken from the French word for shark. Alicia Silverstone stars as Jaelyn and James Tupper as her husband, Kyle, with Deirdre O'Connell as Anne, Jennifer Mudge as Lizzie and Danny Chung as a fisherman.

Jaelyn and Kyle take a holiday at a beach resort in Vietnam, staying in a bungalow built over the water. Since suffering a stillbirth during a home birth, Jaelyn has become withdrawn and traumatized, keeping in touch with family and friends mainly through social media, and the trip is meant to help her recover.
