On their second night, a violent tropical storm floods the bungalow and tears it from its moorings, sending it drifting out to sea and leaving Kyle with a badly injured leg. Days pass as they wait for rescue. When a ship sails by, their attempt to make a smoke signal sets fire to their shelter, and they are forced onto a floating section of wooden floor. Adrift, Kyle apologizes for leaving Jaelyn alone with her grief, and the couple reconcile, but a great white shark then attacks the raft and bites off Kyle's legs, and he bleeds to death. That night the raft reaches a beach, where Jaelyn drags Kyle's body onto the sand before collapsing. By morning the tide has carried the body back out, and sharks devour it before she can reach it; as she wades back, a shark bites her leg before she drives it away. Walking along the coast, she meets a local fisherman in a round coracle, who stitches her wounds, but while she sleeps he dives to check his fish trap and is killed by the shark. When it attacks the coracle, Jaelyn first wounds it with a handheld outboard motor, but it returns and overturns the boat. As she wraps the anchor rope around herself to keep from sinking, the shark lunges again and bites down on the anchor, whose fluke pierces its brain and kills it. Clinging to the upturned coracle, Jaelyn drifts to a fishing village, where fishermen on the beach spot her.

Shot in Orlando, Florida, at Universal Orlando and Full Sail University, with nearly 1,000 visual effects shots, the film was released to video on demand on 28 January 2022. Reviews were largely negative, with 18% of 17 critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Every Breath You Take
documents.tagline: Such things still happen
documents.overview: A psychiatrist, whose client commits suicide, finds his family life disrupted after introducing her surviving brother to his wife and daughter.
documents.plot:
Every Breath You Take, also known as You Belong to Me, is a 2021 psychological thriller directed by Vaughn Stein from a screenplay by David Murray. Casey Affleck plays psychiatrist Philip Clark, Michelle Monaghan his wife, Grace, and Sam Claflin the stranger who enters their lives, with Veronica Ferres, India Eisley and Emily Alyn Lind in supporting roles.

Philip, Grace and their daughter, Lucy, have drifted apart since the death of the younger child, Evan, in a car accident three years earlier. One of Philip's patients, Daphne Flagg, has escaped an abusive relationship with the help of his therapy and is writing a book about her mental illness. After telling Philip that her best friend, Joan, was killed in a hit-and-run, Daphne is found dead outside her home in an apparent suicide. Philip comforts her distraught, estranged British brother, James, who soon visits the Clark home and is invited to dinner by a sympathetic Grace. Philip orders a copy of a book James has written, Shadow Cast.

James grows close to Grace, who confesses that Philip has never faced his grief, and despite trying to end things she sleeps with him. He files a complaint that gets Philip suspended pending investigation, and he also seduces the troubled Lucy. Later he picks up Grace when her car breaks down, drives erratically and knocks her unconscious, but Philip catches up and rescues her. Told that James has committed himself to a psychiatric facility with auditory hallucinations, Philip visits him and learns that he has read Daphne's notes on her therapy and on Philip's family. When Shadow Cast finally arrives, the author photo reveals that the real James Flagg is someone else: the impostor is Eric Dalton, Daphne's abusive American ex-boyfriend, who killed Joan to break Daphne down and then murdered her when she refused to return, and has targeted Philip for helping her leave. Eric escapes the facility after killing a guard and attacks Lucy at home, and after a violent struggle Grace kills him with the blade of Evan's old ice skate.

The project was announced in 2012 with Rob Reiner attached to direct; Stein replaced Christine Jeffs in December 2019, and filming took place in Vancouver. Vertical Entertainment released it in theaters and on demand on April 2, 2021. Critics were largely negative, with 20% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 32.

documents.title: The Fabelmans
documents.tagline: Capture every moment.
documents.overview: Growing up in post-World War II era Arizona, young Sammy Fabelman aspires to become a filmmaker as he reaches adolescence, but soon discovers a shattering family secret and explores how the power of films can help him see the truth.
documents.plot:
The Fabelmans is a coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Steven Spielberg, released in 2022. The movie is semi-autobiographical, drawing inspiration from Spielberg's own childhood experiences.

The story revolves around Max Fabelman (played by Gabriel LaBelle), an 11-year-old boy who moves to Los Angeles with his family. His father, Jon (played by Paul Dano), is a struggling filmmaker trying to make it big in Hollywood. Max struggles to adjust to the new environment and finds solace in filmmaking.

As Max navigates his new life, he befriends a group of kids at school who share his passion for filmmaking. Together, they create their own short films using an old 8mm camera. Through these experiences, Max learns valuable lessons about friendship, perseverance, and the power of storytelling.

Meanwhile, Max's father is dealing with personal struggles, including a troubled marriage and feelings of inadequacy as a filmmaker. As Max tries to help his father find his creative voice, he also begins to develop his own unique filmmaking style.

Throughout the film, Spielberg weaves in nostalgic references to classic Hollywood films and pays homage to the early days of cinema. The movie's cinematography is stunning, capturing the vibrant colors and textures of 1970s Los Angeles.

The Fabelmans is a heartwarming and poignant exploration of childhood creativity, family dynamics, and the power of storytelling. Spielberg's direction is masterful, balancing humor, drama, and nostalgia to create a film that feels both deeply personal and universally relatable.

Overall, The Fabelmans is a beautiful tribute to the art of filmmaking and the magic of childhood imagination. It's a movie that will leave audiences smiling, laughing, and maybe even shedding a tear or two.

documents.title: Cocaine Bear
documents.tagline: Get in line.
documents.overview: An oddball group of cops, criminals, tourists, and teens converge in a Georgia forest where a 500-pound black bear goes on a murderous rampage after unintentionally ingesting cocaine.
documents.plot:
Cocaine Bear is a dark comedy film that delves into the consequences of addiction and the exploitation of nature for human gain. The movie follows the story of a bear that ingests a large amount of cocaine, leading to a series of chaotic events.

At its core, Cocaine Bear explores the theme of the destructive power of addiction. The bear's transformation from a gentle creature to a violent force is a powerful metaphor for the devastating effects of substance abuse on individuals and society as a whole. The film also critiques the exploitation of nature for human purposes, highlighting the consequences of treating animals as mere commodities.

Furthermore, Cocaine Bear touches on themes of class struggle and social inequality. The movie portrays a world where the wealthy and powerful exploit the natural resources and creatures for their own gain, while the poor and marginalized are left to suffer the consequences. This commentary on class struggle is often humorous and satirical, but also serves as a scathing critique of societal ills.

Ultimately, Cocaine Bear is a film that uses humor and absurdity to comment on some very serious issues. It's a wild ride that will keep you laughing and on the edge of your seat, while also making you think about the consequences of our actions on the world around us.

documents.title: Alcarràs
documents.tagline: For every family, there is a season.
documents.overview: For as long as they can remember, the Solé family has spent every summer picking the peaches in their orchard in Alcarràs, a small village in Catalonia. But this year’s crop may well be their last, as they face eviction. The new plans for the land, which include cutting down the peach trees and installing solar panels, cause a rift in this large, tight-knit family. For the first time, they face an uncertain future and risk losing more than their orchard.
documents.plot:
Alcarràs is a 2022 Catalan-language drama film directed by Carla Simón, a Spanish-Italian co-production. Shot in the style of neorealism with a cast of non-professional actors from the region led by Jordi Pujol Dolcet and Anna Otín, it portrays a farming family during what may be their last peach harvest in the village of Alcarràs, in the Lleida area of Catalonia.

For generations, the Solé family has grown peaches on land that was granted to them by the wealthy Pinyol family in gratitude for help during the Spanish Civil War. The arrangement was sealed only by a handshake, and no deed was ever signed. When the Pinyols' heir decides to uproot the orchard and cover the land with solar panels, the Solés are left with no legal claim and must face the end of their way of life once the summer harvest is over.

The film follows the extended family through the hot summer months as they pick fruit and work the farm. Quimet, the stubborn and quick-tempered father, refuses to accept the loss and throws himself into the harvest. His wife, Dolors, tries to hold the family together. Their teenage son, Roger, dreams of earning money by growing marijuana, while their daughter, Mariona, finds an outlet in rehearsing dances for the village festival. Quimet's relationships with other relatives grow strained over how to respond.

The youngest children, including Iris and her cousins, remain mostly unaware of the adults' troubles. They play among the trees, stage mock trials, and build hideouts in the fields, their games suggesting a fading innocence and the family's deep attachment to the land. As the season ends, attempts to negotiate with the new owner come to nothing, and machines arrive to tear out the trees. The family gathers to watch in silence as the orchard they have tended for decades is destroyed.

Alcarràs premiered at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival in February 2022, where it won the Golden Bear, the first Catalan-language film to do so. Critics praised its authenticity, tender performances and moving portrait of rural life and family. It was selected as Spain's submission for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film, though it was not nominated, and won four Gaudí Awards, including Best Film.

documents.title: The Munsters
documents.tagline: Prepare for the strangest love story ever told.
documents.overview: Lily is a typical 150-year-old lovelorn vampire who's looking for the man of her nightmares -- until she lays her eyes on Herman, a 7-foot-tall green experiment with a heart of gold. It's love at first shock as these two ghouls fall fangs over feet for each other in a Transylvanian romance. Unfortunately, it's not all smooth sailing in the cemetery as Lily's father has other plans for his beloved daughter's future, and they don't involve her new bumbling beau.
documents.plot:
The Munsters is a 2022 American horror comedy written, produced and directed by Rob Zombie as a prequel and origin story to the 1960s sitcom. Jeff Daniel Phillips plays Herman Munster, Sheri Moon Zombie plays Lily and Daniel Roebuck plays her father, the Count, with Richard Brake as the mad scientist Dr. Wolfgang, Jorge Garcia as his assistant Floop, Sylvester McCoy as the servant Igor, Catherine Schell as the Count's ex-wife Zoya and Cassandra Peterson as the realtor Barbara Carr.

In Transylvania, Dr. Wolfgang and his hunchbacked helper Floop rob graves to assemble a creature, but Floop takes the head of a corny comedian, Shecky, instead of his brilliant brother. Brought to life, the creation, named Herman, turns out to be a goofy jokester. Meanwhile Zoya, seeking revenge on the Count, pressures his werewolf son Lester, who owes her money, into helping her obtain the family castle for a casino. The Count's daughter Lily, a vampire unlucky in love, sees Herman unveiled on a morning television show and is charmed. She watches him perform with his band at Zoya's nightclub, and the two fall for each other.

The Count dislikes the dim newcomer and tries magic to get rid of him, but Herman and Lily become engaged and marry. Now head of the household, Herman is tricked by Lester into signing the castle's deed over to Zoya. On their honeymoon in Paris, the couple capture a reptilian creature from the sewers and adopt it as their pet, Spot. Evicted and without legal recourse, they follow Herman's dream of stardom to America, where Barbara Carr shows them around Hollywood and they buy the crumbling house at 1313 in Mockingbird Heights. A Halloween block party makes them think they have found fellow monsters, but they are dismayed to discover that their neighbors are ordinary people. Lester then arrives with a check from his Las Vegas winnings, and the Munsters find themselves rich.

The film was released on digital, Blu-ray and DVD and on Netflix in the United States on 27 September 2022. Reviews were mixed: it holds a 52% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 57, with critics noting Zombie's clear affection for the series while finding the story loose and sketch-like.

documents.title: Vanquish
documents.tagline: She's got one night to save her life.
documents.overview: Victoria is a young mother trying to put her dark past as a Russian drug courier behind her, but retired cop Damon forces Victoria to do his bidding by holding her daughter hostage. Now, Victoria must use guns, guts and a motorcycle to take out a series of violent gangsters—or she may never see her child again.
documents.plot:
Vanquish is a 2021 American action thriller directed by George Gallo, who wrote it with Samuel Bartlett. Ruby Rose stars as Victoria, a former drug courier forced back into her old life, and Morgan Freeman plays Damon, a retired, wheelchair-using police officer, with Patrick Muldoon, Julie Lott and Ekaterina Baker.

Victoria works as the evening caregiver for Damon at his palatial home, bringing along her young daughter, Lily, who is ill. When Victoria admits she cannot afford Lily's treatment, Damon offers to pay for it in exchange for a favor. A corrupt cop who ran illicit operations around the city, he wants to pull his money from five associates after a recent double cross, and he asks Victoria, who once worked as a courier for the Russian mob alongside her late brother, to collect it in a single night. She refuses until Lily disappears, and Damon makes clear that her daughter will be returned only when the job is done.

Wearing a body camera so that Damon can watch from his computer, Victoria sets out. At the first stop she recognizes the criminal she is collecting from as the man who killed her brother and kills him and his men. Each subsequent pickup brings her face to face with enemies from her past and ends in a fight, a shootout or a chase, and her trail of violence draws the attention of crooked police officers, federal agents and government operatives. Meanwhile a police officer breaks into Damon's house, and Damon kills him. At her final stop, Victoria is captured and brought to the corrupt Governor, who asks for her help in bringing down Damon; Victoria refuses and kills the Governor. When she returns to Damon's home and is reunited with Lily, he reveals that he never needed the money: the night was a plan to wipe out Victoria's enemies and the corrupt Governor, ridding the city of its criminals. At dawn, Damon lures the crooked officers who worked for the Governor into his house and blows himself up along with them, while Victoria and Lily escape.

Lionsgate released Vanquish in select theaters on April 16, 2021, followed by digital and home video releases later that month. Critics savaged it, giving it 5% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 22; RogerEbert.com called it a dull, threadbare rehash of genre clichés.

documents.title: The Girl Who Believes in Miracles
documents.original_title: The Girl Who Believes in Miracles
documents.tagline: From her lips to God's ears.
documents.overview: When Sara hears a preacher say faith can move mountains, she starts praying. Suddenly people in her town are mysteriously healed! But fame soon takes its toll – can Sara’s family save her before it’s too late?
documents.plot:
The Girl Who Believes in Miracles is a 2021 American Christian drama film directed and produced by Richard Correll. It stars Austyn Johnson as Sara Hopkins, a young girl whose prayers appear to bring about miraculous healings, with Mira Sorvino as her mother, Bonnie, Burgess Jenkins as her father, Alex, Peter Coyote as Sam Donovan, Kevin Sorbo as Dr. Ben Riley, Luke Omalza as her brother, Danny, and Paul-Mikel Williams as her friend Mark. The film was produced by 120 dB Films, Gerson Productions, The Mustard Seed Production and Trailmaker Productions.

Sara is a kind-hearted girl with a deep faith in God. During a visit to a lake with Danny and his girlfriend, Cindy, she finds a dead bird and, to the skepticism of her family, prays that God will bring it back to life, which he does. Not long afterward, Danny pushes his rival, Alvie, out of the path of an oncoming car, and Alvie's dog is struck instead; Sara prays over the animal and it revives, astonishing everyone who sees it. Encouraged, her best friend, Mark, a paraplegic boy who uses a wheelchair, asks her to pray with him, and he is able to walk again.

As word spreads and more miracles are attributed to her, Sara becomes a national celebrity and begins healing blind and sick children. Her family grows alarmed when she collapses after praying so often, and doctors discover that she is dying of an inoperable brain tumor. Her doctor recommends that she be kept comfortable in hospital, but Sara longs to return to the lake where she first saw God. Her grandfather organizes the townspeople to spirit her out of the hospital, and against her parents' wishes they rush her to the lake. There God appears, and Sara's spirit rises to meet him before both vanish, leaving the gathered crowd to mourn her. Danny, however, finds one of her paintings, which shows her leaving God to return to her family; taking it as a sign that she is still alive, he prays for her return, and she wakes, to everyone's joy. Sara modestly insists that it was God who healed the people she prayed for and that she only did what he asked of her.

Distributed by Atlas Distribution Company, the film was released theatrically in the United States on April 2, 2021, and became available on digital platforms on June 1, 2021.

documents.title: Look Both Ways
documents.tagline: Wherever life takes you, let love guide you.
documents.overview: On the eve of her college graduation, Natalie's life diverges into two parallel realities: one in which she becomes pregnant and must navigate motherhood as a young adult in her Texas hometown, the other in which she moves to LA to pursue her career. In both journeys throughout her twenties, Natalie experiences life-changing love, devastating heartbreak and rediscovers herself.
documents.plot:
Look Both Ways is a 2022 American romantic comedy-drama directed by Wanuri Kahiu and written by April Prosser. Lili Reinhart stars as Natalie Bennett, a college student whose life splits into two parallel realities, with Danny Ramirez as her friend Gabe, David Corenswet as Jake, Aisha Dee as Cara, Nia Long as the animator Lucy Galloway, and Luke Wilson and Andrea Savage as Natalie's parents.

In her senior year at the University of Texas, Natalie sleeps with her friend Gabe, and both agree not to make a big deal of it. On graduation night she feels ill, and her best friend Cara buys her pregnancy tests. From that moment the film follows two versions of her life side by side.

When the test is positive, Natalie moves back in with her disappointed parents, who are unimpressed by Gabe's ambitions as a musician but urge her to keep pursuing animation. After their daughter, Rosie, is born, Natalie refuses Gabe's offer to live together and encourages him to date, later regretting it when he becomes involved with Miranda. While visiting Cara in Los Angeles, Natalie rushes home after a worrying call, and learns that Gabe has proposed to Miranda. Pouring herself into her art, she achieves a breakthrough and appears on a panel at South by Southwest in Austin with Lucy, discussing a comic inspired by Rosie. After watching his band play, Natalie learns that Gabe has broken off his engagement because he loves her, and they talk seriously about their future.

When the test is negative, Natalie moves to Los Angeles with Cara and lands a job as Lucy's assistant, where she falls for her colleague Jake, an aspiring producer. Their relationship falters when he takes a year-long job in Nova Scotia. Lucy criticizes Natalie's portfolio as unoriginal and encourages her to find her own voice, so Natalie quits and returns home feeling like a failure. Then her short film is accepted at South by Southwest. In Austin she runs into Gabe, now married, and jokes about how different life would have been had her test been positive. Jake surprises her by attending her screening, and Lucy invites her to reconnect. In both realities, Natalie returns to the bathroom where she took the test and reassures herself that things worked out.

Netflix released the film on August 17, 2022. Reviews were mixed to positive, with 62% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 49; Variety praised its sentiments about risk and fate while faulting its execution.

documents.title: Descendants: The Royal Wedding
documents.overview: Happily-ever-after continues for Auradon's power couple as they prepare to say "I do" at an epic celebration with their friends and family, but Hades threatens to ruin it all.
documents.plot: Happily-ever-after continues for Auradon's power couple as they prepare to say "I do" at an epic celebration with their friends and family, but Hades threatens to ruin it all.

documents.title: This Little Love of Mine
documents.tagline: Follow your heart... to find your calling.
documents.overview: Laura Price is a successful San Francisco lawyer on the cusp of promotion – a far cry from her childhood growing up on a tropical island with best friends Chip and Gem. When the firm’s biggest client – Chip’s grandfather – asks Laura to travel to the island and deliver a contract to make Chip his heir, she leaves behind her practice and fiancé Owen to convince her childhood friend to sign a contract that will make him a billionaire.
documents.plot:
This Little Love of Mine is a 2021 Australian romantic comedy film directed by Christine Luby from a screenplay by Georgia Harrison and produced by The Steve Jaggi Company. It stars Saskia Hampele and Liam McIntyre, with Lynn Gilmartin, Craig Horner, Lawrence Ola, Rajan Velu and Tiriel Mora in supporting roles. Although made in Australia with a largely Australian cast speaking in American accents, the film is set on a South Seas island and was shot in North Queensland. It was first released in April 2021 and arrived on Netflix in July 2021. The film runs 91 minutes.

Laura Price (Hampele) is a high-powered San Francisco corporate lawyer on the verge of being made partner and engaged to the equally ambitious Owen (Horner). She grew up on the tropical island of Sapphire Cove with her best friends Chip and Gem, but has not seen them in years. When her firm's biggest client, Chip's grandfather, a business mogul who must cede control of his company before his 85th birthday, asks her to travel back to the island and get Chip to sign a contract making him his heir and a billionaire, she leaves her practice and her fiancé behind. Chip (McIntyre), however, is happily living on island time as the barefoot captain of a charter boat and ferry and wants nothing to do with the responsibility. The workaholic lawyer and the laid-back islander clash, haggle and strike bargains, such as his offer to read one page of the contract for every fun activity she tries on the island, and between emails, video meetings, pressure from her boss and distracted calls from Owen, Laura finds herself horse riding and snorkelling, rediscovering the place where she grew up and her feelings for Chip.

Critics found the film pleasant to look at but generic. Roger Moore of Movie Nation complained that the decision to scrub every trace of Australia from the film had bleached out its local colour and any chance of drama or romantic friction, calling it so dull that it barely passed Hallmark Channel muster, with a generic plot, bland characters and sleep-inducing dialogue, though he credited the leads for mastering American accents. Jane Freebury of The Canberra Times gave it two stars out of five, writing that it lacked wit and a sense of place. Other reviewers enjoyed its tropical scenery, breezy pace and the chemistry between Hampele and McIntyre.

documents.title: Vortex
documents.tagline: Life is a short party that will soon be forgotten.
documents.overview: Lui, a struggling author with a heart condition, and his wife Elle, a retired psychiatrist, find their idyllic life shattered when Elle begins to succumb to the effects of dementia.
documents.plot:
Vortex is a 2021 French psychological drama written and directed by Gaspar Noé. The Italian horror director Dario Argento stars in his first leading acting role as an elderly film writer, with Françoise Lebrun as his wife and Alex Lutz as their son Stéphane. Shot largely in split screen with a muted, faded palette and a slow, minimal style, the film is an intimate portrait of old age, illness and death. It premiered in the Cannes Premiere section at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival to widespread acclaim, a contrast with the divided reactions to many of Noé's earlier films.

An old married couple, a writer working on a book about cinema and dreams and a retired psychiatrist, live together in a cluttered Paris apartment filled with books, papers and memories. After a brief opening scene showing them together on their balcony, the screen splits into two frames, one following each of them, and the division becomes a visual expression of how they are drifting apart. The wife is suffering from advancing dementia, wandering the neighborhood and losing track of who and where she is, while the husband, who has a serious heart condition, tries to carry on with his writing and to hide the extent of her condition.

Their son Stéphane, who struggles with a history of drug addiction and is raising his young son Kiki alone, visits and urges his parents to move into assisted living where his mother can receive proper care. His father refuses, unwilling to give up the apartment and the possessions that hold his past. As both parents' health declines, the daily routine of the household becomes increasingly fragile and painful, and the film follows the slow, unsparing progress of their decline with long takes and little music, observing the limits of love and the indignity of illness as the end approaches.

Vortex received widespread acclaim. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 92 percent approval rating, with a consensus describing it as Noé at his most unflinchingly pitiless and a haunting contemplation of death for viewers who can endure it, and it has a Metacritic score of 82. Critics particularly praised the performances of Argento and Lebrun and noted that Noé had been inspired in part by his own experiences, including his mother's dementia and a brain hemorrhage he suffered in 2020.

documents.title: Boiling Point
documents.tagline: There is no room for mistakes.
documents.overview: A head chef balances multiple personal and professional crises at a popular restaurant in London.
