Overall, Muppets Haunted Mansion is a fun and spooky comedy that brings a fresh take to the classic Disney theme park attraction. With its talented voice cast, clever writing, and exciting plot twists, it's sure to delight both fans of The Muppets and horror enthusiasts alike.

documents.title: Better Nate Than Ever
documents.tagline: Every adventure begins with a dream.
documents.overview: 13-year-old Nate Foster has big Broadway dreams but there’s only one problem — he can’t even land a part in the school play. When his parents leave town, Nate and his best friend Libby sneak off to the Big Apple for a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to prove everyone wrong. A chance encounter with Nate’s long-lost Aunt Heidi turns his journey upside-down, and together they must learn that life’s greatest adventures are only as big as your dreams.
documents.plot:
Better Nate Than Ever is a heartwarming and uplifting film that explores several key themes. At its core, the movie is about self-discovery and embracing one's true identity. The protagonist, Nate, is a young African American boy who struggles to find his place in the world, particularly when it comes to his love of musical theater.

As Nate navigates his relationships with his family and friends, he must confront the challenges of being different and finding acceptance. Through his experiences, the film highlights the importance of authenticity and staying true to oneself, even in the face of adversity.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, community, and belonging. Nate's journey is not just about finding himself, but also about finding a sense of belonging among people who understand and appreciate him for who he is. The film celebrates the power of found family and the importance of creating one's own support system.

Furthermore, Better Nate Than Ever explores the complexities of family relationships and the challenges of navigating different cultural backgrounds. Nate's experiences as a black boy in a predominantly white world serve as a powerful commentary on issues of racism and representation.

Ultimately, the film is a triumphant celebration of individuality, creativity, and the human spirit. Through Nate's story, we are reminded that it's okay to be different and that embracing our unique qualities can lead to growth, self-acceptance, and happiness.

documents.title: About Fate
documents.tagline: Love appears where you least expect it.
documents.overview: Two strangers believe in love but never seem to be able to find its true meaning. In a wild twist of events, fate puts each in the other's path on one stormy New Year's Eve.
documents.plot: Two strangers believe in love but never seem to be able to find its true meaning. In a wild twist of events, fate puts each in the other's path on one stormy New Year's Eve.

documents.title: Beavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe
documents.original_title: Beavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe
documents.tagline: The dumbest science fiction movie ever made.
documents.overview: In 1998, Beavis and Butt-Head are sentenced to Space Camp by a “creative” judge. Their obsession with a docking simulator (huh huh) leads to a trip on the Space Shuttle, with predictably disastrous results. After going through a black hole, they re-emerge in our time, where they look for love, misuse iPhones, and are hunted by the Deep State. Spoiler: They don’t score.

documents.title: Enola Holmes 2
documents.tagline: Go Big. Go Holmes.
documents.overview: Now a detective-for-hire like her infamous brother, Enola Holmes takes on her first official case to find a missing girl, as the sparks of a dangerous conspiracy ignite a mystery that requires the help of friends — and Sherlock himself — to unravel.
documents.plot:
Enola Holmes 2 is a 2022 mystery film directed by Harry Bradbeer from an original screenplay by Jack Thorne, and the sequel to Enola Holmes (2020). Millie Bobby Brown returns as Enola, the teenage sister of Sherlock Holmes, played by Henry Cavill. Louis Partridge, Susie Wokoma, Adeel Akhtar and Helena Bonham Carter reprise their roles, and David Thewlis and Sharon Duncan-Brewster join the cast. Rather than adapting one of Nancy Springer's novels, the story draws on the real matchgirls' strike of 1888 and the labor activist Sarah Chapman.

Enola has opened a detective agency but is not taken seriously in her brother's shadow. A young match factory worker, Bessie, hires her to find her missing sister, Sarah Chapman. The trail leads from the factory, supposedly struck by typhus, to the Paragon Theatre, where Sarah and her friend Mae also worked as dancers. Enola finds a coded love poem that leads her to Mae, who has been stabbed and is dying. Superintendent Grail then accuses Enola of the murder. Sherlock, meanwhile, is stuck on a case of blackmailed officials. Enola goes to a society ball, where her old friend Tewkesbury teaches her to dance, to reach William Lyon, the factory owner's son and Sarah's secret lover. Grail arrests her first. Her mother Eudoria and the suffragette Edith break her out of jail.

Enola realizes that Cicely, a friendly young woman she met at the ball, is in fact Sarah. Sarah, Mae and William had discovered that the workers were dying from white phosphorus poisoning, not typhus, and were planning to expose it. William is murdered before he can act. The Holmes siblings conclude that Treasury Minister Lord McIntyre made a deal with the factory owner to use the cheap, deadly phosphorus. At the Paragon, Enola defeats Grail, who falls to his death. When McIntyre burns the evidence, Enola and Sherlock reveal that his secretary Mira Troy is the mastermind Moriarty, behind both the blackmail and the killings. The matchgirls go on strike, McIntyre is arrested and Moriarty escapes custody. Enola sets up a new office, and Tewkesbury begins courting her.

Filming took place from autumn 2021 to January 2022, including scenes in Hull. Netflix released the film on November 4, 2022, and it topped the service's charts in 93 countries. Reviews were positive, with Rotten Tomatoes' consensus calling it a satisfying sequel that made the job look positively elementary. Brown won Favorite Movie Actress at the 2023 Kids' Choice Awards.

documents.title: Queen of Spades
documents.tagline: She will reign.
documents.overview: According to legend, an ominous entity known as the Queen of Spades can be summoned by performing an ancient ritual. Four teenagers summon the Queen of Spades, but they could never imagine the horrors that await them.
documents.plot:
Queen of Spades is a 2021 Canadian supernatural horror film directed by Patrick White, a remake of the 2015 Russian film Queen of Spades: The Dark Rite. Produced with Epic Pictures and its genre label Dread, it stars Ava Preston as Anna, Kaelen Ohm as Mary, Daniel Kash as Smirnov, and Jamie Bloch, Eric Osborne and Nabil Rajo. The Queen of Spades figure traces back to Alexander Pushkin's 1833 short story and Tchaikovsky's opera, and has since become a Russian urban legend similar to Bloody Mary.

According to the legend, the Queen of Spades can be summoned by drawing a door and a staircase on a mirror in lipstick and ordering her three times to show herself. If the rite is performed correctly, the specter appears and grants a wish, but she is often more inclined to harm those who call her. In Ottawa, four teenage friends watch a young man jump to his death from a rooftop, muttering "Queen of Spades" as he dies. Curious rather than shaken, they research the legend online and find instructions for the ritual, which says the youngest member of the group must perform it, so thirteen-year-old Anna is chosen. At first nothing seems to happen and they carry on with their lives, but soon they experience disturbing visions and strange events, and one of the boys discovers a mysterious bloody gash on his arm before dying of a heart attack. When Mary, a single mother whose child is among the group, learns about the rite, she seeks out Smirnov, a Russian expert in the supernatural who has written a book about the legend, hoping he can stop the Queen from claiming more victims. Smirnov's attempts include trying to transfer the demon's spirit into a cat.

Queen of Spades was released on video on demand in the United States and Canada in June 2021. Reviews were mixed to negative. Matt Patti of Film Festival Today gave it two and a half stars out of four, finding it unoriginal and burdened by weak early dialogue and rushed exposition, but an effective paranormal horror film with genuinely frightening jump scares and a creepy demon design. Eric Hillis of The Movie Waffler was far harsher, calling it lacklustre low-budget horror that reduces the legend to a third-rate Candyman knockoff with unremarkable deaths and a lazily designed demon, though he felt Ohm gave a performance worthy of a far better movie.

documents.title: 365 Days: This Day
documents.tagline: Oh Yes.
documents.overview: Laura and Massimo are back and hotter than ever. But the reunited couple's new beginning is complicated by Massimo’s family ties and a mysterious man who enters Laura’s life to win her heart and trust, at any cost.
documents.plot:
365 Days: This Day (Polish: 365 dni: Ten dzień) is a Polish erotic drama of 2022 directed by Barbara Białowąs and Tomasz Mandes. The sequel to 365 Days, it adapts This Day, the second novel in Blanka Lipińska's trilogy, and stars Anna-Maria Sieklucka as Laura, Michele Morrone in the dual role of the mafia boss Massimo Torricelli and his twin brother Adriano, Simone Susinna as Nacho, Magdalena Lamparska as Olga and Otar Saralidze as Domenico.

The story opens with Laura marrying Massimo. Having lost their baby in the accident at the end of the previous film, she confides the miscarriage only to her best friend Olga, the only person from her side invited to the Italian wedding, since Massimo fears that her family would discover his criminal life. On returning from their honeymoon the couple catch Olga with Massimo's right-hand man Domenico. Married life soon turns sour: Laura is bored and lonely with nothing to do while Massimo is busy with his business, the two argue daily, and she grows drawn to Nacho, the gardener. At a party she believes she sees Massimo having sex with his former lover Anna, and in her heartbreak she flees with Nacho to an island, where she begins to enjoy a new life while Massimo hunts for her.

Nacho eventually reveals that his father leads a mafia family that rivals Massimo's, and the old man favours Adriano, Massimo's unstable and estranged twin, to take over the Sicilian clan. Laura learns that the man she saw with Anna was in fact Adriano, who now holds her captive. Massimo and Nacho, long rivals, join forces to rescue her, but she is shot by Anna and Adriano before the two men kill them, and the film ends with Laura in Massimo's arms, her fate unresolved.

Principal photography took place in Italy and Poland in 2021 after pandemic delays. Released on Netflix on 27 April 2022, the film was savaged by critics, scoring 0% on Rotten Tomatoes and 8 out of 100 on Metacritic; Variety's Jessica Kiang called it piping hot trash. A further sequel, The Next 365 Days, followed in August 2022.

documents.title: The Next 365 Days
documents.overview: Laura and Massimo's relationship hangs in the balance as they try to overcome trust issues while a tenacious Nacho works to push them apart.
documents.plot:
The Next 365 Days is a Polish erotic drama film directed by Olaf Modrzejowski, based on the novel "365 Dni Prawdziwe" (365 Days) by Blanka Lipińska. The movie serves as a sequel to the original 2020 film.

The story follows Ola Młynarska (played by Anna Maliszewska), who has just been released from prison after serving her sentence for murdering her abusive boyfriend, Sławomir (played by Łukasz Rysiński). As she tries to rebuild her life, Ola is approached by a wealthy and charming businessman named Massimo Torricelli (played by Michele Morrone), who offers her a deal: in exchange for his help with her financial situation, she will become his girlfriend.

Ola accepts the offer, but soon realizes that Massimo's intentions are not entirely pure. Despite their tumultuous relationship, Ola finds herself drawn to Massimo's charismatic and confident personality. As they navigate their complicated feelings for each other, Ola must confront her past traumas and learn to trust herself again.

Throughout the film, Ola struggles with her own darkness and the consequences of her actions in the previous installment. The movie explores themes of toxic relationships, emotional manipulation, and the blurred lines between love and obsession.

The Next 365 Days received mixed reviews from critics, who praised Anna Maliszewska's performance but criticized the film's handling of sensitive topics such as domestic abuse and consent. Despite this, the movie has maintained a dedicated fan base, particularly among viewers who enjoyed the original 2020 film.

Overall, The Next 365 Days is a complex and thought-provoking exploration of toxic relationships and personal growth. While it may not be to everyone's taste, fans of the original film will likely find themselves invested in Ola's journey as she navigates her complicated feelings for Massimo.

documents.title: Paradise City
documents.overview: Renegade bounty hunter Ryan Swan must carve his way through the Hawaiian crime world to wreak vengeance on the kingpin who murdered his father.
documents.plot:
Paradise City is a 2022 American action crime film directed by Chuck Russell from a screenplay he wrote with Corey Large and Edward John Drake. Set on Maui, it reunites Bruce Willis and John Travolta, who had both starred in Pulp Fiction (1994), with Stephen Dorff, Blake Jenner and Praya Lundberg, along with Large, Branscombe Richmond as Senator Kane and Laird Akeo.

Ian Swan is a veteran bounty hunter working in Hawaii with a target on his back. While pursuing a fugitive, he is shot and disappears into the waters off Maui, and he is presumed dead. His son, Ryan, arrives on the island to find out what happened and to track down his father's killers. He teams up with Ian's former partner and protégé, Robbie Cole, now a grizzled bounty hunter himself living off free drinks and dwindling commissions, and with Savannah, a tough local detective who shares Ryan's fighting spirit.

Their investigation leads them to Arlene Buckley, a fussy, exacting and ruthless power broker who is scheming to seize protected Hawaiian land, robbing native islanders of their tribal land rights, and to expand his political influence. After Buckley threatens them, Ryan and his team appear to have run out of options, until an excursion to Paradise City, a closely guarded island community, unites them with an unexpected ally. Along the way, a twist involving a drug cartel baron and cosmetic surgery reshapes what they thought they knew,.

Large had conceived the idea of reuniting Willis and Travolta in 2006, and the project was announced in May 2021. Filming began on May 17, 2021, on Maui and wrapped after three weeks; the Maui County film commissioner noted that preparation was squeezed into two weeks and the script was constantly rewritten because of location restrictions. Paradise City is one of Willis's last films before he retired from acting after being diagnosed with a neurological condition. Saban Films released it in limited theaters and on demand on November 11, 2022, and on DVD and Blu-ray on December 20. Reviews were largely negative, with 14% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 31. The New York Times' Glenn Kenny said it sounded like one of the fake movies joked about on Seinfeld or 30 Rock, and Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times called it TV-cop-show material the stars could not save. Variety's Owen Gleiberman called it junk but found Travolta, Willis and Dorff enjoying themselves.

documents.title: Fate/Grand Order Final Singularity – Grand Temple of Time: Solomon
documents.original_title: Fate/Grand Order -終局特異点 冠位時間神殿ソロモン-
documents.tagline: This is the final battle to take back our future.
documents.overview: The Chaldea Organization must deal with the Grand Temple of Solomon, the King of Magic, which has come to destroy the world.
documents.plot:
Fate/Grand Order Final Singularity – Grand Temple of Time: Solomon (Fate/Grand Order -終局特異点 冠位時間神殿ソロモン-) is a 2021 Japanese animated fantasy action film directed by Toshifumi Akai and animated by CloverWorks, with 3D computer graphics by Shirogumi, and distributed by Aniplex. It adapts the climactic chapter of the first part of the story of Fate/Grand Order, the TYPE-MOON mobile role-playing game written by Kinoko Nasu, who is credited with the original scenario. A sequel to the 2019–2020 television series Fate/Grand Order – Absolute Demonic Front: Babylonia, whose final episode announced it, the film was made by largely the same team, including character designer Tomoaki Takase and composers Keita Haga and Ryo Kawasaki. It was released in Japanese cinemas on 30 July 2021 and runs 94 minutes. The voice cast is led by Nobunaga Shimazaki as Ritsuka Fujimaru and Rie Takahashi as Mash Kyrielight, with Kenichi Suzumura as Romani Archaman, Maaya Sakamoto as Leonardo da Vinci, Ayako Kawasumi as Fou and Tomokazu Sugita as Solomon.

Having fought its way through all seven Singularities that threatened human history, the Chaldea Security Organization at last reaches the endpoint of the Grand Order: the Final Singularity, the Grand Temple of Time, a domain created by Solomon, the King of Magic, who intends to destroy the world. As the final operation looms, Romani Archaman weighs the choices he will soon have to make, Mash Kyrielight reflects on the limits of her own life, and the Master Ritsuka Fujimaru prepares to receive a new Mystic Code. The pair then launch their last mission into the temple, where dozens of Heroic Spirits they have met over the course of their journey arrive to join the battle against Solomon's forces, in a final struggle to reclaim humanity's future.

Kim Morrissy of Anime News Network gave the film a B, likening it to the Avengers: Endgame of the Fate franchise because its appeal hinges on cameos from dozens of Servants rarely seen in animated form. She admitted the plot was a load of nonsense she loved every minute of, praised the animation by the Babylonia team as among the best-looking in the franchise and the satisfying climax and ending, which neatly wraps up the first part of the story, but found the theatrical dialogue potentially cheesy and self-indulgent, the ensemble action scenes too short and the film likely to be off-putting to viewers who had not played the game.

documents.title: Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile
documents.tagline: He knows every scale.
documents.overview: When the Primm family moves to New York City, their young son Josh struggles to adapt to his new school and new friends. All of that changes when he discovers Lyle — a singing crocodile who loves baths, caviar and great music — living in the attic of his new home. But when Lyle’s existence is threatened by evil neighbor Mr. Grumps, the Primms must band together to show the world that family can come from the most unexpected places.
documents.plot:
Lyle, Lyle, Crocodile is a 2022 American musical comedy-drama produced and directed by Will Speck and Josh Gordon from a screenplay by William Davies. Made by Columbia Pictures, it adapts Bernard Waber's children's book of the same name and its predecessor, The House on East 88th Street, which had earlier been turned into a 1987 animated HBO musical special. Shawn Mendes provides the singing voice of Lyle, a crocodile who communicates only through song, with Ben Palacios performing his motion capture. Filming took place in New York City in September 2021, and Sony Pictures Releasing opened the film on October 7, 2022.

Hector P. Valenti, a flamboyant showman who keeps failing auditions for a national talent show, finds a singing baby crocodile in an exotic pet shop and names him Lyle. He stakes his Victorian brownstone on their debut, but Lyle freezes with stage fright, Hector loses the house and leaves Lyle to fend for himself while he tries to earn money. Eighteen months later, the Primm family moves in: math teacher Joseph, his wife Katie, a cookbook author, and Joseph's nervous son, Josh, who struggles at his new school. Josh discovers the now fully grown Lyle, and they become friends after Lyle saves him from a mugger. Katie and Joseph overcome their fear and bond with Lyle too.

Hector returns, using an agreement that lets him live in the house part of the year, and tries again to put Lyle on stage, but the crocodile's stage fright returns. Meanwhile the Primms' unfriendly downstairs neighbor, Alistair Grumps, determined to stop the noise, bribes Hector into selling Lyle, who is locked up at the zoo after failing to sing for the authorities. Guilt-ridden, Hector helps Josh break Lyle out and apologizes to him. At the talent show Lyle finally conquers his fear and performs with Josh and the dance troupe of Josh's friend Trudy. When the Primms are taken to court for keeping Lyle, Hector produces his grandmother's deed to the house, which allows any exotic animal to be kept as a pet, and the judge rules in their favor.

Javier Bardem plays Hector, with Winslow Fegley as Josh, Constance Wu as Katie, Scoot McNairy as Joseph and Brett Gelman as Grumps. Reviews were generally positive, with 71% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and particular praise for Bardem, while audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore. It grossed $111 million worldwide against a $50 million budget.

documents.title: The Invitation
documents.tagline: You are cordially invited to a nightmare generations in the making.
documents.overview: After the death of her mother, Evie is approached by an unknown cousin who invites her to a lavish wedding in the English countryside. Soon, she realizes a gothic conspiracy is afoot and must fight for survival as she uncovers twisted secrets in her family’s history.
documents.plot:
The Invitation is a 2022 American horror thriller directed by Jessica M. Thompson and written by Blair Butler, inspired by Bram Stoker's novel Dracula. Screen Gems acquired Butler's pitch in 2019, and the project, first titled The Bride, lost producers Sam Raimi and Robert Tapert before Thompson came aboard to direct with Emile Gladstone producing. It stars Nathalie Emmanuel and Thomas Doherty, who replaced Garrett Hedlund, and was filmed in Budapest from September 2021.

In New York, struggling artist Evie Jackson works for a catering company with her best friend Grace. After her mother's death, a DNA test connects her with an English cousin, Oliver Alexander, who explains that her great-grandmother Emmaline had a secret child with a Black footman, and invites her to a family wedding in Whitby. At New Carfax Abbey, Evie is charmed by the estate's owner, Walter De Ville, as she meets his butler Mr. Field, the friendly bridesmaid Lucy and the haughty Viktoria. Meanwhile housemaids keep disappearing, and after discovering that Walter has been researching her, Evie confronts him before they make up and sleep together.

At the rehearsal dinner Walter announces that Evie is the bride. Mr. Field slits a maid's throat and serves her blood to Walter, Lucy and Viktoria, revealing them as vampires. The Alexanders are one of three families who have supplied Walter with wives for centuries in return for wealth and protection, and Emmaline, his former bride, had killed herself in guilt. Freed from the cellar by the maid Mrs. Swift, Evie flees to the village, but the elderly couple she turns to, Jonathan and Mina Harker, serve De Ville, who reveals he is Dracula. During the forced wedding, Evie drinks his blood, becomes a vampire, sets the chapel on fire and kills Mr. Field and, finally, Dracula, which returns her to human form, while Lucy destroys herself and Viktoria. Two weeks later, Evie and Grace go after Oliver for his betrayal.

Sony Pictures Releasing opened the film on August 26, 2022. Critics praised Emmanuel but faulted the predictable story and weak scares, giving it a 29% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It nonetheless topped the US box office in its first weekend and earned $38 million worldwide on a $10 million budget, turning a profit, and later reached Netflix's global top five.

documents.title: Gone Mom: The Disappearance of Jennifer Dulos
documents.original_title: Gone Mom: The Disappearance of Jennifer Dulos
documents.overview: Jennifer Dulos, the wealthy, Connecticut mother-of-five who mysteriously vanished.
documents.plot:
Gone Mom: The Disappearance of Jennifer Dulos is a 2021 American biographical crime drama television film directed by Gail Harvey and written by Gregory Small and Richard Blaney, produced by Lighthouse Pictures for Lifetime with Dan Abrams, Ilene Kahn Power and Rachel Stockman as executive producers. Based on the real 2019 disappearance of Jennifer Farber Dulos, a wealthy Connecticut mother of five, it stars Annabeth Gish as Jennifer and Warren Christie as her husband Fotis Dulos, with Laura Harris as her best friend Audrey and Heidi Bauman as Michelle Troconis. It runs 88 minutes and premiered on 5 June 2021 as part of Lifetime's Summer of Secrets slate.

The film moves between two time frames, intercutting the story of the marriage with the police investigation after Jennifer vanishes. Jennifer, a thoughtful aspiring novelist from a very wealthy New York family, and the gregarious, athletic Fotis first met at Brown University but begin a whirlwind romance years later and marry within a year, as Jennifer, then 35, longs for a family. Her friends, especially Audrey, suspect he is after her money. Fotis bankrolls a struggling development company with her family's wealth and spends much of the year away on business and skiing trips while Jennifer, raising their five children largely alone with the help of a nanny, puts aside her writing. He belittles her, flies into rages and makes threats, and eventually openly brings his mistress Michelle into their life, telling Jennifer to accept it. She files for divorce and moves out with the children, leading to a bitter custody battle in which Fotis threatens to take the children to Greece and to kill her. When Jennifer disappears in New Canaan, Audrey points the police towards Fotis, and investigators reconstruct how they believe he attacked her in her garage and cleaned up with rolls of paper towels, tracing his movements on security cameras even though her body is never found. Fotis, charged with her murder, takes his own life while still protesting his innocence, and Michelle is charged as well.

Reviews were broadly favorable. TV Fanatic praised its respectful focus on Jennifer's life, Gish's grace in the role and Christie's balance of charm and volatility. Mark Gabrish Conlan of Movie Magg found it well made and eloquently acted, especially by Gish. Beverly White of MEAWW called it a fascinating cautionary tale and praised Christie, though she found Gish oddly relaxed at times.

documents.title: Injustice
documents.tagline: A threat to Superman is a threat to society.
documents.overview: When Lois Lane is killed, an unhinged Superman decides to take control of the Earth. Determined to stop him, Batman creates a team of freedom-fighting heroes. But when superheroes go to war, can the world survive?
documents.plot:
Injustice is an American adult animated superhero film of 2021 loosely based on NetherRealm Studios' Injustice video games, adapting elements of Injustice: Gods Among Us (2013) and its prequel comic. Directed by Matt Peters from a script by Ernie Altbacker, it is the 47th DC Universe Animated Original Movie. Justin Hartley voices Superman and Anson Mount Batman, with Laura Bailey as Lois Lane, Janet Varney as Wonder Woman, Kevin Pollak as the Joker, Gillian Jacobs as Harley Quinn, Zach Callison as Robin and Anika Noni Rose as Catwoman.

On an alternate Earth, the Joker and Harley Quinn murder Jimmy Olsen, kidnap the pregnant Lois Lane and link a stolen nuclear bomb to her heartbeat. After killing the Flash with a trap, the Joker doses Superman with fear toxin laced with kryptonite, so that the hero believes he is fighting Doomsday when in fact he is killing Lois. Her death triggers the bomb, which destroys Metropolis and kills eleven million people. When the Joker gloats to Batman that he chose Superman as his new target, Superman kills him, then reveals his identity at the United Nations and vows to impose peace by force. The Justice League splits: Wonder Woman backs him, Batman keeps his rule against killing, and others withdraw altogether.

Superman's regime grows harsher. Robin defects to him and accidentally kills Nightwing, who is resurrected by Rama Kushna as Deadwing, while Batman builds an underground Insurgency. A raid on the Fortress of Solitude for a red-sun weapon fails, and when Green Arrow's arrow is deflected and kills Jonathan Kent, Superman murders him. Turning the world into a surveillance state, Superman allies with Ra's al Ghul, whose android Amazo turns on him and kills Hawkman and Cyborg before the heroes destroy it, and Robin, repentant, defeats Ra's. Superman moves to arrest the Insurgents, but Mister Terrific summons heroes from other worlds: an alternate Superman, who is beaten, and an alternate Lois, who lost her own Superman and reminds him that all life is sacred. Realising how far he has fallen, Superman surrenders, and Batman begins rebuilding the world with Catwoman at his side.

Announced in mid-2021, the film leaked online ten days before its release on Blu-ray, 4K and digital on 19 October 2021. Reviews were mixed, with 50% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics liked the action and voice work but faulted the pacing and departures from the source material.

documents.title: Bring It On: Cheer Or Die
documents.original_title: Bring It On: Cheer Or Die
documents.tagline: Bring on the thrills. Bring on the kills. Bring on the cheer.
documents.overview: When a cheer squad practices their routines on Halloween weekend in an abandoned school, they are picked off one by one by an unknown killer.
documents.plot:
Bring It On: Cheer or Die is a 2022 American slasher comedy directed by Karen Lam and the seventh and final installment of the Bring It On series of cheerleading films, following Bring It On: Worldwide Cheersmack (2017). Kerri Medders stars as Abby, with Tiera Skovbye, Missi Pyle, Alten Wilmot and Sierra Holder. Departing from the comedic tone of its predecessors, the film introduces horror elements while retaining a PG-13 rating. It was released on DVD and digital platforms by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on 27 September 2022, ahead of its television premiere on Syfy on 8 October.

Abby is a member of the Diablos, her high school's cheerleading squad, which has a proud competitive history. After an earlier tragedy in which a cheerleader died, the school's overly cautious principal, played by Missi Pyle, bans the squad from performing any risky stunts. With the regional competition approaching, the Diablos fear that their watered-down routine will make them a laughingstock and cost them any chance of winning.

Determined to compete properly, Abby and her teammates hatch a plan to rehearse an ambitious routine in secret. On Halloween they sneak into a nearby abandoned high school, which offers them space to practice away from the eyes of school officials. Soon after they arrive, the cheerleaders begin to disappear one by one. The squad gradually realizes that they are locked inside the derelict building with a masked killer who is stalking them through its corridors, gymnasium and classrooms. As the body count rises, the survivors must rely on teamwork, trust and the athletic skills they have honed as cheerleaders to fight back and escape, while uncovering the secrets of the building and a motive linked to the earlier tragedy that haunts the school.

The film received largely negative reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of 11 percent based on nine reviews. Spooky Sarah Says gave it 2.5 out of 5, describing it as a popcorn movie at a time when much horror is centered on trauma and grief, while Paul Lê of Bloody Disgusting awarded it 1.5 out of 5. Critics generally faulted its lack of scares, its bloodless kills and its flat humor, while noting the novelty of moving the long-running cheerleading franchise into slasher territory.

documents.title: Far from the Tree
documents.overview: On an idyllic beach in the Pacific Northwest, curiosity gets the better of a young raccoon whose frustrated parent attempts to keep them both safe.
documents.plot:
Far from the Tree is a 2021 American animated drama short film written and directed by Natalie Nourigat and produced by Ruth Strother for Walt Disney Animation Studios. It follows a curious young raccoon whose father constantly scolds her for straying into danger, and who later finds herself repeating his behavior with her own child.

On a beach at the edge of a forest, a young raccoon named Marie goes foraging with her father, who bears a scar over one eye. He orders her to stay hidden in a small grotto while he digs for oysters, but Marie keeps wandering out, and each time he angrily drags her back. When she finds a seashell and listens with delight to the sound of the waves inside it, her father chases her back to the grotto and smashes the shell. Chasing a seagull that snatches a fragment, Marie runs into a coyote, which gashes her nose. Her father knocks the coyote away and carries her up into a tree, where he scolds her furiously as she sobs.

Years later, Marie, now an adult still marked by the scar, takes her own son to the beach. Like her father, she tells him to stay in the grotto, and when he slips out to chase seagulls, she snaps at him angrily, before realizing that she is repeating her father's harshness. Instead, she teaches her son about the danger posed by coyotes, shows him how to dig for oysters, and watches over him as he explores. As the sun sets and they return to the forest, she gives him a seashell, which he holds to his ear.

Nourigat developed the film after Disney invited pitches for theatrical shorts in 2018. The project began as a story about human characters drawn from her nostalgia for her childhood in Oregon, but its themes of intergenerational trauma made the tone very dark, and the characters were changed to raccoons, inspired by those Nourigat observed during a research trip to Cannon Beach, Oregon. The animators balanced realistic animal behavior with cartoon appeal. The film relied heavily on Disney's Meander drawing system, previously used for Paperman and Feast, blending hand-drawn line work with computer animation.

Far from the Tree premiered at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival on June 15, 2021, and was released in theaters alongside Encanto that November. It received positive reviews for its emotional storytelling and its themes, with TheWrap naming it one of the best animated films of the year, and it was nominated for Best Short Film by the Hollywood Critics Association.

documents.title: Interceptor
documents.tagline: The world's last defense.
documents.overview: A U.S. Army Captain uses her years of tactical training to save humanity from sixteen nuclear missiles launched at the U.S. as a violent attack threatens her remote missile interceptor station.
documents.plot:
Interceptor is a 2022 Australian-American action thriller film directed by Matthew Reilly in his directorial debut, from a screenplay he wrote with Stuart Beattie. Elsa Pataky stars as Captain J. J. Collins, a U.S. Army officer stationed on a remote nuclear missile interceptor platform in the Pacific Ocean, with Luke Bracey as the former military intelligence officer Alexander Kessel, Aaron Glenane as Corporal Beaver Baker, Mayen Mehta as Corporal Rahul Shah and Colin Friels as Collins's father. Pataky's husband, Chris Hemsworth, an executive producer, appears uncredited as an electronics store salesman.

Terrorists raid the interceptor site at Fort Greely, Alaska, at the same moment that sixteen nuclear warheads are seized in Russia. Collins, forced out of a Pentagon post in retaliation over a sexual misconduct case involving her superior, is now on a station that has suddenly become the country's last defense against nuclear attack. Kessel's operatives storm the platform, killing the commander and the crew and sparing only Collins, Shah and Baker, who has been knocked out. They need the command center to disable the interceptors. Collins and Shah kill an operative who enters through a floor hatch, but Baker wakes and reveals himself as an inside man driven by greed and xenophobia, and the attackers take control at gunpoint. Kessel broadcasts a manifesto denouncing the nation's history and names sixteen target cities before ordering the launch. Collins frees herself, locks Kessel, Baker and one of their men out of the command center and kills two other henchmen. She refuses to yield even when Kessel streams her father's torture. Unable to seize the station, Kessel begins scuttling it. As it sinks, Shah drops through the hatch into the ocean and reactivates the hatches by hand before Baker kills him. Collins hides, kills the last henchman, takes a laptop to the roof, defeats Baker in a hand-to-hand fight and launches the interceptors in time to destroy the warheads. She overpowers Kessel as a Russian submarine arrives to collect the terrorists, but its crew shoots him dead and the captain salutes Collins. Promoted by the president, she recovers in hospital, joined by her father, who was rescued by friends who saw the broadcast.

Shot in New South Wales in 2021, Interceptor had a brief Australian theatrical run from 26 May 2022 before streaming on Netflix from 3 June, where it reached number one. Reviews were mixed, with a 44% Rotten Tomatoes rating.

documents.title: Four to Dinner
documents.overview: In this rom-com challenging the concept of soulmates, parallel storylines portray four single friends as they pair up in different couple combinations.
documents.plot:
Four to Dinner (Italian: 4 metà, also styled Quattro metà, literally "four halves") is a 2022 Italian romantic comedy directed by Alessio Maria Federici from a screenplay by Martino Coli, released worldwide on Netflix in January 2022. Matilde Gioli, Giuseppe Maggio, Matteo Martari and Ilenia Pastorelli play the four single friends at its centre, Giulia, Dario, Matteo and Chiara, with Flavio Furno and Marta Gastini as the married couple Luca and Sara, who frame the story.

The film opens as Luca and Sara, happily married, prepare to host friends for dinner. As the guests arrive, talk turns to whether soulmates really exist, a question that divides the table, and Luca, who believes that a person does not have just one destined partner, offers to tell a story that might settle the argument. He recalls an earlier gathering at the couple's new home, when they invited their four single friends with the well-meant aim of matching them up.

In the first version of events, Dario and the outspoken Giulia hit it off with flirtatious banter, while Matteo and Chiara exchange numbers and begin a romance. Before either relationship can go too far, however, the film rewinds to the day the four first met, and a series of mishaps that keep the original pairs from their first dates leads them to pair off differently: Matteo and Giulia build a tender relationship, while Dario and Chiara clash constantly despite their mutual attraction. The narrative then cuts back and forth between the two parallel lives, often swapping one couple for the other in the same setting, as the relationships move through courtship, conflict and commitment in locations that range from Italy to Lisbon and London. Rather than declaring one combination correct, the story suggests that a soulmate depends on timing, the stage of life a person has reached and the willingness to make a relationship work, and it leaves viewers to decide which pairing is the right one.

Reviewers compared the film to Sliding Doors. Critics generally praised the warmth and chemistry of the four leads, especially Gioli's lively performance as Giulia, but some found the constant cross-cutting more confusing than meaningful. Decider judged it watchable yet forgettable, while Leisurebyte called it an easy, appealing modern romance that handles its double narrative clearly.

documents.title: Falling for Christmas
documents.tagline: This holiday season, fall for the unexpected.
documents.overview: An engaged, spoiled hotel heiress finds herself in the care of a handsome, blue-collar lodge owner and his precocious daughter after getting amnesia in a skiing accident.
documents.plot:
Falling for Christmas is an American Christmas romantic comedy of 2022 directed by Janeen Damian, in her feature directing debut, from a screenplay by Jeff Bonnett and Ron Oliver. Lindsay Lohan stars as Sierra Belmont, a pampered hotel heiress who loses her memory in a skiing accident, with Chord Overstreet as the widowed lodge owner Jake Russell, George Young as her boyfriend Tad and Jack Wagner as her father Beauregard.

Sierra has just been named "vice president of atmosphere" at her father's luxury ski resort in Aspen, a job she has no interest in. With Beauregard away on business, Tad takes her up a mountain for a photo shoot and proposes, but a gust of wind knocks her off balance on her skis. She tumbles down the slope and hits her head on a tree. Jake, whose business pitch her father had just rejected, finds her unconscious and takes her to the hospital, where she wakes with amnesia and the staff cannot identify her. Jake offers her a room at his struggling bed and breakfast, the Northstar Lodge, until her memory returns or someone claims her.

Taking the name Sarah from Avy's stuffed toy, Sierra tries to make herself useful around the lodge. She grows close to Jake and especially to Avy, who lost her mother a couple of years earlier; Sierra's own mother died when she was young, and the shared grief begins to stir her memories. Gradually adapting to ordinary life, she organizes a fundraising party to save the lodge. Tad, meanwhile, is lost in the woods until a recluse named Ralph shelters him and walks him back to town. When Beauregard returns four days later and learns his daughter is missing, he alerts the sheriff.

At the party the town rallies behind the Northstar, which is declared a historic site, but before Jake can thank Sierra, her father and Tad burst in to take her home, and her memory comes back. Back at the resort she surprises everyone by doing her own chores and resigns the job her father created for her, resolving to find her own way. Avy confesses that her Christmas wish was for her father to find love and urges him to go after Sierra. Realizing she loves Jake, Sierra ends her engagement to Tad, who takes it well, having become interested in the guest services manager Terry. Jake declares his love, and Sierra returns to help run the lodge, while Beauregard invests in it out of gratitude.

Netflix released the film on 10 November 2022, and it debuted at number one on the service's most-watched films list. Reviews were mixed.

documents.title: Speak No Evil
documents.overview: A Danish family visits a Dutch family they met on a holiday. What was supposed to be an idyllic weekend slowly starts unraveling as the Danes try to stay polite in the face of unpleasantness.
documents.plot:
Speak No Evil (Danish: Gæsterne, "The Guests") is a 2022 Danish-Dutch psychological horror film directed by Christian Tafdrup from a screenplay he co-wrote with his brother Mads Tafdrup. Morten Burian and Sidsel Siem Koch play a Danish couple and Fedja van Huêt and Karina Smulders the Dutch couple who invite them to visit. It is performed largely in English.

On holiday in Tuscany, the Danish couple Bjørn and Louise and their young daughter, Agnes, befriend the outgoing Dutch couple Patrick and Karin and their son, Abel. Later, an invitation arrives asking them to visit their new friends' home in the Dutch countryside, and the restless Bjørn persuades his wife to accept. The weekend soon becomes uncomfortable. The hosts ignore Louise's vegetarianism, treat Abel, who they say was born without a tongue, with startling harshness, and push their guests' boundaries in ways that are small but unsettling, from leaving the children with an unfamiliar babysitter, Muhajid, to driving drunk and walking in on Louise in the shower. When Louise finds Agnes asleep beside a naked Patrick, the family leaves in the night, but they return when Agnes misses her stuffed rabbit, and the hosts persuade them to stay. Each time, politeness and fear of making a scene keep the guests from acting on their instincts.

They learn that Patrick lied about being a doctor, and on the final night Bjørn discovers a shed full of photographs showing Patrick and Karin with other families with children, along with their belongings, and finds Abel drowned in the pool. The family flees, but Bjørn does not tell Louise what he has seen. When their car breaks down on a remote road, Patrick catches up with them. Bjørn, beaten and passive, fails to resist as Karin cuts out Agnes's tongue and Muhajid takes the girl away. Driven to a deserted quarry, Bjørn asks why they are doing this, and Patrick answers simply: because you let me. The couple are forced to undress and are stoned to death, while the mute Agnes is shown taking Abel's place as the killers target another family.

Speak No Evil premiered in the Midnight section of the 2022 Sundance Film Festival and was released in Danish cinemas on March 17, 2022. Critics praised its direction, performances and mounting dread, as well as its bleak satire of middle-class manners and the danger of passivity in the face of evil. An American remake starring James McAvoy was released in 2024.

documents.title: No Exit
documents.tagline: Who will survive the dead of winter?
documents.overview: Stranded at a rest stop in the mountains during a blizzard, a recovering addict discovers a kidnapped child hidden in a car belonging to one of the people inside the building which sets her on a terrifying struggle to identify who among them is the kidnapper.
documents.plot:
No Exit is an American thriller of 2022 directed by Damien Power and adapted by writers Andrew Barrer and Gabriel Ferrari from Taylor Adams's novel of 2017. Havana Rose Liu stars as Darby Thorne, a recovering addict, with Danny Ramirez as Ash, David Rysdahl as Lars, Dale Dickey as Sandi, Dennis Haysbert as her husband Ed, a former Marine, Mila Harris as the kidnapped girl Jay and Benedict Wall as Corporal Ron Hill.

Told that her mother is undergoing emergency surgery for a brain aneurysm, Darby flees rehab despite her estranged sister Devon's warnings and drives toward Salt Lake City. A blizzard closes the interstate, and Ron directs her to a visitor centre where four strangers are also sheltering: Ash, Lars, Ed and Sandi. Searching outside for a phone signal, Darby finds a young girl bound inside one of their vans. Unable to call for help, she uses a card game to quiz the others about where they are travelling and concludes that Lars is the kidnapper. Sneaking out through a damaged bathroom wall, she promises the girl, Jay, she will save her, and learns that Jay has Addison's disease and needs medication. Darby confides in Ash, who seems to help by modifying a nail gun, but Jay reveals that Ash and Lars are partners. Ash seizes Darby's phone and, after a struggle, the pair force her to help search for Jay, who has escaped into the snow; Ash admits they are delivering her to a trafficking ring run by an Uncle Kenny.

Darby escapes and warns Ed and Sandi, and Ed bargains for Jay's medicine. But Jay recognises Sandi as her housekeeper, who helped arrange the abduction expecting a ransom to clear Ed's gambling debts. Ash kills Ed and Sandi and nails Darby's wrist to a wall, telling her that her mother has died, though a second text shows her message to the police went through. Numbing herself with heroin, Darby frees herself; Jay triggers the nail gun into Lars, who dies after falling. In the final struggle Ron arrives, is deceived by Ash and shoots Darby, and is himself killed by Ash before Darby stabs Ash fatally with a screwdriver and radios for help. Later, sober for 48 days, she is told her sister Devon has come to visit.

Intended for cinemas, the film was released by 20th Century Studios on Hulu in February 2022. Reviews were mixed, with 62% on Rotten Tomatoes, many calling it reasonably diverting popcorn entertainment.

documents.title: The House of Flowers: The Movie
documents.original_title: La Casa de las Flores: la película
documents.overview: The De La Mora siblings concoct a mischievous plan to break into their old family home to retrieve a hidden treasure of significant importance.
documents.plot:
The House of Flowers: The Movie is a poignant and powerful exploration of grief, trauma, and the cyclical nature of life and death. Set against the backdrop of a mysterious and magical flower that blooms only once every 27 years, the film delves into the complex web of emotions and relationships within the Moreno family.

At its core, the movie is a deeply personal and emotional journey for its protagonist, Lila, as she grapples with the loss of her mother and the weight of her family's dark past. Through Lila's story, the film masterfully weaves together themes of trauma, identity, and the struggle to break free from the shackles of one's heritage.

The movie also explores the idea of time and its relationship to human experience, as embodied by the enigmatic flower that serves as a symbol of both life and death. The film's use of this motif allows for a rich exploration of the cyclical nature of time, highlighting how our experiences are intertwined with those of previous generations.

Furthermore, The House of Flowers: The Movie is a powerful commentary on the societal expectations placed upon women, particularly in Latin American cultures. Lila's journey is marked by her struggle to assert her own identity and desires, while navigating the complex web of family obligations and cultural traditions that seek to constrain her.

Ultimately, the film is a hauntingly beautiful exploration of the human experience, one that invites viewers to reflect on their own relationships with grief, trauma, and the complexities of life.

documents.title: Teen Titans Go! See Space Jam
documents.original_title: Teen Titans Go! See Space Jam
documents.overview: The Teen Titans are visited by the Nerdlucks, the Space Jam villains who tried to capture Michael Jordan and the Looney Tunes. Astonished to discover his fellow Titans have never seen Space Jam, Cyborg organizes an exclusive watch party.
documents.plot:
Teen Titans Go! See Space Jam is a 2021 American animated television film directed by Peter Rida Michail and written by Brady Klosterman, a crossover between the Cartoon Network series Teen Titans Go! and the 1996 Warner Bros. film Space Jam. Produced by Warner Bros. Animation with DC Entertainment, it premiered on Cartoon Network on 20 June 2021, ahead of Space Jam: A New Legacy, and was released digitally in late July. Originally titled Space Jam 1.5, it follows the format of Mystery Science Theater 3000: the Titans watch an abridged version of the original film and comment on it throughout. Scott Menville, Khary Payton, Hynden Walch, Tara Strong and Greg Cipes return as Robin, Cyborg, Starfire, Raven and Beast Boy, with John DiMaggio and Fred Tatasciore voicing the Nerdlucks.

The Titans are relaxing by the pool at Titans Tower when a spaceship lands and the Nerdlucks, the small aliens who tried to kidnap Michael Jordan and the Looney Tunes in Space Jam, step out carrying a VHS copy of the film. Robin is convinced they are evil, but the others overrule him and invite them in. Astonished to discover that his teammates have never seen Space Jam, Cyborg organises a watch party. As the film plays, Raven and Starfire supply running commentary, with Starfire pointing out plot holes, Cyborg presents fun facts, Beast Boy keeps count of the film's many butt shots, and Robin keeps a suspicious eye on the guests. When the movie shows the Nerdlucks stealing the talents of NBA players, the Titans pause it and, apart from Robin, let the visitors try the trick on them: Blanko takes Cyborg's powers, Bupkus Raven's, Bang Beast Boy's and Nawt Starfire's, while Pound is left unchanged because Robin has no powers to give. As the screening continues, the question is whether the Nerdlucks have come for an innocent party or have something more sinister in mind.

New animated sequences of the Titans are spliced into the archive footage, which features Michael Jordan, Wayne Knight, Bill Murray and Billy West as Bugs Bunny. Much of the original was trimmed for time, and its well-known songs were replaced with other music, apparently for licensing reasons.

Reviewers found the premise fun but the execution unbalanced. It's A Stampede! praised the humour of the Titans' commentary and its jokes about parts of Space Jam that have aged badly, but felt there was too much of the old film and too little new Titans material, leaving a hybrid that works fully as neither.

documents.title: First Love
documents.overview: A young man’s difficult entry into adulthood, who experiences the highs and lows of his first love, while dealing with the familial fallout spurred by the financial crisis of 2008.
documents.plot:
First Love is a 2022 American romance film written and directed by A. J. Edwards, starring Hero Fiennes Tiffin as Jim Albright and Sydney Park as Ann, with Diane Kruger and Jeffrey Donovan as Jim's parents, Kay and Greg Albright, and Diane Venora as Kay's Aunt Irene. Filmed in Los Angeles, it follows how two young people meet in high school, drift apart and find their way back to each other over the following years, while Jim's family struggles through hard times.

When the 2008 recession costs his father Greg his bank job, high school senior Jim hopes to apply to colleges that might offer him at least a partial track scholarship. Racing to finish a paper in the school library, he catches sight of a fellow senior, Ann, through a bookcase and is instantly smitten. Too shy to approach her normally, Jim pulls her out of Spanish class with a fake note from the administration just so he can talk to her, and after school she asks him for a ride, which turns into an afternoon spent at a spot overlooking the ocean. As Greg searches for work and Kay wrestles with caring for her Aunt Irene, who raised her, and endures criticism of Greg from her brother, Jim and Ann's romance deepens; he brings her home to meet his parents and tells her he loves her. Ann's mother, however, urges her to keep the relationship casual so that she can be free when she goes to college, and when Ann reveals she will attend college in New York while Jim stays in California, she asks to keep things light. The couple drift apart, they graduate, and Jim leaves for UCLA as his unemployed parents are forced to downsize their home. Two years later, Jim finds his parents worn down by financial hardship, just as an unexpected voicemail from Ann gives the pair a chance to discover whether their first love can survive the realities of adult life.

The film was released in theaters and on demand in the United States on June 17, 2022. Its original score by Richard Reed Parry was replaced with one by George Kallis. It holds a 33% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from six reviews, and Matt Zoller Seitz of RogerEbert.com noted the film's considerable untapped potential while finding it watchable thanks to its cinematography and performances.

documents.title: Ben 10: Ben 10,010
documents.overview: In a future where an adult Gwen Tennyson is president and the world is being taken over by the alien horde known as the Xerge, a disillusioned Ben 10000 is called out of retirement to recruit his 10-year old version from the past.
documents.plot: In a future where an adult Gwen Tennyson is president and the world is being taken over by the alien horde known as the Xerge, a disillusioned Ben 10,000 is called out of retirement to recruit his 10-year-old version from the past. Based on the 2016 reboot.

documents.title: Ted Bundy: American Boogeyman
documents.tagline: America's most notorious serial killer.
documents.overview: Set in a gritty and decadent 1970s America, American Boogeyman follows the elusive and charming killer and the manhunt that brought him to justice involving the detective and the FBI rookie who coined the phrase ‘serial killer’.
documents.plot:
Ted Bundy: American Boogeyman is a psychological thriller that delves into the dark and twisted mind of one of America's most infamous serial killers, Ted Bundy. The film masterfully weaves together themes of trauma, manipulation, and the blurring of reality.

At its core, the movie explores the concept of identity and how it can be distorted by traumatic experiences. Bundy's character is a complex web of contradictions, with a charming exterior hiding a sinister and violent interior. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Bundy's actions were not just driven by a desire for power or control, but also by a deep-seated need to cope with his own emotional pain.

The film also examines the theme of gaslighting, where Bundy expertly manipulates those around him, including his victims and even some of his acquaintances. This manipulation is a key aspect of his modus operandi, allowing him to present himself as a normal, even likable person, while concealing his true nature.

Furthermore, Ted Bundy: American Boogeyman touches on the idea of how trauma can be passed down through generations, with Bundy's actions serving as a manifestation of his own traumatic experiences. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, adding depth and complexity to the story.

Overall, the movie presents a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, delving into the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of trauma and manipulation.

documents.title: Masquerade
documents.tagline: The ultimate disguise in terror.
documents.overview: A young girl struggles to survive after a group of home invaders break into her house to steal her family's priceless artwork.
documents.plot:
Masquerade is a 2021 American home invasion thriller written and directed by Shane Dax Taylor. Bella Thorne and Alyvia Alyn Lind star, alongside Austin Nichols, Mircea Monroe and Skyler Samuels. The film was produced by XYZ Films and distributed by Shout! Factory, which released it on July 30, 2021.

The story intercuts two threads. At a local charity event, art broker Daniel and his wife Olivia have too much to drink and accept a ride home from Rose, a waitress who offers to drive them. Meanwhile, in a seemingly parallel storyline, young Casey is being looked after by her babysitter Sofia when the power suddenly goes out. Sofia goes to investigate and is attacked and accidentally killed by two masked burglars who have come to steal the family's valuable art collection. Casey hides from the intruders and finds a revolver.

When Daniel and Olivia arrive home, their house is dark. Daniel goes to inspect the power lines while Olivia is ambushed and knocked unconscious inside. Searching for his wife, Daniel is attacked by a masked Rose, who stabs him and drags him into a room, where she forces him to reveal the combination to his safe. In the parallel storyline, Casey manages to shoot and kill one of the burglars, but the other overpowers her and shoots her with her own weapon. As she lies bleeding on the floor, he taunts her and blames her for what has happened, then removes his mask, revealing himself to be a younger Daniel, before leaving her to die.

The film's final twist reveals that the scenes with Casey were flashbacks to events years earlier. Rose is in fact the adult Casey, who survived the attack. Daniel had murdered her parents and stolen their artwork, the foundation of his career as an art dealer, and Rose has now conspired with Sofia's sister to take revenge on him and reclaim what was taken from her family on that night.

The project was announced in December 2019, when Thorne, Lind, Nichols, Monroe and Samuels were confirmed in the cast, with Taylor directing from his own screenplay; principal photography began the same month. Shout! Factory acquired distribution rights in March 2021. Critical reception was poor. The review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes surveyed fifteen critics and judged only two of the reviews to be positive, giving the film a 13% rating with an average score of 3.4 out of 10.

documents.title: Against the Ice
documents.tagline: Survive the search. Survive each other.
documents.overview: In 1909, two explorers fight to survive after they're left behind while on a Denmark expedition in ice-covered Greenland.
documents.plot:
Against the Ice is a 2022 historical survival drama directed by Peter Flinth, with a screenplay by Nikolaj Coster-Waldau and Joe Derrick adapted from Ejnar Mikkelsen's memoir Two Against the Ice. Coster-Waldau plays the Danish explorer Mikkelsen and Joe Cole his companion Iver Iversen, with Charles Dance, Heida Reed and Gísli Örn Garðarsson. Shot in Iceland and Greenland, it premiered at the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival in February 2022 and was released on Netflix on March 2, 2022.

In 1909, Captain Ejnar Mikkelsen leads the Alabama expedition to Shannon Island in north-east Greenland. His goal is to recover the records of the ill-fated Denmark expedition, whose leader died while mapping the coast. The documents are crucial because the United States claims that a channel divides Greenland in two, which would undermine Denmark's sovereignty over the north of the island. A first attempt to reach the records fails and costs a crewman his toes to frostbite, but on the way Mikkelsen finds the body of a member of the earlier expedition with a map showing the location of a cairn.

Only the inexperienced engineer Iver Iversen volunteers to join him on a second attempt. The two set off by dog sled across the ice, gradually sacrificing their dogs to feed the remaining ones, and fight off a polar bear. After three months they find the cairn and its records, which prove that there is no channel and that Greenland is a single island. Fearing they may not survive the return journey, they leave the documents in a new cairn hundreds of kilometres from their base.

When they finally reach Shannon Island, they find that their ship has been crushed and the crew has gone home, leaving them stranded. They spend two winters in a small hut built from the wreckage, as hope of rescue fades. They retrieve the hidden records, while would-be rescuers visit the hut in their absence and find no one. Isolation and hunger push them towards madness: Mikkelsen imagines his beloved Naja is with him, Iversen sees his grandfather, and Mikkelsen almost shoots his companion.

In 1912 a Norwegian sealing ship finally rescues them, and their evidence supports Denmark's claim to the whole of Greenland. An epilogue notes that Mikkelsen married Naja the following year and that the two men remained lifelong friends. Reviews were mixed, with 57% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: The Exorcism of God
documents.tagline: God and the Devil cannot exist in the same body.
documents.overview: An American priest working in Mexico is considered a saint by many local parishioners. However, due to a botched exorcism, he carries a secret that’s eating him alive until he gets an opportunity to face his demon one final time.
documents.plot:
The Exorcism of God is a 2021 supernatural horror film directed by Alejandro Hidalgo, who co-wrote the screenplay. It stars Will Beinbrink as an American priest confronting the consequences of a failed exorcism, with María Gabriela de Faría, Irán Castillo, Joseph Marcell and Hector Kotsifakis. The film premiered at Fantastic Fest on September 27, 2021, and Saban Films released it in theaters and on digital platforms on March 11, 2022.

In 2003, Father Peter Williams, an American priest working in Mexico, performs an exorcism on a young woman named Magali Velasquez. During the ritual the demon briefly gains the upper hand over him, although exactly what happens is left unclear. Peter continues his ministry and devotes the following years to charitable work in a small Mexican town.

Eighteen years later, a deadly illness begins to spread among the town's children, and a young inmate in the local prison, Esperanza, shows violent signs of demonic possession. Peter is summoned to exorcise her, but the encounter shakes him deeply. Magali then reveals that Esperanza is her daughter and begs him to save her at any cost. Realising he cannot face the threat alone, Peter turns to Father Michael Lewis, an experienced exorcist.

When the two priests return to the prison, they discover that the demon has spread its influence to many of the inmates, and they are forced to barricade themselves in a room. Lewis asks why Peter's prayers seem to have no power and whether he is hiding a sin. Peter confesses that during the exorcism years earlier he was possessed and seduced by the demon in Magali, and that Esperanza is his own daughter. Lewis in turn admits that he never truly defeated the demon, Balban, in the past, but made a pact with it. He is then mortally wounded by a possessed inmate, warning Peter never to bargain with the demon.

Seeking to atone, Peter records a video confession for the Church, but the inmates overpower him. He wakes bound and surrounded by the possessed inmates and Esperanza, fully controlled by Balban, who begins a ritual intended to cut him off from God. As he tries to drive the demon out, he is forced to watch children in the town's church die one by one. Offered a terrible choice between saving the children, saving his daughter or giving up his faith, Peter renounces God and lets Balban take him. The film ends with the possessed priest smiling triumphantly.

Reviews were mixed, with 57% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 41.

documents.title: Not Okay
documents.tagline: Get famous or lie trying.
documents.overview: An ambitious young woman, desperate for followers and fame, fakes a trip to Paris to up her social media presence. When a terrifying incident takes place in the real world and becomes part of her imaginary trip, her white lie becomes a moral quandary that offers her all the attention she’s wanted.
documents.plot:
Not Okay is a 2022 American satirical black comedy-drama film written and directed by Quinn Shephard. Zoey Deutch stars as Danni Sanders, a young woman desperate for online fame, with Mia Isaac, Dylan O'Brien, Nadia Alexander, Embeth Davidtz and Karan Soni. It was released by Searchlight Pictures on Hulu on 29 July 2022. The film opens with a mock content warning about an "unlikable female protagonist," a self-aware joke about audiences' reactions to flawed women characters.

Danni is an aspiring writer working as a photo editor at Depravity, an online magazine in New York City, where she struggles both professionally and socially. Hoping to impress Colin, a coworker and social media influencer on whom she has a crush, she claims she has been invited to a writers' retreat in Paris. She spends the following week in her Brooklyn apartment posting doctored photos of herself in Paris and creates a website for the fictional retreat, gaining a modest following, Colin included. Moments after she posts an edited image of herself at the Arc de Triomphe, terrorist bombings strike several Paris landmarks, including the Arc.

To maintain her lie, Danni claims to have witnessed the attacks and stages her return from Paris. Showered with sympathy by her parents, colleagues and a growing online audience, she leans into the deception and becomes a social media sensation as a survivor. At a trauma support group, she befriends Rowan Aldren, a teenage survivor of a school shooting who has become a prominent anti-gun activist, and, inspired by her, writes a viral essay about her supposed trauma that brings her fame, a hashtag movement and the attention she always craved. But as her friendship with Rowan deepens and her public profile grows, keeping the lie becomes increasingly difficult, and its eventual exposure brings devastating consequences for Danni and for those she has deceived.

Not Okay received generally positive reviews. Critics praised Deutch's daring performance as a deliberately unsympathetic heroine, O'Brien's comic turn as the vapid influencer Colin, and Isaac's moving portrayal of Rowan, as well as Shephard's sharp satire of internet culture and the pursuit of online fame, although some felt its tonal shifts were uneven.

documents.title: Choose or Die
documents.tagline: Sometimes a curse can be a gift.
documents.overview: In pursuit of an unclaimed $125,000 prize, a broke college dropout decides to play an obscure, 1980s survival computer game. But the game curses her, and she’s faced with dangerous choices and reality-warping challenges. After a series of unexpectedly terrifying moments, she realizes she’s no longer playing for the money but for her life.
documents.plot:
Choose or Die, originally titled CURS>R, is a 2022 British science fiction horror thriller directed by Toby Meakins in his feature debut. It stars Iola Evans as Kayla, a struggling student, and Asa Butterfield as her friend Isaac, with Robert Englund and Eddie Marsan. The story centers on a cursed 1980s computer game that forces its players to make terrible choices with real-world consequences.

In the prologue, Hal, a collector of retro video games, installs an old text-based adventure game called CURS>R, only to find that the choices he makes in the game take horrifying effect in his own home. Three months later, Kayla, a college student working as a cleaner to pay for her studies, discovers a copy of the game at the apartment of her friend Isaac, a programmer who is helping her learn to code. The game comes with a phone number promising a prize of 125,000 dollars to anyone who completes it. Desperate for money to help her mother, who has become addicted to drugs after the death of Kayla's brother and is being exploited by a predatory landlord, Kayla begins to play.

She soon realizes that the game can manipulate reality, forcing her to choose between horrifying options that harm the people around her. When she tries to destroy the game, it escapes onto the internet and continues to pursue her, exploiting her deepest traumas, including the drowning of her brother. Working with Isaac, Kayla investigates the game's origins and discovers that its creator embedded an ancient curse in its code to feed on players' suffering. To survive and save the people she loves, Kayla must reach the end of the game and face its final challenge, which leads her to Hal.

The film draws on 1980s gaming nostalgia and pairs its supernatural premise with themes of poverty, trauma and exploitation.

Choose or Die was released on Netflix on 15 April 2022. It received negative to mixed reviews, with 30 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said its frightening promise was muffled by an excessively franchise-focused story, and a Metacritic score of 43. The Guardian gave it two stars out of five.

documents.title: Bright: Samurai Soul
documents.original_title: ブライト: サムライソウル
documents.overview: Izo, a Ronin, and Raiden, an orc, work to bring a young elf girl and the wand she carries to the land of the elves in the north.
documents.plot:
Bright: Samurai Soul (Japanese: Buraito: Samurai Sōru) is a 2021 adult animated action film directed by Kyōhei Ishiguro from a script by Michiko Yokote, and a spin-off of the 2017 film Bright that sets its world of elves, orcs and magic wands in Japan at the time of the Meiji Restoration. Netflix announced it during its Geeked Week in June 2021 and released it on October 12, 2021. Arect produced the animation, rendered in 3D computer graphics styled after Japanese woodblock prints, with character designs by Atsushi Yamagata.

In 1868, the swordsman Izou is defending Shogun Yoshinobu Tokugawa at Edo Castle when a dazzling elven spell halts the battle. Years later he works as a guard at a brothel, where the high courtesan Chihaya, who has lost her memory, takes in Sonya, a defiant young elf girl from Russia, and shows her a map of Hakodate, an elven land across the sea. An army of orcs, goblins and dwarves attacks the brothel in search of the girl, and its leader promises the orc warrior Raiden his freedom if he finds her. Chihaya is fatally stabbed protecting Sonya and, before dying, asks her to carry her hairpin to Hakodate.

Izou and Raiden rescue Sonya. She offers the hairpin to hire Izou as her protector, and Raiden disowns his employer for hunting elves. The trio is ambushed at an inn, where Izou recalls how the traitor Kōketsu cost him his eye, and they plunge into a river. An old centaur named Tsukuyomi rescues the two warriors and sends them after Sonya, who has been taken. In Yokohama, Chihaya's twin sister tells them that the hairpin is actually a magic wand. At the Inferni estate, Kōketsu kills Izou, but Sonya uses the wand to revive him, and together they destroy Kōketsu. Believing that people must solve their own problems, Izou throws the wand into the ocean.

The Japanese voice cast is led by Yūki Nomura, in his first voice role, with Daisuke Hirakawa, Shion Wakayama, the musician Miyavi, also making his voice-acting debut, Maaya Sakamoto, Kenjiro Tsuda and Mamoru Miyano. Simu Liu, Fred Mancuso and Yuzu Harada lead the English dub, which also features Keone Young and Paul Nakauchi. On Rotten Tomatoes, two of the five critics' reviews counted were positive, an approval rating of 40%.

documents.title: Dragon Fury
documents.tagline: They thought they could control it. They were wrong.
documents.overview: A group of soldiers are taken to the mountains of Wales to investigate a strange looking monster.
documents.plot:
Dragon Fury, also known as Dragon's Fury, is a 2021 British low-budget fantasy horror film directed and edited by Scott Jeffrey, who wrote the screenplay with the visual effects designer Rhys Waterfield. Produced by Jagged Edge Productions and distributed by ITN Distribution, it stars Nicola Wright as Vanessa Reid, with Chelsea Greenwood, Sofia Lacey, Chrissie Wunna as Nicole, Andrew Rolfe as Professor Palson, Richard Lovell and Rachel Roberts. Josh Reichental composed the score, and the film runs 88 minutes under the tagline "They thought they could control it. They were wrong."

A remote area of the Welsh mountains has been abandoned for years because of radiation; no one knows why, and no one dares to enter. When a pair of vloggers venture into the hills, they discover the reason when they are burned alive by a dragon. The army calls in Vanessa Reid and her small team of special operatives to investigate the creature. Her unlikely team consists of two women, one of them injured and on crutches and the other soon developing a strange illness that may be linked to the dragons and to the radiation on the mountainside. The trio meet Professor Palson and his assistant Nicole, who clearly know more about what is happening in the mountains than they admit. Most of the action unfolds indoors as a dragon egg prepares to hatch, people begin losing their minds and tensions erupt among the group. A small dragon returns at the end, the creatures turn out to have evolved from the traditional dragon form into something more bird-like, and a closing scene hints at a much larger dragon to come.

The film was scheduled for release in the United Kingdom in September 2021. Reviews were negative. Phil Wheat of Nerdly gave it two out of five, noting that there were few furious dragons in Dragon Fury and that most of its running time was taken up with talk, although he credited thoughtful details in the sparingly used computer-generated effects, such as the dragons casting shadows, and their unusual bird-like design. Ade Smith of Movies & Mania found it a mostly dull drama after a promising opening in a rugged landscape, criticizing its implausible trio of operatives and silly final reveal while praising Wright's performance and Reichental's score. Voices from the Balcony called the computer effects variable, the dragon itself cool-looking, and the plot predictable.

documents.title: Dinosaur Hotel
documents.tagline: The hunt is on. And you're the prey.
documents.overview: Sienna is desperate to win a large cash prize in a secret underground game show. However, Dinosaur's begin to hunt her down for the entertainment of the rich and wealthy. Can she be the last to survive the horrific night to win the prize?
documents.plot:
Dinosaur Hotel is a 2021 British low-budget action horror film directed and photographed by Jack Peter Mundy, previously a cinematographer on several of the producer's films, from a screenplay by Shannon Holiday. It was produced by the prolific Scott Jeffrey, under his Jagged Edge Productions banner, with visual effects designer Rhys Waterfield, and distributed by ITN Distribution. The cast includes Chrissie Wunna, Nicole Nabi, Sofia Lacey, Chelsea Greenwood, Kate Sandison, Aimee Marie Higham, Alexander John and Stephen Staley. Released online in June 2021, the film runs 77 minutes and was followed within weeks by another dinosaur film from Jeffrey, Hatched.

The title refers both to the setting and to a secret underground game show staged there and streamed for the entertainment of the rich. A prologue reveals the game's twisted secret: its contestants are hunted by dinosaurs and there is no real way out. Sienna (Wunna), a down-on-her-luck mother desperate to win the large cash prize, signs up without knowing what the game involves and brings her two children along with her. At the hotel a floating orb relays the commands of the unseen Games Master, informing the women that their phones will not work and that the dinosaurs will try to kill them; whoever survives the night will win. While the other contestants are picked off one by one, Sienna's children wander off to explore before the game begins, venturing into a cave on the property, and her need to keep them safe gives her an edge as she fights to stay alive. One sequence echoes the famous kitchen scene from Jurassic Park, with raptors loose alongside one of her children.

Reviews were negative. Phil Wheat of Nerdly gave it two and a half stars out of five, describing it as Jurassic Park meets Escape Room and the weirdest game show ever conceived; he found the computer-generated dinosaurs fake-looking, the other contestants generic stereotypes and the premise unexplained, noting that Jurassic Games had told a similar story better, though he considered it better than some bigger-budget reality-TV horror films. Ade Smith of Movies & Mania thought the dinosaurs added novelty and the running time was agreeably short, but saw a distinct lack of suspense and urgency and weak acting. Other reviewers criticised its sparse attack scenes and poorly integrated effects.

documents.title: The Weekend Away
documents.tagline: Miles away from home. Where do you turn? Who can you trust?
documents.overview: When her best friend vanishes during a girls' trip to Croatia, Beth races to figure out what happened. But each clue yields another unsettling deception.
documents.plot:
