The Weekend Away is a 2022 American thriller directed by Kim Farrant from a screenplay by Sarah Alderson, adapted from her own 2020 novel of the same name. Leighton Meester stars as Beth, with Christina Wolfe as her best friend Kate, Ziad Bakri, Luke Norris and Amar Bukvić. Shot on location in Croatia, the film was released on Netflix on 3 March 2022 and became one of the service's most-watched titles in the following weeks, with nearly 80 million hours viewed in its first three weeks according to Netflix's own figures.

Beth, an American living in London with her husband Rob and their baby, travels to the Croatian city of Split for a weekend with her glamorous, recently divorced best friend Kate. Beth confides that her marriage has fallen into a rut. The two women go out to a nightclub, where a pair of men flirt with them, and Kate encourages Beth to have some fun. The next morning Beth wakes up with no clear memory of the night and finds that Kate is missing.

Rob and the local police seem unconcerned, but Zain, the friendly taxi driver who drove the women the night before, agrees to help Beth search. With his help she retrieves Kate's purse and phone from one of the men from the club and learns that the men were escorts Kate had hired, and that they are also con artists who drug and rob their clients. Beth goes back to the police, who open an investigation, but soon Kate's body is found in the sea, and Beth herself falls under suspicion. When Rob arrives in Croatia, he immediately distrusts Zain. Searching through Kate's phone for clues, Beth discovers messages revealing that Kate and Rob were having an affair. With the police treating her as their main suspect, Beth races to uncover who really killed her friend, as the tangled relationships among the people around her and Kate's secrets come to light.

The film received mixed to negative reviews, with a 39 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said it was painless enough home viewing but that Meester's performance deserved a better film. Dennis Harvey of Variety acknowledged its credibility gaps but found it a slick, pacey diversion. Critics generally praised Meester and the scenic Croatian locations while finding the plot twists predictable.

documents.title: Mortal Kombat Legends: Battle of the Realms
documents.original_title: Mortal Kombat Legends: Battle of the Realms
documents.tagline: The battle to end all battles.
documents.overview: The Earthrealm heroes must journey to the Outworld and fight for the survival of their homeland, invaded by the forces of evil warlord Shao Kahn, in the tournament to end all tournaments: the final Mortal Kombat.
documents.plot:
Mortal Kombat Legends: Battle of the Realms is a 2021 animated film that serves as a sequel to the previous Mortal Kombat Legends films, specifically Mortal Kombat Legends: Defenders of the Realm (2018). The movie takes place after the events of the first film and continues the story of the Mortal Kombat universe.

The plot begins with the return of Shao Kahn, the Emperor of Outworld, who seeks to conquer Earthrealm once again. However, this time, he is aided by a powerful being known as Kronika, the Timekeeper, who has been imprisoned for centuries but has now broken free from her prison.

Kronika reveals that she will reset the timeline and recreate the universe in her image, erasing all memories of the past and resetting the Mortal Kombat tournament to its original form. She also announces that she will be the one to decide the fate of Earthrealm and its inhabitants.

The story follows a group of characters from the previous films, including Liu Kang, Kitana, Sonya Blade, and Johnny Cage, who must band together once again to stop Kronika's plans. Along the way, they are joined by new allies, such as Cole Young, a young martial artist who becomes the new champion of Earthrealm.

As the battle against Kronika intensifies, the characters discover that she has created an army of robotic warriors known as the "Reapers," which are designed to destroy all life on Earth. The heroes must use their skills and work together to defeat the Reapers and stop Kronika's plans.

Throughout the film, there are also flashbacks and visions of the past, showcasing key moments in the Mortal Kombat history and the relationships between the characters. These sequences provide insight into the motivations and backstories of the characters, adding depth to the story.

In the climactic final battle, the heroes face off against Kronika and her army of Reapers. The fight is intense and action-packed, with many memorable moments and iconic moves from the Mortal Kombat franchise.

Ultimately, the heroes emerge victorious, but not without sacrifices. Liu Kang is mortally wounded in the battle, and as he lies dying, he passes on the mantle of Earthrealm's champion to Cole Young. The film ends with a sense of hope and renewal, as the new generation of heroes takes over and looks towards a brighter future.

Overall, Mortal Kombat Legends: Battle of the Realms is an exciting and action-packed animated film that stays true to the spirit of the Mortal Kombat franchise. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and stunning animation, it is a must-see for fans of the series.

documents.title: Deep
documents.original_title: โปรเจกต์ลับ หลับ เป็น ตาย
documents.overview: Four insomniac med school students are lured into a neuroscience experiment that spirals out of control and must find a way out before it’s too late.
documents.plot:
Deep (Thai: โปรเจกต์ลับ หลับ เป็น ตาย, roughly "Secret Project: Sleep, Live, Die") is a 2021 Thai mystery thriller film produced by Transformation Films and released on Netflix. It was written and directed by a team of students from Bangkok University, with directing credits shared by Sita Likitvanichkul, Jetarin Ratanaserikiat, Apirak Samudkidpisan, Thanabodee Uawithya and Adirek Wattaleela. Panisara Rikulsurakan stars as Jane, with Kay Lertsittichai as Win, Supanaree Sutavijitvong as Cin, Krit Jeerapattananuwong as Peach, Warisara Jitpreedasakul as June and Dujdao Vadhanapakorn as Professor Nichcha.

Jane, a medical student, lives with her delinquent younger sister June and cares for their grandmother. Overwhelmed by studying, housework and debt, she has become an insomniac. Her professor, Nichcha, suggests that she join a study run by a German pharmaceutical company. Its head scientist, Hans Miller, explains that the experiment, called Deep, has three levels and aims to harvest Qratonin, a brain chemical that keeps people awake, through a microchip implanted in the subject's neck. Promised generous rewards, Jane signs a non-disclosure agreement and receives the implant and a watch to monitor her Qratonin level, along with a warning: if she falls asleep for more than 60 seconds before reaching 100 percent, the chip will stop her heart.

Jane meets fellow subjects Win, a partygoer, Peach, a gaming nerd, and Cin, a popular student, and the four, calling themselves Non-Non, complete the first two levels as their sleep deprivation causes vivid hallucinations. When Cin discovers that Peach is the stalker she has been afraid of, she collapses and nearly dies, and the group quits and drifts apart. After Jane sees a student die because of Deep and her grandmother suffers a stroke, she learns that June has joined the experiment too; Hans warns that June's third level has begun and that the chip will not be removed unless Jane brings her friends back. The reunited group enters the final level, but by the sixth day chaos erupts. Jane discovers that the company is a front, Hans is an actor and Nichcha is the mastermind, harvesting Qratonin to revive her comatose lover, Jed, who fell from a building through lack of sleep. Nichcha locks them up, but the friends fake Win's death to trick her and overpower her. She is arrested, the chips are removed and the friends mend their lives.

documents.title: Poker Face
documents.tagline: Everyone has a limit.
documents.overview: A yearly high-stakes poker game between childhood friends turns into chaos when the tech billionaire host unveils an elaborate scheme to seek revenge for the ways they've betrayed him over the years. But as his plans unfold, a group of thieves hatch plans of their own breaking into the mansion thinking it is empty. The old friends quickly band together and the years of playing the game help them win their way through a night of terror.
documents.plot:
Poker Face is a 2022 Australian thriller written and directed by Russell Crowe, who also stars as Jake Foley, a tech billionaire. The cast includes Liam Hemsworth, RZA, Brooke Satchwell and Aden Young, and the film was shot in Australia, with much of the action confined to a single lavish, secluded mansion. The film had a limited theatrical release on 16 November 2022, followed by a video-on-demand release a week later.

Jake Foley, who made a fortune from software, invites his childhood friends to his luxurious, high-security mansion for a night of high-stakes poker. The group includes Mikey, Alex and Paul, men whose lives have taken very different paths since their youth and who have stayed bound by old loyalties and rivalries. As the cards are dealt, it soon becomes clear that Jake has a hidden purpose: he wants his friends to reveal the secrets they have kept for years, and he has taken steps to ensure that they tell the truth.

As the night goes on, the confessions emerge. Mikey admits that his life is miserable and that he has brought a gun with which he intends to kill himself. Alex reveals that he has been sleeping with Jake's wife. Paul confesses that, burdened by debts, he has been passing information about Jake's life to his brother Victor. The evening takes a dangerous turn when Victor and his gang break into the house intending to steal Jake's valuable art collection, and Jake's wife and daughter arrive unexpectedly. Trapped in the mansion with the robbers, the friends must put aside their grievances and band together to survive. Jake uses his skill at bluffing to outwit the intruders, telling Victor that he has drunk poison from one of the wine glasses and tricking him into taking a lethal dose under the pretense of an antidote.

Poker Face received negative reviews from critics, who found the plot convoluted and the shifts in tone awkward, although some praised Crowe's commanding screen presence. Several reviewers felt that its blend of character drama and home-invasion thriller never quite cohered.

documents.title: Bandit
documents.tagline: He pulled off the perfect heist 59 times.
documents.overview: After escaping a Michigan prison, a charming career criminal assumes a new identity in Canada and goes on to rob a record 59 banks and jewellery stores while being hunted by a rogue task force. Based on the story of The Flying Bandit.
documents.plot:
Bandit is a 2022 Canadian biographical crime film directed by Allan Ungar and written by Kraig Wenman. Josh Duhamel stars as Gilbert Galvan Jr., with Elisha Cuthbert, Nestor Carbonell and Mel Gibson. It is based on the true story of Galvan, known as the Flying Bandit, who holds the record for the most consecutive bank robberies in Canadian history, and draws largely on interviews and accounts in the 1996 true crime book The Flying Bandit by Robert Knuckle and Ed Arnold. Redbox Entertainment and Quiver Distribution released the film in North American theaters and on demand on 23 September 2022.

Gilbert Galvan Jr., a charming career criminal, escapes from a prison in Michigan and crosses the border into Ontario, where he takes on a new identity as Robert Whiteman. In Ottawa he falls in love with Andrea, a social worker played by Cuthbert, but he has no way of supporting the comfortable life he wants to give her. Needing money, he returns to crime with the help of Tommy Kay, a local crime boss played by Gibson, who agrees to fund his first heist in exchange for a share of the proceeds.

Galvan discovers that he has a remarkable talent for robbing banks. Using a series of elaborate disguises and posing as a security analyst whose job requires constant travel, he flies across Canada, sometimes robbing banks in several cities in a single day before returning home to his unsuspecting wife. As the robberies pile up, he becomes a folk hero of sorts, and the press nicknames him "the Flying Bandit." His growing notoriety attracts the attention of a determined police detective, Snyder, played by Carbonell, who becomes obsessed with catching him, while his double life puts increasing strain on his marriage and his partnership with Kay grows more dangerous. The film tracks the more than fifty robberies he committed over several years and the investigation that finally brought him down.

Bandit received mixed to positive reviews, with critics singling out Duhamel's charismatic performance and the film's light, playful tone, which treats its true-crime story as a breezy caper rather than a gritty drama.

documents.title: The Seven Deadly Sins: Cursed by Light
documents.original_title: 劇場版 七つの大罪 光に呪われし者たち
documents.overview: With the help of the "Dragon Sin of Wrath" Meliodas and the worst rebels in history, the Seven Deadly Sins, the "Holy War", in which four races, including Humans, Goddesses, Fairies and Giants fought against the Demons, is finally over. At the cost of the "Lion Sin of Pride" Escanor's life, the Demon King was defeated and the world regained peace. After that, each of the Sins take their own path.
documents.plot:
I have information on this movie.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Cursed by Light is a Japanese anime film directed by Norihiro Obuchi and produced by Studio Deen. The story takes place after the events of the third season of the anime series, The Seven Deadly Sins.

The film follows Meliodas, Elizabeth, and their friends as they face a new threat to their kingdom. A mysterious light appears in the sky, which is revealed to be a manifestation of the power of the Holy Knights' former leader, King. This power is known as "Cursed Light" and it's said that anyone who sees it will be consumed by its darkness.

As the story unfolds, Meliodas and his friends discover that the Cursed Light is actually a result of the Holy Knights' failure to defeat the Demon King. The light has become a powerful force that can manipulate people's emotions and desires, making them do its bidding.

The main antagonist of the film is revealed to be a mysterious figure known as "The King," who is actually a former Holy Knight turned traitor. He seeks revenge against Meliodas and his friends for their past actions, which he believes wronged him.

Throughout the story, Meliodas and his friends must navigate the consequences of their own actions and confront their personal demons in order to defeat The King and save their kingdom from destruction. Along the way, they also uncover secrets about the Holy Knights' past and the true nature of the Cursed Light.

The film features stunning animation and action sequences, as well as a deep exploration of the characters' emotional struggles. Overall, The Seven Deadly Sins: Cursed by Light is a thrilling and emotionally resonant conclusion to the series, offering fans a satisfying ending to their favorite storylines.

Note that this summary contains spoilers for those who have not seen the anime series or film.

documents.title: Dead for a Dollar
documents.tagline: Vengeance for the right price.
documents.overview: In 1897, veteran bounty hunter Max Borlund is deep into Mexico where he encounters professional gambler and outlaw Joe Cribbens — a sworn enemy he sent to prison years before. Max is on a mission to find and return Rachel Kidd, the wife of a wealthy businessman, who as the story is told to Max, has been abducted by Buffalo Soldier Elijah Jones. Max is ultimately faced with a showdown to save honor.
documents.plot: In 1897, veteran bounty hunter Max Borlund is deep into Mexico where he encounters professional gambler and outlaw Joe Cribbens — a sworn enemy he sent to prison years before. Max is on a mission to find and return Rachel Kidd, the wife of a wealthy businessman, who as the story is told to Max, has been abducted by Buffalo Soldier Elijah Jones. Max is ultimately faced with a showdown to save honor.

documents.title: Meet Cute
documents.tagline: Who says there's only one chance to make a first impression?
documents.overview: A wildly inventive deconstruction of the romantic comedy built around the question: What would you do if you could travel to your loved ones’ past, heal their traumas, fix their problems, and change them into the perfect partner?
documents.plot:
Meet Cute is a 2022 American romantic dark comedy directed by Alex Lehmann. Kaley Cuoco and Pete Davidson star as a woman who uses a time machine to relive a perfect first date over and over and the man she keeps meeting. Filmed in New York City in August 2021, it was released digitally on Peacock on September 21, 2022.

In Manhattan, Sheila discovers that a tanning bed in the back of a nail salon run by a woman named June is actually a time machine that sends her back one day. One evening she meets Gary, a gentle, slightly awkward man, in a bar. Their date is a delight: they share the same taste in drinks, trade stories about their childhoods and find an easy rapport. During the evening, Sheila casually tells Gary that she has been reliving this same night repeatedly, and the two part on warm terms.

Over the course of months of resets, Sheila reveals more. She first used the machine on the day she had planned to take her own life by jumping from the Manhattan Bridge, and her first date with Gary made her feel happy for the first time in years, so she keeps returning to it. She also mentions a kind cable repairman who was nice to her as a child, without knowing why the memory stays with her. When she tells Gary she loves him, it unsettles him.

After hundreds of identical evenings, Sheila grows restless and decides to improve Gary by traveling further back into his past. Posing as a neighbor, "Uncle Charlie," she gets the young Gary interested in sports and removes several negative influences from his life, turning him into a confident, successful businessman. When she admits what she has done, Gary is horrified, and although Sheila restores his original past, he begins experiencing déjà vu and pieces together the truth. Using what he has learned, Gary travels back in time himself in an attempt to help the young Sheila, and he turns out to have been the cable repairman who showed her kindness when she was a girl.

Realizing that endlessly reliving the same day no longer brings her joy, Sheila returns to the bridge. Alerted by June, Gary catches up with her and convinces her that the future is worth seeing, telling her that they meet again tomorrow. Sheila follows him off the bridge, and as the sun rises, the two begin a genuinely new day together.

Reviews were mixed; Rotten Tomatoes reported 59% approval, and Metacritic gave it 50 out of 100.

documents.title: Something in the Dirt
documents.overview: When neighbors John and Levi witness supernatural events in their LA apartment building, they realize documenting the paranormal could inject some fame and fortune into their wasted lives.
documents.plot:
Something in the Dirt is a 2022 American science fiction comedy horror film directed by and starring Justin Benson and Aaron Moorhead, from a screenplay by Benson. It is the fifth feature from the filmmaking duo, who conceived it during the COVID-19 lockdowns of 2020 and shot it over the course of a year with a crew of just twelve people, using Benson's own apartment as the main location. The film had its world premiere online at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival.

A man wakes up in a small, grimy apartment in Los Angeles. Through conversations with a neighbour we learn that he is Levi, a spear-fisherman who scrapes by on odd jobs, and that the neighbour, John, is an occasional maths teacher who belongs to an evangelical, apocalypse-minded church. The two strangers soon notice that something strange is happening in their building: a quartz object floats and glows of its own accord, revealing a mysterious symbol, and the apartment is troubled by unexplained lights, noises, tremors and radio signals.

Sensing an opportunity, the pair decide to make a documentary about the phenomenon. Their investigation leads them across the city, following a chain of clues and coincidences that seem to connect the events in their apartment to a wider pattern stretching across Los Angeles. As the project grows, so do the tensions between them. Levi repeatedly warns that the pursuit is becoming dangerous and suggests they stop, but John presses ahead regardless. He dismisses Levi's theories in favour of his own constantly shifting explanations, and he begins to show signs of compulsive lying and a callous disregard for others, ignoring unmistakable warnings such as sudden radiation burns and impossibly accelerated plant growth.

Eventually the two men have a bitter falling-out. That night John wakes to find himself floating above his bed before dropping back down, and when he goes outside he sees Levi suspended high in the sky. In documentary-style interviews, John later explains that Levi died, his mangled body found near a house the pair had investigated, surrounded by strange totems and a blacked-out manuscript. Asked to explain what happened, John says only that his calculations were wrong, and remains determined to finish the film.

Critics responded warmly. Rotten Tomatoes reported 91% positive reviews, its consensus saying the film reaffirms the duo's distinctive and darkly alluring vision, and Metacritic gave it a score of 76 out of 100.

documents.title: White Elephant
documents.tagline: Live by a code. Die by a bullet.
documents.overview: An ex-marine enforcer must battle his conscience and code of honor when he is forced to do things for the mob.
documents.plot:
White Elephant is a 2022 American action crime thriller directed by Jesse V. Johnson, who wrote the screenplay with Erik Martinez from his own story. Michael Rooker stars as Gabriel Tancredi, with Bruce Willis as Arnold Solomon, Olga Kurylenko as Vanessa Flynn and John Malkovich as the lawyer Glen Follett, alongside Vadhir Derbez, Michael Rose, Lauren Buglioli and Louie Ski Carr. It was produced by Corey Large through 308 Enterprises and BondIt Media Capital, with music by Sean Murray and cinematography by Jonathan Hall.

Gabriel is a widowed former Marine who has spent years as an enforcer for his friend, the mob boss Arnold Solomon, and is now mentoring a brash young protégé, Carlos Garcia (Derbez). Still mourning his wife, a wildlife activist, and regularly visiting her resting place, he dreams of leaving the life behind and using his skills to protect elephants in Africa, as she always wanted. When Solomon orders a hit on a Mexican gangster, Carlos botches the job and blows up a building, and the attack is witnessed by two police officers, Vanessa Flynn and her partner Walter Koschek (Rose). To protect himself, Solomon orders Gabriel to eliminate both witnesses.

Koschek is quickly killed, but Vanessa, an ex-soldier haunted by the violence she has seen on the job, proves far harder to catch, evading one kill squad after another. As Solomon's increasingly reckless decisions trigger more bloodshed and rival gangs move in, Gabriel finds himself drawn to Vanessa, discovering that she shares a birthday with his late wife. Torn between loyalty and his own code of honor, he decides for the first time in years to do the right thing, turning against Solomon to protect her. The conflict culminates at Gabriel's country house, where he and Vanessa fight off the remaining gunmen of Solomon's organization.

Filmed in Georgia beginning in April 2021, White Elephant is one of the last films Willis made before retiring from acting due to illness; crew members later described him as confused on set, and Johnson said he would not work with him again under such circumstances. The film was released in select US theaters by RLJE Films and on AMC+ on 3 June 2022. Reviews were mostly negative, with critics calling the script thin and repetitive, though Rooker's warm, commanding performance and the violent finale drew praise.

documents.title: Jerry & Marge Go Large
documents.tagline: It's never too late to risk it all.
documents.overview: The remarkable true story of how retiree Jerry Selbee discovers a mathematical loophole in the Massachusetts lottery and, with the help of his wife, Marge, wins $27 million dollars and uses the money to revive their small Michigan town.
documents.plot:
Jerry & Marge Go Large is a 2022 American comedy-drama directed by David Frankel and written by Brad Copeland, based on Jason Fagone's 2018 HuffPost article about a real-life retired couple who legally exploited a loophole in a state lottery. Bryan Cranston and Annette Bening star, with Rainn Wilson, Larry Wilmore and Michael McKean. It premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on June 15, 2022, and was released on Paramount+ two days later.

In the struggling small town of Evart, Michigan, Jerry Selbee is pushed into retirement after 42 years at a factory. A gifted mathematician with time on his hands, he discovers a statistical loophole in the state lottery game WinFall: when the jackpot reaches $2 million without a winner, the money "rolls down" to lower prize tiers, and anyone buying enough tickets is virtually guaranteed a profit. Testing the theory in secret, he first loses money, then buys far more tickets and turns a profit. When his wife, Marge, finds out, she is thrilled and wants to join in. After Michigan's WinFall is discontinued, the couple begin driving to Massachusetts, where a similar game exists, buying tickets at a store in Sunderland.

To increase their stakes, they form a corporation and sell shares to friends and neighbors. Their winnings grow, and the dividends help revive Evart, as shuttered businesses reopen and plans are made to bring back the town's jazz festival. Their success attracts the attention of Tyler, an arrogant Harvard student running his own WinFall syndicate, who discovers their operation and demands that they stop, threatening to hack their accounts. Jerry nearly gives up, but with the encouragement of his son and the town, he keeps playing. When Tyler manipulates the game to trigger a roll-down early, cutting the Selbees out, Jerry confronts him in front of his fellow students, who abandon him, and persuades the lottery commission to announce roll-downs publicly to level the playing field.

A Boston Globe report on the loophole leads to the game's cancellation. The Selbees decide to sit out the final roll-down, but their investors secretly travel to Massachusetts to buy tickets across the state for one last big win. At the revived jazz festival, Jerry and Marge are celebrated as the heroes who brought their town back to life, having won around $27 million over the years.

Reviews were mixed to positive. Rotten Tomatoes reported 67% approval, and Metacritic gave it 52 out of 100.

documents.title: Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog
documents.original_title: Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog
documents.tagline: Ooga! Booga! Booga!
documents.overview: With Mystery, Inc. on the tail of a strange object in Nowhere, Kansas, the strange hometown of Eustice, Muriel, and Courage, the gang soon find themselves contending with a giant cicada monster and her winged warriors.
documents.plot:
Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog is a 2021 animated film that brings together two beloved cartoon franchises, Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog. The movie follows the adventures of Shaggy Rogers (voiced by Robbie Daymond) and Scooby-Doo (voiced by Scott Innes), who are on their way to a music festival in Nowhere, Kansas.

Upon arrival, they meet Eustace Bagge (voiced by Jason Alexander), Courage's owner, and his family. However, things take a dark turn when the town is plagued by supernatural occurrences, including ghostly apparitions, monsters, and unexplained events. The Scooby-Doo gang soon discovers that these events are connected to an ancient curse that has been awakened in Nowhere.

As the mystery unfolds, Shaggy and Scooby team up with Courage (voiced by Eric Bauza) to uncover the truth behind the curse. Along the way, they encounter a range of bizarre characters, including a ghostly cowboy, a possessed preacher, and a mysterious woman who seems to be connected to the curse.

Throughout their investigation, Shaggy and Scooby use their signature skills to gather clues and solve puzzles, while Courage provides his own unique brand of cowardice to help them navigate the supernatural threats. Meanwhile, Eustace's family is torn apart by the events unfolding in Nowhere, leading to a heartwarming moment of connection between Shaggy and Muriel Bagge (voiced by Grey DeLisle).

As the mystery deepens, the Scooby-Doo gang discovers that the curse is connected to an ancient ritual that was performed by the town's founders. They must work together to break the curse and restore peace to Nowhere before it's too late.

The film features a mix of humor, action, and heart, blending the signature styles of both franchises. The animation is vibrant and colorful, with plenty of nods to the original Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog series. The voice cast delivers solid performances, bringing the characters to life in a way that feels true to their respective franchises.

Overall, Straight Outta Nowhere: Scooby-Doo! Meets Courage the Cowardly Dog is a fun and entertaining film that brings together two beloved cartoon franchises in a unique and exciting way. With its blend of humor, action, and heart, it's sure to delight fans of both Scooby-Doo and Courage the Cowardly Dog.

documents.title: Nanny
documents.tagline: We're haunted by what we leave behind.
documents.overview: Aisha, an undocumented immigrant, lands a job as a nanny for a wealthy Manhattan couple. As she prepares for the arrival of the son she left behind in Senegal, a violent presence begins to invade both her dreams and her reality, threatening to destroy the American Dream she is painstakingly piecing together.
documents.plot: Aisha, a Senegalese immigrant who takes a job as a nanny for a wealthy white family in New York City, finds herself consumed by unsettling visions and a growing rage.

documents.title: The Friendship Game
documents.tagline: Win together or die alone
documents.overview: A group of teens in a small town come across a strange object that tests their loyalties to each other with increasingly destructive consequences the deeper into the game they go.
documents.plot:
The Friendship Game is a 2022 Canadian science fiction horror film directed by Scooter Corkle, his second feature, from the first feature-length screenplay by Damien Ober. Produced by Social Construct and Scythia Films, it stars Peyton List, Brendan Meyer, Kelcey Mawema, Kaitlyn Santa Juana and Dylan Schombing, with Miranda Edwards and Jennifer Copping in supporting roles. RLJE Films released it in the United States on 11 November 2022.

Zooza, known as Z (List), Rob (Meyer), Courtney (Mawema) and Cotton (Santa Juana) are close friends in a small town who are at a turning point in their lives as they prepare to leave for college. While browsing at a yard sale, Z and Cotton come across a strange orb-like object, and the ominous woman selling it tells them that it is "the Friendship Game", which tests true friendship by having the players reveal their deepest desires. Unfazed, they buy it, and all four friends place their fingers on the object and confess what they most want. Their wishes come at an unexpected cost that begins to consume their lives: at a party soon afterwards, Cotton tries to warn the others that something is wrong, discovers Z and Rob together and storms off, and then disappears, prompting a police investigation. Meanwhile Kyle (Schombing), who spends most of his time at his computer, has been secretly watching the four friends, and the film increasingly blurs the digital and physical worlds with glitching, warped imagery. Told in chapters from each character's perspective, the story shows how the game sets the friends against one another with increasingly destructive consequences the deeper they go.

Reviews were largely negative, although Peyton List's performance was widely praised. Chase Hutchinson of Collider likened the premise to Wish Upon (2017) and felt the film gestured at the existential, internet-age concerns of We're All Going to the World's Fair, but said that, despite some occasionally enrapturing visuals, it spun its wheels and leaned on conventional scares that failed to land. Bobby LePire of Film Threat called it awful on every level except for List, who he said made the cringe-inducing dialogue believable and was the only cast member to inject real drama or fear, while criticising the rest of the cast, singling out Meyer for lacking screen presence. Screen Rant described it as a frustrating horror mystery that felt like a messy rough draft.

documents.title: Shattered
documents.tagline: She'll love him to death.
documents.overview: Chris, a wealthy divorcee, lives in a high-tech house of his own design in Montana. His life changes when he meets Sky, a mysterious young woman who draws him out of his shell and moves in after Chris is injured.
documents.plot:
Shattered is a 2022 American psychological thriller directed by Luis Prieto and written by David Loughery. Cameron Monaghan stars as Chris, a wealthy, recently separated tech entrepreneur, with Lilly Krug as Sky, the young woman who enters his life, Frank Grillo, Sasha Luss as Chris's estranged wife Jamie, and John Malkovich as Ronald, a motel landlord. It was released in January 2022.

Chris, who made his fortune creating Watchdog, a home security system, lives alone in his isolated, high-tech mansion and has been putting off signing the divorce papers sent by his wife, Jamie, who felt that his work always came first. During a late-night trip to a grocery store he meets Sky, and when her ride is canceled he offers to drive her home. At the run-down motel where she is staying, she hesitates to go inside, explaining that her roommate, Lisa, is unpredictable because of her drug use. Chris invites her back to his house to wait, they spend the night together, and she returns to the motel in the morning to find Lisa furious.

Soon after, Chris visits Sky at her workplace and, returning to his car, interrupts someone trying to break into it. In the ensuing struggle he is badly injured and left with a broken leg in a cast. With his mobility limited, Sky offers to look after him, and he gives her the access codes to his house, which is entirely controlled by Watchdog. When Sky goes back to the motel to collect her belongings, Lisa hints that she knows things about her and that Sky cannot simply leave. The motel's landlord, Ronald, fed up with excuses about overdue rent, lets himself into their rooms and makes a horrifying discovery. As Sky settles into Chris's home, her behavior grows increasingly sinister, and Chris, trapped by his injury inside his own fortress, gradually realizes that the woman caring for him has a hidden agenda involving his money, his security system and his estranged family.

Shattered received negative reviews, holding a 19 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27. Angela Dawson of Forbes was more positive, describing it as a simmering thriller reminiscent of classic femme fatale films with a modern sensibility, while most critics found it derivative and implausible.

documents.title: Taurus
documents.overview: A rising but troubled musician searches for the inspiration to record one last song, pushing himself deep into the void.
documents.plot:
Taurus, previously known as Good News, is a 2022 American drama film directed by Tim Sutton, who wrote it with Colson Baker, the rap-rock musician known as Machine Gun Kelly. Baker, who also served as executive producer and composer, stars as Cole, a fictional rock star closely modeled on his own celebrity image, with Maddie Hasson as his personal assistant, Ilana, Scoot McNairy as his manager, Ray, Ruby Rose as Bub, Megan Fox as his ex, Mae, and Naomi Wild as Lena.

The film follows the final days of Cole, a hugely popular but alienated and self-destructive musician, over the course of about a week in Los Angeles. He drifts between recording sessions, interviews, brand ambassador meetings, barroom binges and occasional, detached visits with his 10-year-old daughter, Rosie, while consuming an ever-growing array of drugs and alcohol. He spends his nights with a drug-dealer friend and a series of interchangeable lovers, returning to a sterile modernist mansion in the Hollywood Hills.

At the center of the story is his relationship with Ilana, his beleaguered and mistreated but devoted assistant, who acts as his surrogate mother, sister and babysitter. She ferries the remote, uncooperative Cole from one obligation to the next, tries to keep him functioning if not sober, absorbs the blame from his sharkish manager whenever he fails to deliver, and cleans up after him each morning. Cole has a tense, nearly wordless confrontation with Mae, and Lena, a singer, records a hook for one of his songs. A cryptic subplot follows a suburban tragedy involving one of Cole's fans. As Cole's physical and mental deterioration accelerates and Ilana's patience wears thin, the story moves toward its grim, inevitable end.

Taurus premiered in the Panorama section of the 72nd Berlin International Film Festival on February 13, 2022, and RLJE Films released it in limited theaters and on demand in the United States on November 18, 2022. Reviews were mixed, with 64% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 51; the Rotten Tomatoes consensus said it fails to delve deeply into the creative process but offers some insight into the double-edged nature of celebrity. Variety's Guy Lodge praised Baker's committed, unflattering performance and the film's atmospheric style but found Cole a hollow center, singling out Hasson as the film's heart. Deadline's Anna Smith found the bickering star-assistant relationship darkly funny and touching.

documents.title: Sonic 30th Anniversary Symphony
documents.overview: 30 years ago, on June 23rd, 1991, Sonic the Hedgehog was released on the SEGA Genesis, beginning a new era of gaming.  Since then, Sonic has been running through countless zones, beating badniks, and saving the world with the help of his friends.  This performance is to thank you, all of you, for being there every step of the way, and to remind us all of the amazing journey we've been on.  Happy 30th Anniversary, Sonic!
