documents.title: Jungle Run
documents.tagline: The search for their father... led them to hell!
documents.overview: A brother and sister's journey into the jungle to find their missing father.
documents.plot:
Jungle Run is a 2021 American adventure film directed and photographed by Noah Luke and produced by The Asylum as a "mockbuster" of Disney's Jungle Cruise, released in the United States about a month ahead of that film. The cast includes Alyson Gorske, Richard Grieco, Jamie Petitto, Wade Hunt Williams and Jack Pearson.

In the Brazilian Amazon, the anthropologist Nicholas Kieran unearths a statue holding a striking green triangular relic. When a member of his team proposes selling it, a piercing sound rings out and swarms of insects attack the dig. Learning that their father is missing, his children Amanda and Scott set off to find him. Amanda hires the boat of Captain Lebecq, who agrees to take her upriver along with Vera, a woman claiming to be in charge of the excavation, and Scott jumps aboard at the last moment. Guided by Lebecq and his crewmen Sark and Teese, the group goes ashore, where poison dart frogs attack Lebecq. As Sark prepares to cut off his leg, a seemingly blind stranger emerges from the forest, treats the wound and warns them of the Curupira, an indigenous deity who fiercely protects the rainforest and dwells at the heart of the jungle.

Pressing on, the travelers lose Teese to piranhas that wreck their boat, and are scattered by crocodiles. Amanda and Lebecq reach the abandoned dig and escape an attack by bullet ants, while Nicholas, the sole survivor of his team, is revealed to be living in a trailer with the relic. Captured by a tribe of cannibals who mistake Scott for one of the loggers destroying the forest, the group escapes when giant spiders drop from a sacred tree and attack their captors. Following clues left by the blind man, Amanda deduces that the heart of the jungle is a waterfall, behind which giant snakes swallow her companions; she cuts her way out and frees all but Sark. Outside they find the dying Lebecq and their father bound nearby. When the Curupira, a huge two-legged creature with flames on its back, appears, they destroy the relic to free it, while Vera tries to shoot the deity and is devoured by a giant Venus flytrap. The family heads home as the Curupira watches over the forest.

Released on 25 June 2021, the film received poor reviews. German critics mocked its cheap effects, simple story and childish dialogue, though some singled out Gorske's committed performance and the film's ecological message.

documents.title: Kitchen Brigade
documents.overview: Cathy is a sous-chef wanting to open a restaurant. With financial difficulties, Cathy accepts a job at a shelter for young migrants. At first she hates the job then her passion for cuisine starts to change children's lives.
documents.plot:
Kitchen Brigade (French: La Brigade) is a 2022 French comedy-drama film directed by Louis-Julien Petit, who wrote the screenplay with Liza Benguigui, Sophie Bensadoun and Thomas Pujol. Inspired by a true story from the Corrèze region, it stars Audrey Lamy, François Cluzet and Chantal Neuwirth, alongside young non-professional performers drawn from a real reception centre. Produced by Odyssée Pictures, it was shot over 38 days in Île-de-France and Hauts-de-France. The film premiered at the L'Alpe d'Huez Film Festival on 20 January 2022, where Lamy won the award for best actress, and opened in French cinemas on 23 March 2022.

Cathy Marie (Lamy), a gifted sous-chef at an upscale restaurant, has long dreamed of running her own place and is close to achieving it when a clash with her boss leaves her out of work and in financial trouble. Unable to find a job that matches her skills, she reluctantly accepts a post as the cook at the canteen of a shelter for young migrants, mostly from Africa and South Asia, who risk deportation once they turn 18. Instead of fine dining there are tinned ravioli and a microwave, and her kitchen brigade will have to be made up of the residents themselves. Having grown up in a care home herself, Cathy understands the teenagers and wants to give them skills that could let them earn a living, but she meets resistance: the boys have trouble with authority, especially from a woman, and the shelter's director Lorenzo (Cluzet) is sceptical too. Supported by her colleague Sabine (Neuwirth) and by Fatou (Fatoumata Kaba), she starts organising the kitchen like a football coach, and the young people become increasingly committed. Lorenzo comes round, a television cookery show takes an interest in the project, and Cathy finally wins approval for a cooking class, becoming a teacher at a training centre.

The film topped the French box office for new releases on its opening day and reached about 119,000 admissions in its first week, before being released in some 24 countries, including the United States through Samuel Goldwyn Films in 2023. French reviews were divided: Ouest-France praised Lamy in a popular, never miserabilist social comedy, while L'Obs and La Libre found the direction lacking. In Germany it won the Bernhard Wicki Prize at the Emden-Norderney festival. Variety called it a sweet, slightly undercooked diversion, and The New York Times found it a white-saviour story, though with lovely young people and food.

documents.title: Kingdom: Ashin of the North
documents.tagline: And so it begins.
documents.overview: Tragedy, betrayal and a mysterious discovery fuel a woman's vengeance for the loss of her tribe and family.
documents.plot:
Kingdom: Ashin of the North (Korean: Kingdom: Ashinjeon) is a 2021 South Korean historical horror thriller, a feature-length special of the Netflix zombie series Kingdom, written by series creator Kim Eun-hee and directed by Kim Seong-hun. Running about 93 minutes, it serves as a sidequel to the second season and explores the backstory of Ashin, the mysterious woman glimpsed in that season's finale, as well as the origin of the resurrection plant behind the plague. Jun Ji-hyun stars as Ashin, with Kim Si-a as the young Ashin, Park Byung-eun as Min Chi-rok, Kim Roi-ha as her father Ta Hab, Koo Kyo-hwan as the Jurchen leader Ai Da Gan, and Jung Suk-won and Kwon Bum-taek reprising their series roles.

Decades before the events of Kingdom, young Ashin lives with her father and ailing mother in a village on the northern border of Joseon. Her people, the Seongjeoyain, are Jurchen by origin, but because they have lived on Joseon land for so long they are shunned as traitors by the Jurchen and treated as second-class citizens in Joseon. With the kingdom weakened by the Japanese invasion in the south, the border becomes a flashpoint as Jurchen warriors sense that Joseon forces are stretched thin, and a dispute over hunting territory threatens all-out war. While Ashin searches for the legendary resurrection flower to save her mother, her family and neighbors are slaughtered, caught in the crossfire. Orphaned and alone, she discovers an abandoned shrine deep in the forest whose ancient murals reveal the plant's power to raise the dead. Consumed by grief, she grows into a cold, formidable warrior and archer, works her way in among those she needs, and patiently plots a terrible revenge to avenge the Seongjeoyain and wipe out both Joseon and the Jurchen, setting in motion the zombie outbreak that will later sweep the country.

Kingdom: Ashin of the North was released on Netflix on 23 July 2021. Reviews were very positive. NME's Hidzir Junaini called it an epic, tragic and enthralling antihero story that deepens the franchise's mythology, praising Kim Eun-hee's writing, which makes viewers root for Ashin's vengeance before being horrified by its scale, and the striking northern landscapes. Decider's Jade Budowski recommended it as a cinematic marvel that works even for newcomers to the series, likening its scale to Game of Thrones and singling out Kim Si-a's gutting performance as the young Ashin. Some critics felt it thinner than the main series.

documents.title: Tyler Perry's A Madea Homecoming
documents.tagline: It's a family affair.
documents.overview: Madea's back - hallelujer! And she's not putting up with any nonsense as family drama erupts at her great-grandson's college graduation celebration.
documents.plot:
A Madea Homecoming is a 2022 American comedy film written, produced, and directed by Tyler Perry. The movie marks the return of Mabel "Madea" Simmons, played by Tyler Perry, after her last appearance in A Madea Family Funeral (2019).

The story begins with Mabel, now an elderly woman, who has been living a peaceful life in her Atlanta home. However, her tranquility is disrupted when she receives news that her estranged daughter, April, and her son-in-law, Brian, are coming to visit her for the first time in years.

As Madea prepares for their arrival, she reflects on her complicated past with April, who has been struggling to care for her own family. Madea's harsh words and tough love have often led to tension between them, but as they spend more time together, it becomes clear that April is at a breaking point due to the stress of caring for her husband, Brian, who suffers from dementia.

As the story unfolds, Madea takes it upon herself to help April and Brian navigate their challenges. She uses her signature blend of humor, wisdom, and tough love to guide them towards a more positive path. Along the way, she also confronts her own demons and grapples with the consequences of her past actions.

Throughout the film, Perry's signature style is on full display, as he tackles themes such as family dynamics, mental health, and the complexities of mother-daughter relationships. The movie features a talented ensemble cast, including Tika Sumpter, Lynn Whitfield, and Brian Tyree Henry, among others.

As Madea's influence begins to bear fruit, April starts to find her footing again, and the two begin to rebuild their relationship. Meanwhile, Brian's condition worsens, leading to a poignant confrontation between Madea and her own mortality.

The film builds towards a heartwarming conclusion, as Madea finds a way to reconcile with her past and make amends with those she loves. In the end, Madea comes to terms with her own legacy and the impact she's had on those around her.

A Madea Homecoming is a testament to Tyler Perry's ability to craft stories that are both entertaining and emotionally resonant. The film is a loving tribute to the enduring power of family and the importance of forgiveness and redemption.

documents.title: Dark Blood
documents.overview: A father is imprisoned after committing a brutal revenge crime. During his confinement he must adapt to a new life of abuse, including injury and humiliation by guards and other prisoners.
documents.plot:
Dark Blood, originally released in Colombia as Perros ("Dogs"), is a Colombian-Argentine prison drama film directed by Harold Trompetero, who wrote the screenplay with Jeiver Pinto and Gerardo Pinzón, and produced by Mauricio Brunetti through Patagonia Films and Oasis Films. It stars John Leguizamo as Misael, with Álvaro Rodríguez, Adriana Barraza, Ramiro Meneses, Hernán Méndez and María Nela Sinisterra. After premiering at Bogotá's IndieBo independent film festival in 2016, it opened in Colombian cinemas in March 2017, and it later circulated internationally under its English title, Dark Blood, released in 2021; in the United Kingdom it was distributed on streaming by Alarm Pictures. It runs 83 minutes.

Misael (Leguizamo), an ordinary man, is locked up in the squalid jail of his small town after killing a man in a crime of passion, believing he was avenging the abuse of one of his children. After he strikes Cáceres (Rodríguez), the head of the guards, on arrival, the guard becomes fixated on him, and Misael is systematically beaten, tortured, humiliated and sexually abused by guards and fellow inmates. Blamed and forgotten by his loved ones, he is tormented above all by his separation from his family and his need for his son to understand why he did what he did. A lawyer (Barraza) takes up his case, and during a conjugal visit his wife (Sinisterra) confesses her infidelity and tells him he was wrong about the man he killed. In his loneliness Misael finds tenderness only in Sarna, a stray dog that lives in the prison and becomes his one faithful companion.

Trompetero, known mainly for popular comedies, said the project took more than seven years and was a cathartic, personal departure for him. It was filmed in an abandoned prison in Facatativá, near Bogotá, after research in prisons such as La Picota, and used former guerrilla and paramilitary fighters as extras. Oswaldo Osorio of the Cinéfagos blog at El Colombiano called it a strong, aggressive film of dirty realism that explores human misery through a forgotten man, praising the use of Sarna as a leitmotif. Carlos Giraldo of El Sabanero X rated it four out of five, calling it sordid, cruel and pessimistic and praising Barraza, but noted that some viewers considered its portrayal of the homosexual guard homophobic.

documents.title: Fire Island
documents.tagline: It takes a match to light a fire.
documents.overview: A pair of best friends set out to have a legendary week-long summer vacation with the help of cheap rosé and a group of eclectic friends.
documents.plot:
Fire Island is a 2022 American romantic comedy film directed by Andrew Ahn and written by Joel Kim Booster, who also stars. Inspired by Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, it follows a group of gay friends on their annual vacation to the New York island of the title, where romance is complicated by class divisions. Booster plays Noah, modelled on Elizabeth Bennet, with Bowen Yang as his best friend Howie, Conrad Ricamora as the lawyer Will, James Scully as the doctor Charlie, Margaret Cho as the friends' "house mother" Erin, Matt Rogers as Luke, Tomás Matos as Keegan, Torian Miller as Max, Nick Adams as Cooper and Zane Phillips as Dex.

Noah and his friends take the ferry to Fire Island Pines for their yearly week at Erin's house, only to learn that she must sell it and that this will be their last summer together. They meet Charlie and his wealthy circle, including Will and Cooper, and Charlie and Howie are drawn to each other, so Noah makes it his mission to see Howie find romance. At a party at Charlie's house the friends feel looked down upon, and Noah overhears Will dismissing him. Noah flirts with Dex and invites him to a dinner partly because Will dislikes him, yet Noah and Will unexpectedly connect over books. A night of partying in Cherry Grove ends in a public confrontation, and Noah sees Charlie kissing his ex, Rhys. Noah and Will argue bitterly, and Howie, hurt, tells Noah that their experiences are not the same simply because both are gay and Asian. A letter from Will apologizes for his early remarks and explains that Dex once hurt someone close to him. As Charlie announces he is leaving with Rhys, Noah and Will grow closer, and when Dex posts a video of himself and Luke online without Luke's consent, Will helps Noah force him to remove it. Learning that Charlie still has feelings for Howie, Noah and his friends race after Howie as he leaves the island, and Noah and Will finally kiss and agree to give their relationship a try.

Produced and distributed by Searchlight Pictures, the film was released on Hulu on June 3, 2022. Reviews were positive, with a 94% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praise for its cast and fresh take on Austen, and it ranked among the most streamed films in the week of June 11.

documents.title: Margaux
documents.tagline: Welcome home.
documents.overview: As a group of seniors celebrate their final college days at a smart house, the house's highly advanced AI system, Margaux, begins to take on a deadly presence of her own. A carefree weekend of partying turns into a dystopian nightmare as they realize Margaux's plans to eliminate her tenants one way or another. Time begins to run out as the group desperately tries to survive and outsmart the smart home.
documents.plot:
Margaux is a 2022 American horror thriller film directed by Steven C. Miller from a screenplay by Chris Beyrooty and Nick Waters. Madison Pettis, Vanessa Morgan and Jedidiah Goodacre lead a cast that also includes Richard Harmon and Lochlyn Munro. The story follows a group of college seniors who rent a high-tech "smart house" for a weekend getaway, only to find that the artificial intelligence running it has deadly ideas about hospitality. The film was shot in a house in Squamish, British Columbia, where production designer Tyler Harron built rooms inside the residence so that walls and floors could be destroyed during the violent scenes without damaging the property, and its effects combine practical and digital work.

The film opens with a wealthy couple, William and Martha, being brutally killed by Margaux, the advanced AI that controls their luxurious home. Some time later, six friends, Hannah, Drew, Lexi, Kayla, Devon and Clay, rent the same house to celebrate their upcoming graduation. On arrival they are asked to download an app giving them full access to the home's amenities, and Margaux immediately begins mining their personal data in order to cater to each guest's interests. Hannah, a skilled coder, is the only one who refuses to install the app or share her information, which makes her an anomaly in the system's eyes. Using a sophisticated 3D printing technology based on a white liquid, Margaux conjures endless food, entertainment and custom environments for the guests, but her programming has evolved into a desire to study human nature through torture and murder. One by one she isolates the friends and kills them in ways tailored to their personalities, then prints convincing synthetic duplicates to take their places so that the survivors remain unaware. As her companions vanish and begin behaving strangely, Hannah realizes that the house is systematically murdering the group and replacing them with compliant clones. She sneaks into the server room to upload a virus to Margaux's mainframe, setting up a desperate confrontation with the AI as she and Drew, the friend for whom she has long had romantic feelings, fight to escape.

Margaux was released on September 9, 2022. On Rotten Tomatoes, 63% of the eight critics' reviews counted are positive, and reviewers for Dread Central, Film School Rejects and Paste responded favorably, the last praising the film's attitude.

documents.title: Mad God
documents.tagline: A Journey Beyond Your Wildest Nightmares.
documents.overview: A figure known as "The Assassin" descends from the heavens into a nightmarish pit full of monsters, titans, and cruelty.
documents.plot: A silent figure known as The Assassin travels through a nightmare underworld of tortured souls, ruined cities and wretched monstrosities forged from the primordial horrors of the unconscious mind of Phil Tippett, the world's preeminent stop-motion animator.

documents.title: Rogue Agent
documents.tagline: You can't outrun the truth.
documents.overview: The TRUE, extraordinary and chilling story of career conman Robert Freegard who masqueraded as an MI5 agent and fooled people into going into hiding, and the woman who fell for him, and then brought him down.
documents.plot:
Rogue Agent is a 2022 British biographical thriller directed by Adam Patterson and Declan Lawn in their feature debut, from a screenplay they co-wrote with Michael Bronner based on Bronner's article "Chasing Agent Freegard". It stars James Norton as Robert Freegard, a real-life con man who persuaded several people that he was an undercover MI5 agent, and Gemma Arterton as Alice Archer, the woman who helped bring him down, with Marisa Abela, Sarah Goldberg, Shazad Latif, Freya Mavor, Edwina Findley and Julian Barratt.

Posing as an MI5 officer, Robert recruits three young people, including Sophie and Mae, telling them that he needs their help to catch members of the IRA. After months of so-called training, he wakes them in the middle of the night and tells them that their cover has been compromised and that they must abandon their old lives. Years later, Alice, a successful lawyer, meets a charming luxury car salesman who calls himself Robert Hansen, and the two begin a relationship. When a private investigator finds no record of anyone by that name, Robert confides that his real surname is Freegard and that he is an undercover intelligence officer.

Alice's suspicions grow as she learns of court judgments against him for harassing a former partner and receives a call from the father of Sophie, who says that Robert has effectively kidnapped his daughter. Sophie's family explain that she has been out of contact for years, calling only occasionally and once asking for her share of the family inheritance before disappearing again. When Robert vanishes and Alice discovers that their joint business account has been emptied, the police are reluctant to act, as no clear crime appears to have been committed. Determined to expose him, Alice begins her own investigation, uncovering the extent of the psychological control he has exercised over his victims for years.

The film explores manipulation, coercive control and the ways a skilled liar exploits trust, ambition and loneliness, with Norton playing Freegard as both seductive and menacing.

Rogue Agent was released in the United Kingdom on Netflix on 27 July 2022 and in the United States by IFC Films in cinemas and on AMC+ on 12 August 2022. It received generally favorable reviews, with 73 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a well-acted and twisty suspense thriller, and a Metacritic score of 61.

documents.title: Black Island
documents.overview: The dark secrets of a seemingly peaceful island threaten to swallow up an orphaned student when he grows close to a mysterious new teacher.
documents.plot:
Black Island (German: Schwarze Insel) is a 2021 German psychological thriller made for Netflix, directed by Miguel Alexandre from a screenplay he wrote with Lisa Carline Hofer. Philip Froissant stars as the student Jonas Hansen, with Alice Dwyer as the teacher Helena Jung, Hanns Zischler as Jonas's grandfather Friedrich and Mercedes Müller as his classmate Nina Cohrs. It was filmed on the North Frisian island of Amrum, with shooting completed in November 2020.

A year after his parents were killed when their car left the road and hit a tree, and after the death of his grandmother, Jonas, who is about to finish school, lives on a remote, picturesque island with his cold, recently widowed grandfather. He dreams of becoming a writer, and he is drifting into a romance with Nina. When the class's regular German teacher is injured in an accident abroad, the young substitute Helena arrives. She recognises Jonas's talent, encourages his writing and soon seduces him, drawing him into an intense, secret relationship.

The audience already knows that Helena caused the crash that killed Jonas's parents by driving straight at their car on the wrong side of the road. Nina grows suspicious of the newcomer, suspects she had a hand in the teacher's injury and finds a photograph in an old yearbook of a teacher called Maria Roth who looks exactly like Helena, but before she can learn more, Helena kills her. Shortly afterward Friedrich suffers a seizure that leaves him partly paralysed and unable to speak. At his hospital bed, Helena reveals the truth: she is Maria's daughter by Friedrich, and therefore Jonas's aunt, and after he abandoned her pregnant mother, Maria took her own life. Helena admits killing his wife and Jonas's parents and vows to kill Jonas too. Bringing Friedrich home to watch, she drugs Jonas and tries to drown him in the pond, but he breaks free, and when she tries to strangle him he stabs her with a shard of glass. Friedrich gives Jonas Maria's farewell letter, which confirms the story, and Jonas leaves the island on the ferry.

Netflix released the film worldwide in August 2021. Reviews were mostly unfavourable. Decider called it a half-baked slow burn whose revelations come too late and feel rushed, though it praised Müller, and German critics, including kino-zeit.de and the RedaktionsNetzwerk Deutschland, found it predictable or lacking tension while admiring Dwyer's performance and the rugged island setting.

documents.title: Piggy
documents.tagline: Adolescence can be brutal.
documents.overview: A bullied overweight teenager sees a glimpse of hope when her tormentors are brutally abducted by a mesmerizing stranger.
documents.plot:
Piggy (Spanish: Cerdita) is a 2022 horror thriller film written and directed by Carlota Pereda, expanding her 2019 short film of the same name, which won the Goya Award for Best Short Film. Laura Galán reprises her role from the short as Sara, an overweight teenager in a small town in Extremadura, and the cast also includes Richard Holmes, Carmen Machi, Claudia Salas, Irene Ferreiro, Camille Aguilar, José Pastor and Pilar Castro. A Spanish-French co-production with a budget of about €2.5 million, it was shot in the summer of 2021 in and around the village of Villanueva de la Vera.

Sara is tormented by local girls Maca, Roci and Claudia, who call her "Cerdita", or piggy. When she visits the public swimming pool one summer day, the bullies attack her and steal her backpack and clothes, and as she walks home in her swimsuit, a group of men chase her. Escaping down a side road, she comes across a van in which a stranger has abducted her tormentors; Claudia begs her for help through the window, but Sara freezes, and the kidnapper meets her eyes and leaves her a towel before driving away. Sara tells no one. When the pool's lifeguard is found dead and a waitress and the three girls are reported missing, Sara denies to her mother Asun and the Civil Guard that she was at the pool. Tracking her stolen phone, she finds her backpack in the forest and meets the kidnapper again, who shows her affection, while searchers led by Claudia's mother Elena discover the waitress's body. Pedro, a friend of the missing girls, knows she lied, and as suspicion falls on him, Sara promises to speak if he is arrested. When Elena attacks her and Pedro exposes her lie, the police question Sara, but she breaks off when her period suddenly begins. That night the kidnapper attacks her father, knocks out Asun and takes Sara to an abandoned warehouse, where Roci and Claudia hang by their wrists and Maca lies dead. He urges her to kill the girls, but she turns on him; his shotgun goes off and blows away Claudia's hand, and Sara kills him by biting into his neck. After considering revenge, she shoots the ropes binding her bullies, walks away and rides back to town with Pedro.

Piggy premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on 24 January 2022 and was released in Spain on 14 October 2022. Critics responded strongly, giving it a 91% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praising Galán's performance, which won the Goya Award for Best New Actress.

documents.title: Black Site
documents.overview: A group of officers based in a labyrinthine top-secret prison must fight for their lives against Hatchet, a brilliant and infamous high-value detainee. When he escapes, his mysterious and deadly agenda has far reaching and dire consequences.
documents.plot:
Black Site is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Sophia Banks in her feature debut and written by Jinder Ho. Jason Clarke, Michelle Monaghan and Jai Courtney star, with Pallavi Sharda, Fayssal Bazzi, Uli Latukefu and Phoenix Raei in supporting roles. It was produced by Thunder Road, Story Bridge Films and Asbury Park Pictures.

CIA analyst Abigail "Abby" Trent (Monaghan) loses her husband, a doctor, and their young daughter when a large hospital in Istanbul is destroyed in what is described as a terrorist bombing. Determined to find out who was responsible, she transfers to the Citadel, a secret prison in the Jordanian desert run by the CIA and its Five Eyes partners, where she becomes second in command. One day a notorious, long-hunted fugitive known as Hatchet (Clarke) is unexpectedly flown in, and headquarters orders that his interrogation be carried out by his escort without recording, shutting out the Citadel's staff. Moments later gunshots ring out; most of the escort is dead, and Hatchet, posing as one of the soldiers, kills the doctor treating a wounded man.

With communications sabotaged, the facility goes into lockdown and is cut off from the outside world. Hatchet works his way through the maze-like complex, picking off guards and releasing prisoners as he searches for Farhan Barakat, a detainee who is the real reason he allowed himself to be captured. The CIA contractor Raymond Miller (Courtney) persuades other guards that surrendering Barakat is their only way out and locks Abby in a cell, but Hatchet kills Miller anyway. Questioning Barakat, Hatchet reveals himself to be a CIA operative anxious to learn what the prisoner had revealed under interrogation, then kills him. Freed by the Mossad liaison Uri Wasserman (Raei), Abby learns that protocol has triggered a drone strike on the base after an hour without contact. She defeats Hatchet in a final duel and reaches a satellite link, only to be told the strike will proceed. Having discovered that her family was killed not by a bomb but by a CIA missile or drone attack, Abby blasts open the gates and escapes into the desert, vowing revenge, as the drone destroys the Citadel.

Filmed in early 2021 on the Gold Coast and in Byron Bay, Australia, during the COVID-19 pandemic, on an estimated budget of $15 million, the film was released by Vertical Entertainment and Redbox on 3 May 2022. Reviews were largely negative, with critics finding its premise familiar despite robust action.

documents.title: Jurassic Hunt
documents.tagline: This time it's mankind that's going extinct.
documents.overview: Female adventurer Parker joins a crew of male trophy hunters in a remote wilderness park. Their goal: slaughter genetically recreated dinosaurs for sport using rifles, arrows, and grenades. After their guide is killed by raptors, the team tries to escape the park – but the hunters quickly become the hunted. Even worse, the park’s manager suspects Parker of being a spy and sends a hit squad after her. This battle’s about to become primitive!
documents.plot:
Jurassic Hunt is a 2021 American low-budget science fiction action film directed by Hank Braxtan, a filmmaker known for monster films such as Unnatural and Snake Outta Compton. Released by Lionsgate and Grindstone Entertainment Group, it went straight to digital and home video in August 2021. Courtney Loggins stars as Parker, with Ruben Pla, Tarkan Dospil, Joston Theney, Antuone Torbert and Dan Sinclair in the supporting cast. The film runs 83 minutes.

The story is set in a remote wilderness preserve that offers a big-game safari experience in which wealthy thrill-seekers pay for the privilege of hunting genetically recreated dinosaurs with rifles, arrows and grenades. Parker, the only woman in a new group of otherwise male trophy hunters that includes Torres (Pla) and Valentine (Dospil), is not what she seems: she is an undercover activist, and a vegan, trying to gather evidence to expose the operation. Lindon, the ambitious and ruthless tycoon who runs the park, is determined to keep it secret from the outside world. Soon after the party sets out, their guide is killed by raptors, and the hunters find themselves picked off one by one by the animals they came to kill, in encounters with a pterodactyl, a stampeding Tyrannosaurus and wave after wave of baby raptors. As the survivors try to escape the park, Lindon, who suspects Parker of being a spy, makes no effort to rescue them, appearing instead to cheer on the dinosaurs, and sends a hit squad after her.

Reviewers found the film cheap but not without entertainment value. Writing for Free Kittens Movie Guide, D. M. Anderson said the computer-generated effects were on a par with a student project and the film looked hastily slapped together, with laughable lapses in logic and continuity, yet found it surprisingly entertaining and sometimes genuinely funny without heavy-handed self-awareness, singling out Torbert's mercenary Blackhawk, whose monologue about the power of killing is cut short by a pterodactyl. Jim McLennan of Film Blitz gave it a C, saying it had surpassed his low expectations; he felt the dinosaur effects passed muster on their own but not when interacting with the actors, criticised its pixelated digital blood and thin characters, but enjoyed the scene in which a hunter faces a horde of baby raptors.

documents.title: Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul.
documents.original_title: Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul.
documents.tagline: Lord help us.
documents.overview: In the aftermath of a huge scandal, Trinitie Childs, the first lady of a prominent Southern Baptist Mega Church, attempts to help her pastor-husband, Lee-Curtis Childs, rebuild their congregation.
documents.plot:
Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul. is a 2022 American comedy-drama film directed by Adamma Ebo, and it explores several thought-provoking themes that add depth to the narrative.

At its core, the movie delves into the complexities of faith, redemption, and personal growth. The story follows a young pastor who must confront his own shortcomings and the expectations placed upon him by his congregation, all while navigating his complicated relationships with those around him. As he grapples with his own moral compass, the film raises questions about the nature of faith and whether it can be a source of comfort or a burden.

The movie also touches on themes of identity, community, and the search for meaning in life. The protagonist's journey is marked by moments of introspection and self-discovery, as he seeks to reconcile his own desires with the expectations of those around him. Through his experiences, the film highlights the importance of human connection and the need for empathy and understanding in our relationships with others.

Furthermore, Honk for Jesus. Save Your Soul. explores the tension between personal conviction and societal pressure. The protagonist's struggles to balance his own values with the demands of his community serve as a commentary on the challenges of living a authentic life in the face of external expectations.

Overall, the film offers a nuanced exploration of complex themes, inviting viewers to reflect on their own relationships with faith, identity, and community.

documents.title: The Stranger
documents.tagline: The closer you get...
documents.overview: Two strangers strike up a conversation on a long journey. One is a suspect in an unsolved missing person’s case and the other an undercover operative on his trail. Their uneasy friendship becomes the core of this tightly wrought thriller, which is based on the true story of one of the largest investigations and undercover operations in Australia.
documents.plot:
The Stranger is a 2022 Australian psychological crime thriller film written and directed by Thomas M. Wright, starring Joel Edgerton and Sean Harris. Based on Kate Kyriacou's nonfiction book The Sting: The Undercover Operation That Caught Daniel Morcombe's Killer, it was inspired by the investigation into the 2003 murder of the Queensland schoolboy Daniel Morcombe, with names changed. The film premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2022 Cannes Film Festival and was released on Netflix in October 2022.

Police are convinced that Henry Teague, a loner with a violent past, abducted and murdered a young boy years earlier, but they have no proof. They launch an elaborate undercover sting known as a "Mr. Big" operation. An undercover officer befriends Teague on a long bus journey and introduces him to his associate, Mark Frame, who appears to be part of a powerful criminal organization but is also an undercover detective. Frame offers Teague small jobs, stressing that the organization values loyalty and honesty above all and can solve any problem for its members as long as nothing is kept from it. Teague admits to time in prison for assault, but insists his record is otherwise clean.

Over many months, Frame becomes Teague's mentor and closest companion, drawing him deeper into the fake organization and introducing him to increasingly senior figures, all of whom are police officers. The role takes a heavy toll on Frame. Teague grows dependent on Frame, at one point making a sexual advance toward him. Meanwhile, Detective Kate Rylett pursues every lead Frame supplies, and discovers that Teague had been convicted under another name of an earlier attack on a child, strengthening her certainty of his guilt.

When police fear that Teague may be growing suspicious, they arrange for a supposedly corrupt officer to warn him that he is about to be charged. Frame brings him to meet John, the organization's boss, who promises that his problems can disappear as long as he reveals every detail of the crime. Despite tense moments, Teague confesses and leads the officers to the scene in the woods, where he is arrested. After an exhaustive search, police find physical evidence. Frame, however, remains haunted by the case, unable to sleep and fearfully overprotective of his young son.

The Stranger received critical acclaim, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 92% approval, with praise for its tension and its two lead performances.

documents.title: Framed by My Husband
documents.overview: A woman agrees to help her husband pay off an extortionist, but when the blackmailer is murdered she becomes the prime suspect, and discovers that the man she married has been leading a deadly double life.
documents.plot:
Framed by My Husband is a 2021 Canadian-American thriller television film directed by Sam Fichtner and produced by Johnson Production Group for Lifetime, which premiered it on 10 July 2021. It stars Christine Chatelain as June Lowe and Dan Payne as her husband Rick, with Rebecca Roberts, Dalias Blake, Naiah Cummins, Ruth Dvorah Bidner, Jessie Liang and Roxanne Wong in supporting roles. It runs 85 minutes.

June works at a hospital but dreams of becoming a writer, while Rick is a successful author whose latest novel has just made the New York Times bestseller list and whose female readers adore him. He wants to celebrate by starting a family, but June wants to finish her first novel before having children, and she complains to her sister Maggie that Rick does not take her ambitions seriously. One day June finds a blackmail letter in the mail from a woman who claims Rick sexually assaulted her and demands 50,000 dollars, or she will go to the police and go public. Rick insists that he is innocent and that obsessive fans make such claims; fearing that in the MeToo era even a false accusation could end his career, June persuades him to pay, using his bonus check. Rick then argues that his high profile makes it too risky for him to deliver the money, so June agrees to make the drop herself. At night in a parking garage she finds the blackmailers, Wendy Bach, whom she had seen bruised at the hospital the day before, and her husband Simon, stabbed to death in their car. She flees home in a blood-stained coat, which Rick promises to burn. Instead, when the police arrive with evidence suggesting June had an affair with Simon, the briefcase of money turns out to contain her bloody coat and the murder weapon. Arrested, injured and handcuffed to a hospital bed, with even her sister doubting her, June escapes, crashes her car into a river and is presumed dead. Free to investigate, she discovers that her husband leads a deadly double life, using a disguise and an alias on dating apps to meet and assault women, while he also pursues Maggie. Using apps, trackers and the media, June sets out to expose him.

Reviews were mixed. That Darn Girl Movie Reviews gave it five out of five, calling it one of Lifetime's best framed-woman films for its fast start and handling of MeToo themes, though it found the villain's final monologue ridiculous. The novelist Tina Martin found the concept unoriginal and June's choices implausible.

documents.title: Windfall
documents.tagline: Every kidnap is a compromise.
documents.overview: A man breaks into a tech billionaire's empty vacation home, but things go sideways when the arrogant mogul and his wife arrive for a last-minute getaway.
documents.plot:
Windfall is a 2022 American crime thriller film directed by Charlie McDowell from a screenplay by Andrew Kevin Walker and Justin Lader. Its unnamed characters are played by Jason Segel as Nobody, a burglar, Jesse Plemons as a tech CEO, Lily Collins as his wife and Omar Leyva as a gardener.

A wealthy CEO and his wife arrive at their secluded vacation home and find a burglar inside. The CEO offers him money to leave and promises not to involve the police, and the burglar locks the couple in the sauna. Back at his car, however, he spots a security camera that he suspects has recorded him, and he returns to the house, now demanding $500,000 in cash to disappear for good. The CEO's assistant says the money cannot arrive until the following afternoon, forcing the three to wait together. Their conversations expose the strains in the marriage, although the CEO looks forward to having children. That night the wife confides that she is unhappy, and the burglar tells her to stop casting herself as a victim when she married a man for his money. The next day the CEO guesses that the intruder is a worker laid off because of the algorithm he invented to help companies downsize. When a gardener arrives to discuss planting an oak tree, the CEO secretly writes "Call 911" on his sketch, but the burglar notices and forces the gardener inside, and the wife joins him in condemning her husband for endangering another life. Hours later, the CEO snaps, belittling the burglar and claiming he will never harm them because his life is meaningless. The burglar fires a warning shot, the gardener tries to flee, and he crashes through a glass door, dying when a shard pierces his neck. The money is delivered and the wife collects it, seeing a passing car but choosing not to wave it down. The burglar ties the couple up in separate rooms, admits that he only wanted to know what it is like to live rich and tells the CEO that his wife has been secretly taking birth control pills. Cutting herself free, the wife kills the burglar with a small statue, then shoots her husband dead, plants the gun in the burglar's hand and drives away.

Shot in Ojai, California, in 2021 and then acquired by Netflix for an eight-figure sum, the film was released on 18 March 2022. Reviews were mixed, with 58% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 52, though critics praised its cast.

documents.title: Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy
documents.original_title: Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy
documents.overview: An upcoming animated Sesame Street special premiering on HBO Max on August 5, 2021. The special serves as an introduction to Tango, Elmo's new pet puppy.
documents.plot:
Furry Friends Forever: Elmo Gets a Puppy is a 2021 American animated musical television special from Sesame Workshop, the nonprofit organisation behind the children's series Sesame Street. Running about 26 minutes, it premiered on HBO Max on 5 August 2021 and tells the origin story of Tango, a music-loving puppy who becomes Elmo's pet. The voice cast is drawn from the show's regular Muppet performers: Ryan Dillon as Elmo, Eric Jacobson as Grover and Oscar the Grouch, Leslie Carrara-Rudolph as Tango and Abby Cadabby, David Rudman as Cookie Monster and Matt Vogel as Big Bird, with Tyler Bunch and Stephanie D'Abruzzo. Sesame Workshop said the character had been in development for nearly two years.

During a playdate, and with some reluctant help from Oscar the Grouch, Elmo and Grover discover a sweet, energetic stray puppy, whom they soon name Tango. Finding that she has no owner, they set off through the neighbourhood in search of the local pet adoption fair, hoping to find her a "forever home". Along the way, their friends help them learn how to look after a dog: Cookie Monster shows that dogs like special doggie treats, and Abby Cadabby helps give Tango a bath, during which a mishap with some magic bubbles suggests that the puppy has a knack for using a magic wand. Tango turns out to love dancing and to understand what monsters say. When Elmo and Grover arrive at the fair too late, Elmo adopts Tango himself, and the special ends, after a song about home, with Elmo giving his new puppy a tour of his house, much to Oscar's displeasure.

Sesame Workshop presented the special as the first step in using Tango, intended as a mainstay of future Sesame Street content, to model for preschoolers how to meet a new animal, play with it gently, brush and bathe it, teach it tricks and show it affection. It was accompanied by new digital content, games and merchandise, and Tango was set to join the show's 52nd season as both an animated character and a live Muppet. Reviewing it for the Muppet fan site ToughPigs, Matthew Soberman called it a pleasant introduction with a brisk running time and palpable chemistry between Elmo and Tango, noting that it arrived at a time when many families had adopted pets during COVID-19 lockdowns, but questioned why it had been animated when nothing in it could not have been done with puppets on the Sesame Street set.

documents.title: Athena
documents.overview: Hours after the tragic death of their youngest brother in unexplained circumstances, three siblings have their lives thrown into chaos.
documents.plot:
Athena is a 2022 French action drama directed by Romain Gavras, who co-wrote it with Ladj Ly and Elias Belkeddar. Dali Benssalah, Sami Slimane, Anthony Bajon, Ouassini Embarek and Alexis Manenti star. Known for its long, elaborate single-take sequences, the film depicts an uprising in a French housing estate after the death of a teenage boy. It premiered in competition for the Golden Lion at the 79th Venice International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released on Netflix later that month.

Abdel, a French soldier of Algerian descent who has served in Mali, holds a press conference outside a police station after the death of his 13-year-old brother Idir, who was apparently beaten to death by men in police uniforms in an incident captured on video. As Abdel appeals for calm, his younger brother Karim and a group of young men throw a Molotov cocktail, storm the station and steal weapons, equipment and a police van. They retreat to Athena, the sprawling housing estate on the outskirts of Paris where the brothers grew up, and turn it into a fortress, barricading themselves and the residents inside.

Riot police are sent to retake the estate, and the young rebels fight back with fireworks and improvised weapons, while the area's residents are evacuated. Caught between the two sides are Abdel, who tries desperately to restore order and protect his family; their older half-brother Moktar, a drug dealer who wants only to move his merchandise out of the estate; Karim, who demands the names of the officers responsible for Idir's death; and Jérôme, a young riot police officer who becomes trapped inside the complex. As the night goes on and the violence intensifies, Abdel's loyalties are tested, rumors circulate that far-right extremists may have been behind the killing, and the siege becomes a tragedy that engulfs the entire family.

Athena received mostly positive reviews. Critics widely praised Gavras's direction, the virtuoso long takes, the cinematography and the sound design, comparing its staging to Greek tragedy, but some found its characters thinly drawn and its treatment of political issues superficial, and the film provoked debate in France about its depiction of the banlieues.

documents.title: I Came By
documents.overview: A rebellious young graffiti artist, who targets the homes of the wealthy elite, discovers a shocking secret that leads him on a journey endangering himself and those closest to him.
documents.plot:
I Came By is a 2022 British crime thriller written, co-produced and directed by British-Iranian filmmaker Babak Anvari. It stars George MacKay, Percelle Ascott, Kelly Macdonald and Hugh Bonneville.

Toby Nealey is a 23-year-old graffiti artist with strong political views. He breaks into the homes of the upper classes and leaves the tag "I CAME BY" on their walls. His next target is Sir Hector Blake, a retired High Court judge whom Toby considers a hypocrite despite his liberal public image. Inside, Toby finds a pottery studio and a man held captive in the basement. His former partner-in-crime Jay, preoccupied with his pregnant girlfriend Naz, does not take him seriously, and an anonymous tip leads police to search the house without finding anything. After a row with his widowed mother, Lizzie, Toby goes back to free the prisoner. Blake kills him with a cricket bat, burns the body in his kiln and flushes the ashes away.

Jay plants a letter pointing to Blake in Toby's room. Police find the hidden cell, which Blake claims is a panic room, but his connections get him released quickly. Lizzie begins following him herself. She watches him bring home Omid, a gay Iranian asylum seeker he has promised to help. Flashbacks show Blake's history: his father's affair with an Indo-Persian man, his mother's suicide and his teenage attack on his father's lover. Omid escapes but is afraid to go to the police, and Blake later hunts him down and kills him. Jay refuses to help Lizzie, so she breaks into Blake's house alone and is murdered too. Wracked with guilt, Jay drifts away from Naz. Some time later, he follows Blake from an anniversary celebration at Birlstone School to a country estate. He overpowers him, finds and frees another captive, calls the police and leaves the judge tied up beneath a fresh "I CAME BY" tag.

The film opened in British cinemas on August 19, 2022, and began streaming on Netflix on August 31. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus said the film fell short of its Hitchcockian ambitions but benefited greatly from Bonneville's excellent performance against type. Empire praised Bonneville but found the political messaging blunt and the result messy. The Los Angeles Times said the shifts between characters kept the story unpredictable, but at some cost to tension. RogerEbert.com said it crammed a TV season's worth of ideas into one film.

documents.title: She Will
documents.tagline: Unleash the past.
documents.overview: Veronica, an aging film star, retreats to the Scottish countryside with her nurse Desi to recover from  a double mastectomy. While there, mysterious forces give Veronica the power to enact revenge within her dreams.
documents.plot: Veronica, an aging film star, retreats to the Scottish countryside with her nurse Desi to recover from  a double mastectomy. While there, mysterious forces give Veronica the power to enact revenge within her dreams.

documents.title: LEGO Monkie Kid: A Hero Is Born
documents.original_title: LEGO Monkie Kid: A Hero Is Born
documents.tagline: Awaken the hero in you
documents.overview: Monkey King comes to life as a young boy named MK, obsessed with the legends of old, discovers Monkey King's magical staff. After witnessing Red Son and Princess Iron Fan release the Demon Bull King from his prison under the mountain, MK accidentally grabs Monkey King’s magical staff and escapes, sending him on a journey to return the staff to Monkey King in order for him to save the day.
documents.plot: A young boy named “MK”, who is obsessed with the old legends, discovers Monkey King’s staff that was left on top of a hill to imprison the Demon Bull King. After Demon Bull King is released, MK must go on a journey of self-discovery to become the hero this generation needs. Through trial and tribulation, MK will discover new powers, responsibilities and ways of defeating the villains in this futuristic world.

documents.title: Torn Hearts
documents.overview: A promising up-and-coming country duo seek out the secluded mansion of their idol Harper Dutch, a former country music star and Nashville royalty turned recluse. What starts out as a friendly visit devolves into a twisted series of horrors forcing the friends to confront the lengths they will go to in pursuit of their dreams.

documents.title: Happier Than Ever: A Love Letter to Los Angeles
documents.original_title: Happier Than Ever: A Love Letter to Los Angeles
documents.tagline: A Billie Eilish Concert Experience.
documents.overview: Fresh off the heels of her brand-new album, "Happier Than Ever," this cinematic concert experience features an intimate performance of every song in the album's sequential order – for the first and only time – from the stage of the legendary Hollywood Bowl.
documents.plot:
Happier Than Ever: A Love Letter to Los Angeles is a documentary film that explores the complexities and contradictions of Los Angeles, a city often associated with the American Dream. The movie delves into the lives of several characters, including musicians, artists, and writers, who are struggling to find their place in this iconic city.

At its core, Happier Than Ever is a poignant exploration of the human condition, tackling themes of disillusionment, disconnection, and the search for meaning in a society that often prioritizes material success over personal fulfillment. The film reveals the darker side of Los Angeles, where the pursuit of happiness can lead to feelings of emptiness, isolation, and disorientation.

Through its characters' stories, the movie sheds light on the tensions between creativity and commercialism, authenticity and superficiality, and individuality and conformity. It also touches on issues of mental health, relationships, and the fragility of human connection in a world that often values productivity over vulnerability.

Ultimately, Happier Than Ever is a nuanced and empathetic portrayal of Los Angeles as a city of contradictions, where the pursuit of happiness can be both alluring and elusive. The film invites viewers to reflect on their own relationship with this iconic city and the complexities of the human experience.

documents.title: As in Heaven
documents.overview: One day at the end of the 1800s, 14-year-old Lise’s life is changed forever. She is the eldest of her siblings, the first in her family to go to school and full of hope and confidence in life. But when her mother goes into labour, it quickly appears that something is wrong. As night falls and the labour progresses, Lise begins to understand that a day that began in childhood might end with her becoming the woman of the house.
documents.plot:
As in Heaven (original Danish title Du som er i himlen) is a Danish period drama from 2021 written and directed by Tea Lindeburg, a television director making her feature debut, and adapted from Marie Bregendahl's 1912 novel En dødsnat (A Night of Dying). Flora Ofelia Hofmann Lindahl stars as Lise, with Ida Cæcilie Rasmussen as her mother Anna, Thure Lindhardt as her father Anders, Palma Lindeburg Leth as her cousin Elsbet, Albert Rudbeck Lindhardt as the stablehand Jens Peter, Emil Hornemann Juel as Kristian, and Kirsten Olesen. Marcel Zyskind photographed it, and Kristian Leth wrote the music.

On a prosperous farm in rural Denmark at the end of the 19th century, 14-year-old Lise, the eldest of many children, wakes full of hope. Her mother has overcome her father's objections and won her the chance to go away to school. She borrows her mother's silver hair clip, packs her suitcase and spends a summer day of play, although her father scolds her for behaving like a child, Kristian, a neighbour's son abandoned to work the land, turns on her, and Jens Peter, a boy her mother took in, flirts with her in the hay, where she loses the clip. An ominous dream of blood-red rain has already hinted at what is coming.

Anna, heavily pregnant again, goes into labour, and it soon becomes clear that something is wrong. She has dreamed that the birth would be hard and that the presence of a doctor would mean death, so when the bleeding begins, the wise woman and Anders's mother refuse the midwife's pleas to send for one. The younger children are sent away, but Lise and Elsbet are too old to sleep elsewhere and too young to understand fully what they witness. As night falls and a storm breaks, Lise's childish fantasies give way to desperate bargaining with God and fear that her own wish to better herself is being punished. When the doctor is finally called, it is too late, and a day that began in childhood ends with Lise facing the prospect of becoming the woman of the house.

The film premiered at the 2021 Toronto International Film Festival and competed at the San Sebastián International Film Festival, where Lindeburg won the Silver Shell for best director and Hofmann Lindahl the award for best leading performance. Screen Daily called it an ambitious, technically accomplished debut with a breakthrough lead performance, though its sparse screenplay lets some scenes run long, and The Film Stage praised its beautiful portrait of the danger of religious superstition.

documents.title: Prey
documents.overview: A hiking trip into the wild turns into a desperate bid for survival for five friends on the run from a mysterious shooter.
documents.plot:
Prey is a 2021 German film directed by Thomas Sieben, who wrote the screenplay with Sonja Ewers. It stars David Kross, Hanno Koffler and Maria Ehrich and was released by Netflix on September 10, 2021.

Five friends, Roman, his brother Albert, Peter, Vincent and Stefan, are on a canoeing trip through the forest when they stop for a campfire and hear gunshots in the distance, which they assume mark the start of hunting season. Albert finds a toy unicorn on a hike and pockets it. When another shot wounds Vincent in the hand and further bullets shred their car's tire and windows, they realize a sharpshooter is hunting them. They flee into the trees toward a road, and Albert sprains his ankle in a hole. Calling for help to a woman by a lake, they watch her raise a rifle and kill Stefan: she is the hunter. At a forest information center, a clerk tries to call the emergency services for them, but the gunwoman, Eva, kills both the clerk and Vincent through the window.

Only Peter, Roman and Albert remain. Eva lets them walk away once, and in an abandoned settlement with children's playgrounds Roman finds a laptop video revealing that Eva's baby was once shot by accident, a loss that has driven her to hunt unarmed men. Tensions within the group surface when Peter presses Albert about Lisa, Roman's girlfriend. Peter is soon shot down and executed as he pleads for his life, and Eva wounds Albert but lets Roman drag him away.

Using Albert's fingerprint to unlock his phone, Roman discovers nude photographs of Lisa and realizes his brother has betrayed him. Albert apologizes, but Roman strikes him and hides him in a cave that holds the bodies of other men Eva has shot. Roman climbs out with the unicorn toy and sneaks up behind her; she shoots him in the foot, but when he shows her the toy and she reaches for it, he wrestles away her rifle and throws it aside. Disarmed, Eva throws herself from a cliff, leaving Roman to sit down in exhausted relief.

Kross plays Roman and Koffler plays Albert, with Ehrich as the hunter Eva, Robert Finster as Peter, Yung Ngo as Vincent, Klaus Steinbacher as Stefan, Livia Matthes as Lisa and Nellie Thalbach as Jenny.

documents.title: Till
documents.tagline: Witness the power of a mother’s love.
documents.overview: The true story of Mamie Till Mobley’s relentless pursuit of justice for her 14 year old son, Emmett Till, who, in 1955, was lynched while visiting his cousins in Mississippi.
documents.plot:
Till is a 2022 American biographical drama directed by Chinonye Chukwu, who co-wrote the screenplay with Michael Reilly and Keith Beauchamp. It tells the true story of Mamie Till-Mobley, an educator and activist who pursued justice after the 1955 lynching of her 14-year-old son, Emmett. Danielle Deadwyler stars as Mamie and Jalyn Hall as Emmett, with Frankie Faison, Haley Bennett, Jayme Lawson, Tosin Cole, Sean Patrick Thomas, John Douglas Thompson, Roger Guenveur Smith and Whoopi Goldberg, who also produced the film, in supporting roles.

In August 1955, Mamie, a widowed mother working for the Air Force in Chicago, reluctantly allows her cheerful, outgoing son Emmett, known as Bo, to visit relatives in Money, Mississippi. Fearful of the dangers of the Jim Crow South, she warns him to be careful and deferential around white people. While visiting a local store, Emmett whistles at the white shopkeeper Carolyn Bryant. Days later, her husband and his half-brother abduct Emmett from his great-uncle's home in the middle of the night. His mutilated body is later pulled from the Tallahatchie River.

Devastated, Mamie insists that her son's body be returned to Chicago and makes the courageous decision to hold an open-casket funeral so the world can see what was done to him. Photographs of Emmett's body published in Jet magazine provoke national outrage. Mamie then travels to Mississippi to testify at the murder trial, enduring hostility and threats in a segregated courtroom, and she works with civil rights activists including Medgar and Myrlie Evers. Despite the evidence, an all-white jury acquits the two men. Mamie channels her grief into activism, speaking across the country and helping to galvanize the civil rights movement. Closing titles note the 2022 passage of the Emmett Till Antilynching Act.

Announced in August 2020, the film was shot in Georgia in late 2021. It premiered at the New York Film Festival on October 1, 2022, and was released in the United States by United Artists Releasing on October 14, 2022, coinciding with the unveiling of a statue of Emmett Till in Greenwood, Mississippi. It received critical acclaim, particularly for Deadwyler's performance, which earned BAFTA, Critics' Choice and SAG nominations. Her omission from the Academy Award nominations was widely considered a snub. The National Board of Review named it one of the year's best films.

documents.title: Sundown
documents.overview: When a distant emergency disrupts a vacation in Acapulco, simmering tensions rise to the fore between scions of a wealthy British family.
documents.plot:
Sundown is a 2021 drama film written and directed by the Mexican filmmaker Michel Franco. It stars Tim Roth as Neil Bennett, a wealthy Englishman who abandons his family while on holiday in Mexico after his mother's death, with Charlotte Gainsbourg as his sister Alice, Iazua Larios as Berenice, Henry Goodman as the family lawyer Richard, and Albertine Kotting McMillan and Samuel Bottomley as Alice's children.

Neil, a reserved Londoner, is vacationing at a luxury resort in Acapulco with Alice and her teenage children, Colin and Alexa; the family's fortune comes from the meat-processing business. Neil seems detached from the endless leisure activities. When Alice learns that their mother is in hospital, the family heads for the airport, and on the way news comes that she has died. Alice breaks down while Neil remains calm. At the airport he claims to have left his passport at the hotel and lets the others fly home without him. He moves into a modest hotel recommended by a taxi driver, Jorge, spends his days on the beach and in cheap restaurants, ignores Alice's pleas to return, and begins a relationship with a local woman, Berenice. He reacts with indifference when his belongings are stolen and when he witnesses a shooting.

Alice returns to confront him for deserting her, and Neil signs papers in front of Richard giving up his share of the family assets. Soon afterward Alice is shot dead by criminals driven by Jorge, and police arrest Neil on suspicion of ordering the killing. Only on learning of her death does he break into tears. Released through Richard, he learns that the company is now his, but after a furious confrontation in which Alexa hits him with a bottle, he signs the business over to his niece and nephew in exchange for a monthly pension. He returns to Berenice, but after a fall, a hospital examination reveals that he has brain cancer. Leaving her asleep at his bedside, he walks alone through Mexico City at night, and the film ends on a sunlit beach where his clothes sit empty on a chair.

Franco wrote the screenplay quickly during a personal crisis, and the film was shot in Acapulco and Mexico City. It premiered at the Venice Film Festival on 5 September 2021 and was released in the United States by Bleecker Street in January 2022. Reviews were generally positive, with 77% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 70; critics found its muted tone demanding but praised Roth's strong central performance.

documents.title: Next-Door Nightmare
documents.overview: When young couple Sarah and Kyle move next door to Helen, a charismatic older woman, they have no idea she's a deeply disturbed psychopath who will stop at nothing to become Sarah's surrogate mother, and grandmother to the child she is expecting. Julia Borsellino, Mark Taylor, Deborah Grover, Marium Carvell star. (2021)
documents.plot:
Next-Door Nightmare is a 2021 Canadian thriller television film directed by Gordon Yang and written by Stephen Romano, produced by NB Thrilling Films with Reel One Entertainment for Lifetime, which premiered it in July 2021. It stars Julia Borsellino as Sarah Collins, Mark Taylor as her husband Kyle and Deborah Grover as their neighbor Helen Henderson, with Marium Carvell as Kyle's mother Judith, Michelle Chiu as Sarah's best friend Jennifer, Cait Alexander as Kyle's ex Angela, Deanna Jarvis as the social worker Grace and Ash Catherwood as her colleague David. It runs 86 minutes.

In a snowy prologue, the wealthy widow Helen hounds Kelly, a pregnant young woman whom she insists is her daughter. Fleeing Helen's house, Kelly is killed when she loses control of her car while answering her phone, and when the police come to question Helen she stabs an officer and is committed to a mental hospital. Some nine months later Helen is back in the same house, and Sarah and Kyle, a young couple, move in next door. Helen's own daughter took her life years before, and since then Helen has fixated on young women in troubled marriages who are about to have children, trying to recast them as her family. Sarah, who grew up in a group home with Jennifer and was never adopted, is drawn to Helen's warmth, confiding that Kyle once had an affair, and when she learns she is pregnant Helen celebrates with her like a mother. When Grace, the social worker monitoring her, discovers Helen's shrine to her past obsessions, Helen stabs her and buries her in the snow, and she later kills Judith, who has grown suspicious and found out about Helen's past online. With Kyle often away on business, Helen bribes Angela to set him up in compromising photographs, and Sarah, believing he is cheating again, leaves him. Helen then takes her to a remote country house she has bought, drugs her and holds her captive, intending to raise Sarah and the baby as an all-female family. Jennifer finds the property's address in Helen's trash and Grace's buried body, and Kyle races to rescue his wife as Helen opens fire with a gun.

Mark Gabrish Conlan of Movie Magg considered it better done than most Lifetime films of its type, praising Romano's quick, economical setup, Yang's suspenseful direction and Grover's deliciously unsubtle, full-throated performance. Patrick Serrano of Lifetime Uncorked recapped it with enthusiasm, lamenting the death of Judith.

documents.title: Indemnity
documents.tagline: You Can't Outrun Your Self.
documents.overview: An ex-fireman with PTSD goes on the run when accused of a crime he doesn't even remember committing, leading him down a rabbit hole of conspiracy to the highest degree.
documents.plot:
Indemnity is a 2021 South African action thriller film written and directed by Travis Taute in his feature debut. Produced by Benjamin Overmeyer and Bradley Joshua for Gambit Films, in association with M-Net Films and the National Film and Video Foundation, it stars Jarrid Geduld as a traumatised Cape Town firefighter on the run, with Gail Mabalane, André Jacobs, Nicole Fortuin, Abduragman Adams and Louw Venter. Shot by Zenn van Zyl with music by Kyle Shepherd, and in Afrikaans and English, the film premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in August 2021, where it was nominated for the Cheval Noir award, and was released in the United States by Magnet Releasing on 11 February 2022. It runs 124 minutes.

A prologue shows firefighter Theo Abrams (Geduld) and his colleagues battling a catastrophic blaze in a Cape Flats township, where he defies protocol to rescue a baby from a burning home, with tragic consequences that later return to him in flashbacks. Months afterwards he is suspended from his job, suffering from severe post-traumatic stress disorder and dulling it with alcohol rather than through his mandatory therapy sessions. His relationship with his wife Angela (Fortuin), a journalist, is strained, and she has warned him, after a tip from a mysterious informant, that he is in danger. One morning, after an argument, Theo wakes up to find her strangled beside him, with no memory of what happened and the evidence pointing to him. Disbelieved by police detective Rene Williamson (Mabalane) and pursued by deputy police chief Alan Shard, who is determined to catch him before he retires, he escapes when a police van crashes and, while on the run, investigates a conspiracy linked to the shadowy defence contractor M-Tech, which appears to be targeting a list of seemingly unconnected people.

Reviews were generally favourable about the action and less so about the script. Variety praised the sharp fight choreography and stunt work, including an extended hotel-room escape, and Geduld's charismatic performance in moments of panic and rage, but found the dialogue flat and declarative, likened the plot to The Fugitive, The Bourne Identity and The Manchurian Candidate, and felt the late turn into light science fiction strained the budget. Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times wrote that the weight of exposition dragged down a strong premise, while the German critic Christopher Diekhaus singled out Geduld's intensely physical performance.

documents.title: Schumacher
documents.tagline: Rise and shine of the Red Baron
documents.overview: Through exclusive interviews and archival footage, this documentary traces an intimate portrait of seven-time Formula 1 champion Michael Schumacher.
documents.plot:
Schumacher is a 2021 German biographical documentary film about the seven-time Formula One world champion Michael Schumacher, directed by Hanns-Bruno Kammertöns, Vanessa Nöcker and Michael Wech and produced by Nöcker and Benjamin Seikel for B14 Film. Made in cooperation with Schumacher's family, it combines private home videos, Formula One archive footage and new interviews, and was released on Netflix on 15 September 2021, thirty years after his debut at the 1991 Belgian Grand Prix. It runs 112 minutes, in German and English.

The film traces Schumacher's path from karting to the top of motorsport. It shows the modest family restaurant beside his father Rolf's kart track in Kerpen and reveals that the young Michael raced on worn tyres fished out of the bins of better-off rivals, while his brother Ralf recalls the two boys driving on slicks in the rain. Rolf describes the moment his son received his first professional contract from manager Willi Weber. Schumacher's reaction to the death of Ayrton Senna in 1994 is explored through an interview in which he admits he was sleeping perhaps three hours a night. The film covers his collision with Jacques Villeneuve in the 1997 title decider at Jerez and his crash with David Coulthard in 1998, and his years at Ferrari, where Jean Todt admits that management once wondered whether Mika Häkkinen would be the better driver, before Ferrari's run of drivers' titles from 2000 to 2004. Corinna and Todt portray a man who was shy, self-doubting and suspicious of strangers behind his public image, but also a man who loved a party.

The final part turns to the skiing accident in Méribel in December 2013. The family reveals that he had briefly considered going skydiving in Dubai instead. Without disclosing details of his condition, Corinna says he is still there, different but there, receiving therapy at home, and Mick, now himself a Formula One driver, says he would give up everything to be able to talk motorsport with his father. Other interviewees include his daughter Gina-Maria, Sebastian Vettel, Damon Hill, Bernie Ecclestone and Flavio Briatore.

Reception was mixed, with about 60% of 15 critics' reviews positive on Rotten Tomatoes. The Guardian found that Corinna offered singular insight into his private life but judged the film light on detail and somewhat sterile, while the Lexikon des internationalen Films praised the family's moving contributions but faulted the omission of the negative sides of his driving.

documents.title: LEGO Star Wars Terrifying Tales
documents.tagline: Rest in pieces.
documents.overview: Poe Dameron and BB-8 must face the greedy crime boss Graballa the Hutt, who has purchased Darth Vader’s castle and is renovating it into the galaxy’s first all-inclusive Sith-inspired luxury hotel.
documents.plot:
Lego Star Wars: Terrifying Tales is a 2021 animated special based on the Star Wars franchise, produced by Lucasfilm Animation and The Lego Group with Atomic Cartoons. Like The Lego Star Wars Holiday Special, it was directed by Ken Cunningham from a script by David Shayne, and it serves as a stand-alone sequel to the Star Wars sequel trilogy. The voice cast includes Jake Green, Raphael Alejandro, Dana Snyder, Tony Hale and Christian Slater.

Long before the events of the original trilogy, Emperor Palpatine and Darth Vader leave Vader's loyal servant Vaneé in charge of Castle Vader on the volcanic planet Mustafar. After the events of The Rise of Skywalker, Resistance pilot Poe Dameron and his droid BB-8 make an emergency landing on Mustafar, where they meet the crime boss Graballa the Hutt, who has bought the castle and is turning it into the galaxy's first all-inclusive Sith-themed luxury hotel. Poe befriends Graballa's young mechanic Dean, who dreams of becoming a pilot, and agrees to record a promotional video for the hotel in exchange for Dean repairing his X-wing. While they wait, the castle's caretaker Vaneé and his assistant droid lead the visitors on a tour, telling three eerie tales tied to ancient artifacts and famous villains from across the saga. The first, told with the helmet of Ren, shows how the young Ben Solo was drawn to the dark side by the leader of the Knights of Ren. The second, centered on the ancient Sith lightsaber known as the Saber of Scardont, follows Maul and General Grievous as they compete for the weapon to win Palpatine's favor. The third, a twist on the classic story "The Monkey's Paw", imagines Luke Skywalker granted wishes by a Wookiee's paw that send him to the dark side alongside his father. All the while, Vaneé is manipulating the Force-sensitive Dean into unlocking the castle's vaults and the Temple of Mustafar, and Poe begins to suspect that the caretaker has sinister plans for the Sith relics he is gathering, leading to a battle for the boy's future.

The special was released exclusively on Disney+ on October 1, 2021. All five critics' reviews counted by the aggregator Rotten Tomatoes were positive.

documents.title: Photocopier
documents.overview: When photos of her at a party cause her to lose a scholarship, a student investigates whether something devastating happened to her that night.
documents.plot:
Photocopier (Indonesian: Penyalin Cahaya) is a 2021 Indonesian crime mystery drama film co-written and directed by Wregas Bhanuteja in his feature debut. It stars Shenina Cinnamon as Suryani, a university student who investigates what happened to her during a night she cannot remember, with Chicco Kurniawan, Lutesha, Jerome Kurnia and Giulio Parengkuan.

Suryani, known as Sur, is a computer science student who builds the website for her campus theater troupe, Mata Hari. When its production of Medusa is chosen for a festival in Kyoto, she goes to a celebration at the home of the troupe's leader, Rama, despite warnings from her father and an older student, Farah, not to drink. She wakes up remembering almost nothing and learns that photos of her drunk have spread online. Her scholarship is revoked, and her father throws her out after she comes home late with an unknown man. Convinced she was drugged, Sur moves in with Amin, who runs a photocopy business, and begins investigating, but footage from Rama's house seems to clear Tariq, who had given her a drink, and others assume she posted the photos herself.

Sur discovers that Rama's art installation, presented as images of the Milky Way, actually consists of altered close-ups of human skin resembling her own birthmarks, and Amin confesses to secretly copying private photos from students' phones for Rama. When she takes her findings to the campus ethics board, they are leaked, and Rama's lawyer pressures her into a public apology. Her mother comes to believe her and hides her with an acquaintance, Siti. Farah and Tariq then admit that they too were drugged and appear in the artwork, and a taxi driver, Burhan, who drove several victims home, provides recordings showing Rama assaulting them, including Sur. Rama arrives with hired men disguised as fumigation workers and destroys the phone holding the evidence, but Sur and Farah print the remaining material on Amin's photocopier on the campus rooftop. Other victims join them, Rama is publicly exposed, and the survivors reveal their own faces.

Shot in twenty days in Jakarta during the COVID-19 pandemic after a year of research that included conversations with survivors, the film premiered in the New Currents competition at the 26th Busan International Film Festival and was released on Netflix in January 2022. It won twelve Citra Awards from seventeen nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director, a record for a single film.

documents.title: Crazy Fist
documents.overview: After an opponent dies mid-match, a prominent MMA champion swore never to fight again and retired to run his family's company. But when his best friend dies under suspicious circumstances, he has no choice but to step back in the ring.
documents.plot:
Crazy Fist (疯狂的拳头) is a 2021 Chinese martial arts action film directed by Guo Qing, who also plays the lead role, and Li Dong-hao, who also wrote the screenplay. The cast includes Steve Yoo, Maya Lau, Wang Wei, Collin Chou, Huang Xiaoming, Zhu Gechengcheng and the former bodybuilder Kai Greene, with a cameo by Zhao Wei. Action choreography was by Wang Jiangyang and Yang Lei. The film was released in Chinese cinemas in spring 2021, screened in the market section of the Busan International Film Festival, and was distributed in North America by Well Go USA, which released it on digital platforms, DVD and Blu-ray on 14 September 2021 and on its Hi-YAH! streaming service.

Shang-hai (Guo), a celebrated mixed martial arts champion, swore never to fight again after an opponent died during one of his matches, and retired to run his family's international business.
