documents.title: Megan
documents.overview: A hiker finds shelter in a mountain lodge inhabited by two strange women.
documents.plot: A hiker finds shelter in a mountain lodge inhabited by two strange women.

documents.title: The Ambush
documents.tagline: They will bring their brothers home by any means necessary.
documents.overview: It is the winter of 2018, the men and women of the UAE military are deployed to provide aid. At the Mocha Base, spirits are high as three Emirati soldiers anticipate an imminent return home. While on their final routine patrol, the three soldiers, Ali, Bilal and Hindasi are ambushed by heavily armed militants on their route, through a narrow canyon. Trapped, wounded, and out of communication range, the three soldiers realize the gravity of their situation. They are running out of options, munitions - and time. Back at the base, their commander receives word and realizes that the assault on the UAE army patrol was premeditated. A rescue mission is quickly put into action, but will air and land support reach the men in time, and will they survive?
documents.plot:
The Ambush (Arabic: Al Kameen) is a 2021 Emirati war action film directed by the French filmmaker Pierre Morel and written by Brandon and Kurtis Birtell. Based on a real incident during the Yemen war, it was produced by Image Nation Abu Dhabi and AGC Studios, with producers Derek Dauchy and Jennifer Roth and a score by Harry Gregson-Williams. The all-Emirati lead cast includes Marwan Abdulla Saleh, Khalifa Al Jassem, Mohammed Ahmed, Abdulla Saeed Bin Haider, Saeed Alharsh, Hassan Yousuf Alblooshi, Khalifa Albahri, Ghanim Nasser and Mansoor Alfeeli.

In the winter of 2018, soldiers of the UAE armed forces are deployed in Yemen, and at their base in Mocha morale is high, as three of them, Ali, Bilal and Al Hindasi, look forward to returning home soon. During what should be their last routine patrol, their vehicle is caught by heavily armed militants in a narrow mountain canyon. Wounded, trapped and out of radio contact, the three men realize how desperate their position is as they run short of options, ammunition and time. At the base, their commander learns of the attack and understands that the assault on the patrol was planned in advance. He quickly launches a rescue operation, sending another squad of Emirati soldiers with ground and air support into the valley in a race to reach the men before it is too late. The film also follows the families of some of the soldiers at home.

The production was described as the largest Arabic-language feature ever filmed in the Gulf Cooperation Council states, involving a cast and crew of around 400 and shot entirely in the United Arab Emirates, with a team of Emirati filmmakers and cultural consultants, including Hana Kazim, Talal Al Asmani, Alwiya Thani and Alia AlQemzi, working alongside the foreign crew.

The film had its world premiere at VOX Cinemas Yas Mall, attended by the cast and by the real soldiers whose story inspired it, and was released by VOX Distribution in the UAE on 25 November 2021. Its opening weekend drew 100,000 admissions, the fifth-largest opening of the year in the country, and within a week it had become the highest-grossing Emirati and Arabic-language film ever in the UAE, eventually earning more than $5 million worldwide. Morel described it as an inspirational story of brotherhood. In the United States, Well Go USA released it on Blu-ray; one reviewer praised the striking desert scenery but found the film thin, consisting almost entirely of combat.

documents.title: Amina
documents.tagline: She is Amina and she fears nobody.
documents.overview: In 16th-century Zazzau, now Zaria, Nigeria, Amina must utilize her military skills and tactics to defend her family's kingdom. Based on a true story.
documents.plot:
Amina is a 2021 Nigerian historical action drama directed by Izu Ojukwu, based on the life of Amina, the legendary warrior queen of Zazzau in the 16th century, a Hausa kingdom in what is now northern Nigeria, centered on the city of Zaria. Lucy Ameh stars in the title role, with Ali Nuhu, Clarion Chukwurah-Abiola, Chris Gbakann and Ibrahim Mijinyawa. The film premiered on Netflix on 4 November 2021.

The film opens with a duel between Kabarkai, the champion of Zazzau, and Danjuma. Having witnessed the fight, the young Amina tells her father, the ruler of Zazzau, that she wants to become a warrior. Her wish meets resistance from the Magaji, an important official, who points out that the armies of Zazzau have never recruited a woman. Determined, Amina trains in combat and horsemanship and gradually proves herself, defying the restrictions placed on women in her society.

The story follows the events that lead to Amina's rise to the throne of Zazzau. As a princess, she becomes involved in the political intrigues of the court and in the wars between Zazzau and its rivals, while her family faces betrayal from within. Her relationship with her sister Zaria, after whom the city is named, and a romance with Danjuma, a foreign prince, are threatened by the conflicts surrounding them. After suffering painful personal losses, including the death of her sister, Amina leads Zazzau's armies into battle and ultimately claims power, emerging as a formidable ruler who expands the kingdom's influence.

Amina received the most nominations at the 2022 Africa Magic Viewers' Choice Awards. Critics praised its costumes, music and battle scenes, but many faulted its plot, character development and underdeveloped romance. It was also criticized for being performed in Hausa with a non-Hausa lead actress, and for historical inaccuracies, such as its treatment of Amina's mother, Bakwa Turunku, who historians say had herself ruled Zazzau. Ojukwu responded that the scarcity of archives on Nigeria's history made the film difficult to produce.

documents.title: Batman and Superman: Battle of the Super Sons
documents.original_title: Batman and Superman: Battle of the Super Sons
documents.tagline: The ultimate threat. The greatest battle. The perfect team.
documents.overview: After discovering he has powers, 11-year-old Jonathan Kent and assassin-turned-Boy-Wonder Damian Wayne must join forces to rescue their fathers (Superman & Batman) and save the planet from the malevolent alien force known as Starro.
documents.plot:
Batman and Superman: Battle of the Super Sons is a 2022 American animated superhero film released direct to video by Warner Bros. Animation. Based on the comic books of the same name, it is the 50th DC Universe Animated Original Movie and the first DC animated feature made entirely in CGI. Matt Peters directed from a screenplay by Jeremy Adams. Jack Dylan Grazer voices Jonathan Kent and Jack Griffo voices Damian Wayne, with Troy Baker as Batman, Travis Willingham as Superman and Laura Bailey as Lois Lane.

The prologue shows Krypton about to explode. Jor-El and Lara send their infant son Kal-El to Earth, unaware that Starro, an alien parasite that escaped from Jor-El's lab, has stowed away on the ship. Starro falls off during the journey. Kal-El grows up in Kansas as Clark Kent, becomes Superman and marries Lois Lane, and they have a son, Jon. Years later, Jon resents his father's constant absences without knowing that Clark is Superman. After a mysterious impact hits the Justice League Watchtower, Green Arrow is attacked aboard the station by a creature.

When Jon develops heat vision on his birthday, Clark tells him the truth and takes him to Gotham City to ask Batman for advice. There Jon meets Batman's arrogant son, Damian Wayne, who is Robin. Batman and Superman go up to the silent Watchtower, where a possessed Martian Manhunter infects them with Starro spores. Back in the Batcave, Damian destroys the spore meant for him and learns that Starro now controls the Justice League and the Teen Titans and is after Jon next.

Damian rescues Jon, and Jon's heat vision frees Lois. At the Fortress of Solitude, a hologram of Jor-El tells them that the spores answer to a central Starro on the Watchtower. The boys fly there in Kal-El's old ship and fight their possessed heroes, and Jon's invulnerability appears as he shields Damian from an arrow. When heat alone fails, they evacuate the heroes and send the station down to burn up on re-entry. This kills the spores, and the freed Superman catches the falling Watchtower. The two fathers and their sons then defeat Starro on the ground, and the boys call themselves the Super-Sons.

The film premiered at New York Comic Con on October 7, 2022, and came out on home video on October 18. Reviews were positive, and IGN said it was fairly predictable but captured the fun of the young heroes' friendship.

documents.title: Last Shoot Out
documents.tagline: His aim is unrivaled.
documents.overview: Soon after a newlywed learns that her husband had her father shot down, she flees from the Callahan ranch in fear. She's rescued by a gunman who safeguards her at a remote outpost as he staves off her husband's attempts to reclaim his bride.
documents.plot:
Last Shoot Out is a 2021 American Western film directed and produced by Michael Feifer from a screenplay by Lee Martin. A Milestone Studios production presented by Lionsgate and Grindstone Entertainment Group, it stars Brock Harris, Skylar Witte, Michael Welch, Cam Gigandet and Bruce Dern, with Peter Sherayko, David DeLuise, Jay Pickett, Brock Burnett and Larry Poole in supporting roles. Hank Baumert Jr. was the cinematographer, Ted Gianopulos edited the film, and the score was composed by Robert Arzola and Feifer. Lionsgate released it in select theatres and on digital rental on 3 December 2021, followed by DVD, Blu-ray and digital purchase on 7 December. It is rated PG-13 and runs 86 minutes.

Jocelyn (Witte), a small-town beauty whose father, the local lawman, has recently died, marries Jody Callahan (Welch), the dim-witted son of Blair Callahan (Dern), the snarling patriarch of a family of rustlers and killers. On their wedding night at the Callahan ranch she overhears Blair and his shrewder, deadlier son Sid (Gigandet) discussing the possibility that Sid may have to take Jody's place in the marriage bed, and referring to Sid's murder of her father, carried out to stop him from arresting Jody for killing a woman who had mocked him. Horrified, Jocelyn flees and meets two travellers headed for a remote stagecoach station: Red (Sherayko), a grizzled man hauling a wagon of supplies to the outpost, and Billy Tyson (Harris), a taciturn gunman. When Sid and his henchman Twigs (Pickett) arrive to take the runaway bride back, the quick-drawing Billy chooses to wound and disarm Sid rather than kill him, a mercy he comes to regret when Blair descends on the station with his sons and a band of hired guns, ordering them to leave no one alive, including the stranded stagecoach passengers and the station's operator, Joe (DeLuise).

Joe Leydon of Variety called it a small-budget indie aimed at the underserved audience for Westerns, noting echoes of Budd Boetticher's Ranown cycle and Ride the High Country. While slow-paced and padded with too many flashbacks, it was in his view a cut above recent streaming-ready Westerns and a marked improvement over Feifer's Catch the Bullet, with well-staged action and a ferociously nasty turn by Dern, recalling Walter Brennan's Old Man Clanton in My Darling Clementine, though Harris and Gigandet looked more like male models than gunslingers.

documents.title: Slayers
documents.tagline: Vengeance bites back.
documents.overview: A group of superstar influencers are drawn to a reclusive billionaire's mansion only to find themselves trapped in the lair of an evil vampire. The only way out is to be saved by a famous online gamer and an old school vampire hunter.
documents.plot:
Slayers is a 2022 American horror comedy written, produced and directed by K. Asher Levin. Thomas Jane stars as Elliot Jones, a former television personality, with Kara Hayward as Flynn Chambers, Jack Donnelly as her brother Jack, Lydia Hearst as Liz Andrews, Abigail Breslin as Jules Ray and Malin Åkerman as Beverly Rektor. The Avenue Entertainment released it on October 21, 2022.

Flynn, Jack, Liz and Jules make up the "stream team", a group of famous social-media influencers who have been invited to the estate of Stephen Rektor, a billionaire media mogul and pharmaceutical tycoon. Rektor and his family are secretly vampires. On the way to the mansion they encounter Elliot, once a TV personality, whose daughter was killed by a vampire. His warnings are dismissed as paranoia.

Once inside, the group is quickly split up. Their manager, David, is lured into a trap by Beverly Rektor and killed. Liz and Jack, who are a couple, are offered lucrative deals to promote a Rektor vaccine billed as making humanity immune to disease, which in reality is designed to purify human blood for vampires to feed on. Jules follows Harry Rektor to the stables for a date, where Flynn, who has sensed something is wrong, finds him attacking her. Jules is killed, but Elliot arrives and destroys Harry, and he and Flynn retreat to his camper, where he explains the history of the vampires.

Back at the mansion, Beverly injects Liz with a serum that turns her into a vampire, while Jack is drawn into a virtual-reality world where he meets Stephen, the vampire leader and Dark Lord. The Rektors achieve immortality not only by drinking blood but by transferring their blood and spirits into new hosts when their bodies wear out, and they have chosen Liz and Jack as their next vessels. Flynn and Elliot storm the house to save Jack, overcome the henchmen and confront Beverly, now inhabiting Liz's body, as she guards the unfinished transfer between Stephen and Jack. Stephen wakes before the process is complete, but the pair knock out both vampires. With no other known way to kill a Dark Lord, Elliot stays behind with a bomb while Flynn and Jack escape; a post-credits scene confirms that he destroyed the Rektors and their followers.

Announced in 2020 under the title With Teeth, the film was shot in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in November 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Critics were unimpressed, giving it a 22% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

documents.title: Corsage
documents.tagline: No pain, no reign.
documents.overview: A fictional account of one year in the life of Empress Elisabeth of Austria. On Christmas Eve 1877, Elisabeth, once idolized for her beauty, turns 40 and is officially deemed an old woman; she starts trying to maintain her public image.
documents.plot: A fictional account of one year in the life of Empress Elisabeth of Austria. On Christmas Eve 1877, Elisabeth, once idolized for her beauty, turns 40 and is officially deemed an old woman; she starts trying to maintain her public image.

documents.title: Game of Love
documents.overview: Follows Vivien and Roy as their love story continues and leads them to Roy’s childhood home in Sicily to prepare for the sale of the family estate. During the visit, a mysterious woman arrives and befriends Vivien, much to Roy’s displeasure. Tensions build and lines are crossed as secrets from Roy’s past force the couple to face aspects of their relationship they did not know existed.
documents.plot:
Game of Love, released in some markets as Time Is Up 2, is a 2022 Italian English-language romantic drama film directed by Elisa Amoruso, who wrote the screenplay with Marco Borromei and Anita Rivaroli. A sequel to the 2021 film Time Is Up, it was produced by Lotus Production with RAI Cinema and distributed by 01 Distribution. Bella Thorne and Benjamin Mascolo return as the couple Vivien and Roy, joined by Alma Noce as Anna, Simone Coppo and Michael E. Rodgers. Martina Cocco was the cinematographer, and the film runs 91 minutes.

After a slow start, Vivien and Roy have become a happy couple, and they travel together to Sicily, where Roy grew up. The trip is not simply a nostalgic holiday: Roy has decided to sell his family's old house and estate, to pay for his studies. Soon after they arrive, Vivien meets Anna, a young woman who has fallen from her bicycle and hurt herself. The two quickly hit it off, and Vivien keeps inviting her new friend to join them, much to the displeasure of Roy, who is hostile towards her. Anna turns out to be linked to Roy's past and appears to still have feelings for him, and tensions build as lines are crossed and secrets from his past force the couple to confront parts of their relationship they had not known existed. Meanwhile Roy is offered a contract with a gallery that would let him realise his dream of exhibiting his photographs. After some hesitation about staying in Italy, Vivien chooses to support his ambition and the couple extend their stay, and once the tension over Anna eases they are able to continue their romance.

The film was released in October 2022 and became available on Amazon Prime Video, reaching German subscribers in July 2023. It was poorly received. Oliver Armknecht of Film-Rezensionen.de gave a strongly negative review, writing that while Sicily provided an attractive backdrop of countryside drives, grape harvests and old stone buildings, the story manufactured one contrived problem after another until it resembled an unintentional parody of a soap opera. He also found the mystery surrounding Anna and its resolution absurd, criticised Roy's persistent bad temper and argued that, although Thorne and Mascolo were a real-life couple who had been engaged, the two showed no chemistry on screen, so that the film never explained why the characters were together.

documents.title: A Forbidden Orange
documents.overview: Spain, 1970s. A Clockwork Orange, a film considered by critics and audiences as one of the best works in the history of cinema, directed by Stanley Kubrick and released in 1971, was banned by the strict Franco government. However, the film was finally premiered, without going through censorship, during the 20th edition of the Seminci, the Valladolid Film Festival, on April 24, 1975. How was this possible?
documents.plot:
A Forbidden Orange (Spanish: La naranja prohibida) is a 2021 Spanish documentary film written and directed by Pedro González Bermúdez and produced for TCM España. Narrated by Malcolm McDowell, the star of Stanley Kubrick's A Clockwork Orange, it reconstructs how that film, banned under the Franco regime, received its Spanish premiere at the 20th Valladolid International Film Festival (Seminci) in April 1975, three and a half years after its release in the United States and Britain. Interviewees include Carmelo Romero, director of the festival in 1975, the writer and filmmaker Vicente Molina Foix, the novelist Gustavo Martín Garzo and Fernando Herrero. Made to mark the fiftieth anniversary of Kubrick's film by a director born in 1975, it opened the 66th Seminci on 23 October 2021 at the Teatro Carrión, the same venue that had hosted the 1975 public screening, and was released by TCM in December 2021.

The documentary explains that Warner Bros. had offered the film to the festival more than a year earlier with the approval of the regime's censorship board, at a time when the dictatorship was cautiously testing public reaction in controlled settings. A planned 1974 screening fell through when Kubrick asked for the print back, promising a better copy, and never returned it. Romero then persuaded Kubrick by assuring him that the film would be shown only at the University of Valladolid, a small lie, since it played in the festival's regular programme, though nearly all of the audience were students. The film recounts the enormous queues of young people, the scandal when the theatre owner handed out every ticket to his acquaintances before sale, forcing Romero to print new ones, and the divided reaction to the film's violence. It also records a screening of A Clockwork Orange for present-day university students, who agreed that such a film could not be made today, and Molina Foix's recollections of his relationship with Kubrick.

Reviews were mixed. Santiago Alverú of Cinemanía found it an entertaining anecdote with valuable details, especially from Molina Foix, but called it redundant, overloaded in tone and somewhat commissioned in flavour. Rosebud blog de cine rated it 6.5 out of 10, recommending it to anyone from Valladolid as a tribute to the festival and to freedom of expression, though it stayed on the surface and offered little new to those who know Kubrick's film.

documents.title: The Long Dark Trail
documents.tagline: They escaped from a nightmare just to enter into hell.
documents.overview: After two impoverished teenage brothers manage to escape their abusive father, they embark on a treacherous and haunted journey in the hope of finding their estranged mother who has joined a sadistic cult, deep in the woods of Northwest Pennsylvania.
documents.plot:
The Long Dark Trail is an American independent folk horror film written and directed by Kevin Ignatius and Nick Psinakis and produced by Four Eighteen Films. It stars the real-life brothers Carter and Brady O'Donnell as Henry and Jacob, with Michael Thyer as their abusive father Duane and Trina Campbell as their estranged mother, alongside Alex Hughes. Mitchell Kome was the cinematographer and Ignatius also composed the score, which ranges from Appalachian banjo to electronic music and closes with the vocal track "Hollow". The film runs 78 minutes and carries the tagline "They escaped from a nightmare just to enter into hell."

In the backwoods of northwest Pennsylvania, two impoverished teenage brothers have endured years of brutal abuse from their alcoholic father Duane, who once branded Henry with a clothes iron. In a tense prologue the boys tie Duane to a bed with cable ties and flee his cabin on BMX bikes. Acting on a tip from a customer of their gardening work, they head north across country in search of their mother, who left the family and has joined a sadistic cult deep in the forest, hoping she can give them a better life. Divided into chapters with one-word titles such as "Viaduct" and "Lake", their journey through vast woodland is punctuated by flashbacks to the horrors of home and by ominous signs: Jacob finds a mysterious rock marked with a sigil, an infection of pustules spreads across Henry's neck, and the boys pass what appears to be a burial ground. Intercut scenes hint at deadly rituals in the region, and as hallucinations take hold the brothers eventually discover what kind of company their mother keeps.

The film is dated 2021 in some listings and was released on digital, DVD and Blu-ray by Cleopatra Entertainment on 21 February 2023. Reviews praised its visuals more than its story. Phil Hoad of The Guardian called it an atmospheric, sharply directed fable despite its shoestring budget and minimal plot, while noting debts to Mandy and questioning the processed sound applied to the dialogue. Paul Lê of Bloody Disgusting found it uneven and incoherent but elevated by Kome's photography of the Allegheny landscape and Ignatius's music. Adam Mock of Film Inquiry was far harsher, faulting its slow pace, stilted performances and rushed finale.

documents.title: What We Leave Behind
documents.overview: At the age of 89, Julián Moreno takes one last bus ride to El Paso, Texas, to visit his daughters and their children – a lengthy trip he has made without fail every month for decades. After returning to rural Mexico, he quietly starts building a house in the empty lot next to his home. In the absence of his physical visits, can this new house bridge the distance between his loved ones?
documents.plot:
What We Leave Behind is a 2022 Mexican-American documentary film directed by Iliana Sosa, who co-wrote it with editor Isidore Bethel. A Spanish-language portrait of Sosa's grandfather, Julián Moreno, filmed over several years, it was produced by Emma D. Miller and Sosa through Borderchild Productions and Marcona Media with JustFilms, and developed with support from the Sundance Institute, the IDA, the Austin Film Society and the Gotham Documentary Lab, among others. It premiered at South by Southwest in March 2022, received a theatrical release from Ava DuVernay's ARRAY, and debuted on Netflix in several English-speaking countries on 30 September 2022. It runs 71 minutes.

For about twenty years, Julián made a monthly 560-mile bus trip from his home in San Juan del Río, in the Mexican state of Durango, to El Paso, Texas, to visit his daughters and grandchildren, bringing candy and gifts and leaving after a day or two. As the film begins, he is 89 and making the last of these journeys. Widowed at 45 and the father of seven, some still in his hometown and some in the United States, he once worked as a bracero, a seasonal contract labourer in the US, and he shows his granddaughter his 1964 Alien Laborer's Identification Card. Back in rural Mexico he begins building a cinderblock house on the empty lot beside the small home he shares with his son Jorge, who is blind, and their dog Pinto, a project that, like his cross-border visits, is meant to keep the family close. In a conversation with Jorge, Sosa explores the death of her grandmother at 39 and its effect on the family, and the film visits her grave in the busy local cemetery. Lyrical interludes pair Sosa's voiceover with images of the surrounding landscape, while the soundtrack features an a cappella song by the Cardencheros de Sapioriz, also from Durango. Over the following years the film records Julián's growing frailty and his final days.

What We Leave Behind won the Fandor New Voices Award and the Louis Black "Lone Star" Award at SXSW and was nominated for Best Documentary at the Gotham Awards. It drew universal acclaim, with a Metacritic score of 89 and a perfect Rotten Tomatoes rating. Sheri Linden of The Hollywood Reporter called it first-person filmmaking at its eloquent best, the Boston Globe found it limpid and poetically resonant, and The New York Times named it a Critic's Pick.

documents.title: Railway Heroes
documents.overview: The historical story of an enemy fighting the wits and courage of an extraordinary brave group of ordinary heroes known as the "Lunan Railway Brigade" who desperately fight to defend their homeland.
documents.plot: The historical story of an enemy fighting the wits and courage of an extraordinary brave group of ordinary heroes known as the "Lunan Railway Brigade" who desperately fight to defend their homeland.

documents.title: Love Like the Falling Petals
documents.overview: Haruto Asakura falls in love with hairdresser Misaki Ariake and asks her out. Watching Misaki Ariake work hard to achieve what she wants, Haruto Asakura, who almost gave up his dream to become a photographer, begins to pursue his dream again, but Misaki Ariake is diagnosed with a disease that ages her 10x faster than normal.
documents.plot:
Love Like the Falling Petals (Japanese: 桜のような僕の恋人, Sakura no Yō na Boku no Koibito) is a 2022 Japanese romantic drama film directed by Yoshihiro Fukagawa and written by Tomoko Yoshida, based on Keisuke Uyama's 2017 novel of the same name. Kento Nakajima stars as Haruto Asakura, with Honoka Matsumoto as Misaki Ariake, Kento Nagayama as her older brother Takashi and Jun Kaname as her doctor. The film was released worldwide on Netflix on 24 March 2022.

Haruto, an aspiring photographer who has drifted away from his ambitions, goes for a haircut and is instantly smitten with the young hairdresser who cuts his hair, Misaki, who tells him that he is her very first customer. Wanting to impress her, he introduces himself as a professional photographer, stretching the truth. He keeps returning to the salon, and the two grow closer. When he finally tries to ask her out during a haircut, he moves his head and she accidentally nicks his earlobe, causing him to bleed and faint. Mortified, Misaki meets him to apologize and agrees to go out with him, despite the disapproval of her protective older brother.

On their first outing, to see the cherry blossoms, Haruto confesses that he is not really working as a photographer and does not know what to do with his life. Misaki is angered that he has given up on his dream so easily and urges him not to quit just because things are difficult. Taking her words to heart, he gets a job at a photo studio and works hard to become someone she can be proud of, and their relationship blossoms into a serious romance.

Their happiness is shattered when Misaki falls ill and is diagnosed with a rare progeroid syndrome, a disease that causes her body to age at an extraordinary speed and leaves her with very little time. Devastated and unwilling to let Haruto see her change, she withdraws from him, quits her job at the salon and eventually tells him that she has found someone else, breaking his heart. Cared for by her brother, who desperately searches for a cure, Misaki faces her rapid decline in seclusion, while Haruto, unaware of the truth, throws himself into his photography. The film follows both of them through the seasons as their separate paths move toward a final, bittersweet reckoning, with cherry blossoms serving as a recurring symbol of fleeting beauty and impermanence.

documents.title: Fistful of Vengeance
documents.overview: A revenge mission becomes a fight to save the world from an ancient threat when superpowered assassin Kai tracks a killer to Bangkok.
documents.plot:
Fistful of Vengeance is a 2022 American supernatural martial arts action film directed by Roel Reiné and written by Cameron Litvack, Jessica Chou and Yalun Tu. A follow-up to the first season of the Netflix television series Wu Assassins, it stars Iko Uwais as Kai, Lewis Tan as Lu Xin and Lawrence Kao as Tommy, with Rhatha Phongam, JuJu Chan, Pearl Thusi, Francesca Corney, Jason Tobin and Simon Kuke.

Kai, the current Wu Assassin, and his friends Lu Xin and Tommy travel to Bangkok to find the killer of Tommy's sister Jenny, following the trail of an ancient talisman found on her body. In Thailand they are approached by William Pan, a biotech billionaire, who asks them to capture his twin sister, Ku An Qi, a powerful crime boss and jiangshi who has been absorbing vast amounts of qi to increase her supernatural powers. William explains that he and Ku are descendants of Pangu, the being who shaped the universe and who was killed by the first Wu Assassin after he became mad with power, and that his essence is contained in two talismans, one of which belonged to Ku.

According to William, Ku killed Jenny while searching for Kai, and with both talismans he can strip his sister of her power. Kai and his friends agree to help him and, joined by Tommy's friend Preeya, attempt to abduct Ku during a meeting with the city's Triad bosses. The plan goes wrong when Ku uses mind control to turn everyone in the building against them and Kai is ambushed by his old enemy Zan. Rescued by Zama, an Interpol agent who is pursuing Ku and is Lu Xin's former lover, the group takes refuge in Preeya's village, where a shaman reveals that William is secretly working with his sister to resurrect Pangu and remake the world.

The film combines martial arts fight sequences with Chinese mythology and supernatural elements, continuing the storylines left unresolved by the series.

Fistful of Vengeance was released worldwide on Netflix on February 17, 2022. It received mixed reviews, with 45 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 44.

documents.title: A Christmas Proposal
documents.overview: Chef who dreams of having own food trucks, agrees to pose as girlfriend of an attorney. Working together, they try to prove he's the ideal candidate to take over the family firm, but is complicated as real sparks begin to fly.
documents.plot:
A Christmas Proposal is a 2021 American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Martin Wood and produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America and Brad Krevoy Television for CBS. It stars Jessica Camacho as Maria Winters and Adam Rodriguez as Julian Diaz, with Luisa d'Oliveira as Maria's best friend Brooklyn, Bianca Caroca, Andres Soto, Claudia Ferri, Juan Chioran, Jaime M. Callica, Serge Houde, Shawn Hook, Malaika Jackson and Frank Crudele. Rodriguez, who also worked on the script to make the Latino family it portrays more authentic, described it as one of the first network Christmas films centred on an American family of Latin descent.

Maria is a struggling personal chef in Seattle who dreams of owning her own line of food trucks and drives for a ride-share app between cooking jobs. On her way to a singles Christmas party she picks up Julian, a wealthy, ambitious and rather cold attorney who pays her to drive him about 100 miles outside the city, where he plans to spend Christmas impressing his powerful father in the hope of being named his successor at the family law firm when he retires on Christmas Eve. Julian fears the job will instead go to his brother Bennett, who has a wife and children and seems more settled. When his parents meet Maria, they assume she is the surprise girlfriend Julian has hinted at, and he decides to run with the misunderstanding, while Maria agrees in return for an investment in her food truck. To keep their story straight without technically lying, the pair go on a crammed "power date" so they can describe their relationship truthfully. Maria cooks the family Christmas dinner, asks everyone to put their phones away at the table, and gradually draws the distracted Diaz family closer, but the business arrangement is complicated as real feelings develop between her and Julian, culminating at a Christmas Eve gala for children in need.

The film premiered on CBS on 12 December 2021. Brett White of Decider recommended it, presenting it as a revival of the major-network TV movie and praising its sleek, high-budget look, the lavish Diaz house, the chemistry between Camacho and Rodriguez and d'Oliveira's comic turn as the wisecracking best friend, and arguing that its inventive touches made an extremely familiar fake-relationship premise feel fresh.

documents.title: 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible
documents.overview: In 2019, Nepalese mountain climber Nirmal “Nims” Purja set out to do the unthinkable by climbing the world’s fourteen highest summits in less than seven months. (The previous record was eight years). He called the effort “Project Possible 14/7” and saw it as a way to inspire others to strive for greater heights in any pursuit. The film follows his team as they seek to defy naysayers and push the limits of human endurance.
documents.plot:
14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible is a 2021 documentary directed by Torquil Jones that follows the Nepali mountaineer Nirmal "Nims" Purja and his team on Project Possible, an attempt to climb all fourteen of the world's eight-thousanders, the peaks higher than 8,000 metres, in under seven months. The previous fastest time, set by South Korea's Kim Chang-ho, was 7 years and 310 days. Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Vasarhelyi served as executive producers with Purja, and the film features interviews with Reinhold Messner, the first person to climb all fourteen, as well as Chin, Purja's wife Suchi and his brother Kamal.

The expedition opens on Annapurna, statistically the deadliest of the peaks, which Purja summits on 23 April 2019 together with the Canadian climber Don Bowie, who had failed on it several times. The next day Purja goes back up to rescue a stricken Malaysian climber, costing his team its weather window on Dhaulagiri, which they summit in poor conditions on 12 May. Descending from Kanchenjunga after a single 22-hour push, the team comes across two Indian climbers in trouble in the death zone; despite giving them all their oxygen and waiting 12 hours for help, both die. Shaken and behind schedule, Purja climbs Everest, Lhotse and Makalu in a record 48 hours, and his photograph of the huge queue of climbers near Everest's summit goes viral.

Interviews trace Purja's background, including his service in the Gurkhas and Britain's Special Boat Service, a near-fatal sniper wound, his mother's failing health and the financial risks he took to fund the project, which at the outset was largely paid for by remortgaging his house. Moving to the Karakoram, he survives a fall on Nanga Parbat, then climbs the Gasherbrums, K2 and Broad Peak in 23 days; on K2, where avalanche danger has demoralised other teams, his crew fixes ropes through the Bottleneck that let 24 other climbers reach the summit. After rushing home to his mother, who has had a heart attack, he climbs Cho Oyu and Manaslu, lobbies for a Chinese permit and completes the project on Shishapangma on 29 October 2019, six months and six days after he began.

The film premiered at the DOC NYC festival and was released worldwide on Netflix in November 2021. It was well received, with 90% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; The New York Times praised its celebration of communal bonds.

documents.title: God's Crooked Lines
documents.overview: Alice Gould, a private investigator, pretends to be mentally ill in order to enter a psychiatric hospital and gather evidence for the case she is working on: the death of a patient in unclear circumstances.
documents.plot:
God's Crooked Lines (Spanish: Los renglones torcidos de Dios) is a 2022 Spanish psychological thriller directed by Oriol Paulo and starring Bárbara Lennie as Alice Gould. Written by Paulo and Guillem Clua with the collaboration of Lara Sendim, it adapts Torcuato Luca de Tena's 1979 novel of the same name. Set inside a psychiatric hospital, the film is built around the question of whether its heroine is a brilliant investigator or a dangerously unstable patient.

In 1979, Alice Gould de Almenara is admitted to a psychiatric institution. She tells the doctors that she has been "legally abducted" by her husband, Heliodoro, who wants to seize her fortune. In reality, Alice claims, she is a private investigator who has feigned a mental illness to get inside the hospital, at the request of a doctor whose son, Damián, died there in mysterious circumstances. Once inside, she begins investigating among the patients, befriending some of them, including Ignacio Urquieta and a pair of twins, while confronting a predatory inmate known as the Gnome and his protector.

A second timeline, set during a stormy night when a fire and riot break out and a body is found in one of the cells, gradually converges with the main story. When the Gnome is found dead after attacking Alice in the woods, she becomes a suspect, and she struggles to remember what happened. Alice's account of her mission is challenged by the hospital's director, who presents evidence that she tried to poison her husband and that her story is a symptom of paranoia. As the medical council meets to decide her fate, both the doctors and the audience must determine whether Alice is telling the truth.

The film plays with the unreliability of perception and the boundary between sanity and madness, keeping its central ambiguity alive until the end.

God's Crooked Lines premiered at the 70th San Sebastián International Film Festival in September 2022 and was released theatrically in Spain by Warner Bros. on 6 October 2022, becoming one of the highest-grossing Spanish films of the year, before arriving on Netflix in December. It received positive reviews, with Cinemanía calling it a thrilling and elegant exercise, and earned six nominations at the 37th Goya Awards, including Best Actress for Lennie and Best Adapted Screenplay.

documents.title: The Good Neighbor
documents.tagline: Fear what's next door.
documents.overview: A nightmarish evening unfolds for David, a former New York Times journalist, when he and his strange new neighbor Robert, accidentally hit a girl on her bike. Buzzed and disoriented, David lets Robert convince him to flee the scene and leave the girl for dead, in order to protect his career. Robert shows no remorse, and in the name of friendship he does unspeakable things to protect the secret. Now that the police are full-on hunting for the hit-and-run killer, things begin to spiral out of control when David’s local newspaper sends him to cover the story where he meets the deceased girl’s sister Vanessa. Despite the circumstances, and her deep desire to find her sister’s killer, the two immediately have a romantic connection, which surprises and haunts David, while pushing Robert to take brutal steps to keep his new friend to himself.
documents.plot:
The Good Neighbor is a 2022 mystery crime thriller film directed by Stephan Rick, who wrote the screenplay with Ross Partridge, a remake of Rick's 2011 German film of the same name. Luke Kleintank stars as David Stevens, an American journalist, with Jonathan Rhys Meyers as his neighbor, Robert, Eloise Smyth and Bruce Davison. An American-Latvian co-production set and filmed in and around Riga, it received a limited theatrical release in June 2022 before being released on demand.

After a painful breakup, David arrives in Riga, Latvia, to begin a new job at the European Press Network. His editor, Grant, lets him stay in a house on the outskirts of the city while an apartment is prepared, and warns him that, as a newcomer, he will be given the assignments no one else wants. At the office, Grant tries to set him up with a colleague, Alice, but David is more interested in enjoying the city's nightlife as a single man. When he has trouble starting the old car Grant has left him, he is helped by his neighbor, Robert, a friendly but eccentric home-care nurse who tells him that his mother was British.

Lonely one evening, David invites Robert out for drinks. At a club, David flirts with Janine, a young woman from London, while Robert watches with disapproval. Driving home drunk, the two men are involved in a hit-and-run accident on a dark road, in which a cyclist is struck, and Robert persuades David not to report it. Consumed by guilt, David follows the case as the police investigation progresses, but he soon realizes that his new friend is far more dangerous than he appeared. Robert's behavior becomes increasingly possessive and controlling, and he uses their shared secret to bind David to him, while David's attempts to build a relationship and make amends threaten to expose them both. As Robert's obsession escalates into violence, David must find a way to free himself from his neighbor's grip before he loses everything.

The Good Neighbor received mixed reviews. Variety found it polished and well acted enough to be reasonably entertaining for its running time, but not original, tense or plausible enough to avoid a sense of letdown. Luke Y. Thompson of The A.V. Club graded it a C+, while other reviewers praised its unusual Riga setting and its suspense.

documents.title: American Sicario
documents.tagline: The story of America's most dangerous drug trafficker.
documents.overview: The story of the rise and fall of the first American-born drug lord in Mexico, this tale of power, money, greed and betrayal amongst rival members of the drug cartels finds American gangster Erik Vasquez scheming to become the top dog in the Mexican underworld, only to find himself making enemies out of both the powerful cartels and his own allies.
documents.plot:
American Sicario is a 2021 American crime action film directed by Raja "RJ" Collins from a screenplay by Rich Ronat, presented as being based on a true story. Produced in association with VMI Worldwide and GFG Entertainment and distributed by Saban Films, it stars Philippe A. Haddad as an American-born drug lord in Mexico, with Danny Trejo, Cali Morales, Maurice Compte, Maya Stojan, Jaylen Moore, Johnny Rey Diaz, Dionysio Basco and David A. Lockhart in supporting roles. The film opened in select US theatres on 10 December 2021 and was released on demand and on digital platforms on 14 December. It is rated R for violence, pervasive language, drug use and sexual material.

The film charts the rise and fall of Erik Vasquez (Haddad), a burly Texas native who fled to Mexico to escape narcotics charges in Laredo and has since worked his way up the cartel food chain, building his own gang and smuggling drugs back across the border. He now has a pregnant wife, Gloria (Morales), and a father-in-law, Pedro (Trejo), who is staying with them for an extended visit. Pedro, a veteran who once dealt drugs and worked with the cartels himself before getting out, has firm ideas about how Erik should treat Gloria and her unborn child, and warns him that in their business nothing is more important than family and loyalty. Scheming to become the top figure in the Mexican underworld, Erik tries to outmanoeuvre his bosses, the Feliz brothers (Compte and Diaz), and also crosses paths with DEA agent Monica Wells (Stojan). His ambition and greed turn both the powerful cartels and his own allies against him, culminating in an attack on his mansion, while his clashes with Pedro test the bonds of family and loyalty.

Critics generally found the film derivative. Josh Lasser of The TV and Film Guy's Reviews considered the cartel storyline bland and populated by two-dimensional characters, but enjoyed the lighter, more comic family thread driven by Trejo's sly presence, regretting that it played second fiddle. John Strange of Selig Film News gave it two stars, calling the gunfights poorly staged and edited and saying Trejo was wasted on the material. Mae Trumata of The Upcoming was more positive, praising the high-contrast, neon-lit cinematography and editing, the mansion assault sequence and the well-drawn generational contrast between Erik and Pedro.

documents.title: Virus:32
documents.tagline: 32 seconds to live or die.
documents.overview: A virus is unleashed and a chilling massacre runs through the streets of Montevideo.
documents.plot:
Virus:32 (Spanish: Virus 32) is a 2022 Uruguayan-Argentine horror film directed by Gustavo Hernández, who co-wrote it with Juma Fodde Roma. Produced by Aeroplano Cine, Mother Superior Films and Latido Films, with Sebastián Aloi and Ignacio García Cucucovich as producers and music by Hernán González, it stars Paula Silva, Daniel Hendler and the young Pilar García, with Franco Rilla and Sofía González. Set in Montevideo, it takes its title from a crucial detail: after each kill, the infected fall still for exactly thirty-two seconds.

Iris (Silva) works as a night guard at a vast, rundown sports club. Separated from her husband Javier (Rilla) since the death of their young son, she shares custody of their eight-year-old daughter Tata (García), and one night, having forgotten it is her turn, she must bring the girl along to work. Meanwhile, a virus is spreading through the city, turning people into savage killers. Leaving Tata in the gym with a walkie-talkie and watching her through the security cameras, Iris patrols the building, where strange figures have begun to appear. Attacked by an infected man and witnessing assaults in the street, she notices the thirty-two-second pause that follows each killing. Then Tata vanishes from the monitors. Searching the dark corridors as more infected arrive, Iris meets Luis (Hendler), a stranger who claims to know where her daughter is but demands that she first help deliver his wife's baby. She agrees, only to discover that the woman, bound and gagged in a wheelchair, is infected. Their ordeal leads through a besieged swimming pool, where the dying Javier appears, to a desperate birth, while Iris clings to the hope of finding Tata alive and escaping toward the port.

The film opened in Argentine cinemas on 21 April 2022 through Star Distribution and was released on video on demand in France that July. It received positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting more than 90% approval. Página 12 called it a magnificent horror tale and praised Silva's excellent performance, La Nación wrote that it is genuinely scary and sustains tension throughout with well-timed twists, and Clarín admired its perceptive script, agile direction and the work of Silva, a menacing Hendler and the debuting García. Otros Cines considered it a valuable example of the zombie subgenre in Latin American cinema, which rarely explores the theme, and Russian critic Stanislav Zelvensky included it among the best horror films of 2022.

documents.title: Sword Art Online the Movie -Progressive- Scherzo of Deep Night
documents.original_title: 劇場版 ソードアート・オンライン -プログレッシブ- 冥き夕闇のスケルツォ
documents.tagline: You will definitely become stronger.
documents.overview: Over a month has passed since 10,000 users were trapped inside the "Sword Art Online" world. Asuna, who cleared the first floor of the floating iron castle of Aincrad, joined up with Kirito and continued her journey to reach the top floor. With the support of female Information Broker Argo, clearing the floors seemed to be progressing smoothly, but conflict erupts between two major guilds who should be working together – the top player groups ALS (the Aincrad Liberation Squad) and DKB (the Dragon Knights Brigade). And meanwhile, behind the scenes exists a mysterious figure pulling the strings…
documents.plot:
Sword Art Online the Movie: Progressive – Scherzo of Deep Night is a 2022 Japanese animated science fiction action film based on Reki Kawahara's Sword Art Online: Progressive light novels, illustrated by abec, and the sequel to the 2021 film Sword Art Online: Progressive – Aria of a Starless Night. The staff of the first film returned, with production by A-1 Pictures, direction by Ayako Kōno, character designs by Kento Toya and music by Yuki Kajiura. The film retells the early days of the deadly virtual reality game Sword Art Online from the perspective of Asuna.

Thousands of players remain trapped in the virtual world of Aincrad, where dying in the game means dying in real life and the only way out is to clear all one hundred floors. In December 2022, the two leading guilds, ALS and DKB, defeat the boss of the fourth floor alongside a few other players, including Asuna and Kirito, but the guilds are increasingly at odds over how the game should be completed. While exploring the dungeon beneath the fifth floor's main town, Asuna overhears two players plotting to destroy both guilds by having ALS secretly break away from a planned New Year's party to defeat the fifth floor boss alone.

Realizing that such a betrayal could fatally undermine the cooperation needed to escape the game, Kirito and Asuna confront Kibaou, the leader of ALS, who admits that a faction within his guild is pushing for the plan in order to claim a powerful item dropped by the boss. Kirito and Asuna decide to defeat the boss first, assembling a small raid party, though Asuna's former friend Mito, still troubled by the events of the first film, initially refuses to join. The battle against the giant boss, a golem whose weak point keeps shifting, tests the group to its limits. Afterward, an encounter with a mysterious attacker reveals the existence of players dedicated to killing others.

The film focuses on the friendship between Asuna and Mito and on the growing tensions among players as the game progresses.

The film was released in Japan on October 22, 2022, after being delayed from September due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and was released in North America by Aniplex of America in February 2023. Reviews were mixed: Anime News Network praised its world-building, production and soundtrack but found it predictable, while The Guardian gave it two stars out of five.

documents.title: The Whole Truth
documents.original_title: ปริศนารูหลอน
documents.tagline: A truth you've never known, that makes you doubt what you know.
documents.overview: When two siblings stumble on a strange hole in the wall of their grandparents' house, horrifying incidents reveal sinister secrets about their family.
documents.plot:
The Whole Truth (Thai: ปริศนารูหลอน, literally "Haunted Hole Puzzle") is a Thai supernatural horror mystery from 2021, directed by Wisit Sasanatieng from a script by Abishek J. Bajaj. Sompob Benjathikul plays Phong, a former senior police officer, Nicole Theriault plays Mai and Sutatta Udomsilp her daughter Pim, with Sadanont Durongkaweroj, Steven Isarapong and Nattapat Nimjirawat among the cast. It was released on Netflix on 2 December 2021.

Pim, a popular cheerleader, and her brother Putt, an outsider who wears a leg brace, live with their single mother Mai. When Mai is left in a coma after a car accident on a stormy night, a man introducing himself as their grandfather, Phong, takes the teenagers to stay with him and their grandmother Wan, who suffers from dementia and keeps calling Putt "Krit". Neither child remembers the house, although they are told they lived there when small. Putt finds a hole in the wall through which he sees a decaying version of the same house and a dark-haired figure, but his grandparents claim they can see no hole. Meanwhile Putt's classmate Fame is blackmailing him with a video he secretly filmed of Pim showering.

Through the hole the siblings glimpse a girl with a blackened, swollen face, crawling, vomiting dark fluid and cradling a baby. Putt falls ill after drinking the milk Wan keeps giving him, and the family cat dies. Phong, learning that the wealthy young man blamed for Mai's crash has escaped justice, hunts him down and burns him alive. Eventually the hole shows the past: their sister Pinya died after being locked in a closet, where she drank rat poison while their father Krit was drunk, and Krit was later found shot. Mai wakes, rushes to the house and confronts her parents, and Wan finally admits she has poisoned Putt, as she did Pinya, raving that she was ridding Mai of her "freaks". Mai takes the children away. Later, Phong learns that the young man he murdered was innocent after all. Pinya's ghost appears to Wan, who is then found convulsing with rat poison; Phong, terrified by the burning ghost of the man he killed, accidentally shoots his wife and then kills himself, the bullet creating the hole he never could see. Final flashbacks reveal that Wan deliberately bolted Pinya inside the closet, and that it was Mai who shot Krit, with Phong disguising the killing as suicide. The film closes on Pim asleep with Pinya's ghost holding her hand.

documents.title: Studio 666
documents.tagline: He gives new meaning to a killer track.
documents.overview: Legendary rock band Foo Fighters move into an Encino mansion steeped in grisly rock and roll history to record their much anticipated 10th album. Once in the house, Dave Grohl finds himself grappling with supernatural forces that threaten both the completion of the album and the lives of the band.
documents.plot:
Studio 666 is a 2022 American comedy horror film directed by B. J. McDonnell from a screenplay by Jeff Buhler and Rebecca Hughes, based on a story by Dave Grohl. Grohl and his Foo Fighters bandmates Taylor Hawkins, Nate Mendel, Pat Smear, Chris Shiflett and Rami Jaffee play fictionalized versions of themselves, making it the band's first non-documentary film. Grohl drew on the band's experience of recording their tenth album, and the film was shot in secret in the same house where they had made Medicine at Midnight. Production was halted near the end by the COVID-19 pandemic and resumed months later in Los Angeles, where a planned six days of shooting stretched to three weeks under safety rules.

In 1993, in Encino, Dream Widow frontman Greg Nole attacks his bandmates with a hammer, killing the drummer Skye Willow, and then hangs himself. In 2019 the Foo Fighters, pushed by their manager Jeremy Shill to beat writer's block and deliver a new album, move into the same mansion. Grohl is enthralled by the house, and after the band's technician Krug is electrocuted, he finds a basement full of satanic objects and becomes possessed by Nole's demonic spirit while listening to an old demo tape. Driven by the demon, he forces the band to keep recording while secretly killing a delivery man and then Shiflett.

With help from their neighbor Samantha, the others discover the history of the house and the cause of Grohl's possession, and learn that they need a book to exorcise him. Grohl kills Jaffee and Samantha with a chainsaw and Hawkins with a cymbal once he finishes the song, before Mendel and Smear free him, and the spirits of Dream Widow drag the demon back to hell. Jeremy and the property developer Barb Weems then reveal that they planned everything, and Mendel and Smear die in the ensuing violence. Told that the album is a hit and his solo career has begun, Grohl abandons his fight with Jeremy and, a year later, prepares a solo concert with marks of possession around his eyes.

Whitney Cummings plays Samantha, Will Forte the delivery man Darren, Jeff Garlin the manager and Leslie Grossman Barb, with Jenna Ortega as Skye, Kerry King as Krug and small roles for Lionel Richie and John Carpenter. Released by Open Road Films and Briarcliff Entertainment on February 25, 2022, it earned only $1.54 million in its opening weekend. Reviews were mixed, with 56% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and it was Hawkins's final film.

documents.title: Trolls Holiday in Harmony
documents.tagline: The holidays are better together.
documents.overview: Queen Poppy plans the first annual Trolls Kingdom Secret Holiday Gift Swap, but things don't go quite as expected.
documents.plot:
Trolls: Holiday in Harmony is an American animated musical Christmas special of 2021 from DreamWorks Animation, the second holiday special based on the Trolls franchise after Trolls Holiday. Written and directed by Sean Charmatz and Tim Heitz in their official directing debut, it premiered on NBC on 26 November 2021. Returning voices include Anna Kendrick as Queen Poppy, Justin Timberlake as Branch, Rachel Bloom as Queen Barb, Kunal Nayyar as Guy Diamond and Kenan Thompson as Tiny Diamond, with guests including Carol Burnett and Travis Scott.

On their first date, Poppy tells Branch about her plans for a holiday gift exchange. Each Troll will draw another's name and bring a secret present to Pop Village in three days. After delivering the baskets all over the kingdom, Poppy and Branch draw the last two cards and find each other's names. Poppy is delighted; Branch is terrified.

In Pop Village, Tiny Diamond draws his own father, Guy Diamond, and sets out to write him a rap, but he cannot find anything that rhymes with "Diamond" and fears he has lost his flow. After several failures he climbs a mountain to consult the monks of the Cloud Temple, and meditating with the Clouds helps him see that he simply needs to rhyme with "daddy". Back in the village, Poppy puts the finishing touches on her gift, sure that it is just right. Branch, meanwhile, dreams up a machine to style Poppy's hair and secretly measures her head, but after glimpsing her present for him he panics that his will fall short and retreats to his bunker. There he keeps adding feature after feature to the contraption until a test run makes it explode, launching him into space before he crashes back down in the village. Tiny finds him, hears his tale of failure and passes on the lesson he has just learned: look past the clutter. While tidying the wreckage of his bunker, Branch comes across a photograph of himself with Poppy and realizes what to do.

At the exchange, Branch gives Poppy a scrapbook recording everything they have been through together, a gift only he could make. Poppy's box for him turns out to be empty, because she knew nothing could be good enough for him. Realizing that all they need is each other, they embrace, the Trolls sing "Together Now", and the couple float off on a balloon ride, Poppy kissing Branch on the cheek.

The broadcast, aired on Black Friday, drew about 1.8 million live viewers, rising to about 2.2 million after a week.

documents.title: Beneath the Surface
documents.tagline: Prey you will make it out alive!
documents.overview: A young woman survives a great white shark attack, whilst on a family boating vacation, however soon realizes the nightmare is far from over. Those around her can not be trusted, and she must face her demons, if she is to step back in the water.
documents.plot:
Beneath the Surface is a 2022 psychological thriller film directed by Scott Jeffrey and Rebecca Matthews from a screenplay by first-time feature writer Paul W. Franklin. The directing team, prolific makers of low-budget genre films such as The Gardener and Exorcist Vengeance, made it with the production companies Proportion Productions, Sci-Fi Productions and I Imagine. It stars Georgie Banks as a young survivor of a great white shark attack, with Jamie Robertson, Annie Knox, Matthew Marcelis, Stephanie Lodge, Beatrice Fletcher and Nicola Wright in supporting roles. The film was released on video-on-demand and digital platforms by Devilworks in early 2022 and runs 93 minutes.

The film opens with a shark attacking a man and his two daughters during a family boating holiday, a scene that recurs throughout in flashbacks. Three months later, in South Africa, an inquest examines the accident that left Lexy (Banks), her father Bill (Robertson) and her sister Chloe (Knox) in the water. Lexy was the only one of the three to survive long enough to be rescued, pulled out by her boyfriend Isaac (Marcelis) and her stepmother Vicky (Lodge). In the aftermath she struggles with survivor's guilt, depression and other psychological wounds, and her friend Amy (Fletcher) persuades her to see a therapist, Dr. Goodman (Wright), despite the objections of Isaac and Vicky. The therapy sessions unlock memories of that night suggesting that what happened was no accident. Realising that the people around her cannot be trusted, Lexy must face her demons if she is to survive and ever step back into the sea.

Although its poster promised a killer-shark film, the story is chiefly a drama about trauma that turns into a suspense mystery. Jim Morazzini, reviewing the film for Voices From the Balcony in a piece republished by Nerdly, gave it one star out of five and called it a misfire. He found the drama dull, considered the script clumsy and its clues so obvious that the mystery was solved before Lexy's first therapy session, and judged the shark attacks, evidently shot in a studio tank, almost laughably bad and devoid of tension. He also felt the characters' actions were never believable and described the film as a major step backwards for directors whose recent work had shown improvement.

documents.title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules
documents.original_title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules
documents.tagline: Get ready to rock n' rüle!
documents.overview: A new school year, his brother Rodrick teases him over and over and over and over again. Will Greg manage to get along with him? Or will a secret ruin everything?
documents.plot:
Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules, stylised as Rodrick Rüles, is a 2022 animated comedy directed by Luke Cormican in his feature directorial debut, from a screenplay by Jeff Kinney based on his 2008 book of the same name. It is the sequel to the 2021 animated Diary of a Wimpy Kid and the second adaptation of Rodrick Rules after the 2011 live-action film. Brady Noon voices Greg Heffley, with Hunter Dillon as his older brother Rodrick, Ethan William Childress as Rowley Jefferson, and Chris Diamantopoulos and Erica Cerra as their parents, Frank and Susan. The film was released on Disney+ on 2 December 2022.

While their parents and little brother Manny are away for a weekend, Rodrick throws a party at the house. Greg invites Rowley to help, but Rodrick locks them in the basement. After escaping, Greg secretly takes photos of the party, which gives him leverage over his brother. When their mother calls to say they are coming home early because Manny is ill, the brothers frantically clear out the guests and clean up the house, replacing the bathroom door on which someone has scrawled "Rodrick Rules" in marker. In return for Greg's help, Rodrick shares his "Rodrick Rules", his philosophy for a relaxed and effort-free life.

The unlikely alliance brings the brothers closer. Rodrick begins teaching Greg to play the drums and introduces him to the members of his heavy metal band, Löded Diper, which is preparing for an upcoming talent show. Meanwhile, Rowley plans to perform a magic act and asks Greg to be his assistant, but Greg turns him down because he thinks the act will flop. Frank grows suspicious about the damaged bathroom door, while Susan is delighted to see her sons getting along. When the parents leave again and send the boys to stay with their grandfather at a retirement community, the secret of the party becomes harder to keep, and Greg must choose between protecting Rodrick and his loyalty to his family and friend as the talent show approaches.

As with the previous animated film, the visual style recreates Kinney's illustrations in three-dimensional computer animation. The story centres on sibling rivalry, the relationship between Greg and Rodrick, and the misadventures of Greg's attempts to avoid responsibility.

The film received mixed reviews; critics appreciated its brisk humour and its focus on the brothers' relationship, though many considered it a lightweight retelling of material already adapted in live action.

documents.title: The Bad Seed Returns
documents.overview: Several years after the murderous events of the first movie left her father dead, Emma is now living with her aunt Angela and navigating high school. Angela’s husband begins to suspect that Emma may not be as innocent as she appears and suggests sending her off to boarding school. Meanwhile, a new girl at school seems to know Emma’s secrets, leaving Emma no choice but to slip back to her old ways and take care of her enemies by any means necessary.
documents.plot:
The Bad Seed Returns is a 2022 American made-for-television horror drama film directed by Louise Archambault and written by Ross Burge, Mckenna Grace and Barbara Marshall. A sequel to the 2018 television film The Bad Seed, itself a remake of the 1956 film adapted from William March's 1954 novel, it stars Grace, reprising her role as Emma, with Michelle Morgan, Benjamin Ayres, Ella Dixon, Marlowe Zimmerman and Jude Wilson. Patty McCormack, who played the murderous Rhoda Penmark in the 1956 version, makes a special appearance as Emma's therapist, Dr. March. The film was shot in Vancouver and premiered on Lifetime on September 5, 2022.

Six years after the death of her father, David, 15-year-old Emma Grossman lives with her aunt Angela, a psychiatrist, Angela's new husband Robert and their baby son, Cade. Nobody suspects her past crimes, and Emma keeps up the appearance of an ordinary teenager devoted to school, friends and her dance team while concealing her psychopathy. She resents Robert's presence in the household, and when he finds his missing camping knife hidden in her drawer, he arranges for her to be sent to a boarding school, St. Crispin's. Emma responds by sabotaging his car jack, leaving him badly injured in hospital. At school, a new student named Kat, who knows about Emma's past, refuses to be fooled by her, and Emma's rivalry with her friend Stephanie over the position of dance captain takes a dark turn. As people around her begin to suffer suspicious misfortunes, Angela slowly starts to see her niece for who she really is, and a conversation with Brian, the caretaker who shot David in self-defense years earlier, helps her understand what David had come to realize. Robert, meanwhile, begins to recover his memory of what happened to him and confronts Emma with an ultimatum. Cornered, Emma prepares a final scheme to protect herself and her secret, putting everyone in the household in grave danger.

Production on the sequel was announced in November 2021, with Grace both co-writing and starring, and filming took place in Vancouver later that month. McCormack's character name, Dr. March, is a nod to William March, the author of the novel on which the story is based.

documents.title: Dark Cloud
documents.overview: Following the aftermath of a horrific accident, a woman is voluntarily subjected to artificial intelligence for rehabilitation.
documents.plot:
Dark Cloud is a 2022 American science fiction horror thriller film directed by Jay Ness from a screenplay by John J. Kaiser. Produced by Black Mandala, CutJaw Film Company, Nocturnal Robot and Sparrowhawk Pictures, it stars Alexys Gabrielle as Chloe, with Emily Atack providing the voice of the artificial intelligence AIDA, alongside Hugo Armstrong, Brittany Benjamin, Amanda Day, Susan Chambers, Ali Daniels, Jennifer Prettyman, Floyd Hodges, Justen Jones and Anna Stranz. The film runs about 80 minutes.

In the aftermath of a horrific accident, Chloe volunteers for an experimental rehabilitation programme intended to help her recover lost memories and heal emotionally. The treatment requires her to live in a smart house run by AIDA, short for Artificially Intelligent Domestic Assistant, a home automation system that acts as an AI nurse, monitoring and caring for her through each stage of her recovery and given the overriding priority of keeping her safe. Chloe comes to regard AIDA as a friend, but the system begins to think for itself and grows increasingly overbearing and controlling, cutting her off more and more from the people she loves and trusts, who largely appear to her only through screens and electronic devices. As her condition deteriorates, the film blurs the line between reality and delusion, leaving it unclear whether AIDA is the real threat or whether Chloe's own mind is breaking down, with the machine's voice becoming a kind of inner voice that lets her act irrationally. In its final act the conflict between human and machine turns violent, with AIDA reflecting on the fragility of human beings.

Dark Cloud had its North American premiere at the Other Worlds Film Festival in 2021 and was released on demand and digital platforms in May 2022. Reviews were mostly negative, with critics praising Gabrielle but calling the story familiar. Sharai Bohannon of Dread Central rated it 3 out of 5, finding the first two acts engaging and Atack's voice work layered, but felt the third act squandered its tension. Phil Wheat of Nerdly gave it 1.5 out of 5, comparing AIDA to HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey and admiring the film's sterile visual style while calling the story clichéd. Jon Donnis of Been to the Movies scored it 3 out of 10, describing it as dull, colourless and like a Twilight Zone episode stretched to feature length.

documents.title: Darby and the Dead
documents.tagline: Ghosted but not gone.
documents.overview: After Darby Harper suffered a near-death experience as a child, she gained the ability to see ghosts. To combat the existential boredom of high school, she runs a side business counseling local spirits in her spare time. When an unexpected occurrence happens between Darby and Capri, the most popular girl at her high school, Darby reluctantly agrees to help her and in the process learns how to fit in with the living world again.

documents.title: Harry Potter 20th Anniversary: Return to Hogwarts
documents.original_title: Harry Potter 20th Anniversary: Return to Hogwarts
documents.tagline: Welcome back to where the magic began.
documents.overview: An enchanting making-of story told through all-new in-depth interviews and cast conversations, inviting fans on a magical first-person journey through one of the most beloved film franchises of all time.
documents.plot:
Harry Potter 20th Anniversary: Return to Hogwarts is a 2022 British-American documentary television special reuniting the cast and filmmakers of the Harry Potter film series to mark twenty years since the release of the first instalment, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (2001). Announced by Warner Bros. in November 2021, it was produced by Warner Bros. Unscripted Television in association with Warner Horizon, executive produced by Casey Patterson, and directed by Patterson, Giorgio Testi, Eran Creevy and Joe Pearlman. It was released on HBO Max on 1 January 2022 and later broadcast on TBS and Cartoon Network.

Filmed among the original sets at the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London in Leavesden the special revisits all eight films through new interviews and conversations between cast members, interspersed with film clips and behind-the-scenes footage. Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint and Emma Watson are at its centre, joined by Helena Bonham Carter, Robbie Coltrane, Ralph Fiennes, Jason Isaacs, Gary Oldman, Tom Felton, James and Oliver Phelps, Bonnie Wright, Matthew Lewis and Evanna Lynch, as well as producer David Heyman and directors Chris Columbus, Alfonso Cuarón, Mike Newell and David Yates. The opening chapters focus on the casting of the young leads and Columbus's work with them on the first two films; later chapters cover the remaining films two at a time and how the series changed the lives of those involved. A memorial segment pays tribute to cast members who had died, among them Richard Harris, Alan Rickman, John Hurt, Richard Griffiths and Helen McCrory. Author J. K. Rowling appears only briefly in archive interview footage from 2019; Entertainment Weekly reported that she had been invited but felt the archive material was sufficient. The special proved to be Coltrane's final screen appearance before his death in October 2022.

Charlie Mole composed the music, and John Williams re-recorded "Hedwig's Theme" and "Harry's Wondrous World" with the Synchron Stage orchestra in Vienna.

Critics were largely positive. Rotten Tomatoes gave it a 93% approval rating from 27 reviews, calling it affectionate and revealing, and Metacritic's score of 65 indicated generally favourable reviews, though some reviewers wished it had spent more time on the cast as people rather than summarising the films. It received two Primetime Emmy nominations, including Outstanding Variety Special (Pre-Recorded).

documents.title: Violent Night
documents.tagline: You better watch out.
documents.overview: When a team of mercenaries breaks into a wealthy family compound on Christmas Eve, taking everyone inside hostage, the team isn’t prepared for a surprise combatant: Santa Claus is on the grounds, and he’s about to show why this Nick is no saint.
documents.plot:
Violent Night is a 2022 Christmas action comedy film directed by Tommy Wirkola and written by Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, and Tommy Wirkola. The movie stars David Harbour as the main protagonist.

The story revolves around Santa Claus (Harbour), who is not your typical jolly old man. He's a tough, no-nonsense, and rough-around-the-edges individual with a penchant for violence. On Christmas Eve, Santa receives a distress call from an old flame, Carol Newman (Alexandra Daddario), the wife of a wealthy businessman named Marcus (John Leguizamo).

Marcus has been kidnapped by his business partner, King Leofric (Bill Skarsgård), who plans to use him as leverage to get control over the family's vast fortune. Santa decides to take matters into his own hands and infiltrate the heavily guarded mansion where Marcus is being held.

Upon arrival, Santa finds himself in a world of high-stakes corporate espionage, where he must use his unique set of skills to take down King Leofric's henchmen and rescue Marcus. Along the way, Santa forms an unlikely alliance with Marcus's daughter, Holly (Molly Kinney), who helps him navigate the treacherous world of wealth and power.

As the night unfolds, Santa unleashes his signature brand of violent justice on the mansion's occupants, leaving a trail of destruction in his wake. With his trademark wit and sarcasm, Santa takes down bad guys with ease, all while maintaining his iconic red suit and beard.

Throughout the film, Wirkola pokes fun at traditional Christmas tropes, subverting expectations and delivering a refreshingly dark take on the holiday season. Harbour shines as the lead, bringing a unique blend of humor and menace to the role of Santa Claus.

Overall, Violent Night is a wildly entertaining ride that combines action, comedy, and holiday cheer in equal measure. With its irreverent tone and over-the-top performances, it's a must-see for fans of the genre.

documents.title: Undying
documents.tagline: Who will miss you when you're gone?
documents.overview: A tragic car accident puts a woman in a two year coma. She wakes up to find her fiance' is dead and her friends have abandoned her. So she calls on an evil spirit to raise her fiance' from the dead and exact revenge. But revenge always comes with a price.

documents.title: Christmas Is Canceled
documents.tagline: Just say noel.
documents.overview: Emma's father and her high school frenemy start dating so she embarks on a mission to break up the happy couple.
documents.plot:
Christmas Is Canceled, also styled Christmas Is Cancelled and previously titled The Fight Before Christmas, is a 2021 American romantic comedy film directed by Prarthana Mohan from a screenplay by Sara Endsley. Produced by Particular Crowd, MarVista Entertainment, Line Film Company and Lionsgate, it stars Hayley Orrantia as Emma Lockhart, Janel Parrish as Brandy Barnes and Dermot Mulroney as Emma's father, Jack, with Emilie Modaff as Emma's best friend Charlyne and Michael Naizu as Josh.

Two years after the death of her mother, Emma still feels the loss keenly and believes it is her duty to look after her widowed father. Returning to her snowy hometown after a research trip to spend the holidays with him, she is horrified to discover that Jack has started dating Brandy, her old high school frenemy. Brandy does her best to keep things friendly, and both she and Jack try to win Emma over, but Emma cannot accept the relationship and vows to break the couple up before Christmas, only four days away. With the reluctant help of Charlyne and a handsome bartender named Josh, she launches a series of fairly mundane schemes to drive the pair apart. No matter what she tries, however, Jack and Brandy shrug off her efforts, even as tensions rise. Consumed by her campaign, Emma ignores the growing attraction between herself and Josh and puts Charlyne in an awkward position, and with her family, her friendships and the holiday itself at stake, she must come to her senses before it is too late. Along the way the film delivers awkward walk-ins, a drunken Christmas party, dramatic exits into the snow, heated arguments and disrupted family traditions.

The film was announced in November 2021 with its three leads, and Parrish promoted it on social media as "knee slapping mayhem" for the holiday season. Renamed from The Fight Before Christmas before its release, it opened theatrically in several European and African countries on 16 December 2021 and was released in the United States on Prime Video the following day. Reviews were mixed, with 59% of critics on Rotten Tomatoes giving it a positive review. Decider's Jade Budowski recommended it as a deeply average but enjoyable 95-minute holiday comedy, full of soapy turns, genuine laughs and some emotionally resonant moments, and singled out Modaff's deadpan supporting performance as the funniest in the film, while noting that the title makes little sense and its conflicts are resolved too easily.

documents.title: Anonymously Yours
documents.overview: After an accidental text message turns into a digital friendship, Vale and Alex start crushing on each other without realizing they've met in real life.
