documents.title: One Piece Film Red
documents.tagline: An almighty voice. With fiery red locks.
documents.overview: Uta — the most beloved singer in the world. Her voice, which she sings with while concealing her true identity, has been described as “otherworldly.” She will appear in public for the first time at a live concert. As the venue fills with all kinds of Uta fans — excited pirates, the Navy watching closely, and the Straw Hats led by Luffy who simply came to enjoy her sonorous performance — the voice that the whole world has been waiting for is about to resound.
documents.plot:
One Piece Film Red is a 2022 Japanese animated adventure film directed by Goro Taniguchi, produced by Toei Animation, and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures and Toho.

The film takes place after the Wano Country arc of the One Piece manga and anime series. The story follows Monkey D. Luffy and his crew, the Straw Hat Pirates, as they search for a mysterious island called "Red Island" (also known as "Red Land"). According to legend, Red Island is said to be the birthplace of the legendary pirate Shanks, who is considered one of the most powerful pirates in the world.

Upon arrival at Red Island, Luffy and his crew discover that it's actually a massive, ancient temple filled with treasures and mysterious artifacts. However, they soon realize that they're not alone on the island, as they encounter a group of powerful warriors known as the "Red Pirates," who are also searching for the legendary treasure.

As Luffy and his crew navigate through the island, they uncover the secrets behind Red Island's ancient history and the true nature of the Red Pirates. Along the way, they face off against various formidable foes, including the enigmatic and powerful "Pirate King" of Red Island.

Throughout the film, Taniguchi explores themes of friendship, camaraderie, and the power of unity among pirates. The animation is stunning, with vibrant colors and intricate details that bring the world of One Piece to life in a way that's both faithful to the original manga and anime series and visually stunning in its own right.

One Piece Film Red features an all-star voice cast, including Ichiro Okamoto as Monkey D. Luffy, Akemi Okamura as Roronoa Zoro, and Hiroaki Hirata as Sanji. The film also includes cameos from other One Piece characters, adding to the excitement and nostalgia for fans of the series.

Overall, One Piece Film Red is a thrilling adventure that's sure to delight both longtime fans of the One Piece franchise and newcomers alike. With its stunning animation, engaging storyline, and memorable characters, it's a must-see for anyone who loves action-packed adventures with a dash of humor and heart.

documents.title: Significant Other
documents.tagline: Do you really know the one you love?
documents.overview: Ruth and Harry decide to take a romantic backpacking trip through the Pacific Northwest, but amongst the beautiful scenery, Ruth makes an unexpected discovery that sets her off on a strange, frightening new path. The couple aren't alone in the woods, and they might not be the same when they come out...if they come out.

documents.title: Close
documents.overview: Two thirteen year olds have always been incredibly close but they drift apart after the intimacy of their relationship is questioned by schoolmates. When tragedy strikes, one is forced to confront why he distanced himself from his closest friend.
documents.plot:
Close is a 2022 coming-of-age drama film directed by Lukas Dhont, who co-wrote it with Angelo Tijssens, reuniting the team behind his first feature, Girl (2018). It stars Eden Dambrine as Léo and Gustav De Waele as Rémi, two thirteen-year-old boys whose intense friendship is shattered when their classmates question its intimacy, with Émilie Dequenne as Rémi's mother, Sophie, Léa Drucker as Léo's mother, Nathalie, and Kevin Janssens as Rémi's father, Peter. Dhont drew on psychologist Niobe Way's study of intimacy among teenage boys.

In rural Belgium, Léo and Rémi are inseparable, often sleeping in the same bed at Rémi's house, where Sophie and Peter treat Léo like a second son. They play together at the flower farm where Léo's family works. At school, a group of girls asks whether they are a couple; Léo forcefully denies it while Rémi says nothing. Unsettled by this perception and by homophobic taunts from other boys, Léo makes new friends and takes up ice hockey, leaving Rémi out. During a sleepover he chooses a separate mattress, and when he wakes to find Rémi beside him, he reacts aggressively. Léo withdraws further, cycling with other students and spending time on the farm, and when Rémi confronts him the two come to blows.

After a school trip that Rémi misses, the class learns that he has taken his own life. Léo, believing his withdrawal was to blame, shuts down emotionally, unable to speak during the counseling sessions the school provides, and bristles when classmates describe Rémi as happy. He buries himself in hockey and farm work, finding comfort only from his older brother, Charlie. Longing to stay close to Sophie but afraid to confess, he watches her grief, and at a dinner between the families Peter breaks down when Charlie talks about his future. When summer begins, Léo turns up at Sophie's workplace, and as she drives him home he admits that he thinks Rémi's death is his fault. After a tense moment, she embraces him and they weep together. Later, Rémi's parents have moved away, and Léo crosses the fields where the boys once ran, finally allowing himself to grieve.

Close premiered in competition at the 2022 Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Grand Prix, and was released in France and the Benelux in November 2022. Acclaimed by critics, with 91% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 81, it was nominated for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film.

documents.title: The Key Game
documents.overview: Laura has been with Antonio all her life and, just when she begins to wonder if that is really the life she wants, Sergio and Siena cross paths in their lives. Sergio is a former high school classmate and Siena, his millennial girlfriend who arrives to revolutionize everyone's lives. Laura, Raquel and Cris, close friends for years, convince their respective husbands to play a game that Siena proposes to them: the game of keys. The game consists of everyone putting their keys in a bowl. At random, each one chooses some keys and he must go to spend the night with the owner of the keys. This game will revolutionize the group of friends and their lives. It will make them discover who they are and what they really want.
documents.plot:
The Key Game (Spanish: El juego de las llaves) is a 2022 Spanish erotic romantic comedy film directed by Vicente Villanueva from a screenplay by Marta Buchaca. An Atresmedia Cine production produced by Kiko Martínez and distributed by Warner, it is based on the Mexican television series of the same name that found an international audience on Amazon Prime Video. The ensemble cast stars Eva Ugarte as Laura, Ricard Farré as her partner Antonio, Miren Ibarguren as Raquel, Tamar Novas as Kike, María Castro as Cris, Dani Tatay as Dani, Fernando Guallar as Sergio and Justina Bustos as Siena, with Alina Nastase as Natasha and Cintia García as Gala. Filming began in Valencia, where the story is set, on 21 June 2021, and the film runs 107 minutes.

Laura has been with Antonio all her life and is starting to wonder whether this is really the life she wants when Sergio, a former high school classmate, reappears together with Siena, his young millennial girlfriend and Instagram influencer, who sets out to shake up everyone's lives. Laura and her close friends of many years, Raquel and Cris, each of whom for different reasons misses excitement and good sex in a relationship dulled by routine, persuade their husbands to try a game Siena proposes: the key game. Everyone drops their keys into a bowl, each player draws a set at random and must spend the night with its owner. The partner swapping unleashes jealousy, envy and frustration among the four couples, but it also forces them to discover who they really are and what they actually want, with Raquel and Kike making their own discovery without leaving home. The story builds to an orgy sequence that nods to Eyes Wide Shut, and ends with a wedding and one of the women expecting a baby.

The film opened in Spanish cinemas on 13 April 2022. Critics found it light but held together by its cast. Juan Pando of Fotogramas praised Villanueva's direction of actors, singling out Ibarguren as the life of the party, Novas's comic turn and Bustos as a revelation, although he considered the final orgy a pale reflection of Kubrick's. Oskar Belategui of El Correo called it a comedy more bland than spicy and a familiar tangle set in a chic, designer Valencia, rescued mainly by Ibarguren's comic gifts, while Sergio F. Pinilla of Cinemanía placed it alongside other recent Spanish sex comedies such as Kiki, el amor se hace.

documents.title: Madagascar: A Little Wild Holiday Goose Chase
documents.original_title: Madagascar: A Little Wild Holiday Goose Chase
documents.overview: Melman the Giraffe meets Hank, a goose who has been separated from his family and along with his friends, they embark on a wild goose chase around the city to reunite Hank with his merry flock.
documents.plot:
Madagascar: A Little Wild Holiday Goose Chase is a 2021 American animated holiday television special based on the preschool series Madagascar: A Little Wild, itself a spin-off of the Madagascar film franchise. Directed by Chad Van De Keere from a script by Laura Zak, it features the voices of Luke Lowe as Melman the giraffe, Shaylin Becton as Gloria the hippo, Tucker Chandler as Alex the lion and Amir O'Neil as Marty the zebra, with Mark Whitten as a lost goose, alongside Jasmine Gatewood and Eric Petersen. The 24-minute special premiered on 26 November 2021 on the streaming services Hulu and Peacock.

As in the series, the franchise's heroes are portrayed as young animals living together in the same habitat at New York's Central Park Zoo. With the holidays approaching, the anxious Melman has been meticulously charting the friends' naughty and nice deeds and fears that the naughty column is too long to earn them a place on the nice list. He leads the group in a series of good deeds around the zoo, involving the zoo train and a troop of chimpanzees who communicate in sign language, but each attempt backfires. Deciding they need to do good in the wider world, the friends slip out of the zoo by sliding through the city's sewers and emerge in the streets of New York, decorated for both Christmas and Hanukkah. There they meet Hank, a scatterbrained Canada goose who has become separated from his migrating family and cannot tell north from south. Seeing their chance at the perfect good deed, the friends embark on a wild goose chase around the city to reunite Hank with his flock, repeatedly confused by city noises that honk like geese. Along the way Melman learns that being good for its own sake matters more than being rewarded, and that being together is more important than presents.

John Serba of Decider recommended streaming it, calling the special mildly amusing and almost charming, a gentle and perfectly fine distraction for young children that would hold its target audience's attention, though unlikely to make anyone older than ten laugh out loud and not exactly a holiday classic. Joly Herman of Common Sense Media rated it suitable for ages five and up, noting its strong diversity, its mild peril and its messages about helping strangers and doing good deeds, while observing that male characters received more dialogue than female ones.

documents.title: My Fake Boyfriend
documents.tagline: Real love is hard to find.
documents.overview: A young man in a tricky situation follows the advice of his unconventional best friend and uses social media to create a fake boyfriend to keep his awful ex-lover out of his life. But everything backfires when he meets the real love of his life, and breaking up with his fake boyfriend proves hard to do.
documents.plot: A young man in a tricky situation follows the advice of his unconventional best friend and uses social media to create a fake boyfriend to keep his awful ex-lover out of his life. But everything backfires when he meets the real love of his life, and breaking up with his fake boyfriend proves hard to do.

documents.title: Run & Gun
documents.overview: After leaving a life of crime and violence, Ray is a reformed good guy, enjoying a quiet family life in the ‘burbs. But when his past is discovered, Ray is blackmailed into one last job to collect a mysterious package. After a deadly double-cross, he finds himself wounded and on the run from ruthless assassins who will stop at nothing to get what he has. Now, with the lives of his loved ones hanging in the balance and danger at every turn, Ray’s only hope is to draw upon his violent past to survive.
documents.plot:
Run & Gun, also known as The Ray, is an American action thriller written and directed by Christopher Borrelli, set among the ruins of California's Salton Sea. It stars Ben Milliken as Ray, a former criminal, with Mark Dacascos as Brando, Janel Parrish as Ray's girlfriend Faith, Richard Kind as the eccentric mob boss Grayson, Celestino Cornielle as Ninni, Brad William Henke as Billings, Ari Barkan as Perry and Hudson Yang.

The story opens with two men being driven into the desert by a mobster to be executed. One of them, Ray, survives a hanging, kills the assassin and befriends the other captive, Lupe. Two years later, Ray has gone straight as a successful insurance investigator, living in an RV and dating Faith, a single mother who invites him to move in with her and her son. His new life is threatened when Lupe, now in prison, warns him that gangsters have seen him visiting.

Soon afterwards, Ray is summoned by Grayson, who forces him to carry out two tasks or see Faith and her son killed: poison a neighbor's tree, and intercept a mysterious package bound for a rival. Grayson's assistant Brando gives Ray a bag containing 440,000 dollars to exchange for the package, but after the handover Ray is ambushed and shot in the stomach by Ninni and his brother, who pursue him across the desert. Ray kills the brother, hides the money and the package in an abandoned car, and staggers wounded through the wasteland until he reaches a factory, where a security guard named Billings offers to help. Ray soon discovers that his rescuer is even more dangerous than the gangsters hunting him, and he must survive long enough to recover the bags and protect the people he loves.

The film combines a crime thriller with darkly comic touches, including Grayson's obsession with the Mandela effect and the theory that the package can influence what the world believes.

Run & Gun was released in the United States in 2022 after a limited release under its original title. Reviewers generally described it as a modest, quirky low-budget crime thriller with uneven pacing and a predictable plot.

documents.title: No Limit
documents.overview: Roxana Aubrey decides to drop her studies and escape her life in Paris for a free diving course in the south of France. She is quickly pulled into a life that reaches new depths brought by the weight of an ocean's descent.
documents.plot:
No Limit (French: Sous emprise, also known as Apnea) is a 2022 French drama film written and directed by David M. Rosenthal. Inspired by the story of the French freediver Audrey Mestre, who died in 2002 during a controversial attempt at a no-limit world record dive with her husband, the Cuban champion Francisco "Pipín" Ferreras, it stars Camille Rowe and the rapper Sofiane Zermani (Fianso), with César Domboy, Laurent Fernandez, Zacharie Chasseriaud and Muriel Combeau. Produced by Nolita Cinema, with music by Atli Örvarsson and cinematography by Thomas Hardmeier, it was shot in La Ciotat, Porquerolles, Villefranche-sur-Mer, Guadeloupe and Belgium, and the record-holding freediver Stéphane Mifsud helped prepare the actors for the diving scenes. It was released worldwide on Netflix on 9 September 2022.

Roxana Aubry (Rowe), who learned to freedive as a child with her grandfather, drops out of her studies in Paris and travels to the south of France for a freediving course run by the record-setting champion Pascal Gauthier (Zermani). There she meets one of the instructors, the kind safety diver Tom (Domboy), but is soon drawn into a passionate affair with the domineering Pascal. Invited along as Pascal attempts a world-record 172-metre dive, she watches him succeed, but one of his safety divers fails to resurface and dies despite her attempts at resuscitation. Roxana joins Pascal's team and tours Europe with him, first as support and then as a competitor herself. When blackouts during dives force Pascal to stop competing, he becomes her coach, and as she breaks records and becomes a celebrity of the sport, he grows controlling, unfaithful and jealous of her success. He pushes her to attempt a 180-metre no-limit world record. On the day of the attempt Tom checks her equipment and then notices Pascal secretly handling it. At the bottom, the lift bag meant to carry her back up fails to inflate; Tom manages to fix it, but Roxana drowns before reaching the surface. The film strongly implies that Pascal sabotaged the dive, and ends with her grandfather scattering her ashes at sea.

The film was number one among Netflix films in France and number two worldwide. Ferreras reportedly sued Netflix, saying it portrayed his relationship with Mestre as abusive and violent. John Serba of Decider found it beautifully shot but slow and tedious, though he credited Rowe with an empathetic performance.

documents.title: Bubble
documents.tagline: Is she a calamity or a blessing?
documents.overview: In an abandoned Tokyo overrun by bubbles and gravitational abnormalities, one gifted young man has a fateful meeting with a mysterious girl.
documents.plot:
Bubble (Japanese: バブル, Hepburn: Baburu) is a 2022 Japanese animated post-apocalyptic fantasy film produced by Wit Studio. It was directed by Tetsurō Araki and written by Gen Urobuchi, with character designs by Takeshi Obata and music by Hiroyuki Sawano, a team of creators known for their work on series such as Attack on Titan and Death Note. Jun Shison and Riria voice the leads, with Alice Hirose, Mamoru Miyano and Yuki Kaji. The film had early screenings at the Berlin International Film Festival in February 2022, was released worldwide on Netflix on 28 April 2022 and opened in Japanese cinemas in May.

In the near future, mysterious bubbles that defy the laws of physics fall over the world. An explosion at Tokyo Tower concentrates the bubbles over Tokyo, distorting gravity and making the city uninhabitable, and it is cut off from the rest of the world. Despite the restrictions, groups of young people continue to live in the ruined, flooded city, competing in parkour team battles across its collapsed buildings to win supplies. Hibiki, an eighteen-year-old member of a team called the Blue Blazes, is an extraordinarily gifted runner but keeps to himself because of his sensitivity to sound.

Tokyo Tower, surrounded by gravity anomalies, remains impossible to reach. One day Hibiki, drawn by a mysterious song that only he can hear, tries to climb toward the tower but falls into the sea. He is saved by a girl who seems to have been born from the bubbles themselves. She knows nothing about being human but learns quickly from Hibiki and his friends, and because she knows the song that echoes in his head, he names her Uta, meaning "song." Uta joins the Blue Blazes, and together they win parkour matches against rival teams, but she discovers that touching Hibiki causes her body to dissolve into bubbles. The film draws loosely on Hans Christian Andersen's The Little Mermaid, as Uta's connection with Hibiki grows and the bubbles that created her threaten to engulf the city once more.

Bubble received mixed reviews. Critics praised its visual style, its dynamic parkour sequences and Sawano's score, but many found its story thin and its characters underdeveloped given the prestigious team behind it.

documents.title: Teen Titans Go! & DC Super Hero Girls: Mayhem in the Multiverse
documents.original_title: Teen Titans Go! & DC Super Hero Girls: Mayhem in the Multiverse
documents.overview: With the help of an ancient Kryptonian power, Lex Luthor unites the world’s Super-Villains to capture all of Earth's Super Heroes, until…only the DC Super Hero Girls are left to stop the Legion of Doom. Our heroes must cross dimensions to rescue their fellow Super Heroes from the Phantom Zone, but a fortuitous wrong turn leads them to Titans Tower – where they find much-needed allies in the Teen Titans!
documents.plot:
Teen Titans Go! & DC Super Hero Girls: Mayhem in the Multiverse is a 2022 American direct-to-video animated superhero comedy that brings together the casts of the television series Teen Titans Go! and DC Super Hero Girls. The fourth Teen Titans Go! film and the first DC Super Hero Girls feature built around the 2019 series, it also served as that show's finale. Its voice cast includes Greg Cipes as Beast Boy, Scott Menville as Robin, Khary Payton as Cyborg, Hynden Walch as Starfire, Tara Strong as Raven, Batgirl and Harley Quinn, and Grey Griffin as Wonder Woman.

At the Teen Titans' base, Beast Boy finds a strange crystal just as the villain Control Freak arrives to show the Titans a new superhero crossover, so they settle down to watch. The film within the film follows the Super Hero Girls, whose enemies, the Super Villain Girls, escape through a portal. Lex Luthor, who has found a mysterious amulet, rescues them and forms the Legion of Doom to trap every hero in the Phantom Zone. The amulet holds Cythonna, the Kryptonian goddess of darkness, imprisoned long ago by her brother Rao.

When the girls find a rune bearing Cythonna's name, Supergirl's cousin Clark dismisses it as legend. At the Fortress of Solitude they clash with Superman's robots and then the Justice League, and Wonder Woman hands the crucial crystals to Superman, but Batgirl secretly takes them. A message from Jor-El reveals that Cythonna means to escape by feeding on wicked souls and conquer the universe, and the girls realise she is controlling Luthor.

The League falls into the Legion's trap: Superman is locked in a box of Kryptonite and the others are sent to the Phantom Zone. Harley Quinn helps Wonder Woman escape, but the girls quarrel over her choices and split up until Bumblebee reunites them. As the United Nations surrenders the world to the Legion, Cythonna seizes Supergirl as a host, and Zatanna's magic accidentally strands the girls in the Titans' world. With the Titans' help, and encouragement from Raven, Zatanna returns them home, where they free their allies, defeat the Legion and banish Cythonna. Back in the Titans' universe, Cythonna turns out to be possessing Control Freak, and the Titans thwart her too.

The film was released on DVD and Blu-ray on May 24, 2022, and premiered on Cartoon Network four days later.

documents.title: Barbarian
documents.tagline: Some stay for a night. Some stay for a week. Some never leave.
documents.overview: In town for a job interview, a young woman arrives at her Airbnb late at night only to find that it has been mistakenly double-booked and a strange man is already staying there. Against her better judgement, she decides to stay the night anyway.
documents.plot:
Barbarian is a 2022 American horror film written and directed by Zach Cregger in his solo writing and directing debut. Georgina Campbell, Bill Skarsgård and Justin Long star, with Matthew Patrick Davis and Richard Brake. The story follows a woman who discovers a terrible secret in the house she has rented for the night. The film premiered at San Diego Comic-Con in July 2022 and was released in cinemas by 20th Century Studios on 9 September 2022.

On the night before a job interview in Detroit, Tess Marshall arrives at a rental house in the run-down Brightmoor neighborhood, only to find that it has been double-booked and is already occupied by a man named Keith. Despite her unease, the rain and a lack of other options persuade her to stay, and Keith turns out to be friendly. During the night she wakes to find her door open, though Keith insists he did not open it. The next day her interviewer warns her about the neighborhood, and when Tess returns to the house a homeless man runs toward her shouting at her to leave. Accidentally locked in the basement, she discovers a hidden room containing a camera, a bucket, a stained mattress and a bloody handprint. Keith frees her but insists on investigating, and when he does not return, Tess follows him into a tunnel beneath the house, where a horrifying discovery awaits.

The film then abruptly shifts to AJ Gilbride, a television actor played by Long, whose career is collapsing after he is accused of sexual assault by a co-star. Desperate for money to fund his legal defense, AJ plans to sell some of his properties, among them the Detroit house. When he visits it and finds Tess's belongings, he becomes curious about the extensive underground spaces, which he begins to measure in the hope of increasing the property's value. As the two storylines converge, the history of the house and its former owner, Frank, is gradually revealed, along with the origins of the monstrous figure that lives below.

Barbarian received positive reviews from critics, who praised its unpredictable structure, tonal shifts, humor and performances, especially Campbell's and Long's. It was a surprise box-office hit, grossing about $46 million worldwide against a budget of roughly $4.5 million, and it was widely considered one of the best horror films of the year.

documents.title: Renegades
documents.tagline: Armed for war and out for justice.
documents.overview: When a retired Green Beret soldier is murdered by an Albanian drug gang in London, four of his veteran SAS comrades set out to avenge him, dispensing their own brand of justice on the streets of London.
documents.plot:
Renegades is a 2022 British crime action thriller directed by Daniel Zirilli and produced by Shogun Films. Built around a cast of veteran actors, it stars Nick Moran as Carl Burton, Lee Majors as Major Carver, Ian Ogilvy as Major Frederick Peck, Billy Murray as Major George "Woody" Woodward and Paul Barber as Sergeant Robert Harris, alongside Danny Trejo as Sanchez, Patsy Kensit as Judy Carver, Louis Mandylor as Anthony Goram, Michael Paré as CIA agent Donovan, Stephanie Beacham as Hartigan and Jeanine Nerissa Sothcott as Detective Moore, with Tom Lister Jr. and Michael Brandon.

Burton is a low-profile former SAS soldier suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder. He is picked up on the street by an old acquaintance, the American veteran and retired Green Beret Carver, who has a grudge against a gang of criminals in his London neighborhood that is trafficking women and dealing drugs. When Carver's attempt to deal with the gangsters fails and he is murdered by them, Burton and three of his old SAS comrades, Peck, Woodward and Harris, band together to avenge their friend, dispensing their own brand of justice on the streets of London. Along the way they receive help from Sanchez, a friendly gangster, from Carver's daughter Judy, a politician, and from a few police officers, in a campaign marked by gory shootouts and explosions.

The film was shot in London, wrapping in October 2021, and the filmmakers cited Harry Brown and The Wild Geese as influences. It was released for streaming in the United Kingdom on 1 October 2022 and on digital platforms in January 2023. Reviews were mixed. In The Guardian, Leslie Felperin gave it two stars out of five, describing a cheap thriller that belatedly cashes in on the "geri-action" trend of films like Red and The Expendables, with inept, low-energy action and stilted dialogue that she likened to the output of an AI chatbot. Other reviewers were kinder: IndieWrap called it highly engaging and spectacularly entertaining, Chris Ward enjoyed it as a mash-up of The Expendables, Death Wish and Cockney gangster movies, and Jim McLellan gave it a B-minus, placing it between the serious Harry Brown and the silly Cockneys vs Zombies and finding Guy Ritchie's influence palpable, while singling out Ogilvy's charm.

documents.title: Guardians of Time
documents.tagline: The war of time will begin.
documents.overview: One day, in the family manor, four cousins discover a passage to a mysterious world. Trapped in this unearthed land, the Kingdom of Keoherus, they must confront the Guardian of Time and face dark forces and beast to hopefully get home.
documents.plot:
Guardians of Time is a 2022 American family fantasy adventure film directed by Stephen Shimek from a screenplay by Sebastien Semon, Katy Baldwin and Jerome Reygner-Kalfon. Produced by Ace Entertainment Films, it stars Samantha Ryan, Ava Torres, Carley Coleman and Nia Salaam as four girls transported to a magical realm, with David Fletcher-Hall, Skip Schwink, Katie Burgess, Natalie Daniels, Harper Heath and Drew Pollock in supporting roles. Rated PG for some peril and fantasy violence, it was released on DVD by Lionsgate in October 2022.

Sisters Sybil (Ryan) and Alex (Torres) and their cousins Zoey (Coleman) and Theo (Salaam) are left at the sprawling family manor of the sisters' grandfather, Papa Nickolaou (Fletcher-Hall), while their parents go away on a trip. On the first afternoon Sybil begins to see strange visions. Exploring her grandfather's library, Alex finds an old book titled The Beginning is the End is the Beginning, filled with mysterious drawings and symbols. The youngest sister, feeling alienated and left out by the others, sets in motion the events that lead them through a hidden passage into the Kingdom of Keoherus, a mysterious land resembling a prehistoric wilderness. Trapped there, the four must confront the Guardian of Time, battle dark forces and face ancient beasts including rock and tree monsters, dinosaurs and a dragon, gaining special powers along the way. Working together to rescue Alex and find their way back to the manor, they learn to trust one another, to accept themselves and not to grow up too fast, while the others come to appreciate the girl who had felt excluded. The story also weaves in references to Amelia Earhart and to Greek and Roman mythology.

Reviews were mixed to negative. John Delia Sr. of ACED Magazine found it a fun adventure aimed at girls from ten into their teens, praising the storyline, the acting and its moral lessons about friendship and standing up for one another, though he called the special effects somewhat elementary. Common Sense Media rated it suitable for ages eight and up, commending its diverse cast of smart, strong and adventurous girls and its coming-of-age themes, while warning that its monsters might scare younger viewers. Jeremy Butler of Upcoming Discs was scathing, judging the obvious green-screen work and sub-par computer graphics below B-movie quality, the characters forgettable and the theme of the excluded younger sibling a cliché.

documents.title: Brian and Charles
documents.tagline: Some friendships are built to last.
documents.overview: An endearing outlier, Brian lives alone in a Welsh valley, inventing oddball contraptions that seldom work. After finding a discarded mannequin head, Brian gets an idea. Three days, a washing machine, and sundry spare parts later, he’s invented Charles, an artificially intelligent robot who learns English from a dictionary and proves a charming, cheeky companion. Before long, however, Charles also develops autonomy. Intrigued by the wider world — or whatever lies beyond the cottage where Brian has hidden him away — Charles craves adventure.
documents.plot:
Brian and Charles is a 2022 British comedy-drama film that tells the story of an unlikely friendship between a lonely inventor, Brian, and his creation, a talking teddy bear named Charles. The movie explores themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human need for connection.

At its core, Brian and Charles is a heartwarming tale about the transformative power of friendship and companionship. Brian, a reclusive inventor, finds solace in his creations, but even they can't fill the void left by his own emotional numbness. That is until Charles, the talking teddy bear, enters his life, bringing with him a sense of purpose and belonging.

As their relationship deepens, the film delves into the complexities of Brian's inner world, revealing a character struggling to cope with the loss of his wife and the pressures of his own isolation. Through Charles' unwavering loyalty and affection, Brian begins to confront his emotional scars and slowly rebuilds his sense of self.

The movie also touches on the theme of creativity and the importance of human connection in sparking imagination and innovation. Brian's inventions are a testament to his boundless creativity, but it's only when he shares them with Charles that he finds true fulfillment.

Ultimately, Brian and Charles is a poignant exploration of what it means to be human, highlighting the importance of relationships, empathy, and understanding in breaking down even the most profound emotional barriers.

documents.title: A Love Song
documents.overview: Two childhood sweethearts, now both widowed, share a night by a lake in the mountains.
documents.plot:
A Love Song is a 2022 American drama written, directed, produced and co-edited by Max Walker-Silverman in his feature directorial debut. Dale Dickey and Wes Studi star as two childhood friends who reunite for a night beside a lake in the mountains, with Michelle Wilson, Benja K. Thomas and John Way in supporting roles.

Faye, a lonely widow, waits at a lakeside campsite in the Colorado mountains for Lito, a childhood friend she has not seen in many years. Unsure when he will arrive or even what he looks like now, she passes the time watching birds and stars and meeting her neighbors. A polite group of siblings is waiting for her to move so they can dig up their father's coffin and rebury him elsewhere, and an engaged lesbian couple invites her to dinner, where one of the women, Jan, nervously asks whether marriage is worthwhile.

When Lito finally arrives, the two spend the day sharing memories, playing music and remembering their late spouses. He takes her photograph, which embarrasses Faye, who would prefer that he remember her as she was when young. That night, after admitting how much they miss their partners and bonding over their grief, they sleep together. In the morning Lito sets out to pick flowers for Faye but is overcome with emotion, and when she comes out to greet him he awkwardly thanks her for the invitation and confesses that he cannot begin a romance with her. Hurt but understanding, Faye helps him on his way. She then hikes alone through the landscape and watches the stars, slowly coming to terms with her feelings and disappointment. The next morning she visits Jan and urges her to marry and enjoy her life, then drives away from the campsite as the siblings begin digging up their father's coffin.

The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 20, 2022, and also screened at the Berlin International Film Festival and the Tribeca Film Festival. Bleecker Street and Stage 6 Films acquired worldwide distribution rights and released it in the United States on July 29, 2022. Critics praised the film, giving it 95% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a brilliant and too-rare showcase for its veteran leads that tells a small, stirring tale with quiet grace, and a Metacritic score of 78. The National Board of Review named it one of the top ten independent films of 2022, and it received two nominations at the 38th Independent Spirit Awards.

documents.title: Downfall: The Case Against Boeing
documents.overview: Investigators reveal how Boeing’s alleged priority of profit over safety could have contributed to two catastrophic crashes within months of each other.
documents.plot:
Downfall: The Case Against Boeing is a 2022 American documentary directed by Rory Kennedy. Through interviews with journalists, engineers, former Boeing employees, pilots, members of Congress and relatives of victims, together with archival footage, it investigates the events that led to the crashes of two Boeing 737 MAX aircraft within five months of each other, and the investigations that followed. It premiered in a virtual screening at the 2022 Sundance Film Festival on 21 January 2022 and was released on Netflix the following month.

In October 2018, Lion Air Flight 610 crashed into the Java Sea shortly after takeoff from Jakarta, and in March 2019, Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crashed minutes after leaving Addis Ababa. Together the two disasters killed 346 people. The documentary examines how investigators traced both crashes to a flight-control software system on the 737 MAX, known as MCAS, which could repeatedly push the plane's nose down on the basis of faulty sensor data, and how pilots had not been adequately informed about the system or trained to handle it.

The film places the crashes within the broader history of Boeing, arguing that the company, once renowned for an engineering culture focused on safety and excellence, underwent a profound shift after its 1997 merger with McDonnell Douglas, when financial performance and shareholder value came to dominate decision-making. It describes how the pressure to compete with Airbus, whose fuel-efficient A320neo threatened Boeing's market share, led the company to rush the 737 MAX into service as an update of an older design rather than develop a new aircraft. Interviewees criticize Boeing's initial attempts to blame the foreign pilots, as well as the close relationship between the company and the Federal Aviation Administration, which had delegated much of the certification process to Boeing itself. Kennedy has said that for decades Boeing showed that a focus on safety and ingenuity was the key to profit, until it was taken over by people for whom Wall Street was everything, and that elected officials must hold companies accountable for the public interest.

The documentary was well received by critics, who praised its clear explanation of the technical and corporate failures and its emotional interviews with the victims' families, though some felt it covered ground already familiar from news reporting.

documents.title: The Princess
documents.tagline: Her life. Our obsession.
documents.overview: Decades after her untimely death, Princess Diana continues to evoke mystery, glamour, and the quintessential modern fairy tale gone wrong. As a symbol of both the widening fissures weakening the British monarchy and the destructive machinery of the press, the Princess of Wales navigated an unparalleled rise to fame and the corrosive challenges that came alongside it. Crafted entirely from immersive archival footage and free from the distraction of retrospective voices, this hypnotic and audaciously revealing documentary takes a distinctive formal approach, allowing the story of the People’s Princess to unfold before us like never before.
documents.plot:
The Princess is a 2022 British documentary film about Diana, Princess of Wales, directed by Ed Perkins and produced by Lightbox in association with Sky and HBO Documentary Films. Released on the twenty-fifth anniversary year of her death, it revisits the life of one of the most photographed and discussed women of the twentieth century entirely through material recorded at the time.

Rather than relying on a narrator or on newly filmed interviews with biographers, friends and royal commentators, the film is assembled from archival footage and audio: television news reports, interviews, press coverage and the voices of members of the public recorded at the time. Told in the present tense, it immerses viewers in events as they unfolded, drawing on recently revealed testimony and rarely seen recordings to create the sense of watching history happen in real time.

The documentary follows Diana from the frenzy surrounding her engagement to Prince Charles and the couple's wedding in 1981, through her rapid transformation into a global celebrity, the strains of her marriage, the public revelations about the royal family's private life, the couple's separation and divorce, and finally the car crash in Paris in 1997 and the outpouring of grief that followed. Along the way it shows the relentless attention of the press and photographers and the public's appetite for every detail of her life.

By stripping away retrospective commentary, Perkins invites viewers to consider their own role, and that of the media and the monarchy, in shaping the story of a woman whose life was consumed as a spectacle. The film functions less as a conventional biography than as a study of fame, voyeurism and collective fascination.

The Princess premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2022, was screened at Sundance London that June and opened in British cinemas on 30 June 2022. It premiered in the United States on HBO and HBO Max on 13 August 2022 and on Sky Documentaries in the United Kingdom the following day. Critics responded favorably, giving it about 85 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 69; the consensus noted that while it adds little that is truly new, its recontextualization of her public life forces viewers to rethink it.
cast: King Charles III of the United Kingdom
Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom

documents.title: Monica, O My Darling
documents.overview: A slick robotics expert joins a murderous plot after a passionate affair takes a sudden turn, but nothing — not even death — is what it seems to be.
documents.plot:
Monica, O My Darling is a 2022 Indian Hindi-language neo-noir crime comedy thriller directed by Vasan Bala and starring Rajkummar Rao, Huma Qureshi and Radhika Apte. Adapted from Keigo Higashino's 1989 Japanese mystery novel Burutasu no Shinzō (Heart of Brutus), it takes its title from a line in a song from the 1971 film Caravan. It was released on Netflix on 11 November 2022.

At Unicorn, a robotics company, an employee named Dev is killed by an industrial robot during a night shift; the death is ruled an accident and a safety officer is fired. Six months later, the ambitious engineer Jayant Arkhedkar is promoted to the board and engaged to Nikki, the daughter of the chairman, Satyanarayan Adhikari. However, he has been having an affair with the secretary, Monica Machado, who tells him she is pregnant with his child and demands money. Jayant then learns that the chairman's son, Nishikant, and the company's finance chief, Arvind, have also been involved with Monica and are being blackmailed by her in the same way.

The three men devise an elaborate plan to murder Monica and dispose of her body, signing a contract to bind one another to it. But the scheme goes awry: the next day Monica is alive, and the body that has been dumped is Nishikant's. As police officer ACP Naidu investigates, Arvind is killed by a venomous snake delivered to his home, and Jayant narrowly survives attempts on his own life. Monica denies being responsible and appears to have figured out the killer's identity, but before she can tell Jayant she dies from venom slipped into her wine.

Jayant learns that the robot that killed Dev was manually overridden, and discovers that the murderer was his friend Gaurav, the fiancé of Jayant's sister Shalu, who had been in love with her. Gaurav confesses to killing Nishikant, who had been using him, and Arvind, but denies murdering Monica. Jayant kills him in self-defense. Naidu, however, privately reveals that Monica's death was arranged by Satyanarayan, the true father of her child, leaving Jayant entangled in the company's corruption in the film's final twist.

Monica, O My Darling received positive reviews, with praise for Bala's direction, the performances of Rao, Qureshi and Apte, its music and its homage to vintage Hindi crime films, though some critics found its second half overlong. It won four Filmfare OTT Awards, including Best Web Original Film.

documents.title: Something from Tiffany's
documents.overview: A woman’s life is upended when an engagement ring meant for someone else leads her to the person she’s meant to be with.
documents.plot:
Something from Tiffany's is a 2022 American romantic comedy-drama film directed by Gillian Robespierre, written by Emily Halpern and Sarah Haskins, and produced by Amazon Studios.

The movie follows the story of Jill Newman (played by Zoey Deutch), a young woman who has just been fired from her job as an editor at a publishing company. Feeling lost and uncertain about her future, Jill returns to her hometown in New Jersey after being away for several years.

Upon her return, Jill is forced to confront her complicated past and the choices she made that led her to where she is today. She also reconnects with her high school best friend, Kate (played by Gigi Hadid), who has become a successful businesswoman.

As Jill navigates her way through this new chapter in her life, she meets a charming and handsome stranger named Max (played by Pierce Brosnan) at Tiffany & Co., where he is buying a ring for his girlfriend. Despite their instant attraction, Jill is hesitant to get involved with someone new, fearing that it will distract her from finding herself.

Throughout the film, Jill's journey is interwoven with flashbacks of her past relationships and experiences, which provide insight into her character development and growth. The movie explores themes of identity, love, and self-discovery, as Jill learns to let go of her fears and take control of her life.

The title "Something from Tiffany's" refers to a phrase that Max tells Jill, suggesting that sometimes the best things in life come from unexpected places. As Jill navigates her way through this new chapter, she begins to realize that this phrase holds true for her as well.

Overall, Something from Tiffany's is a heartwarming and engaging film that explores themes of identity, love, and self-discovery. With its talented cast, witty dialogue, and relatable protagonist, the movie is sure to resonate with audiences looking for a feel-good romantic comedy-drama.

documents.title: Suzume
documents.tagline: On the other side of the door, was time in its entirety.
documents.overview: A coming-of-age story for the 17-year-old protagonist, Suzume, set in various disaster-stricken locations across Japan, where she must close the doors causing devastation.
documents.plot:
Suzume (Suzume no Tojimari) is a 2022 Japanese animated fantasy adventure written and directed by Makoto Shinkai, the final film in his "disaster trilogy" after Your Name (2016) and Weathering with You (2019). Produced by CoMix Wave Films and Story Inc., it stars Nanoka Hara as Suzume Iwato and Hokuto Matsumura as Souta Munakata, with music by Radwimps and Kazuma Jinnouchi.

Seventeen-year-old Suzume lives with her aunt Tamaki in Kyushu and dreams of wandering a ruined city as a child, looking for her late mother. One morning, she meets a young man searching for abandoned places with doors and directs him to a derelict hot-spring resort. There she finds a freestanding door that opens onto a starlit field she cannot enter, and she pulls up a stone cat statue that turns into a living cat and runs away. From school, she sees a column of smoke rising from the resort that no one else notices, and she helps the young man, Souta, lock the door. Souta is a "Closer" who seals such doors across Japan to keep a giant supernatural worm from emerging and causing earthquakes. The cat, called Daijin, was a keystone holding the worm back. It turns Souta into the small chair he was sitting on.

Suzume and the chair-bound Souta chase Daijin across Japan by ferry and car. In Ehime and Kobe they close more doors with help from new friends, and Suzume learns that the doors lead to the Ever-After, where the dead go. In Tokyo, Daijin reveals that he has passed the keystone's role to Souta, and Suzume is forced to use the crystallizing Souta to pin down the worm. To save him, she travels with Tamaki and Souta's friend Tomoya to her childhood home in Tōhoku, destroyed by the 2011 earthquake and tsunami that killed her mother, where she first entered the Ever-After. There, with the help of Daijin and a second keystone, Sadaijin, she frees Souta, and the cats become keystones again to seal the worm. Suzume meets her younger self and gives her the chair her mother made, helping her to go on living. A year later, she and Souta meet again.

Inspired by the 2011 Tōhoku disaster, the film premiered in IMAX in Japan on November 7, 2022, and was released by Toho on November 11. It grossed about $315 million worldwide, becoming one of the highest-grossing anime films, with record runs in China and South Korea. Critics praised its animation, music and emotional power, and Rotten Tomatoes reported 96% positive reviews.

documents.title: The Infernal Machine
documents.tagline: What he created will destroy him.
documents.overview: Reclusive and controversial author Bruce Cogburn is drawn out of hiding by an obsessive fan, forcing the novelist to confront a past that he thought he could escape, and to account for events set in motion by his bestseller decades earlier. Cogburn's search for who is behind the manipulation and mental torment he encounters leads to an emotional roller-coaster ride full of fear and danger, where things are not always as clear as they seem to be, and where past deeds can have dire consequences.
documents.plot:
The Infernal Machine is a psychological mystery thriller of 2022 written and directed by Andrew Hunt, based on a story by Louis Kornfeld. Guy Pearce stars as Bruce Cogburn, a reclusive novelist, with Alice Eve as the police officer Laura Higgins, Alex Pettyfer as the convicted gunman Dwight Tufford and Jeremy Davies as Elijah Barrett. Paramount Pictures released it in the United States on 23 September 2022 and in the United Kingdom that December.

Cogburn is the controversial author of a single famous book, The Infernal Machine. For 25 years he has lived in self-imposed isolation in the American Southwest, having fled there in 1981 after a young man opened fire at a university in Knoxville, Tennessee, killing 13 people, and blamed the massacre on the novel. His seclusion is disturbed when his post office box begins filling with letters from William DuKent, a writer who wants to interview him. Cogburn drives 45 minutes to the nearest phone booth to leave ever more threatening messages telling DuKent to stop, but the letters keep coming, and his drinking and paranoia deepen. Using a false name, he visits the gunman, Dwight Tufford, in prison. Tufford later breaks out and turns up at Cogburn's house, where the writer manages to kill him.

Cogburn did not write The Infernal Machine: he stole it from Elijah Barrett, one of his students when he taught creative writing. After finishing the manuscript, Barrett suffered a breakdown and set himself on fire, leaving him in a coma. Cogburn, whose own writing had been repeatedly turned down by publishers as mediocre, published the novel under his name once he heard that Barrett's family planned to switch off his life support. But Barrett survived, and in the present he has written a second book, The Divine Apostate, also under Cogburn's name. After forcing a confrontation, Barrett tries to burn both himself and his former teacher to death, but Cogburn crawls out of the fire, injured, and survives. Back home, he mails a letter to his agent admitting that he was not the real author of The Infernal Machine and that he had stolen it.

The film was shot over five weeks in the Algarve in Portugal, at Moviebox Studios and around Loulé, and was financed by executive producer Jack Christian's company, Filmology Finance. It received mixed reviews, with 46% of the 13 critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes giving it a positive notice.

documents.title: Code Name Banshee
documents.tagline: Two assassins. One secret. No turning back.
documents.overview: Caleb, a former government assassin in hiding, who resurfaces when his protégé, the equally deadly killer known as Banshee, discovers a bounty has been placed on Caleb's head.
documents.plot:
Code Name Banshee is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Jon Keeyes from a screenplay by Matthew Rogers. Jaime King stars as Delilah, a contract killer known professionally as Banshee, with Antonio Banderas as her former mentor Caleb, Tommy Flanagan as the rival assassin Anthony Greene, Catherine Davis as Caleb's daughter, Hailey, and Aleksander Vayshelboym as Kronos, alongside Dylan Flashner, Dina Plotch and Kim DeLonghi.

The film opens with a flashback establishing that several people were framed by the CIA years earlier, events tied to the disappearance and presumed death of Delilah's father. In the present, Delilah arrives for a job only to discover that she has been set up by Greene, a fellow killer connected to her father's fate. Greene wants to find Caleb, the man who trained Delilah, who has since retired from the business and gone off the grid, and on whose head there is a large bounty.

Delilah rejects Greene's threatening offer, but he turns her computer-hacking assistant, Kronos, who tells Greene and his crew of hired guns that she probably knows where Caleb is hiding. With Greene closing in, Delilah seeks out her old mentor, now living quietly and running a bar, and the two reconnect over a fireside conversation that touches on his regrets and on whether there is more to life than killing for money. Caleb's young adult daughter, Hailey, believes her father is simply a construction worker who has fallen foul of the mob. As Greene's men attack, including a fight at Caleb's bar in which Delilah takes on three opponents, Delilah, Caleb and Hailey are drawn into a violent showdown, while flashbacks trace Delilah's past and the path that led her into her line of work.

Screen Media released Code Name Banshee in theaters and on demand on 1 July 2022. Reviews were negative. Brent Simon of The A.V. Club called it a cliché-driven, rinse-and-repeat exercise in expended bullets, faulting its generic staging, muddled flashbacks and dark visual palette, though he credited Flanagan's calibrated villain, King's straight performance and the notes of regret Banderas brings to his underused role. Jeffrey Anderson of Common Sense Media gave it two stars out of five, praising King in a warrior role but finding so little going on that the film felt like a warmup act, and Alex Saveliev of Film Threat, rating it 4/10, criticized its haphazard editing, visible stunt doubles, washed-out colors and predictable twists.

documents.title: Gasoline Alley
documents.tagline: Justice gets dirty.
documents.overview: A man implicated in the triple homicide of three Hollywood starlets begins his own investigation. Needing assistance, he enlists the two detectives on his tail in order to expose a conspiracy more explosive than any of them imagined.
documents.plot:
Gasoline Alley is a 2022 American neo-noir action thriller directed by Edward John Drake and distributed by Saban Films, one of several low-budget films Drake made with Bruce Willis during the actor's final working years. Devon Sawa stars as the tattoo artist Jimmy Jayne, with Luke Wilson and Willis as the Los Angeles police detectives Freddy Vargas and Bill Freeman, Kat Foster as Jimmy's on-and-off girlfriend Christine, Sufe Bradshaw as the singer Eleanor, Kenny Wormald as the television actor Bourke and Rick Salomon as Persi.

Jimmy, an ex-convict who served time in prison, runs a tattoo parlour called Gasoline Alley, tends his 1966 Chevelle and drinks at a Melrose bar where his late mother once worked. There he crosses paths with a party girl named Star, and soon afterward Vargas and Freeman tell him that she has been killed along with other young women, and that he is their prime suspect, since a lighter bearing his studio's name was found at the scene. Determined not to go back inside for something he did not do, Jimmy starts investigating on his own.

Bourke, a vain actor Jimmy once protected in prison, tells him that Star ran with Persi, a pornographer and small-time criminal, and soon someone in Persi's Land Rover is shooting at Jimmy's car. Slipping into a drug-fuelled party at Persi's house, Jimmy is surprised to see Freeman there, and when a bouncer from the party turns up dead in the trunk of his Chevelle, it is clear he is being set up to take the fall. With help from Eleanor, who knew Star from Persi's gatherings and knows who supplies his drugs, Jimmy follows a trail of narcotics, dead women and police corruption. Freeman turns out to be involved in a human-trafficking ring using a tunnel between San Diego and Tijuana, and the story ends in a shootout in a warehouse in Mexico, where Jimmy, a skilled marksman, takes down the crooked detective and his accomplice and sets the building on fire.

Shot in Tifton, Georgia, in spring 2021 despite its Los Angeles setting, the film was released in theaters, on digital platforms and on demand on 25 February 2022. Reviews were mostly negative, with about a quarter of critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes. Decider credited Sawa with giving Jimmy real backbone but faulted the aimless pace and uneven story, while CBR found it an entertaining, at times unintentionally comic noir held together by a game cast.

documents.title: Curious George: Cape Ahoy
documents.overview: With help from a local fisherman, his niece and an adorable baby seal, George embarks on a quest in search of the long-lost shipwreck of legendary sea captain Trumpet Tooter.
documents.plot:
Curious George: Cape Ahoy is a 2021 American animated family adventure film directed by Doug Murphy, the sixth feature in the film series based on Margret and H. A. Rey's books about the mischievous monkey George and his best friend Ted, the Man with the Yellow Hat. Produced by Imagine Entertainment, Universal Animation Studios and Universal 1440 Entertainment, it features Frank Welker as George and Jeff Bennett as Ted, with Christopher Swindle as the fisherman Elmer, Romi Dames as his niece Emma, Rita Moreno as Gertrude, Luka Jones as Rocco and Kimberly Brooks as Gwen, along with Dee Bradley Baker.

Ted takes George to his favorite vacation spot, a little seaside town, hoping to relive happy memories of its annual Codfest. He has prepared a highly detailed itinerary built around cod fishing, but, as usual, things do not go as planned. Inspired by a pirate book that Ted reads to him, George becomes fascinated with the legend of the sea captain Trumpet Tooter, whose ship was lost long ago, and sets out to find the sunken wreck. With help from Elmer, a local fisherman, his niece Emma and an adorable baby seal, George drags the reluctant Ted into an exciting search beneath the waves, exploring the ocean first in a submersible and later scuba diving in wetsuits. Along the way the friends rescue the pup's mother, help a humpback whale that has become stuck in a reef and make new friends among the townspeople, including a scientist who studies the local marine life, an author and the owner of the town museum. Ted, who prefers to keep to a strict schedule, learns that it is all right to be flexible, to let plans change and to be open to new adventures instead of simply repeating old ones.

The film premiered on the streaming service Peacock on 30 September 2021. Common Sense Media described it as a simple, charming ocean story for preschoolers, praising its catchy music and lovable characters, its gentle message about adapting when plans go awry and helping others in need, and the surprising number of science facts woven into the story, such as how long whales can hold their breath and how compressed air is used. The reviewer also noted the diverse cast of characters in the little beach town and the patient, forgiving friendship between George and Ted, which offers a model that both young children and parents can relate to as they confront new experiences every day.

documents.title: ODDTAXI in the Woods
documents.original_title: 映画 オッドタクシー イン・ザ・ウッズ
documents.overview: Reconstruction of the television anime that will also depict what happens after its finale with a new story written by Kazuya Konomoto.
documents.plot:
Odd Taxi: In the Woods (Japanese: 映画 オッドタクシー イン・ザ・ウッズ) is a Japanese animated mystery feature from 2022, with Baku Kinoshita directing a screenplay by Kazuya Konomoto. It reworks Odd Taxi, the original 13-episode television anime produced by OLM and P.I.C.S. that premiered in April 2021 and became a sleeper hit, and it adds new material set after the series finale. The main television cast returns, including Natsuki Hanae as the taxi driver Hiroshi Odokawa, Riho Iida as the nurse Miho Shirakawa, Ryōhei Kimura as Ayumu Gōriki, Suzuko Mimori as Rui Nikaidō, Moeka Koizumi as Shiho Ichimura and Kenji Hamada as Dobu. The music is by the hip-hop artists OMSB, PUNPEE and VaVa.

As in the series, the world is populated by anthropomorphic animals. Odokawa is an eccentric, taciturn 41-year-old walrus who drives a taxi, has no family and keeps others at arm's length. He does, however, talk with his passengers, among them a college student desperate to go viral, a nurse hiding a secret, a struggling comedian, a street tough and a rising idol, and these conversations gradually draw him into the case of a missing girl, a member of the idol group Mystery Kiss.

Rather than simply condensing the episodes, the film rebuilds the story around a series of interviews in which the supporting characters testify, as if in a police investigation, about what happened on the fateful night of October 4. Their subjective accounts recast footage from the television anime and give the film the feel of a true-crime documentary, threading the seemingly unrelated events together without revealing every answer at once. The film ends with an extended version of Odokawa's confrontation with Sakura Wadagaki, whom the series had revealed to have killed and taken the place of the missing girl, Yuki Mitsuya, followed by a new epilogue set immediately after the series' final scene; the end credits show that Odokawa survived and that Sakura was arrested.

The film was announced on 25 December 2021, the date of the series finale within its story, and Asmik Ace released it in Japan on 1 April 2022, with Crunchyroll handling North America. It grossed about $438,000 at the Japanese box office. Anime News Network gave it a B+, praising the clever documentary-style framing that makes it a cohesive work in its own right and an acceptable first viewing, while noting that it offers little new story and that the series remains the fuller telling.

documents.title: War of the Worlds: Annihilation
documents.overview: A mother and son find themselves faced with a brutal alien invasion where survival will depend on discovering the unthinkable truth about the enemy.
documents.plot:
War of the Worlds: Annihilation is a 2021 American science fiction action film directed by Maximilian Elfeldt, who also co-edited it, from a screenplay by Conor Dowling. It was produced by The Asylum as an original film for the streaming service Tubi, the studio's second for the platform after Swim. It stars Arie Thompson, William Baldwin, Noel Gugliemi and Rashod Freelove. Shot in Los Angeles, with some scenes filmed at the March Field Air Museum, it was released in December 2021 and, unusually for an Asylum production, runs almost two hours.

A shower of meteorites, undetected even by NASA's constant monitoring, strikes the Earth, and each impact releases a gas that is toxic to humans. The military, led by General Skuller (Baldwin), insists that this is a deliberate alien attack and prepares for battle, while cyber-operations specialist Ashlaya Wellish (Thompson) sees flaws in his theory and has her warnings ignored. Skuller is proved right when vast spaceships appear in the sky and beings from another galaxy land, finding the planet's atmosphere and vegetation ideal for their survival. As chaos spreads, Ashlaya's husband Jutta (Michael Marcel) is sent out on patrol, and their son Lucas (Kennedy Porter) is trapped at his school, trying to seal the building against the poisonous substance. Giant tentacles, mech-like robots and looters soon join the danger. Along the way the family's story crosses with that of Tiago (Gugliemi), a survivalist, and Patlin (Freelove), a doctor who survived the attack on his hospital and who rescues a young alien named Gwen (Emree Franklin). Eventually Ashlaya and her companions join Skuller and what is left of his troops, and Ashlaya, seeking to make amends, finds a way to fight back, as survival comes to depend on discovering the unthinkable truth about the enemy.

The supporting cast includes Joseph Michael Harris, Andrew Rogers and Bradford Haynes. The film received little promotion. The website Voices From the Balcony called it surprisingly good for an Asylum film, finding the computer-generated alien ships and giant robots mostly convincing and the tone more serious than many of the studio's releases, and judged it enjoyable though somewhat long; Germany's TV Movie described Elfeldt as a low-budget professional. A sequel, War of the Worlds: Extinction, followed in 2024.

documents.title: My Father's Violin
documents.overview: Through their shared grief and connection to music, an orphaned girl bonds with her emotionally aloof, successful violinist uncle.
documents.plot:
My Father's Violin (Turkish: Babamın Kemanı) is a 2022 Turkish musical drama directed by Andaç Haznedaroğlu, whose earlier Netflix titles include Hot Sweet Sour and Have You Ever Seen Fireflies?. Produced by BKM, it stars Gülizar Nisa Uray as Özlem, Engin Altan Düzyatan as her uncle Mehmet, Belçim Bilgin as his wife Suna and Selim Erdoğan as Özlem's father Ali Rıza, with Ayfer Dönmez, Yiğit Çakır, Yener Sezgin and Erdem Baş. It was released on Netflix on 21 January 2022 and runs 112 minutes.

Ali Rıza is a street musician in Istanbul who plays the violin with a close-knit band for tourists, passers-by and restaurant diners. His red-haired eight-year-old daughter Özlem accompanies them everywhere, dancing and urging audiences to applaud and fill the hat, until the police chase the band away. Ali Rıza teaches her that everyone is a melody, and that one only needs to know how to listen. Coughing up blood and hiding from Özlem that he is dying, and with the girl's mother long gone, he seeks out his estranged brother Mehmet, a world-famous violinist, as her last hope. The two had escaped an abusive guardian as children, but Mehmet still resents what he sees as his brother's abandonment, and the reunion after more than three decades goes badly. After Ali Rıza's death, Mehmet, busy preparing for a major concert, refuses to take responsibility for the girl, but Suna, who longs for a child, arranges for social services to make him her guardian. The cold, arrogant musician gradually softens as Özlem, who never goes anywhere without her violin, forces her way into his heart. Their shared love of music binds them, and Mehmet even joins his late brother's band of buskers, taking Ali Rıza's place, while he comes to realize that his bitterness toward his brother was his own problem all along.

Reviews were moderately positive. Decider's Johnny Loftus recommended it, praising the real chemistry between Düzyatan and the precocious, quick-witted Uray and the film's respect for the power of music and family. In The New Indian Express, Bhuvanesh Chandar gave it three out of five, admiring the performances, especially Uray's, and its colorful visuals, and observing that the brothers' contrasting musical styles mirror their characters, but found the writing predictable and melodramatic and noted that Özlem's grief is barely shown. Other critics similarly called it a satisfying feel-good drama whose musical scenes lack realism.

documents.title: Wrong Place
documents.overview: A methamphetamine cook hunts down the former police chief of a small town in order to silence him before he can deliver eyewitness testimony against his family, but ultimately finds himself up against more than he had bargained for.

documents.title: A Jazzman's Blues
documents.tagline: Never stop loving.
documents.overview: A tale of forbidden love and family drama unravels 40 years of secrets and lies against a soundtrack of juke joint blues in the Deep South.
documents.plot:
A Jazzman's Blues is a 2022 American drama film written, produced and directed by Tyler Perry, starring Joshua Boone, Amirah Vann, Solea Pfeiffer, Austin Scott, Brent Antonello and Ryan Eggold. Perry wrote the screenplay, his first, in 1995, and the project passed through years of development before being made for Netflix.

In 1987, an elderly woman, Hattie Mae, visits Johnathan Dupree, the attorney general of Hopewell, Georgia, who is seeking re-election on a racist platform, and urges him to investigate the 1947 lynching of her son, Horace John Boyd, known as Bayou. She gives him a bundle of letters addressed to a Leanne J. Harper, and he begins to read. In flashback, Bayou is a sensitive, musically gifted young man, belittled by his guitarist father, Buster, who favors Bayou's older brother, Willie Earl, a talented trumpeter. Bayou falls for Leanne, a lonely, educated girl mocked by the town, who teaches him to read. Their secret romance is threatened by her abusive grandfather, and her mother, Ethel, takes her away to Boston, intercepting Bayou's letters. Buster abandons the family for Chicago, followed by Willie Earl.

After serving in the army, Bayou returns to Hopewell, where Hattie runs a juke joint. Willie Earl arrives with his manager, Ira, who hears Bayou sing and offers him an audition in Chicago. Leanne is back too, married to John, the brother of Sheriff Jackson, and passing as white at her mother's urging. When Ethel catches the reunited lovers, she falsely claims Bayou whistled at Leanne, and he flees to Chicago, where he becomes a star at the Capitol Royale while Willie Earl's drug use costs him his job. Back home, the sheriff's crackdown ruins Hattie's business. Bitter, Willie Earl tells the sheriff that Bayou is returning to Georgia, where he plans to escape with Leanne and their son, and Bayou is caught and lynched by a mob. In 1987, Johnathan realizes from the letters that he is the son of Bayou and Leanne. He gives the letters to his mother and steps outside to reckon with his identity as a fair-skinned Black man.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11, 2022, and was released on Netflix on September 23. It received generally favorable reviews, with 67% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 62, making it Perry's most acclaimed film, a distinction previously held by I Can Do Bad All By Myself (2009).

documents.title: Rescued by Ruby
documents.overview: Chasing his dream to join an elite K-9 unit, a state trooper partners with a fellow underdog: clever but naughty shelter pup Ruby. Based on a true story.
