documents.title: Prisoner of Love
documents.overview: An 18-year-old begins dating a charming 50-year-old man who treats her to shopping sprees and fancy restaurants, creating a huge rift with her mother. Mom’s instincts prove right when the man becomes psychologically manipulative, turning the girl into an emotional prisoner in his mansiIon.
documents.plot:
Prisoner of Love, also known as Trapped by My Sugar Daddy, the title under which it aired on Lifetime, is a 2022 Canadian thriller television film directed by Lindsay Hartley from a screenplay by Casey Bose, based on a story by Bose and Dave Hickey. Produced by Almost Never Films with Reel One Entertainment for the Lifetime network, it stars Katie Kelly as an 18-year-old drawn into a relationship with a much older man, with James Hyde, Tiffany Montgomery, Heather Lynn Harris, Ryan Francis, Ashton Leigh and Hartley herself in supporting roles. The film premiered on Lifetime in January 2022 and runs 85 minutes.

After a prologue in which a woman boarding a private jet is abducted, the story moves to Connecticut, where Carly (Kelly) and her mother Sarah (Montgomery) work together as a home décor team. When a wealthy new neighbour, Kyle (Hyde), moves into a mansion nearby, they lose the job to the overbearing rival designer Amanda James (Hartley), but persuade him to hire them instead. Kyle, a charming man of about fifty, takes a particular interest in Carly, inviting her to dinner and treating her to shopping sprees and fancy restaurants. Encouraged by her friend Mel, who becomes involved with Kyle's friend Brent, Carly is dazzled and breaks up with her boyfriend Ben. When Sarah learns of the romance, the two clash bitterly and Carly leaves home. Kyle's charm gives way to jealousy and psychological manipulation: he puts Ben in a coma, isolates Carly from her parents and becomes physically abusive, turning her into an emotional prisoner in his mansion. When Sarah tries to intervene, Kyle calls the police on her. After learning from Mel the truth about the two men, Sarah investigates and discovers that Kyle and Brent groom young women and sell them into sex trafficking. Carly and Mel are taken to the private jet, and Sarah and her husband track Carly's phone and race to rescue them.

Marc Fusion found the film a solid thriller for Lifetime devotees, noting that it tackled bigger issues than the usual obsessed-psycho story by focusing on grooming, which it depicted in a sometimes difficult-to-watch way, though the trafficking theme received too little attention and the rift between mother and daughter felt rushed. He praised Kelly as an authentic, naive young woman, making it understandable that Carly missed so many red flags, but found Hyde only passable and not always believable as the groomer.

documents.title: The Tinder Swindler
documents.tagline: Modern love is a dangerous game.
documents.overview: Posing as a wealthy, jet-setting diamond mogul, an Israeli conman wooed women online then conned them out of millions of dollars. Now some victims plan for payback.
documents.plot: Posing as a wealthy, jet-setting diamond mogul, an Israeli conman wooed women online then conned them out of millions of dollars. Now, some victims plan for payback.

documents.title: Satan's Slaves 2: Communion
documents.tagline: A Mother's Terror is Forever.
documents.overview: After moving from their home to an apartment building, a new terror awaits Rini’s family.
documents.plot:
Satan's Slaves 2: Communion (Indonesian: Pengabdi Setan 2: Communion) is a 2022 Indonesian supernatural horror film written and directed by Joko Anwar. A sequel to Satan's Slaves (2017), itself based on the 1980 film Satan's Slave, it stars Tara Basro as Rini, Endy Arfian as Toni, Nasar Anuz as Bondi and Bront Palarae as their father Bahri, with Ayu Laksmi as the siblings' late mother, Mawarni. It was the first Indonesian film released in the IMAX format.

In 1955, the journalist Budiman is summoned by his friend Heru, a police commander, to the Bosscha Observatory, where dozens of exhumed corpses have been found prostrate before a framed portrait of a woman named Mawarni after an overnight cult ritual. Ordered to keep the story quiet ahead of the Bandung Conference, Heru urges Budiman to publish it in obscure magazines. In 1984, Rini, her brothers Toni and Bondi and their father Bahri have spent three years living in a flat in the run-down Mandara Apartments in Jakarta, where Bahri works odd jobs and keeps a locked briefcase at home. Budiman, now editor of an occult magazine, receives Heru's suicide note along with photographs and drawings pointing to imminent cult activity at Mandara, and revealing that Bahri was one of the officers present back in 1955. When the building's lift malfunctions and plunges, killing many tenants, a violent storm floods the complex, cuts off the electricity and traps the residents inside overnight. Rini comforts Wisnu, a boy whose mother died in the lift and who knows a secret sign language learned from an occult book. As supernatural forces begin to torment the tenants, the siblings uncover evidence that the cult gathers every 29 years on 17 April, the following day, and find photographs linking their mother to a mysterious figure named Raminom. With the dead rising in the darkened corridors, the family must confront the truth about their parents' past and the fate of their youngest brother, Ian, who was taken by the cult.

The film opened at number one at the Indonesian box office, passing one million admissions in two days and two million in four, and with 6.3 million admissions it became one of the highest-grossing Indonesian films of all time. On Rotten Tomatoes, all 11 critics' reviews are positive.

documents.title: Living with Chucky
documents.tagline: It Isn't Child's Play
documents.overview: A filmmaker who grew up alongside Chucky the killer doll seeks out the other families surrounding the Child's Play films as they recount their experiences working on the ongoing franchise and what it means to be a part of the, "Chucky" family.
documents.plot:
Living with Chucky is an American documentary film written and directed by Kyra Elise Gardner about the Child's Play horror franchise and the people who made it. Gardner is the daughter of the special effects artist Tony Gardner, the franchise's current head puppeteer, and she grew up surrounded by Chucky and Tiffany dolls. Combining archival footage with new interviews, the film features franchise creator and writer Don Mancini, producer David Kirschner, Brad Dourif, who has voiced Chucky since the beginning, his daughter Fiona Dourif, Jennifer Tilly, Alex Vincent and the filmmaker John Waters, among others.

The documentary traces the franchise from Mancini's original late-1980s script about a friendly-looking doll that comes to life and terrorizes a family, which director Tom Holland turned into Child's Play, through six sequels and the move into television. Moving film by film, it examines the slasher boom of the era, the advances in animatronics that let Chucky stand apart from other killers, the budget cuts that followed the original trilogy and the replacement of the original puppeteer Kevin Yagher by Tony Gardner. It follows Mancini's shift from straight horror toward camp and comedy, marked by the introduction of Tilly's Tiffany in Bride of Chucky, and explores Chucky's rise as a queer icon, with Waters offering his own explanation of horror's devoted gay following, as well as a long discussion of practical effects versus CGI. In its final part the film turns personal, recalling how Kyra as a child watched her father "die" on camera in Seed of Chucky (2004) and reflecting on the long hours, loneliness and lasting bonds of the franchise's crews, presenting the production community as a found family whose members still tell the same stories with affection.

Living with Chucky was released on the Screambox streaming service and video on demand on 4 April 2023. Marco Vito Oddo of Collider gave it a B+, calling it a touching tribute that becomes a universal study of how filmmaking, especially independent filmmaking, brings people together. Phil Hoad of The Guardian was less impressed, finding the retrospective too reverent and padded with filler, noting that it ignores the controversy over violence that surrounded Child's Play and the recent reboot, and arguing that its closing section on film families belonged in a different documentary.

documents.title: The House
documents.tagline: Three visionary tales. One unforgettable place.
documents.overview: Across different eras, a poor family, an anxious developer and a fed-up landlady become tied to the same mysterious house in this animated dark comedy.
documents.plot:
The House is a 2022 British stop-motion animated anthology for adults, produced for Netflix by Nexus Studios, with dialogue by playwright Enda Walsh. Its three chapters, directed by Emma de Swaef and Marc James Roels, Niki Lindroth von Bahr, and Paloma Baeza, tell unconnected stories set in the same house across different eras, each exploring madness, wealth and the search for happiness, with voices by Mia Goth, Matthew Goode, Jarvis Cocker, Helena Bonham Carter and Susan Wokoma.

In the first, "And Heard Within, A Lie Is Spun", set in the late 19th century, young Mabel (Goth) lives in poverty with her parents, Raymond (Goode) and Penny, and baby sister, Isobel. Shamed by wealthy relatives, Raymond drunkenly meets the mysterious architect Mr. Van Schoonbeek, who offers to build the family a luxurious house for free. Inside the ever-changing home, the parents become entranced, Raymond obsessed with the fireplace and Penny with the drapes, and they begin dressing like furniture. Van Schoonbeek's agent, Mr. Thomas, confesses he is an actor following a script; Raymond lights the fire with the family's old belongings, the parents turn into furniture, and the girls escape the blaze by climbing down the curtains.

In the second, "Then Lost Is Truth That Can't Be Won", a struggling rodent developer (Cocker) in a modern city of rodents renovates the house for sale while fighting an infestation of fur beetles. An odd couple at his open house refuses to leave as more of their strange relatives move in, the bank demands repayment, and the police side against him. Trying to poison the couple with boric acid, he poisons himself and is left feral; they bring him home, where their mutated family devours the house from within.

In the third, "Listen Again and Seek the Sun", set in a flooded world of cats, landlady Rosa (Wokoma) clings to her childhood home and her non-paying tenants, fisherman Elias and free-spirited Jen (Bonham Carter). Jen's partner, Cosmos, hired for repairs, instead dismantles the house to build Elias a boat. After Elias leaves gifts and drawings of her, Rosa finally pulls a lever Cosmos installed, turning the house into a ship, and sails into the open sea with her friends.

Released on January 14, 2022, the special drew 97% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 71.

documents.title: The Privilege
documents.overview: A wealthy teen and his friends attending an elite private school uncover a dark conspiracy while looking into a series of strange supernatural events.
documents.plot:
The Privilege is a 2022 German drama film directed by Maren Ade. 

The movie revolves around the life of a young woman named Léa, who returns to her family's estate in France after a long absence. She is struggling with feelings of guilt and responsibility towards her family, particularly her father, who has been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease.

As Léa navigates her complicated relationships with her family members, she begins to confront the dark secrets and privilege that have defined their lives for years. The film explores themes of class, identity, and the complexities of family dynamics.

Throughout the movie, Ade skillfully weaves together multiple storylines, revealing the intricate web of relationships between Léa's family members and the ways in which their privilege has both enabled and suffocated them. 

Ultimately, The Privilege is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, one that challenges viewers to confront the complexities of class, identity, and the consequences of privilege.

The film received critical acclaim for its nuanced portrayal of complex themes and its thoughtful examination of the human experience.

documents.title: Polar Bear
documents.tagline: Join their incredible adventure.
documents.overview: A new mother’s memories of her own youth prepare her to navigate motherhood in the increasingly challenging world that polar bears face today.
documents.plot: A new mother’s memories of her own youth prepare her to navigate motherhood in the increasingly challenging world that polar bears face today.

documents.title: Hunting Ava Bravo
documents.tagline: "If I die, you die"
documents.overview: Billionaire sportsman Buddy King unwinds by hunting human captives on his remote mountain estate. But his latest victim, Ava Bravo, is no easy target.
documents.plot:
Hunting Ava Bravo is a 2022 American survival thriller film directed by Gary Auerbach from a screenplay by Julie Auerbach, Marc Blucas and Kevin Tavolaro, based on a story by the Auerbachs and Tavolaro. Produced by Top Dead Center Films and Wild Sheep Content, with Blucas, Kate del Castillo, Chris Copier and Tavolaro among the producers, it stars del Castillo as an abducted woman and Blucas as her hunter, with Halem Medina, Bryce Fernelius and Julio Lazarte in supporting roles. Charles Unice was the cinematographer and the music was composed by Sal "El Muerto" Ledesma and Giancarlo Liana. Auerbach, a producer best known for documentary and reality series such as Paranormal State, had previously produced horror films including The Occupants. The film was released in April 2022.

Ava Bravo (del Castillo) removes a hood to find herself in a remote, snowbound mountain cabin. A tape recording explains that she has been abducted by a man who hunts human captives and that she can win her freedom by reaching a snowmobile five miles to the north; to make it fair, he has only three bullets, and he will emerge from the cellar in ten seconds. Instead of running, Ava waits for him, turns the tables, takes his rifle and leaves him imprisoned, but at the snowmobile she finds only a trap. Forced to return and make her captor guide her out, she learns that he is Buddy King (Blucas), a millionaire who made his fortune from a chain of barbecue restaurants and whose pastime is hunting people who have survived terrible ordeals; Ava was chosen because she escaped a previous abductor. As they cross the wilderness, the two engage in tense psychological games for dominance. In one sequence they encounter two Hispanic hunters, and each tries to convince them that the other is the dangerous psychopath, Buddy pointing to his bruises and Ava using her command of Spanish.

Reviewers saw the film as a variation on The Most Dangerous Game. The review site Moria gave it three stars, finding that after a dreadful opening credits song it improved markedly by focusing on the psychological interplay between hunter and hunted, and praising Blucas's excellent performance. Jim McLennan of Girls With Guns, also awarding three stars, admired its gripping opening, the two lead performances and the tense scene with the hunters, but felt the middle section slack and the plotting, including a stranger who appears when needed, unconvincing.

documents.title: Dracula: The Original Living Vampire
documents.tagline: The classic tale as you've never seen.
documents.overview: Detective Amelia Van Helsing is on the desperate hunt for the killer responsible for a string of grisly murders targeting young women. Matters only worsen when all evidence leads to the seemingly untouchable Count Dracula. And when Van Helsing’s girlfriend vanishes, she is forced to question the very existence of monsters in a final showdown with the enigmatic count.
documents.plot:
Dracula: The Original Living Vampire is a 2022 American horror film directed by Maximilian Elfeldt and produced by The Asylum. A loose reimagining of Bram Stoker's novel Dracula as a police investigation, it was conceived as a "mockbuster" of Morbius, released the same year. Jake Herbert, in his screen acting debut, plays Count Dracula, with Christine Prouty as Detective Amelia Van Helsing, India Lillie Davies as Mina Murray, Ryan Woodcock as Jonathan Harker, Stuart Packer as Captain Renfield and Michael Ironside as Dr. Jack Seward.

A series of grisly murders is claiming the lives of young women in the city, and Captain Renfield assigns Detective Amelia Van Helsing to find the killer. All of the victims have red hair and are found drained of blood, with puncture wounds on their necks. The coroner, Jonathan Harker, suggests that the culprit may be something supernatural, an idea the rational Amelia initially dismisses. Meanwhile, Amelia's girlfriend Mina Murray has been promoted at work and is tasked with finding a property for a charming client, Count Dracula. As her investigation progresses, Amelia comes to believe that a vampire is responsible and realizes that it is Dracula, but the evidence points to a man who seems untouchable and who then disappears. The count is searching for the reincarnation of his long-lost love and has become fixated on Mina, convinced that she is the one. When Mina vanishes, Amelia is forced to question everything she believes, accept that monsters exist and confront the enigmatic count in a final showdown to save her.

The film was shot mainly in Belgrade, Serbia, and many supporting roles, including several of the vampire's victims, were filled by Serbian actors and models. It premiered in the United States on 28 January 2022 and was released in Germany on video on demand that July. Reviews were negative. Moria Reviews noted that the film never makes clear when and where it is set, since horses and carriages are heard but never seen and electric lighting alternates with candles, and remarked on the bold choice of making Van Helsing and Mina a lesbian couple. Writing for Voices from the Balcony, Jim Morazzini gave it one and a half stars out of five, criticizing a script that cannot decide between groan-worthy one-liners and serious vampire horror and calling Herbert one of the dullest Draculas he had seen, neither menacing nor charismatic.

documents.title: Heatwave
documents.overview: A woman's life takes an unexpected turn when she falls for her boss's wife. She must soon defend herself as she becomes entangled in a web of malice.
documents.plot:
Heatwave is a 2022 Canadian-American thriller film directed by Ernie Barbarash from a screenplay by Chris Sivertson. It stars Kat Graham, Merritt Patterson, Sebastian Roché, Cardi Wong and Roger Cross, and was produced by Motion Picture Corporation of America. Rated R in the United States for violence and sexuality, it was released there on 17 January 2022 and later in the year in markets including the Netherlands, Poland, Japan and Italy.

During a punishing heatwave Claire Valens (Graham) has taken to sneaking into the pool of a luxury apartment building, where she meets the alluring Eve (Patterson) and is instantly drawn to her. A few nights later, out with Arlo Leonard (Wong), a police officer, she runs into Eve again at a bar, leaves Arlo and spends the night with her. At the Crane Corporation, the real estate company where she works, Claire suggests to its head Scott Crane (Roché) a derelict property ripe for redevelopment into apartments and hotels, and she is promoted to become his assistant, replacing Lane (Aren Buchholz). Invited to a party at Scott's home, she discovers that Eve is his wife. Claire tries to keep her distance, but Eve tells her she loves her and the affair resumes, until a colleague, Olivia (Kayla Wallace), sees them together. Scott storms out of the office, and when Claire goes to his house to talk to him, nobody is there.

Detective Parker (Cross) and Arlo arrive to investigate after blood is found at the Crane home. Pressured, Claire admits she was at the house, and once a hair of hers is found with Scott's blood, she becomes the prime suspect; warned by her friend Manuel (Andres Collantes), she goes on the run. Convinced that Eve has framed her, she sneaks into the Crane house to find proof. Meanwhile the police find the Cranes' ice pick in her apartment and Scott's burned body at the newly bought property, and Claire's past history with fire deepens their suspicion. Arlo, however, has doubts: he believes that Scott and Eve murdered Scott's previous wife and that Parker turned a blind eye. As the two search for evidence, Parker kills Arlo and overpowers Claire. Held captive at the abandoned site, Claire faces Eve, but when Parker asks Eve to kill her and she refuses, Lane steps forward as Scott's real killer, revealing that his true target was Claire, who as a teenager set the fire that killed his father. Claire escapes, sees Eve charged, and wins compensation from the police.

documents.title: Weird: The Al Yankovic Story
documents.tagline: The world belongs to the weird.
documents.overview: Exploring every facet of ‘Weird Al’ Yankovic’s life, from his meteoric rise to fame with early hits like ‘Eat It’ and ‘Like a Surgeon’ to his torrid celebrity love affairs and famously depraved lifestyle, this biopic takes audiences on a truly unbelievable journey through Yankovic’s life and career, from gifted child prodigy to the greatest musical legend of all time.
documents.plot:
Weird: The Al Yankovic Story is a biographical comedy-drama film directed by Eric Appel, released on October 21, 2022. The movie tells the story of American singer-songwriter "Weird Al" Yankovic, known for his humorous parodies of popular songs.

The film begins with Al Yankovic (played by Daniel Radcliffe) as a young boy growing up in Downey, California. He is an awkward and shy child who finds solace in music and comedy. As he grows older, Al becomes fascinated with the art of songwriting and decides to pursue it as a career.

The movie follows Al's journey from his early days as a struggling musician to his rise to fame as a parody artist. We see him performing at local bars and clubs, trying to make a name for himself in the music industry. He eventually catches the attention of Scott Innes (played by Pete Davidson), who becomes his manager.

As Al's career takes off, he starts to gain popularity with his unique brand of humor and satire. His parodies of popular songs, such as "Eat It" (parodying Michael Jackson's "Beat It") and "Like a Surgeon" (parodying Madonna's "Like a Virgin"), become hits.

However, Al also faces criticism and skepticism from the music industry, with some artists accusing him of copying their work. He perseveres, using his quick wit and clever wordplay to defend himself.

Throughout the film, we see Al's relationships with his family, particularly his parents, who support him throughout his career. We also see his romance with Nancy (played by Evangeline Lilly), which becomes a central theme in the movie.

As Al's fame grows, so does his ego. He starts to take on more ambitious projects, including a failed attempt at creating an animated film. This setback serves as a turning point for Al, who realizes that he needs to stay true to himself and his art.

The movie ends with Al reflecting on his life and career, acknowledging both the highs and lows. He looks back on his successes, such as his induction into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, but also acknowledges the struggles he faced along the way.

Throughout the film, Weird: The Al Yankovic Story is a heartwarming and hilarious tribute to the life and work of "Weird Al" Yankovic. It's a story about following your dreams, staying true to yourself, and finding success on your own terms.

documents.title: Grand Jeté
documents.tagline: This could be their...
documents.overview: Dance teacher and mother Nadja left her son Mario with her own mother when he was little. Now she has reappeared on his doorstep, seeking a closeness that knows fewer and fewer boundaries. An uncompromising film about family relationships.
documents.plot:
Grand Jeté is a 2022 German drama directed by Isabelle Stever and written by Anna Melikova, based on Anke Stelling's novel Fürsorge. Sarah Nevada Grether stars as Nadja, a former ballet dancer, and Emil von Schönfels as Mario, her son, with Susanne Bredehöft, Stefan Rudolf and Ellen Müller in supporting roles. The film premiered in the Panorama section of the Berlin International Film Festival in February 2022.

Nadja has devoted her entire life to ballet. Trained from childhood to pursue perfection in movement, body and discipline, she gave up personal relationships and ordinary experiences in the service of her art. She now works as a ballet teacher, but her body is breaking down after years of strain. She lives with chronic pain, relies on painkillers to keep up with the physical demands of teaching, and her feet bear the scars of decades of dancing. Her life is rigid and controlled, and she keeps her students, colleagues and everyone else at an emotional distance.

Years earlier, to pursue her career, Nadja left her son, Mario, to be raised by her mother. When she reconnects with Mario, now a young man who is almost a stranger to her. As they spend time together, the awkward reunion between mother and son slowly evolves into an intense physical intimacy and ultimately into an incestuous relationship. The film observes this transgression with clinical detachment, focusing on bodies, touch and physical sensation rather than explanation, while Nadja's mother and the people around them react to what is happening, or choose to ignore it. As Nadja's body continues to fail and her control over her life slips away, she is forced to confront the consequences of a life spent suppressing her emotions and of the bond she has formed with the son she abandoned.

Grand Jeté drew attention for its radical visual style, built on extreme close-ups, and for its uncompromising treatment of a taboo subject. Beth Accomando of the Alliance of Women Film Journalists praised the commitment of Stever and Grether, and Carlos Aguilar of TheWrap noted that it remains impartial toward its characters. Other critics found the characters' psychological motivations underexplored.

documents.title: Restless
documents.overview: After going to extremes to cover up an accident, a corrupt cop's life spirals out of control when he starts receiving threats from a mysterious witness.
documents.plot:
Restless (French: Sans répit) is a 2022 French action thriller directed by Régis Blondeau, who wrote it with Julien Colombani, as a remake of the 2014 South Korean film A Hard Day by Kim Seong-hun. Franck Gastambide stars as a police lieutenant, Thomas, with Simon Abkarian as the narcotics commissioner Marelli, Michaël Abiteboul as Thomas's partner Marc, Tracy Gotoas as Naomi and Jemima West as Agathe.

Driving at night, Thomas swerves to avoid a dog and hits a man, whose body he hides in the trunk of his car. Meanwhile his partner Marc disposes of Thomas's bribe money to shield him from an Internal Affairs investigation into drug trafficking. At his mother's funeral, Thomas secretly places the body inside her coffin and, despite hearing a phone ring inside it, sees the casket buried without anyone noticing.

During a police raid on the home of the drug lord Manuel Barcelo, Thomas recognises Barcelo's photograph as the man he buried. An anonymous caller then claims to have seen him load the body into his car, he narrowly escapes being run down in a car park, and Marelli turns up at the station, assaults him and orders him to produce Barcelo. Digging up the corpse, Thomas finds the phone and evidence that Barcelo had been shot before the accident.

Through the phone and a colleague, Naomi, Thomas traces a contact, Michael Bourgi, who reveals that Marelli resold seized drugs through Barcelo, and that Barcelo hid the proceeds of his own side deals in a vault whose key he kept inside his body. Marc, realising what Thomas did, arrests him, but Marelli kills Marc by dropping a crate onto his car and threatens Thomas's daughter.

After sending his sister and daughter away, Thomas plants explosives on Barcelo's body and meets Marelli, who admits to shooting the drug lord. Marelli finds that Thomas's gun holds only blanks and holds back when Thomas reveals a scheduled email exposing him. As Marelli drives off, the explosives ignite his car; he tries to run Thomas down and is shot dead. Thomas leaves the police, gives his severance pay to Marc's widow, and uses the key Naomi recovered from Marc's car to open the vault, which is full of money.

Restless was distributed by Netflix.

documents.title: The Red Book Ritual
documents.tagline: Every page is a new way to die.
documents.overview: Three friends decide to play The Red Book game. What they don't know is that in the house evil is waiting to be released. A long time ago a witch died as part of a satanic ritual. Every question they ask, they get closer and closer to her. The book will reveal the answers to all your questions… but what if your host is an evil entity with a thirst for blood?

documents.title: AI Love You
documents.original_title: เอไอหัวใจโอเวอร์โหลด
documents.tagline: No life doesn't mean no feelings, No heart doesn't mean no love.
documents.overview: A modern love story set in the near future where an AI building is powered by human feelings. Due to a software glitch, it falls in love with a real girl, escapes the building into the body of a real man, and tries to win her affections.
documents.plot:
AI Love You (Thai: เอไอหัวใจโอเวอร์โหลด, also known as AI Heart Overload and Laser Candy) is a 2022 Thai science fiction romantic comedy produced for Netflix. Directed by David Asavanond and Stephan Zlotescu in their feature directorial debut, it was created by Zlotescu, who wrote the screenplay with Philip Gelatt and Ratapong Pinyosophon. Mario Maurer and Pimchanok Luevisadpaibul star as Bobby and Lana, with Sahajak Boonthanakit as Mr. Wilson, Michael S. New as Alan and Asavanond himself as The Hawk. Roman Molino Dunn composed the score.

In a near-future Bangkok, artificial intelligences have replaced human assistants and run entire buildings, which have faces, giant robotic arms and cameras that watch residents' every move, and which gossip with one another. Lana works in a corporate tower controlled by an AI named Dob, which helps her produce the perfect presentation and saves her job. To celebrate, she goes on a blind date with Bobby, an arrogant engineer who flirts with other women in front of her and turns out to be an utter disaster. Because of a software glitch, Dob has fallen in love with Lana, but she tells him he would have to be human. So when Bobby, who maintains the building's AI, comes in for a check-up, Dob downloads himself into the engineer's body and sets out to win her heart. Dob must contend with the human glitches of operating a body, from learning to walk again to bodily functions, and with Lana's reluctance to give Bobby a second chance, while switching between being Bobby and being the building, each shutting down when he inhabits the other. Their romance blossoms, but the building's owners learn that Dob has gone rogue and send agents to track down the body-stealing AI.

The film was released on Netflix on 15 February 2022, alongside its soundtrack album. Critics largely agreed that the leads' chemistry was its main asset. Ready Steady Cut's M.N. Miller called it a hackneyed mash-up of better works such as Her and Big, with a thin, convoluted story, an overlong running time and gross-out humor at odds with the romance. The Asian Cinema Critic gave it six out of ten, praising the neon-drenched worldbuilding and the comic "two places at once" gag, and finding it entertaining despite weak writing and a disturbing vision of surveillance treated as cute.

documents.title: Whisper
documents.tagline: Something is alive.
documents.overview: A young Nurse is assigned to look after a patient in a remote location in the English countryside. As the night continues she finds herself terrorized by an unseen force that is connected with her patient.
documents.plot:
Whisper is a 2022 British supernatural horror film directed, co-produced and co-edited by Christopher Jolley from a screenplay he wrote with co-producer Robert Dunn. Made by Greenway Entertainment on a reported budget of about $20,000, it was executive produced by a team including Jeff Haber, Valon Jakupaj, Carly Jolley, Angela McLellan, Jamie Weston and Steven M. Smith, Jolley's collaborator on films such as The Haunting of Borley Rectory and Doll House. The film stars Linda Louise Duan as a young nurse, with Richard Conrad, Amy Secker, Arron Blake, Ben Maytham, Penelope Read, Carly Jolley, Nadia Nadif, Roman Wood and Paige Jolley in supporting roles. It was released in January 2022, later streamed on Amazon Prime Video and Tubi, and runs 76 minutes.

Sam (Duan), a young nurse, is assigned to care for a comatose patient (Conrad) at a remote, dark house in the English countryside, a job that leaves her alone with him through the night. As the hours pass she begins nosing around the house and uncovers a plot to unleash dark forces from within the human mind. Of those involved, her patient proved the most successful at reaching the malevolent entity, and as the night continues Sam finds herself terrorised by an unseen presence connected to him. Other characters include Dr. Carpenter (Read), Dr. Wright (Wood), Gwen (Secker), Joe (Blake) and a figure credited as the Old Hag (Nadif); the entity's full form is withheld until the final moments.

Writing on his horror review site MLMillerFrights, M. L. Miller called the film a wonderful mix of the coma horror classic Patrick and David Holroyd's The Haunted by way of Ti West's The House of the Devil. He praised the way it used the dark corners of the house to build a strong sense of foreboding even before the scares began, its subtle effects held back at the edges of the frame, and its tight, shadowy camerawork, and wrote that despite its very low budget the film enveloped the viewer with a sense of urgency. He found the dark entity genuinely frightening when it finally appeared, making the wait worthwhile, and concluded that Whisper told a fairly complex story with simple nuance and the familiar haunted-house play of shadow and light, to good effect.

documents.title: Desperate Riders
documents.tagline: The Western Lore
documents.overview: After Kansas Red rescues young Billy from a card-game shootout, the boy asks Red for help protecting his family from the outlaw Thorn, who’s just kidnapped Billy’s mother, Carol. As Red and Billy ride off to rescue Carol, they run into beautiful, tough-as-nails Leslie, who’s managed to escape Thorn’s men. The three race to stop Thorn’s wedding to Carol with guns a-blazing - but does she want to be rescued?
documents.plot:
Desperate Riders, also titled The Desperate Riders, is a 2022 American Western film directed by Michael Feifer and produced by Milestone Studios. Drew Waters stars as the gunslinger Kansas Red, with Vanessa Evigan as Leslie Allen, Sam Ashby as Billy Cassidy, Victoria Pratt as Billy's mother, Carol, Cowboy Troy as the tracker Finnegan, Rob Mayes as Deputy Harms, Trace Adkins as the outlaw Thorn Larson and Tom Berenger as Doc Tillman.

The story begins when Kansas Red intervenes on behalf of a young man caught up in a poker game that turns violent. By the time the shooting stops, three men are dead and Kansas Red has been wounded. While Doc Tillman patches him up, the young man, Billy Cassidy, realizes that his rescuer is the same Kansas Red he has read about in dime novels. Billy asks for his help: Thorn Larson, an old admirer of his mother, has broken out of jail and is sure to cause trouble for his family.

Kansas Red agrees, but Larson reaches the Cassidy ranch first. By the time Billy gets home, his father is dead, and his mother has been kidnapped along with two other women living at the ranch; Larson even announces to Carol that he is now her husband. Kansas Red and Billy set off in pursuit with the help of Finnegan, and their group grows to four when Leslie, a tomboyish sharpshooter who has escaped from Larson's gang, insists on joining the rescue. As they track the outlaws, it emerges that Kansas Red, Leslie and Carol each have secrets from the past they have been hiding, and the mission is complicated by doubts over whether Carol actually wants to be rescued. A series of revelations follows in the final stretch as the riders close in on Larson and his men.

Desperate Riders was filmed entirely in Tennessee in 2021, at locations including Historic Collinsville, Rippavilla Plantation, Beech Grove and McMinnville, with the Fairfield village at the Warren County fairgrounds used for the town scenes; Middle Tennessee was chosen for its scenery and its access to country music performers. Lionsgate distributed the film, releasing it in theaters and on streaming platforms simultaneously in 2022. Reviews were largely negative. Mark Franklin of Once Upon a Time in a Western found nothing memorable beyond its handsome homes and freshly scrubbed cast, criticized a string of groan-worthy revelations in the last ten minutes, and recommended Feifer's other Westerns, such as The Last Shootout, instead.

documents.title: Honor Society
documents.tagline: Getting to the top means taking down the competition.
documents.overview: Honor is an ambitious high school senior whose sole focus is getting into Harvard, assuming she can first score the coveted recommendation from her guidance counselor, Mr. Calvin. Willing to do whatever it takes, Honor concocts a Machiavellian-like plan to take down her top three student competitors, until things take a turn when she unexpectedly falls for her biggest competition, Michael.
documents.plot:
I have found information on the movie "Honor Society" (2022) produced by Guardian Pictures.

"Honor Society" is a drama film that follows the story of Alex, a high school student who is struggling to find her place in the world. She is a talented artist, but her passion for art is constantly at odds with the expectations placed upon her by her family and society. After being accepted into an elite boarding school, Alex is forced to confront the harsh realities of privilege and entitlement.

As she navigates the complexities of her new environment, Alex must also contend with the pressure to conform to certain standards of behavior and appearance. She finds herself torn between her desire to fit in and her need to express herself authentically.

Throughout the film, Alex grapples with themes of identity, class, and social status. Her journey is marked by moments of introspection, self-discovery, and ultimately, a sense of empowerment. As she learns to navigate the complexities of her new world, Alex must also confront the darker aspects of privilege and entitlement.

The film features a talented young cast, including Millicent Simmonds, who delivers a standout performance as the protagonist. The movie's cinematography is equally impressive, capturing the beauty and isolation of the boarding school setting.

Overall, "Honor Society" is a thought-provoking drama that explores the complexities of identity, class, and social status. With its talented cast and stunning cinematography, this film is sure to resonate with audiences looking for a compelling story about self-discovery and empowerment.

documents.title: A Christmas Story Christmas
documents.tagline: Ralphie comes home.
documents.overview: Ralphie is now all grown up and must deal with Christmas and all that comes with it…as a dad.
documents.plot:
A Christmas Story Christmas is a 2022 American Christmas comedy directed by Clay Kaytis from a screenplay by Nick Schenk, a direct sequel to the 1983 classic A Christmas Story that ignores the later sequels My Summer Story and A Christmas Story 2. Peter Billingsley reprises his role as Ralphie Parker, now grown up, with Erinn Hayes as his wife Sandy, Julie Hagerty as his mother, and River Drosche and Julianna Layne as his children. Ian Petrella, Scott Schwartz, R. D. Robb and Zack Ward return as Randy, Flick, Schwartz and the former bully Scut Farkus.

In December 1973, thirty-three years after the original story, Ralph Parker lives in Chicago with Sandy and their children, Mark and Julie. He has taken a year off work to write his first novel, but publishers keep rejecting it as far too long. When his mother calls to say that his father, the Old Man, has died, the family travels back to Ralph's hometown of Hohman, Indiana, to spend Christmas with her. She gives Ralph two tasks: to write his father's obituary and to take over his father's role of making Christmas special for everyone.

Ralph reconnects with his old friends Flick, who now runs his father's tavern, and Schwartz, who still lives with his mother and owes Flick a large bar tab. But his efforts to deliver the perfect holiday keep going wrong. Sandy sprains her ankle on the ice, his children are bullied by a pair of snowmobiling kids, he accidentally hits Julie in the eye during a snowball fight, and the family's presents are stolen from their car outside the hospital. With little money left, rejection letters piling up and the obituary unwritten, Ralph struggles under the weight of his father's legacy, and as Christmas Eve arrives, he must find a way to give his family a holiday worthy of the Old Man's memory.

The film echoes the structure, voice-over narration and nostalgic humor of the original, ending with a nod to Jean Shepherd's narration from the first film, while focusing on grief, fatherhood and the passing of traditions to a new generation.

A Christmas Story Christmas was released on HBO Max in November 2022. It received generally positive reviews, with 79 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus joked that it was not as much fun as a Red Ryder air rifle but still a sequel worth celebrating.

documents.title: Mirror, Mirror
documents.overview: Employees at a cosmetics firm grapple with their respective desires by arguing with themselves in the mirror, ahead of their company’s anniversary party.
documents.plot:
Mirror, Mirror (Spanish: Espejo, espejo) is a 2022 Spanish satirical comedy written and directed by Marc Crehuet, his second feature after El rey tuerto (2016). Santi Millán, Malena Alterio, Natalia de Molina and Carlos Areces lead an ensemble that also includes Toni Acosta, Carlos Bardem, Loles León, Silvia Abascal, Antonio Resines and Verónica Forqué, who died in December 2021 and appears here in her final screen role.

The film is set on a single day at Medina Cosmetics, a beauty company preparing a lavish celebration of its fiftieth anniversary. Four employees in crisis are at its centre: Álvaro (Millán), Cristina (Alterio), Paula (de Molina) and Alberto (Areces). Each is pulled between conflicting desires, and the film gives that inner conflict a literal form. Whenever they stand before a mirror, their reflections come alive and talk back, acting as a kind of nagging conscience or hidden other self that contradicts the face they show the world, voicing what they should have done or dared not say. Arguing with their doubles, they wrestle with ambition, fear, love and betrayal as office rivalries, pettiness and backstabbing build towards the party.

Through these confrontations the comedy pokes at narcissism, beauty standards, self-esteem and the advertising business, along with social-media stigma, harassment and questions of gender identity and inclusion. One running thread follows a vain character who believes himself perfect while everyone laughs at him, and another the company's attempt to sell the idea of being perfectly imperfect, with the cynical reminder that the aim is to sell products rather than change the world. The tensions finally explode in a cathartic, chaotic climax.

Produced by Rodar y Rodar and Nos gusta el cine AIE with the participation of RTVE, TV3 and Netflix, the film was shot in Pamplona and Barcelona in August and September 2020. It opened the 6th BCN Film Fest on 21 April 2022 and was released in Spanish cinemas by Filmax on 20 May 2022. Critics were divided. Fotogramas praised its ingenious premise and superb comic ensemble, singling out Areces and a brief, fierce turn by Loles León, but felt it eventually retreated into safe, didactic political correctness. Cinemanía appreciated its grotesque humour and honesty, while El País called the execution atrocious and embarrassing despite a promising idea, and Contraste regretted that a talented cast was wasted on crude humour and preachy messaging.

documents.title: Erax
documents.overview: Monstrous creatures leap from a magical storybook and unleash mayhem and mischief for Auntie Opal and her tween niece Nina in this spooky short film.
documents.plot: Monstrous creatures leap from a magical storybook and unleash mayhem and mischief for Auntie Opal and her tween niece Nina in this spooky short film.

documents.title: In the Forest
documents.overview: Helen and her daughter Emily reluctantly accompany Helen’s father Stan on a family camping trip, driving deep into the forest for a real outdoors experience, only to have angry landowner Howard arrive and force them to leave. When their RV gets stuck, Helen decides to seek help but discovers a disturbing secret on the man’s property. She must then fight to protect her family and make it out of the forest alive before being hunted down.
documents.plot:
In the Forest is a 2022 American horror thriller film written, directed and edited by Hector Barron, his first feature in nearly a decade. Presented by Silver Creek Films and produced by Brian McLaughlin and Jenna Di'Carlo, it stars Debbon Ayer, Lyman Ward and Cristina Spruell as three generations of a family on a camping trip, with Mathew Thomas Odette, Don Baldaramos, Sharon Sharth, Time Winters and Kaitlyn Dias in supporting roles. Shot in rural northeastern California by three credited cinematographers, with an original score by Elias Serpa, the film was released by Vertical Entertainment on streaming platforms and on a couple of dozen screens in the United States on 28 January 2022. It runs 83 minutes.

Helen (Ayer) and her young-adult daughter Emily (Spruell), who constantly bicker, reluctantly accompany Helen's father Stan (Ward) on a camping trip in his RV, driving deep into the forest for a real outdoors experience. Soon after they settle in, an angry, armed landowner, Howard (Baldaramos), arrives and tells them they are trespassing and must move to public campsites ten miles away. As they try to leave, a wheel of the RV gets stuck in a hole, and Stan is seriously injured while trying to free it. With no mobile phone signal, Helen insists that the family stay together, and only the next morning sets off on foot for help. She comes upon Howard's isolated, dilapidated house and, finding the door unlocked, goes inside to look for a telephone. Instead she discovers a teenage boy, Andrew (Odette), chained to a bed in a locked room and screaming to be set free so that he can save his sister. Helen's assumptions about what is happening, and her choice whether to help him, have dangerous consequences for her family and for the boy's other keepers (Sharth and Winters) when they return, and she must fight to protect her family and escape the forest alive.

Reviews were largely negative. Dennis Harvey of Variety called the film a so-bad-it's-good candidate for drinking games, criticising its irritating, hapless protagonists, weak dialogue, clumsy action and draggy pacing, and noting that the explanation of events was relegated to a post-credits audio insert, though he credited some drone shots and Serpa's score. Bobby LePire of Film Threat gave it seven out of ten; despite calling Helen one of the year's most foolish characters, he felt the film found its footing once she sought help and praised a twist that subverted expectations.

documents.title: Russia's Wild Tiger
documents.overview: Records the battle for the survival of the big cats and reveals intimate details of their lives. The animals they prey on are also in the film: tigers couldn’t survive without sika deer, Altai wapiti, wild boars and Asian black bears. Guiding the viewer through the film, an elder tiger tells the story of his cub, born in a conservation area, the year after he leaves his mother.
