documents.title: Broken Idol: The Undoing of Diomedes Díaz
documents.original_title: Diomedes: el ídolo, el misterio y la tragedia
documents.overview: This documentary chronicles Diomedes Díaz's rise as one of Colombia's most iconic singers, and his downfall after being accused of killing a fan.
documents.plot:
Broken Idol: The Undoing of Diomedes Díaz (Spanish: Diomedes: el ídolo, el misterio y la tragedia) is a 2022 Colombian biographical documentary film directed by Jaime Barbosa and Jorge Durán for Netflix. Running about 101 minutes, it traces the career of the vallenato singer Diomedes Díaz, known as the King of Vallenato and one of Colombia's best-selling and most beloved performers, and the case surrounding the death of Doris Adriana Niño, a young woman who was his fan. The film combines archival concert footage and interviews Díaz gave during his lifetime with testimony from his family, friends, fans, colleagues, music industry figures, lawyers, investigators and Niño's relatives.

The documentary follows Díaz from a childhood of extreme poverty and his early struggle to make a name for himself in the competitive world of vallenato to his rise as a superstar in the 1980s and 1990s, whose songs drew on his own experiences and filled concerts with huge crowds. It portrays an exuberant, impulsive figure with a famous smile and a diamond set in his tooth, who boasted of fathering dozens of children with many women and whose drinking and drug use grew alongside increasingly chaotic shows. The second half turns to May 1997, when Niño, who had met Díaz at a concert and had a relationship with him, went to his Bogotá apartment and never returned home; her body was found the next morning in a cow pasture near Tunja. The film examines the conflicting accounts of that night, the investigation that connected Díaz and members of his entourage to her death, her brother's efforts to defend her reputation, Díaz's denials, his flight from justice and the trial in which he was convicted of involuntary manslaughter. It leaves viewers to weigh the competing versions for themselves.

The documentary was released on Netflix on 30 March 2022. Romey Norton of Ready Steady Cut considered it a good, intriguing watch, praising its energetic Colombian music, quick cutting and contrasting cinematography, and its wide range of interviewees, including the victim's brother, whose determination she found moving. Pooja Sharma of Leisurebyte called it a gripping and thorough account of an icon whose story had been curiously under-told, presenting it as the sad tale of a man so consumed by fame that he lost sight of everything else. Díaz died of a heart attack in Valledupar at the age of 56, days after releasing his thirtieth album.

documents.title: Sinister Stepsister
documents.overview: Jeff Mitchell seems to have it all. He has an interesting and lucrative job, a loving wife, and two amazing kids. Therefore, life is good. However, on one bright day, a cosmic sucker punch comes out of the blue. When Jeff was in high school, unbeknownst to him, he got his girlfriend pregnant. Next, the girl moved away, had the baby, and raised her as a single mother, never telling her daughter, Carlee, who her real father was. However, Carlee's mother recently died in a tragic accident, prompting Carlee to try and uncover the truth. Maybe Jeff is not so lucky after all?
documents.plot:
Sinister Stepsister is a 2022 American thriller television film directed by John Murlowski from a screenplay by Adam Rockoff. Produced by Maple Island Films and Reel One Entertainment, it stars Annika Foster as a young woman who claims to be a long-lost daughter, with Tu Morrow, Jhey Castles, Matthew Pohlkamp, Johan Gran, Jacob Taylor, Dayne Jarrah and Madison Russ in supporting roles. The film premiered in March 2022 on the Lifetime Movie Network and runs 84 minutes.

Jeff Mitchell (Pohlkamp) appears to have it all: an interesting, well-paid job, a loving wife, Lisa (Castles), and two children, the caring Noah (Jarrah) and the mildly rebellious Ella (Morrow). When his talented colleague Blake (Taylor) is promoted over him to replace their boss, Jeff goes to a bar to consider his next steps. There a young woman, Carlee Byrne (Foster), introduces herself; he mistakes her approach for flirtation, but she asks whether he remembers Jennifer, his high-school girlfriend, and reveals that Jennifer became pregnant by him without his knowledge, moved away and raised her daughter alone, never telling her who her father was. Jennifer's recent death in an accident has prompted Carlee to seek the truth. Stunned, Jeff and Lisa ask her to take a paternity test; when the results appear to confirm that she is his daughter, Jeff welcomes her into the family. Ella, however, does not trust her, and she is right: Carlee is dangerous and willing to kill to secure a perfect family. To protect her secret she fakes lab results, poisons a man and commits murder, and when Ella's boyfriend Ryan (Gran) tries to catch her in a lie, she warns him off with a knife at his throat.

Reviews were mixed. Phil Wheat of Nerdly described the film as another riff on Single White Female that followed a very familiar formula but was too clean-cut and watered down to make an impact; he found Morrow's tenacious, genuine performance as Ella the only real standout, considered Foster's Carlee too two-dimensional to be an intriguing villain and criticised the weak ending, though he suggested fans of home-invasion thrillers might enjoy it. That Darn Girl Movie Reviews gave it three out of five stars, calling it entertaining though predictable, describing Carlee as a worthy foe for Ella and singling out her chilling exchanges with Ryan.

documents.title: Silverton Siege
documents.tagline: Freedom is a fight.
documents.overview: After a failed sabotage mission, a trio of anti-apartheid freedom fighters ends up in a tense bank hostage situation. Based on a true story.
documents.plot:
Silverton Siege is a 2022 South African action thriller directed by Mandla Dube and inspired by the real Silverton bank siege of January 1980 in Pretoria, in which members of uMkhonto we Sizwe, the armed wing of the African National Congress, took hostages in a bank. Thabo Rametsi, Noxolo Dlamini and Stefan Erasmus star as the three freedom fighters, with Arnold Vosloo as the police captain pursuing them and Tumisho Masha. The film was released internationally on Netflix on 27 April 2022.

Calvin Khumalo, Terra Mabunda and Aldo Erasmus are anti-apartheid guerrillas in MK planning to sabotage a fuel depot outside Silverton, a suburb of Pretoria. Their mission is foiled because the security police, led by Captain Langerman, have been tipped off. Forced to abort, they flee toward the city; after Terra's partner Masego is shot and their van disabled, they escape through sewer tunnels and emerge in the heart of Pretoria near Church Square. Spotted by police, they take refuge inside a branch of the Volkskas Bank.

Calvin addresses the frightened customers and staff, explaining that the group is not there to rob the bank and asking for calm cooperation so that no one is hurt. Christine, a bank supervisor, proves helpful and sympathetic. Police surround the building, and when Langerman calls each of the fighters by name over a loudhailer, they become convinced that there is an informant inside their organization. They demand a helicopter with an unarmed black pilot, intending to take a hostage with them, but an attempted escape to the helicopter turns out to be a trap, and everyone returns to the bank. As the standoff grows tense and the world's press gathers outside, the fighters change strategy, using the media attention to demand the release of Nelson Mandela, who was then imprisoned, turning the siege into a political statement against apartheid while the police prepare to storm the building.

The film received mixed to positive reviews, with a 75 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on eight reviews. Critics praised the performances of the three leads, which gave the characters depth and complex motivations, especially during the tense standoff, although some noted that the film fictionalizes important elements of the historical events.

documents.title: King Tweety
documents.tagline: MEET THE NEW ROYAL FAMILY.
documents.overview: Everyone's favorite yellow canary unexpectedly becomes next in line for the crown when the queen of an island paradise disappears. His Little Highness’ entourage includes motorbike daredevil Granny and sly Sylvester, whose allegiance is tested when he uncovers a sinister plot to eliminate Tweety for good.
documents.plot:
King Tweety is a 2022 American animated direct-to-video comedy produced by Warner Bros. Animation and starring the Looney Tunes characters Tweety and Sylvester, with a voice cast that includes Eric Bauza, Candi Milo, Jon Daly, Niccole Thurman and Flula Borg. It was the first new direct-to-video Looney Tunes feature since Looney Tunes: Rabbits Run in 2015, Tweety's second direct-to-video starring vehicle after Tweety's High-Flying Adventure (2000), and the first Looney Tunes film directed by a woman.

Watching the evening news, Tweety, Sylvester and Granny learn that Aoogah, the bird queen of the Canary Islands, has mysteriously vanished, and that Tweety bears all the marks of a member of the royal bird family. The kingdom invites Tweety and Granny to fly from New York so that Tweety can be crowned, but cats are forbidden there, so Sylvester stows away. When he is discovered, Tweety insists that he be allowed to stay as his "brother". The royal adviser and sorcerer Diego von Schniffenstein gives them a tour of the islands, home to both birds and dogs, and helps prepare Tweety for his lavish coronation.

At the ceremony, Sylvester discovers that Diego was responsible for the queen's disappearance and is now plotting against Tweety. He spends the following day foiling Diego's assassination attempts while hunting for proof, but Tweety inadvertently gets them both caught, and Diego kidnaps the new king and frames Sylvester for eating him. Granny, who has seen the evidence against Diego, breaks Sylvester out of jail, and they use one of Tweety's magical royal tail feathers to track him to a ship offshore. There Tweety finds Aoogah alive. Diego reveals that he made himself immortal seven centuries ago, led a failed uprising of dogs against the birds, and has been secretly killing monarchs to collect their feathers, which he has made into a boa that magnifies his magic.

Sylvester sneaks aboard, defeats the henchdogs and frees the captives, but Diego uses the boa to transform into a giant. When Sylvester distracts him and the birds pull the boa apart, the feathers become the spirits of past rulers, who help defeat the sorcerer. Homesick, Tweety returns the crown to Aoogah, who decides she needs a vacation and joins the trio in New York. Common Sense Media awarded the film three out of five stars.

documents.title: The Aviary
documents.tagline: Believing is deceiving.
documents.overview: A twisted journey of two women’s desperate flee to escape the clutches of Skylight, an insidious cult. Lured in by the promise of “freedom” in the isolated desert campus called The Aviary, Jillian and Blair join forces to escape in hopes of real freedom. Consumed by fear and paranoia, they can’t shake the feeling that they are being followed by the cult’s leader, Seth, a man as seductive as he is controlling. The more distance the pair gains from the cult, the more Seth holds control of their minds. With supplies dwindling and their senses failing, Jillian and Blair are faced with a horrifying question: how do you run from an enemy who lives inside your head?
documents.plot:
The Aviary is a 2022 American psychological thriller written and directed by Chris Cullari and Jennifer Raite. Malin Åkerman and Lorenza Izzo star as two women fleeing a cult, with Chris Messina as its leader and Sandrine Holt. The film was released by Saban Films on 29 April 2022.

Jillian and Blair, two women who have been members of a secretive self-help community, escape from its compound in the middle of the night and set out on foot across the New Mexico desert. They hope to reach a town and a rendezvous point where they believe help will be waiting. The group, which presents itself as a wellness retreat, is controlled by Seth, a charismatic and manipulative leader who has exerted enormous psychological power over his followers, including both women.

As they cross the empty landscape, the two women's supplies of water dwindle, the heat and exhaustion take their toll, and they begin to fear that Seth or his followers are tracking them. The longer they walk, the more Seth seems to be present in their minds, his voice and teachings echoing in their memories. Memories of life inside the group surface as they walk, showing how its leader exploited their vulnerabilities. Tension grows between them as they argue about directions and whom to trust, and doubts arise over whether both of them truly want to leave Seth behind. Strange signs and inexplicable events make them question their perceptions, and the desert becomes a psychological trap as they try to determine whether the danger is real, whether they are truly free, and whether they will ever escape the hold the cult has over them.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 63 percent approval rating based on 27 reviews, with a consensus stating that its adroitly assembled cast lends extra weight to an uneven depiction of how dangerous cults can be, and it has a Metacritic score of 57. Critics praised the performances of Åkerman, Izzo and Messina and the film's atmosphere of paranoia, but some felt the story lost momentum and that its ambiguous ending was unsatisfying.

documents.title: The Mystery of Marilyn Monroe: The Unheard Tapes
documents.original_title: The Mystery of Marilyn Monroe: The Unheard Tapes
documents.tagline: The brighter the star, the darker the truth.
documents.overview: This documentary explores the mystery surrounding the death of movie icon Marilyn Monroe through previously unheard interviews with her inner circle.
documents.plot:
The Mystery of Marilyn Monroe: The Unheard Tapes is a 2022 American documentary directed by Emma Cooper for Netflix. It examines the life and early death of actress Marilyn Monroe through archival footage and previously unheard interviews with people who knew her.

The film is built around the research of Anthony Summers, author of the 1985 book Goddess. Summers began investigating after the Los Angeles County District Attorney reopened the inquiry into Monroe's death. Over three years he recorded about 650 interviews with people who knew Monroe or had information about how she died. Actors lip-sync the original audio in reenactments.

It traces Monroe's rise in Hollywood and her affairs with powerful men who helped her career. Jane Russell recalls her work ethic; others describe mental health struggles rooted in her troubled childhood. The film covers her marriage to playwright Arthur Miller, whose left-wing ties brought FBI scrutiny to the couple, and her growing dependence on prescription drugs before their divorce in 1961. It then turns to her relationships with the Kennedy family. Witnesses describe her affairs with John F. Kennedy and Robert F. Kennedy, often at the Malibu beach house of Peter Lawford and his wife Patricia Kennedy Lawford. Summers argues that in the Cold War climate of 1962, the FBI feared that Monroe, given her leftist politics, might repeat what the brothers told her, and the Kennedys tried to cut her off.

The documentary then compares the official account of Monroe's death in August 1962 with the testimony Summers gathered. In the official version, her housekeeper Eunice Murray found the bedroom locked in the early morning, and psychiatrist Ralph Greenson broke in to find her dead, leading to a ruling of probable suicide by overdose. Several interviewees instead describe an emergency that began hours earlier, the arrival of publicist Arthur P. Jacobs and an ambulance ride with Greenson. They say Monroe died at or on the way to the hospital before being returned to her bed. Investigator Fred Otash and surveillance expert Reed Wilson say Lawford hired them to remove evidence of the Kennedy connection. Summers still does not believe Monroe was murdered. He concludes she died by suicide or an accidental overdose and attributes any cover-up to her ties with the Kennedys. A 1982 district attorney review upheld the ruling.

Netflix released the film on April 27, 2022, and it drew about 23 million viewing hours in two weeks.

documents.title: Dakota
documents.tagline: No dog left behind.
documents.overview: Dakota, an ex-service dog, joins single mum Kate and her daughter Alex to live on their small-town family farm. Dakota quickly adjusts to her new home and becomes somewhat of a local hero, soon becoming inseparable from Alex. But when the farm’s existence is threatened by the town’s rogue sheriff, Dakota must help the family band together and save the land.

documents.title: Rainbow
documents.tagline: This is not a movie, it’s a trip!
documents.overview: A modern tale of a teenager’s coming-of-age journey loosely inspired by the classic novel “The Wonderful Wizard of Oz.”
documents.plot:
Rainbow is a 2022 Spanish fantasy drama directed by Paco León and loosely based on L. Frank Baum's 1900 novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz. The singer Dora Postigo stars as Dora, a teenager with an extraordinary musical gift, with Áyax Pedrosa, Wekaforé Jibril, Carmen Maura, Carmen Machi and Luis Bermejo. León described it as not a musical but a film with a great deal of music. It premiered at the 70th San Sebastián International Film Festival on 18 September 2022, was released in selected Spanish cinemas on 23 September and arrived on Netflix on 30 September.

The film reimagines Baum's story as a contemporary coming-of-age road movie set in Spain. Dora is a gifted young singer living with her father, Diego. After a bitter argument with her father, she decides to leave home, taking her dog Toto with her, and sets out on a journey toward the faraway "Ciudad Capital," hoping that there she will find what she is looking for.

Along the way, Dora meets a series of characters who mirror the companions of Baum's Dorothy, outsiders who are each looking for something they believe they lack and who join her on the road. The journey through a stylized, colorful landscape of highways, villages and strange encounters becomes a search for identity and belonging, as the travelers confront their insecurities, and Dora's music and the people she meets help her understand her past and decide who she wants to be. Rather than retelling the novel faithfully, León uses its familiar structure as a framework for a story about youth, family, diversity and self-acceptance, in which music plays a central role.

Critical reception in Spain was largely negative. Fernando Bernal of Cinemanía gave it one star out of five, writing that the road movie never manages to pick up speed and that its sequences falter in their own rhythm. Elsa Fernández-Santos of El País described a film capable of both the best and the worst, uneven and largely botched, though she acknowledged a beautiful epilogue and the courage to look to the future.

documents.title: Shark Bait
documents.tagline: Terror runs deep.
documents.overview: A group of friends enjoying a weekend steal a couple of jetskis racing them out to sea, ending up in a horrific head-on collision. They struggle to find a way home with a badly injured friend while from the waters below predators lurk.
documents.plot:
Shark Bait, also released under the title Jetski, is a 2022 British survival horror thriller directed by James Nunn from a screenplay by Nick Saltrese, a writer previously known for British television soap operas. Filmed in Malta and sold internationally by Altitude, it stars Holly Earl as Nat, with Jack Trueman as her boyfriend Tom, Catherine Hannay as Milly, Malachi Pullar-Latchman as Tyler and Thomas Flynn as Greg. The film runs 87 minutes.

Five young friends are enjoying their last spring break before graduation at a beach resort in Mexico. After a night of drinking and partying, during which the cautious Nat, the only one who speaks Spanish, ignores a local amputee's warning about what lurks in the water, the group steals two jet skis early in the morning and races them out to sea. A reckless game of chicken ends in a head-on collision: one machine is left capsized and abandoned, Greg suffers a badly broken leg, and the five end up crowded onto a single stalled jet ski drifting farther from shore. Because the craft were taken without permission while nobody was around, no one knows they are missing, and their only slim hope is that someone notices when they fail to board their flight home. Tensions boil over when it emerges that Milly slept with Tom behind Nat's back the night before. Tyler, despite a head injury, tries to swim for help, but a great white shark begins circling, and the predator toys with the survivors one by one as they search for a way to save themselves, leaving Nat to fight for her life in the final stretch.

Shark Bait was released in the United States on 13 May 2022 and on DVD and digital platforms in the United Kingdom on 6 June 2022. Reviews were mixed to negative. Jennie Kermode of Eye for Film was the most positive, praising an opening that pays intelligent tribute to Jaws, convincing shark footage, effective action and a predator presented as an animal with a mind of its own. Blueprint: Review found it handsome and well made, with a standout turn from Earl, but faulted its thin plot, unlikable characters and needless melodrama. In The Guardian, Phil Hoad gave it a scathing review, calling it a depressingly unimaginative thriller that lacks tension compared with Open Water or The Shallows and joking that the shark had more charisma than the cast.

documents.title: Fullmetal Alchemist: The Revenge of Scar
documents.original_title: 鋼の錬金術師 完結編 復讐者スカー
documents.tagline: The promised day is coming soon
documents.overview: The Elric brothers meet their toughest opponent yet — a lone serial killer with a large scar on his forehead.
documents.plot:
Fullmetal Alchemist: The Revenge of Scar (Japanese: Hagane no Renkinjutsushi Kanketsu-hen: Fukushūsha Scar) is a 2022 Japanese fantasy action film directed by Fumihiko Sori, who co-wrote the screenplay with Takeshi Miyamoto. Based on Hiromu Arakawa's manga, it is the sequel to the 2017 live-action Fullmetal Alchemist and the first half of a two-part finale, followed by Fullmetal Alchemist: The Final Alchemy in June 2022. Ryosuke Yamada returns as Edward Elric, with Atomu Mizuishi as Alphonse, Tsubasa Honda as Winry and Dean Fujioka as Roy Mustang, while Mackenyu plays the vengeful Scar. Announced as part of the manga's 20th-anniversary celebrations, it was meant to shoot in Italy like its predecessor, but because of the COVID-19 pandemic open sets were built in Kyonan, Chiba. Warner Bros. Japan released it on 20 May 2022, and it reached Netflix in August.

Travelling by train to Central City, Ed and Al meet Ling Yao (Keisuke Watanabe), a prince from Xing seeking the secret of immortality. When bandits hijack the train, the brothers fight them on the locomotive, are unexpectedly helped by the homunculus Envy, and use alchemy to stop a bomb plot. In Central they learn that a serial killer is murdering State Alchemists. Slipping away from their bodyguards, they meet May Chang, a girl from Xing, and are attacked by Scar, an Ishvalan who badly damages Al's armour and destroys Ed's automail arm before Mustang drives him off. While Ed returns to Resembool for repairs, he encounters his estranged father Van Hohenheim (Seiyo Uchino), and Scar recovers among Ishvalan refugees. Ling proposes an alliance to capture Scar and the homunculi, but the trap collapses: Winry learns that Scar killed her parents, a doctor couple, during the Ishval war and tries to shoot him, King Bradley (Hiroshi Tachi) wounds Ling's bodyguard Lan Fan, and Scar escapes with May. Riza Hawkeye tells Ed about the massacre of Ishval, in which Scar lost his brother. Later, when Al and May find Scar, Winry dresses his wound and he expresses remorse. In a final clash, the homunculus Gluttony swallows Ed, Ling and Envy, and inside his stomach Envy reveals that Gluttony is a failed Gate of Truth created by Father before transforming into a monstrous dragon.

The ensemble also includes Yuina Kuroshima as Lan Fan, Ron Monroe as May, Kokoro Terada as Selim Bradley, Yuki Yamada as Kimblee, Kanata Hongo as Envy and Jun Fubuki as Pinako Rockbell.

documents.title: Fullmetal Alchemist: The Final Alchemy
documents.original_title: 鋼の錬金術師 完結編 最後の錬成
documents.tagline: Hope is Unbreakable
documents.overview: The Elric brothers’ long and winding journey comes to a close in this epic finale, where they must face off against an unworldly, nationwide threat.
documents.plot:
Fullmetal Alchemist: The Final Alchemy (Hagane no Renkinjutsushi Kanketsu-hen: Saigo no Rensei) is a 2022 Japanese live-action fantasy action film directed by Fumihiko Sori, who co-wrote the screenplay with Takeshi Miyamoto, based on Hiromu Arakawa's manga. It is the third film in the live-action series and the second half of a two-part finale following Fullmetal Alchemist: The Revenge of Scar. Produced by Oxybot and distributed by Warner Bros. Japan, it stars Ryosuke Yamada as Edward Elric, with Atomu Mizuishi as his brother Alphonse, Tsubasa Honda as Winry Rockbell, Dean Fujioka as Roy Mustang, Misako Renbutsu as Riza Hawkeye, Kanata Hongo as Envy, Yuina Kuroshima as Lan Fan, Mackenyu as Scar, Hiroshi Tachi as King Bradley, Kokoro Terada as Selim Bradley, Chiaki Kuriyama as Olivier Mira Armstrong, Yukie Nakama as Trisha Elric and Seiyo Uchino as both Van Hohenheim and the villain known as Father.

Edward escapes from inside the homunculus Gluttony and, at the Gate of Truth, finds Alphonse's real body, which refuses to leave without its soul. Mustang and Hawkeye discover that King Bradley is the homunculus Wrath and that the military's generals are complicit, while the brothers learn that Father, a being who resembles Hohenheim, plans to open the Gate using a nationwide transmutation circle drawn by wars the army has orchestrated. Ed travels to the northern fortress of Briggs to seek General Olivier Armstrong's help, and Al finds their father, who reveals his past as a slave whose blood created a homunculus in a flask; that creature sacrificed the people of the ancient kingdom of Xerxes to gain a body and immortality. The heroes, joined by Scar, Ling and his possessed alter ego Greed, descend beneath Central City for a final confrontation. Father absorbs the souls of the country but is thwarted by Hohenheim, and in the ensuing battle Al sacrifices himself to restore his brother's arm. Ed defeats Father, then gives up his own alchemy to bring Al back whole, and the brothers return home to Winry.

The two-part finale was announced in March 2022 as part of the manga's 20th anniversary. Filming was originally planned in Italy, like the first film, but because of the COVID-19 pandemic it took place on an open set built in Kyonan, Chiba Prefecture. The Final Alchemy was released in Japanese theaters on 24 June 2022, five weeks after The Revenge of Scar, and became available worldwide on Netflix on 24 September 2022.

documents.title: The Chalk Line
documents.overview: After a couple finds a traumatized child of unknown origins, wife Paula must decipher the girl's strange behaviors to unlock her identity and dark past.
documents.plot:
The Chalk Line (Spanish: Jaula, meaning "Cage") is a 2022 Spanish mystery psychological thriller film directed by Ignacio Tatay in his feature debut and co-written by Tatay and Isabel Peña. Elena Anaya stars as a woman who takes in a mysterious young girl, with Pablo Molinero and Carlos Santos. It was released theatrically in Spain in September 2022.

Paula and her husband, Simón, live in an exclusive neighborhood of villas outside the city. Driving home one night, they find a little girl wandering alone in the middle of the road and take her to the hospital. She will not speak, and the only clue to her identity is that she responds to the name Clara. When no family can be found, her doctor suggests that a home environment might help, and Paula, who has bonded with the girl, persuades Simón to foster her temporarily. Clara will move only within boundaries chalked on the floor, so the couple draw lines throughout the house for her, and she reacts with terror when one is threatened, crying a strange word, "buma."

When a friend of Paula's swallows a shard of glass during breakfast, Simón suspects Clara put it there, and Clara is taken back to the hospital. Paula discovers that Clara understands German and realizes that "buma" means Buhmann, the bogeyman. Soon after, Paula herself chokes on a piece of glass, and Clara vanishes from the house, though she has never been seen to cross a chalk line. Paula becomes consumed by the search, alienating her friends and husband, who reveals that he knows she has been secretly undergoing fertility treatments. The police suspect her of instability after a call from Clara proves to have come from Paula's own phone.

Paula steals police files and finds a similar case: Ingrid, a Swiss teenager found dead and malnourished in France. A drawing by Clara leads her to suspect their friendly neighbor, Eduardo. In fact, Eduardo had abducted Ingrid as a child and kept her captive in his basement, where she gave birth to Clara, and it was he who released the girl onto the road and later planted the glass and took Clara back. Eduardo captures Paula in his basement, but she gives Clara a piece of chalk to hide and buys time for her to escape. Police eventually raid the house, and Clara is reunited with her grandmother, while Paula, now pregnant, moves to the city with Simón.

The film received mostly positive reviews, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 67% approval from nine critics, with one review calling it a memorable debut.

documents.title: Spirit Halloween: The Movie
documents.tagline: One Spirit. One Store. One Night.
documents.overview: A group of middle schoolers discover a Spirit Halloween store is haunted and must survive the night.
documents.plot:
Spirit Halloween: The Movie is a 2022 American fantasy comedy film directed by Sean McNamara and written by Sean McNamara, David Kirschner, and Chris McKenna. The movie follows the story of Ollie (played by Justin Long), a young man who returns to his hometown of Salem, Massachusetts, for Halloween.

Ollie's family has owned Spirit Halloween, a seasonal retail chain that sells Halloween decorations and costumes, for generations. However, when Ollie's father passes away, he leaves behind a mysterious will that reveals a shocking secret: the company is actually a front for an ancient curse that has been protecting Salem from supernatural forces.

The curse was placed by a witch named Winifred (played by Janina Gavankar), who was wronged by the town's founders. The curse can only be broken if Ollie, who is the last living heir of the company, can find and destroy the three magical artifacts needed to lift it.

As Ollie delves deeper into the mystery, he meets a group of allies, including a witch named Willow (played by Zoey Deutch) and a warlock named Rowan (played by Willa Amai). Together, they embark on a quest to find the artifacts, which are hidden in various locations around Salem.

Along the way, Ollie must confront his own destiny and the dark forces that have been manipulating him from the beginning. He also discovers that he has a special connection to the curse and the town's history, which makes him both the key to breaking it and the target of those who seek to keep it in place.

As the story unfolds, Ollie and his friends face numerous challenges and obstacles, including ghostly apparitions, magical creatures, and treacherous rival treasure hunters. In the end, they must work together to find the final artifact and break the curse before it's too late.

The movie features a blend of humor, action, and fantasy elements, with plenty of nods to classic Halloween movies and traditions. The film's visuals are also noteworthy, with a vibrant color palette and creative use of special effects to bring the supernatural world to life.

Overall, Spirit Halloween: The Movie is a fun and entertaining take on the Halloween genre, with a strong cast of characters and a compelling storyline that explores themes of identity, community, and the power of tradition.

documents.title: Last Seen Alive
documents.tagline: He'll stop at nothing to get her back.
documents.overview: After Will Spann's wife suddenly vanishes at a gas station, his desperate search to find her leads him down a dark path that forces him to run from authorities and take the law into his own hands.
documents.plot:
Last Seen Alive is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Brian Goodman from a screenplay by Marc Frydman, starring Gerard Butler, who also produced it, with Jaimie Alexander and Russell Hornsby. Shot under the title Chase, it follows a man who takes the law into his own hands to find his missing wife. It was released in the United States on June 3, 2022.

Will Spann, a wealthy real-estate agent, is driving his wife, Lisa, to her parents' house at a moment when their marriage is in trouble. While he fills the tank at a gas station, Lisa goes into the store for water and never comes back. Finding only her belongings, Will calls 911 and is told by Detective Paterson to wait, but instead he goes to Lisa's parents, Barry and Anna Adams, who have never fully trusted him and can tell him nothing. Back at the station, the clerk, Oscar, claims the security cameras are broken, but Will spots one that is working, fights Oscar for the recorder and hands it to the police. The footage shows Lisa leaving with a man before a passing truck blocks the view. Angered when Paterson asks about Lisa's life insurance, Will shows the video to her parents, who recognize their handyman, Knuckles.

Will tracks down and overpowers Knuckles, who admits that he delivered Lisa to a man named Frank and agrees to lead Will to his hideout. Forced to abandon his SUV, with the bound Knuckles in the back, when police pull him over, Will makes his way through the forest to Frank's camp, a run-down drug lab where he also finds Oscar. A gunfight leaves Frank and one of his men dead, apparently taking Lisa's location with them, while Paterson learns from Knuckles, who had been coerced by Frank, that Lisa is supposedly dead. When Oscar demands money for information, the drug lab explodes and kills him. As Paterson finds the grave Knuckles described empty, Will hears banging from a shed and discovers Lisa tied up but alive. Paterson later notes that some of the burned bodies had gunshot wounds, but chooses not to pursue it.

Butler plays Will, Alexander plays Lisa and Hornsby plays Paterson, with Ethan Embry as Knuckles, Michael Irby as Oscar and David Kallaway as Frank. Critics were dismissive, giving it 13% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and noting how closely its plot resembles the 1997 Kurt Russell thriller Breakdown. When it reached Netflix on October 1, 2022, however, it became the service's most-watched film in the United States and ranked in its top ten in many other countries.

documents.title: Hawa
documents.overview: A teenage girl lives with her grandmother and worries she will be removed by social services. She sets off to get adopted by someone she admires more than anything, one of the most powerful women in the world.
documents.plot:
Hawa is a 2022 French comedy-drama directed by Maïmouna Doucouré, her second feature after Cuties, written by Doucouré with Alain-Michel Blanc and Zangro, who also produced it through Bien ou Bien Productions for Amazon Prime Video. Newcomer Sania Halifa, discovered through an open casting call, plays the title role, with the Malian singer Oumou Sangaré as her grandmother Maminata, Titouan Gerbier as Erwan and Jérôme Pouly as Jackie; the singer Yseult and the astronaut Thomas Pesquet appear as themselves. According to Doucouré, the story is about wanting to rise above one's social class.

Hawa is a fifteen-year-old Parisian girl with albinism, thick glasses and a blonde afro, who is often bullied for her looks but never backs down. She lives with Maminata, a griot who sings stories in the oral tradition and hopes to pass that art on to her. The grandmother is terminally ill and is searching for a family to take Hawa in, while the girl, who earns money at a corner grocery, rejects every candidate and faces the prospect of a foster home. After reading that Michelle Obama is in Paris promoting her memoir Becoming, Hawa decides that the former First Lady, whose daughters have left home, would be the ideal adoptive mother. Riding her scooter across the city with help from her shy friend Erwan, she slips backstage at a rehearsal for a concert by Yseult, who is charmed by her nerve, steals an invitation to a gala, sneaks into a children's hospital to pitch herself to Obama, wins the support of Thomas Pesquet and finally makes her way through the luggage area of Charles de Gaulle Airport toward Obama's plane, while at home Maminata's health keeps declining.

Hawa premiered in the Platform section of the Toronto International Film Festival on 13 September 2022, also screened at the Calgary International Film Festival, and was released on Prime Video on 9 December 2022. Critics responded warmly. In Variety, Tomris Laffly called it a big-hearted, crowd-pleasing contemporary fable with a disarming sense of humor, praising Halifa's lived-in performance, Sangaré's screen presence and the tight structure. Decider's John Serba recommended it as an understated neo-fairy tale that skirts magical realism and ends on a moving finale, though he admitted its set pieces defy logic. French press reviews were positive, averaging 3.2 out of 5 on AlloCiné.

documents.title: Jennifer Lopez: Halftime
documents.tagline: It’s just the beginning.
documents.overview: Global superstar Jennifer Lopez reflects on her multifaceted career and the pressure of life in the spotlight in this intimate documentary.
documents.plot:
Jennifer Lopez: Halftime is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Amanda Micheli about the singer, actress and dancer Jennifer Lopez, with a particular focus on her performance at the Super Bowl LIV halftime show and her acclaimed role in the film Hustlers (2019). Produced by Lopez's manager Benny Medina and her producing partner Elaine Goldsmith-Thomas among others, it premiered as the opening night film of the Tribeca Film Festival on 8 June 2022 and was released on Netflix on 14 June 2022.

The film opens at Lopez's family party for her 50th birthday in July 2019 and follows her over the next six months. Behind the scenes, it tracks the awards campaign for Hustlers, which brought her the strongest reviews of her career after years of popular but critically derided comedies and her first Golden Globe nomination since Selena, along with her hopes for a first Academy Award nomination, which ultimately does not come. In parallel, it shows her preparing the halftime show of 2 February 2020 with her music director and choreographers, frustrated at having to share the brief slot with Shakira, and fighting the network executives to keep a segment with children in cages as a statement about the treatment of migrants at the border, a battle she wins. Glimpses of the past include her debut as a Fly Girl on In Living Color, her breakthrough in Selena, the video for "Waiting for Tonight" and her decision to wear again the Versace dress that caused a sensation at the 2000 Grammy Awards. She also reflects on the intense tabloid scrutiny of her private life, the obstacles she has faced as a Latina, and her views on the politics of the Trump era. The film closes with her performance at the inauguration of Joe Biden. Interviewees include Ben Affleck, Shakira, Hustlers director Lorene Scafaria, Constance Wu and Julia Stiles.

To coincide with the release, Lopez recorded "Same Girl (Halftime Remix)" with French Montana and a rendition of "This Land Is Your Land" and "America the Beautiful". The film debuted at number two worldwide on Netflix. Reviews were generally positive, with an 84% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Richard Roeper of the Chicago Sun-Times called it a solid, entertaining insider's look at her life, and The Detroit News found it inspirational, whereas Owen Gleiberman of Variety felt that, as a celebration of her success that avoids her personal life, it was too celebratory to have much drama.

documents.title: Beyond the Universe
documents.overview: While waiting for a kidney transplant, a young pianist finds an unexpected connection with her doctor — and the courage to fulfill her musical dreams.
documents.plot:
Beyond the Universe (Portuguese: Depois do Universo) is a 2022 Brazilian romantic drama written and directed by Diego Freitas and produced by Camisa Listrada. Singer Giulia Be makes her lead acting debut opposite Henry Zaga, with João Côrtes, João Miguel, Denise Del Vecchio, Leo Bahia, Viviane Araújo and Othon Bastos in supporting roles. The film premiered on Netflix on 27 October 2022, and within a day of its release it had entered the platform's global top ten of most-watched films.

Nina Soares is a gifted pianist who began playing at the age of eight and dreamed of joining a symphony orchestra. At fourteen she collapsed during an important recital and was diagnosed with lupus. Now a young adult, she learns that the disease has severely damaged her kidneys, which function at less than ten percent of their capacity. She is placed on the national transplant waiting list, behind thousands of other patients, and must undergo dialysis sessions lasting four hours, three times a week.

On the day she is due to begin treatment, Nina sees that the São Paulo Symphony Orchestra is looking for a piano soloist and decides to audition, despite her illness. She arranges to practise after hours at the conservatory where she teaches. One day, while she plays a public piano in a train station near the hospital, a young man named Gabriel, distracted by her music, crashes his bicycle into the instrument. Gabriel turns out to be a resident doctor at the hospital where Nina receives dialysis, known among patients for his warmth and good humour. A romance gradually develops between them, and Gabriel encourages Nina to pursue her dream of performing with the orchestra, even as her health becomes more fragile and the wait for a donor kidney grows more urgent.

The film is a sentimental love story about illness, hope and the pursuit of art, in the tradition of romantic dramas centred on young patients. It also draws attention to organ donation and to the long transplant waiting lists in Brazil.

Beyond the Universe was popular with Netflix audiences, while critics regarded it as a heartfelt but predictable romantic drama, praising the chemistry between its two leads.

documents.title: When Christmas Was Young
documents.overview: The story follows a headstrong music manager in desperate need of a hit song for his last remaining client, who finds himself falling for a gifted singer-songwriter with abandoned dreams of making it big, as he attempts to secure the rights to a Christmas song she wrote years ago.
documents.plot:
When Christmas Was Young is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Monika Mitchell for CBS, produced by Lighthouse Pictures and EveryWhere Studios with the singer-songwriter Sheryl Crow as an executive producer. Crow also wrote the film's music, including its title song. It stars Tyler Hilton as the music manager Luke Dawson and Karen David as Melody, with Meghan Heffern, Jordana Largy, Hayley Sales, Dhirendra, Jake Foy, Jayce Barreiro, Grace Sunar and Anastasia Bandey. Both leads are singer-songwriters in real life, and the casting reversed Hilton's usual screen persona: best known for playing the musician Chris Keller on One Tree Hill, he here plays the manager rather than the artist and does not sing, while David performs several songs.

Luke is a cocky, self-assured music manager who believes he is at the top of his game, though in truth his career is heading for disaster, he is lonely and he has only one client left, for whom he desperately needs a hit. He travels to Nashville to buy the rights to a Christmas song written years earlier by Melody, a gifted singer-songwriter and single mother who long ago gave up her dreams of making it big. Luke assumes the deal is a formality, but Melody firmly refuses to sell, and the two clash immediately. As he works to change her mind, Luke tries the charm that usually wins people over, yet none of it works on Melody, whose self-assurance and warmth take him by surprise. While she gradually comes out of her shell, the manager who is used to changing others finds himself changed, and with the rest of his life falling apart he begins to fall for her, even as he still needs her song.

The film premiered on CBS on 18 December 2022 and was made available on Paramount+. In interviews, Hilton said he was drawn by the chance to play a cocky man knocked down a peg and to work with Mitchell, a friend, and with Crow, a former label mate at Warner Bros. He and David described the experience as magical, recalling that they bonded over similar early careers in music, including rejections and changes of record deals and managers, and that each built a playlist to get into character, Hilton's leaning on George Thorogood. They also explained that they had to work to make their characters' initial antagonism convincing because they got along so well off screen.

documents.title: Aftersun
documents.tagline: Memory burns.
documents.overview: At a fading vacation resort, 11-year-old Sophie treasures rare time together with her loving and idealistic father, Calum. Twenty years later, Sophie’s tender recollections of their last holiday become a powerful and heartrending portrait of their relationship.
documents.plot:
Aftersun is a 2022 British drama film written and directed by Charlotte Wells. The movie premiered at the 2022 Toronto International Film Festival and received critical acclaim for its poignant portrayal of grief, love, and self-discovery.

The story revolves around Cal (played by Paul Mescal), a young man who accompanies his mother, Mary (played by Frankie Corio), on a family vacation to a Greek island. The trip is intended to be a relaxing getaway, but it becomes an opportunity for Cal to reconnect with his mother and confront the complexities of their relationship.

As they spend more time together, Cal begins to realize that his mother's behavior is not just a result of her age or health issues, but also a coping mechanism for her own emotional pain. Mary has been struggling to come to terms with the loss of her husband, who passed away a few years prior, and Cal's presence serves as a reminder of their shared grief.

Throughout the film, Wells employs a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between the present day and the summer of 1997 when Cal was a teenager. This technique allows the audience to witness the evolution of Cal and Mary's relationship over time, highlighting the ways in which they both grow and change.

As the vacation progresses, Cal becomes increasingly aware of his mother's emotional state, and he begins to take on more responsibility for her care. He also starts to explore his own desires and aspirations, including a budding romance with a young woman named Sophie (played by Celia Rowlson-Hall).

One of the most striking aspects of Aftersun is its use of music as a narrative device. The film features a soundtrack that perfectly captures the mood and atmosphere of each scene, from the upbeat pop songs of 1997 to the more introspective indie tracks of the present day.

The movie's climax is both heartbreaking and hopeful, as Cal comes to terms with his mother's mortality and finds a way to move forward despite her passing. The film ends on a bittersweet note, with Cal reflecting on the lessons he learned from his mother and the ways in which she continues to shape his life.

Overall, Aftersun is a powerful and moving exploration of love, loss, and self-discovery. With its nuanced performances, thoughtful direction, and evocative soundtrack, it's a film that will linger with audiences long after the credits roll.

documents.title: Gabriel's Inferno: Part IV
documents.plot: A captivating exploration of seduction, forbidden love and redemption: the passionate story of one man's escape from his own personal hell as he tries to earn the impossible, forgiveness and love.

documents.title: Dangerous Liaisons
documents.overview: The innocent Célène might be falling in love with popular surfer Tristan at her new school. But she has no idea that, in actuality, she’s the object of a cruel bet between Tristan and Instagram influencer Vanessa.
documents.plot:
Dangerous Liaisons (French: Les Liaisons dangereuses) is a 2022 French teen romantic drama directed by Rachel Suissa for Netflix, a modern adaptation of Pierre Choderlos de Laclos's 18th-century epistolary novel in which the letters of the original are replaced by Instagram posts and stories. Produced by Autopilot Entertainment, it stars Paola Locatelli as Célène and Simon Rérolle as Tristan, with Ella Pellegrini as Vanessa, Héloïse Janjaud as Célène's cousin Charlotte, Jin Xuan Mao as Tao and Alexis Michalik. The film runs 109 minutes.

The story opens on a dramatic night when both Tristan and Célène appear close to despair, with Tristan narrating that fame is power in the modern age, before flashing back to show how they got there. In Biarritz, Célène, a shy and studious seventeen-year-old who prefers literature to social media and is in a long-distance relationship, is starting at a new school, Victor Hugo High. There she meets Tristan, a champion surfer with 3.5 million Instagram followers, after he saves her dog from being run over by a driver livestreaming at the wheel. Tristan and Vanessa, the pampered child star of a film series who is afraid of becoming a has-been, present themselves online as a couple, but their relationship is a sham; the two cynics actually enjoy scheming to destroy other people's romances. Unaware that she is the object of a cruel bet between them, Célène falls for Tristan as he sets out to seduce her, manipulating those around her, including her friend Tao, a DJ and dealer, and her goofy cousin Charlotte. Preparations for the school musical, a costume party with spiked punch and a surfing lesson that ends in a romantic beach hut push the scheme forward, while Célène, who joins Instagram under a provocative handle, gradually discovers the power and cruelty of online fame.

Released on Netflix on 8 July 2022, the film drew mostly negative reviews. Decider's John Serba advised viewers to skip it, calling it a toothless social-media remake that pales beside the 1988 Stephen Frears film and Cruel Intentions, with a soft Tristan, an underwritten heroine and a drawn-out ending, though he praised Janjaud's spirited comic performance and the idea behind Vanessa's character. The New York Times and Firstpost likewise found its social-media update colorful but shallow and clichéd.

documents.title: 4 Horsemen: Apocalypse
documents.tagline: The end is here.
documents.overview: A small team of scientists must race against time to stop what seems to be a cascade of global disasters signaling the possible apocalypse and end of days.
documents.plot:
4 Horsemen: Apocalypse is a 2022 American science fiction disaster film directed by Geoff Meed and produced by David Michael Latt for The Asylum. Meed co-wrote the screenplay with Lauren Pritchard and Joe Roche, who also devised the story. Dominique Swain leads the cast as the military officer Bridget Norris, with Arie Thompson as the volcanologist Dr. Lynise Hughes, Eric St. John as Major Oakley Jones, Eva Ceja as the meteorologist Dakota Lenna and Brandon Alan Smith as the microbiologist Elliot Rodney.

The world is in an alarming state: famines caused by global warming, a new pandemic fueled by antibiotic resistance and escalating violence and unrest across the globe, followed by storms, volcanic eruptions, earthquakes and swarms of locusts. More and more world leaders fear that the cascade of disasters signals the coming apocalypse and the end of days. At the Pentagon, Norris is ordered to assemble a small team of specialists, Hughes, Lenna and Rodney, who are sent with a military peacekeeping force under the deeply religious Major Jones to the apparent epicenter of the catastrophes, a lake region in Brazil. Working from an abandoned observatory, the scientists determine that the eruptions originate beneath a central lake and are setting off a chain reaction around the world. Racing to learn whether the disaster can be stopped, and whether it is supernatural, Rodney improvises homemade bombs designed to wipe out the locust swarms by disrupting their oxygen, to be detonated by a gunshot fired from a moving helicopter, while others attempt to seal the volcanic lake by crashing a helicopter into it. Meanwhile, a fungus released by the volcano causes soldiers who inhale it to hallucinate and turn violent, and Jones believes he sees the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse riding across the sky.

Filmed in California, the film was released on video on demand in the United States on 29 April 2022 and reached German video stores that September. Reviews were poor. Moria Reviews gave it two stars, finding the concept awkwardly handled, with the supposed end of the world reduced to events around a single Brazilian lake, though it enjoyed the brief computer-generated glimpses of the Horsemen and Roche's inventive pseudo-scientific schemes. Film-rezensionen.de awarded it two out of ten, calling it boring because of its drawn-out dialogue, criticizing its failure to engage with the biblical background and calling it a typical cheap Asylum production.

documents.title: F*ck Love Too
documents.overview: In this romantic comedy, several friends, each dealing with unhappy love lives, turn to each other for help - but not always with the best results.
documents.plot: In this romantic comedy, several friends, each dealing with unhappy love lives, turn to each other for help - but not always with the best results.

documents.title: Must Love Christmas
documents.overview: A renowned romance novelist famous becomes involved in a love triangle between her childhood crush and a reporter.
documents.plot:
Must Love Christmas is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Martin Wood from a screenplay by Mark Amato. Produced by Brad Krevoy Television and the Motion Picture Corporation of America, it stars Liza Lapira as a reclusive romance novelist, with Neal Bledsoe, Nathan Witte, Ian Collins, Simone Bailly and Adam Beauchesne in supporting roles. The film premiered on CBS on 11 December 2022, as the network's second original Christmas film of the season after Fit for Christmas, and was also made available on Paramount+. It runs 85 minutes.

Natalie Wolf (Lapira) is an acclaimed author of Christmas love stories who is herself unlucky in love and has lived as a recluse since being burned by a journalist years earlier. Struggling with her latest novel, she follows her editor's advice to list the five qualities she wants in a partner and to get out and experience the world, agreeing to a book signing near Buffalo, her first public appearance in six years, on condition that she speaks to no journalists. Nick Winters (Bledsoe), a reporter for the magazine SHE, needs a major cover story to boost sales and stave off a merger with a rival publication, and sees the elusive author as the answer. Natalie recognises that he is no fan and rebuffs him. When a blizzard strands them both in the small town of Cranberry Falls, Natalie is stunned to be rescued by the tow-truck driver Caleb (Witte), her high-school crush and the model for the hero of her current book, who has organised the town's annual Dickens Festival, commemorating a stay by Charles Dickens at the local inn, and its toy drive. Joined by his photographer Lucas (Collins), a devoted fan of Natalie's books who begins a romance with her publicist Ryan (Beauchesne), Nick decides to chronicle her reunion with the one who got away without her help, only to find himself falling for her.

Reviews were favourable. Decider recommended streaming it, observing that the film began as a formulaic holiday romance but stood out by adding a love triangle, a second romance and Natalie's imagined scenes from her novels, playfully expanding the genre's conventions, and crediting its charming performers. Steve Gidlow of MediaVillage called it a refreshing take on a familiar story thanks to strong lead performances, and Lapira said she enjoyed playing a character far less self-assured than her role in The Equalizer.

documents.title: Blowback
documents.tagline: Be careful who you betray.
documents.overview: When a master thief is sabotaged during a bank heist and left for dead, he seeks revenge on his former crew one target at a time. Now, with the cops and the mob closing in, he's in the race of his life to reclaim an untold fortune in cryptocurrency from those who double-crossed him.
documents.plot:
Blowback is a 2022 American action crime thriller film directed by Tibor Takács from a screenplay credited to Matthew Eason, Robert Giardina and Robert Edward Thomas. Produced by Premiere Entertainment Group and distributed by Saban Films, it stars Cam Gigandet as a thief seeking revenge on the crew that betrayed him, with Randy Couture, Michele Plaia, Louis Mandylor, William McNamara, Benjamin Abiola, Rafael Cabrera, Chris Maher and Texas Battle in supporting roles. Set in Las Vegas, the film was released in June 2022. It is rated R for violence, drug use and language and runs 93 minutes.

Nick (Gigandet), a rideshare driver, has a teenage daughter (Melissa Diaz) who is gravely ill in hospital, and whose only chance of survival is an experimental treatment that his insurance and meagre earnings cannot cover. Through a contact at a bank, he learns of a valuable delivery and plans an inside job. He reconnects with his former girlfriend Veronica (Plaia), whose boyfriend Jack (Couture), the main investor in her gym and a hardened criminal, connects him with a crew of thieves; with his tech-savvy friend Xander (Abiola) also on board, the group is told to stick to the plan and that nobody will get hurt. The robbery goes largely as planned, but afterwards Jack's men shoot Nick, leave him for dead and take the stolen case, which holds hard drives containing millions of dollars in cryptocurrency. Patched up by a disgraced, drug-addicted doctor (McNamara) living in an RV, Nick sets out to recover the fortune and take revenge on his former crew one target at a time, enlisting the help of the mobster who owns the case, while Detective Cooper (Mandylor) leads a police investigation that keeps closing in on the trail of violence.

Reviews were generally negative. Roger Moore of Movie Nation found it a routine, bloody and slow-footed cops-and-robbers tale whose cryptocurrency angle threatened to date it instantly; he thought the leads were not bad but that the script was fatally flawed, particularly in handing Nick a "gangster ex machina" who solves his problems for him. Peter Gray of The AU Review called it a generic, disposable heist film that hit every expected beat yet had an odd watchability, largely thanks to Gigandet's sympathetic performance. Mark Dujsik of Mark Reviews Movies wrote that it consisted almost entirely of plot, with characters too thin even to count as archetypes.

documents.title: South Park the Streaming Wars
documents.overview: Cartman locks horns with his mom in a battle of wills while an epic conflict unfolds that threatens South Park’s very existence.
documents.plot:
"South Park: The Streaming Wars" is a 2022 American adult animated comedy television special written and directed by Trey Parker. The third South Park special made for Paramount+, it was released on June 1, 2022, and counts as the 318th episode of the series. Voices include Parker, Matt Stone, April Stewart and Kimberly Brooks.

Denver is suffering a severe drought caused by ManBearPig, and as streams dry up, protesters, including waterpark owner Pi Pi, are told that the city's water is going to agriculture. In South Park, Stan Marsh and Tolkien Black worry about Stan's father, Randy, who quarrels with Tolkien's father, Steve. Eric Cartman, unhappy about living in an abandoned hot dog stand, notices a house being built across the street for golf course owner Talnua Cussler and urges his mother, Liane, to get breast implants to attract him. She refuses, reminds him that he is the one who made her quit her job, and tells him the surgery would cost $10,000.

Steve learns he can sell part of his water if it reaches Denver's reservoir, so at Stan and Tolkien's suggestion they build a small boat and float it downstream. The test works, and Steve begins selling subscriptions to his "streaming service", with Pi Pi among his customers. When a jealous Randy wants boats too, Stan and Tolkien recruit Kyle, Kenny and Butters, and finally Cartman, after he claims his mother needs surgery without saying what kind. Cussler orders 10,000 boats for $15,000, covering the cost, but when Cartman presents the surgery to Liane, she holds firm, unmoved even when he threatens to have it done himself.

Steve hears from a dying real estate agent that land near the streams has been sold to a wealthy buyer. When Randy and Stan visit Cussler to end the deal, they find him killed by ManBearPig. At his waterpark, Pi Pi refuses to give up his streaming rights and reveals that he is working with the commissioner and ManBearPig, who stabs Steve and throws him down a water slide. Pi Pi then betrays the commissioner, plotting to replace Denver's water with his park's urine-tainted water. At school, Cartman arrives with breast implants, Tolkien learns his father is missing, and as Denver wastes its dwindling water, Randy begins investigating.

It stems from Parker and Stone's $900 million deal, announced in 2021, for 14 Paramount+ projects, which the creators called specials rather than films. Bubbleblabber rated it 9 out of 10, praising its gags and forward-looking satire.
