As the night spirals out of control, Dom sends wave after wave of increasingly dangerous hired guns. He has Ray kidnapped and confronts him personally, but Ray manages to escape. Ana enlists the help of her old friend Mimi and Mimi's husband, Tom, and together the group fights off the soldiers Dom has hired. Forced to work together and confront the lies in their marriage, Ray and Ana turn the tables on their enemies: Ray disguises himself as one of the gunmen in order to get close to Dom, and with Ana's help he eliminates the mob boss, saving their restaurant and their lives.

Reviews were moderately positive, with a 64% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from a small sample of critics. Variety's Joe Leydon called it a hoot, Comic Book Resources described Johnson's performance as a pleasant surprise amid forgettable action B-movies, and MovieWeb praised its slick fight scenes and amusing supporting characters while noting its thin premise.

documents.title: The Perfumier
documents.overview: To regain her sense of smell and get back her lover, a detective joins forces with a perfume maker who uses deadly methods to create the perfect scent.
documents.plot:
The Perfumier (German: Der Parfumeur) is a 2022 German crime thriller film written and directed by Nils Willbrandt and produced by Moovie and Constantin Television for Netflix. Very loosely inspired by Patrick Süskind's novel Perfume, it stars Emilia Schüle as Sunny, a police detective who has lost her sense of smell, and Ludwig Simon as Dorian, a perfume maker obsessed with creating the scent of love. The supporting cast includes Sólveig Arnarsdóttir, Anne Müller, Robert Finster and August Diehl.

Sunny is investigating the murders of two women whose bodies were dismembered to remove their sweat glands. At the same time she is consumed by her affair with the married Juro and desperate to keep her sensual hold on him, a struggle made harder by her inability to smell. In the course of the investigation she encounters Dorian, a suspect who is trying to distill the essence of love even if it means drawing on gruesome sources, and she suspects that he may hold the key to restoring her lost sense. When she discovers that one of his compounds has an irresistible effect on Juro, she cannot resist using it. The detective and the suspected killer enter an uneasy partnership in which Dorian tries to help Sunny regain her sense of smell through both physical and psychological methods, seeking to unlock something buried inside her. Dorian, who admits he has never known love, wonders whether he can still create it, and the film explores the links between scent, desire and obsession through surreal, neon-lit imagery, with Sunny narrating the story in voice-over throughout.

The Perfumier was released on Netflix on 21 September 2022. Critics were largely negative, and the film holds a low Rotten Tomatoes score. Marshall Shaffer of Decider called it a confusing, frustrating mix of crime drama, erotic thriller and character study that never makes smell feel real or urgent, though he credited Schüle with a committed performance that makes the most absurd elements plausible. Lori Meek of Ready Steady Cut found it boring and nonsensical, criticizing the relentless narration, one-dimensional characters and pretentious visual style, and noted that the plot shares little with Süskind's book beyond a killer obsessed with scents, recommending the 2006 film Perfume: The Story of a Murderer as a better adaptation.

documents.title: Saguaro
documents.tagline: Movin’ on
documents.overview: Paul, a teenager in Arizona, tries to repair his relationships before moving to Oregon at the end of the summer.
documents.plot: Paul, a teenager in Arizona, tries to repair his relationships before moving to Oregon at the end of the summer.

documents.title: A Christmas to Treasure
documents.overview: The passing of a beloved old neighbor reunites six friends for a hometown holiday treasure hunt, where sparks fly once again between brand strategist Austin and his former best friend Everett.
documents.plot:
A Christmas to Treasure is a 2022 American Christmas romantic comedy television film written and directed by Jake Helgren and produced by The Ninth House. It stars Taylor Frey and Kyle Dean Massey, with Katie Walder, Mary-Margaret Humes, Roberto Aguire, Nikki McKenzie, Cort McCown, Norman Towns and Autumn Federici in supporting roles. The film premiered on Lifetime on 16 December 2022 and runs about 90 minutes.

Austin Craig (Frey), a quick-witted brand strategist, works with his childhood friend Tipper Tisdale (Walder), and the pair are close to landing an event that could take their business to the next level when each receives a mysterious letter from Mrs. Marley, a beloved old neighbour who has recently died. Growing up, Mrs. Marley and her husband opened their large house to the neighbourhood children, hosting an annual Candy Cane Carnival and a Christmas treasure hunt every year, and in her letter she invites the six childhood friends to reunite in their hometown of Belleville for one last hunt. Her death has hit Everett Matthews (Massey), Austin's former best friend, especially hard, since he cared for her in her final years. While he is decorating her old house for Christmas on his own, their friend Ricky Treviño (Aguire) brings the bad news that the house will be sold to a land developer and turned into a ski resort unless Everett can raise $200,000. Everett is determined to find Mrs. Marley's buried treasure to save it, while Austin hopes to use part of the money to build his company. As the friends, including Michelle Wu (McKenzie) and the professional basketball player Clay King (Towns), follow her clues and contend with a scheming estate agent, Rochelle Raimo (Federici), Austin and Everett revisit their complicated history, including Everett's painful coming out, and the old sparks between them reignite.

Decider recommended the film, calling it "a lot of movie", with a larger lead cast and bigger premise than most holiday television films, but praising the multi-faceted, lived-in characterisations of the principal characters, Frey's snarky yet cuddly Austin, and a memorable fast-talking bluffing scene for Walder. The reviewer found the elaborate Marley backstory distracting and felt that two of the friends were underused, but concluded that the film understood that the most important parts were its small, intimate details.

documents.title: 13:14: The Challenge of Helping
documents.tagline: If a natural disaster affected your country, what would you do?
documents.overview: On September 19, 2017, at 1:14 p.m., an earthquake devastated Mexico City and its environs. Immediately, citizens mobilized to help, including the actor and youtuber Juanpa Zurita who quickly organized a group of friends that included singers, actors, content creators and other celebrities from the world of entertainment who helped him raise funds for the reconstruction of the city.
documents.plot:
13:14: The Challenge of Helping (Spanish: 13:14: El reto de ayudar) is a 2022 Mexican documentary film directed by Santiago Fábregas and produced by Amazon Studios, 3Pas Studios and Arco Entertainment Media for Prime Video. It is fronted and produced by the actor and YouTuber Juanpa Zurita, with Eugenio Derbez among its producers, and features Pambo, Lele Pons, Sofía Niño de Rivera, Pati Chapoy, Montserrat Oliver, Juca Viapri, Chloe Campero, Mikel Arreola and other figures from entertainment and social media. Axel Pedraza was the cinematographer and Amado López composed the music. The film runs 89 minutes under the tagline "If a natural disaster affected your country, what would you do?"

The title refers to the moment, 1:14 p.m. on 19 September 2017, when an earthquake devastated Mexico City and its surroundings. As citizens mobilised to help, Zurita quickly organised a group of friends, including singers, actors, content creators and other celebrities, to raise money for reconstruction through the Love Army México initiative, and the project set out to build fifty homes for families affected by the quake in Ocuilan, in the State of Mexico. Through interviews, phone calls, video meetings and footage from the site, the film follows the troubled process that followed over the next four years: disagreements among the organisers, the discovery that construction costs exceeded commercial prices, money running out, and Zurita having to contribute his own funds, until 47 houses were finally delivered and the original goal was acknowledged as unmet. It also responds to accusations in the press that the donations had been mishandled, with media figures and friends of Zurita speaking in his defence.

The documentary premiered on Prime Video in September 2022 and drew a largely negative critical response in Mexico. Alejandro Badillo of Neotraba described it as an example of the white saviour complex, arguing that it used the people of Ocuilan as a backdrop to clear Zurita's name. Ernesto Eslava of Por si alguien preguntaba called it manipulative, noting that the affected residents speak for only a few minutes and that it never explains how the money was spent or the beneficiaries chosen, and the film critic Kristoff Raczynski, as reported by Milenio, dismissed it as one of the worst documentaries he had seen.

documents.title: Tom and Jerry Snowman's Land
documents.tagline: Ready...Set...Snow.
documents.overview: It’s time to chase that holiday spirit with Tom and Jerry! With magic in the air, Jerry and his nephew, Tuffy, make a snow mouse that miraculously comes to life! To keep their new friend, Larry the snow mouse from melting, Tuffy and Jerry must race him to the fabled Snowman’s Village. In hot pursuit, Tom and devious Dr. Doublevay have their own plans for Larry’s magic.
documents.plot:
Tom and Jerry: Snowman's Land is a 2022 American animated Christmas direct-to-video film starring the classic cat-and-mouse duo. Produced by Warner Bros. Animation and Turner Entertainment, with animation by Renegade Animation in the United States and Slap Happy Cartoons in Canada, it features the voices of Carlos Alazraqui, Kimberly Brooks, Joey D'Auria, Regi Davis and Laraine Newman, with archival recordings of William Hanna for the title characters. It was released digitally on November 15, 2022, and on DVD on November 29, 2022.

In the snowy town of Goodberry, Tom and Jerry are up to their usual antics until Tom gets into trouble with his owner, the greedy Dr. Doublevay. Jerry lives with his kindly owner, Mrs. LePage, who is struggling financially and tries to make ends meet by selling little snow mice to children, a business Jerry helps with. Jerry's young nephew Tuffy, however, dreams of putting on a magic show, an idea Jerry dismisses. Disappointed, Tuffy goes outside and builds a snow mouse of his own to help the family. To his amazement, the snow mouse magically comes to life, and the two quickly become best friends. Tuffy names his new companion Larry and introduces him to Jerry, who is reluctant but agrees to let him stay.

Larry soon proves surprisingly helpful, recovering money for Mrs. LePage after Tom ruins her savings. But as time passes, Larry begins to melt. To save him, Tuffy and Jerry set off on a journey to bring him to the fabled Snowman's Village, a magical place where living snow creatures can survive. Tom and Dr. Doublevay have plans of their own for the remarkable snow mouse and follow the mice throughout their adventure, setting traps and causing havoc along the way. When Jerry and Larry rescue Tom from one of the traps meant for them, the cat has a change of heart. Upon reaching the Snowman's Village, Tom saves the mice, and the four join forces to defeat Doublevay. In gratitude, Tom moves in with Tuffy, Jerry and Mrs. LePage, and the new family celebrates together whenever Larry comes back to visit.

The film continued Warner Bros.' long-running series of direct-to-video Tom and Jerry features. Common Sense Media gave it three stars out of five, noting that it is cute and less violent than some earlier entries, though the story is nothing new, and Geek Vibes Nation called it an enjoyable, lighthearted holiday entry for the duo.

documents.title: Capturing the Killer Nurse
documents.overview: Charlie Cullen was an experienced registered nurse, trusted and beloved by his colleagues at Somerset Medical Center in New Jersey. He was also one of history’s most prolific serial killers, with a body count potentially numbering in the hundreds across multiple medical facilities in the Northeast.
documents.plot: Charlie Cullen was an experienced registered nurse, trusted and beloved by his colleagues at Somerset Medical Center in New Jersey. He is also one of history’s most prolific serial killers, with a body count potentially numbering in the hundreds across multiple medical facilities in the Northeast.

documents.title: The Redeem Team
documents.tagline: Everything to lose. Everything to prove.
documents.overview: Using unprecedented Olympic footage and behind-the-scenes material, The Redeem Team tells the story of the US Olympic Men's Basketball Team’s quest for gold at the 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing following the previous team’s shocking performance four years earlier in Athens.
documents.plot:
The Redeem Team is a 2022 American sports documentary directed by Jon Weinbach, who was also involved in the production of The Last Dance. It chronicles the 2008 United States men's Olympic basketball team and its campaign at the Beijing Summer Olympics to restore American dominance in international basketball after the team's disappointing bronze medal finish at the 2004 Athens Olympics. The film was produced by Greg Groggel and Diego Hurtado de Mendoza, with executive producers including Frank Marshall, Mike Tollin, Dwyane Wade and LeBron James.

After a series of embarrassing defeats in international competition, culminating in the bronze medal in Athens, American basketball was widely seen as having lost its aura of invincibility. The documentary follows the effort to rebuild the national program and reclaim the gold medal, an undertaking that required the country's biggest stars to commit to playing together and subordinate their egos to the team.

Featuring prominent players such as Kobe Bryant, LeBron James and Dwyane Wade, the film traces the team's preparation, challenges and triumphs on the way to the Beijing Games. It highlights the transformation of the team's culture under head coach Mike Krzyzewski, who emphasized discipline, teamwork and a commitment to excellence,. Combining archival footage, interviews with players and coaches, and behind-the-scenes access to the team during the 2008 Olympics, the documentary builds toward the team's pursuit of the gold medal in Beijing. The film's soundtrack includes music by DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince, Jadakiss and Public Enemy.

The documentary presents the team's victory not only as a sporting comeback but as a source of national pride during a turbulent period for the United States. Weinbach has said that at the time there was little optimism about America's place in the world and that people were looking for things to feel good about.

The Redeem Team was released on Netflix on October 7, 2022. It received positive reviews, with 93 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 76. The Guardian described it as blending sports storytelling with a sense of patriotic renewal, framing the gold medal as both athletic redemption and collective healing.

documents.title: Wildcat
documents.overview: Back from war in Afghanistan, a young British soldier struggling with depression and PTSD finds a second chance in the Amazon rainforest when he meets an American scientist, and together they foster an orphaned baby ocelot.
documents.plot:
Wildcat is a 2022 American documentary film directed by the photojournalist Trevor Frost and Melissa Lesh about animal rescue work in the Peruvian Amazon. It premiered at the 2022 Telluride Film Festival and was released in theaters on 21 December 2022 by Amazon Studios before streaming on Prime Video. In 2023, it won the Emmy Award for Outstanding Nature Documentary.

The film follows Harry Turner, a young British army veteran who suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder after serving in Afghanistan. Struggling to find his footing after leaving the military, he travels to a remote part of the Amazon rainforest in Peru, where he meets Samantha Zwicker, an American wildlife biologist who runs a project rescuing animals threatened by poaching and habitat destruction. The documentary also explores Zwicker's own troubled personal history and her driven, sometimes fraught approach to her mission.

At the heart of the film is the pair's effort to raise an orphaned baby ocelot named Khan and prepare him to survive on his own in the jungle. Turner devotes himself completely to the animal, living alongside him, teaching him to hunt and gradually encouraging his independence, and the bond becomes a lifeline for the young veteran. But before Khan is old enough to be released, he is killed by an illegal shotgun trap set by poachers, a loss that devastates Turner and plunges him back into crisis. A year later, Turner and Zwicker take on another baby ocelot, Keanu, and this time succeed in raising him to the age at which he can return to the wild. The film also follows a visit from Turner's family, drawing parallels between his devotion to his younger brother and the care he gives to the ocelots, and charts the strain that the work and their own traumas place on the relationship between Turner and Zwicker.

The film was assembled from footage gathered over several years in the rainforest. Wildcat received largely positive reviews, holding a 92 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 49 reviews; the site's consensus noted that, although it raises uncomfortable ethical questions, the film is an affecting testament to the healing power of bonds between species. Stephen Farber of The Hollywood Reporter called it a riveting journey into the wild, while noting that it leaves questions about its subjects' relationship unanswered.

documents.title: Play Dead
documents.tagline: Some things are worse than death.
documents.overview: Criminology student Chloe fakes her own death to break into a morgue, in order to retrieve a piece of evidence that ties her younger brother to a crime gone wrong. Once inside, she quickly learns that the fearsome Coroner uses the morgue as a front for a sick and twisted business. As a frightening game of cat and mouse ensues, Chloe will discover that the scariest thing about the morgue is not the dead, but the living.
documents.plot:
Play Dead is a 2022 American horror thriller directed by Patrick Lussier and written by Simon Boyes and Adam Mason. Bailee Madison stars as Chloe Albright, a criminology and forensics student, with Anthony Turpel as her brother T.J., Chris Lee as Ross and Jerry O'Connell as a coroner with a terrible secret.

Chloe and T.J. have lost their father, whose death was ruled a suicide, voiding his life insurance, and debts are about to cost them their home. T.J. believes he has found a solution: he and his friend Ross, Chloe's ex-boyfriend, plan a robbery with a fake gun. Ross goes into the store while T.J. waits behind the wheel, but the owner opens fire, Ross is shot down and T.J. flees. But Ross's phone, now held by police, contains evidence that will incriminate T.J. Desperate to keep her brother out of prison, Chloe comes up with a daring plan. She injects herself with a drug that slows her vital signs until she appears dead, so that she will be taken to the morgue, where the phone has been logged as evidence.

The plan works until Chloe discovers that the coroner on duty is a cold-blooded killer. He runs a lucrative sideline harvesting and selling organs and body parts from the dead, and he justifies it as a way of ridding society of its "bottom feeders". Strapped to a gurney, Chloe is told that everything she is and has done is worth less than the sum of her parts. Trapped inside the locked building with no easy escape, she must outwit him in a cat-and-mouse game through examination rooms, corridors and underground passages.

In May 2022, Voltage Pictures pre-sold the film to buyers at the Cannes Film Festival. Critics acknowledged the implausibility of the premise but found the film tense and effective. Phil Hoad of The Guardian gave it three stars out of five, praising Madison's performance as a determined final girl and especially O'Connell's controlled turn as the sharpest tailored killer since Patrick Bateman, calling the film "a terrible advert for organ donation but a compact and resourceful thriller." Adam Sweeting of The Arts Desk wrote that despite its low budget the film never felt cheap. He praised Lussier's assured pacing and described O'Connell's coroner as a chilling embodiment of the banality of evil.

documents.title: BTS: Permission to Dance on Stage - LA
documents.original_title: BTS: PERMISSION TO DANCE 온 스테이지 – LA
documents.overview: Purple colors the city of Los Angeles, as BTS brings their "Permission to Dance" concert to SoFi Stadium for the first time in two years. In a stadium radiating anticipation and cheer, splendid performances from "On" to "Permission to Dance" glorify the stage that now comes to life on screen. Be united once again by the power of music.
documents.plot:
BTS: Permission to Dance on Stage – LA is a 2022 South Korean concert film directed by Sam Wrench and Junsoo Park, recorded during the boy band BTS's four sold-out shows at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, in late November and early December 2021. The shows formed part of Permission to Dance on Stage, a twelve-date series of stadium concerts held with and without live audiences in place of a conventional tour, and the film features the members, among them Kim Nam-joon (RM), Kim Seok-jin (Jin), Min Yoon-gi (Suga), Jung Ho-seok (J-Hope) and Park Ji-min.

After the COVID-19 pandemic forced the cancellation of their Map of the Soul Tour, BTS, the top-grossing touring act of 2019, had spent nearly two years performing only to online audiences. The Los Angeles concerts were the band's first performances in front of an in-person crowd since 2019, and the film captures the reunion between the group and its fans, known as ARMY. Running about two and a half hours, the show opens with the members emerging from a cage for a marching-band version of "On", followed by "Fire", "Dope" and "DNA". Slower songs such as "Blue and Grey" and "Black Swan", performed with dancers in white-feathered sleeves, lead into a medley of "Blood Sweat & Tears" and "Fake Love" on a set inspired by their music videos, complete with waterfalls and giant sculpted hands. The band sings "Life Goes On" on a giant bed and then an oversized sofa, plays live-band versions of "Boy with Luv", "Dynamite" and "Butter", and performs B-sides including "Airplane pt. 2", "Silver Spoon", "Telepathy" and "So What", before an encore that builds to "Permission to Dance". Individual nights featured special guests, with Megan Thee Stallion joining a remix of "Butter" and Coldplay's Chris Martin performing "My Universe" with the group.

The four SoFi Stadium shows grossed $33.3 million from 214,000 tickets, according to Billboard the biggest box office total for any act in nearly a decade and the highest-grossing engagement of 2021, making BTS the first non-English-language act to pass $30 million in a single engagement. Critics praised the concerts, with Consequence calling them "four days of pure joy" and listing them among the best live shows of 2021. The film premiered on Disney+ worldwide as a surprise release on 8 September 2022, during the service's annual Disney+ Day event.

documents.title: Selena Gomez: My Mind & Me
documents.tagline: Every breath, a breakthrough.
documents.overview: After years in the limelight, Selena Gomez achieves unimaginable stardom. But just as she reaches a new peak, an unexpected turn pulls her into darkness. This uniquely raw and intimate documentary spans her six-year journey into a new light.
documents.plot:
Selena Gomez: My Mind & Me is a 2022 American documentary film directed by Alek Keshishian that follows the singer and actress Selena Gomez over a period of six years. Produced by Lighthouse Management + Media and Interscope Films, it documents her struggles with her physical and mental health following her diagnoses of lupus and bipolar disorder, and features Gomez herself along with her close friend of more than a decade, Raquell Stevens.

The project began around 2015, after Keshishian directed the music video for Gomez's song "Hands to Myself". He has said that he had no interest in making a traditional pop documentary and wanted to show something more authentic, a goal Gomez shared, and that he had no idea at the outset that the film would become a six-year labor of love.

The documentary opens at a moment when Gomez has achieved enormous fame. Behind the glamour of concerts, tours and publicity, however, she is suffering from exhaustion, anxiety and depression, and an unexpected turn pulls her into darkness. Shot in an intimate, diary-like style, the film follows her through periods of crisis and recovery: the cancellation of a world tour, her treatment, her efforts to understand her illnesses and the slow process of learning to live with them. It shows her returning to her roots in Texas, revisiting people and places from her childhood, and travelling to Kenya for a charitable project, while she reflects on the pressures of growing up in the public eye. Much of the film is narrated through Gomez's own words, including passages from her journals, presenting an unvarnished portrait of a star trying to reconcile her public image with her private reality.

Critics noted that, unlike many music documentaries designed to burnish a celebrity image, the film operates in a rawer register, with Gomez trying to communicate honestly rather than perfectly, and it was praised for its transparency about mental health.

My Mind & Me premiered on the opening night of AFI Fest at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Hollywood on November 2, 2022, and was released on Apple TV+ and in select theaters two days later. Its trailer debuted on World Mental Health Day, and the song "My Mind & Me", heard over the end credits, was released as a single. It received positive reviews, with 97 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 68; The New York Times called it an honest portrait of stardom and mental illness.

documents.title: I'm Glad It's Christmas
documents.overview: An aspiring Broadway singer is convinced to participate in a small-scale production for her local Christmas celebration. Along the way, she finds hope and unexpected mentorship towards her dream career. But will her professional success come at the cost of her chance at love?
documents.plot:
I'm Glad It's Christmas is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas musical romance television film directed by Ernie Barbarash from a screenplay by Joel Canfield, Lisa Canfield and Steve Gottfried. Produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America, Brad Krevoy Television and Hideaway Pictures with Northern Ontario Film Studios, and listed for a time under the title Someday at Christmas, it stars Jessica Lowndes, Paul Greene and the soul singer Gladys Knight, with Teagan Sellers, Peggy Prud'homme and Sierra Wooldridge. It premiered on the Great American Family channel on 26 November 2022 and runs 85 minutes.

Holly (Lowndes) moved to New York five years earlier to pursue a career on Broadway. She has made it into the chorus a couple of times but has never landed a leading role, since casting directors love her voice but always find her too young, too old, too tall or too short. By day she works in a retail shop, where she sings as she works and some customers admit they come in just to hear her. One morning on her way to work she literally bumps into Jason (Greene), a father who writes jingles for local commercials and hopes to move up to national advertising campaigns. Holly's voice catches the attention of Cora (Knight), a property entrepreneur who owns the building that houses the shop and who wants to revive a community Christmas show that was a local tradition for decades. Convinced that Holly is the perfect voice to showcase, Cora pairs her with Jason to debut a new Christmas song he has written. As the two refine the song and their performance, and Holly bakes cookies with Jason's daughter Angela (Sellers), whose custody he shares, they discover they have more in common than music. Both are reluctant to get involved, however: Holly plans to leave New York if she has not landed a role by the end of the year, and Jason worries that Angela is growing attached to her, while Cora's encouragement offers Holly unexpected mentorship toward her dream career.

Reviews were mixed. Kristen of TV Tweetie found it enjoyable, cute and solid, praising Lowndes's amazing voice, Greene's performance and the special pleasure of hearing Knight perform, though she felt some of the heroine's decisions were out of character. Cassandra Morgan called the singing gorgeous and Knight a joy but considered the script weak and the plot boring, citing the underused Angela, who keeps leaving scenes, and a running joke about Holly's scarf that is quickly dropped.

documents.title: The Hip Hop Nutcracker
documents.overview: Features Rev Run as he brings audiences on a hip-hop reimagining of The Nutcracker ballet set in NYC.
documents.plot:
The Hip Hop Nutcracker is a 2022 American holiday dance special released on Disney+ that adapts the long-running stage production of the same name, a reimagining of Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker set to a remixed version of his score. Directed for the screen by Nikki Parsons and Elizabeth Avellan, it is emceed by the legendary Rev Run and features the dancer Mikhail Baryshnikov and the dance crew Jabbawockeez alongside Cache Melvin as Maria-Clara, Allison Holker and Stephen Boss as her parents, Comfort Fedoke as Drosselmeyer, Fik-Shun Stegall as a nut vendor and Jean Sok as the Mouse King.

The story moves the classic tale to a contemporary New York setting. The only thing young Maria-Clara wants for Christmas is for her mother and father, who once lit up the dance floor together, to reunite. Her wish might come true thanks to Drosselmeyer, a mysterious toy shop owner and wizard played as a voguing figure in a red cape, a vendor of nuts and a little midnight magic, while the Mouse King tries to stand in the way. Rather than dialogue, the plot is carried mostly by brief narrative captions and by the dancing itself, with Rev Run contributing rapped verses. The choreography tours roughly forty years of hip-hop dance, including breaking, voguing, turfing, popping and locking, while keeping traditional ballet in the mix. Sets include a row of brownstones that serves as the backdrop for the Baryshnikov and Jabbawockeez number, dreamlike expressionist designs and a combination nightclub and soda shop that replaces the ballet's Land of Sweets, where the moves and fashions of successive decades of hip-hop are celebrated.

The special premiered on Disney+ on 25 November 2022. Brett White of Decider recommended it, finding that the filmed version captured the kinetic energy of the stage show without feeling like a static recording, praising the sets, Fedoke's captivating Drosselmeyer and the way the special brings decades of hip-hop dance history into viewers' homes, and suggesting it would delight young dancers. He noted that the stage production predates Hamilton by several years and that a full-length filmed version of the stage show was also available to stream through PBS. Other reviewers praised the dancing while criticizing the editing and camera work.

documents.title: Aníkúlápó
documents.tagline: He who has death in his pouch.
documents.overview: It tells the story of Saro, a man seeking for greener pasture, but unfolding events and his affair with the king's wife, he encounters his untimely death and with Akala, a mystical bird believed to give and take life.
documents.plot: After an affair with a queen leads to his demise, an eager traveler encounters a mystical bird with the power to give him another life.

documents.title: Grimcutty
documents.tagline: Feed the frenzy.
documents.overview: A suburban teen girl and her little brother must stop a terrifying internet meme brought to life by the hysteria of their parents.
documents.plot:
Grimcutty is a 2022 American monster horror film written and directed by John Ross and produced by 20th Digital Studio and Capture. Sara Wolfkind stars as the teenager Asha Chaudhry, with Shannyn Sossamon and Usman Ally as her parents, Leah and Amir, and Callan Farris as her younger brother Kamran. The film was released in October 2022 on Hulu in the United States, on Star+ in Latin America and on Disney+ in other territories.

Asha is a teenager who spends much of her time online, where she runs a YouTube channel devoted to ASMR videos. Her parents, Amir and Leah, are increasingly anxious about what their children are exposed to on the internet. When news spreads of a viral online challenge involving a sinister figure known as the Grimcutty, which supposedly urges children to harm themselves and others, local parents are swept up in panic. Amir and Leah react by restricting their children's access to phones and computers and monitoring them closely, convinced that the meme poses a real danger.

Asha insists that the Grimcutty is simply a hoax amplified by frightened adults, but strange events soon begin to suggest otherwise. A gangly, menacing creature resembling the figure from the meme starts appearing to teenagers in the neighborhood, attacking them, while the adults blame the violence on the challenge itself. Asha discovers that the monster has been brought to life by the collective fear of the adults who believe in it, and that their attempts to protect their children only make it stronger. With her parents refusing to listen and blaming everything on the internet, Asha teams up with her little brother Kamran to find a way to destroy the Grimcutty before it claims more victims, while trying to make the adults understand the real source of the threat.

The film was inspired by the Momo Challenge, an internet moral panic about a supposed suicide game that peaked in 2019 and was widely regarded as a hoax. Grimcutty received generally negative reviews, with a 22 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Some reviewers found its satirical premise about parental panic clever, and Mike Mack of Laughing Place called it a fine watch, while others felt the execution was slow and underdeveloped.

documents.title: Matriarch
documents.tagline: The mother of all evil.
documents.overview: Afflicted with a mysterious disease after surviving an overdose, a woman returns to her childhood home to confront her personal demons but instead discovers a real one.
documents.plot:
Matriarch is a 2022 folk horror film written and directed by Ben Steiner in his feature debut, expanding on his 2018 short film Urn. Jemima Rooper stars as Laura, a troubled executive, and Kate Dickie as her estranged mother, Celia, with Sarah Paul as Abi, Simon Meacock as Leonard, Nick Haverson as Gerald and Celinde Schoenmaker as Katrin. The film mixes psychological drama about the damage done by bad parenting with supernatural and body horror.

Laura lives in the city and works in a high-pressure executive job. She struggles to sustain relationships and relies on cocaine and alcohol to cope with stress. After a near-fatal overdose, and suffering from a strange illness that causes her body to ooze a black liquid, she reaches a breaking point and accepts an invitation from Celia, from whom she has long been estranged, to return to her childhood home in a rural village. Her questions about the cause of their estrangement, and whether her mysterious condition might be hereditary, hang over the visit.

The homecoming offers little comfort. Something is wrong with the village, whose residents behave strangely, are sometimes unwelcoming and seem unnaturally youthful, while the relationship between mother and daughter grows more strained and toxic as Laura is forced to confront her childhood traumas. Encounters with a former flame and old neighborly grudges complicate her stay, and hints of pagan ritual and a strange conspiracy surround Celia. As Laura gradually uncovers the truth about her mother's hold over the community and the black substance connected to it, the slow-building folk horror erupts into a third act of gruesome body horror, shocking surprises and dark rituals.

Matriarch was released on Hulu in the United States and on Disney+ in the United Kingdom on October 21, 2022, as part of Hulu's Halloween programming. It holds an 85% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Noel Murray of the Los Angeles Times praised the way it shifts between the physical threat of dark supernatural forces and the harm done by a lifetime of bad parenting, and Starburst called it a slowly simmering powder keg mixing human drama with touches of Cronenberg and The Devils. Meagan Navarro of Bloody Disgusting, awarding two and a half skulls out of five, praised Rooper and Dickie and its striking imagery but found it overly ambitious and its resolutions unsatisfying, while Ben Kenigsberg of The New York Times called the dark, barely legible finale a letdown.

documents.title: Detective Knight: Rogue
documents.overview: As Los Angeles prepares for Halloween, mask-wearing armed robbers critically wound detective James Knight’s partner in a shootout following a heist. With Knight in hot pursuit, the bandits flee L.A. for New York, where the detective’s dark past collides with his present case and threatens to tear his world apart…unless redemption can claim Knight first.
documents.plot:
Detective Knight: Rogue, also released simply as Knight, is a 2022 American action thriller directed by Edward John Drake from a screenplay by Drake and Corey Large. The first of three Detective Knight films, it stars Bruce Willis as James Knight, a veteran Los Angeles police detective, with Lochlyn Munro, Jimmy Jean-Louis, Beau Mirchoff and Large. Produced by Large, Randall Emmett and George Furla, it was released by Lionsgate in limited theaters and on demand on 21 October 2022, and was among Willis's final films before he retired from acting following a diagnosis of aphasia.

In Los Angeles, four masked criminals, Casey, Mercer, Mike and Sykes, rob an armored truck carrying cash. In the shootout that follows, Knight's partner, Fritz, is badly wounded, and the robbers escape to New York. Officer Sango explains that similar heists have been taking place across the country, and that an aircraft belonging to Winna, a former bookie who runs a New York shell company, has been present in every city where a robbery occurred.

In New York, Casey's wife confronts him about his substance abuse and changes in personality, and he promises to change. He takes one more job from Winna: stealing a valuable sports card from a high-security auction, which he plans without the volatile Mercer. Knight and Sango question Winna, who refuses to talk, but his bodyguard gives them Casey's name and warns them to stay away. Knight recognizes Casey as a former American football player and tracks him down, while the gang discovers that Winna was once a confidential informant who helped Knight find the man who killed his father. As the auction heist goes wrong and tensions within the gang erupt, Knight, haunted by his past and willing to bend the rules, closes in on the robbers and the man behind them, leading to violent confrontations.

The film received mostly negative reviews, with a 43 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on seven reviews. Anton Bitel criticized its lack of substance, and Jeffrey Anderson of Common Sense Media, rating it two out of five, called it one of the better of Willis's low-budget action films but noted the uncomfortable vacancy where its star should be. It was followed by Detective Knight: Redemption and Detective Knight: Independence.

documents.title: Christmas on Candy Cane Lane
documents.overview: Ivy Donaldson struggles with her mom's shadow, Muriel, the Christmas darling of Icicle Falls. She is now separated from her husband Rob and tries her best with her daughter, but after a series of strange but comical events everybody gets together in unexpected but festive ways.
documents.plot:
Christmas on Candy Cane Lane is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas comedy television film directed by Christie Will Wolf from a screenplay by Teena Booth, adapted from the novel of the same name by Sheila Roberts, the eighth book in her Icicle Falls series. Produced by the Motion Picture Corporation of America, Brad Krevoy Television and Candace Cameron Bure's company Candy Rock Entertainment, with Bure as an executive producer, it stars her Full House and Fuller House co-star Andrea Barber, with Dan Payne and Kerensa Cooper. The film premiered on the Great American Family channel on 3 December 2022 and runs 85 minutes.

In the small town of Icicle Falls, one street, Candy Cane Lane, is famous for going all out at Christmas, and its residents are expected to decorate their houses lavishly and welcome crowds of visitors. Ivy Donaldson (Barber) has found the season hard since the death a few years earlier of her mother, Muriel, the town's beloved queen of Christmas, who owned a Christmas shop and headed the committee that ran the street's festivities. Feeling it was her duty to carry on, Ivy took over the shop and moved into her mother's house to keep the Candy Cane Lane traditions alive, but she cannot escape constant comparisons with her mother. The pressure of living up to Muriel's standards has strained everything in her life: she is now separated from her husband Rob (Payne), and their teenage daughter Jordan (Cooper) is tired of their lives revolving around the neighbourhood's activities. As the holidays approach, someone starts tampering with the candy cane decorations across the street, and a series of strange but comic mishaps, including Ivy and Rob dressing up as Mr. and Mrs. Claus, brings the family back together in unexpected and festive ways, as Ivy learns to follow her own dreams rather than carry a legacy that has become a burden.

Reviews were unenthusiastic. Kristen of TV Tweetie found it cute but "kind of meh", praising the striking Claus costumes, the performances of Payne and Cooper as a husband and daughter hoping to reunite the family, and its message about letting go of traditions that are burdens rather than gifts, though she felt Barber's acting style was very familiar. Cassandra Morgan advised against watching it, arguing that it had a good premise but tried to be a comedy, a romance and a mystery at once without letting its slapstick jokes land.

documents.title: The Trapped 13: How We Survived The Thai Cave
documents.original_title: 13 หมูป่า: เรื่องเล่าจากในถ้ำ
documents.overview: In this compelling documentary, members of the Thai youth soccer team tell their stories of getting trapped in Tham Luang Cave in 2018 — and surviving.
documents.plot: In this compelling documentary, members of the Thai youth soccer team tell their stories of getting trapped in Tham Luang Cave in 2018 — and surviving.

documents.title: Burning Patience
documents.overview: Mario is a young fisherman who dreams of becoming a poet. He gets a job as the postman to Pablo Neruda when the legendary writer moves there after being exiled from Chile.
documents.plot:
Burning Patience (Spanish: Ardiente paciencia) is a 2022 Chilean romantic drama directed by Rodrigo Sepúlveda from a screenplay by Guillermo Calderón, based on Antonio Skármeta's novel, which had already inspired Skármeta's own 1983 film and Michael Radford's Il Postino (1994). Produced by Fábula, it was the first Chilean film produced by Netflix. Andrew Bargsted stars as Mario and Vivianne Dietz as Beatriz, with Claudio Arredondo as the poet Pablo Neruda, Paola Giannini as Beatriz's mother Elba, Amalia Kassai as Clarita, Rodolfo Pulgar as Cosme, Pablo Macaya as Jorge, Trinidad González as Elvira and Giordano Rossi as Julio.

The story is set in 1969 on the coast of Chile at Isla Negra, where Neruda lives, hoping to devote his later years to writing while being pressed by supporters to run for president. Mario, a young man barely out of his teens who tells his father he has no interest in continuing the family's fishing tradition, takes a job at the post office because he owns a bicycle, and becomes the postman for a single client, the famous poet, whose thoughts he constantly interrupts. Mario falls for Beatriz, a newcomer who works at the inn and cantina run by her mother, but Elba fiercely opposes the romance, warning her daughter against men who seduce with words. To win Beatriz over, Mario writes her love letters, but he plagiarizes Neruda's poems, and since everyone in Chile knows the poet's verses by heart, she catches him. The two begin exchanging notes through a young nun, with Beatriz challenging Mario to express himself as a real poet, and later send messages through the dedications of the local radio station, while Neruda mentors the young man in metaphor and love.

Netflix announced the project with Fábula in November 2021; Boris Quercia was initially reported as director before Sepúlveda took over. Filming began on 4 April 2022 in Isla Negra, the village of Neruda's favorite house. The film premiered in the Galas section of the Mar del Plata International Film Festival in Argentina in November 2022 and was released on Netflix on 7 December 2022. Reviews were mildly positive. Roger Moore of Movie Nation called it a lightly charming romance that works on its own terms and finishes wonderfully, singling out Giannini's disapproving mother, but felt it never surpasses Il Postino and missed a more larger-than-life Neruda. Other critics similarly found it sweet and pleasant but unremarkable.

documents.title: Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
documents.original_title: Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
documents.overview: Join the likes of Tatiana Maslany, Mark Ruffalo, Tim Roth, and Benedict Wong as they reveal how Marvel Studios’ She-Hulk: Attorney at Law was conceived and shaped. Discover what it took for She-Hulk’s creators to pull off the show’s tricky tone and deliver Marvel Studios’ first truly comedic series – one that boldly breaks the fourth wall to acknowledge its own audience, no less!
documents.plot:
Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law (2022) is a documentary series that delves into the creation and production of the popular Disney+ show She-Hulk: Attorney at Law. At its core, the series explores the themes of identity, empowerment, and self-discovery.

The documentary sheds light on how the show's protagonist, Jennifer Walters, navigates her journey from being a lawyer to becoming the superhero known as She-Hulk. The series highlights how the character's transformation is not just physical but also emotional, as she grapples with her newfound powers and the responsibilities that come with them.

Throughout the documentary, it becomes clear that the show's creators aimed to explore themes of female empowerment and self-acceptance. Jennifer Walters' journey serves as a metaphor for the struggles women face in patriarchal societies, where they are often expected to conform to societal norms and expectations. The series shows how She-Hulk's character defies these expectations, embracing her uniqueness and using her powers to challenge the status quo.

The documentary also touches on the theme of identity, particularly in the context of Jennifer Walters' complicated relationship with her father, Bruce Banner. Their dynamic serves as a microcosm for the complexities of family relationships and the struggles that come with navigating one's own identity.

Ultimately, Marvel Studios Assembled: The Making of She-Hulk: Attorney at Law presents a powerful exploration of what it means to be a strong, empowered woman in a world that often seeks to constrain her. Through Jennifer Walters' journey, the series shows how embracing one's true self can lead to transformation and growth, both personally and professionally.

documents.title: It's a Wonderful Binge
documents.tagline: It's the most wonderful high of the year.
documents.overview: Like the original film, the sequel is set in a near future where all drinking and drugs are banned except for on one glorious day known as The Binge. This year, that day happens to miraculously land on Christmas.
documents.plot:
It's a Wonderful Binge (originally titled The Binge 2: It's a Wonderful Binge) is a 2022 American Christmas comedy film written and directed by Jordan VanDina. A sequel to the 2020 Hulu film The Binge, itself a comic riff on The Purge, it stars Dexter Darden and Eduardo Franco, with Zainne Saleh, Marta Piekarz, Tim Meadows, Kaitlin Olson, Danny Trejo, Nick Swardson, Tony Cavalero, Patty Guggenheim, Paul Scheer and Karen Maruyama. Produced by LD Entertainment and American High, it was shot mainly in Syracuse, New York, in February 2022, and was released on Hulu on 9 December 2022 with a TV-MA rating.

In a near future where drink and drugs are banned on every day but one, known as the Binge, the authorities move the annual day of indulgence from spring to Christmas Eve. Friends Hags (Darden) and Andrew (Franco) are fired from their jobs as costumed mascots at a children's fun centre. Hags plans to propose to his girlfriend Sarah (Saleh), whose father Keegan (Meadows) is overprotective, and must then recover the engagement ring her grandmother (Maruyama) gave him after it is accidentally donated to an orphanage. Andrew, overwhelmed by his loud, dysfunctional family, wanders through town wondering what the world would be like had he never been born, until an "Angel" (Trejo) shows him alternative realities, in sequences that turn to black and white in homage to It's a Wonderful Life. Meanwhile Kimmi (Piekarz), Andrew's love interest, is sent by her mother, Mayor Spengler (Olson), who is trying to keep the Binge out of her tidy Christmas party, to catch her Christmas owl after it escapes and eats a bag of drugs, while her uncle Kris (Swardson) turns up unannounced, having broken out of jail in a stolen police car. Scheer plays a newscaster whose live reports grow stranger as the night goes on, and Cavalero returns as Pompano Mike. The film features several original songs, including the carollers' "Worst/Best Christmas Ever".

Like its predecessor, the film received generally negative reviews, holding a 25% rating on Rotten Tomatoes from twelve reviews. Alex Maidy of JoBlo called it a bad movie and an even worse comedy, and John Serba of Decider found it sloppy, though he enjoyed Trejo and the claymation homage. Alex Reif of Laughing Place was more positive, calling it a funny, edgy adults-only alternative to typical holiday fare, and Bill Goodykoontz of The Arizona Republic gave it two and a half stars.

documents.title: Cici
documents.overview: A family migrates to the city after a tragic loss. When they reunite in their hometown 30 years later, buried emotions and painful secrets resurface.
documents.plot:
Cici is a 2022 Turkish drama film written and directed by Berkun Oya and produced by Krek Film for Netflix. It stars Yılmaz Erdoğan as the patriarch Bekir, Nur Sürer and Funda Eryiğit as his wife Havva in later and earlier life, Okan Yalabık as their son Kadir, Ayça Bingöl as their daughter Saliha, Fatih Artman as the youngest son Yusuf, Olgun Şimşek as Cemil, İncinur Daşdemir as Yusuf's wife and Şevval Balkan as Saliha's daughter Naz. Yağız Yavru was the cinematographer, and the film, which uses no background score, runs 151 minutes.

Moving between several timelines, the film opens on a farm in the Turkish countryside decades earlier, where Bekir rules his family with an iron fist. His wife Havva resents his infidelity and the harshness with which he treats their children: he regularly slaps his eldest son Kadir, keeps the children out of school and records them with a video camera, while Saliha secretly meets Cemil, a boy with a remarkable singing voice who works on the farm, and young Yusuf is his father's favourite. After a particularly cruel punishment of Kadir, Bekir falls ill, and following the family's loss they move to the city. Some thirty years later Kadir, now a filmmaker, returns to the old house to shoot a film drawn from his childhood memories, recreating episodes such as the day his father punished him with a hosepipe. When the production stalls he stays on, and during the COVID-19 pandemic the family is reunited under the same roof: Havva, now suffering from dementia, has been released from her care home into Saliha's care, Saliha is divorced with a teenage daughter, and Yusuf, married with a son, is unhappy and frustrated that the farm has not been sold. As Kadir excavates their past, old tensions revive, Cemil and Saliha confront their unspoken romance, and painful family secrets come to light.

The film was released on Netflix on 27 October 2022. Marshall Shaffer of Decider recommended it as a modest meta-movie in the tradition of 8½, praising its exploration of the borders between reality and fiction and singling out Sürer's performance, while finding it overlong. Akash Deshpande of High on Films admired Yavru's photography and sound but found its shifts into comedy jarring, and Lori Meek of Ready Steady Cut praised the performances but called it a slow melodrama whose relationships remained underexplored.

documents.title: Entergalactic
documents.tagline: Love will find us all.
documents.overview: Ambitious artist Jabari attempts to balance success and love when he moves into his dream Manhattan apartment and falls for his next-door neighbor.
documents.plot:
Entergalactic is a 2022 American adult animated musical romantic comedy created by the musician and actor Kid Cudi as a visual companion to his album of the same name. Initially announced as a television series, it was redeveloped as a feature-length special and directed by Fletcher Moules, with Kenya Barris among the producers. Cudi voices Jabari, with Jessica Williams as Meadow, Timothée Chalamet, Ty Dolla Sign, Laura Harrier, Vanessa Hudgens, Christopher Abbott, 070 Shake and Teyana Taylor. It premiered on Netflix on 30 September 2022, the same day the album was released.

Jabari is a charming, streetwear-loving artist in New York City who is on the verge of real success. Mr. Rager, the character he has spray-painted on walls throughout the city, has been chosen to be developed into a comic book, and Jabari moves into a stylish new apartment in Manhattan to celebrate. Shortly after the move he meets his neighbor Meadow, a cool, independent photographer who documents the city's streets.

The two are instantly drawn to each other, and their relationship blossoms through playful encounters, late-night conversations and shared passion for their art. However, Jabari is still entangled with his ex, Carmen, and is uncertain whether he can balance his budding career, the pressure of his new comic and his friendships with the demands of a serious relationship. Meadow, meanwhile, is wary of being hurt again. With advice from his friends, including his stoner neighbor Len, Jabari must decide whether he can make room for love in his life. Throughout the story, the narrative is punctuated by musical sequences set to songs from Cudi's album, in which the characters' emotions are expressed through bold colors, surreal imagery and dreamlike visual effects.

Entergalactic received positive reviews, with critics praising its vibrant animation, which blends 2D and 3D styles in a manner reminiscent of Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, its soundtrack and its warm portrayal of a Black romance in New York. Some found the story slight compared with its visual ambition. Its release alongside the album made it one of the most ambitious music-driven animated projects of the year.

documents.title: The Holiday Sitter
documents.tagline: Say guncle.
documents.overview: Sam is a workaholic bachelor who babysits his niece and nephew before the holidays when his sister and her husband have to go out of town. Completely out of his element, he recruits help from their handsome neighbor Jason and finds himself in an unexpected romance.
documents.plot: Sam is a workaholic bachelor who babysits his niece and nephew before the holidays when his sister and her husband have to go out of town. Completely out of his element, he recruits help from their handsome neighbor Jason and finds himself in an unexpected romance.

documents.title: As Good as Dead
documents.tagline: A violent past. A man on the edge.
documents.overview: An ex-cop in self-imposed witness protection in Mexico becomes a target when a fight video of his apprentice goes viral.
documents.plot:
As Good as Dead is a 2022 Mexican-American martial arts action crime film directed by R. Ellis Frazier and written by Michael Jai White, who also stars alongside Tom Berenger. The supporting cast includes Luca Oriel, Guillermo Iván, Gabriela Quezada, Louis Mandylor, Michael Copon and Gillian White. Produced by Odyssey Motion Pictures, Badhouse Studios Mexico and Jaigantic Studios, it was released in the United States in theatres and on video on demand on 16 December 2022 and runs 88 minutes.

Bryant (White), a reclusive former police officer living in self-imposed witness protection in Mexico, works by day as an unremarkable surveyor and spends his free time training outside his trailer in the desert, which doubles as a heavily fortified bunker. Oscar (Oriel), a bullied teenager in Nogales who looks after his younger siblings, secretly mimics Bryant's moves from a distance to learn to fight, and Bryant eventually takes him under his wing as a martial arts mentor, teaching him a distinctive defensive style while warning him never to use it in public. Complications arrive when Oscar's gangster brother Hector (Iván) is released early from prison and wants to cash in on Oscar's new skills at a local gym run by the father of Marisol (Quezada). Furious that Oscar has brought his criminal brother to his home, Bryant cuts the boy off. When Oscar wins his first fight, phone footage of his unusual technique goes viral and reaches the imprisoned corrupt policeman Sonny Kilbane (Berenger) and his crooked lawyer Piro (Mandylor), who send heavily armed mercenaries after Bryant. As his dangerous past catches up with him, Bryant is forced into a life-and-death struggle to clear his name, save Oscar and reclaim what he left behind, forging an uneasy alliance and bantering with Hector while fighting through waves of henchmen.

The film holds a 71% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from seven reviews. Alan Ng of Film Threat rated it 8 out of 10, calling it a fun, 1990s-style indie action film and Karate Kid homage with a simple David-and-Goliath story and a varied range of set pieces. Brent McKnight of The Last Thing I See gave it a C+, describing a convoluted but briskly paced, self-aware and playful B-movie with solid action, while noting its cheap, schlocky production. Jennifer Green of Common Sense Media awarded it two stars out of five.

documents.title: Christmas Class Reunion
documents.overview: High school classmates, who once dubbed themselves the “cursed class,” reconnect at Christmas for their 15-year reunion. Over the course of their time reconnecting, the classmates challenge each other to remember who they were, who they are, and who they want to be.
documents.plot:
Christmas Class Reunion is a 2022 Canadian Christmas romantic comedy-drama television film directed by Jonathan A. Rosenbaum from a screenplay by Erin Rodman, produced by Lighthouse Pictures for Hallmark Channel. Adapted from Paul E. Wootten's book of the same name, it stars Aimee Teegarden as Elle and Tanner Novlan as Devin, with Dejan Loyola, Maya Ford, Stephanie Bennett, Marshall Williams, Dylan Archambault, Yasmeen Kelders as Devin's daughter Skylar and Andy Thompson. The film runs 84 minutes; it marked Novlan's first Hallmark role, after he had become known for playing John Finnegan on the soap opera The Bold and the Beautiful.

Elle, a former class valedictorian who has become a powerhouse in the tech industry, is the class president of a group of high school classmates who once dubbed themselves the "cursed class" after a run of disasters stretching back to their senior winter formal and continuing through their previous reunions. Determined to break the bad luck, she meticulously plans their fifteen-year reunion at Christmas, only to find that much of it depends on Devin, the former class clown and vice-president, whose events company is supplying the equipment and who had not intended to attend. When fire and water damage leaves them scrambling for a new venue, the two opposites work together to find another location, and Elle comes to appreciate the spontaneous approach to life of Devin, a single father devoted to his teenage daughter and his business. At the same time her career unravels when the CEO of her company, whom she cannot reach, is reported to be under FBI investigation. Elle had also hoped to reconnect with her high school crush, Kam, but spending time with him shows her that what she wanted at seventeen is not what she needs now. Alongside them, classmates including Sam, a successful broadcaster who still feels invisible, and a pair of high school sweethearts going through a rough patch challenge one another to remember who they were, who they are and who they want to be.

The film premiered on Hallmark Channel on 10 December 2022 as part of its Countdown to Christmas season. Alonso Duralde of TheWrap ranked it 33rd of the network's 43 new holiday films of 2022, crediting a valiant attempt at a different kind of storytelling and an appealing cast but finding it undermined by contrivances and illogical character choices. Kristen of TV Tweetie called it predictable and ho-hum, though she liked Novlan.

documents.title: Five More Minutes: Moments Like These
documents.original_title: Five More Minutes: Moments Like These
documents.overview: The second holiday story inspired by Scotty McCreery’s song “Five More Minutes,” a young widow’s Christmas wish for her son is answered in unexpected ways when she returns to their old home for the holidays.
documents.plot:
Five More Minutes: Moments Like These is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas fantasy drama television film directed by Kevin Fair from a screenplay by Andy Sandberg. The second holiday film inspired by Scotty McCreery's country song "Five More Minutes", following the 2021 Five More Minutes, it was produced by Front Street Pictures, Johnson Production Group and Take Five Productions. It stars Ashley Williams and Lucas Bryant, with Brady Droulis and Lane Edwards. The film premiered on Hallmark Movies & Mysteries on 17 December 2022 and runs 84 minutes.

Four years after her husband Brian (Edwards) died in a car accident, Kaitlyn (Williams) is raising their ten-year-old son Adam (Droulis) alone in Los Angeles, having moved away from Colorado because she could not bear to stay without him. Adam has grown increasingly withdrawn, retreating into video games. A regular client offers Kaitlyn a tempting job, but it would mean relocating to London. For Christmas she takes Adam back to Brian's family in the Colorado town of Hollowford to prepare their beloved, long-empty house for sale, wishing she could have five more minutes with her husband. At a local Christmas fair she meets Matthew (Bryant), a handsome former schoolmate and friend of Brian's, and they hit it off, but their budding relationship suffers when she learns he failed to disclose that he represents a large company that wants her house and land. His apology and his warm bond with Adam restore her trust, and he helps her fix up the house. Meanwhile, Adam has brief encounters every few days with a series of progressively older boys who mysteriously vanish, but not before drawing him into friendships, charity work and community life. When Kaitlyn agrees to sell and move to London, Adam, who wants to stay, pulls away, and in the basement she realises that the boys were Brian's spirit returning to help their son, before Brian appears and they share five minutes together.

The film was generally well received. TheWrap ranked it 14th of Hallmark's 43 new Christmas films of 2022, crediting Williams with injecting wit and life into a story that could have been a sappy bummer and praising her palpable chemistry with Bryant. Rebekah's Readings and Watchings gave it 8 out of 10, praising Williams's toned-down turn and the child actor. Cassandra Morgan found it more realistic and emotional than its predecessor, though she felt Adam was a little too good and the story too divided between mother and son.

documents.title: Undercover Holiday
documents.tagline: He's the kind of bodyguard you take home to your home.
documents.overview: When returning home for the holidays, newly minted pop star Jaylen tells her protective family that Matt is her new beau, when in reality, he’s her overzealous security guard.
documents.plot:
Undercover Holiday is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy-drama television film produced by Cineflix Productions for Hallmark Channel. It stars Noemi Gonzalez as the pop star Jaylen and Stephen Huszar as her bodyguard Matt, with Mishka Thébaud, Ann Pirvu, Diana Salvatore, Amanda Martínez, Juan Chioran and Allison Feliciano. The film runs 84 minutes and was promoted with the tagline "He's the kind of bodyguard you take home to your home."

Jaylen's life has changed dramatically since she won a singing competition and became one of the hottest new pop stars in the country. The attention has also brought her a stalker, and her record label hires Matt, a former Navy SEAL, to protect her. When she returns home for the holidays to her large, multi-generational family, the Rodriguezes, Jaylen knows that her loving but overprotective relatives, who already consider Los Angeles an unsafe place, would be alarmed to learn that she needs a security guard. She therefore introduces Matt as her new boyfriend and insists that he keep up the charade throughout the visit. The deception proves awkward for both of them: in addition to spending time with friends and family, Jaylen has a series of publicity events to attend, which makes Matt's job harder, and the serious, overzealous bodyguard struggles to relax as she wants him to while pretending to be in love. Staying with her family, Matt, a man used to a solitary life, gets to experience a Christmas full of warmth and family traditions, and comes to appreciate the support Jaylen enjoys. In turn, he helps her see that she should take control of her career rather than let her label dictate her music, as she wants to release songs in both English and Spanish despite the company's resistance. As the fake relationship continues, the two must decide whether to keep things strictly professional or admit to feelings that have become real.

The film premiered on Hallmark Channel on 4 December 2022. Reviews were lukewarm. Alonso Duralde of TheWrap, ranking all 43 of Hallmark's new Christmas films of 2022, placed it 32nd, describing it as a Hallmark fake-boyfriend movie crossed with The Bodyguard whose results were middling. Kristen of TV Tweetie enjoyed Jaylen as a strong, independent heroine who stands up to her family and label, and liked the depiction of the Rodriguez family's Christmas traditions, but found the film slow and unoriginal and did not recommend it.

documents.title: 'Twas the Night Before Christmas
documents.tagline: Raise the curtain. Lift your spirits.
documents.overview: A former actress trying to break into directing tests her skills with a town’s annual Christmas Eve courtroom production in which the true authorship of the famous poem “A Visit from St. Nick” is debated.
documents.plot:
'Twas the Night Before Christmas is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film directed by Gary Yates, who co-wrote the screenplay with C. Jay Cox. Produced by Muse Entertainment, it stars Torrey DeVitto and Zane Holtz, with Shawn Ahmed, Amanda Barker, Tanisha Thammavongsa, Richard Waugh, Shaun Austin-Olsen, Sophie Bastelle and Jennie Esnard in supporting roles. The film premiered on the Hallmark Channel on 17 December 2022 as part of its Countdown to Christmas season, and runs 84 minutes.

Madison Rush (DeVitto), an actress eager to reinvent herself and move into directing, especially in the theatre, has co-written a play for a town's annual Christmas Eve production: a mock courtroom trial to decide the true authorship of the famous poem "A Visit from St. Nicholas", better known as "'Twas the Night Before Christmas", which is traditionally credited to Clement Clarke Moore (Austin-Olsen) but also claimed for Major Henry Livingston Jr. (Waugh). To draw audiences she recruits her friend and former co-star Connor Avery (Holtz), a charming actor who trained as a lawyer, acts to pay the bills and is a devoted father to his daughter, and who soon talks his way into the bed and breakfast where she is staying. Madison insists she does not date actors, but Connor keeps hinting that she was his favourite on-screen kiss. As the producer keeps throwing her curveballs, her co-writer has to leave for Los Angeles and the ghosts of Livingston and Moore turn up to argue their cases, Madison, who believes returning to the stage is what her late father would have wanted, struggles to hold the show together. When the troublesome lead actress, Lena (Bastelle), drops out the night before the performance, Connor and her friends help Madison see that she should play the lead herself, realising that she does not have to choose between acting and directing, and that she can date an actor after all.

TheWrap ranked it 10th of Hallmark's 43 new Christmas films of 2022, saying that although it tried to embrace many ideas, it somehow came together thanks mainly to the chemistry between DeVitto and Holtz. Erin E. Gross of Fangirlish also praised the leads' great on-screen chemistry and Madison's growth. Cassandra Morgan found it neither terrible nor good, arguing that it failed to make viewers care about the couple, the lead actress or the authorship mystery, which ended without a real resolution.

documents.title: A Fabled Holiday
documents.tagline: A love story not quite by the book.
documents.overview: Talia and her childhood best friend Anderson unexpectedly reunite in a curiously familiar looking town full of Christmas spirit that restores its visitors when they need it most.
documents.plot:
A Fabled Holiday is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas fantasy romantic comedy-drama television film produced by BRB Pictures for Hallmark Channel's Countdown to Christmas season. It stars Brooke D'Orsay as Talia and Ryan Paevey as Anderson, with John Prowse as Charles, Patti Allan as Mildred, John Murphy as Mayor Miles, Rochelle Greenwood as Judy and Daphne Hoskins as Izzy, alongside Jake Guy, Benjamin Jacobson, Carmel Amit, David Attar and Madeline Hirvonen. The film runs 84 minutes under the tagline "A love story not quite by the book."

As children, Talia and Anderson were best friends who loved the classic Wunderbrook Christmas Story, a fairytale book given to Talia by her father shortly before he died. After his death Talia and her mother moved away, and although the two friends kept in touch for a time, thirty years pass without contact. Talia now runs a bookstore and has given up on her dream of becoming an author after repeated rejections from publishers, while Anderson is a surgeon shaken by the loss of his first patient as an attending physician. A chance meeting in her bookstore reunites them, and soon circumstances beyond their control bring both of them, along with other wayward guests, to the Gingerbread Inn in the cosy town of Wunderbrook, which looks curiously like the one in their beloved book. The guests include a married couple, Diane and Keith, who have lost their way, and Charles, an elderly widower afraid both of moving on and of being alone. The town's residents, led by Mayor Miles, have until Christmas Eve to set each visitor back on the right path during Wonder Week, a festival of tree lightings, markets and a mysterious procession, while the sharp-tongued Mildred plays her own part. As Talia sets out to solve the mystery of the town, she and Anderson rediscover their friendship and the possibility of something more.

The film premiered on Hallmark Channel on 3 December 2022. Brett White of Decider recommended it, likening the eerie town and its residents to Stephen King or the Endless of The Sandman and praising Prowse and Allan, while noting that Anderson never sparked as Talia did. Erin E. Gross of Fangirlish thought highly of it and hoped for sequels exploring Wunderbrook's secrets. Alonso Duralde of TheWrap ranked it 29th of Hallmark's 43 new holiday films, calling it a big swing but finding the leads miscast.

documents.title: Hanukkah on Rye
documents.tagline: Two rival delis serving a whole latke of love.
documents.overview: A matchmaker connects Molly and Jacob, but their new romance is put to the test when they realize that they are competing deli owners. Will a Hanukkah miracle keep them together?
documents.plot:
Hanukkah on Rye is a 2022 American Hanukkah romantic comedy television film directed by Peter DeLuise from a screenplay by Julie Sherman Wolfe. Produced for Hallmark Media with Just To Be Clear Productions, it stars Yael Grobglas and Jeremy Jordan, with Linda Darlow, Paula Shaw, David Eisner, Lisa Horner and Harry Nelken, and features the singer-songwriter Lisa Loeb, who contributed a new Hanukkah song. The film premiered on the Hallmark Channel on 18 December 2022 and runs 84 minutes.

Molly (Grobglas) hopes to take over Gilbert's, her family's struggling, staunchly traditional deli on New York's Lower East Side, from her parents, if it does not go out of business first. Jacob (Jordan) is the heir to Zimmer's, a Los Angeles deli that has thrived by embracing modernity, serving fajitas and decorating with light-up menorahs, and his parents send him to New York to scout locations for a new franchise. The building he settles on turns out to be just down the street from Gilbert's. Meanwhile the two singletons' meddling grandmothers have signed them up with an elite Jewish matchmaker whose supposedly foolproof method requires clients to write longhand letters to an anonymous match. As Molly and Jacob spar in person over their rival businesses, they are also falling in love through their letters. Bonding over the scarcity of good Hanukkah songs and their families' stories of immigrant ancestors pursuing the American dream, the pair must discover whether their romance can survive their families' competing business interests, in a story that takes in a latke competition and climaxes with an old immigration tale.

The film was well received. TheWrap ranked it fourth of Hallmark's 43 new holiday films of 2022, describing it as a big bowl of The Shop Around the Corner with a dollop of Crossing Delancey and praising the lovely lead performances, Wolfe's sprightly screenplay and Loeb's new song. Talia Lakritz of Business Insider called it an authentic, delightful rom-com that finally got Hallmark's Hanukkah films right after earlier efforts that felt like Christmas movies with Jewish characters added as an afterthought. Irene Katz Connelly of the Forward found it schlocky but an indisputable improvement, with jokes that felt written by and for Jews, though she considered it essentially a knockoff of Nora Ephron's You've Got Mail.

documents.title: Haul Out the Holly
documents.tagline: There glows the neighborhood.
documents.overview: Emily arrives home, hoping to visit her parents, only to discover that they are leaving on a trip of their own. As she stays at their house for the holidays, their HOA is determined to get Emily to participate in the neighborhood’s many Christmas festivities.
documents.plot:
Haul Out the Holly is a 2022 Canadian-American Christmas romantic comedy television film produced for Hallmark Channel by Hallmark Media. It stars Lacey Chabert as Emily and Wes Brown as Jared, with Stephen Tobolowsky as the eccentric neighbour Ned, Melissa Peterman as Pamela, Ellen Travolta, Peter Jacobson and Carrie Morgan as Emily's parents and Eliza Hayes Maher. Its title comes from a lyric of "We Need a Little Christmas", and it was promoted with the tagline "There glows the neighborhood." By Decider's count it was Chabert's twelfth Hallmark holiday film, and the actress described it as her first romantic comedy for the network.

Emily is a freelance copy editor who grew up on Evergreen Lane, a relentlessly festive street whose homeowners' association her parents shaped for decades with strict holiday rules, making her childhood Christmases feel like all work and no play. When her boyfriend breaks up with her, ruining her holiday plans, she accepts her parents' invitation to come home, only to learn on arrival that they are leaving for Florida, where they are house-hunting, and that she will spend Christmas alone in her childhood home. Without the decorations her parents normally put up, the house falls foul of the HOA, now led by Jared, an architect and Emily's childhood friend, who keeps arriving at her door with citations and a tape measure. Pressed by Jared and a collection of quirky neighbours, including Ned, who initiates her into "Team Kringle", and the exacting Pamela, Emily is drawn into the neighbourhood's many traditions: a Christmas carnival, a tree lighting, a snowman tableau and a cookie contest. As she decorates the house and takes part, she finds Jared's childlike Christmas devotion oddly charming, comes to understand why her parents valued service to the community during the holidays, and grows closer to him.

The film premiered on Hallmark Channel in November 2022. Brett White of Decider called it a quick-witted treat that succeeded by committing fully to the classic Hallmark format, praising Tobolowsky and Peterman as possibly the two funniest performances of the season and declaring Chabert the network's holiday queen. Alonso Duralde of TheWrap ranked it third of Hallmark's 43 new holiday films of 2022 for its genuine laughs, while Jodi Walker of The Ringer enjoyed the supporting cast but found the neighbourhood's pressure on Emily cult-like, comparing it to Midsommar.

documents.title: Holiday Heritage
documents.overview: Ella returns to her hometown to mend fences with her fractured family. With the help of Griffin, her ex-boyfriend, she encourages her family to celebrate Christmas and Kwanzaa and to heal their past wounds before it’s too late.
documents.plot:
Holiday Heritage is a 2022 Canadian Christmas and Kwanzaa family drama television film directed by Alfons Adetuyi from a screenplay by Rhonda Baraka. Produced by Muse Entertainment, it was the Hallmark Channel's first film built around Kwanzaa. It stars Lyndie Greenwood, Brooks Darnell, Holly Robinson Peete and Darlene Cooke, with Jennifer de Lucia, Jason Verma and Rothaford Gray in supporting roles, and features a score by Michael Richard Plowman.
